grade9-biology.explanation: An endemic species occurs naturally in one place only.

grade9-biology.question: Name the square frame used to sample the organisms in a measured area of ground.
grade9-biology.answer: Quadrat
grade9-biology.hint: It is placed at random on the ground.
grade9-biology.explanation: A quadrat samples a measured square so the organisms in it can be counted.

grade9-biology.question: Give the term for the large-scale cutting down of forest.
grade9-biology.answer: Deforestation
grade9-biology.hint: One word.
grade9-biology.explanation: Deforestation is the clearing of forest on a large scale.

grade9-biology.question: State one way of protecting biodiversity in Mauritius.
grade9-biology.answer: Protect the native forest
grade9-biology.hint: Think about habitat, or about introduced species.
grade9-biology.explanation: Protecting habitat, controlling invasive species and captive breeding all help.

grade9-biology.question: Name the natural event, common in Mauritius, that destroys habitats by uprooting trees.
grade9-biology.answer: Cyclone
grade9-biology.hint: It arrives in the summer months.
grade9-biology.explanation: Cyclones strip and uproot trees, destroying habitat.

grade9-biology.question: What does the term biodiversity refer to?
options: The number of individual animals in a habitat
The range of non-living conditions in an environment
The variety of living organisms in a given area
The total mass of all plants in an ecosystem
grade9-biology.answer: The variety of living organisms in a given area
acceptableAnswers: The variety of living organisms in a given area
grade9-biology.hint: Bio = life; diversity = variety.
grade9-biology.explanation: Biodiversity is the variety of all living things — including species, habitats and genetic variation — found in a given area.

grade9-biology.question: Which of the following is an example of species diversity?
options: All the members of one ant colony living in the same nest
A forest containing trees, ferns, insects, birds and mammals
A single lake covering a very large geographical area
Two dogs of the same breed having slightly different coat colours
grade9-biology.answer: A forest containing trees, ferns, insects, birds and mammals
acceptableAnswers: A forest containing trees, ferns, insects, birds and mammals
grade9-biology.hint: Species diversity is about the range of different species present.
grade9-biology.explanation: Species diversity measures the number of different species in an area; a forest with many types of organisms has high species diversity.

grade9-biology.question: A scientist notes that the individuals in a population of Mauritian pink pigeons have slightly different beak sizes and feather patterns. Which type of biodiversity does this illustrate?
grade9-biology.answer: Genetic diversity within a species
grade9-biology.hint: The differences are between individuals of the same species.
grade9-biology.explanation: Genetic diversity refers to the variation in genes between individuals of the same species; different beak sizes and feather patterns in a pigeon population arise from genetic differences.

grade9-biology.question: Which of the following best describes habitat diversity?
options: The variation in DNA sequences between members of a population
The total number of different species found in one square metre
The range of different types of ecosystems and habitats in a region
The number of individuals of a single species in one habitat
grade9-biology.answer: The range of different types of ecosystems and habitats in a region
acceptableAnswers: The range of different types of ecosystems and habitats in a region
grade9-biology.hint: Habitat diversity is about the variety of places where organisms live.
grade9-biology.explanation: Habitat diversity refers to the variety of different habitats and ecosystems — such as coral reefs, forests, wetlands and grasslands — present in a region.

grade9-biology.question: How many main components of biodiversity are scientists generally agreed upon?
options: One — species diversity is the only recognised measure
Four — species, gene, habitat and climate diversity
Two — plant diversity and animal diversity only
Three — species, genetic and habitat diversity
grade9-biology.answer: Three — species, genetic and habitat diversity
acceptableAnswers: Three — species, genetic and habitat diversity
grade9-biology.hint: Think of the three levels at which biodiversity is measured.
grade9-biology.explanation: Biodiversity is measured at three levels: species diversity (range of species), genetic diversity (variation within species) and habitat/ecosystem diversity (range of habitats).

grade9-biology.question: A coral reef off the coast of Mauritius contains hundreds of species of fish, coral, molluscs and echinoderms. Which type of biodiversity is this BEST describing?
options: Genetic diversity within the coral species
Habitat diversity across the whole island
Species diversity in a marine habitat
Ecosystem services of the Indian Ocean
grade9-biology.answer: Species diversity in a marine habitat
acceptableAnswers: Species diversity in a marine habitat
grade9-biology.hint: The question counts different types of organisms.
grade9-biology.explanation: The presence of hundreds of different species in the coral reef is a measure of high species diversity; it is not describing variation within one species or the range of different habitats.

grade9-biology.question: Why is it important to consider genetic diversity as well as species diversity when measuring biodiversity?
options: Species diversity always includes genetic diversity, so they are the same measure
Counting species is impossible, so genetic measures are used instead
Genetic diversity determines how well a species can adapt to future changes
Genetic diversity only matters for domesticated crops, not wild species
grade9-biology.answer: Genetic diversity determines how well a species can adapt to future changes
acceptableAnswers: Genetic diversity determines how well a species can adapt to future changes
grade9-biology.hint: Think about what happens when all individuals of a species are genetically identical.
grade9-biology.explanation: High genetic diversity gives a species a wider range of traits; if conditions change, some individuals are more likely to survive. Low genetic diversity increases the risk of extinction from disease or climate change.

grade9-biology.question: A conservation scientist says: "Mauritius has lost biodiversity at all three levels." What does this mean?
options: The total mass of organisms has fallen, food chains are shorter, and the climate has become wetter
Fewer species exist now, individuals within species are more similar genetically, and fewer habitat types remain
The country now imports more food, tourism has declined, and the sea temperature has dropped
Animals can no longer breed successfully, plants produce fewer seeds, and rivers have dried up
grade9-biology.answer: Fewer species exist now, individuals within species are more similar genetically, and fewer habitat types remain
acceptableAnswers: Fewer species exist now, individuals within species are more similar genetically, and fewer habitat types remain
grade9-biology.hint: Match the three components of biodiversity to the three losses described.
grade9-biology.explanation: Loss of biodiversity at all three levels means: reduced species diversity (fewer species), reduced genetic diversity (less variation within remaining species) and reduced habitat diversity (fewer different ecosystems surviving).

grade9-biology.question: A tropical island has 200 species, all of which are tree species. A nearby island has 50 species spread across insects, birds, reptiles, plants and fungi. Which island has GREATER biodiversity? Explain.
options: The 50-species island — it has greater variety across different groups of organisms
The 200-species island — it has the highest total number of species present
Both islands are equal — species count is the only valid measure of biodiversity
Neither can be compared — they have different climates and areas
grade9-biology.answer: The 50-species island — it has greater variety across different groups of organisms
acceptableAnswers: The 50-species island — it has greater variety across different groups of organisms
grade9-biology.hint: Biodiversity is about variety, not just total number.
grade9-biology.explanation: True biodiversity reflects variation across different groups; an island with 50 species spread across many taxonomic groups shows greater ecological and functional diversity than one with 200 species all from the same group.

grade9-biology.question: Which of these habitats is generally considered to have the HIGHEST species biodiversity on Earth?
grade9-biology.answer: Tropical rainforests
grade9-biology.hint: Warm, wet, productive environments support the most life.
grade9-biology.explanation: Tropical rainforests receive high rainfall and sunlight all year, providing food and shelter for an enormous number of species — they contain over half of all known species despite covering less than 6% of land.

grade9-biology.question: Black River Gorges National Park in Mauritius protects native forests, rivers and grasslands. Which aspect of biodiversity does this park best preserve?
options: Species diversity, by introducing new species from other countries
Climate diversity, by controlling rainfall in the park area
Habitat diversity, by maintaining several different ecosystem types
Genetic diversity, by keeping all animals genetically identical
grade9-biology.answer: Habitat diversity, by maintaining several different ecosystem types
acceptableAnswers: Habitat diversity, by maintaining several different ecosystem types
grade9-biology.hint: The park contains multiple different ecosystem types.
grade9-biology.explanation: Black River Gorges protects native forests, wetlands and grasslands in one area; this maintains habitat diversity by keeping several ecosystem types intact within a single protected region.

grade9-biology.question: Scientists find that all remaining individuals of an endangered Mauritian plant species are genetically nearly identical. Why is this a serious concern even if their numbers are currently stable?
options: Conservationists cannot measure biodiversity if all individuals look the same
Genetically identical plants always produce seeds that fail to germinate properly
Identical genes mean the plants will produce poisonous fruits over time
A single disease or climate change event could kill all individuals simultaneously
grade9-biology.answer: A single disease or climate change event could kill all individuals simultaneously
acceptableAnswers: A single disease or climate change event could kill all individuals simultaneously
grade9-biology.hint: Think about what genetic uniformity means for resilience.
grade9-biology.explanation: When all individuals share very similar genes, none may carry traits that resist a new pathogen or cope with changed conditions; a single outbreak could wipe out the entire population, making extinction highly likely.

grade9-biology.question: Which term describes the benefits that humans receive from natural ecosystems?
grade9-biology.answer: Ecosystem services
grade9-biology.hint: Think about what nature does for people.
grade9-biology.explanation: Ecosystem services are the benefits that healthy ecosystems provide to humans, including clean air, clean water, food production, medicine and climate regulation.

grade9-biology.question: Which process, carried out by flowering plants, is an ecosystem service that is essential for food production?
options: Respiration of roots in the soil
grade9-biology.answer: Pollination of crops by insects
grade9-biology.hint: Without this service, most fruit and vegetable crops would not produce food.
grade9-biology.explanation: Many crop plants depend on insects (especially bees) for pollination; loss of insect diversity directly reduces crop yields and threatens food security.

grade9-biology.question: Many modern medicines were first discovered from wild organisms. Which of the following best illustrates this link between biodiversity and medicine?
options: Penicillin was discovered from the Penicillium mould fungus
Doctors use electricity generated by hydroelectric dams
Vaccines are produced entirely from chemicals in a factory
Surgery is performed using instruments made from iron ore
grade9-biology.answer: Penicillin was discovered from the Penicillium mould fungus
acceptableAnswers: Penicillin was discovered from the Penicillium mould fungus
grade9-biology.hint: The first widely used antibiotic came from a fungus.
grade9-biology.explanation: Penicillin, the first widely used antibiotic, was isolated from the Penicillium fungus; many cancer drugs, pain killers and other medicines also originate from wild plants, animals and microorganisms.

grade9-biology.question: How does a high level of biodiversity in crop wild relatives help to secure the future of food production?
options: Wild relatives do not need water, making farming cheaper in dry regions
Wild relatives carry genes that can be used to breed disease-resistant or climate-tolerant crop varieties
Wild relatives attract pollinators that then move exclusively to farmed fields
Wild relatives produce more food per hectare than cultivated varieties on all soil types
grade9-biology.answer: Wild relatives carry genes that can be used to breed disease-resistant or climate-tolerant crop varieties
acceptableAnswers: Wild relatives carry genes that can be used to breed disease-resistant or climate-tolerant crop varieties
grade9-biology.hint: Genetic diversity in wild plants gives breeders raw material to improve crops.
grade9-biology.explanation: Wild relatives of crop plants often carry genes for pest resistance, drought tolerance or disease resistance; breeders use these genes to develop improved varieties that can feed a growing and changing world.

grade9-biology.question: Why does a diverse ecosystem tend to be more stable than one with only a few species?
options: Diverse ecosystems always receive more rainfall and have richer soils than simple ones
If one species declines, others can fill its role and maintain ecosystem function
A greater number of species means that food chains are shorter and simpler
More species means more predators, which keeps all population sizes exactly equal
grade9-biology.answer: If one species declines, others can fill its role and maintain ecosystem function
acceptableAnswers: If one species declines, others can fill its role and maintain ecosystem function
grade9-biology.hint: More species means more redundancy in the system.
grade9-biology.explanation: In a species-rich ecosystem, several organisms may perform similar roles (e.g. as pollinators or decomposers); if one declines, others compensate, so the ecosystem continues to function.

grade9-biology.question: Forests help regulate the climate by absorbing large quantities of which gas?
grade9-biology.answer: Carbon dioxide
grade9-biology.hint: Trees use this gas during photosynthesis.
grade9-biology.explanation: Trees absorb carbon dioxide during photosynthesis and store the carbon in their trunks, roots and leaves; forests therefore act as large carbon sinks that help slow climate change.

grade9-biology.question: Mangrove forests along the Mauritian coastline protect the shoreline from storm damage and trap sediment. Which category of ecosystem service does this represent?
options: Cultural services — they provide places for recreation and tourism
Provisioning services — they provide materials for human use
Supporting services — they directly produce oxygen for breathing
Regulating services — they control natural processes
grade9-biology.answer: Regulating services — they control natural processes
acceptableAnswers: Regulating services — they control natural processes
grade9-biology.hint: The mangroves are controlling (regulating) a natural process: erosion.
grade9-biology.explanation: Regulating services are ecosystem benefits that involve the regulation of natural processes; mangroves reduce coastal erosion, absorb wave energy and stabilise sediment, all of which regulate the impact of storms.

grade9-biology.question: In Mauritius, the dodo became extinct in the 17th century. The tambalacoque tree (Calvaria major) was thought to depend on the dodo to disperse its seeds. What does this illustrate about biodiversity?
options: Biodiversity loss only matters when it affects species that humans can eat
Extinction of large birds always causes an increase in insect populations
Trees with large seeds can only be dispersed by large extinct animals
The loss of one species can affect the survival of other species in the same ecosystem
grade9-biology.answer: The loss of one species can affect the survival of other species in the same ecosystem
acceptableAnswers: The loss of one species can affect the survival of other species in the same ecosystem
grade9-biology.hint: Think about what happens when a seed disperser disappears.
grade9-biology.explanation: The dodo ate tambalacoque fruits and the seeds passed through its gut; with the dodo gone, seeds could not germinate as effectively, showing how extinction of one species can threaten others linked to it in the ecosystem.

grade9-biology.question: A reef tourist site in Mauritius depends on healthy coral reefs with high fish diversity. Which ecosystem service does this represent AND why is biodiversity essential to it?
options: Supporting service — the reef produces oxygen that tourists breathe while snorkelling
Regulating service — the reef controls ocean temperature, which tourists prefer for swimming
Cultural service — tourists pay to see diverse marine life, so fewer species directly reduces economic income
Provisioning service — tourists consume fish directly from the reef during their visit
grade9-biology.answer: Cultural service — tourists pay to see diverse marine life, so fewer species directly reduces economic income
acceptableAnswers: Cultural service — tourists pay to see diverse marine life, so fewer species directly reduces economic income
grade9-biology.hint: Tourism gives people experiences and cultural enrichment — which service category is that?
grade9-biology.explanation: Tourism is a cultural ecosystem service; tourists are attracted by the diversity and beauty of the reef ecosystem, so a loss of fish species or coral diversity directly reduces the value and income that this service provides.

grade9-biology.question: Wetland ecosystems in Mauritius naturally filter pollutants from water before it reaches the sea. Which category of ecosystem service is this?
options: Regulating services — the wetland controls a natural water-purification process
Supporting services — the wetland produces the nutrients that other ecosystems need
Cultural services — the wetland is used for outdoor recreation and education
Provisioning services — the wetland provides clean drinking water directly to homes
grade9-biology.answer: Regulating services — the wetland controls a natural water-purification process
acceptableAnswers: Regulating services — the wetland controls a natural water-purification process
grade9-biology.hint: Filtering and purifying water is a regulation of a natural process.
grade9-biology.explanation: Wetlands trap sediment and absorb nutrients and pollutants from run-off water; this is a regulating service because the ecosystem is moderating a natural process (the water cycle and water quality).

grade9-biology.question: Why is it important to conserve genetic diversity in wild plant species, even those that humans do not currently use?
options: Genetic diversity in wild plants prevents invasive species from establishing nearby
Wild plants with more genetic diversity always grow faster in all conditions
All wild plants produce oxygen that is more pure than that from cultivated species
Those plants may contain genes useful to medicine or agriculture in the future
grade9-biology.answer: Those plants may contain genes useful to medicine or agriculture in the future
acceptableAnswers: Those plants may contain genes useful to medicine or agriculture in the future
grade9-biology.hint: We cannot predict which species or genes will become useful.
grade9-biology.explanation: Many medicines and improved crop varieties have been developed from species once considered unimportant; conserving wild genetic diversity preserves options for future scientific discoveries.

grade9-biology.question: A keystone species is one that has a disproportionately large effect on its ecosystem relative to its population size. What would most likely happen if a keystone predator were removed from an ecosystem?
options: Biodiversity would increase because fewer animals are being eaten and killed
Other predators would immediately take over the same role with no effect on biodiversity
Producer populations would decrease because less predator dung fertilises the soil
Prey populations would explode and out-compete other species, reducing overall biodiversity
grade9-biology.answer: Prey populations would explode and out-compete other species, reducing overall biodiversity
acceptableAnswers: Prey populations would explode and out-compete other species, reducing overall biodiversity
grade9-biology.hint: Think about what controls prey numbers in the absence of a predator.
grade9-biology.explanation: Without the keystone predator, certain prey populations grow unchecked, consuming so much vegetation or smaller prey that other species are displaced, leading to a collapse in species diversity in the ecosystem.

grade9-biology.question: What is a quadrat used for in ecological field work?
options: Sampling the species and abundance of organisms in a defined area
Testing the pH and mineral content of a soil sample
Measuring the temperature of water in a river or pond sample
Counting the total number of animals in a very large territory
grade9-biology.answer: Sampling the species and abundance of organisms in a defined area
acceptableAnswers: Sampling the species and abundance of organisms in a defined area
grade9-biology.hint: A quadrat marks out a fixed area for counting.
grade9-biology.explanation: A quadrat is a square frame (e.g. 1 m × 1 m) placed on the ground; scientists count all individuals of each species inside it to estimate abundance across a larger area.

grade9-biology.question: Why must quadrats be placed randomly in a survey area?
options: To make sure every quadrat lands in the most species-rich part of the area
To ensure that only rare species are recorded and common ones are ignored
To avoid bias and ensure the sample represents the whole area fairly
To save time by concentrating sampling in easy-to-reach locations
grade9-biology.answer: To avoid bias and ensure the sample represents the whole area fairly
acceptableAnswers: To avoid bias and ensure the sample represents the whole area fairly
grade9-biology.hint: Non-random placement would bias the results.
grade9-biology.explanation: Random placement ensures that each part of the survey area has an equal chance of being sampled, so the results give a representative and unbiased estimate of the whole area.

grade9-biology.question: How are random numbers typically used in quadrat surveys?
options: To count how many species are found inside each individual quadrat
To determine which species to record and which ones to ignore
To calculate the total area covered by the quadrats placed in the field
To generate random coordinates that determine where each quadrat is placed
grade9-biology.answer: To generate random coordinates that determine where each quadrat is placed
acceptableAnswers: To generate random coordinates that determine where each quadrat is placed
grade9-biology.hint: Lay a grid and use numbers to choose x and y positions.
grade9-biology.explanation: A pair of random numbers from a table or calculator is used to select the x and y coordinates on a grid overlaid on the survey area, ensuring that quadrat positions are unbiased.

grade9-biology.question: A student places 10 quadrats of 1 m² each in a 100 m² field and counts 30 daisy plants in total. What is the best estimate for the total number of daisies in the field?
grade9-biology.answer: 300 daisy plants
grade9-biology.hint: Find the mean per quadrat, then scale up to the full area.
grade9-biology.explanation: Mean per quadrat = 30 ÷ 10 = 3 plants per m². Total estimate = 3 × 100 = 300 daisy plants.

grade9-biology.question: What is the main limitation of using only one quadrat to estimate species abundance in a large habitat?
options: One quadrat takes too long to complete compared to using many
One quadrat cannot be placed randomly without mathematical equipment
One quadrat may not be representative of the whole area
A single quadrat always records too many species to count accurately
grade9-biology.answer: One quadrat may not be representative of the whole area
acceptableAnswers: One quadrat may not be representative of the whole area
grade9-biology.hint: A single measurement is always less reliable than many.
grade9-biology.explanation: A single quadrat gives only one data point; that particular spot may be unusually rich or poor in species compared to the rest of the habitat, making the estimate unreliable.

grade9-biology.question: A student places quadrats only under trees because it is easier to work in the shade. How does this affect the reliability of the results?
options: It has no effect because species are randomly distributed under trees anyway
It reduces reliability because trees produce more oxygen, affecting plant growth
It improves reliability because shade provides consistent temperature conditions
It introduces systematic bias — shaded areas may have different species from sunny patches
grade9-biology.answer: It introduces systematic bias — shaded areas may have different species from sunny patches
acceptableAnswers: It introduces systematic bias — shaded areas may have different species from sunny patches
grade9-biology.hint: Placing quadrats in chosen spots rather than randomly is biased sampling.
grade9-biology.explanation: Choosing to sample only under trees is a biased approach; shade-tolerant species would be over-represented and sun-loving species ignored, so the data would not reflect the true composition of the habitat.

grade9-biology.question: What does percentage cover measure in a quadrat?
options: The percentage of the total survey area sampled by the quadrat
The number of individual plants of each species inside the quadrat
The fraction of the quadrat area covered by a particular species
The proportion of species in the quadrat that are rare or endangered
grade9-biology.answer: The fraction of the quadrat area covered by a particular species
acceptableAnswers: The fraction of the quadrat area covered by a particular species
grade9-biology.hint: You estimate how much of the square is taken up by that species.
grade9-biology.explanation: Percentage cover estimates what proportion of the quadrat area is occupied by a species; it is useful for plants that are difficult to count individually, such as grasses.

grade9-biology.question: A researcher is comparing the biodiversity of two grassland sites. She uses more quadrats at one site than the other because it is larger. Why is this a sensible decision?
options: Larger sites have more sunlight, so more quadrats are needed to record light levels
More quadrats always produce lower estimates, correcting for the site being larger
More quadrats in a larger site give a more representative sample of its greater area
The number of quadrats must match the number of species expected to be found
grade9-biology.answer: More quadrats in a larger site give a more representative sample of its greater area
acceptableAnswers: More quadrats in a larger site give a more representative sample of its greater area
grade9-biology.hint: Sample size should relate to the area being studied.
grade9-biology.explanation: Using more quadrats in a larger area ensures that a similar proportion of the site is sampled; using the same small number of quadrats in a much larger area would mean each quadrat represents a greater unseen area, reducing reliability.

grade9-biology.question: Quadrats are most suitable for surveying which type of organism?
options: Microscopic organisms such as bacteria and single-celled algae
Underground organisms such as earthworms and burrowing beetles
Fast-moving animals such as fish, birds and running insects
Plants and slow-moving animals such as limpets and barnacles
grade9-biology.answer: Plants and slow-moving animals such as limpets and barnacles
acceptableAnswers: Plants and slow-moving animals such as limpets and barnacles
grade9-biology.hint: Think about which organisms stay in one place long enough to be counted.
grade9-biology.explanation: Quadrats work best for organisms that do not move or move very slowly; plants, lichens, barnacles and limpets stay within the quadrat long enough to be counted accurately.

grade9-biology.question: What is a tropical cyclone?
options: A sudden cold snap that kills tropical plants and animals in hours
A long dry period with no rainfall lasting several months or years
A gradual rise in sea level that floods low-lying coastal habitats
An intense rotating storm with very strong winds and heavy rainfall
grade9-biology.answer: An intense rotating storm with very strong winds and heavy rainfall
acceptableAnswers: An intense rotating storm with very strong winds and heavy rainfall
grade9-biology.hint: Mauritius experiences these storms, especially between November and April.
grade9-biology.explanation: A tropical cyclone is a powerful rotating storm system characterised by very strong winds, heavy rain and low atmospheric pressure; Mauritius lies in the cyclone belt of the Indian Ocean.

grade9-biology.question: How does a cyclone directly reduce biodiversity in a forest ecosystem?
options: Low air pressure during a cyclone causes animals to lose their sense of direction
Strong winds uproot trees and destroy nesting sites, killing or displacing many species
Heavy rain raises ocean salinity, which kills freshwater species in coastal rivers
Cyclones bring cold air that freezes tropical organisms not adapted to low temperatures
grade9-biology.answer: Strong winds uproot trees and destroy nesting sites, killing or displacing many species
acceptableAnswers: Strong winds uproot trees and destroy nesting sites, killing or displacing many species
grade9-biology.hint: Think about the physical destruction caused by high winds.
grade9-biology.explanation: Cyclone winds can snap and uproot trees, strip leaves, flatten undergrowth and destroy nesting holes; this eliminates food sources and shelter for birds, mammals and invertebrates, causing deaths and habitat loss.

grade9-biology.question: How does a severe drought reduce plant biodiversity in a tropical region?
options: Lack of rain increases soil pH until all plant nutrients become unavailable
Drought raises soil temperature until all plant seeds are destroyed by heat
Drought causes animals to migrate away, removing pollination of all plant species
Water stress kills species that are not drought-tolerant, leaving only hardy survivors
grade9-biology.answer: Water stress kills species that are not drought-tolerant, leaving only hardy survivors
acceptableAnswers: Water stress kills species that are not drought-tolerant, leaving only hardy survivors
grade9-biology.hint: Plants that need regular moisture cannot survive long dry periods.
grade9-biology.explanation: Prolonged drought deprives plants of the water needed for photosynthesis and growth; species with shallow roots or high water requirements die first, leaving mainly drought-tolerant species and reducing species diversity.

grade9-biology.question: Which natural disaster is Mauritius MOST frequently affected by that can damage forest biodiversity?
grade9-biology.answer: Tropical cyclones
grade9-biology.hint: Mauritius is located in the Indian Ocean cyclone belt.
grade9-biology.explanation: Mauritius is regularly struck by tropical cyclones between November and April; their strong winds and flooding cause significant damage to native vegetation and wildlife populations.

grade9-biology.question: Following a severe drought, a population of frogs in a Mauritian river declines sharply. What is the most likely direct reason?
options: Low rainfall increases soil nitrogen, which is toxic to amphibian skin
Frogs are sensitive to sound, and drought causes louder conditions that stress them
Reduced water levels shrink the aquatic habitat that frogs depend on for breeding
Drought raises air temperature until frogs cannot move fast enough to catch prey
grade9-biology.answer: Reduced water levels shrink the aquatic habitat that frogs depend on for breeding
acceptableAnswers: Reduced water levels shrink the aquatic habitat that frogs depend on for breeding
grade9-biology.hint: Frogs need standing or flowing water to lay eggs and for tadpoles to develop.
grade9-biology.explanation: Frogs are aquatic breeders; drought reduces or eliminates pools and streams, so eggs and tadpoles die and adults lose their breeding habitat, causing the population to fall sharply.

grade9-biology.question: After a cyclone, some native bird species recover their population quickly while others remain at very low numbers for years. What factor most likely explains this difference?
options: Bird species that are native to Mauritius always out-compete introduced species after a cyclone
Recovery speed depends entirely on how much financial aid is provided by conservationists
Species with larger body sizes always recover more rapidly than small species after storms
Species with flexible diets and multiple nesting options recover faster than specialised species
grade9-biology.answer: Species with flexible diets and multiple nesting options recover faster than specialised species
acceptableAnswers: Species with flexible diets and multiple nesting options recover faster than specialised species
grade9-biology.hint: Specialists depend on one food source or nest site that may be destroyed.
grade9-biology.explanation: Generalist species can switch to alternative food sources and nest in various sites; specialists that depend on one tree species for food or nesting have fewer options after a cyclone destroys those resources.

grade9-biology.question: How can a powerful cyclone damage coral reef biodiversity around Mauritius?
options: Cyclones lower sea temperature until coral is unable to photosynthesise and dies immediately
Storm surges carry freshwater offshore that permanently increases the salinity of the reef
High winds remove all dissolved carbon dioxide from the sea, preventing coral growth
Strong waves and debris physically break apart coral structures and smother reefs with sediment
grade9-biology.answer: Strong waves and debris physically break apart coral structures and smother reefs with sediment
acceptableAnswers: Strong waves and debris physically break apart coral structures and smother reefs with sediment
grade9-biology.hint: Think about the physical impact of storm waves on a shallow reef.
grade9-biology.explanation: Cyclone waves can be several metres high; they smash coral branches, overturn boulders, and deposit sediment over living coral, blocking light and suffocating the organisms, causing significant reef damage.

grade9-biology.question: A conservationist argues that drought is a greater long-term threat to biodiversity than a single cyclone. Which argument best supports this view?
options: Drought only affects plants, whereas cyclones damage both plants and animals simultaneously
Biodiversity always increases after a cyclone because new habitats are created by fallen trees
Cyclones last only a few days, so animals can always escape their path by moving away
Drought can persist for months or years, causing cumulative mortality that species cannot recover from
grade9-biology.answer: Drought can persist for months or years, causing cumulative mortality that species cannot recover from
acceptableAnswers: Drought can persist for months or years, causing cumulative mortality that species cannot recover from
grade9-biology.hint: Compare the duration and ongoing impact of each natural disaster.
grade9-biology.explanation: A cyclone is an acute event lasting hours to days; species begin to recover almost immediately. Drought is a chronic stress lasting months or years, draining water resources and causing prolonged mortality with no recovery window.

grade9-biology.question: Which natural process removes water from the soil and reduces its availability for plants during a dry period?
options: Decomposition by bacteria, which uses up water molecules quickly
Pollination by insects, which moves water droplets between flowers
Evaporation from the soil surface and transpiration by plants
Photosynthesis in green leaves, which converts water to sugar
grade9-biology.answer: Evaporation from the soil surface and transpiration by plants
acceptableAnswers: Evaporation from the soil surface and transpiration by plants
grade9-biology.hint: Two processes remove water from plants and soil to the air.
grade9-biology.explanation: During dry periods, evaporation from the soil and transpiration through plant leaves continuously remove water; without rainfall to replenish it, soil moisture drops and plants become water-stressed.

grade9-biology.question: Flash flooding caused by heavy cyclone rainfall can reduce soil biodiversity by:
options: Washing away topsoil and the organisms it contains into rivers and the sea
Cooling the soil so rapidly that all soil organisms enter permanent dormancy
Raising soil oxygen levels until anaerobic bacteria are killed instantly
Adding excess minerals to the soil that stimulate bacterial overgrowth
grade9-biology.answer: Washing away topsoil and the organisms it contains into rivers and the sea
acceptableAnswers: Washing away topsoil and the organisms it contains into rivers and the sea
grade9-biology.hint: Topsoil contains the most organic matter and living organisms.
grade9-biology.explanation: Flash floods carry away the nutrient-rich topsoil layer along with seeds, invertebrates and microorganisms; this strips the land of the biological resources needed for plant regrowth and soil ecosystem recovery.

grade9-biology.question: Why are endemic island species, such as those found only in Mauritius, particularly vulnerable to natural disasters compared to species with wide geographical ranges?
options: Island species are always smaller, which makes them weaker and less able to survive storms
They exist in only one location, so a single disaster can affect their entire global population
Natural disasters cannot reach islands because they are surrounded by ocean
Island species never evolved defensive behaviours, leaving them helpless against any threat
grade9-biology.answer: They exist in only one location, so a single disaster can affect their entire global population
acceptableAnswers: They exist in only one location, so a single disaster can affect their entire global population
grade9-biology.hint: If a species lives only on one island, there is nowhere else for it to survive.
grade9-biology.explanation: An endemic species found only on Mauritius has its entire global population in one place; a severe cyclone or drought that devastates that island threatens the species with total extinction, as there are no other populations elsewhere.

grade9-biology.question: After a major cyclone, which of the following would BEST help a forest ecosystem to recover its biodiversity?
options: Burning the fallen wood to release nutrients quickly into the soil for faster growth
Introducing new predator species to control the populations of surviving prey animals
Protecting the area from further disturbance so that natural succession can occur
Immediately planting fast-growing exotic trees to replace all the fallen native trees
grade9-biology.answer: Protecting the area from further disturbance so that natural succession can occur
acceptableAnswers: Protecting the area from further disturbance so that natural succession can occur
grade9-biology.hint: Natural recovery needs time and stability — not new disturbances.
grade9-biology.explanation: Given adequate protection from further disturbance (especially human interference), native species naturally recolonise and regenerate over time through ecological succession; introducing exotics or burning debris can hinder this process.

grade9-biology.question: What is deforestation?
options: The natural death of old trees that have reached the end of their lifespan
The movement of forest species to new areas due to climate change
The large-scale removal of trees and forest habitats by humans
The replanting of trees on previously farmed agricultural land
grade9-biology.answer: The large-scale removal of trees and forest habitats by humans
acceptableAnswers: The large-scale removal of trees and forest habitats by humans
grade9-biology.hint: It involves humans clearing forest areas.
grade9-biology.explanation: Deforestation is the human-driven process of clearing forests, typically for agriculture, logging, urban development or charcoal production, resulting in the permanent loss of woodland habitat.

grade9-biology.question: How does deforestation in Mauritius directly reduce biodiversity?
options: It destroys the habitat that native species depend on, leaving them without food or shelter
It removes all the carbon dioxide from the air, preventing photosynthesis by remaining plants
It causes sea levels to rise around the island, flooding coastal wetland habitats
It increases rainfall so much that rivers flood and destroy aquatic ecosystems
grade9-biology.answer: It destroys the habitat that native species depend on, leaving them without food or shelter
acceptableAnswers: It destroys the habitat that native species depend on, leaving them without food or shelter
grade9-biology.hint: When the habitat disappears, the species that live there disappear too.
grade9-biology.explanation: Native Mauritian species — from birds and reptiles to insects and plants — are adapted to forest habitats; when those forests are cleared, species lose their food sources, nesting sites and shelter, leading to local extinction.

grade9-biology.question: What is an invasive alien species?
options: A species introduced from another region that establishes and spreads, harming native biodiversity
A species that migrates naturally between habitats each season as conditions change
Any animal that is kept as a pet and occasionally escapes into the wild briefly
A native species that suddenly grows much faster than it did in previous years
grade9-biology.answer: A species introduced from another region that establishes and spreads, harming native biodiversity
acceptableAnswers: A species introduced from another region that establishes and spreads, harming native biodiversity
grade9-biology.hint: It is non-native, introduced — usually by humans — and causes ecological harm.
grade9-biology.explanation: Invasive alien species are organisms brought to a new region (intentionally or accidentally) where they have no natural predators or competitors; they spread rapidly and out-compete or prey on native species.

grade9-biology.question: Which of the following is a well-known invasive alien plant species in Mauritius that threatens native forest?
grade9-biology.answer: Psidium cattleianum (strawberry guava)
grade9-biology.hint: This fruit-bearing shrub has spread widely across Mauritian native forests.
grade9-biology.explanation: Strawberry guava (Psidium cattleianum) was introduced to Mauritius and has become one of the most destructive invasive plants, out-competing native vegetation in the Black River Gorges and other protected areas.

grade9-biology.question: How do invasive alien species reduce native biodiversity?
options: They carry diseases that only affect invasive species, reducing their own populations first
They produce chemicals that increase soil fertility, which native plants cannot tolerate
They out-compete native species for food, space and light, causing native populations to decline
They always hybridise with native species, producing sterile offspring that cannot reproduce
grade9-biology.answer: They out-compete native species for food, space and light, causing native populations to decline
acceptableAnswers: They out-compete native species for food, space and light, causing native populations to decline
grade9-biology.hint: Invasive species often spread rapidly because they face fewer competitors or predators.
grade9-biology.explanation: In their new environment, invasive species often face no natural predators or diseases that control them; they grow faster or reproduce more quickly than native species and crowd them out of available resources.

grade9-biology.question: Why are invasive alien species often so successful in their new environment?
options: They have no natural predators, parasites or competitors in the new region to control their populations
They carry genetic mutations that allow them to adapt instantly to the new climate
Humans always protect invasive species from harm because they are rare in the new country
They are always larger and physically stronger than the native species they encounter
grade9-biology.answer: They have no natural predators, parasites or competitors in the new region to control their populations
acceptableAnswers: They have no natural predators, parasites or competitors in the new region to control their populations
grade9-biology.hint: Biological controls that limited the species at home are absent in the new place.
grade9-biology.explanation: In their native range, invasive species are kept in check by predators, parasites and competitors that co-evolved with them; in the new environment these controls are absent, allowing the species to reproduce unchecked.

grade9-biology.question: How does water pollution from agricultural run-off affect aquatic biodiversity?
options: Pesticide residues in water raise the pH until fish scales dissolve and the fish die
Run-off adds so much calcium to the water that invertebrate shells become too thick to open
Excess fertilisers cause algal blooms that deplete oxygen and kill aquatic animals
Agricultural water heats rivers to above 50 °C, which cooks all aquatic invertebrates
grade9-biology.answer: Excess fertilisers cause algal blooms that deplete oxygen and kill aquatic animals
acceptableAnswers: Excess fertilisers cause algal blooms that deplete oxygen and kill aquatic animals
grade9-biology.hint: This process is called eutrophication.
grade9-biology.explanation: Fertiliser run-off enriches water with nitrates and phosphates; algae multiply rapidly, blocking light and then dying; their decomposition by bacteria consumes dissolved oxygen, causing hypoxia and death of fish and invertebrates.

grade9-biology.question: What is habitat fragmentation, and why is it particularly harmful to biodiversity?
options: The introduction of new species into a fragmented habitat to replace lost native ones
A process where habitats are divided into smaller sections that are then individually protected
Breaking large habitats into isolated patches — species cannot move between patches to breed or find food
The physical removal of all plants from a habitat, leaving bare rock and soil behind
grade9-biology.answer: Breaking large habitats into isolated patches — species cannot move between patches to breed or find food
acceptableAnswers: Breaking large habitats into isolated patches — species cannot move between patches to breed or find food
grade9-biology.hint: Small isolated populations are at much greater risk of extinction than large connected ones.
grade9-biology.explanation: Habitat fragmentation divides continuous habitats with roads, farms or buildings; isolated populations become too small to be genetically viable, cannot migrate to new areas, and are more vulnerable to local extinction events.

grade9-biology.question: How does the widespread use of pesticides in agriculture reduce biodiversity?
options: Pesticides kill non-target organisms such as insects and birds that feed on treated plants
Pesticides are only harmful to the specific pest species and have no wider effects
Pesticides attract invasive species that then colonise areas of treated farmland
Pesticides improve soil quality so much that only a few dominant plant species can thrive
grade9-biology.answer: Pesticides kill non-target organisms such as insects and birds that feed on treated plants
acceptableAnswers: Pesticides kill non-target organisms such as insects and birds that feed on treated plants
grade9-biology.hint: Most pesticides are not perfectly selective — other organisms are also affected.
grade9-biology.explanation: Many pesticides kill non-target insects including pollinators such as bees; animals that eat treated insects (e.g. insectivorous birds) are also affected through bioaccumulation, reducing species diversity across food chains.

grade9-biology.question: What does the term habitat destruction mean in the context of biodiversity loss?
options: The natural process by which old habitats are replaced by newer ones over geological time
The protection of habitats by creating national parks and nature reserves around them
The permanent alteration of a natural habitat so that it can no longer support its native species
The temporary disturbance of a habitat that species can recover from within a few weeks
grade9-biology.answer: The permanent alteration of a natural habitat so that it can no longer support its native species
acceptableAnswers: The permanent alteration of a natural habitat so that it can no longer support its native species
grade9-biology.hint: Destruction means the habitat can no longer function as it did.
grade9-biology.explanation: Habitat destruction occurs when human activities permanently change a natural environment — through building, farming, mining or drainage — so that the species that previously lived there can no longer survive.

grade9-biology.question: Why are small islands such as Mauritius particularly vulnerable to the effects of invasive alien species?
options: Island governments cannot afford to remove invasive species, unlike mainland countries
Islands always have warmer climates that allow invasive species to breed all year round
Islands have high genetic diversity in native species that makes them easy for invaders to exploit
Island species evolved in isolation and lack defences or behaviours to deal with new predators or competitors
grade9-biology.answer: Island species evolved in isolation and lack defences or behaviours to deal with new predators or competitors
acceptableAnswers: Island species evolved in isolation and lack defences or behaviours to deal with new predators or competitors
grade9-biology.hint: Isolation means no co-evolution with certain types of threats.
grade9-biology.explanation: Mauritian species evolved on an isolated island with no mammalian predators for millions of years; they have no evolved fear responses or physical defences against introduced predators such as rats, cats and mongooses.

grade9-biology.question: How does climate change threaten the coral reefs around Mauritius?
options: Warmer air temperatures evaporate the ocean until reefs are exposed to air and dry out
Rising sea temperatures cause coral bleaching, which can kill the coral and destroy reef biodiversity
Climate change causes more lightning strikes that directly burn coral during tropical storms
Climate change increases river flow, which carries so much freshwater that reefs freeze
grade9-biology.answer: Rising sea temperatures cause coral bleaching, which can kill the coral and destroy reef biodiversity
acceptableAnswers: Rising sea temperatures cause coral bleaching, which can kill the coral and destroy reef biodiversity
grade9-biology.hint: Coral lives in symbiosis with algae; heat disrupts this relationship.
grade9-biology.explanation: When sea temperatures rise above 1–2 °C above normal for extended periods, corals expel their symbiotic algae (zooxanthellae), turning white (bleaching); without the algae they lose their food source and may die, devastating reef biodiversity.

grade9-biology.question: A 1 m² quadrat is placed randomly in a field. It contains 8 dandelion plants. The field has a total area of 50 m². Estimate the total number of dandelion plants in the field.
grade9-biology.hint: Multiply the count in the quadrat by the number of times the quadrat fits into the field.
grade9-biology.explanation: The quadrat is 1 m², so it fits into the 50 m² field 50 times. Estimated total = 8 × 50 = 400 dandelion plants.

grade9-biology.question: A student counts 12 buttercup plants in a 0.5 m² quadrat. The total area of the grassland being surveyed is 20 m². Estimate the total number of buttercup plants in the grassland.
grade9-biology.hint: First find the number of plants per m², then multiply by the total area.
grade9-biology.explanation: 12 plants in 0.5 m² = 24 plants per m². Total estimate = 24 × 20 = 480 buttercup plants.

grade9-biology.question: A 2 m × 2 m quadrat placed in a meadow contains 20 clover plants. Estimate the total number of clover plants in a 400 m² meadow.
grade9-biology.hint: Calculate the area of the quadrat first, then find plants per m², then scale up.
grade9-biology.explanation: Quadrat area = 2 × 2 = 4 m². Density = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 plants per m². Total = 5 × 400 = 2000 clover plants.

grade9-biology.question: Five 1 m² quadrats are placed randomly in a habitat. The number of grass plants counted in each quadrat is 4, 6, 5, 3 and 7. Calculate the mean number of grass plants per quadrat.
grade9-biology.hint: Add all five counts together, then divide by the number of quadrats.
grade9-biology.explanation: Total = 4 + 6 + 5 + 3 + 7 = 25. Mean = 25 ÷ 5 = 5 plants per quadrat.

grade9-biology.question: Give one example of a habitat in Mauritius that is known for high biodiversity.
grade9-biology.answer: Coral reef
grade9-biology.hint: Think about Mauritius environments on land and in the sea.
grade9-biology.explanation: Mauritius has highly biodiverse habitats including its coral reef system, the native forests of Black River Gorges National Park, and coastal mangroves.

grade9-biology.question: State one ecosystem service that forests provide to humans.
grade9-biology.answer: Carbon dioxide absorption / carbon storage
grade9-biology.hint: Think about what trees do for the environment and for people.
grade9-biology.explanation: Forests provide many ecosystem services including: absorbing carbon dioxide, purifying water, preventing soil erosion, providing timber, and supplying medicines from plants.

grade9-biology.question: State one reason why quadrats must be placed randomly when conducting a biodiversity survey.
grade9-biology.answer: To prevent bias in the results
acceptableAnswers: To prevent bias in the results
so results represent the whole area
to ensure all areas have equal chance of being sampled
grade9-biology.hint: Think about what goes wrong if you choose where to place each quadrat.
grade9-biology.explanation: Random placement prevents the scientist from (deliberately or accidentally) choosing areas that are unusually rich or poor in species, making the sample representative of the whole habitat.

grade9-biology.question: Name one natural threat to biodiversity in Mauritius.
grade9-biology.answer: Tropical cyclone
grade9-biology.hint: Think about natural events that damage habitats in the Indian Ocean region.
grade9-biology.explanation: Mauritius is regularly affected by tropical cyclones and periods of drought, both of which can damage habitats and reduce biodiversity.

grade9-biology.question: Give one example of an invasive alien species found in Mauritius.
grade9-biology.answer: Psidium cattleianum (strawberry guava)
grade9-biology.hint: Think of a plant or animal brought to Mauritius that now threatens native species.
grade9-biology.explanation: Mauritius has many invasive alien species including strawberry guava (Psidium cattleianum), the common myna bird (Acridotheres tristis), the mongoose, and the giant African land snail.

grade9-biology.question: What is photosynthesis?
options: The way a plant spreads its seeds
The process by which green plants make their own food
The process by which plants take in their oxygen at night
The way a plant takes water up its stem
grade9-biology.answer: The process by which green plants make their own food
acceptableAnswers: The process by which green plants make their own food
grade9-biology.hint: The plant makes food rather than taking it in.
grade9-biology.explanation: Photosynthesis is how a green plant makes glucose using light energy.

grade9-biology.question: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
grade9-biology.answer: Carbon dioxide
grade9-biology.hint: It enters through the stomata.
grade9-biology.explanation: Carbon dioxide is taken in from the air and used to build glucose.

grade9-biology.question: Which gas do plants give out during photosynthesis?
grade9-biology.answer: Oxygen
grade9-biology.hint: It is the waste product of the process.
grade9-biology.explanation: Oxygen is released as a by-product of photosynthesis.

grade9-biology.question: Which green substance in a leaf absorbs the light energy?
grade9-biology.answer: Chlorophyll
grade9-biology.hint: It is what makes a leaf green.
grade9-biology.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy and makes it available for photosynthesis.

grade9-biology.question: Where in a plant cell does photosynthesis take place?
grade9-biology.answer: In the chloroplasts
grade9-biology.hint: They are the structures that contain the chlorophyll.
grade9-biology.explanation: Chloroplasts contain the chlorophyll, so photosynthesis happens inside them.

grade9-biology.question: Why is photosynthesis important for animals as well as plants?
options: It provides animals with the water they drink
It keeps the soil warm enough for animals to live in
It removes all of the nitrogen from the air that animals breathe
It supplies the oxygen animals breathe and the food chains start there
grade9-biology.answer: It supplies the oxygen animals breathe and the food chains start there
acceptableAnswers: It supplies the oxygen animals breathe and the food chains start there
grade9-biology.hint: Think about what animals get from plants, directly or indirectly.
grade9-biology.explanation: Photosynthesis releases the oxygen animals need and makes the food that every food chain begins with.

grade9-biology.question: Which is the correct word equation for photosynthesis?
grade9-biology.answer: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen
grade9-biology.hint: The raw materials are on the left.
grade9-biology.explanation: Carbon dioxide and water are the raw materials; glucose and oxygen are the products.

grade9-biology.question: In the word equation for photosynthesis, what is needed but is NOT a reactant?
grade9-biology.answer: Light energy and chlorophyll
grade9-biology.hint: They are usually written above the arrow.
grade9-biology.explanation: Light and chlorophyll are needed for the reaction but are not used up as raw materials, so they go above the arrow.

grade9-biology.question: The word equation for respiration is the reverse of photosynthesis. Which equation is it?
grade9-biology.answer: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water
grade9-biology.hint: Swap the two sides of the photosynthesis equation.
grade9-biology.explanation: Respiration uses glucose and oxygen and releases carbon dioxide and water - the reverse of photosynthesis.

grade9-biology.question: In the leaf shown, which layer contains the most chloroplasts?
options: W, the thin protective layer on the top surface
Z, the small opening in the lower surface
Y, the loosely packed layer lower down
X, the layer of tall cells packed near the top
grade9-biology.answer: X, the layer of tall cells packed near the top
acceptableAnswers: X, the layer of tall cells packed near the top
grade9-biology.hint: Which layer is nearest the light and most tightly packed?
grade9-biology.explanation: X is the palisade layer: tall cells packed just under the surface, holding most of the chloroplasts to catch the light.

grade9-biology.question: In the leaf shown, what is the opening marked Z?
options: A root hair, which takes in water
A vein, which carries water to the leaf
A stoma, which lets gases in and out
A chloroplast, which absorbs the light
grade9-biology.answer: A stoma, which lets gases in and out
acceptableAnswers: A stoma, which lets gases in and out
grade9-biology.hint: It is a gap in the lower surface.
grade9-biology.explanation: Z is a stoma: a pore in the lower epidermis through which carbon dioxide enters and oxygen and water vapour leave.

grade9-biology.question: In the leaf shown, why does the layer marked Y have large air spaces between its cells?
options: So gases can move easily through the leaf
So the leaf can store more water there
So the leaf is stronger in the wind
So light can be reflected back up to the sky
grade9-biology.answer: So gases can move easily through the leaf
acceptableAnswers: So gases can move easily through the leaf
grade9-biology.hint: Think about what has to travel between the stoma and the cells.
grade9-biology.explanation: The air spaces of the spongy layer let carbon dioxide diffuse to the cells and oxygen diffuse out.

grade9-biology.question: Why is a leaf broad and flat?
options: It gives a large surface area to absorb light
It stops any water from reaching the leaf
It allows the leaf to store a lot of starch
It makes the leaf heavier so it does not blow away
grade9-biology.answer: It gives a large surface area to absorb light
acceptableAnswers: It gives a large surface area to absorb light
grade9-biology.hint: Think about catching as much light as possible.
grade9-biology.explanation: A broad flat leaf presents a large surface to the light and a short distance for gases to diffuse.

grade9-biology.question: Why is a leaf thin?
options: Gases have only a short distance to diffuse
It allows the leaf to fall off more easily
It reduces the amount of chlorophyll needed
It stops insects from eating the leaf
grade9-biology.answer: Gases have only a short distance to diffuse
acceptableAnswers: Gases have only a short distance to diffuse
grade9-biology.hint: Think about how far a gas has to travel inside it.
grade9-biology.explanation: A thin leaf means a short diffusion path, so carbon dioxide reaches the cells quickly.

grade9-biology.question: What is the job of the veins in a leaf?
options: To let gases pass in and out of the leaf
To carry water in and carry the food made away
To absorb all the light energy for photosynthesis
To protect the leaf from being eaten
grade9-biology.answer: To carry water in and carry the food made away
acceptableAnswers: To carry water in and carry the food made away
grade9-biology.hint: They are the transport system.
grade9-biology.explanation: The veins bring water to the leaf cells and carry the glucose made away to the rest of the plant.

grade9-biology.question: Which of these is NOT needed for photosynthesis?
grade9-biology.answer: Oxygen
grade9-biology.hint: One of these is a product, not a requirement.
grade9-biology.explanation: Oxygen is released by photosynthesis; light, carbon dioxide and water are what it needs.

grade9-biology.question: A plant is kept in complete darkness for a week. What happens to photosynthesis?
options: It continues at the same rate as before
It speeds up, because the plant rests
It stops, because there is no light energy
It continues, but produces carbon dioxide instead
grade9-biology.answer: It stops, because there is no light energy
acceptableAnswers: It stops, because there is no light energy
grade9-biology.hint: Light is one of the essential factors.
grade9-biology.explanation: Without light there is no energy to drive the reaction, so photosynthesis stops.

grade9-biology.question: A plant is given more light and photosynthesis speeds up, then stops speeding up. What is the likely reason?
options: Light has stopped being needed by the plant
Another factor, such as carbon dioxide, has become limiting
The plant has completely run out of its chlorophyll
The plant has begun to respire instead
grade9-biology.answer: Another factor, such as carbon dioxide, has become limiting
acceptableAnswers: Another factor, such as carbon dioxide, has become limiting
grade9-biology.hint: Something else must be in short supply.
grade9-biology.explanation: Once light is plentiful, the rate is held back by whichever factor is now in shortest supply.

grade9-biology.question: Why does a plant kept without water stop photosynthesising?
options: Water is what absorbs the light energy
Water is needed only by the roots
Water is one of the raw materials it needs
Water is the waste product it must get rid of
grade9-biology.answer: Water is one of the raw materials it needs
acceptableAnswers: Water is one of the raw materials it needs
grade9-biology.hint: Look at the left-hand side of the word equation.
grade9-biology.explanation: Water is a reactant in photosynthesis, so without it the reaction cannot proceed.

grade9-biology.question: Which chemical is used to test a leaf for starch, and what colour shows starch is present?
options: Iodine solution, which turns bright red
grade9-biology.answer: Iodine solution, which turns blue-black
grade9-biology.hint: Limewater is the test for a gas, not for starch.
grade9-biology.explanation: Iodine solution turns from brown to blue-black where starch is present.

grade9-biology.question: Why is a plant kept in the dark for two days before a starch test?
options: To make the leaves greener before testing
To let the plant absorb more carbon dioxide
To make the iodine work more quickly
To remove the starch already stored in its leaves
grade9-biology.answer: To remove the starch already stored in its leaves
acceptableAnswers: To remove the starch already stored in its leaves
grade9-biology.hint: The test must show only starch made during the experiment.
grade9-biology.explanation: Destarching empties the leaves first, so any starch found afterwards must have been made during the test.

grade9-biology.question: Why is a leaf boiled in ethanol before the iodine is added?
options: To remove the green chlorophyll so the colour change can be seen
To make the leaf absorb the iodine more slowly
To kill any insects living on the leaf surface
To add some extra starch to the leaf before it is tested
grade9-biology.answer: To remove the green chlorophyll so the colour change can be seen
acceptableAnswers: To remove the green chlorophyll so the colour change can be seen
grade9-biology.hint: The leaf is green, and so is the result hard to read.
grade9-biology.explanation: Ethanol dissolves the chlorophyll, decolourising the leaf so the blue-black of the iodine test is visible.

grade9-biology.question: Why is the ethanol heated in a water bath rather than directly over a flame?
options: A flame would turn the ethanol into starch
Ethanol will not become hot enough over a flame
A water bath heats the ethanol much faster
grade9-biology.answer: Ethanol catches fire very easily
grade9-biology.hint: It is a safety precaution.
grade9-biology.explanation: Ethanol is highly flammable, so it is heated indirectly in hot water and never over a naked flame.

grade9-biology.question: A variegated leaf, green in the middle and white at the edges, is tested for starch after a day in the light. What is the result?
options: Only the green part turns blue-black
No part of the leaf turns blue-black
Only the white part turns blue-black
grade9-biology.answer: Only the green part turns blue-black
acceptableAnswers: Only the green part turns blue-black
grade9-biology.hint: Which part contains chlorophyll?
grade9-biology.explanation: Only the green parts have chlorophyll, so only they photosynthesise and make starch.

grade9-biology.question: A leaf is sealed in a flask with soda lime, which absorbs carbon dioxide. After a day in the light, the starch test is negative. What does this show?
options: Carbon dioxide is needed for photosynthesis
grade9-biology.answer: Carbon dioxide is needed for photosynthesis
acceptableAnswers: Carbon dioxide is needed for photosynthesis
grade9-biology.hint: Only one factor was removed by the soda lime.
grade9-biology.explanation: The only thing taken away was carbon dioxide, and no starch was made, so carbon dioxide is essential.

grade9-biology.question: In that experiment, why is a second identical leaf set up without the soda lime?
options: To give the first leaf a great deal more light to work with
To make the experiment take a shorter time
To use up the oxygen made by the first leaf
As a control, to show the result is due to the missing carbon dioxide
grade9-biology.answer: As a control, to show the result is due to the missing carbon dioxide
acceptableAnswers: As a control, to show the result is due to the missing carbon dioxide
grade9-biology.hint: A fair test needs something to compare against.
grade9-biology.explanation: The control is identical except for the one factor being tested, so any difference must be caused by that factor.

grade9-biology.question: Name the green pigment that absorbs light for photosynthesis.
grade9-biology.answer: Chlorophyll
grade9-biology.hint: It makes leaves green.
grade9-biology.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs the light energy used in photosynthesis.

grade9-biology.question: Complete the word equation: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + ______
grade9-biology.answer: Oxygen
grade9-biology.hint: It is the gas given off.
grade9-biology.explanation: Photosynthesis produces glucose and oxygen.

grade9-biology.question: Name the small openings in the lower surface of a leaf that let gases in and out.
grade9-biology.answer: Stomata
grade9-biology.hint: Each one is called a stoma.
grade9-biology.explanation: Gases pass in and out through the stomata.

grade9-biology.question: Name the solution used to test a leaf for starch.
grade9-biology.answer: Iodine
grade9-biology.hint: It turns blue-black if starch is present.
grade9-biology.explanation: Iodine solution is the test for starch.

grade9-biology.question: State one factor, apart from water, that is essential for photosynthesis.
grade9-biology.answer: Light
grade9-biology.hint: Look at what appears above and to the left of the arrow.
grade9-biology.explanation: Light, carbon dioxide and chlorophyll are all essential.

grade9-biology.question: In which organelle does photosynthesis take place in plant cells?
grade9-biology.answer: Chloroplast
grade9-biology.hint: It is the green organelle found in plant cells.
grade9-biology.explanation: Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts, where the pigment chlorophyll captures light energy to drive the reaction.

grade9-biology.question: Which two substances are the raw materials (reactants) for photosynthesis?
grade9-biology.answer: Carbon dioxide and water
grade9-biology.hint: Think about what the plant takes in — from the air and from the soil.
grade9-biology.explanation: Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the air through their stomata and water from the soil through their roots — these are the two reactants for photosynthesis.

grade9-biology.question: What are the two main products made during photosynthesis?
grade9-biology.answer: Glucose and oxygen
grade9-biology.hint: One product stores energy; the other is a gas released into the air.
grade9-biology.explanation: Photosynthesis produces glucose (stored as chemical energy) and oxygen (released as a by-product through the stomata).

grade9-biology.question: What is the role of chlorophyll during photosynthesis?
options: To remove excess oxygen that builds up in the cell
To produce carbon dioxide for use in the leaf
To pump water upward from the roots to the leaf
To absorb light energy to drive the reaction
grade9-biology.answer: To absorb light energy to drive the reaction
acceptableAnswers: To absorb light energy to drive the reaction
grade9-biology.hint: It is a pigment — its job is to capture light.
grade9-biology.explanation: Chlorophyll is a green pigment that absorbs light energy (mainly red and blue wavelengths) and transfers it to drive the chemical reactions of photosynthesis.

grade9-biology.question: Photosynthesis converts one form of energy into another. Which of the following correctly describes this conversion?
options: Electrical energy from the soil is converted into light energy in the chloroplast
Light energy is converted into chemical energy stored in glucose
Chemical energy in glucose is converted into light energy in the leaf
Heat energy from the air is converted into glucose by the chloroplasts
grade9-biology.answer: Light energy is converted into chemical energy stored in glucose
acceptableAnswers: Light energy is converted into chemical energy stored in glucose
grade9-biology.hint: Energy is captured from sunlight and locked away in a sugar molecule.
grade9-biology.explanation: Photosynthesis is an energy-conversion process: light energy absorbed by chlorophyll is used to build glucose molecules, storing the energy as chemical potential energy.

grade9-biology.question: After photosynthesis, the glucose produced in a leaf can be used for which of the following?
options: Aerobic respiration to release energy for the plant
Breaking down carbon dioxide into carbon and oxygen
Producing more chlorophyll without any additional energy
Absorbing mineral ions directly from the soil
grade9-biology.answer: Aerobic respiration to release energy for the plant
acceptableAnswers: Aerobic respiration to release energy for the plant
grade9-biology.hint: Glucose is a fuel — what do living things do with fuel?
grade9-biology.explanation: Plants use glucose as a respiratory substrate to release energy for growth and other life processes; they can also convert it to starch for storage or cellulose for cell walls.

grade9-biology.question: Where does the carbon in the glucose produced during photosynthesis originally come from?
options: From carbon dioxide absorbed from the air
From minerals taken up by the roots from the soil
From water molecules absorbed through the stomata
From the carbon atoms inside the chlorophyll molecule
grade9-biology.answer: From carbon dioxide absorbed from the air
acceptableAnswers: From carbon dioxide absorbed from the air
grade9-biology.hint: Trace the carbon — where does CO₂ go once inside the leaf?
grade9-biology.explanation: CO₂ diffuses into the leaf through the stomata; during photosynthesis, its carbon atoms are incorporated into glucose molecules.

grade9-biology.question: A plant is kept in the dark for 48 hours. What happens to its rate of photosynthesis?
options: Photosynthesis stops completely because there is no light energy
Photosynthesis increases because darkness stimulates chlorophyll production
Photosynthesis slows slightly but continues using stored energy
Photosynthesis continues unchanged using heat energy instead of light
grade9-biology.answer: Photosynthesis stops completely because there is no light energy
acceptableAnswers: Photosynthesis stops completely because there is no light energy
grade9-biology.hint: Light is an essential requirement, not just an accelerator.
grade9-biology.explanation: Without light, chlorophyll cannot absorb energy, and the reactions of photosynthesis cannot proceed; the rate falls to zero in total darkness.

grade9-biology.question: Why is glucose often converted to starch for storage in plant leaves rather than remaining as glucose?
options: Starch molecules are small enough to be transported easily in the phloem
Starch releases more energy than glucose when broken down in respiration
Starch is insoluble, so it does not affect the osmotic balance of the cell
Glucose is too reactive and would damage the cell membrane over time
grade9-biology.answer: Starch is insoluble, so it does not affect the osmotic balance of the cell
acceptableAnswers: Starch is insoluble, so it does not affect the osmotic balance of the cell
grade9-biology.hint: Think about what would happen to the cell if a lot of soluble glucose built up inside it.
grade9-biology.explanation: Glucose is soluble and would raise the solute concentration inside the cell, causing water to enter by osmosis; starch is insoluble and has no osmotic effect, making it a safer long-term store.

grade9-biology.question: A sealed transparent container holds a plant in bright light. After several hours, what would you expect to happen to the CO₂ concentration inside the container?
options: It rises, because plants release CO₂ during the day the same as at night
It falls to zero within minutes as the plant absorbs all available CO₂
It falls, because the plant uses CO₂ faster than it produces it in the light
It stays the same, because photosynthesis and respiration always balance exactly
grade9-biology.answer: It falls, because the plant uses CO₂ faster than it produces it in the light
acceptableAnswers: It falls, because the plant uses CO₂ faster than it produces it in the light
grade9-biology.hint: In bright light, which process dominates — photosynthesis or respiration?
grade9-biology.explanation: In bright light, the rate of photosynthesis exceeds the rate of respiration, so CO₂ is consumed faster than it is produced; the net result is a fall in CO₂ concentration inside the container.

grade9-biology.question: A plant is placed in a sealed dark container. What would you expect to happen to the O₂ concentration over time?
options: It rises sharply, because darkness triggers an increase in the rate of photosynthesis
It falls, because the plant consumes oxygen in respiration without replacing it by photosynthesis
It stays the same, because dark conditions switch off all gas exchange completely
It rises, because plants always produce oxygen regardless of light conditions
grade9-biology.answer: It falls, because the plant consumes oxygen in respiration without replacing it by photosynthesis
acceptableAnswers: It falls, because the plant consumes oxygen in respiration without replacing it by photosynthesis
grade9-biology.hint: Plants respire continuously but only photosynthesise in light.
grade9-biology.explanation: All living cells, including plant cells, carry out aerobic respiration at all times and consume oxygen; in darkness, photosynthesis (which produces oxygen) stops, so the O₂ concentration falls.

grade9-biology.question: Which of the following correctly explains why plants are described as producers in a food chain?
options: They manufacture their own food from inorganic materials using light energy
They produce carbon dioxide that feeds the consumers higher in the chain
They manufacture food by breaking down organic material in the soil
They produce oxygen, which all other organisms in the food chain require
grade9-biology.answer: They manufacture their own food from inorganic materials using light energy
acceptableAnswers: They manufacture their own food from inorganic materials using light energy
grade9-biology.hint: The word "produce" here refers to making food, not just releasing a gas.
grade9-biology.explanation: Producers are organisms that manufacture organic molecules (glucose) from inorganic raw materials (CO₂ and water) using an external energy source (sunlight); this is photosynthesis.

grade9-biology.question: Which of the following correctly shows the word equation for photosynthesis?
