grade9-biology.explanation: Readings go straight into a table prepared beforehand, with the quantities and units already headed, so nothing is lost or mis-remembered.

grade9-biology.question: A column of a results table records the mass of a potato chip in grams. Which heading is correct?
grade9-biology.answer: Mass of chip / g
grade9-biology.hint: The heading names the quantity and gives the unit.
grade9-biology.explanation: A heading gives the quantity and its unit, written "Mass of chip / g", so the unit is not repeated beside every number in the column.

grade9-biology.question: Which chart best shows how many of each species were found in a quadrat survey?
grade9-biology.answer: A bar chart
grade9-biology.hint: The species are separate groups, not a continuous scale.
grade9-biology.explanation: Species are separate categories, so a bar chart with gaps between the bars is used; a line graph is for two quantities that vary continuously.

grade9-biology.question: A pupil plots the height of a bean plant against the number of days since sowing. What goes on the horizontal axis?
grade9-biology.answer: The number of days
grade9-biology.hint: The axis across the page carries the variable that was changed.
grade9-biology.explanation: The independent variable goes across the page and the measured quantity goes up it, so days are plotted horizontally and height vertically.

grade9-biology.question: Why must the scale on a graph axis go up in equal steps?
options: So the graph fits on a single page only
So the points are joined up with a ruler
So the shape of the graph is not distorted
So the axis needs no label or unit at all
grade9-biology.answer: So the shape of the graph is not distorted
acceptableAnswers: So the shape of the graph is not distorted
grade9-biology.hint: Think what uneven steps would do to a straight line.
grade9-biology.explanation: An even scale means equal distances stand for equal changes, so the pattern the graph shows is the pattern in the data.

grade9-biology.question: How should a pupil draw a specimen seen down a microscope?
options: With a pen and arrows drawn across the lines
With a ruler to draw the outline of the cells
With a soft pencil, shading and some colour
With a sharp pencil and clear unbroken lines
grade9-biology.answer: With a sharp pencil and clear unbroken lines
acceptableAnswers: With a sharp pencil and clear unbroken lines
grade9-biology.hint: A biological drawing is a record, not a picture.
grade9-biology.explanation: A biological drawing uses a sharp pencil and clean continuous lines with no shading or colour, so the structures are recorded exactly as seen.

grade9-biology.question: How should the label lines on a biological drawing be drawn?
options: In colour to match the part being named
With arrowheads at the end of each line
With a ruler and not crossing each other
grade9-biology.answer: With a ruler and not crossing each other
acceptableAnswers: With a ruler and not crossing each other
grade9-biology.hint: A label line must point to one part and one part only.
grade9-biology.explanation: Label lines are ruled, do not cross, and end without an arrowhead on the exact structure being named, so no label is ambiguous.

grade9-biology.question: Why is a tally kept while counting the woodlice found under a log?
options: It removes the need to count at all
It records each one as it is seen
It shows the mass of each woodlouse
It makes the total larger than it is
grade9-biology.answer: It records each one as it is seen
acceptableAnswers: It records each one as it is seen
grade9-biology.hint: The animals move while the counting is going on.
grade9-biology.explanation: A tally records each animal at the moment it is seen, so none is missed or counted twice while the count is under way.

grade9-biology.question: Five leaves measure 6.2, 5.8, 6.0, 6.4 and 6.1 cm. How should these be entered in the table?
grade9-biology.answer: All to one decimal place
grade9-biology.hint: Every value in a column is written the same way.
grade9-biology.explanation: A column is recorded to one consistent number of decimal places, matching the precision of the instrument that was used.

grade9-biology.question: What should appear at the top of every results table?
options: The name of the school and class
A copy of the whole hypothesis
A title saying what was measured
grade9-biology.answer: A title saying what was measured
acceptableAnswers: A title saying what was measured
grade9-biology.hint: A reader must know what the numbers are.
grade9-biology.explanation: A short title tells a reader what investigation the numbers come from before they read a single value.

grade9-biology.question: A pupil records the pulse rate of ten classmates before and after exercise. Which table layout is best?
options: One row for all the readings together
One row per pupil, one column per reading
One column holding every number found
A separate table for every single pupil
grade9-biology.answer: One row per pupil, one column per reading
acceptableAnswers: One row per pupil, one column per reading
grade9-biology.hint: Each pupil gives a pair of readings that belong together.
grade9-biology.explanation: A row per pupil with a column for each reading keeps the pair side by side, so the two columns can be compared straight down the page.

grade9-biology.question: Why should a reading be written down at the moment it is taken?
options: The instrument cannot be read a second time
Memory is unreliable and readings get lost
Readings change value if they are not used
Writing later makes the table look neater
grade9-biology.answer: Memory is unreliable and readings get lost
acceptableAnswers: Memory is unreliable and readings get lost
grade9-biology.hint: Think about the last reading of a long afternoon.
grade9-biology.explanation: Readings written later are remembered wrongly or lost altogether, and a lost reading cannot be recovered once the apparatus is packed away.

grade9-biology.question: A pupil will count bubbles from pond weed for one minute at each of five lamp distances. Which table should be prepared first?
options: Distance / cm and the name of the plant
Time / min and the mass of the plant
Distance / cm and bubbles per minute
Bubbles per minute and the date only
grade9-biology.answer: Distance / cm and bubbles per minute
acceptableAnswers: Distance / cm and bubbles per minute
grade9-biology.hint: The table needs one column for what is changed and one for what is measured.
grade9-biology.explanation: The table carries the independent variable in the first column and the dependent variable in the second, both headed with their units.

grade9-biology.question: In a quadrat survey a pupil writes "12" with no unit, but writes "6.2 cm" for a leaf. Why is that correct?
options: A count cannot be written in a table
A count is measured with a metre rule
A count of plants has no unit to give
A count is always smaller than a length
grade9-biology.answer: A count of plants has no unit to give
acceptableAnswers: A count of plants has no unit to give
grade9-biology.hint: Ask what was counted and what was measured.
grade9-biology.explanation: A count is a pure number and carries no unit, while a length is a measurement and must always be given with the unit used.

grade9-biology.question: Eight of ten seeds germinate in a warm dish and two of ten in a cold dish. Which conclusion do the results support?
options: All the seeds would germinate given time
Warmth increased germination in this test
Cold seeds germinate faster than warm ones
Warmth has no effect on these bean seeds
grade9-biology.answer: Warmth increased germination in this test
acceptableAnswers: Warmth increased germination in this test
grade9-biology.hint: Compare the two counts and say only what they show.
grade9-biology.explanation: Four times as many seeds germinated in the warm dish, so warmth increased germination in this test; nothing beyond the test may be claimed.

grade9-biology.question: Pulse rates of 72, 74, 73, 75 and 76 beats per minute were recorded. What is the mean?
grade9-biology.hint: Add the five readings, then divide by five.
grade9-biology.explanation: The five readings total 370, and 370 ÷ 5 = 74 beats per minute.

grade9-biology.question: Why is the mean of five pulse readings more useful than a single reading?
options: It makes the number easier to write down
It makes every reading exactly the same
It reduces the effect of a stray reading
It removes the need to repeat at all
grade9-biology.answer: It reduces the effect of a stray reading
acceptableAnswers: It reduces the effect of a stray reading
grade9-biology.hint: One reading on its own could be a fluke.
grade9-biology.explanation: Averaging several readings lets an unusually high or low one pull the result less far, so the mean is closer to the true value.

grade9-biology.question: One bubble count in a photosynthesis investigation is far below all the others. What should the pupil do?
options: Ignore it without saying anything at all
Change the hypothesis to match the count
Repeat that reading and check the set-up
Rub it out and write a value that fits
grade9-biology.answer: Repeat that reading and check the set-up
acceptableAnswers: Repeat that reading and check the set-up
grade9-biology.hint: An odd reading is a signal, not a nuisance.
grade9-biology.explanation: An anomalous reading is repeated and the apparatus checked; it may be a mistake, or it may be the most interesting thing in the results.

grade9-biology.question: The table shows a germination investigation. How many seeds germinated at 15 °C?
grade9-biology.hint: Find the row for 15 and read across.
grade9-biology.explanation: The row for 15 °C gives 13 seeds germinated out of the 20 sown.

grade9-biology.question: Using the same table, which statement describes the pattern?
options: More seeds germinate as it gets warmer
Fewer seeds germinate as it gets warmer
The number falls and then rises again
The number stays the same throughout
grade9-biology.answer: More seeds germinate as it gets warmer
acceptableAnswers: More seeds germinate as it gets warmer
grade9-biology.hint: Read down both columns together.
grade9-biology.explanation: Each rise in temperature is matched by a rise in the number germinating, although the increase becomes much smaller above 20 °C.

grade9-biology.question: Using the same table, predict how many seeds would germinate at 12 °C.
grade9-biology.answer: About 10
grade9-biology.hint: Look at the values in the rows either side of 12.
grade9-biology.explanation: Seven germinated at 10 °C and thirteen at 15 °C, so a value at 12 °C lies between them, at about ten.

grade9-biology.question: What must a conclusion be based on?
options: The tidiest graph drawn by the group
The prediction made before the test began
The opinion held by most of the class
The results that were actually measured
grade9-biology.answer: The results that were actually measured
acceptableAnswers: The results that were actually measured
grade9-biology.hint: A conclusion is read out of the data, not decided in advance.
grade9-biology.explanation: A conclusion states what the measurements show; a prediction that the results contradict is reported as unsupported, not written up as the answer.

grade9-biology.question: Two pupils carry out the same investigation and get different results. What is the best next step?
options: Decide that neither result can be used
Take the result of the older pupil only
Take the mean of the two different results
Repeat the investigation and compare again
grade9-biology.answer: Repeat the investigation and compare again
acceptableAnswers: Repeat the investigation and compare again
grade9-biology.hint: Which result can be reproduced?
grade9-biology.explanation: Repeating shows which result can be obtained again; averaging two results that disagree hides the disagreement instead of settling it.

grade9-biology.question: Leaf discs in sodium hydrogencarbonate solution rise to the surface sooner under a bright lamp. What does this suggest?
options: The discs float because they are lighter
Light has no effect on the leaf discs
grade9-biology.answer: Brighter light speeds up photosynthesis
grade9-biology.hint: The discs rise as a gas collects inside them.
grade9-biology.explanation: Oxygen made during photosynthesis collects in the discs and lifts them, so discs that rise sooner in brighter light show a faster rate.

grade9-biology.question: A graph of bean plant height against time rises steeply, then becomes flat after day 12. What does the flat part show?
options: The plant lost height after day 12
The plant grew faster after day 12
grade9-biology.answer: The plant stopped growing taller
grade9-biology.hint: A flat line means the measured value is not changing.
grade9-biology.explanation: A horizontal line means height stayed the same as time went on, so growth in height had stopped by day 12.

grade9-biology.question: A graph shows that as milk sales rose, children grew taller. A pupil concludes that milk makes children taller. What is wrong?
options: The graph shows no pattern at all
A graph can never show two quantities
A correlation does not prove a cause
The two lines fall rather than rise
grade9-biology.answer: A correlation does not prove a cause
acceptableAnswers: A correlation does not prove a cause
grade9-biology.hint: Two things can rise together because a third thing changed.
grade9-biology.explanation: Two quantities rising together is a correlation; showing that one causes the other needs a controlled investigation, not a graph.

grade9-biology.question: When a leaf is tested for starch, why is the ethanol heated in a beaker of hot water instead of over a Bunsen flame?
options: Ethanol boils at a very high point
Ethanol turns the leaf green again
Ethanol is heavier than the water
grade9-biology.answer: Ethanol catches fire very easily
grade9-biology.hint: Think what ethanol vapour does near a naked flame.
grade9-biology.explanation: Ethanol is highly flammable, so the Bunsen is turned off and the tube stood in hot water; heating it over a flame risks setting the vapour alight.

grade9-biology.question: How should a microscope be carried from the cupboard to the bench?
options: By the stage, with one hand only
By the eyepiece, held up to the light
By the arm, with a hand under the base
By the mirror, kept level at all times
grade9-biology.answer: By the arm, with a hand under the base
acceptableAnswers: By the arm, with a hand under the base
grade9-biology.hint: The heaviest part needs supporting.
grade9-biology.explanation: One hand grips the arm and the other supports the base, so the instrument cannot swing, tip or drop its eyepiece out.

grade9-biology.question: A pupil cuts a finger on a broken microscope slide. What should be done first?
options: Write the accident in the report
Wash the slide and use it again
grade9-biology.answer: Tell the teacher straight away
grade9-biology.hint: An injury is dealt with before anything else.
grade9-biology.explanation: The teacher is told at once so the wound is treated and the broken glass cleared safely; the write-up comes long afterwards.

grade9-biology.question: Why must hands be washed after handling pond water?
options: It may leave the fingers slightly wet
It may stain the skin a green colour
It may make the hands feel very cold
grade9-biology.answer: It may carry harmful micro-organisms
grade9-biology.hint: Think what lives in still water besides the plants.
grade9-biology.explanation: Pond water carries bacteria and other micro-organisms that can cause illness if they reach the mouth, so hands are washed before anything else is touched.

grade9-biology.question: Why are agar plates in a school laboratory incubated at about 25 °C rather than at 37 °C?
options: It keeps the lid sealed onto the dish
It discourages bacteria that harm humans
It makes the bacteria grow much faster
It stops the agar jelly from melting away
grade9-biology.answer: It discourages bacteria that harm humans
acceptableAnswers: It discourages bacteria that harm humans
grade9-biology.hint: What temperature is the inside of a person?
grade9-biology.explanation: Micro-organisms that infect people grow best at body temperature, so school cultures are kept nearer 25 °C to discourage them.

grade9-biology.question: Why is the lid of an agar plate taped at four points instead of being sealed all the way round?
options: It keeps the agar from drying out fully
Air can still reach the growing colonies
It makes the plate easier to open later
The tape would not stick all the way round
grade9-biology.answer: Air can still reach the growing colonies
acceptableAnswers: Air can still reach the growing colonies
grade9-biology.hint: Which micro-organisms grow where there is no air?
grade9-biology.explanation: Taping at points holds the lid on while letting air in, which discourages the airless conditions that favour more dangerous bacteria.

grade9-biology.question: Why must nothing be eaten or drunk in a biology laboratory?
options: Eating slows the practical work down a great deal
Crumbs left on the bench look untidy to others
Chemicals and micro-organisms may be swallowed
A spilled drink would wet the floor tiles
grade9-biology.answer: Chemicals and micro-organisms may be swallowed
acceptableAnswers: Chemicals and micro-organisms may be swallowed
grade9-biology.hint: Think what may be on a bench, a hand or a beaker.
grade9-biology.explanation: Stains, preservatives and cultures reach the mouth through food and drink, so nothing is ever eaten at the bench and hands are washed before leaving.

grade9-biology.question: Why should long hair be tied back during a practical lesson?
options: It could reach a flame or an apparatus
It could make the eyepiece hard to use
It could pick up dust from the benches
It could hide the label on a specimen
grade9-biology.answer: It could reach a flame or an apparatus
acceptableAnswers: It could reach a flame or an apparatus
grade9-biology.hint: Think what hangs forward when a pupil leans over the bench.
grade9-biology.explanation: Loose hair falls forward over a burner or into a specimen, so it is tied back before any practical work begins.

grade9-biology.question: During a dissection, in which direction should the blade of a scalpel be moved?
options: Across the palm of the free hand
Towards the hand holding the specimen
Upwards, towards the face of the pupil
Away from the hand holding the specimen
grade9-biology.answer: Away from the hand holding the specimen
acceptableAnswers: Away from the hand holding the specimen
grade9-biology.hint: Where would the blade go if it slipped?
grade9-biology.explanation: A blade that slips carries on in the direction it was travelling, so it is always drawn away from the fingers and away from the body.

grade9-biology.question: A pupil with a cut on one hand is asked to handle soil in an investigation. What should they do?
options: Cover the cut with a waterproof dressing
Wash the cut and carry on without gloves
Rub soil away from the cut afterwards
Leave the cut open so it dries quickly
grade9-biology.answer: Cover the cut with a waterproof dressing
acceptableAnswers: Cover the cut with a waterproof dressing
grade9-biology.hint: A cut is a way in.
grade9-biology.explanation: Soil carries bacteria, including tetanus, and broken skin lets them in, so the cut is covered before the soil is touched at all.

grade9-biology.question: Why are safety goggles worn when iodine solution is used?
options: It would smell strongly of the solution
It would make the eyes water briefly
It would stain the eyebrows brown
It would sting and damage the eyes
grade9-biology.answer: It would sting and damage the eyes
acceptableAnswers: It would sting and damage the eyes
grade9-biology.hint: Think what a splash would do.
grade9-biology.explanation: Iodine solution irritates and can damage the eye, and a splash from a dropper reaches the face easily, so goggles are worn throughout.

grade9-biology.question: What must happen to used agar plates at the end of an investigation?
options: They are opened and rinsed at the sink
They are sterilised before being thrown away
They are put straight into the paper bin
They are stored on the shelf for next term
grade9-biology.answer: They are sterilised before being thrown away
acceptableAnswers: They are sterilised before being thrown away
grade9-biology.hint: The colonies are still alive.
grade9-biology.explanation: Plates are heated in an autoclave or pressure cooker to kill the cultures first; unopened, unsterilised plates must never reach an ordinary bin.

grade9-biology.question: Why must a pupil never prick a finger to make a slide of their own blood?
options: Blood can carry infections between people
Blood dries far too quickly to be of use
Blood is much too dark to be seen clearly
Blood cells are far too small for a slide
grade9-biology.answer: Blood can carry infections between people
acceptableAnswers: Blood can carry infections between people
grade9-biology.hint: What can pass from one person to another in blood?
grade9-biology.explanation: Blood can carry viruses such as HIV and hepatitis, and a shared lancet or spilled drop can pass them on, so school blood sampling is not permitted.

grade9-biology.question: Why should practical work be carried out with a partner rather than alone?
options: The results will always agree with each other
Help is at hand if something goes wrong
The work can be finished in half the time
Only one pupil then needs to wear goggles
grade9-biology.answer: Help is at hand if something goes wrong
acceptableAnswers: Help is at hand if something goes wrong
grade9-biology.hint: Think about an accident with nobody else there.
grade9-biology.explanation: A partner can call the teacher, steady apparatus or fetch help, which is why investigations are done in cooperation and never alone.

grade9-biology.question: A spirit lamp is knocked over and burning alcohol spreads across the bench. What should be done first?
options: Blow hard at the flames until they go out
Tell the teacher and stand well clear
Pour cold water over the burning spirit
Carry the lamp outside to the corridor
grade9-biology.answer: Tell the teacher and stand well clear
acceptableAnswers: Tell the teacher and stand well clear
grade9-biology.hint: Carrying or fanning a fire makes it travel.
grade9-biology.explanation: The teacher smothers the flames with a damp cloth or fire blanket; water spreads burning spirit and moving or blowing on it spreads it further.

grade9-biology.question: A pupil collects pond water, examines a drop under a microscope, then goes straight out to lunch. Which precaution was missed?
options: Collecting more pond water than needed
Using a lower power on the microscope
Drawing the specimen before going out
grade9-biology.answer: Washing their hands before eating
grade9-biology.hint: What could travel from the sample to the mouth?
grade9-biology.explanation: Micro-organisms from the pond sample are on the fingers, so hands are washed thoroughly before food is handled or the laboratory is left.

grade9-biology.question: Why is a jar of preserved biological material never opened at a pupil bench?
options: The label would peel away from the glass jar
The jar is a good deal heavier than it looks
The specimen inside would be far too small to see
The preserving fluid gives off harmful fumes
grade9-biology.answer: The preserving fluid gives off harmful fumes
acceptableAnswers: The preserving fluid gives off harmful fumes
grade9-biology.hint: It is the liquid, not the specimen, that is the hazard.
grade9-biology.explanation: Preserving fluids give off irritating fumes, so a jar is opened only by the teacher, in a fume cupboard or a well ventilated room.

grade9-biology.question: Why are stools pushed under the bench during a practical lesson?
options: So nobody trips while carrying apparatus
So the class can be counted more easily
So the benches look tidy for the teacher
So there is room to store the microscopes
grade9-biology.answer: So nobody trips while carrying apparatus
acceptableAnswers: So nobody trips while carrying apparatus
grade9-biology.hint: Think about a pupil crossing the room with a hot beaker.
grade9-biology.explanation: A clear gangway means nobody trips while carrying glassware, cultures or hot apparatus, which is when a fall does most harm.

grade9-biology.question: Which section of a report states what the investigation set out to find?
grade9-biology.answer: The aim
grade9-biology.hint: It is written before the work is done.
grade9-biology.explanation: The aim states the purpose of the investigation; the method says how it was done and the results record what was measured.

grade9-biology.question: Which section sets out, step by step, how the investigation was carried out?
grade9-biology.answer: The method
grade9-biology.hint: It is the part another pupil would follow.
grade9-biology.explanation: The method describes each step in order, in enough detail that somebody else could carry out the same investigation.

grade9-biology.question: Why is the method of a germination investigation written in enough detail for someone else to follow?
options: So another pupil can repeat it exactly
So the report fills more pages of writing
So the conclusion can be written first
So the teacher can see the neat handwriting
grade9-biology.answer: So another pupil can repeat it exactly
acceptableAnswers: So another pupil can repeat it exactly
grade9-biology.hint: What makes a finding trustworthy?
grade9-biology.explanation: A method that can be repeated lets others check the result, and a finding nobody else can reproduce cannot be trusted.

grade9-biology.question: In which tense is the method of an investigation report normally written?
grade9-biology.answer: The past tense
grade9-biology.hint: The work has already been done.
grade9-biology.explanation: The method reports work already carried out, so it reads "the seeds were soaked overnight", not "soak the seeds overnight".

grade9-biology.question: A report of a photosynthesis investigation includes a drawing of the apparatus. What must the drawing carry?
options: The results written across the middle
A scale bar showing the true size
Colour shading on every glass part
Labels naming each piece of apparatus
grade9-biology.answer: Labels naming each piece of apparatus
acceptableAnswers: Labels naming each piece of apparatus
grade9-biology.hint: A reader must be able to name what they are looking at.
grade9-biology.explanation: The apparatus diagram is a labelled line drawing, so a reader can identify the funnel, the tube and the plant without reading the method again.

grade9-biology.question: Where in a report do the numbers measured during the investigation belong?
options: In a results table with headed columns
In the middle of the method paragraph
In the aim, before the work is begun
In the conclusion, written as sentences
grade9-biology.answer: In a results table with headed columns
acceptableAnswers: In a results table with headed columns
grade9-biology.hint: Numbers are set out, not buried in prose.
grade9-biology.explanation: Measurements belong in a headed results table where the pattern can be read down the columns; the conclusion then says what that pattern means.

grade9-biology.question: What should the conclusion of an investigation do?
options: Answer the aim using the results found
Give the opinion of the whole group
List the apparatus that was used again
Repeat the method in shorter sentences
grade9-biology.answer: Answer the aim using the results found
acceptableAnswers: Answer the aim using the results found
grade9-biology.hint: Look back at what the investigation set out to do.
grade9-biology.explanation: The conclusion answers the aim in one or two sentences, using the measurements as its evidence and going no further than they allow.

grade9-biology.question: Why does a report include an anomalous reading as well as the rest?
options: They improve the mean of the readings
They are needed to draw the graph line
They make the table look much longer
A reader must see all the evidence
grade9-biology.answer: A reader must see all the evidence
acceptableAnswers: A reader must see all the evidence
grade9-biology.hint: What would leaving it out do to the report?
grade9-biology.explanation: Every reading taken is shown and the odd one is identified and discussed; quietly deleting it hides evidence and makes the results look better than they are.

grade9-biology.question: A pupil presents a germination investigation to the class. Which is the most useful visual aid?
options: A page of writing read out to the class
A list of every pupil in the working group
A photograph of the pupil holding a dish
A bar chart of the seeds that germinated
grade9-biology.answer: A bar chart of the seeds that germinated
acceptableAnswers: A bar chart of the seeds that germinated
grade9-biology.hint: Which one shows the result at a glance?
grade9-biology.explanation: A chart of the results carries the finding itself, so the audience sees the pattern while the speaker explains what caused it.

grade9-biology.question: Why is the source of information taken from a website given in a report?
options: So the writing does not have to be neat
So the website gets more visitors to it
So the report is longer than the others
So the reader can check where it came from
grade9-biology.answer: So the reader can check where it came from
acceptableAnswers: So the reader can check where it came from
grade9-biology.hint: A reader must be able to judge the claim.
grade9-biology.explanation: Naming the source lets a reader find it, judge how reliable it is, and see which parts of the report are the pupil’s own work.

grade9-biology.question: A pupil writes "the plant seemed to like the light". How should this be written in a report?
options: The plant produced more bubbles in light
The plant was happier when it had light
The plant enjoyed the brightest lamp most
The plant preferred to be near the window
grade9-biology.answer: The plant produced more bubbles in light
acceptableAnswers: The plant produced more bubbles in light
grade9-biology.hint: A report states what was measured.
grade9-biology.explanation: A report records observations anyone could check; how a plant seemed to feel is not an observation and cannot be measured or repeated.

grade9-biology.question: What belongs in the apparatus list of a report?
options: Every item used, named and counted
The results taken with each item
The names of everyone in the group
Only the items that were expensive
grade9-biology.answer: Every item used, named and counted
acceptableAnswers: Every item used, named and counted
grade9-biology.hint: The list must let someone set the work up again.
grade9-biology.explanation: The list names each item and how many were used, so a reader can assemble exactly the same apparatus before reading the method.

grade9-biology.question: Why is a graph often clearer than a table in a report?
options: A graph takes up less space on paper
The pattern can be seen at a glance
A graph needs no labels on its axes
The numbers are more exact on a graph
grade9-biology.answer: The pattern can be seen at a glance
acceptableAnswers: The pattern can be seen at a glance
grade9-biology.hint: Think what a rising line shows that a column of numbers does not.
grade9-biology.explanation: A graph turns a column of numbers into a shape, so a trend, a levelling off or an anomaly is visible immediately.

grade9-biology.question: Two pupils write up the same pond weed investigation and reach different conclusions from the same table. What should a reader do first?
options: Accept the longer of the two reports
Ask the pupils to agree on one of them
Check both conclusions against the table
Accept the conclusion written most neatly
grade9-biology.answer: Check both conclusions against the table
acceptableAnswers: Check both conclusions against the table
grade9-biology.hint: The evidence is the same for both of them.
grade9-biology.explanation: The data decide between them, so each conclusion is read back against the table; presentation and agreement settle nothing.

grade9-biology.question: In an oral presentation of an investigation, what is given straight after the results?
options: The title of the whole report
grade9-biology.answer: The conclusion drawn from them
grade9-biology.hint: A presentation follows the same order as the report.
grade9-biology.explanation: Aim, method, results, conclusion is the order in both a report and a talk, so the conclusion follows immediately once the results are shown.

grade9-biology.question: A spreadsheet is used to draw the graph of a germination investigation. What must the pupil still check?
options: That the graph is printed in colour
That the font is large enough to read
That the file is saved as a picture
That the axes are labelled with units
grade9-biology.answer: That the axes are labelled with units
acceptableAnswers: That the axes are labelled with units
grade9-biology.hint: Software draws whatever it is given.
grade9-biology.explanation: A spreadsheet will plot any numbers at all, so the pupil remains responsible for axis labels, units and a scale that rises in equal steps.

grade9-biology.question: A report ends: "These results prove that all seeds need warmth to germinate." Why is that claim too strong?
options: The investigation used ten seeds a dish
Only one kind of seed was tested here
The results were written in a table
The conclusion is placed at the end
grade9-biology.answer: Only one kind of seed was tested here
acceptableAnswers: Only one kind of seed was tested here
grade9-biology.hint: What was actually investigated?
grade9-biology.explanation: One species was tested, so the conclusion may be stated for that seed only; a claim about all seeds would need far wider evidence.

grade9-biology.question: Give the term for the set-up in which the factor being tested is deliberately left out.
grade9-biology.answer: Control
grade9-biology.hint: It is the comparison the other set-ups are judged against.
grade9-biology.explanation: The control is an otherwise identical set-up without the factor under test, so any difference can be attributed to that factor.

grade9-biology.question: Give the term for a variable that is deliberately kept the same throughout an investigation.
grade9-biology.answer: Controlled variable
grade9-biology.hint: It is neither changed nor measured.
grade9-biology.explanation: A controlled variable is held constant so that it cannot affect the result and the outcome can be attributed to the independent variable.

grade9-biology.question: Name the chart used to display how many of each species were counted in a quadrat survey.
grade9-biology.answer: Bar chart
grade9-biology.hint: The species are separate groups, not a continuous scale.
grade9-biology.explanation: Separate categories are shown as a bar chart with gaps between the bars; a line graph is used for two continuously varying quantities.

grade9-biology.question: Give the term for the running record made by marking each animal as it is counted.
grade9-biology.answer: Tally
grade9-biology.hint: It is kept while the counting is still going on.
grade9-biology.explanation: A tally records each animal at the moment it is seen, so none is missed or counted twice during the count.

grade9-biology.question: State what is calculated by adding five pulse readings together and dividing by five.
grade9-biology.answer: The mean
grade9-biology.hint: It is a single value standing for the whole set.
grade9-biology.explanation: The mean is the total of the readings divided by how many there were, and it reduces the effect of any one stray value.

grade9-biology.question: Give the term for a link between two quantities that rise together, which by itself does not show that one causes the other.
grade9-biology.answer: Correlation
grade9-biology.hint: It describes a pattern, not a cause.
grade9-biology.explanation: A correlation means two quantities change together; establishing that one causes the other needs a controlled investigation.

grade9-biology.question: State what must be done to used agar plates before they are thrown away.
grade9-biology.answer: Sterilised
grade9-biology.hint: The colonies on them are still alive.
grade9-biology.explanation: Used plates are heated in an autoclave or pressure cooker to kill the cultures before they are disposed of.

grade9-biology.question: State the first thing a pupil should do after cutting a finger on a broken slide.
grade9-biology.answer: Tell the teacher
grade9-biology.hint: An injury comes before the practical work.
grade9-biology.explanation: The teacher is told at once so the wound is treated and the broken glass cleared away safely.

grade9-biology.question: Name the section of a report that states what the investigation set out to find.
grade9-biology.answer: Aim
grade9-biology.hint: It is written before any measurements are taken.
grade9-biology.explanation: The aim states the purpose of the investigation and is what the conclusion must answer.

grade9-biology.question: Name the section of a report in which the measurements taken are set out in a table.
grade9-biology.answer: Results
grade9-biology.hint: It comes after the method and before the conclusion.
grade9-biology.explanation: The results section holds the measurements, set out in a table with headed columns, before any interpretation is offered.

grade9-biology.question: State the tense in which the method of an investigation report is written.
grade9-biology.answer: Past tense
grade9-biology.hint: The work has already been carried out.
grade9-biology.explanation: The method reports work already done, so it is written in the past tense throughout.

grade9-biology.question: Which component of blood helps in blood clotting?
grade9-biology.answer: Platelets
grade9-biology.hint: It is the smallest of the cell fragments in blood.
grade9-biology.explanation: Platelets clump together at a wound and trigger the clotting process that seals it. Red cells carry oxygen, white cells fight infection and plasma is the liquid they all travel in.

grade9-biology.question: The diagram shows a section through an artery. What does X represent?
options: A thin layer of muscle and elastic fibres
A thick layer of muscle and elastic fibres
grade9-biology.answer: A small lumen
grade9-biology.hint: X points at the space in the middle, not at the wall. Compare how wide that space is with the thickness of the wall around it.
grade9-biology.explanation: The label points to the central channel, the lumen, and in an artery it is narrow compared with the very thick muscular wall. That thick wall and narrow lumen are what let an artery withstand high pressure; a vein has the reverse.

grade9-biology.question: Which one of the following reproduces asexually?
grade9-biology.answer: Amoeba
grade9-biology.hint: Asexual reproduction needs only one parent and no gametes.
grade9-biology.explanation: An amoeba is a single-celled organism that simply divides in two, so one parent produces two identical offspring. Cats, elephants and pigeons all reproduce sexually.

grade9-biology.question: Which of the following is a sexually transmitted disease?
grade9-biology.answer: Gonorrhoea
grade9-biology.hint: Which one is passed on through sexual contact?
grade9-biology.explanation: Gonorrhoea is a bacterial infection spread by sexual contact. Cholera comes from contaminated water, COVID-19 spreads through the air and a stroke is not an infection at all.

grade9-biology.question: Which of the following may lead to an increase in the spread of AIDS?
grade9-biology.answer: Sharing contaminated needles
grade9-biology.hint: HIV travels in body fluids. Which option moves blood from one person to another?
grade9-biology.explanation: A used needle carries blood, so sharing needles passes HIV directly from one person to another. Condoms reduce the spread, and diet and exercise do not transmit the virus either way.

grade9-biology.question: Which part of the female reproductive system produces eggs?
grade9-biology.answer: Ovary
grade9-biology.hint: Its name comes from the Latin for egg.
grade9-biology.explanation: The ovary produces and releases the egg cells. The oviduct carries the egg, the uterus is where a fertilised egg develops and the vagina is the entrance to the system.

grade9-biology.question: Which of the following can be estimated using a quadrat?
grade9-biology.answer: Algae
grade9-biology.hint: A quadrat is a fixed square frame laid on the ground. What kind of organism stays inside it long enough to be counted?
grade9-biology.explanation: A quadrat counts organisms that do not move away, so it suits plants and algae. Birds, dogs and fish move around, so they would be counted twice or missed entirely.

grade9-biology.question: Which green pigment, present in leaves, traps light energy?
grade9-biology.answer: Chlorophyll
grade9-biology.hint: It is what makes a leaf green.
grade9-biology.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy for photosynthesis and gives leaves their green colour. Haemoglobin is the red pigment in blood, and starch is the food that photosynthesis produces.

grade9-biology.question: The diagram shows the structure of a leaf. What do P and Q represent?
options: P network of veins, Q midrib
P leaf apex, Q network of veins
P leaf margin, Q network of veins
grade9-biology.answer: P leaf margin, Q midrib
grade9-biology.hint: One label points at the outer EDGE of the leaf, the other at the single thick line running down its centre.
grade9-biology.explanation: P points to the outer edge, the leaf margin. Q points to the single thick vein running from the stalk to the tip, the midrib. The finer branching lines would be the network of veins, and the tip would be the apex.

grade9-biology.question: Why should a leaf be heated in alcohol before testing it for starch?
options: To remove colour from the leaf
To remove oxygen from the leaf
To stop all chemical reactions in the leaf
grade9-biology.answer: To remove colour from the leaf
acceptableAnswers: To remove colour from the leaf
grade9-biology.hint: The starch test uses iodine, which turns blue-black. What would stop you seeing that colour change?
grade9-biology.explanation: Alcohol dissolves the green chlorophyll out of the leaf. Without that step the leaf stays green and the blue-black iodine colour cannot be seen. Boiling in water is what kills the leaf and stops reactions.

grade9-biology.question: What is a difference between sexual and asexual reproduction?
options: Sexual reproduction needs only one parent; asexual reproduction needs two
Only asexual reproduction produces offspring that vary
Only sexual reproduction produces identical offspring
Sexual reproduction needs two parents; asexual reproduction needs only one
grade9-biology.answer: Sexual reproduction needs two parents; asexual reproduction needs only one
acceptableAnswers: Sexual reproduction needs two parents; asexual reproduction needs only one
grade9-biology.hint: Count the parents, and think about whether the offspring are identical.
grade9-biology.explanation: Sexual reproduction joins gametes from two parents, so the offspring vary. Asexual reproduction uses one parent and produces offspring genetically identical to it.

grade9-biology.question: Which pair of plants reproduces asexually?
grade9-biology.answer: Potato and ginger
grade9-biology.hint: Which of these are grown by planting a piece of the parent plant rather than a seed?
grade9-biology.explanation: A potato tuber and a ginger rhizome each grow into a new plant identical to the parent, with no seed and no second parent. The others are all grown from seed, which is sexual reproduction.

grade9-biology.question: What is meant by biodiversity?
options: The variety of rocks and soils in an area
The number of plants grown on a farm
The variety of living organisms in an area
The total number of animals in an area
grade9-biology.answer: The variety of living organisms in an area
acceptableAnswers: The variety of living organisms in an area
grade9-biology.hint: The word joins "bio" (life) with "diversity" (variety).
grade9-biology.explanation: Biodiversity is the variety of living organisms in a habitat - the range of different species, not simply how many individuals there are.

grade9-biology.question: Which pair are natural calamities that affect biodiversity?
grade9-biology.answer: Cyclone and drought
grade9-biology.hint: Which two happen without any human action?
grade9-biology.explanation: A cyclone and a drought are natural events. Pollution and deforestation are caused by people, so they are human activities rather than natural calamities.

grade9-biology.question: Which is an ecological benefit of biodiversity?
options: It earns foreign currency from exports
It attracts tourists to the country
It keeps food chains and food webs stable
It provides jobs in the fishing industry
grade9-biology.answer: It keeps food chains and food webs stable
acceptableAnswers: It keeps food chains and food webs stable
grade9-biology.hint: Ecological means about the ecosystem itself, not about money or people.
grade9-biology.explanation: A varied community keeps food chains and webs stable, so losing one species does not collapse the system. Tourism, jobs and export earnings are socio-economic benefits.

grade9-biology.question: The diagram shows part of the circulatory system, with an artery on one side and a vein on the other. What does structure A represent?
grade9-biology.answer: Capillaries
grade9-biology.hint: A points to the fine network between the artery and the vein.
grade9-biology.explanation: The mesh of extremely fine vessels linking the artery to the vein is the capillary network. Their walls are one cell thick, which is what allows exchange with the surrounding tissue.

grade9-biology.question: What is the function of capillaries?
options: To carry blood away from the heart at high pressure
To return blood to the heart against gravity
To allow exchange of substances between blood and body cells
grade9-biology.answer: To allow exchange of substances between blood and body cells
acceptableAnswers: To allow exchange of substances between blood and body cells
grade9-biology.hint: Their walls are only one cell thick. What does that make possible?
grade9-biology.explanation: Capillary walls are one cell thick, so oxygen and nutrients pass out to the cells and waste passes in - the exchange the whole circulatory system exists to deliver. Carrying blood at pressure is the artery’s job, and valves stop backflow in veins.

grade9-biology.question: Which statement correctly describes a difference in the way arteries and veins carry blood?
options: Veins carry blood in spurts; arteries carry it steadily
Arteries carry blood towards the heart; veins carry blood away from it
Both carry blood at the same pressure
Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry blood towards it
grade9-biology.answer: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry blood towards it
acceptableAnswers: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry blood towards it
grade9-biology.hint: Think about direction first, then pressure.
grade9-biology.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, at high pressure and in surges; veins return it towards the heart at low pressure and steadily, which is why they need valves.

grade9-biology.question: What is the stretching and recoiling of the artery walls known as?
grade9-biology.answer: The pulse
grade9-biology.hint: You can feel it at the wrist.
grade9-biology.explanation: Each surge of blood from the heart stretches the artery wall, which then recoils. That wave is the pulse, and it can be felt wherever an artery runs close to the skin.

grade9-biology.question: Which pair are risk factors for coronary heart disease?
options: Smoking and a diet high in fat
Regular exercise and a balanced diet
grade9-biology.answer: Smoking and a diet high in fat
acceptableAnswers: Smoking and a diet high in fat
grade9-biology.hint: Which habits damage or narrow the arteries?
grade9-biology.explanation: Smoking damages artery walls and a high-fat diet builds fatty deposits that narrow the coronary arteries. The other options all reduce the risk.

grade9-biology.question: How do white blood cells protect the body from germs?
options: They engulf germs and produce antibodies
They carry oxygen to the germs
They dissolve germs with stomach acid
They clot the blood around germs
grade9-biology.answer: They engulf germs and produce antibodies
acceptableAnswers: They engulf germs and produce antibodies
grade9-biology.hint: There are two kinds of white blood cell, and they defend in two different ways.
grade9-biology.explanation: Some white blood cells engulf and digest germs; others make antibodies that stick to germs and destroy them. Carrying oxygen is the red cell’s job and clotting is the platelet’s.

grade9-biology.question: A drawing of a cell is printed at a magnification of × 8000. How is the actual size of the cell worked out?
options: Measure the drawing, then divide by 8000
Measure the drawing, then multiply by 8000
Divide 8000 by the size of the drawing
grade9-biology.answer: Measure the drawing, then divide by 8000
acceptableAnswers: Measure the drawing, then divide by 8000
grade9-biology.hint: The drawing is 8000 times bigger than the real cell. To undo that, do the opposite operation.
grade9-biology.explanation: Magnification = image size ÷ actual size, so actual size = image size ÷ magnification. Measure the drawing with a ruler and divide by 8000. Multiplying would make an already-enlarged picture larger still.

grade9-biology.question: What are the small pores in a leaf called?
grade9-biology.answer: Stomata
grade9-biology.hint: They are mostly on the underside of the leaf and can open and close.
grade9-biology.explanation: The pores are stomata (one is a stoma). Each is opened and closed by a pair of guard cells.

grade9-biology.question: What is the function of the stomata in a leaf?
options: To allow gases to enter and leave the leaf
To trap light energy for photosynthesis
To transport food to the roots
To absorb water from the soil
grade9-biology.answer: To allow gases to enter and leave the leaf
acceptableAnswers: To allow gases to enter and leave the leaf
grade9-biology.hint: Photosynthesis needs one gas in and gives another out.
grade9-biology.explanation: Stomata let carbon dioxide in and oxygen out (and water vapour escapes through them too). Light is trapped by chlorophyll, water is absorbed by roots and food is carried in the phloem.

grade9-biology.question: In an experiment on pond weed carried out in a dark room, bubbles were produced only when both light and a carbon dioxide source were present; with either one missing, no bubbles were produced.What conclusion can be drawn?
options: Both light and carbon dioxide are needed for photosynthesis
Carbon dioxide alone is enough for photosynthesis
Neither light nor carbon dioxide affects photosynthesis
Light alone is enough for photosynthesis
grade9-biology.answer: Both light and carbon dioxide are needed for photosynthesis
acceptableAnswers: Both light and carbon dioxide are needed for photosynthesis
grade9-biology.hint: Compare the test where both were present with the three where one or both were missing.
grade9-biology.explanation: Bubbles of oxygen appeared only when light AND carbon dioxide were both present, so both are required. Removing either one stopped photosynthesis, which is exactly what a controlled experiment is designed to show.

grade9-biology.question: In the pond-weed experiment, light and carbon dioxide were changed between tests. Which variable should be kept constant?
options: Whether a carbon dioxide source is added
Whether the lamp is switched on
grade9-biology.answer: The temperature of the water
grade9-biology.hint: A controlled variable is one you hold still. Two here are being changed on purpose, and one is what you measure.
grade9-biology.explanation: Temperature (and the type and amount of pond weed) must be held constant, or a change in bubbles could be caused by something other than light or carbon dioxide. Those two are the independent variables and the bubble count is the dependent one.

grade9-biology.question: What did Christiaan Barnard perform for the first time in 1967?
grade9-biology.answer: A human heart transplant
grade9-biology.hint: It involved replacing an organ.
grade9-biology.explanation: In December 1967 Christiaan Barnard carried out the first human-to-human heart transplant, in Cape Town.

grade9-biology.question: The first heart transplant patient lived for 18 days after the operation. What does that show?
options: A scientific first is not the same as a complete success
The patient was cured completely by the surgery
The operation had no value to medicine at all
Heart transplants can never work in practice
grade9-biology.answer: A scientific first is not the same as a complete success
acceptableAnswers: A scientific first is not the same as a complete success
grade9-biology.hint: Think about what came after that first attempt.
grade9-biology.explanation: The operation proved a transplant was possible; making patients survive long term took many more years of work.

grade9-biology.question: Why does the body sometimes reject a transplanted organ?
options: The body cannot produce enough new blood
The immune system treats it as foreign and attacks it
The organ has no blood supply of its own
The organ is always too large for the space
grade9-biology.answer: The immune system treats it as foreign and attacks it
acceptableAnswers: The immune system treats it as foreign and attacks it
grade9-biology.hint: It is the same system that fights infection.
grade9-biology.explanation: The immune system recognises the transplanted tissue as foreign and attacks it, which is why patients take drugs to suppress it.

grade9-biology.question: Which is an ethical question raised by organ transplantation?
options: Who should receive an organ when there are too few
Whether the heart is inside the chest cavity
How many hours the operation takes
grade9-biology.answer: Who should receive an organ when there are too few
acceptableAnswers: Who should receive an organ when there are too few
grade9-biology.hint: An ethical question is about what OUGHT to be done.
grade9-biology.explanation: Deciding fairly who receives a scarce organ is a question of values, not a question science alone can answer.

grade9-biology.question: A website claims a new product "cures every illness". How should this claim be treated?
options: As true, because it is written on a website
With caution, because no evidence is offered for it
As true, if the website looks professional
As true, because it is a very strong claim
grade9-biology.answer: With caution, because no evidence is offered for it
acceptableAnswers: With caution, because no evidence is offered for it
grade9-biology.hint: Ask what evidence supports the claim.
grade9-biology.explanation: A claim with no evidence behind it is not established, however confidently or professionally it is presented.

grade9-biology.question: Which question is most useful when judging a scientific claim?
options: How confidently the claim is stated
What evidence supports it, and who checked that evidence
Whether the website has attractive pictures on it
How many people have shared it online
grade9-biology.answer: What evidence supports it, and who checked that evidence
acceptableAnswers: What evidence supports it, and who checked that evidence
grade9-biology.hint: Science is judged on evidence, not on popularity.
grade9-biology.explanation: Evidence and independent checking are what make a claim trustworthy; popularity and presentation are not.

grade9-biology.question: Why should the source of a scientific claim be considered?
options: Only claims from other countries can be trusted
A longer article is always more reliable
A source that profits from the claim may be biased
The source never affects how reliable a claim is
grade9-biology.answer: A source that profits from the claim may be biased
acceptableAnswers: A source that profits from the claim may be biased
grade9-biology.hint: Ask who benefits if the claim is believed.
grade9-biology.explanation: Someone with something to gain has an interest in the conclusion, so their evidence needs independent checking.

grade9-biology.question: What makes a question an ethical question rather than a scientific one?
options: It asks what is true, not what ought to be done
It can always be settled by an experiment
It has no possible answer of any kind
It asks what ought to be done, not what is true
grade9-biology.answer: It asks what ought to be done, not what is true
acceptableAnswers: It asks what ought to be done, not what is true
grade9-biology.hint: Ethics is about right and wrong.
grade9-biology.explanation: Science establishes what is the case; ethics asks what we ought to do about it, which measurement alone cannot settle.

grade9-biology.question: Which of these is an ethical issue raised by a new medical technology?
options: Whether everyone will be able to afford it
How the medicine is stored in a fridge
grade9-biology.answer: Whether everyone will be able to afford it
acceptableAnswers: Whether everyone will be able to afford it
grade9-biology.hint: Three of these are technical questions.
grade9-biology.explanation: Fair access is a question of values; the other three are answered by measurement.

grade9-biology.question: A discovery can be used to help people or to harm them. What does this show about science?
options: A discovery can only ever be used one way
Discoveries should therefore never be made
Scientists alone should decide every use
How a discovery is used is a decision for society
grade9-biology.answer: How a discovery is used is a decision for society
acceptableAnswers: How a discovery is used is a decision for society
grade9-biology.hint: The knowledge and its use are two different things.
grade9-biology.explanation: Knowledge itself is neutral; deciding how it is applied is a choice society makes, and one scientists share in.

grade9-biology.question: Name the surgeon who performed the first human heart transplant in 1967.
grade9-biology.answer: Christiaan Barnard
grade9-biology.hint: He worked in Cape Town.
grade9-biology.explanation: Christiaan Barnard performed the first human-to-human heart transplant.

grade9-biology.question: In which city did Christiaan Barnard carry out the first human heart transplant?
grade9-biology.answer: Cape Town
grade9-biology.hint: It is a coastal city in South Africa.
grade9-biology.explanation: The operation was performed at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town in December 1967.

grade9-biology.question: Christiaan Barnard was a surgeon from which country?
grade9-biology.answer: South Africa
grade9-biology.hint: The hospital was Groote Schuur.
grade9-biology.explanation: Barnard was a South African surgeon, and the first transplant was carried out in his own country rather than in Europe or America.

grade9-biology.question: In which year was the first human-to-human heart transplant performed?
grade9-biology.hint: It was in the same decade as the first Moon landing.
grade9-biology.explanation: The operation took place in December 1967, two years before the first Moon landing.

grade9-biology.question: Who was the first patient to receive a transplanted human heart?
grade9-biology.answer: Louis Washkansky
grade9-biology.hint: He survived the operation by eighteen days.
grade9-biology.explanation: Louis Washkansky received the heart in December 1967; Philip Blaiberg was Barnard’s second patient and lived far longer.

grade9-biology.question: The heart used in the first transplant came from a young woman killed in a road accident. What is such a person called?
grade9-biology.answer: The donor
grade9-biology.hint: The organ is given, not taken.
grade9-biology.explanation: The person whose organ is given for transplant is the donor; the person who receives it is the recipient or patient.

grade9-biology.question: The first transplant patient died of pneumonia eighteen days after the operation. Why was he at risk of infection?
options: Drugs had weakened his immune system
He was not allowed to drink water
The new heart could not pump blood
The operation had taken many hours
grade9-biology.answer: Drugs had weakened his immune system
acceptableAnswers: Drugs had weakened his immune system
grade9-biology.hint: Something had to stop his body attacking the new heart.
grade9-biology.explanation: Drugs were given so his body would not reject the heart, but the same drugs lowered his defence against infection, and pneumonia killed him.

grade9-biology.question: Barnard’s second transplant patient lived for more than eighteen months. What did that show?
options: Rejection had been solved completely then
Heart transplants had become very common
The first patient had not been treated
The technique was improving with practice
grade9-biology.answer: The technique was improving with practice
acceptableAnswers: The technique was improving with practice
grade9-biology.hint: Compare eighteen days with eighteen months.
grade9-biology.explanation: Surviving eighteen months rather than eighteen days showed real progress, but rejection and infection remained serious problems for years afterwards.

grade9-biology.question: Which advance did most to turn heart transplants into a long-term success?
options: Faster ways of stitching a wound
grade9-biology.answer: Better drugs to prevent rejection
grade9-biology.hint: The surgery worked from the start; something else did not.
grade9-biology.explanation: Barnard showed the operation was possible in 1967; it became a lasting treatment only when drugs could hold rejection back without leaving patients defenceless.

grade9-biology.question: Why is a donor heart matched to the patient before a transplant?
options: To lower the cost of the operation
To make the operation take less time
To reduce the chance of rejection
To keep the heart beating in transport
grade9-biology.answer: To reduce the chance of rejection
acceptableAnswers: To reduce the chance of rejection
grade9-biology.hint: The closer the match, the less the immune system objects.
grade9-biology.explanation: A closely matched heart looks less foreign to the immune system, so it is less likely to be attacked and less immunosuppressive drug is needed.

grade9-biology.question: Transplants depend on people agreeing in advance to donate their organs. Why does that make it a question for society?
options: It depends on how fast surgeons can work
It depends on what people choose to allow
It depends on the size of the hospital
It depends on the cost of the equipment
grade9-biology.answer: It depends on what people choose to allow
acceptableAnswers: It depends on what people choose to allow
grade9-biology.hint: Surgery is possible; the organs still have to be offered.
grade9-biology.explanation: The operation is a technical matter, but whether organs are available at all rests on what people and their families are willing to agree to.

grade9-biology.question: What is meant by saying that a body has rejected a transplanted organ?
options: The surgeon removes the organ once more
The patient refuses to accept the organ
The organ is the wrong size for the space
The immune system attacks the new organ
grade9-biology.answer: The immune system attacks the new organ
acceptableAnswers: The immune system attacks the new organ
grade9-biology.hint: It is the same system that fights infection.
grade9-biology.explanation: The immune system recognises the transplanted tissue as foreign and attacks it, which is why patients take drugs to hold that response back.

grade9-biology.question: Which statement about the first heart transplant is a fact rather than an opinion?
options: The operation was the finest ever done
The patient lived for eighteen days
The patient should not have agreed to it
The surgeon deserved far more praise
grade9-biology.answer: The patient lived for eighteen days
acceptableAnswers: The patient lived for eighteen days
grade9-biology.hint: A fact can be checked; an opinion cannot.
grade9-biology.explanation: The eighteen days is a recorded, checkable fact; the other three are judgements that different people could reasonably disagree about.

grade9-biology.question: A magazine writes that Barnard "cured heart disease in 1967". Why is that wrong?
options: Heart disease was unknown in South Africa
One operation on one patient cures nothing
Barnard worked on lungs and not on hearts
The operation was carried out much later
grade9-biology.answer: One operation on one patient cures nothing
acceptableAnswers: One operation on one patient cures nothing
grade9-biology.hint: What happened to the patient after eighteen days?
grade9-biology.explanation: A single operation on a single patient who died within three weeks was a first, not a cure; heart disease remains a leading cause of death today.

grade9-biology.question: Two websites give different numbers for how many plant species are found only in Mauritius. What should a pupil do?
options: Look for the source of each number
Choose the larger of the two numbers
Add the two numbers together to check
Choose the website with more pictures
grade9-biology.answer: Look for the source of each number
acceptableAnswers: Look for the source of each number
grade9-biology.hint: Ask where each figure came from.
grade9-biology.explanation: A number is only as good as its source, so the survey or study behind each figure is what decides which one to use.

grade9-biology.question: Which source of information about a new medicine is likely to be most reliable?
options: A study checked by other scientists
An advertisement made by the maker of it
A comment posted underneath a video
A message forwarded on by a friend
grade9-biology.answer: A study checked by other scientists
acceptableAnswers: A study checked by other scientists
grade9-biology.hint: Who has looked at the evidence besides the person making the claim?
grade9-biology.explanation: A study reviewed by independent scientists has been checked by people with no interest in the result; the other three carry no such check.

grade9-biology.question: Why is a result that several separate groups have obtained more trustworthy?
options: A longer claim is always a stronger claim
A repeated result is less likely to be chance
More groups means the work costs more money
The first group is usually the least careful
grade9-biology.answer: A repeated result is less likely to be chance
acceptableAnswers: A repeated result is less likely to be chance
grade9-biology.hint: Think what one unlucky sample could produce.
grade9-biology.explanation: One group can be unlucky, mistaken or biased; the same result found independently several times is far harder to explain away as chance.

grade9-biology.question: A website selling a herbal remedy says it "cures asthma". What should be looked for before believing it?
options: The price the remedy is being sold for
Evidence from a properly controlled trial
How many pictures the website contains
The number of people who have shared it
grade9-biology.answer: Evidence from a properly controlled trial
acceptableAnswers: Evidence from a properly controlled trial
grade9-biology.hint: What would show the remedy, and not something else, did the work?
grade9-biology.explanation: Only a controlled trial, in which a treated group is compared with a control group, can show that the remedy itself produced the improvement.

grade9-biology.question: Why should the date on a scientific web page be checked?
options: Newer evidence may have replaced it
A page without a date cannot be found
Older pages are harder to read online
A dated page is written by a scientist
grade9-biology.answer: Newer evidence may have replaced it
acceptableAnswers: Newer evidence may have replaced it
grade9-biology.hint: Scientific understanding changes as evidence builds.
grade9-biology.explanation: Advice on treatment, conservation or disease is revised as new evidence arrives, so an undated or very old page may be giving superseded information.

grade9-biology.question: A newspaper reports that "scientists say chocolate prevents heart disease". What is missing?
options: Which shops are selling the chocolate
How much the chocolate costs to buy
How much chocolate a bar contains
grade9-biology.answer: Which scientists, and what evidence
grade9-biology.hint: The headline names nobody and cites nothing.
grade9-biology.explanation: Without the study, its size and who carried it out, there is nothing to judge; "scientists say" is not itself evidence for anything.

grade9-biology.question: A pupil researching biodiversity finds a useful page written by a charity that is asking for donations. How should the page be used?
options: Copied straight into the report as it is
Used, but checked against another source
Accepted because the cause is a good one
Ignored because it is asking for money
grade9-biology.answer: Used, but checked against another source
acceptableAnswers: Used, but checked against another source
grade9-biology.hint: Having an interest in the answer is not the same as being wrong.
grade9-biology.explanation: An organisation with a cause may present evidence selectively without being dishonest, so its figures are used but confirmed elsewhere.

grade9-biology.question: What does it mean to say that a source is biased?
options: It was written a very long time ago
It favours one conclusion over others
It is written in more than one language
It contains a number of spelling errors
grade9-biology.answer: It favours one conclusion over others
acceptableAnswers: It favours one conclusion over others
grade9-biology.hint: Ask who gains if the reader is convinced.
grade9-biology.explanation: A biased source leans towards one conclusion, often because the writer has something to gain from it, so its evidence needs independent checking.

grade9-biology.question: Which question best tests whether a health claim is scientific?
options: How many people believe it is true
What evidence was collected, and how
How famous the person saying it is
How often it appears on the internet
grade9-biology.answer: What evidence was collected, and how
acceptableAnswers: What evidence was collected, and how
grade9-biology.hint: Science is judged on evidence, not on popularity.
grade9-biology.explanation: How the evidence was gathered decides whether a claim stands; fame, popularity and repetition change nothing about whether it is true.

grade9-biology.question: A forwarded phone message claims that a fruit "kills all viruses". Why should it be treated with caution?
options: No evidence travels with the message
The message was sent by a classmate
Forwarded messages are hard to read
The fruit does not grow in Mauritius
grade9-biology.answer: No evidence travels with the message
acceptableAnswers: No evidence travels with the message
grade9-biology.hint: What arrived with the claim?
grade9-biology.explanation: A forwarded message carries the claim but not the study behind it, so there is nothing to check and no way to judge whether it is true.

grade9-biology.question: Why is a result from a sample of 1000 people usually more reliable than one from 10?
options: A larger sample is less affected by chance
A larger sample is always cheaper to test
A smaller sample takes far longer to test
A smaller sample is harder to write down
grade9-biology.answer: A larger sample is less affected by chance
acceptableAnswers: A larger sample is less affected by chance
grade9-biology.hint: Think how much one unusual person changes each result.
grade9-biology.explanation: One unusual person changes a group of ten far more than a group of a thousand, so the larger sample gives a result closer to the true value.

grade9-biology.question: Two graphs show the same HIV figures, but one has a stretched vertical scale so the rise looks much steeper. What does this show?
options: One of the two graphs must be false
HIV data cannot be shown on a graph
How a graph is drawn can mislead
The steeper graph is the correct one
grade9-biology.answer: How a graph is drawn can mislead
acceptableAnswers: How a graph is drawn can mislead
grade9-biology.hint: The numbers are identical in both.
grade9-biology.explanation: The same data can be made to look dramatic or gentle by the choice of scale, which is why an axis and its scale are read before the shape of the line.

grade9-biology.question: What is the best reason for reading more than one source on a topic?
options: One source may leave something out
More sources fill more pages of notes
The longest source is the best of them
Sources always agree with each other
grade9-biology.answer: One source may leave something out
acceptableAnswers: One source may leave something out
grade9-biology.hint: What would you never notice from a single page?
grade9-biology.explanation: A second source may add evidence the first omitted or disagree with it, and either way the reader learns something a single page could not show.

grade9-biology.question: Who checks a scientific paper before a journal publishes it?
options: The company that made the product
Other scientists in the same field
The readers who buy the journal
grade9-biology.answer: Other scientists in the same field
acceptableAnswers: Other scientists in the same field
grade9-biology.hint: The checkers must understand the work.
grade9-biology.explanation: Papers are reviewed by independent scientists working on the same subject, who judge the methods and the evidence before publication is allowed.

grade9-biology.question: A claim on a website has no author, no date and no references. How should it be treated?
options: As true because it is written down
As unsupported until it is checked
As proved because a website printed it
As false because there is no author
grade9-biology.answer: As unsupported until it is checked
acceptableAnswers: As unsupported until it is checked
grade9-biology.hint: An unchecked claim is not the same as a false one.
grade9-biology.explanation: With no author, date or references there is nothing to check, so the claim is set aside as unsupported rather than accepted or declared false.

grade9-biology.question: Which of these is an ethical question about dissecting animals in school?
options: Where the specimen jars are stored
How the specimen should be preserved
Which instruments cut the tissue best
Whether animals should be used at all
grade9-biology.answer: Whether animals should be used at all
acceptableAnswers: Whether animals should be used at all
grade9-biology.hint: Three of these can be settled by trying them out.
grade9-biology.explanation: Whether it is right to use an animal is a question of values; the other three are practical questions answered by observation.

grade9-biology.question: An unborn baby can now be tested for certain diseases. Which is the ethical question this raises?
options: What parents should be told, and when
How the sample is stored in the lab
Which machine takes the sample best
How long the test takes to complete
grade9-biology.answer: What parents should be told, and when
acceptableAnswers: What parents should be told, and when
grade9-biology.hint: Which of these has no measurement that could answer it?
grade9-biology.explanation: What families should be told, and what they may then decide, is a matter of values; the sampling, the timing and the storage are technical questions.

grade9-biology.question: Why must consent be obtained before a person takes part in a medical trial?
options: The trial can then be finished more quickly
They have a right to decide for themselves
The medicine then costs less to produce
The results are then easier to write up
grade9-biology.answer: They have a right to decide for themselves
acceptableAnswers: They have a right to decide for themselves
grade9-biology.hint: Whose body is being used?
grade9-biology.explanation: A person must understand the risks and agree freely before taking part; consent protects the volunteer, not the convenience of the trial.

grade9-biology.question: The result of a person’s HIV test is kept confidential. Why is that an ethical duty?
options: The doctor may not remember it correctly
Private medical information belongs to them
The result could change if tested again later
The laboratory has too many results to file
grade9-biology.answer: Private medical information belongs to them
acceptableAnswers: Private medical information belongs to them
grade9-biology.hint: Think about the harm that follows if it is shared.
grade9-biology.explanation: A person’s medical information is theirs to share or withhold, and disclosure can cost them work, housing and relationships, so confidentiality is a duty.

grade9-biology.question: Endangered species are protected by law in Mauritius. Which is an ethical argument for protecting them?
options: They are found on more than one island
They can be counted easily using a quadrat
They were discovered a long time ago
Other living things have a right to exist
grade9-biology.answer: Other living things have a right to exist
acceptableAnswers: Other living things have a right to exist
grade9-biology.hint: One of these is a claim about what ought to be.
grade9-biology.explanation: Saying that other species have a right to exist is a claim about values; where they live and how they are counted are matters of fact.

grade9-biology.question: Which of these questions can science answer, rather than ethics?
grade9-biology.answer: How quickly the virus spreads
grade9-biology.hint: Which one could be settled by measurement?
grade9-biology.explanation: The rate of spread is measured from case data; who should be treated first, and what is fair or right, are judgements measurement cannot make.

grade9-biology.question: A new medicine is costly and there is not enough for everyone. What kind of question is "who should receive it"?
grade9-biology.answer: An ethical question
grade9-biology.hint: It asks what ought to happen.
grade9-biology.explanation: Deciding fairly who receives a scarce treatment is a question about what ought to be done, which no experiment can settle.

grade9-biology.question: Why might a scientist refuse to work on a project even though it could be done?
options: They prefer to work on their own ideas
They cannot measure the results of it
They judge the use of it to be wrong
They have run out of laboratory space
grade9-biology.answer: They judge the use of it to be wrong
acceptableAnswers: They judge the use of it to be wrong
grade9-biology.hint: Being able to do something is not a reason to do it.
grade9-biology.explanation: A scientist may decide the likely use of the work is harmful; that is an ethical judgement, separate from whether the work is technically possible.

grade9-biology.question: Genetically modified crops can raise the yield of a harvest. Which is an ethical concern about them?
options: Which fertiliser the crop needs most
Who controls the seed that farmers buy
How the seed is stored before sowing
How quickly the crop grows in a field
grade9-biology.answer: Who controls the seed that farmers buy
acceptableAnswers: Who controls the seed that farmers buy
grade9-biology.hint: Three of these could be answered by a field trial.
grade9-biology.explanation: Who owns and controls the seed decides who benefits from the technology, which is a question about fairness rather than about the crop itself.
