grade9-chemistry.hint: Some reactions cannot be done in a school laboratory.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A simulation lets a hazardous or expensive reaction be explored safely, although it models the reaction rather than measuring it.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which chart best shows the percentage of each gas in clean dry air?
grade9-chemistry.answer: A pie chart
grade9-chemistry.hint: The parts add up to one whole.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A pie chart shows how a whole is divided. A line graph is for a quantity that changes continuously.

grade9-chemistry.question: A graph is copied from a website into a report. What must go with it?
options: A note saying the graph was easy to find
The number of times it was viewed
A drawing of the person who made it
The address of the page it came from
grade9-chemistry.answer: The address of the page it came from
acceptableAnswers: The address of the page it came from
grade9-chemistry.hint: A reader may want to see it where it came from.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The source lets a reader find the original, check that it says what you claim, and see how the data were collected.

grade9-chemistry.question: Two websites give different values for the pH of rainwater. What is the best next step?
options: Use the value from the page that loaded fastest
Look for a third, independent source and compare
Write both down and let the reader pick one
Take the value that appears on the prettier page
grade9-chemistry.answer: Look for a third, independent source and compare
acceptableAnswers: Look for a third, independent source and compare
grade9-chemistry.hint: Agreement between independent sources is the test.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A third independent source shows which value is supported. Loading speed and appearance say nothing at all about accuracy.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why are the raw data files from an investigation saved as well as the graph?
options: A saved file makes the graph print more clearly
Saved files take up much less space than graphs
The graph can be redrawn if a mistake is found
The graph cannot be shown without the raw file
grade9-chemistry.answer: The graph can be redrawn if a mistake is found
acceptableAnswers: The graph can be redrawn if a mistake is found
grade9-chemistry.hint: What if the axes turned out to be the wrong way round?
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Keeping the raw data means the analysis can be repeated or corrected. A graph on its own cannot be reworked.

grade9-chemistry.question: What is one advantage of a digital balance over a beam balance?
options: It works without any electricity being supplied
It never needs to be set to zero before use
It measures volume as well as mass in one go
The reading is a number, so nobody misreads it
grade9-chemistry.answer: The reading is a number, so nobody misreads it
acceptableAnswers: The reading is a number, so nobody misreads it
grade9-chemistry.hint: Think about two people reading the same instrument.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A digital display removes the judgement needed to read a scale, so two people record the same value.

grade9-chemistry.question: A class wants to share its results with a school in another country. Which ICT tool suits this best?
options: A shared online document and a video call
A poster pinned on the laboratory wall
A photograph kept on one pupil’s phone
A note written in the practical notebook
grade9-chemistry.answer: A shared online document and a video call
acceptableAnswers: A shared online document and a video call
grade9-chemistry.hint: The other school is not in the room.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A shared document and a call let both schools see and discuss the same results. The other three stay where they are.

grade9-chemistry.question: What is a hypothesis?
options: A statement that can be tested by experiment
A measurement taken during an experiment
A summary written after an experiment ends
The list of apparatus used in an experiment
grade9-chemistry.answer: A statement that can be tested by experiment
acceptableAnswers: A statement that can be tested by experiment
grade9-chemistry.hint: It comes before the work, not after it.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A hypothesis is a testable statement made before the experiment. The results then either support it or they do not.

grade9-chemistry.question:
A pupil tests the idea that magnesium reacts faster with acid at a higher temperature. The same volume of acid, of the same concentration, is warmed to five different temperatures and the time for the ribbon to disappear is measured each time.
What is the independent variable?
grade9-chemistry.answer: The temperature of the acid
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is the one deliberately changed.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The independent variable is the one the pupil chooses and changes, which here is the temperature of the acid.

grade9-chemistry.question:
A pupil tests the idea that magnesium reacts faster with acid at a higher temperature. The same volume of acid, of the same concentration, is warmed to five different temperatures and the time for the ribbon to disappear is measured each time.
What is the dependent variable?
grade9-chemistry.answer: The time taken to disappear
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is the one measured at the end.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The dependent variable is what is measured to show the effect, which here is the time for the ribbon to disappear.

grade9-chemistry.question:
A pupil tests the idea that magnesium reacts faster with acid at a higher temperature. The same volume of acid, of the same concentration, is warmed to five different temperatures and the time for the ribbon to disappear is measured each time.
Which of these must be kept the same each time?
grade9-chemistry.answer: The concentration of the acid
grade9-chemistry.hint: Anything else that could change the time.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Controlled variables are held constant so that only temperature can explain the change. A different concentration would alter the time as well.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why is only one variable changed at a time?
options: So the change in the result has one cause
So the results do not have to be repeated
So fewer pieces of apparatus have to be used
So the experiment can be finished more quickly
grade9-chemistry.answer: So the change in the result has one cause
acceptableAnswers: So the change in the result has one cause
grade9-chemistry.hint: Two changes at once give two possible reasons.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: If two variables change together you cannot say which one caused the difference, so the test is not fair.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which of these is a testable hypothesis?
options: Chemistry is harder than any other subject
Powdered marble looks nicer than lumps do
Marble is the most interesting rock there is
Powdered marble reacts faster than lumps
grade9-chemistry.answer: Powdered marble reacts faster than lumps
acceptableAnswers: Powdered marble reacts faster than lumps
grade9-chemistry.hint: Which one could you actually measure?
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A testable hypothesis predicts something that can be measured. Interest, difficulty and appearance are opinions, not measurements.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why is “copper is the most beautiful metal” not a scientific hypothesis?
options: Copper is not a metal that can be tested
Beauty cannot be measured in an experiment
A hypothesis may never mention a colour
Only three metals may be named at one time
grade9-chemistry.answer: Beauty cannot be measured in an experiment
acceptableAnswers: Beauty cannot be measured in an experiment
grade9-chemistry.hint: Ask what instrument would test it.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A hypothesis must be testable. There is no measurement that could decide which metal is the most beautiful.

grade9-chemistry.question: Iron nails are used to test whether rusting needs both air and water. Which tube is the control?
options: A nail in ordinary water open to the air
A nail in dry air over a drying agent
A nail in boiled water sealed under oil
A nail in oil with no water present
grade9-chemistry.answer: A nail in ordinary water open to the air
acceptableAnswers: A nail in ordinary water open to the air
grade9-chemistry.hint: The control is the one in which rusting is expected.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The control has both air and water present, so it shows what happens when nothing is removed and gives the other tubes something to be compared with.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why is an experiment repeated three times?
options: To make sure the apparatus does not get cold
To use up all the chemicals that were prepared
To check that the readings agree with each other
To give every member of the group a turn at it
grade9-chemistry.answer: To check that the readings agree with each other
acceptableAnswers: To check that the readings agree with each other
grade9-chemistry.hint: A single reading could be a mistake.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Repeats show whether a value is reliable. With one reading only, an error would never be revealed.

grade9-chemistry.question: Powdered marble and marble lumps of the same mass are added to the same acid. What is the prediction?
options: The powder reacts faster than the lumps
Both react at exactly the same speed here
The lumps give off much more gas in total
The lumps stop reacting before the powder
grade9-chemistry.answer: The powder reacts faster than the lumps
acceptableAnswers: The powder reacts faster than the lumps
grade9-chemistry.hint: Which one has more surface touching the acid?
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Powder has a far greater surface area, so more particles are exposed and the reaction is faster. The total gas is the same, because the mass of marble is the same.

grade9-chemistry.question: Manganese(IV) oxide is added to hydrogen peroxide to test whether it is a catalyst. What must be kept the same in both tests?
options: The volume of gas that is given off in total
The time taken for the bubbling to stop
The volume and concentration of the peroxide
The number of bubbles counted in a minute
grade9-chemistry.answer: The volume and concentration of the peroxide
acceptableAnswers: The volume and concentration of the peroxide
grade9-chemistry.hint: A controlled variable is never one you measure.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Only the catalyst should differ, so the peroxide must be identical in both tubes. The gas and the time are the measurements, so they cannot be controlled.

grade9-chemistry.question: A pupil wants to find which of three antacid tablets neutralises the most acid. What must be the same for each tablet?
options: The concentration of the acid used each time
The mass of each tablet after the reaction
The time each tablet takes to dissolve fully
The volume of acid that each tablet neutralises
grade9-chemistry.answer: The concentration of the acid used each time
acceptableAnswers: The concentration of the acid used each time
grade9-chemistry.hint: One of these is the thing you are measuring.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The acid must be identical so that only the tablets differ. The volume neutralised is the measurement, so it cannot be fixed in advance.

grade9-chemistry.question: How should a pupil test whether concentration affects the rate of a reaction?
options: Change the volume of acid for each attempt
Change the metal used for each concentration
Change the concentration and the temperature
Change only the concentration of the acid
grade9-chemistry.answer: Change only the concentration of the acid
acceptableAnswers: Change only the concentration of the acid
grade9-chemistry.hint: One variable at a time.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Only the concentration may change. Altering anything else means a difference in rate could have had another cause.

grade9-chemistry.question: The results do not support the hypothesis. What should the pupil do?
options: Leave the conclusion out of the report
Change the results until they agree with it
Write the hypothesis again after the results
Report that and say what the results show
grade9-chemistry.answer: Report that and say what the results show
acceptableAnswers: Report that and say what the results show
grade9-chemistry.hint: A hypothesis that fails is still a result.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A hypothesis that is not supported is reported honestly. Learning that an idea is wrong is a genuine scientific finding.

grade9-chemistry.question: A good hypothesis is based on:
options: What is already known about the topic
What takes the least time to carry out
What the rest of the class has decided
What the pupil hopes will be the result
grade9-chemistry.answer: What is already known about the topic
acceptableAnswers: What is already known about the topic
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is a reasoned prediction, not a wish.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A hypothesis grows out of what is already known, such as the fact that particles move faster when hotter, and is then tested.

grade9-chemistry.question: Potassium nitrate is dissolved in water at 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60 °C to find how much dissolves. What is the dependent variable?
options: The temperature of the water used
The mass that dissolves in the water
The volume of water in each beaker
The type of salt that is being used
grade9-chemistry.answer: The mass that dissolves in the water
acceptableAnswers: The mass that dissolves in the water
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is what is measured at each temperature.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Temperature is chosen and changed, so it is the independent variable. The mass that dissolves is measured and depends on it.

grade9-chemistry.question: Where is the unit written in a results table?
options: In the title of the table
grade9-chemistry.answer: In the column heading
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is written once, not fifty times.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The unit goes in the column heading, such as “Time / s”, so that each cell below holds a number only.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which quantity is written in the first column of a results table?
grade9-chemistry.answer: The independent variable
grade9-chemistry.hint: The one whose values you chose.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The independent variable heads the first column, listed in order, with the measured values beside it.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which axis of a graph carries the independent variable?
grade9-chemistry.answer: The horizontal axis
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is usually called the x-axis.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The independent variable goes on the horizontal axis and the dependent variable on the vertical axis.

grade9-chemistry.question: A burette is read to the nearest:
grade9-chemistry.answer: 0.05 cm³
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is graduated in divisions of 0.1.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A burette is graduated in 0.1 cm³ and is read to the nearest half division, which is 0.05 cm³.

grade9-chemistry.question: The volume of gas collected is measured every 30 seconds. Which graph should be drawn?
grade9-chemistry.answer: A line graph
grade9-chemistry.hint: Both quantities change continuously.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Two continuous quantities are plotted as a line graph, so that the shape of the change can be seen.

grade9-chemistry.question: Four different antacids are compared. Which chart should be drawn?
grade9-chemistry.answer: A bar chart
grade9-chemistry.hint: The four antacids are separate items.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A bar chart compares separate categories. A line graph would imply values between the bars, which is meaningless here.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why are all the masses in a table recorded to the same number of decimal places?
options: It stops the balance from drifting off zero
It shows the balance was read the same way
It makes the numbers add up more easily
It saves the time needed to write them out
grade9-chemistry.answer: It shows the balance was read the same way
acceptableAnswers: It shows the balance was read the same way
grade9-chemistry.hint: Decimal places show how precise the instrument is.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Recording 2.40 g rather than 2.4 g states the precision of the balance, and a consistent table shows every reading was taken in the same way.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why is the mass of the empty crucible recorded as well as the final mass?
options: The crucible loses mass while it is heated
The balance needs a second reading to work
The crucible must be weighed before heating
The mass of the solid is the difference
grade9-chemistry.answer: The mass of the solid is the difference
acceptableAnswers: The mass of the solid is the difference
grade9-chemistry.hint: You cannot weigh the solid on its own.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The solid cannot be weighed by itself once it is in the crucible, so the empty mass is subtracted from the total.

grade9-chemistry.question: What must be written along each axis of a graph?
grade9-chemistry.answer: The quantity and its unit
grade9-chemistry.hint: A number on an axis has to say what it is.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Each axis is labelled with the quantity and its unit, such as “Volume of gas / cm³”, or the graph cannot be read.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why is a scale chosen that fills most of the grid?
options: The axes do not have to be labelled at all
A full grid uses less paper than a small one
The line will then always be perfectly straight
The points are spread out and easier to read
grade9-chemistry.answer: The points are spread out and easier to read
acceptableAnswers: The points are spread out and easier to read
grade9-chemistry.hint: Think about points crowded into one corner.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A scale that fills the grid spreads the points out, so the trend is clear and a value can be read off accurately.

grade9-chemistry.question: A pupil tests four gases with a lighted splint and a glowing splint. How should the results be recorded?
options: As a pie chart of the gases
As a line graph of the tests
In a single sentence of prose
grade9-chemistry.answer: In a table of observations
grade9-chemistry.hint: The results are descriptions, not numbers.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Qualitative results are set out as a table of observations. A graph needs numbers, and there are none here.

grade9-chemistry.question: A reading is clearly out of step with the rest. How is it entered in the table?
options: Written in with a different unit
Left out so the pattern stays clear
Written in and marked as anomalous
grade9-chemistry.answer: Written in and marked as anomalous
acceptableAnswers: Written in and marked as anomalous
grade9-chemistry.hint: Nothing is ever rubbed out of a results table.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Every reading is recorded. An anomalous one is marked, so that a reader can see it was noticed and left out of the mean.

grade9-chemistry.question: A flask of acid and marble chips stands on a balance and loses mass as gas escapes. Which table headings suit the results?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Time / s and Mass / g
grade9-chemistry.hint: Each heading names the quantity and its own unit.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Time is measured in seconds and mass in grams, so the headings are “Time / s” and “Mass / g”. A unit must match the quantity it belongs to.

grade9-chemistry.question: A titration gives one rough titre and then three accurate ones. What should the table record?
options: Only the smallest titre that was measured
Every titre, with the rough one marked
Only the mean of all four of the titres
Only the three that agree with each other
grade9-chemistry.answer: Every titre, with the rough one marked
acceptableAnswers: Every titre, with the rough one marked
grade9-chemistry.hint: The rough titre is still a reading you took.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: All readings are recorded. The rough titre is identified so that a reader can see why it was left out of the mean.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why are readings written down as soon as they are taken?
options: The paper would otherwise be left blank
A reading loses its unit after a minute
A remembered number is easily changed
The balance forgets its last reading
grade9-chemistry.answer: A remembered number is easily changed
acceptableAnswers: A remembered number is easily changed
grade9-chemistry.hint: Memory is not a measuring instrument.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Writing a reading down at once means the value recorded is the one that was actually read, not a number recalled later.

grade9-chemistry.question: The graph shows the volume of gas given off as marble chips react with acid. When is the reaction fastest?
options: At the start, where the line is steepest
It goes at the same speed throughout
At the end, where the line is level
In the middle, halfway through the reaction
grade9-chemistry.answer: At the start, where the line is steepest
acceptableAnswers: At the start, where the line is steepest
grade9-chemistry.hint: Steeper means more gas in the same time.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The steepest part of the curve is where gas is produced fastest, and that is at the start when the acid is most concentrated.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why does the line on a gas-volume graph become horizontal at the end?
options: The acid has become much more concentrated
One of the reactants has been used up
The marble chips have grown larger in size
The gas has escaped through the delivery tube
grade9-chemistry.answer: One of the reactants has been used up
acceptableAnswers: One of the reactants has been used up
grade9-chemistry.hint: No more gas is being made.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A horizontal line means the volume is no longer rising, so the reaction has stopped because one of the reactants has run out.

grade9-chemistry.question: Two curves are drawn for powdered marble and marble lumps of equal mass. What do they show?
options: The lumps reacted faster and gave much more gas
Both reacted at the same speed but gave less gas
The powder gave far more gas than the lumps did
The powder reacted faster but gave the same gas
grade9-chemistry.answer: The powder reacted faster but gave the same gas
acceptableAnswers: The powder reacted faster but gave the same gas
grade9-chemistry.hint: Compare the steepness, then compare the final height.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The steeper curve reacts faster, because powder has more surface area. Both level off at the same volume, because the mass of marble is the same.

grade9-chemistry.question: One point on a graph lies well off the line. What should be done?
options: Draw the line through the other points
Join every point with short straight lines
Draw the line so it passes through it too
Rub the point out before drawing the line
grade9-chemistry.answer: Draw the line through the other points
acceptableAnswers: Draw the line through the other points
grade9-chemistry.hint: The other points share a pattern.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A best-fit line follows the trend of the reliable points. The anomalous point is left on the graph and identified, not erased.

grade9-chemistry.question: A table shows that magnesium fizzes strongly in acid, zinc fizzes slowly and copper does not react. Which conclusion does it support?
options: All three metals react with acid at some speed
Magnesium is the most reactive of the three
Copper is the most useful metal of the three
Zinc would react faster than magnesium in air
grade9-chemistry.answer: Magnesium is the most reactive of the three
acceptableAnswers: Magnesium is the most reactive of the three
grade9-chemistry.hint: Only say what the observations show.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The strongest fizzing means the fastest reaction with acid, so magnesium is the most reactive. Nothing here measured usefulness or behaviour in air.

grade9-chemistry.question: Sales of sunglasses and the mass of carbon dioxide released both rose over ten years. What does this show?
options: The two rose together, which does not prove a link
The two have no connection with each other at all
Carbon dioxide in the air makes people buy sunglasses
Buying sunglasses causes carbon dioxide to be made
grade9-chemistry.answer: The two rose together, which does not prove a link
acceptableAnswers: The two rose together, which does not prove a link
grade9-chemistry.hint: Two things rising together is not the same as one causing the other.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A correlation shows two quantities changing together. Establishing a cause needs a mechanism and further evidence, and there is none here.

grade9-chemistry.question: Titres of 25.10, 25.20 and 27.60 cm³ are obtained. Which should be used for the mean?
options: The first two, because they agree closely
The last one, because it is the largest of them
The middle one, because it lies between them
All three, because each one was measured
grade9-chemistry.answer: The first two, because they agree closely
acceptableAnswers: The first two, because they agree closely
grade9-chemistry.hint: Concordant titres agree within about 0.10 cm³.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Only concordant titres are averaged. 27.60 cm³ is far from the others, so it is recorded as anomalous and left out of the mean.

grade9-chemistry.question: Gas is collected over water, but the bung is fitted a moment after the acid is added. What is the effect?
options: The gas dissolves and the volume stays the same
Some water enters, so the volume is far too big
Some gas escapes, so the volume is too small
The reaction stops before the gas is collected
grade9-chemistry.answer: Some gas escapes, so the volume is too small
acceptableAnswers: Some gas escapes, so the volume is too small
grade9-chemistry.hint: The reaction is fastest at the very beginning.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Gas is produced fastest at the start, so a delay in fitting the bung lets some escape and every reading afterwards is lower than it should be.

grade9-chemistry.question: What causes a parallax error when a burette is read?
options: The tap is left open while the reading is taken
The eye is not level with the liquid surface
The liquid is coloured and hides the scale
The burette is filled above the zero mark
grade9-chemistry.answer: The eye is not level with the liquid surface
acceptableAnswers: The eye is not level with the liquid surface
grade9-chemistry.hint: It depends on where your eye is.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Reading from above or below makes the scale appear to line up with the wrong mark. The eye must be level with the bottom of the meniscus.

grade9-chemistry.question: How is the reliability of a set of results improved?
options: By drawing the graph more neatly
By repeating and taking a mean
By using a larger sheet of paper
grade9-chemistry.answer: By repeating and taking a mean
acceptableAnswers: By repeating and taking a mean
grade9-chemistry.hint: A single reading proves very little.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Repeats show whether readings agree, and a mean of concordant repeats is closer to the true value than any single reading.

grade9-chemistry.question: Four metals are added to dilute acid. W fizzes strongly, X slowly, Y very slowly and Z not at all. What is the order of reactivity, most reactive first?
grade9-chemistry.answer: W, X, Y, Z
grade9-chemistry.hint: The strongest fizzing is the most reactive.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: How vigorously each metal fizzes shows how readily it reacts, so W is the most reactive and Z, which does not react at all, is the least.

grade9-chemistry.question: Equal volumes of three acids are neutralised by the same alkali. The temperature rises by 5.2, 6.8 and 4.1 °C. Which released the most heat?
options: They all released the same heat
grade9-chemistry.answer: The one that rose by 6.8 °C
grade9-chemistry.hint: More heat gives a bigger temperature rise.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The same mass of solution is warmed each time, so the largest temperature rise means the most heat was released.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why does a conclusion refer back to the hypothesis?
options: To make the conclusion long enough to read
To show the hypothesis was written first
To repeat what the hypothesis said again
To say whether the results support it
grade9-chemistry.answer: To say whether the results support it
acceptableAnswers: To say whether the results support it
grade9-chemistry.hint: The hypothesis was the idea being tested.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The whole purpose of the experiment was to test the hypothesis, so the conclusion must say whether the results support it or not.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which statement is a conclusion rather than an observation?
options: Zinc is more reactive than copper
The zinc fizzed and the copper did not
A colourless gas came off the zinc
The solution turned from blue to green
grade9-chemistry.answer: Zinc is more reactive than copper
acceptableAnswers: Zinc is more reactive than copper
grade9-chemistry.hint: Which one explains rather than describes?
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The others record what was seen. Saying that zinc is more reactive interprets those observations, which makes it a conclusion.

grade9-chemistry.question: Bubbles are counted by eye as a gas is given off. Suggest the best improvement.
options: Count the bubbles more slowly than before
Ask two pupils to count the same bubbles
Use a larger flask so bubbles are bigger
Collect the gas in a syringe and read it
grade9-chemistry.answer: Collect the gas in a syringe and read it
acceptableAnswers: Collect the gas in a syringe and read it
grade9-chemistry.hint: Counting fast bubbles by eye is not accurate.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A gas syringe measures the volume directly and does not depend on how fast a person can count, so the readings are far more accurate.

grade9-chemistry.question: A pupil repeats a reaction three times. The magnesium disappears after 24 s, 26 s and 25 s. Calculate the mean time in seconds.
grade9-chemistry.hint: Add the three times, then divide by three.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: 24 + 26 + 25 = 75, and 75 ÷ 3 = 25 s. A mean of repeats reduces the effect of any single poor reading.

grade9-chemistry.question: A burette reads 1.20 cm³ before a titration and 26.70 cm³ after it. Calculate the titre in cm³.
grade9-chemistry.hint: Subtract the first reading from the second.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: 26.70 − 1.20 = 25.50 cm³. The titre is always the difference between the two burette readings, never the final reading on its own.

grade9-chemistry.question: An empty crucible has a mass of 24.50 g. With copper oxide in it the mass is 26.90 g. Calculate the mass of copper oxide in g.
grade9-chemistry.hint: Subtract the mass of the empty crucible.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: 26.90 − 24.50 = 2.40 g. The solid cannot be weighed on its own, so it is found by difference.

grade9-chemistry.question: A flask of acid and marble chips has a mass of 152.60 g at the start and 150.20 g at the end. Calculate the mass of gas lost in g.
grade9-chemistry.hint: The gas that escaped is the mass that has gone.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: 152.60 − 150.20 = 2.40 g. The mass lost is the carbon dioxide that escaped from the open flask.

grade9-chemistry.question: Titres of 25.10, 25.20 and 25.30 cm³ are concordant. Calculate the mean titre in cm³.
grade9-chemistry.hint: Add the three titres, then divide by three.

grade9-chemistry.question: 60 cm³ of gas is collected in 30 seconds. Calculate the average rate in cm³ per second.
grade9-chemistry.hint: Divide the volume by the time.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: 60 ÷ 30 = 2 cm³ per second. An average rate is the total change divided by the total time taken.

grade9-chemistry.question: During a neutralisation the temperature rises from 21.0 °C to 27.5 °C. Calculate the temperature rise in °C.
grade9-chemistry.hint: Subtract the starting temperature from the final one.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: 27.5 − 21.0 = 6.5 °C. Neutralisation is exothermic, so the temperature of the mixture rises.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the piece of apparatus used to hold a hot evaporating basin.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Tongs
grade9-chemistry.hint: Never with bare hands.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Tongs hold hot apparatus so that hands are never in contact with it.

grade9-chemistry.question: A drop of acid splashes into a pupil’s eye. State what must be done immediately.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Wash the eye with plenty of water
acceptableAnswers: Wash the eye with plenty of water
rinse it with plenty of water
wash the eye with plenty of water
grade9-chemistry.hint: Dilute and remove it at once, then get help.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The eye is rinsed with plenty of running water straight away and the teacher is told, so that medical help can be arranged.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the equipment that draws toxic gases safely away from the laboratory.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Fume cupboard
grade9-chemistry.hint: Work with chlorine is done inside it.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A fume cupboard extracts toxic gases so that they are not breathed in.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the section of a report that lists the chemicals and equipment used.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Apparatus
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is written before the method.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The apparatus and materials section lists everything used, so the work can be set up again exactly.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the section of a report that states what the investigation set out to find.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Aim
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is the first thing written.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The aim states the purpose of the investigation.

grade9-chemistry.question: Give the word for what you see or measure during an experiment, before any explanation is added.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Observation
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is not yet a conclusion.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: An observation is what happened; a conclusion is what it means.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the document a chemical supplier provides that lists the hazards of a substance.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Safety data sheet
grade9-chemistry.hint: Its initials are SDS.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A safety data sheet gives the hazards, handling, storage and first-aid measures for a substance.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the ICT tool used to calculate means and draw graphs from a results table.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Spreadsheet
grade9-chemistry.hint: It works in rows and columns.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A spreadsheet holds data in rows and columns and can calculate from it and plot it.

grade9-chemistry.question: Give the word for presenting somebody else’s writing as your own.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Plagiarism
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is avoided by naming the source.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Plagiarism is using another person’s work without credit; naming the source avoids it.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the variable that is deliberately changed in an investigation.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Independent variable
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is the one you choose.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The independent variable is chosen and changed by the experimenter.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the variable that is measured to find the effect of the change.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Dependent variable
grade9-chemistry.hint: Its value depends on the one you changed.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The dependent variable is measured, and its value depends on the independent variable.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the experiment set up for comparison, in which the factor being tested is left out.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Control
grade9-chemistry.hint: It shows what happens when nothing is changed.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A control gives a baseline, so any difference in the other tubes can be put down to the factor being tested.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the type of graph drawn when both quantities change continuously.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Line graph
grade9-chemistry.hint: The points are joined with a line.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A line graph is used for two continuous quantities, such as volume of gas against time.

grade9-chemistry.question: Besides the quantity, what must a results-table column heading carry?
grade9-chemistry.answer: The unit
grade9-chemistry.hint: Time / s carries it after the stroke.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The unit goes in the heading, so that every cell below holds a number only.

grade9-chemistry.question: Give the word for a result that does not fit the pattern of the others.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Anomalous
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is recorded and marked, never rubbed out.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: An anomalous result is recorded and identified, then left out of the mean.

grade9-chemistry.question: Give the word describing titres that are close enough in value to be averaged.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Concordant
grade9-chemistry.hint: They agree within about 0.10 cm³.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Concordant titres agree within about 0.10 cm³ and are the ones averaged; a titre far from the rest is anomalous.

grade9-chemistry.question: The diagram shows a molecule of ammonia. How many hydrogen atoms are there in one molecule?
grade9-chemistry.hint: Count only the circles labelled H.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The nitrogen atom is joined to three hydrogen atoms, which is why ammonia is written NH3.

grade9-chemistry.question: What is the valency of aluminium?
grade9-chemistry.hint: Aluminium is in Group III of the periodic table.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Aluminium is in Group III, so it loses three electrons and has a valency of 3 - which is why its oxide is Al2O3.

grade9-chemistry.question: A methane molecule is one carbon atom joined to four hydrogen atoms. What is its formula?
grade9-chemistry.answer: CH<sub>4</sub>
grade9-chemistry.hint: The small number goes after the atom it counts.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: One carbon and four hydrogens is written CH4. The subscript follows the symbol it belongs to, so C4H would mean four carbons and one hydrogen.

grade9-chemistry.question: The ozone layer is depleted by ...........
grade9-chemistry.answer: chlorofluorocarbons
grade9-chemistry.hint: These were once used in fridges and aerosol cans, and are known by their initials.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) release chlorine high in the atmosphere, which breaks ozone apart. Sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen cause acid rain instead.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which of the following will cause eutrophication?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Fertilisers from agriculture
grade9-chemistry.hint: Eutrophication starts with too many nutrients in the water.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Fertiliser washed into a river adds nitrates and phosphates. Algae grow rapidly, block the light, then die and decay - and the decay uses up the dissolved oxygen, killing the fish.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which gas is produced when zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Hydrogen
grade9-chemistry.hint: A metal plus an acid always gives a salt and one particular gas.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Metal + acid → salt + hydrogen. Here zinc + hydrochloric acid gives zinc chloride and hydrogen, which is tested with a lighted splint and a squeaky pop.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which one of the following metals does not burn or glow when heated in air?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Copper
grade9-chemistry.hint: The least reactive metal of the four reacts with oxygen least readily.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Copper is the least reactive here: heated in air it only forms a black coating of copper oxide, without burning or glowing. Magnesium burns with a brilliant white flame, and iron and zinc glow.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which substance is used to control the acidity of soil?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Calcium hydroxide
grade9-chemistry.hint: To cancel an acid you add the opposite kind of substance.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Calcium hydroxide (slaked lime) is a base, so it neutralises acid in the soil and raises the pH. Nitric acid would make the soil more acidic, and the other two are fertilisers.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which one of the following salts is insoluble in water?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Magnesium carbonate
grade9-chemistry.hint: All nitrates are soluble, and so are almost all sulfates. Most carbonates are not.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Most carbonates are insoluble, and magnesium carbonate is one of them. All nitrates dissolve, ammonium compounds all dissolve, and zinc sulfate is soluble too.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which separation technique is used to obtain water from sea water?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Distillation
grade9-chemistry.hint: You want the LIQUID back, not the salt.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Distillation boils the water off and condenses the vapour back to pure liquid water, leaving the salt behind. Crystallisation would keep the salt and lose the water.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which separation technique is used to obtain iodine from a mixture of iodine and sand?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Sublimation
grade9-chemistry.hint: Iodine turns straight from solid to vapour when heated, without melting.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Iodine sublimes - it goes from solid to vapour and back to solid without becoming a liquid - while sand does not. Heating the mixture and collecting the deposit separates them.

grade9-chemistry.question: During sublimation, what precaution prevents the vapour from escaping?
options: Cover the dish with an inverted funnel
Heat the mixture as strongly as possible
Leave the apparatus open to the air
Add water to the mixture before heating
grade9-chemistry.answer: Cover the dish with an inverted funnel
acceptableAnswers: Cover the dish with an inverted funnel
grade9-chemistry.hint: The vapour has to be trapped somewhere it can cool and turn solid again.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: An inverted funnel over the dish catches the vapour so it re-solidifies on the cool inside surface, and a cotton wool plug in the stem stops any escaping. Leaving it open loses the product - and iodine vapour is harmful.

grade9-chemistry.question: What are the symbols for potassium and oxygen?
grade9-chemistry.answer: K and O
grade9-chemistry.hint: Potassium takes its symbol from its Latin name, kalium.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Potassium is K (from kalium) and oxygen is O. P is the symbol for phosphorus, which is why potassium cannot use it.

grade9-chemistry.question: Potassium has a valency of 1 and oxygen a valency of 2. What is the formula of potassium oxide?
grade9-chemistry.answer: K<sub>2</sub>O
grade9-chemistry.hint: Swap the valencies: each element takes the other’s number as its subscript.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Potassium (valency 1) and oxygen (valency 2) cross over to give K2O - two potassium atoms are needed to balance one oxygen atom.

grade9-chemistry.question: What is the formula of calcium chloride? (Calcium has valency 2, chlorine valency 1.)
grade9-chemistry.answer: CaCl<sub>2</sub>
grade9-chemistry.hint: Cross the valencies over.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Calcium’s valency of 2 needs two chlorine atoms of valency 1, giving CaCl2.

grade9-chemistry.question: What is the formula of iron (III) sulfate? (The sulfate ion is SO4 with valency 2.)
grade9-chemistry.answer: Fe<sub>2</sub>(SO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>
grade9-chemistry.hint: “Iron (III)” tells you iron’s valency is 3. Cross it with the sulfate’s valency of 2, and bracket the sulfate group.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Iron (III) has valency 3 and sulfate has valency 2, so crossing over gives two iron and three sulfate groups: Fe2(SO4)3. The brackets are essential - without them the 3 would apply only to the oxygen.

grade9-chemistry.question: Complete the word equation: Magnesium + Oxygen → ...........
grade9-chemistry.answer: Magnesium oxide
grade9-chemistry.hint: A metal burning in oxygen forms one simple product.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A metal plus oxygen gives a metal oxide, so magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide. Magnesium burns with a brilliant white flame and leaves a white ash.

grade9-chemistry.question: Complete the word equation: Aluminium + Chlorine → ...........
grade9-chemistry.answer: Aluminium chloride
grade9-chemistry.hint: A metal plus a halogen gives a salt whose name ends in -ide.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Metal + chlorine gives a metal chloride, so the product is aluminium chloride. Names ending in -ate (such as chlorate) contain oxygen as well.

grade9-chemistry.question: Complete the word equation: Hydrogen + Oxygen → ...........
grade9-chemistry.answer: Water
grade9-chemistry.hint: The product is the most familiar compound there is.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Hydrogen burns in oxygen to form water (H2O). Hydrogen peroxide is H2O2, a different compound made a different way.

grade9-chemistry.question: Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere measured 230 ppm in 1950 and 450 ppm in 2000. What was the increase?
grade9-chemistry.answer: 220 ppm
grade9-chemistry.hint: An increase is the later figure minus the earlier one.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: 450 − 230 = 220 ppm. Adding the two figures would give the meaningless total of 680.

grade9-chemistry.question: What is a greenhouse gas?
options: A gas that makes rainwater acidic
A gas that destroys the ozone layer
A gas used to grow plants in a greenhouse
A gas that traps heat in the atmosphere
grade9-chemistry.answer: A gas that traps heat in the atmosphere
acceptableAnswers: A gas that traps heat in the atmosphere
grade9-chemistry.hint: The name describes what it does to heat, not to plants.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A greenhouse gas lets sunlight through but absorbs the heat radiated back from the surface, warming the atmosphere. Ozone depletion and acid rain are caused by different gases.

grade9-chemistry.question: Apart from carbon dioxide, which of these is a greenhouse gas?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Methane
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is given off by cattle, paddy fields and rubbish tips.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Methane is a powerful greenhouse gas. Nitrogen, oxygen and argon make up most of the air but do not trap heat in this way.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which pair of activities has increased the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere?
options: Planting trees and using solar panels
Recycling paper and cycling to school
Using wind turbines and public transport
grade9-chemistry.answer: Burning fossil fuels and deforestation
grade9-chemistry.hint: One releases carbon dioxide; the other removes what would have absorbed it.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, and deforestation removes the trees that would have absorbed it - so the two act together. Every other option reduces emissions.

grade9-chemistry.question: Sodium reacts with water to form sodium hydroxide and a gas. Which gas is produced?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Hydrogen
grade9-chemistry.hint: A metal reacting with water gives a hydroxide and one gas.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Metal + water → metal hydroxide + hydrogen. With sodium the reaction is vigorous enough that the hydrogen often ignites.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which observation is made when sodium reacts with water?
options: It sinks to the bottom and stays still
It dissolves slowly with no visible change
It turns black and gives off a brown gas
It floats and moves rapidly on the surface, fizzing
grade9-chemistry.answer: It floats and moves rapidly on the surface, fizzing
acceptableAnswers: It floats and moves rapidly on the surface, fizzing
grade9-chemistry.hint: Sodium is less dense than water, and a gas is being produced.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Sodium floats (it is less dense than water), melts into a ball from the heat released, and darts about fizzing as hydrogen is given off. The solution formed turns red litmus blue.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which is the balanced equation for sodium reacting with water?
grade9-chemistry.answer: 2Na + 2H<sub>2</sub>O → 2NaOH + H<sub>2</sub>
grade9-chemistry.hint: Count each kind of atom on both sides - they must match.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: 2Na + 2H2O → 2NaOH + H2 balances: 2 Na, 4 H and 2 O on each side. The unbalanced version leaves hydrogen unequal.

grade9-chemistry.question: What name is given to the reaction between sodium hydroxide and an acid?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Neutralisation
grade9-chemistry.hint: A base cancelling an acid produces a salt and water.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: An acid reacting with a base is neutralisation: acid + base → salt + water. Here it gives a sodium salt and water.

grade9-chemistry.question: Metal X does not react with cold water but does react with steam. Metal Y reacts with neither. Which pair could X and Y be?
grade9-chemistry.answer: X = iron, Y = copper
grade9-chemistry.hint: Place the metals on the reactivity series: the more reactive a metal, the more readily it attacks water.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Iron is unreactive enough to ignore cold water but does react with steam, while copper sits low enough to react with neither. Sodium and potassium react violently with cold water, so neither can be X or Y.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which salt is used for enhancement of taste in food?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Sodium chloride
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is on every kitchen table.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Sodium chloride is common table salt, used to season food. Sodium hydrogen carbonate is baking soda and calcium sulfate is plaster of Paris.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which salt is used in baking?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Sodium hydrogen carbonate
grade9-chemistry.hint: It gives off carbon dioxide when heated, which makes a cake rise.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Sodium hydrogen carbonate (baking soda) decomposes on heating and releases carbon dioxide, and those bubbles make the mixture rise.

grade9-chemistry.question: Crude oil is separated into petrol, diesel and other fractions by:
grade9-chemistry.answer: Fractional distillation
grade9-chemistry.hint: The fractions have different boiling points.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Fractional distillation separates crude oil into fractions using their different boiling points.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which industry in Mauritius uses distillation to produce its product?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Rum distilleries
grade9-chemistry.hint: The name of the industry contains the technique.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Rum distilleries use distillation to concentrate and purify the spirit produced from sugar cane.

grade9-chemistry.question: Essential oils are extracted from plants by passing steam through them and then cooling the vapour. Which technique is this?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Distillation
grade9-chemistry.hint: Something is vaporised and then condensed.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Steam distillation carries the oil off as a vapour, which is then condensed and collected.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why is air cooled to a very low temperature before its gases are separated?
options: So the gases dissolve completely in water
So the gases become liquids that can be distilled apart
So the gases react together and form a compound
So the gases become solids that can be filtered
grade9-chemistry.answer: So the gases become liquids that can be distilled apart
acceptableAnswers: So the gases become liquids that can be distilled apart
grade9-chemistry.hint: Distillation needs liquids to work with.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Cooling liquefies the air, and the liquid is then fractionally distilled to separate nitrogen from oxygen.

grade9-chemistry.question: What is chromatography used for?
options: Turning a solid directly into a gas
Increasing the speed of a reaction
Measuring the temperature of a slow reaction
Separating and identifying the substances in a mixture
grade9-chemistry.answer: Separating and identifying the substances in a mixture
acceptableAnswers: Separating and identifying the substances in a mixture
grade9-chemistry.hint: The result is a set of separated spots.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Chromatography separates the components of a mixture so they can be identified and compared.

grade9-chemistry.question: How is chromatography used in sport?
options: To check the temperature of the track
To measure how fast an athlete can run
To detect banned drugs in an athlete’s sample
To decide which athlete has trained hardest
grade9-chemistry.answer: To detect banned drugs in an athlete’s sample
acceptableAnswers: To detect banned drugs in an athlete’s sample
grade9-chemistry.hint: It identifies substances that should not be present.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A sample is separated by chromatography and compared with known drugs to detect banned substances.

grade9-chemistry.question: How is chromatography used to check food?
options: To find out how long the food will keep fresh
To measure how much the food weighs
To decide how the food should be cooked
To detect pesticide residues and unlawful additives
grade9-chemistry.answer: To detect pesticide residues and unlawful additives
acceptableAnswers: To detect pesticide residues and unlawful additives
grade9-chemistry.hint: It finds substances that should not be there.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Chromatography separates a food extract so that contaminants and additives can be identified.

grade9-chemistry.question: A pure substance is tested by chromatography. What result is expected?
options: No spot at all, because it is pure
A continuous line rather than a spot
Several spots, one for each of the impurities
A single spot, because there is only one substance
grade9-chemistry.answer: A single spot, because there is only one substance
acceptableAnswers: A single spot, because there is only one substance
grade9-chemistry.hint: Each substance gives one spot.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A pure substance separates into one spot; more than one spot means the sample is a mixture.

grade9-chemistry.question: What is meant by climate change?
options: A single storm that causes serious damage
The change from day to night each 24 hours
A long-term change in the usual weather patterns of the Earth
The difference in the weather between two nearby towns
grade9-chemistry.answer: A long-term change in the usual weather patterns of the Earth
acceptableAnswers: A long-term change in the usual weather patterns of the Earth
grade9-chemistry.hint: Climate is weather averaged over a long time.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Climate change is a lasting shift in average weather patterns, not a single event or a daily variation.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which human activity contributes most to climate change?
options: Recycling paper and glass at home
Planting more trees along the roadside
Burning fossil fuels for energy and transport
grade9-chemistry.answer: Burning fossil fuels for energy and transport
acceptableAnswers: Burning fossil fuels for energy and transport
grade9-chemistry.hint: Which one releases carbon dioxide?
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Burning coal, oil and gas releases the carbon dioxide that drives the enhanced greenhouse effect.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which hazard is a small island state such as Mauritius especially exposed to?
options: A permanent fall in air temperature
The loss of all its underground caves
The disappearance of its rivers overnight
Coastal flooding as sea levels rise
grade9-chemistry.answer: Coastal flooding as sea levels rise
acceptableAnswers: Coastal flooding as sea levels rise
grade9-chemistry.hint: Think about where an island meets the sea.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: With most of its people and infrastructure near the coast, a rising sea threatens flooding and erosion.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which measure would reduce a country’s contribution to climate change?
options: Clearing forest to create more farmland
Encouraging every household to use two cars
Generating more electricity from wind and solar
grade9-chemistry.answer: Generating more electricity from wind and solar
acceptableAnswers: Generating more electricity from wind and solar
grade9-chemistry.hint: Reduce the carbon dioxide released.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Renewable generation displaces fossil fuels and so cuts carbon dioxide emissions.

grade9-chemistry.question: The graph shows carbon dioxide and global temperature since 1960. What does it show?
options: Neither has changed over the period
Carbon dioxide has risen while temperature has fallen
Both have risen over the period
Both have fallen over the period
grade9-chemistry.answer: Both have risen over the period
acceptableAnswers: Both have risen over the period
grade9-chemistry.hint: Follow each line from left to right.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Both lines rise from left to right, so carbon dioxide and temperature have increased together.

grade9-chemistry.question: The two lines on that graph rise together. What can be concluded from the graph alone?
options: The two quantities have nothing to do with each other
The two are correlated, but the graph alone does not prove cause
Carbon dioxide definitely causes the temperature rise
The temperature rise definitely causes the carbon dioxide rise
grade9-chemistry.answer: The two are correlated, but the graph alone does not prove cause
acceptableAnswers: The two are correlated, but the graph alone does not prove cause
grade9-chemistry.hint: Two things rising together is not the same as one causing the other.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The graph establishes a correlation; showing cause needs the physics of how the gas traps heat, not just the two lines.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why do scientists use measurements taken over many decades rather than a few years?
options: Old measurements are always more accurate
A few years of data cannot be plotted on a graph
Long records are quicker to collect than short ones
Short periods vary too much to show a long-term trend
grade9-chemistry.answer: Short periods vary too much to show a long-term trend
acceptableAnswers: Short periods vary too much to show a long-term trend
grade9-chemistry.hint: Climate is an average over a long time.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Year-to-year variation is large, so only a long record separates a genuine trend from ordinary fluctuation.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the technique used to separate crude oil into petrol, diesel and other fractions.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Fractional distillation
grade9-chemistry.hint: The fractions have different boiling points.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Fractional distillation separates crude oil into its fractions.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the technique used to detect banned drugs in an athlete’s sample.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Chromatography
grade9-chemistry.hint: It separates a mixture into spots.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Chromatography separates the sample so banned substances can be identified.

grade9-chemistry.question: State one hazard that climate change brings to a small island state.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Coastal flooding
grade9-chemistry.hint: Think about where an island meets the sea.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Rising seas bring coastal flooding and erosion, and warming brings stronger storms and coral bleaching.

grade9-chemistry.question: In a fractionating column, where are the fractions with the highest boiling points collected?
options: At the bottom, where it is hottest
In the middle of the column
At the very top, where it is coolest
grade9-chemistry.answer: At the bottom, where it is hottest
acceptableAnswers: At the bottom, where it is hottest
grade9-chemistry.hint: A high boiling point means it condenses first.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The column is hottest at the bottom, so fractions with the highest boiling points condense there. The lightest fractions rise to the cool top.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which fraction of crude oil is used as the fuel in a car engine?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Petrol
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is the lightest of these.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Petrol is a light fraction used in car engines. Kerosene fuels aircraft and bitumen surfaces roads.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why can crude oil be separated by fractional distillation?
options: Its parts react with each other on heating
Its parts have exactly the same density
Its parts have different boiling points
Its parts have different colours entirely
grade9-chemistry.answer: Its parts have different boiling points
acceptableAnswers: Its parts have different boiling points
grade9-chemistry.hint: Something has to differ between the parts.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Distillation separates liquids whose boiling points differ, so each fraction condenses at a different height in the column.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which two gases are obtained on a large scale by distilling liquid air?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Nitrogen and oxygen
grade9-chemistry.hint: They are the two main gases in air.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Air is cooled until it liquefies and then fractionally distilled: nitrogen boils off first, leaving oxygen behind.

grade9-chemistry.question: What is the oxygen from an air distillation plant mainly used for in a hospital?
options: Keeping the operating theatre very cool
Lighting the lamps above the operating table
Helping patients who cannot breathe well
grade9-chemistry.answer: Helping patients who cannot breathe well
acceptableAnswers: Helping patients who cannot breathe well
grade9-chemistry.hint: Think about a patient with lung trouble.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Medical oxygen supports patients whose lungs cannot take in enough of it from the air.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why is nitrogen from liquid air sealed inside packets of crisps?
options: It makes the packet float in a shop
It is cheaper than the air outside a packet
It is unreactive, so the food keeps longer
It gives the crisps their salty flavour
grade9-chemistry.answer: It is unreactive, so the food keeps longer
acceptableAnswers: It is unreactive, so the food keeps longer
grade9-chemistry.hint: What in ordinary air makes food go stale?
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Nitrogen is unreactive, so it keeps oxygen away from the food and the fat does not turn rancid.

grade9-chemistry.question: Essential oils are obtained from plants by steam distillation. What happens in the condenser?
options: The liquid is filtered to remove the leaves
The liquid reacts with the steam to form oil
The vapour is cooled back into a liquid
The vapour is heated further into a gas
grade9-chemistry.answer: The vapour is cooled back into a liquid
acceptableAnswers: The vapour is cooled back into a liquid
grade9-chemistry.hint: A condenser does what its name says.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Steam carries the oil over as a vapour; the condenser cools it back to a liquid, which is then separated from the water.

grade9-chemistry.question: What is distillation used for in a rum distillery?
options: To concentrate and purify the alcohol
To colour the spirit before it is sold
To ferment the cane juice into alcohol
To dissolve the sugar out of the cane
grade9-chemistry.answer: To concentrate and purify the alcohol
acceptableAnswers: To concentrate and purify the alcohol
grade9-chemistry.hint: Fermentation happens before this step.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Fermentation produces a dilute alcohol; distillation then separates and concentrates it, because alcohol boils below water.

grade9-chemistry.question: How is drinking water obtained from seawater by distillation?
options: The water is boiled off and the salt stays
The salt dissolves and the water evaporates
The salt is boiled off and the water stays
Both boil off together and are then cooled
grade9-chemistry.answer: The water is boiled off and the salt stays
acceptableAnswers: The water is boiled off and the salt stays
grade9-chemistry.hint: Which of the two has a boiling point you can reach?
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Water boils and is condensed as pure water. The salt is not volatile, so it is left behind in the flask.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why is distillation an expensive way to purify water?
options: The water has to be filtered many times first
A great deal of energy is needed to boil it
The apparatus has to be replaced every day
Salt must be bought to add to the seawater
grade9-chemistry.answer: A great deal of energy is needed to boil it
acceptableAnswers: A great deal of energy is needed to boil it
grade9-chemistry.hint: Think about the heating.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Boiling water needs a large amount of energy, which is why distillation is used mainly where fresh water is genuinely scarce.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why is distilled water used in a car battery rather than tap water?
options: It carries a charge of its own
It is much colder than tap water
It boils at a much lower point
grade9-chemistry.answer: It contains no dissolved salts
grade9-chemistry.hint: Tap water is not pure.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Distilled water has had its dissolved salts removed, so it does not react with or damage the plates of the battery.

grade9-chemistry.question: A mixture of ethanol and water is distilled. Ethanol boils at 78 °C and water at 100 °C. What is collected first?
options: Neither, because the mixture cannot be separated
Water, because it boils at the higher temperature
Both together, because they mix in all proportions
Ethanol, because it boils at the lower temperature
grade9-chemistry.answer: Ethanol, because it boils at the lower temperature
acceptableAnswers: Ethanol, because it boils at the lower temperature
grade9-chemistry.hint: The lower boiling point vaporises first.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The liquid with the lower boiling point vaporises first, so ethanol distils over at about 78 °C, before the water.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why is the starting line on a chromatogram drawn in pencil?
options: Pencil marks can be rubbed out afterwards
Pencil does not dissolve in the solvent
Pencil is easier to see than ink is
Pencil dries much faster than ink does
grade9-chemistry.answer: Pencil does not dissolve in the solvent
acceptableAnswers: Pencil does not dissolve in the solvent
grade9-chemistry.hint: What would happen to a line drawn in ink?
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Ink would dissolve and travel up the paper, adding spots of its own. Pencil is insoluble and stays where it was drawn.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why must the solvent level start below the pencil line?
options: The solvent would evaporate far too fast
The line would be washed off the paper first
The paper would not absorb the solvent
The spots would dissolve into the solvent
grade9-chemistry.answer: The spots would dissolve into the solvent
acceptableAnswers: The spots would dissolve into the solvent
grade9-chemistry.hint: Think about a spot sitting in the liquid.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: If the line is below the solvent, the spots dissolve into the liquid in the beaker instead of travelling up the paper.

grade9-chemistry.question: The chromatogram shows a food colouring X beside three known dyes. How many dyes are in X?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Two
grade9-chemistry.hint: Count the separate spots in that lane.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Each spot is one substance, so a lane carrying two spots means the colouring is a mixture of two dyes.

grade9-chemistry.question: On a chromatogram, how is one of the dyes in an unknown identified?
options: Its spot is the last one to appear on the paper
Its spot rises to the same height as a known one
Its spot is the darkest of all the spots shown
Its spot is nearest to the pencil line at the base
grade9-chemistry.answer: Its spot rises to the same height as a known one
acceptableAnswers: Its spot rises to the same height as a known one
grade9-chemistry.hint: Compare each lane with the known ones beside it.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A substance travels the same distance under the same conditions, so a spot level with a known dye identifies it.

grade9-chemistry.question: A sample gives a single spot on a chromatogram. What does that show?
options: The solvent was the wrong one
The sample did not dissolve at all
The sample is a pure substance
grade9-chemistry.answer: The sample is a pure substance
acceptableAnswers: The sample is a pure substance
grade9-chemistry.hint: One substance gives one spot.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A single spot means only one substance is present, so the sample is pure. A mixture separates into two or more spots.

grade9-chemistry.question: How is chromatography used to test an athlete for banned drugs?
options: The sample is heated until the drug burns off
The sample is weighed against a known mass
The sample is compared with known drug spots
The sample is timed as it runs up the paper
grade9-chemistry.answer: The sample is compared with known drug spots
acceptableAnswers: The sample is compared with known drug spots
grade9-chemistry.hint: A known reference is run alongside it.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The sample is separated and each spot compared with reference samples of the banned substances. A matching spot shows the drug is present.

grade9-chemistry.question: How does chromatography help check food for pesticide residues?
options: It destroys any pesticide that is present
It shows how long the food will stay fresh
It measures how much the food itself weighs
It separates the extract so residues show up
grade9-chemistry.answer: It separates the extract so residues show up
acceptableAnswers: It separates the extract so residues show up
grade9-chemistry.hint: Residues are present in tiny amounts inside a mixture.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: An extract of the food is separated so that traces of pesticide appear as spots of their own and can be identified.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which industry uses chromatography to check that a medicine is pure?
grade9-chemistry.answer: The pharmaceutical industry
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is the industry that makes medicines.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Medicine manufacturers use chromatography to show that a batch contains the drug itself and no unwanted extra substances.

grade9-chemistry.question: How is chromatography used by a forensic scientist?
options: To read writing that has been rubbed out
To find out when the note was actually written
To measure the mass of the note that was left
To compare ink from a note with known pens
grade9-chemistry.answer: To compare ink from a note with known pens
acceptableAnswers: To compare ink from a note with known pens
grade9-chemistry.hint: Inks are mixtures of dyes.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Ink is a mixture of dyes, so its chromatogram acts like a fingerprint and can be matched to a particular pen.

grade9-chemistry.question: What is the solvent front on a chromatogram?
options: The furthest the solvent has travelled
The point at which two spots overlap
The edge of the paper nearest the beaker
The line on which the spots were placed
grade9-chemistry.answer: The furthest the solvent has travelled
acceptableAnswers: The furthest the solvent has travelled
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is marked as soon as the paper is taken out.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The solvent front is the highest level the solvent reached. Distances are measured from the pencil line up to it.

grade9-chemistry.question: A drink is tested and gives a spot level with a dye that is banned in food. What can be concluded?
options: The drink contains that banned dye
The drink contains only that one dye
The drink is safe because it was tested
The drink has no colouring in it at all
grade9-chemistry.answer: The drink contains that banned dye
acceptableAnswers: The drink contains that banned dye
grade9-chemistry.hint: A matching spot identifies a substance.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A spot at the same height as a known dye identifies it. It does not show that nothing else is present, and testing alone does not make a drink safe.

grade9-chemistry.question: Two dyes in a mixture do not separate on the paper. What should be tried next?
options: A smaller spot of the same mixture
A shorter piece of paper than before
A cooler place to stand the beaker in
A different solvent for the same mixture
grade9-chemistry.answer: A different solvent for the same mixture
acceptableAnswers: A different solvent for the same mixture
grade9-chemistry.hint: How far a dye travels depends on the liquid.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Different solvents carry dyes different distances, so changing the solvent is the usual way to separate substances that ran together.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which gas released by burning fossil fuels contributes most to the greenhouse effect?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Carbon dioxide
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is the product of burning carbon completely.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Carbon dioxide is released in enormous quantities when fossil fuels burn and is the main greenhouse gas from human activity.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which greenhouse gas comes mainly from cattle and from flooded rice fields?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Methane
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is the main gas in natural gas.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Methane is produced by cattle and by flooded rice fields, and traps far more heat per molecule than carbon dioxide does.

grade9-chemistry.question: How does cutting down a forest add to global warming?
options: Fewer trees means the soil becomes much colder
Fewer trees make the wind blow much harder
Fewer trees remove carbon dioxide from the air
Fewer trees allow more oxygen to reach the sea
grade9-chemistry.answer: Fewer trees remove carbon dioxide from the air
acceptableAnswers: Fewer trees remove carbon dioxide from the air
grade9-chemistry.hint: What do trees do with carbon dioxide?
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Trees absorb carbon dioxide as they photosynthesise. Removing them leaves more of it in the atmosphere, and burning them releases still more.

grade9-chemistry.question: Carbon dioxide dissolves in seawater. What is the chemical effect on the ocean?
grade9-chemistry.answer: It becomes more acidic
grade9-chemistry.hint: What does a dissolved acidic gas do to pH?
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Carbon dioxide dissolves to form carbonic acid, lowering the pH. This ocean acidification makes it harder for corals and shellfish to build their shells.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which of these is a renewable source of electricity?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Solar panels
grade9-chemistry.hint: Which one does not run out?
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Sunlight is renewable and releases no carbon dioxide in use. Coal, diesel and natural gas are all fossil fuels.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why does bagasse count as a better fuel than coal for the climate?
options: Bagasse burns without needing any oxygen
The cane regrows and takes the gas back in
Bagasse contains no carbon of any kind at all
Bagasse gives out no heat when it is burned
grade9-chemistry.answer: The cane regrows and takes the gas back in
acceptableAnswers: The cane regrows and takes the gas back in
grade9-chemistry.hint: The crop is grown again each year.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Sugar cane absorbs carbon dioxide as it grows, so burning the bagasse returns carbon taken from the air only months earlier. Coal releases carbon stored for millions of years.

grade9-chemistry.question: How does using an electric bus instead of a diesel bus help a town?
options: No passengers have to pay for the journey
No exhaust gases are given off in the town
No metal is needed to build the vehicle
No electricity is needed to run the vehicle
grade9-chemistry.answer: No exhaust gases are given off in the town
acceptableAnswers: No exhaust gases are given off in the town
grade9-chemistry.hint: Think about what comes out of the exhaust pipe.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: An electric bus releases no exhaust gases where it runs. How clean it is overall still depends on how the electricity was generated.

grade9-chemistry.question: What is meant by carbon capture and storage?
options: Carbon dioxide is trapped and stored underground
Carbon dioxide is released high in the atmosphere
Carbon dioxide is burned to make it harmless
Carbon dioxide is turned into oxygen by a machine
grade9-chemistry.answer: Carbon dioxide is trapped and stored underground
acceptableAnswers: Carbon dioxide is trapped and stored underground
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is taken out before it ever reaches the air.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The gas is captured at the power station and stored in rock deep underground, so that it does not enter the atmosphere at all.

grade9-chemistry.question: Which hazard of a warming climate most threatens a coral reef?
options: Warmer seawater makes it grow faster
Warmer seawater becomes far less salty
grade9-chemistry.answer: Warmer seawater causes bleaching
grade9-chemistry.hint: Corals lose the algae that live inside them.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: When the sea warms, corals expel the algae that feed them and turn white. A bleached reef can die, taking its fish with it.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why does a rising sea level threaten Mauritius more than a large inland country?
options: It receives far less rain than a large country
Most of its towns and roads are on the coast
Its land is entirely below the level of the sea
It has no rivers to carry the extra water away
grade9-chemistry.answer: Most of its towns and roads are on the coast
acceptableAnswers: Most of its towns and roads are on the coast
grade9-chemistry.hint: Think about where the people actually live.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: An island has a long coastline, and most of its people, roads and hotels sit close to the sea, so flooding and erosion reach them first.

grade9-chemistry.question: A family wants to cut its carbon footprint. Which change does most?
options: Fitting a solar water heater on the roof
Washing the car with a hose every weekend
Leaving the lights on only at night time
Buying bottled water instead of tap water
grade9-chemistry.answer: Fitting a solar water heater on the roof
acceptableAnswers: Fitting a solar water heater on the roof
grade9-chemistry.hint: Which one replaces a fuel with sunlight?
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A solar heater replaces electricity or gas with sunlight for a large daily energy demand. The other three save nothing, or use more.

grade9-chemistry.question: A country replaces a coal power station with a wind farm. What is the main effect?
options: The same carbon dioxide is released as before
More carbon dioxide is released each year
Less carbon dioxide is released each year
No electricity can be generated at any time
grade9-chemistry.answer: Less carbon dioxide is released each year
acceptableAnswers: Less carbon dioxide is released each year
grade9-chemistry.hint: Which of the two burns a fuel?
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A wind farm burns nothing, so replacing coal generation cuts the carbon dioxide released, although the output varies with the wind.

grade9-chemistry.question: The table shows the carbon dioxide in the air. What does it show between 1960 and 2020?
options: A steady rise in every reading
A rise and then a fall again
No change over the whole period
A steady fall in every reading
grade9-chemistry.answer: A steady rise in every reading
acceptableAnswers: A steady rise in every reading
grade9-chemistry.hint: Read the second column downwards.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Each value is larger than the one above it, so the concentration has risen throughout the period.

grade9-chemistry.question: Using the table, between which two readings is the increase the largest?
grade9-chemistry.hint: Work out each difference in turn.
