grade9-chemistry.explanation: The differences are 22, 30, 20 and 25 ppm, so the largest rise was the 30 ppm between 1980 and 2000.

grade9-chemistry.question: What does ppm mean when carbon dioxide in the air is measured?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Parts per million
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is a way of writing a very small proportion.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: ppm means parts per million: 414 ppm is 414 molecules of carbon dioxide in every million molecules of air.

grade9-chemistry.question: A pupil says a graph of temperature and carbon dioxide proves that the gas caused the warming. What is wrong with that?
options: A graph cannot show two lines at one time
A graph shows a link, not what caused it
The two lines are measured in the same unit
Temperature cannot be plotted against a year
grade9-chemistry.answer: A graph shows a link, not what caused it
acceptableAnswers: A graph shows a link, not what caused it
grade9-chemistry.hint: Two lines rising together - what does that alone tell you?
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The graph shows a correlation. Cause is established by the physics of how carbon dioxide traps heat, together with other evidence, not by the shape of two lines.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why are climate records averaged over thirty years?
options: Thirty years of data is quicker to collect
One cold year does not mean the trend has ended
A shorter record cannot be drawn on a graph at all
Older readings are always more accurate
grade9-chemistry.answer: One cold year does not mean the trend has ended
acceptableAnswers: One cold year does not mean the trend has ended
grade9-chemistry.hint: Weather varies a great deal from year to year.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Climate is weather averaged over decades. A single cool year is ordinary variation and says nothing about the long-term trend.

grade9-chemistry.question: The bar chart shows where a country’s carbon dioxide comes from. Which source releases the most?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Electricity
grade9-chemistry.hint: Find the tallest bar.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The tallest bar is electricity generation, so that is the largest single source in this country.

grade9-chemistry.question: Using that bar chart, which two sources together release more than half the total?
grade9-chemistry.answer: Electricity and transport
grade9-chemistry.hint: Add each pair and compare it with the whole.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Electricity (40) and transport (25) total 65 out of 100, which is more than half. No other pair reaches that.

grade9-chemistry.question: A country cut its emissions but the world total still rose. What does that show?
options: Other countries increased theirs by more
The country did not really cut anything
Cutting emissions has no effect on totals
The world total cannot ever be measured
grade9-chemistry.answer: Other countries increased theirs by more
acceptableAnswers: Other countries increased theirs by more
grade9-chemistry.hint: The world total is a sum of every country.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A world total is the sum of all countries. One country falling while the total rises means increases elsewhere outweighed that cut.

grade9-chemistry.question: A graph of sea level rises by 3 mm each year. What does the gradient of the line represent?
options: How fast the sea level is rising
How long the readings were taken for
How high the sea level has become
grade9-chemistry.answer: How fast the sea level is rising
acceptableAnswers: How fast the sea level is rising
grade9-chemistry.hint: A steeper line means a faster change.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The gradient is the change in sea level divided by the time, which is the rate at which the sea is rising.

grade9-chemistry.question: Why are measurements of carbon dioxide taken far away from any city?
options: Cities have no equipment that could be used
City air would give a local reading only
Cities are always warmer than the countryside
The gas cannot be measured inside a city
grade9-chemistry.answer: City air would give a local reading only
acceptableAnswers: City air would give a local reading only
grade9-chemistry.hint: The aim is a value for the whole atmosphere.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Traffic and industry raise the concentration locally. A remote station measures the well-mixed background value that represents the atmosphere.

grade9-chemistry.question: A projection shows three possible temperatures for the year 2100. Why is more than one line drawn?
options: Future emissions are not yet decided
Temperature can be measured three ways
Three separate countries made the graph
grade9-chemistry.answer: Future emissions are not yet decided
acceptableAnswers: Future emissions are not yet decided
grade9-chemistry.hint: The future depends on what people do next.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Each line is a scenario for a different level of future emissions, so the spread shows how much the outcome depends on the choices made now.

grade9-chemistry.question: One year in a long temperature record is much cooler than those around it. How should it be treated?
options: Kept in the record and explained if possible
Removed so the rising trend looks clearer
Used on its own to show the world is cooling
Replaced by the average of the years beside it
grade9-chemistry.answer: Kept in the record and explained if possible
acceptableAnswers: Kept in the record and explained if possible
grade9-chemistry.hint: A single year is not a trend, but it is still data.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The reading is real and is kept. A large volcanic eruption, for example, cools a single year. Removing it would hide evidence.

grade9-chemistry.question: Two countries of very different size are compared. Which figure allows a fair comparison?
options: The number of people in the country
The emissions for the whole country
The area of land the country covers
grade9-chemistry.answer: The emissions for each person
grade9-chemistry.hint: One country may have far more people than the other.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Emissions per person allow countries of very different sizes to be compared. A total on its own largely reflects population.

grade9-chemistry.question: Use the table. Calculate the increase in carbon dioxide from 1960 to 2020, in ppm.
grade9-chemistry.hint: Subtract the 1960 value from the 2020 value.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: 414 − 317 = 97 ppm. That is a rise of nearly a third in sixty years.

grade9-chemistry.question: Use the table. Calculate the increase in carbon dioxide from 2000 to 2020, in ppm.
grade9-chemistry.hint: Subtract the 2000 value from the 2020 value.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: 414 − 369 = 45 ppm in twenty years, which is faster than the 22 ppm of the twenty years to 1980.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the part of a distillation apparatus in which vapour is turned back into a liquid.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Condenser
grade9-chemistry.hint: Cold water flows through its outer jacket.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The condenser cools the vapour so that it condenses and runs down into the receiver.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the gas obtained from liquid air that is given to patients in hospital.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Oxygen
grade9-chemistry.hint: It makes up about a fifth of the air.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Oxygen is separated from liquid air and supplied to patients who cannot take in enough of it from the air.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the process used to obtain essential oils from plants using steam.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Steam distillation
grade9-chemistry.hint: Steam carries the oil over as a vapour.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Steam distillation carries the oil off as a vapour, which is condensed and then separated from the water.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the technique that separates the dyes in a food colouring.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Chromatography
grade9-chemistry.hint: The dyes travel up a strip of paper.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Chromatography separates a mixture into its components as a solvent carries them different distances.

grade9-chemistry.question: A sample gives one spot on a chromatogram. State what this tells you about the sample.
grade9-chemistry.answer: It is pure
grade9-chemistry.hint: One substance gives one spot.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: One spot means one substance, so the sample is pure.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the line, drawn in pencil, on which the spots are placed at the start.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Baseline
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is drawn before any spot is added.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: The baseline, or start line, is drawn in pencil because pencil does not dissolve in the solvent.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the greenhouse gas produced when a fossil fuel burns completely.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Carbon dioxide
grade9-chemistry.hint: Limewater turns milky with it.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Complete combustion of a fossil fuel produces carbon dioxide, the main greenhouse gas from human activity.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the greenhouse gas released by cattle and by flooded rice fields.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Methane
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is the main gas in natural gas.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Methane traps far more heat per molecule than carbon dioxide, although there is much less of it in the air.

grade9-chemistry.question: Name the effect on seawater of carbon dioxide dissolving in it.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Ocean acidification
grade9-chemistry.hint: It lowers the pH of the sea.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Dissolved carbon dioxide forms carbonic acid and lowers the pH of the sea. This is called ocean acidification.

grade9-chemistry.question: Give, written in full, the unit used for the amount of carbon dioxide in the air.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Parts per million
grade9-chemistry.hint: Its short form is ppm.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Concentrations this small are given in parts per million.

grade9-chemistry.question: Two quantities rise together on a graph. Give the word for that relationship.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Correlation
grade9-chemistry.hint: It is not the same thing as cause.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: A correlation means the two change together; showing that one causes the other needs further evidence.

grade9-chemistry.question: A student monitored dissolved oxygen (DO) levels at four points along a river below a farm that uses nitrate fertiliser. State the dissolved oxygen reading at point A. (answer in mg/L)
grade9-chemistry.hint: Read the value from the table for point A.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Point A, 500 m above the farm, shows 9.2 mg/L — the baseline before any farm runoff.

grade9-chemistry.question: A student monitored dissolved oxygen (DO) levels at four points along a river below a farm that uses nitrate fertiliser. Between which two points is the dissolved oxygen the lowest? Suggest why.
grade9-chemistry.hint: Find the minimum value, then explain what causes oxygen to fall near the farm.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Point C (1.8 mg/L) is the lowest. After the fertiliser enters the river, algae bloom; the algae die and are decomposed by bacteria whose aerobic respiration removes oxygen, reaching the lowest level at C before the river recovers at D.
grade9-chemistry.answer: B and C

The diagram below shows the apparatus used to separate a salt solution by distillation. Parts are labelled A–D.
<svg viewBox="0 0 340 200" width="340" role="img" aria-label="a labelled distillation apparatus diagram"><ellipse cx="80" cy="140" rx="55" ry="40" fill="none" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="135" y1="115" x2="230" y2="85" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="215" y="65" width="80" height="30" rx="4" fill="none" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="295" y1="80" x2="320" y2="100" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="2"/><ellipse cx="325" cy="108" rx="12" ry="8" fill="none" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="2"/><rect x="5" y="155" width="150" height="10" rx="3" fill="#fde68a" stroke="#b45309" stroke-width="1"/><text x="60" y="125" font-size="10" fill="#0f172a" font-weight="bold">A</text><text x="120" y="75" font-size="10" fill="#0f172a" font-weight="bold">B</text><text x="248" y="60" font-size="10" fill="#0f172a" font-weight="bold">C</text><text x="312" y="60" font-size="10" fill="#0f172a" font-weight="bold">D</text><text x="60" y="178" font-size="9" fill="#78350f">Heat source</text></svg>

grade9-chemistry.hint: The long slanted tube where vapour is cooled.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Part C is the condenser (Liebig condenser). Cold water flows through its outer jacket to cool and condense the vapour back into a liquid.
grade9-chemistry.answer: condenser

The diagram below shows the apparatus used to separate a salt solution by distillation. Parts are labelled A–D.

grade9-chemistry.hint: Where is the mixture placed?
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Part A is the distillation flask (round-bottomed flask) where the salt solution is placed and heated. The mixture boils in this vessel.
grade9-chemistry.answer: distillation flask

grade9-chemistry.question:
A student investigates the reactions of three metals — magnesium, iron and copper — with dilute hydrochloric acid.
Write a balanced equation for the reaction of magnesium with dilute hydrochloric acid.
grade9-chemistry.hint: Metal + HCl → metal chloride + hydrogen gas.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. Mg²⁺ needs two Cl⁻ ions; two HCl provide two Cl and two H, forming one H₂.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂

grade9-chemistry.question:
A student investigates the reactions of three metals — magnesium, iron and copper — with dilute hydrochloric acid.
Write a balanced equation for the reaction of iron with dilute hydrochloric acid.
grade9-chemistry.hint: Iron forms Fe²⁺ with dilute acid.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Fe + 2HCl → FeCl₂ + H₂. Iron(II) chloride is formed because Fe loses 2 electrons to become Fe²⁺.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Fe + 2HCl → FeCl₂ + H₂

<svg viewBox="0 0 360 160" width="360" role="img" aria-label="a results table for displacement reactions between four metals and three salt solutions"><text x="180" y="14" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="#0f172a">Displacement Reaction Results</text><rect x="10" y="20" width="340" height="135" fill="none" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="100" y1="20" x2="100" y2="155" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="190" y1="20" x2="190" y2="155" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="275" y1="20" x2="275" y2="155" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="10" y1="47" x2="350" y2="47" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="10" y1="80" x2="350" y2="80" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1"/><line x1="10" y1="113" x2="350" y2="113" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1"/><text x="16" y="40" font-size="9" fill="#0f172a">Metal</text><text x="106" y="34" font-size="9" fill="#0f172a">CuSO₄ solution</text><text x="196" y="34" font-size="9" fill="#0f172a">FeSO₄ solution</text><text x="281" y="34" font-size="9" fill="#0f172a">ZnSO₄ solution</text><text x="16" y="70" font-size="9" fill="#334155">Zinc (Zn)</text><text x="140" y="70" font-size="9" fill="#15803d">✓</text><text x="230" y="70" font-size="9" fill="#15803d">✓</text><text x="310" y="70" font-size="9" fill="#6b7280">✗</text><text x="16" y="103" font-size="9" fill="#334155">Iron (Fe)</text><text x="140" y="103" font-size="9" fill="#15803d">✓</text><text x="230" y="103" font-size="9" fill="#6b7280">✗</text><text x="310" y="103" font-size="9" fill="#6b7280">✗</text><text x="16" y="136" font-size="9" fill="#334155">Copper (Cu)</text><text x="140" y="136" font-size="9" fill="#6b7280">✗</text><text x="230" y="136" font-size="9" fill="#6b7280">✗</text><text x="310" y="136" font-size="9" fill="#6b7280">✗</text></svg>
Write the order of reactivity of these three metals, from most reactive to least reactive, using the data in the table.
grade9-chemistry.hint: The most reactive metal displaces the most other metals from their solutions.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Zn displaces both Cu and Fe (2 reactions). Fe displaces only Cu (1 reaction). Cu displaces none (0). Order: Zn > Fe > Cu.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Zn > Fe > Cu

A class carries out displacement reactions to determine a reactivity order. Their results are shown in the table below (✓ = reaction, ✗ = no reaction).

Write a balanced ionic equation for the reaction of zinc with copper sulfate solution.
grade9-chemistry.hint: Spectator ions do not appear in the ionic equation.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s). The SO₄²⁻ ion is a spectator ion and is omitted.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu

grade9-chemistry.question:
Acid rain is formed when sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen dissolve in atmospheric water droplets.
Write the equation for the formation of sulfuric acid from sulfur dioxide in the atmosphere.
grade9-chemistry.hint: SO₂ + water + oxygen → an acid.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: 2SO₂ + O₂ + 2H₂O → 2H₂SO₄. (Or acceptably: SO₂ + H₂O → H₂SO₃, then H₂SO₃ + ½O₂ → H₂SO₄.)
grade9-chemistry.answer: 2SO₂ + O₂ + 2H₂O → 2H₂SO₄

grade9-chemistry.question:
A student wishes to prepare pure copper sulfate crystals starting from copper oxide and dilute sulfuric acid.
Write the balanced equation for the reaction of copper oxide with sulfuric acid.
grade9-chemistry.hint: Base + acid → salt + water.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: CuO + H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + H₂O.
grade9-chemistry.answer: CuO + H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + H₂O

Which gas in the table has the highest global warming potential per molecule?
grade9-chemistry.hint: Read the GWP column.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: SF₆ has the highest GWP (23,500 times that of CO₂ over 100 years).
grade9-chemistry.answer: SF₆

grade9-chemistry.question:
A student has the following four mixtures to separate. She must choose the best technique for each.
Mixture 2: Salt dissolved in water. Name the technique to recover PURE WATER (not the salt).
grade9-chemistry.hint: You need to collect the water, not the salt.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Distillation. The water is evaporated from the solution and condensed as pure distillate; the salt remains in the flask.
grade9-chemistry.answer: distillation

grade9-chemistry.question:
A student has the following four mixtures to separate. She must choose the best technique for each.
Mixture 3: Copper sulfate dissolved in water. Name the technique to obtain copper sulfate crystals.
grade9-chemistry.hint: You want the solid, not the liquid.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Crystallisation (evaporation to saturation followed by cooling). The solution is evaporated to a saturated solution and then cooled slowly; CuSO₄·5H₂O crystals form and are collected by filtration.
grade9-chemistry.answer: crystallisation

grade9-chemistry.question:
A student has the following four mixtures to separate. She must choose the best technique for each.
Mixture 4: Ethanol (b.p. 78 °C) and water (b.p. 100 °C) — both liquids, fully miscible. Name the most effective technique.
grade9-chemistry.hint: They are both liquids with different but fairly close boiling points.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Fractional distillation. Because the boiling points are different but relatively close (22 °C apart), a fractionating column is needed to achieve good separation — the more volatile ethanol is enriched at the top of the column and collected first.
grade9-chemistry.answer: fractional distillation

grade9-chemistry.question:
Use the reactivity series (K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Hg > Ag > Au) to answer the following questions.
Predict the products and write a balanced equation for: Mg(s) + 2AgNO₃(aq) → ?
grade9-chemistry.hint: Mg > Ag in reactivity; Mg²⁺ will form.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Mg + 2AgNO₃ → Mg(NO₃)₂ + 2Ag. Magnesium displaces silver: Mg gives 2 electrons to 2 Ag⁺ ions, forming Mg²⁺ and 2 Ag atoms. Silvery solid (Ag) deposits on the magnesium; the solution becomes colourless as Ag⁺ is removed.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Mg + 2AgNO₃ → Mg(NO₃)₂ + 2Ag

grade9-chemistry.question:
A student investigates the combustion of different fuels.
Write the balanced equation for the complete combustion of butane, C₄H₁₀.
grade9-chemistry.hint: Balance C, then H, then O. Oxygen is always the last to balance.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: 2C₄H₁₀ + 13O₂ → 8CO₂ + 10H₂O. C: 8 on each side; H: 20 on each side; O: 26 on each side (from 13O₂). Note: multiplying through by 2 avoids fractions.
grade9-chemistry.answer: 2C₄H₁₀ + 13O₂ → 8CO₂ + 10H₂O

grade9-chemistry.question:
A student titrates 25.0 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution of unknown concentration with 0.10 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid. The mean titre is 22.4 cm³.
Write the balanced equation for the reaction between HCl and NaOH.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O.
grade9-chemistry.answer: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O

grade9-chemistry.question: A student titrates 25.0 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution of unknown concentration with 0.10 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid. The mean titre is 22.4 cm³. Calculate the number of moles of HCl used in the titration. (answer in mol)
grade9-chemistry.hint: n = c × V (remember to convert cm³ to dm³).

grade9-chemistry.question: A student titrates 25.0 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution of unknown concentration with 0.10 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid. The mean titre is 22.4 cm³. Using your answer to part (b), calculate the concentration of the NaOH solution. Show your working. (answer in mol/dm³)
grade9-chemistry.hint: Moles of NaOH = moles of HCl (1:1 ratio). Then c = n/V.

grade9-chemistry.question:
A student titrates 25.0 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution of unknown concentration with 0.10 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid. The mean titre is 22.4 cm³.
The student uses phenolphthalein indicator. State the colour change at the end point when acid is added to alkali.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Pink to colourless (at the point of neutralisation, when the last drop of acid decolorises the solution permanently).
grade9-chemistry.answer: pink to colourless

Use the table to deduce the order of reactivity of the five metals (most reactive first).
grade9-chemistry.hint: Compare the vigour and conditions needed.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Sodium > Calcium > Magnesium > Iron > Copper. Sodium reacts with cold water most vigorously; copper does not react with water or steam at all.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Na > Ca > Mg > Fe > Cu

grade9-chemistry.answer: 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂

grade9-chemistry.question: Work out the formula of magnesium nitrate given that Mg has valency 2 and NO₃ has valency 1.
grade9-chemistry.hint: Cross the valencies: Mg²⁺ needs two NO₃⁻ ions.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Mg²⁺ and NO₃⁻ (valency 1): two nitrate ions balance one Mg²⁺ ion. Formula: Mg(NO₃)₂.
grade9-chemistry.answer: Mg(NO₃)₂

grade9-chemistry.question: How many atoms are in one formula unit of Mg(NO₃)₂? (answer in atoms)
grade9-chemistry.hint: Expand the bracket first.
grade9-chemistry.explanation: 1 Mg + 2 N + 6 O = 9 atoms.

grade9-chemistry.question: Write a word equation for the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate.
grade9-chemistry.hint: What two products are formed when CaCO₃ is heated strongly?
grade9-chemistry.explanation: Calcium carbonate → calcium oxide + carbon dioxide. (CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂)
grade9-chemistry.answer: calcium carbonate → calcium oxide + carbon dioxide
acceptableAnswers: calcium carbonate → calcium oxide + carbon dioxide

grade9-chemistry.explanation: Sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄). (Also accept sulfurous acid H₂SO₃ as an intermediate.)

grade9-chemistry.answer: flue-gas desulfurisation

grade9-english.question: Jane is the _____________ girl in her class.
grade9-english.explanation: Superlative of tall uses -est: tallest.

grade9-english.question: There is not _____________ milk left in the fridge.
grade9-english.explanation: "Much" is used with uncountable nouns like milk.

grade9-english.question: Sahil is the _____________ boy on the football team.
grade9-english.explanation: One-syllable adjectives form the superlative with -est.

grade9-english.question: There is too _____________ sugar in this tea.
grade9-english.explanation: "Much" modifies uncountable nouns; sugar is uncountable.

grade9-english.question: Kevin and his brother make their bed _____________.
grade9-english.explanation: "They" (Kevin and his brother) → reflexive is "themselves".

grade9-english.question: Sarah and her friend cleaned their room _____________.
grade9-english.explanation: Two people (they) → reflexive pronoun is "themselves".

grade9-english.question: The book _____________ I borrowed from the library is very interesting.
grade9-english.explanation: "Which" introduces a relative clause referring to a thing (book).

grade9-english.question: We stayed _____________ my uncle's place during the holidays.
grade9-english.explanation: "Stay at" a place — at is used for specific locations.

grade9-english.question: The film will start _____________ half an hour.
grade9-english.explanation: "In" expresses a future period of time: in half an hour.

grade9-english.question: We went _____________ the park for a picnic on Sunday.
grade9-english.explanation: "Go to" a place — "to" expresses direction or destination.

grade9-english.question: The train will arrive _____________ ten minutes.
grade9-english.explanation: "In ten minutes" — "in" is used for future durations.

grade9-english.question: Yesterday, my cousins _____________ to visit me after school.
grade9-english.explanation: "Yesterday" signals simple past tense.

grade9-english.question: Devika _____________ to visit me tomorrow morning.
grade9-english.explanation: "Tomorrow" signals simple future; will + base verb.

grade9-english.question: If I eat fruits and vegetables every day, I _____________ healthy.
grade9-english.explanation: First conditional (real/possible): if + present → will + base verb.

grade9-english.question: If I study hard, I _____________ pass the examination.
grade9-english.explanation: First conditional with a real future outcome uses "will".

grade9-english.question: Which is the correct passive form of: "The teacher praised the students"?
options: The students have praised the teacher.
The students were praised by the teacher.
The students are praised by the teacher.
The students had been praised by the teacher.
grade9-english.answer: The students were praised by the teacher.
acceptableAnswers: The students were praised by the teacher.
grade9-english.explanation: Simple past passive: subject + was/were + past participle + by + agent.

grade9-english.question: Which is the correct passive form of: "Riva left a bag on the train"?
options: A bag had left on the train by Riva.
A bag left by Riva on the train.
A bag is left by Riva on the train.
A bag was left by Riva on the train.
grade9-english.answer: A bag was left by Riva on the train.
acceptableAnswers: A bag was left by Riva on the train.
grade9-english.explanation: Past passive: object becomes subject + was + past participle.

grade9-english.question: Choose the correct direct speech for: "The teacher asked us if we were hungry."
grade9-english.explanation: Indirect "if we were hungry" → direct "Are you hungry?" (present tense, second person).

grade9-english.question: Choose the correct indirect speech for: "Did you see the accident?" the policeman asked him.
options: The policeman asked him did he see the accident.
The policeman asked him if he had seen the accident.
The policeman asked him if you had seen the accident.
The policeman asked him if he saw the accident.
grade9-english.answer: The policeman asked him if he had seen the accident.
acceptableAnswers: The policeman asked him if he had seen the accident.
grade9-english.explanation: Questions in indirect speech use "if/whether" and backshift tenses: did see → had seen.

grade9-english.question: Which version correctly punctuates the list: "Tim bought three apples two oranges and one kiwi"?
options: Tim bought three apples, two oranges and one kiwi.
Tim bought three apples; two oranges; and one kiwi.
Tim bought three apples two oranges, and one kiwi.
Tim bought, three apples, two oranges, and one kiwi.
grade9-english.answer: Tim bought three apples, two oranges and one kiwi.
acceptableAnswers: Tim bought three apples, two oranges and one kiwi.
grade9-english.explanation: Commas separate items in a list; no comma before the final "and".

grade9-english.question: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
grade9-english.explanation: Names (Mary) and proper nouns (England — a country) begin with a capital letter.

grade9-english.question: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
options: Anne went out with her friends on thursday.
anne went out with her friends on Thursday.
anne went out with her Friends on Thursday.
Anne went out with her friends on Thursday.
grade9-english.answer: Anne went out with her friends on Thursday.
acceptableAnswers: Anne went out with her friends on Thursday.
grade9-english.explanation: Names and days of the week (Thursday) are proper nouns — they start with a capital.

grade9-english.question: His bag is too _____________. He cannot carry it alone.
grade9-english.explanation: "Heavy" describes the weight of the bag, which is why it cannot be carried alone.

grade9-english.question: There's a wedding in my family. I need to buy some _____________ clothes.
grade9-english.explanation: A wedding is a formal occasion, so buying new clothes is appropriate.

grade9-english.question: I am very _____________. My father is ill.
grade9-english.explanation: A sick parent causes anxiety; "worried" fits this emotional context.

grade9-english.question: James has been _____________ permission to go home early.
grade9-english.explanation: "Given permission" is the correct collocation — you give or grant permission.

grade9-english.question: It is very _____________ today. Make sure you wear warm clothes.
grade9-english.explanation: Wearing warm clothes is a response to cold weather.

grade9-english.question: The students _____________ that the school was dirty and needed cleaning.
grade9-english.explanation: "Complained" means to express dissatisfaction — appropriate here.

grade9-english.question: I'm _____________. I will do well in my test. I have revised well.
grade9-english.explanation: Having revised well leads to confidence about performance.

grade9-english.question: The _____________ in this orchestra are all very young but exceptionally talented.
grade9-english.explanation: An orchestra is made up of musicians who play instruments.

grade9-english.question: Choose the correct adverb form of "usual": She is _____________ late for class.
grade9-english.explanation: Adverbs are formed by adding -ly to adjectives: usual → usually.

grade9-english.question: Choose the correct adjective form of "health": Eating vegetables keeps you _____________.
grade9-english.explanation: The adjective is formed by adding -y to the noun: health → healthy.

grade9-english.question: The correct simple past tense of the irregular verb "fly" is:
grade9-english.explanation: "Fly" is irregular: fly → flew → flown. "Flied" is a common error.

grade9-english.question: The correct past participle of "eat" in the sentence "The food had been _____________ before we arrived" is:
grade9-english.explanation: "Eat" is irregular: eat → ate → eaten. Past participle is "eaten".

grade9-english.question: Choose the correct noun form of "originate": Scientists studied the _____________ of the disease.
grade9-english.explanation: The root noun is "origin"; "origination" also works but "origin" is simpler and more natural here.

grade9-english.question: Which word is formed correctly using the prefix meaning "not"?
grade9-english.explanation: The prefix "un-" added to "happy" gives "unhappy" — meaning not happy.

grade9-english.question: Read the line: "The wind howled through the empty streets." What figurative device is used?
grade9-english.explanation: Personification gives a non-human thing (wind) a human action (howling).

grade9-english.question: Which of the following is an example of a simile?
options: The flowers danced in the breeze.
grade9-english.explanation: A simile makes a comparison using "like" or "as".

grade9-english.question: What is the main effect of personification in the line: "The old house groaned under the weight of its secrets"?
options: It compares the house directly to a person.
It tells us the house is very noisy.
It makes the house seem alive and mysterious.
It explains why the house is old.
grade9-english.answer: It makes the house seem alive and mysterious.
acceptableAnswers: It makes the house seem alive and mysterious.
grade9-english.explanation: Personification creates atmosphere by giving the house human qualities — making it feel living and eerie.

grade9-english.question: In a first-person narrative, the story is told using which pronouns?
grade9-english.explanation: First-person narrators refer to themselves as "I" (singular) or "we" (plural).

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct preposition to complete the sentence.

"The ambassador arrived _____ Mauritius last Monday after a long flight from Geneva."
grade9-english.hint: We use this preposition with countries and large places.
grade9-english.explanation: "Arrive in" is used with countries, cities, and large places. "Arrive at" is used with specific buildings or small locations (e.g., the airport). You arrive in Mauritius but at the hotel.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct preposition to complete the sentence.

"She was praised _____ her outstanding performance in the NCE examinations."
grade9-english.hint: Think about the idiom "praised for (a reason)".
grade9-english.explanation: "Praised for" is the correct collocation. You praise someone FOR a reason or achievement. "Praised by" indicates the agent doing the praising, not the reason.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct preposition to complete the sentence.

"The bridge collapsed _____ the weight of the overloaded lorries that crossed it daily."
grade9-english.hint: Think about what preposition follows "collapsed" when the cause is a heavy load.
grade9-english.explanation: "Collapse under the weight" is the standard idiom. "Under" here conveys the sense of being unable to bear the pressure from above.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct preposition to complete the sentence.

"All members of staff must comply _____ the revised health and safety regulations immediately."
grade9-english.hint: The verb "comply" is always followed by a specific preposition.
grade9-english.explanation: "Comply with" is the fixed collocation. One complies WITH a rule, regulation, or request — not to, by, or for it.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct preposition to complete the sentence.

"The teacher insisted _____ punctuality and would not accept any excuse for lateness."
grade9-english.hint: The verb "insist" is followed by a specific preposition when expressing a strong requirement.
grade9-english.explanation: "Insist on" is the correct collocation when expressing that something is required or demanded. "Insist on punctuality" = demand punctuality as a requirement.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the phrasal verb that best completes the sentence.

"After months of disagreement, the two neighbouring countries finally agreed to _____ their differences and cooperate on trade."
grade9-english.hint: Which phrasal verb means to ignore or stop allowing something to affect you?
grade9-english.explanation: "Put aside" means to ignore or temporarily set something aside so it does not hinder progress. "Put off" = delay; "put down" = suppress or criticise; "put out" = extinguish or inconvenience.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the phrasal verb that best completes the sentence.

"A thorough investigation into the financial fraud was _____ by a team of senior detectives."
grade9-english.hint: Which phrasal verb means to perform or execute a task?
grade9-english.explanation: "Carry out" means to perform or execute something, especially a task or investigation. "Carry on" = continue; "carry away" = lose control of oneself; "carry off" = succeed at something difficult.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the phrasal verb that best completes the sentence.

"The factory was forced to _____ production entirely after a fire destroyed the main assembly hall."
grade9-english.hint: Which phrasal verb means to stop operating completely?
grade9-english.explanation: "Shut down" means to cease operations completely, especially of a machine, factory, or system. "Shut out" = exclude; "shut up" = stop talking (informal); "shut off" = cut the supply of something such as water or electricity.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct reflexive pronoun to complete the sentence.

"The students built the entire outdoor stage _____ without hiring any contractors."
grade9-english.hint: The subject is "the students" — which form of reflexive pronoun agrees with a plural third-person subject?
grade9-english.explanation: "Themselves" is the reflexive pronoun for a plural third-person subject. "Their own" is a possessive determiner. "Each other" and "one another" are reciprocal pronouns, implying two people doing something to each other.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct reflexive pronoun to complete the sentence.

"After the earthquake, many families had to provide for _____ because emergency aid was slow to arrive."
grade9-english.hint: The action (providing) is directed back at the subject (the families).
grade9-english.explanation: "Themselves" is correct because the action reflects back onto the subject. "Provide for themselves" means the families provided for themselves — subject and object are the same people.

grade9-english.question: Identify the sentence that uses an emphasising pronoun correctly.
options: Himself, the president signed the declaration before the cameras.
The president signed the declaration himself, and it was himself who drafted it.
The president himself signed the peace declaration, lending it historic weight.
The president signed the declaration by himself to emphasise his authority.
grade9-english.answer: The president himself signed the peace declaration, lending it historic weight.
acceptableAnswers: The president himself signed the peace declaration, lending it historic weight.
grade9-english.hint: An emphasising pronoun can be removed without changing the core meaning. Which option uses "himself" purely for emphasis, placed immediately after the noun it emphasises?
grade9-english.explanation: In the correct sentence, "himself" is an emphasising pronoun placed directly after "president" for emphasis — it can be removed without altering the meaning. Option B repeats the pronoun awkwardly. Option C places the pronoun at the front, which is non-standard. Option D uses "by himself" which means "alone", not emphasis.

grade9-english.question: Choose the sentence in which the underlined word functions as an emphasising pronoun (not a reflexive pronoun).
options: They introduced <u>themselves</u> to the new teacher at the start of term.
He locked <u>himself</u> out of the house by accident.
Even the critics <u>themselves</u> were moved to tears by the final performance.
She hurt <u>herself</u> badly when she slipped on the wet floor.
grade9-english.answer: Even the critics <u>themselves</u> were moved to tears by the final performance.
acceptableAnswers: Even the critics <u>themselves</u> were moved to tears by the final performance.
grade9-english.hint: An emphasising pronoun is used for emphasis only and can be omitted. A reflexive pronoun is required because the subject and object are the same person.
grade9-english.explanation: In the correct sentence, "themselves" emphasises "critics" but is not required grammatically — you can say "Even the critics were moved to tears" with no change in meaning. In the other sentences, the pronoun is reflexive and grammatically required.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct relative pronoun to complete the sentence.

"The scientist _____ research won the Nobel Prize was born in a small village in Rodrigues."
grade9-english.hint: The pronoun must show possession (the research belongs to the scientist).
grade9-english.explanation: "Whose" is the possessive relative pronoun, used when the relative clause describes something belonging to the antecedent. "The scientist whose research…" = the research belongs to the scientist.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct relative pronoun to complete the sentence.

"She was the only candidate _____ had submitted a complete portfolio before the closing date."
grade9-english.hint: The relative pronoun refers to a person and functions as the subject of the clause.
grade9-english.explanation: "Who" is used when the antecedent is a person and the pronoun is the subject of the relative clause. "Which" refers to things. "Whose" is possessive. "Whom" is used when the pronoun is the object.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct determiner to complete the sentence.

"_____ information you provided was extremely helpful to the investigation."
grade9-english.hint: The speaker is referring to specific information that was already provided.
grade9-english.explanation: "The" is used for specific, identifiable information — information already known to both speaker and listener. "A" is for indefinite singular countable nouns. "Some" and "any" are used for unspecified amounts and do not suit this context.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct determiner to complete the sentence.

"She has _____ patience for people who consistently arrive late to important meetings."
grade9-english.hint: "Patience" is uncountable. Which determiner conveys a negative sense (not much)?
grade9-english.explanation: "Little" (without "a") is used with uncountable nouns to express a negative quantity — almost none. "A little" means some (positive). "Few" and "a few" are used with countable plurals, not uncountable nouns like "patience".

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct determiner to complete the sentence.

"He read _____ the articles in the scientific journal before making his final recommendation."
grade9-english.hint: The noun "articles" is plural. Which determiner works with "the articles"?
grade9-english.explanation: "All the articles" is correct — "all" can precede a definite article and a plural noun. "Every article" and "each article" require the singular form. "Whole" cannot precede "the articles" in this construction.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct determiner to complete the sentence.

"Despite applying for scholarships, _____ of the two students received any funding."
grade9-english.hint: "Neither" is specifically used when referring to exactly two people or things.
grade9-english.explanation: "Neither" is used when referring to two people or things and means "not one and not the other". "None" is used for three or more. "Both" would mean both received funding, contradicting the context.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct determiner to complete the sentence.

"The committee reviewed _____ proposal individually before casting their final votes."
grade9-english.hint: The sentence emphasises individual consideration of each proposal one by one.
grade9-english.explanation: "Each" emphasises individual consideration within a group, one at a time. "Every" is similar but less emphatic. "All" would require the plural "proposals". "Both" implies exactly two.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct determiner to complete the sentence.

"The teacher gave the class _____ extra time to finish the examination paper."
grade9-english.hint: "Time" is uncountable. Which option means "some" (a positive, small amount)?
grade9-english.explanation: "A little extra time" means some small amount of extra time — positive and helpful. "Little" (without "a") would mean almost none, implying the teacher was unhelpful. "A few" and "few" are for countable plural nouns.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the attitude adverb that best reflects the speaker's viewpoint in the sentence.

"The surgery lasted over twelve hours; _____, the patient made a full recovery within a week."
grade9-english.hint: The outcome (full recovery) is positive. Which adverb expresses the speaker's relief about a positive outcome?
grade9-english.explanation: "Fortunately" expresses the speaker's relief or pleasure that a good outcome occurred. "Unfortunately" would contradict the positive result. "Consequently" is a logical connector, not an attitude adverb. "Remarkably" could work but "fortunately" more directly signals the speaker's attitude.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the attitude adverb that best completes the sentence.

"She had worked tirelessly on the project for six months. _____, her contribution was not acknowledged in the final report."
grade9-english.hint: The speaker is expressing sorrow or disappointment about an unfair situation.
grade9-english.explanation: "Regrettably" signals that the speaker finds the situation unfortunate or unfair — it expresses the speaker's attitude of sorrow or disapproval. "Fortunately" would be inappropriate (the outcome is negative). "Naturally" and "Consequently" are not attitude adverbs expressing emotion.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the attitude adverb that best completes the sentence.

"_____, the local authorities had been aware of the flood risk for several years before the disaster struck."
grade9-english.hint: The speaker is reporting what seems to be true based on available evidence, without claiming certainty.
grade9-english.explanation: "Apparently" signals that the speaker is presenting information based on evidence or reports, not first-hand knowledge. "Hopefully" expresses a wish. "Admittedly" concedes a point. "Clearly" claims certainty — but the context implies inference from evidence, not direct knowledge.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the attitude adverb that best completes the sentence.

"The committee voted to postpone the annual exhibition. _____, many volunteers had already committed weeks of preparation time."
grade9-english.hint: The speaker is expressing how the decision felt to those who had worked hard.
grade9-english.explanation: "Disappointingly" conveys the speaker's attitude that the outcome is a letdown, particularly for the volunteers. "Surprisingly" might fit if the postponement was unexpected, but does not capture the emotional impact on the volunteers. "Luckily" is positive and inappropriate here. "Presumably" indicates assumption, not attitude.

grade9-english.question: Which sentence demonstrates correct tense consistency?
options: While she presents her report to the board, a fire alarm went off.
While she was presenting her report to the board, a fire alarm went off.
While she presented her report to the board, a fire alarm goes off.
While she was presenting her report to the board, a fire alarm goes off.
grade9-english.answer: While she was presenting her report to the board, a fire alarm went off.
acceptableAnswers: While she was presenting her report to the board, a fire alarm went off.
grade9-english.hint: The background action (presenting) and the sudden event (alarm) should both be in a consistent past tense.
grade9-english.explanation: The past continuous ("was presenting") describes the background action in progress, and the simple past ("went off") describes the sudden interruption. Both tenses are in the past and work together logically.

grade9-english.question: Which sentence demonstrates correct tense consistency?
options: By the time the ambulance arrived, the patient already lost consciousness.
By the time the ambulance arrives, the patient had already lost consciousness.
By the time the ambulance arrived, the patient had already lost consciousness.
By the time the ambulance had arrived, the patient already lost consciousness.
grade9-english.answer: By the time the ambulance arrived, the patient had already lost consciousness.
acceptableAnswers: By the time the ambulance arrived, the patient had already lost consciousness.
grade9-english.hint: "By the time" + simple past requires past perfect in the other clause to show which event happened first.
grade9-english.explanation: "By the time" + simple past ("arrived") sets the reference point, and the past perfect ("had already lost") shows the earlier completed action. Mixing present and past tenses in this structure is incorrect.

grade9-english.question: Which sentence demonstrates correct tense consistency throughout?
options: She realised she has made a terrible mistake when the door closed behind her.
She realised she had made a terrible mistake when the door closed behind her.
She realised she was making a terrible mistake when the door will close behind her.
She realises she had made a terrible mistake when the door closed behind her.
grade9-english.answer: She realised she had made a terrible mistake when the door closed behind her.
acceptableAnswers: She realised she had made a terrible mistake when the door closed behind her.
grade9-english.hint: The main verb is in the simple past. What tense is needed in the subordinate clause to show an earlier completed action?
grade9-english.explanation: "Realised" (simple past) is the main verb. The mistake happened before the realisation, so the past perfect ("had made") is correct. "Closed" (simple past) correctly describes the simultaneous event.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.

"By this time next year, the construction company _____ the new motorway linking the north and south of the island."
grade9-english.hint: The phrase "by this time next year" signals a future point by which an action will be finished.
grade9-english.explanation: The future perfect ("will have completed") is used for an action that will be finished before a specific point in the future. "Will complete" is simple future (does not emphasise completion). "Are going to complete" is future intention. "Would have completed" is conditional perfect.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.

"The research team hopes that, by 2030, they _____ an effective vaccine for the tropical disease."
grade9-english.hint: "By 2030" marks a future deadline. Which tense expresses completion before that deadline?
grade9-english.explanation: The future perfect ("will have developed") expresses an action that the team hopes to complete before the future deadline of 2030. "Will develop" does not emphasise completion by a deadline. "Would have developed" is a conditional. "Have developed" is present perfect.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.

"By the time you read this letter, I _____ the country and started a new life abroad."
grade9-english.hint: The action of leaving will be completed before the future moment of reading.
grade9-english.explanation: The future perfect ("will have left") describes an action that will be completed before a specific future moment — the moment the letter is read. "Will leave" is simple future. "Would have left" is conditional perfect. "Am leaving" is present continuous.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.

"By the end of this semester, she _____ at this institution for exactly three years."
grade9-english.hint: The sentence emphasises the ongoing duration of an activity up to a future point.
grade9-english.explanation: The future perfect continuous ("will have been studying") emphasises the duration of a continuous activity leading up to a future moment. "Will have studied" (future perfect) focuses on completion, not duration. "Will be studying" is future continuous with no emphasis on duration to that point.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.

"Next month, the medical researchers _____ on this clinical trial for two years without interruption."
grade9-english.hint: The phrase "for two years" signals duration leading up to the future point "next month".
grade9-english.explanation: The future perfect continuous ("will have been working") emphasises the continuous duration (two years) of an activity up to a specific future point (next month). "Will have worked" states completion without emphasising the ongoing process.

grade9-english.question:
The following sentence is in the active voice:

"The government has introduced a series of measures to combat climate change."

Which passive transformation is grammatically correct?
options: A series of measures to combat climate change is being introduced by the government.
A series of measures to combat climate change have been introduced by the government.
A series of measures to combat climate change has been introduced by the government.
A series of measures to combat climate change was introduced by the government.
grade9-english.answer: A series of measures to combat climate change has been introduced by the government.
acceptableAnswers: A series of measures to combat climate change has been introduced by the government.
grade9-english.hint: The tense is present perfect ("has introduced"). The subject of the passive is "a series of measures" — singular.
grade9-english.explanation: "A series of measures" is a singular noun phrase, so the passive requires "has been introduced" (present perfect passive, singular). "Have been introduced" is plural. "Was introduced" is simple past. "Is being introduced" is present continuous passive.

grade9-english.question:
The following sentence is in the active voice:

"Scientists are currently studying the long-term effects of microplastics on marine life."

Which passive transformation is grammatically correct?
options: The long-term effects of microplastics on marine life are currently studied by scientists.
The long-term effects of microplastics on marine life were currently being studied by scientists.
The long-term effects of microplastics on marine life are currently being studied by scientists.
The long-term effects of microplastics on marine life have currently been studied by scientists.
grade9-english.answer: The long-term effects of microplastics on marine life are currently being studied by scientists.
acceptableAnswers: The long-term effects of microplastics on marine life are currently being studied by scientists.
grade9-english.hint: The active sentence uses present continuous ("are studying"). What is the present continuous passive?
grade9-english.explanation: The present continuous passive is "are being studied". "Are studied" is the simple present passive. "Were being studied" is past continuous passive. "Have been studied" is present perfect passive — none of these match the present continuous active.

grade9-english.question:
The teacher said, "You must submit your essays by Friday."

Which reported speech transformation is correct?
options: The teacher said that you must submit your essays by Friday.
The teacher said that they must submit their essays by Friday.
The teacher said that they will have to submit their essays by Friday.
The teacher said that they had to submit their essays by Friday.
grade9-english.answer: The teacher said that they had to submit their essays by Friday.
acceptableAnswers: The teacher said that they had to submit their essays by Friday.
grade9-english.hint: In reported speech, "must" (obligation) changes to "had to", and pronouns shift from second to third person.
grade9-english.explanation: "Must" shifts to "had to" in reported speech (past reporting verb). "You" shifts to "they" (third person). "Your" shifts to "their". Keeping "must" unchanged is only valid if the obligation still applies at the time of reporting — in a past reporting context, "had to" is standard.

grade9-english.question:
"Have you ever visited the Blue Bay Marine Park?" she asked him.

Which reported speech transformation is correct?
options: She asked him whether he had ever visited the Blue Bay Marine Park.
She asked him whether has he ever visited the Blue Bay Marine Park.
She asked him if he has ever visited the Blue Bay Marine Park.
She asked him had he ever visited the Blue Bay Marine Park.
grade9-english.answer: She asked him whether he had ever visited the Blue Bay Marine Park.
acceptableAnswers: She asked him whether he had ever visited the Blue Bay Marine Park.
grade9-english.hint: Yes/no questions in reported speech use "if" or "whether" + subject + verb (no inversion), with tense backshift.
grade9-english.explanation: Questions in reported speech use "whether" or "if" followed by subject + verb in normal order (no inversion). "Have" backshifts to "had". The reported clause must not use question word order ("had he visited" or "has he visited" would be wrong).

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct verb form to complete the perfect conditional sentence.

"If the engineers _____ the structural fault earlier, the collapse would not have occurred."
grade9-english.hint: This is a Type 3 conditional (past unreal). What tense is used in the "if" clause of a Type 3 conditional?
grade9-english.explanation: In a Type 3 (past hypothetical) conditional, the "if" clause uses the past perfect ("had identified") and the main clause uses "would have + past participle". Using "would have" in the "if" clause is incorrect in standard English.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the correct verb form to complete the perfect conditional sentence.

"She would have achieved far better results if she _____ more seriously during the academic year."
grade9-english.hint: The main clause ("would have achieved") tells you this is a Type 3 conditional. What form goes in the "if" clause?
grade9-english.explanation: The main clause uses "would have achieved" — a Type 3 (past unreal) conditional. The "if" clause requires the past perfect ("had studied"). Using "studied" alone would create a Type 2 (present unreal) conditional, which contradicts the main clause.

grade9-english.question: Which sentence uses commas correctly to set off a non-defining relative clause?
options: Mount Pieter Both which, is the second highest peak in Mauritius, attracts thousands of hikers each year.
Mount Pieter Both, which is the second highest peak in Mauritius, attracts thousands of hikers each year.
Mount Pieter Both, which is the second highest peak in Mauritius attracts thousands of hikers each year.
Mount Pieter Both which is the second highest peak in Mauritius attracts thousands of hikers each year.
grade9-english.answer: Mount Pieter Both, which is the second highest peak in Mauritius, attracts thousands of hikers each year.
acceptableAnswers: Mount Pieter Both, which is the second highest peak in Mauritius, attracts thousands of hikers each year.
grade9-english.hint: A non-defining relative clause adds extra, non-essential information and must be enclosed in commas.
grade9-english.explanation: A non-defining relative clause — one that adds extra information but is not needed to identify the noun — must be enclosed by commas on both sides. The clause "which is the second highest peak in Mauritius" is non-essential (the mountain is already named) and must be separated by commas.

grade9-english.question: Which option correctly punctuates the following direct speech?
options: "I have never seen such dedication in a student," said the professor.
"I have never seen such dedication in a student", said the professor.
"I have never seen such dedication in a student." said the professor.
"I have never seen such dedication in a student" said the professor.
grade9-english.answer: "I have never seen such dedication in a student," said the professor.
acceptableAnswers: "I have never seen such dedication in a student," said the professor.
grade9-english.hint: The comma separating speech from the reporting clause should be inside the closing quotation mark.
grade9-english.explanation: When a reporting clause follows a quotation, the comma goes inside the closing quotation mark, not after it. A full stop inside the quotation mark followed by "said" (option D) is incorrect because the sentence continues.

grade9-english.question: Which sentence uses the dash correctly to indicate a sudden break or interruption in thought?
options: She was about to reveal the name of the informant: then the lights went out.
She was about to reveal the name of the informant — then the lights went out.
She was about to reveal the name of the informant, then the lights went out.
She was about to reveal the name of the informant; then the lights went out.
grade9-english.answer: She was about to reveal the name of the informant — then the lights went out.
acceptableAnswers: She was about to reveal the name of the informant — then the lights went out.
grade9-english.hint: A dash creates a dramatic pause or signals an abrupt change. Which punctuation mark here best captures the sudden interruption?
grade9-english.explanation: The em dash is used to create a dramatic pause or signal an abrupt break in thought. The comma (option B) is too weak for the dramatic effect. The colon (option C) introduces an explanation or list. The semicolon (option D) links independent clauses without the abruptness a dash conveys.

grade9-english.question: Which sentence uses the semicolon correctly?
options: The coastal villages were evacuated promptly; nevertheless, several homes were still damaged by the storm surge.
The coastal villages were evacuated promptly; several homes were damaged; by the storm surge.
The coastal villages were evacuated promptly, nevertheless; several homes were damaged by the storm surge.
The coastal villages were evacuated promptly: nevertheless, several homes were damaged by the storm surge.
grade9-english.answer: The coastal villages were evacuated promptly; nevertheless, several homes were still damaged by the storm surge.
acceptableAnswers: The coastal villages were evacuated promptly; nevertheless, several homes were still damaged by the storm surge.
grade9-english.hint: A semicolon can link two independent clauses, especially when followed by a transitional adverb like "nevertheless".
grade9-english.explanation: A semicolon before "nevertheless" correctly links two independent clauses with a contrasting relationship. Option B misuses the semicolon mid-phrase. Option C places the comma after "nevertheless" in the wrong position. Option D uses a colon, which introduces a list or explanation rather than a contrast.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the verb that collocates most naturally with the noun to complete the sentence.

"The minister _____ a press conference to address public concerns about the proposed legislation."
grade9-english.hint: Think about the standard verb-noun pairing for organising and conducting a press conference.
grade9-english.explanation: "Hold a press conference" is the standard collocation. While "give" and "make" are used with some nouns (give a speech, make a statement), the fixed pairing for press conferences is "hold".

grade9-english.question:
Choose the verb that collocates most naturally with the noun to complete the sentence.

"After decades of painstaking research, the team finally _____ a breakthrough in the treatment of the disease."
grade9-english.hint: The fixed phrase for a scientific advance uses a specific verb.
grade9-english.explanation: "Make a breakthrough" is the standard collocation in English. "Achieve a breakthrough" is increasingly common but less idiomatic. "Reach" and "find" do not collocate with "breakthrough".

grade9-english.question:
Choose the verb that collocates most naturally with the noun phrase to complete the sentence.

"The new environmental law will _____ effect from the first of January next year."
grade9-english.hint: There is a fixed three-word expression used when a law or policy becomes active.
grade9-english.explanation: "Come into effect" is the standard phrase meaning to become active or enforceable. "Take effect" is also used but "take into effect" is not. "Go into effect" is used in American English but less standard. "Put into effect" means to implement, not to become active.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the verb that collocates most naturally with the noun phrase to complete the sentence.

"The safety committee agreed to _____ stringent measures to prevent further industrial accidents."
grade9-english.hint: Think about the standard verb used with "measures" when acting to prevent or address a problem.
grade9-english.explanation: "Take measures" is the standard collocation meaning to act in order to achieve a result. "Make measures" and "do measures" are incorrect. "Apply measures" is occasionally used but is less idiomatic than "take measures".

grade9-english.question:
Choose the word that most precisely fits the context.

"The politician's speech was full of _____ statements that meant one thing to some listeners and something quite different to others."
grade9-english.hint: Which word specifically means capable of being interpreted in more than one way?
grade9-english.explanation: "Ambiguous" precisely means having two or more possible meanings, which fits the context of deliberate double interpretation. "Vague" means lacking detail. "Obscure" means difficult to understand. "Indirect" means not straightforward in approach, but does not capture the double-meaning quality.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the word that most precisely fits the context.

"The ancient ruins were discovered _____ when construction workers were digging the foundations for a new shopping complex."
grade9-english.hint: Which word means "by accident" — without any intention or planning?
grade9-english.explanation: "Accidentally" means without intention — the workers did not plan to find the ruins. "Unexpectedly" focuses on the element of surprise, not the lack of intention. "Coincidentally" implies a chance overlap of separate events. "Incidentally" means as a secondary or unrelated point.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the word that most precisely fits the context.

"The professor spoke in such _____ language that even experienced colleagues found it difficult to follow her argument."
grade9-english.hint: Which word specifically implies that the language is unnecessarily twisted or difficult to follow — not just difficult?
grade9-english.explanation: "Convoluted" suggests language that is intricate and tortuous in an unnecessary way — the difficulty comes from poor expression, not from the subject matter. "Complicated" and "complex" simply mean not simple. "Technical" implies specialist vocabulary, not unnecessary complexity.

grade9-english.question:
Choose the word that most precisely fits the context.

"The author paused at the end of each chapter to allow her ideas to _____ with the reader before introducing the next argument."
grade9-english.hint: Which word suggests that the ideas have a deep, meaningful effect — like a note that continues to vibrate after being struck?
grade9-english.explanation: "Resonate" (from the Latin for echoing sound) implies that ideas have a lasting, meaningful effect on an audience. "Connect" is general. "Register" means to be noticed or understood. "Impact" is a noun used informally as a verb and does not carry the same quality of depth or reverberation.

grade9-english.question:
Read the following sentence:

"The archaeologist unearthed a trove of ancient artefacts at the excavation site near Grand Port."

The word trove most nearly means:
options: a small number of scattered items
grade9-english.hint: Think about the compound word "treasure trove" — what does "trove" contribute to that phrase?
grade9-english.explanation: "Trove" means a collection or store of valuable or pleasant things. It is most commonly seen in the phrase "treasure trove". It does not refer to a physical chamber or a formal record.

grade9-english.question:
Read the following sentence:

"The orator's eloquent address moved the delegates to a standing ovation."

The word eloquent most nearly means:
grade9-english.hint: Consider the effect described (a standing ovation). What quality of speech would produce such a response?
grade9-english.explanation: "Eloquent" describes speech or writing that is fluent, expressive, and persuasive. The standing ovation confirms the emotional and persuasive impact. "Formal" and "detached" contradict the emotional response. "Lengthy" and "brief" refer to length, not quality.

grade9-english.question:
Read the following sentence:

"The government's ambivalent stance on the referendum disappointed supporters on both sides of the debate."

The word ambivalent most nearly means:
options: highly influential in shaping others' opinions
strongly committed to one position above others
having mixed or conflicting feelings about something
reluctant to discuss the matter in public
grade9-english.answer: having mixed or conflicting feelings about something
acceptableAnswers: having mixed or conflicting feelings about something
grade9-english.hint: The prefix "ambi-" means "both". How does that help you understand the meaning?
grade9-english.explanation: "Ambivalent" derives from "ambi-" (both) + "valent" (having power/feeling) — it describes having simultaneous, conflicting feelings or attitudes towards something. The context ("disappointed both sides") confirms neither side felt the government was clearly on their side.

grade9-english.question:
Read the following sentence:

"The scientist's assertion that the compound was entirely safe was later proved to be erroneous."

The word erroneous most nearly means:
grade9-english.hint: Think about the root "error". What does this word share with "error"?
grade9-english.explanation: "Erroneous" means mistaken or incorrect — it shares the Latin root "error" (wandering, mistake). It does not imply deliberate dishonesty or intention to mislead. "Controversial" means causing disagreement, which is a separate concept.

grade9-english.question:
Which form of the word in brackets correctly completes the sentence?

"The _____ of the new hospital wing was celebrated by the entire community." (DEDICATE)
grade9-english.hint: A noun is needed to act as the subject of the sentence.
grade9-english.explanation: "Dedication" is the noun form of "dedicate", formed with the suffix "-tion". It means the act of dedicating or committing to something. "Dedicated" is an adjective or past participle. "Dedicating" is a verb form (gerund or present participle). "Dedicatedly" is an adverb.

grade9-english.question:
Which form of the word in brackets correctly completes the sentence?

"Her outstanding _____ as a marine biologist brought her international recognition." (ACHIEVE)
grade9-english.hint: The blank needs a noun meaning "a thing accomplished successfully".
grade9-english.explanation: "Achievement" is the noun formed from "achieve" with the suffix "-ment". It refers to a thing accomplished. "Achiever" is a person who achieves. "Achieving" is a verb form. "Achievable" is an adjective meaning possible to achieve.

grade9-english.question:
Which form of the word in brackets correctly completes the sentence?

"The minister gave a notably _____ response when asked directly about the missing funds." (EVASION)
grade9-english.hint: The blank follows an adverb ("notably") and must be an adjective describing the response.
grade9-english.explanation: "Evasive" is the adjective formed from "evasion" (the act of evading). It describes something or someone that deliberately avoids a direct answer. "Evasion" is a noun. "Evasively" is an adverb. "Evaded" is a past tense/past participle verb.

grade9-english.question:
Which form of the word in brackets correctly completes the sentence?

"It is considered _____ to attempt to climb the mountain without proper equipment or training." (HAZARD)
grade9-english.hint: The blank follows the verb "is" and a linking verb structure — an adjective is needed.
grade9-english.explanation: "Hazardous" is the adjective formed from "hazard" with the suffix "-ous", meaning full of danger or risk. "Hazard" is a noun or verb. "Hazardously" is an adverb. "Hazarding" is a verb form (gerund or present participle).

grade9-english.question:
Which form of the word in brackets correctly completes the sentence?

"The detective examined every detail of the crime scene _____, leaving nothing overlooked." (METHOD)
grade9-english.hint: The blank modifies a verb ("examined") — an adverb is needed.
grade9-english.explanation: "Methodically" is the adverb formed from "methodical" (adjective) → "-ally" suffix. It means in an orderly, systematic way and here modifies the verb "examined". "Methodical" is the adjective. "Method" is the noun. "Methodology" is a noun meaning a system of methods.

grade9-english.question:
Which form of the word in brackets correctly completes the sentence?

"The candidate responded _____ to every question during the panel interview." (CONFIDENCE)
grade9-english.hint: The blank modifies the verb "responded" — which form functions as an adverb?
grade9-english.explanation: "Confidently" is the adverb formed from "confident" (adjective) by adding "-ly". It modifies the verb "responded". "Confident" is the adjective. "Confidence" is the noun. "Confiding" means sharing secrets in trust — a different word entirely.

grade9-english.question:
Which form of the word in brackets correctly completes the sentence?

"The new legislation will _____ the way companies are required to report their environmental impact." (REVOLUTION)
grade9-english.hint: A verb is needed to complete the modal "will _____ the way".
grade9-english.explanation: "Revolutionise" is the verb formed from the noun "revolution" with the suffix "-ise". It means to change something dramatically. "Revolution" is a noun. "Revolutionary" is an adjective. "Revolving" means turning in a circle.

grade9-english.question:
Which form of the word in brackets correctly completes the sentence?

"The council voted to _____ the coastal road in preparation for increased tourist traffic." (WIDE)
grade9-english.hint: A verb in the base form is needed after "to" (infinitive).
grade9-english.explanation: "Widen" is the verb formed from the adjective "wide" by adding "-en". It means to make wider. "Wide" is the adjective. "Widely" is the adverb. "Widening" is the present participle or gerund form — not the base infinitive form needed after "to".

grade9-english.question: The word MONOTONOUS contains the prefix MONO-. Which word uses the prefix MONO- with the same meaning of "one" or "single"?
grade9-english.hint: Think about which word has one person, one language, or one speaker at its root.
grade9-english.explanation: "Monologue" = MONO- (one) + LOGUE (speech) — a speech by one person. "Monster" comes from Latin "monstrum" (warning sign) — no MONO- prefix. "Monument" comes from Latin "monumentum" (reminder). "Monopoly" does contain MONO- (one seller), so it is also correct — but "monologue" more transparently shows the prefix in its educational sense. Note: if "monopoly" is your choice, that is also a valid analysis.

grade9-english.question: Which word correctly uses the negative prefix ANTI- meaning "against" or "opposed to"?
grade9-english.hint: In which word does ANTI- mean "against" a concept or group?
grade9-english.explanation: "Antisocial" uses ANTI- (against) + social — meaning opposed to or harmful to social norms. "Anticipated" derives from Latin "anticipare" (to take before) — the "anti-" is part of the root, not a negative prefix. "Antiquated" and "antique" derive from Latin "antiquus" (old) — no negative prefix is present.

grade9-english.question:
Read the passage below and answer the question.

"The coral reefs surrounding Mauritius have provided coastal protection and sustained local fishing communities for centuries. Scientists now warn that rising sea temperatures have bleached over 30% of these reefs in the past decade. Once bleached, corals may recover if temperatures drop, but prolonged heat exposure kills them permanently. Without reefs, storm surges will strike the coast with far greater force. Local fishermen report declining catches, and the tourism industry — which contributes nearly 8% of GDP — faces an uncertain future."

According to the passage, what proportion of Mauritius's coral reefs have been bleached in the past decade?
grade9-english.hint: Look for the specific statistic given in the passage about reef bleaching.
grade9-english.explanation: The passage states directly: "rising sea temperatures have bleached over 30% of these reefs in the past decade." The 8% figure refers to the tourism industry's contribution to GDP, not reef bleaching.

grade9-english.question: Using the coral reef passage (see question 065), what can be inferred about the relationship between the health of the reefs and coastal communities?
options: Tourism is the leading cause of coral reef bleaching in Mauritius.
The tourism industry is currently unaffected by changes to the reef ecosystem.
The government has invested tourism revenue in a reef restoration programme.
The welfare of coastal communities depends on reef survival in multiple ways.
grade9-english.answer: The welfare of coastal communities depends on reef survival in multiple ways.
acceptableAnswers: The welfare of coastal communities depends on reef survival in multiple ways.
grade9-english.hint: The passage mentions several different groups that rely on the reefs. What can you infer from the combination of these details?
grade9-english.explanation: The passage links reef health to coastal protection (storm surges), fishing livelihoods (declining catches), and the tourism industry (economic contribution). Together, these imply that coastal communities depend on the reefs in multiple interconnected ways — this is an inference, not a directly stated conclusion.

grade9-english.question: In the coral reef passage (see question 065), the word sustained is used in the phrase "sustained local fishing communities for centuries". In this context, sustained most nearly means:
options: fed directly on a daily basis
grade9-english.hint: Consider the word "centuries" — which definition fits with that timescale?
grade9-english.explanation: "Sustained" here means supported or maintained over time. The phrase "for centuries" confirms the long timescale. "Fed directly" is too narrow (reefs support communities economically, not only as a food source). "Recently" contradicts "centuries".

grade9-english.question: Which statement best describes the author's viewpoint as expressed in the coral reef passage (see question 065)?
options: The author presents only scientific data, without expressing any personal viewpoint.
The author is alarmed by the speed of reef decline and its wide-ranging consequences.
The author is primarily concerned with the economic impact on the tourism sector.
The author is optimistic that the reefs will recover once sea temperatures fall.
grade9-english.answer: The author is alarmed by the speed of reef decline and its wide-ranging consequences.
acceptableAnswers: The author is alarmed by the speed of reef decline and its wide-ranging consequences.
grade9-english.hint: Look at word choices like "warn", "kills permanently", and "uncertain future". What attitude do these suggest?
grade9-english.explanation: Words like "warn", "kills them permanently", and "uncertain future" signal urgency and concern. The passage covers ecological, social, and economic consequences, suggesting a comprehensive alarm rather than a narrow economic focus. The use of "warn" (scientists) and the passive tone do not imply optimism.
