options: They are automatically merged into a single file
They can be compared without switching between windows
grade9-ict.answer: They can be compared without switching between windows
acceptableAnswers: They can be compared without switching between windows
grade9-ict.hint: It is about reading them together.
grade9-ict.explanation: Side-by-side view shows both documents at the same time, which is what comparing them requires.

grade9-ict.question: A report and a set of notes are both open. How does a user switch between them?
options: Select the other document from the window list or the taskbar
Save the first document under a new name and open that
Print the first document and read it on paper instead
Close the first document every time the other is needed
grade9-ict.answer: Select the other document from the window list or the taskbar
acceptableAnswers: Select the other document from the window list or the taskbar
grade9-ict.hint: Both are already open.
grade9-ict.explanation: Open documents each have a window, so switching is a matter of selecting the other one - closing and reopening is unnecessary.

grade9-ict.question: A mail merge needs two things. What are they?
options: A main document and a data source
A table of contents and an index
grade9-ict.answer: A main document and a data source
acceptableAnswers: A main document and a data source
grade9-ict.hint: One holds the wording, the other the names.
grade9-ict.explanation: Mail merge joins a main document, holding the standard wording, to a data source holding the recipients.

grade9-ict.question: In a mail-merged letter, what does a merge field such as <<Surname>> do?
options: It is replaced by that recipient’s surname in each copy
It numbers the pages of the letter
It prints the word Surname on every single letter
It sets the font used in the letter
grade9-ict.answer: It is replaced by that recipient’s surname in each copy
acceptableAnswers: It is replaced by that recipient’s surname in each copy
grade9-ict.hint: It is a placeholder, not text.
grade9-ict.explanation: A merge field is a placeholder that takes its value from the matching column of the data source for each record.

grade9-ict.question: A school must send the same letter to 250 parents, each addressed personally. What is the most efficient method?
options: Sending one letter to the head of school
grade9-ict.answer: Mail merge
grade9-ict.hint: One letter, many recipients.
grade9-ict.explanation: Mail merge produces one personalised copy per record from a single main document.

grade9-ict.question: What is the name for the box where a row and a column meet?
grade9-ict.answer: Cell
grade9-ict.hint: It is the smallest unit you can type into.
grade9-ict.explanation: A cell is the single box formed where a row and a column cross.

grade9-ict.question: In a spreadsheet, what identifies the cell in column C, row 5?
grade9-ict.answer: C5
grade9-ict.hint: The column letter comes first.
grade9-ict.explanation: A cell reference is the column letter followed by the row number, so column C row 5 is C5.

grade9-ict.question: What does the range B2:B8 refer to?
options: All the cells from B2 down to B8
B2 divided by the value in B8
grade9-ict.answer: All the cells from B2 down to B8
acceptableAnswers: All the cells from B2 down to B8
grade9-ict.hint: The colon means "through to".
grade9-ict.explanation: A colon defines a range, so B2:B8 is every cell from B2 through to B8 inclusive - seven cells.

grade9-ict.question: How many cells are there in the range A1:A10?
grade9-ict.hint: Count both ends.
grade9-ict.explanation: A1:A10 includes both A1 and A10, so it is 10 cells.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is a range covering two columns?
grade9-ict.answer: A1:B5
grade9-ict.hint: Look at the column letters at each end.
grade9-ict.explanation: A1:B5 runs from column A to column B, so it spans two columns and five rows - 10 cells.

grade9-ict.question: Which character must a spreadsheet formula begin with?
grade9-ict.hint: It tells the spreadsheet this is a calculation, not text.
grade9-ict.explanation: A formula begins with an equals sign; without it the entry is treated as ordinary text.

grade9-ict.question: Which formula adds the contents of A1 and A2?
grade9-ict.hint: It must start with an equals sign.
grade9-ict.explanation: =A1+A2 starts with an equals sign and adds the two cells. Without the = it would be stored as text.

grade9-ict.question: Which formula multiplies cell B3 by 5?
grade9-ict.hint: The multiplication sign on a keyboard is the asterisk.
grade9-ict.explanation: Spreadsheets use * for multiplication, so =B3*5 multiplies B3 by 5.

grade9-ict.question: Which symbol is used for division in a spreadsheet formula?
grade9-ict.hint: It is on the same key as the question mark on many keyboards.
grade9-ict.explanation: The forward slash / is used for division.

grade9-ict.question: Cell A1 holds 10, A2 holds 4. What does =A1-A2*2 display?
grade9-ict.hint: Multiplication is done before subtraction.
grade9-ict.explanation: The spreadsheet does A2*2 = 8 first, then 10 - 8 = 2.

grade9-ict.question: Cell A1 holds 6, A2 holds 2. What does =(A1+A2)/4 display?
grade9-ict.hint: Work out the bracket first.

grade9-ict.question: Which function adds up a range of cells?
grade9-ict.answer: SUM
grade9-ict.hint: Three letters.
grade9-ict.explanation: =SUM(A1:A10) adds every value in the range.

grade9-ict.question: Which function finds the arithmetic mean of a range?
grade9-ict.answer: AVERAGE
grade9-ict.hint: The spreadsheet name is not the mathematical name.
grade9-ict.explanation: =AVERAGE(B1:B20) gives the mean of the range.

grade9-ict.question: Which function returns the largest value in a range?
grade9-ict.answer: MAX
grade9-ict.hint: Short for maximum.
grade9-ict.explanation: =MAX(C1:C30) returns the largest value in the range.

grade9-ict.question: Which function counts how many cells in a range contain numbers?
grade9-ict.answer: COUNT
grade9-ict.hint: It counts entries, it does not add them.
grade9-ict.explanation: =COUNT(A1:A50) returns how many cells in the range hold a number.

grade9-ict.question: A teacher has 30 marks in B2:B31. Which formula gives the class average?
grade9-ict.answer: =AVERAGE(B2:B31)
grade9-ict.hint: The range needs a colon, and the function is AVERAGE.
grade9-ict.explanation: =AVERAGE(B2:B31) takes the mean of all 30 marks.

grade9-ict.question: Which formula finds the lowest mark in the range D2:D41?
grade9-ict.answer: =MIN(D2:D41)
grade9-ict.hint: Short for minimum.
grade9-ict.explanation: =MIN(D2:D41) returns the smallest value in the range.

grade9-ict.question: A shopkeeper puts the price in B2 and the quantity in C2. Which formula gives the total cost?
grade9-ict.hint: Total cost is price times quantity.
grade9-ict.explanation: Multiplying price by quantity gives the total, so =B2*C2.

grade9-ict.question: What is displayed by =SUM(A1:A3) when A1 = 5, A2 is empty and A3 = 7?
grade9-ict.hint: An empty cell counts as nothing, not as an error.
grade9-ict.explanation: SUM ignores the empty cell, so the result is 5 + 7 = 12.

grade9-ict.question: What is the name for a single page of a spreadsheet file?
grade9-ict.answer: Worksheet
grade9-ict.hint: The whole file is the workbook.
grade9-ict.explanation: A workbook is the file; each page inside it is a worksheet.

grade9-ict.question: Write the formula that adds cells A1, A2 and A3 using a function and a range.
grade9-ict.answer: =SUM(A1:A3)
grade9-ict.hint: Use SUM with a colon between the two ends of the range.
grade9-ict.explanation: =SUM(A1:A3) adds every cell from A1 to A3.

grade9-ict.question: Write the formula that subtracts cell B2 from cell B1.
grade9-ict.hint: Start with an equals sign; the first cell comes first.
grade9-ict.explanation: =B1-B2 takes the value in B2 away from the value in B1.

grade9-ict.question: Write the formula that finds the highest value in the range C1 to C20.
grade9-ict.answer: =MAX(C1:C20)
grade9-ict.hint: MAX, with the range in brackets.
grade9-ict.explanation: =MAX(C1:C20) returns the largest value in that range.

grade9-ict.question: Write the cell reference for the cell in column F, row 12.
grade9-ict.hint: Column letter first, then the row number.
grade9-ict.explanation: Column F row 12 is written F12.

grade9-ict.question: Name the function that counts how many cells in a range contain numbers.
grade9-ict.answer: COUNT
grade9-ict.hint: It counts rather than adds.
grade9-ict.explanation: COUNT returns how many cells in a range hold a numeric value.

grade9-ict.question: Arranging a list of names from A to Z is called:
grade9-ict.answer: Sorting
grade9-ict.hint: Every row stays; only the order changes.
grade9-ict.explanation: Sorting reorders the rows; it does not remove any of them.

grade9-ict.question: What does filtering a list do?
options: Adds the values in a column
Deletes the rows that do not match
Shows only the rows that match a condition
Puts the rows in alphabetical order
grade9-ict.answer: Shows only the rows that match a condition
acceptableAnswers: Shows only the rows that match a condition
grade9-ict.hint: Nothing is deleted; some rows are hidden.
grade9-ict.explanation: A filter hides the rows that do not match, leaving the matching ones on screen. Removing the filter brings them all back.

grade9-ict.question: Sorting a column of marks in descending order puts them:
grade9-ict.answer: Largest first
grade9-ict.hint: Descending means going down.
grade9-ict.explanation: Descending order starts at the largest value and works down to the smallest.

grade9-ict.question: A teacher wants to see only the pupils who scored below 40. Which tool does this without deleting anything?
grade9-ict.answer: A filter
grade9-ict.hint: The other rows must come back afterwards.
grade9-ict.explanation: A filter temporarily hides the rows that do not match the condition; sorting would merely reorder them.

grade9-ict.question: Which feature automatically colours a cell red when its value falls below a set figure?
grade9-ict.answer: Conditional formatting
grade9-ict.hint: The formatting depends on a condition.
grade9-ict.explanation: Conditional formatting applies a chosen format only when the cell meets the rule you set.

grade9-ict.question: What does merging cells do?
options: Adds all of their values together
Joins several cells into one larger cell
grade9-ict.answer: Joins several cells into one larger cell
acceptableAnswers: Joins several cells into one larger cell
grade9-ict.hint: It changes the shape, not the arithmetic.
grade9-ict.explanation: Merging combines the selected cells into a single cell, which is how a heading is centred across a table.

grade9-ict.question: Which formatting would display the number 0.75 as 75%?
grade9-ict.answer: Percentage format
grade9-ict.hint: The stored value does not change.
grade9-ict.explanation: Percentage format displays the stored value multiplied by 100 with a % sign; the underlying number is unchanged.

grade9-ict.question: A long list is scrolled down and the column headings disappear off the top. Which feature keeps them visible?
grade9-ict.answer: Freeze panes
grade9-ict.hint: The heading row must stay put while the rest moves.
grade9-ict.explanation: Freezing the top row keeps the headings on screen while the data below scrolls.

grade9-ict.question: Which chart is best for comparing the total sales of five different shops?
grade9-ict.answer: A bar chart
grade9-ict.hint: Five separate things are being compared.
grade9-ict.explanation: A bar chart compares separate categories directly by the length of each bar.

grade9-ict.question: Which chart is best for showing how a temperature changed each hour through one day?
grade9-ict.answer: A line chart
grade9-ict.hint: The data is continuous, over time.
grade9-ict.explanation: A line chart joins the points, which shows a trend over time better than separate bars.

grade9-ict.question: A chart must show what share of a class chose each of four sports. Which chart is best?
grade9-ict.answer: A pie chart
grade9-ict.hint: The four shares add up to one whole class.
grade9-ict.explanation: A pie chart shows parts of a single whole, which is exactly what shares of a class are.

grade9-ict.question: Which three labels should a chart normally carry so it can be understood?
options: A chart title and a label on each axis
The file name, the date and the author
The formula, the range and the sheet name
The printer name, the paper size and the margins
grade9-ict.answer: A chart title and a label on each axis
acceptableAnswers: A chart title and a label on each axis
grade9-ict.hint: A reader must know what is being plotted against what.
grade9-ict.explanation: Without a title and labelled axes a chart cannot be read, however accurate the data behind it.

grade9-ict.question: Which flowchart symbol is drawn as an oval?
grade9-ict.answer: Start or Stop
grade9-ict.hint: It appears exactly twice in most flowcharts.
grade9-ict.explanation: The oval (terminator) marks where an algorithm begins and where it ends.

grade9-ict.question: Which flowchart symbol is drawn as a diamond?
grade9-ict.answer: Decision
grade9-ict.hint: It is the only symbol with more than one way out.
grade9-ict.explanation: The diamond is a decision: it asks a question and has a Yes branch and a No branch.

grade9-ict.question: Which flowchart symbol is drawn as a rectangle?
grade9-ict.answer: Process
grade9-ict.hint: It is where a calculation or an assignment happens.
grade9-ict.explanation: The rectangle is a process step - a calculation, or storing a value.

grade9-ict.question: Which flowchart symbol is drawn as a parallelogram (a slanted box)?
grade9-ict.answer: Input or Output
grade9-ict.hint: It is used when data comes in or a result is shown.
grade9-ict.explanation: The parallelogram is used for input and output - reading a value or displaying one.

grade9-ict.question: How many arrows normally leave a decision symbol?
grade9-ict.hint: One for each answer to the question.
grade9-ict.explanation: A decision has two exits, usually labelled Yes and No.

grade9-ict.question: A flowchart reads: START, INPUT n, n = n + 3, OUTPUT n, STOP. If the input is 7, what is output?
grade9-ict.hint: Follow the single process box.
grade9-ict.explanation: 7 + 3 = 10, so 10 is output.

grade9-ict.question: A flowchart reads: START, INPUT a, INPUT b, c = a * b, OUTPUT c, STOP. With a = 6 and b = 4, what is output?
grade9-ict.hint: The process box multiplies.

grade9-ict.question: A flowchart asks "Is m greater than 50?" With m = 50, which branch is taken?
grade9-ict.answer: The No branch
grade9-ict.hint: "Greater than" does not include equal to.
grade9-ict.explanation: 50 is not GREATER than 50, so the condition is false and the No branch is taken.

grade9-ict.question: An algorithm reads: total = 0; for each of 4 numbers, total = total + number. The numbers are 3, 5, 2, 6. What is total at the end?
grade9-ict.hint: Add them one at a time, starting from zero.

grade9-ict.question: Carrying out steps one after another, in order, is called:
grade9-ict.answer: Sequence
grade9-ict.hint: The simplest of the three structures.
grade9-ict.explanation: Sequence is simply doing one step after another in the order written.

grade9-ict.question: Choosing between two paths using a condition is called:
grade9-ict.answer: Selection
grade9-ict.hint: It is what a decision diamond does.
grade9-ict.explanation: Selection chooses between alternatives depending on whether a condition is true.

grade9-ict.question: Repeating a set of steps a number of times is called:
grade9-ict.answer: Repetition
grade9-ict.hint: Also known as iteration or looping.
grade9-ict.explanation: Repetition (iteration) runs the same steps more than once.

grade9-ict.question: Which keyword usually begins a selection statement?
grade9-ict.answer: IF
grade9-ict.hint: It is followed by a condition.
grade9-ict.explanation: IF begins a selection; FOR and WHILE begin repetition.

grade9-ict.question: A loop that repeats a known number of times is best written with:
grade9-ict.answer: FOR
grade9-ict.hint: You already know how many repetitions are needed.
grade9-ict.explanation: A FOR loop is used when the number of repetitions is known in advance; WHILE is used when it is not.

grade9-ict.question: Which Python statement displays a message on the screen?
grade9-ict.answer: print("Hello")
grade9-ict.hint: Five letters, all lower case.
grade9-ict.explanation: print() is the Python statement that writes output to the screen.

grade9-ict.question:
What does this Python code display?
x = 4
y = 3
print(x * y)
grade9-ict.hint: The value, not the letters, is printed.
grade9-ict.explanation: x is 4 and y is 3, so x * y is 12 and 12 is displayed.

grade9-ict.question: Which Python statement reads a value typed by the user?
grade9-ict.answer: input()
grade9-ict.hint: The opposite of print.
grade9-ict.explanation: input() waits for the user to type something and returns it.

grade9-ict.question:
What does this Python code display?
n = 10
if n > 5:
    print("Big")
else:
    print("Small")
grade9-ict.answer: Big
grade9-ict.hint: Is 10 greater than 5?
grade9-ict.explanation: 10 is greater than 5, so the condition is true and "Big" is displayed.

grade9-ict.question:
How many times does this loop print?
for i in range(3):
    print(i)
grade9-ict.hint: range(3) produces 0, 1, 2.
grade9-ict.explanation: range(3) gives three values - 0, 1 and 2 - so print runs three times.

grade9-ict.question: In a flowchart, what do the arrows between symbols show?
options: The order the steps are carried out in
grade9-ict.answer: The order the steps are carried out in
acceptableAnswers: The order the steps are carried out in
grade9-ict.hint: They are called flow lines.
grade9-ict.explanation: The arrows are flow lines: they show the order in which the steps are followed.

grade9-ict.question: Name the flowchart symbol drawn as a diamond.
grade9-ict.answer: Decision
grade9-ict.hint: It asks a question.
grade9-ict.explanation: The diamond is the decision symbol.

grade9-ict.question: Name the flowchart symbol used for input and output.
grade9-ict.answer: Parallelogram
grade9-ict.hint: It is a slanted box.
grade9-ict.explanation: The parallelogram is used for input and output steps.

grade9-ict.question: Name the control structure that repeats a group of steps.
grade9-ict.answer: Repetition
grade9-ict.hint: Also called iteration.
grade9-ict.explanation: Repetition, also called iteration or looping, repeats a group of steps.

grade9-ict.question: Write the Python statement that displays the word Hello on the screen.
grade9-ict.answer: print("Hello")
grade9-ict.hint: Use print with the word in quotation marks.
grade9-ict.explanation: print("Hello") writes Hello to the screen.

grade9-ict.question: An algorithm reads: INPUT p, q = p * 2, q = q + 1, OUTPUT q. If p is 5, what number is output?
grade9-ict.hint: Do the two process steps in order.

grade9-ict.question: Which symbol must every flowchart begin and end with?
grade9-ict.answer: An oval
grade9-ict.hint: It is the terminator.
grade9-ict.explanation: A flowchart starts with a START oval and finishes with a STOP oval.

grade9-ict.question: An algorithm must read a pupil’s mark before it can work anything out. Which symbol is drawn for that step?
grade9-ict.answer: A parallelogram
grade9-ict.hint: Data is coming in.
grade9-ict.explanation: Reading a value is an input step, and input is drawn as a parallelogram.

grade9-ict.question: An algorithm must decide whether a mark is a pass or a fail. Which symbol is drawn for that step?
grade9-ict.answer: A diamond
grade9-ict.hint: It has two ways out.
grade9-ict.explanation: A decision is drawn as a diamond, with a Yes branch and a No branch leaving it.

grade9-ict.question: A flowchart must add 10% to a price. Which symbol holds that step?
grade9-ict.answer: A rectangle
grade9-ict.hint: It is a calculation.
grade9-ict.explanation: A calculation or assignment is a process step, drawn as a rectangle.

grade9-ict.question: In a flowchart, where do the two arrows from a decision symbol normally lead?
options: To the steps taken when the answer is Yes and when it is No
Both of them always lead to exactly the same next step
Both of them lead back to the START oval at the top
To an output step that prints the whole flowchart
grade9-ict.answer: To the steps taken when the answer is Yes and when it is No
acceptableAnswers: To the steps taken when the answer is Yes and when it is No
grade9-ict.hint: Each answer needs its own path.
grade9-ict.explanation: The two exits are labelled Yes and No and lead to the steps carried out in each case.

grade9-ict.question: An algorithm reads a length in metres and must output it in centimetres. What must the process step do?
grade9-ict.answer: Multiply the length by 100
grade9-ict.hint: A centimetre is smaller than a metre, so there are more of them.
grade9-ict.explanation: There are 100 centimetres in a metre, so the value in metres is multiplied by 100.

grade9-ict.question: An algorithm works out the area of a rectangle. Which calculation belongs in the process box?
grade9-ict.answer: area = length * width
grade9-ict.hint: Area is found by multiplying.
grade9-ict.explanation: The area of a rectangle is its length multiplied by its width.

grade9-ict.question: A shop gives 20% discount. An algorithm reads the price into p. Which line gives the amount to pay?
grade9-ict.answer: pay = p * 0.8
grade9-ict.hint: If 20% is taken off, what fraction is left?
grade9-ict.explanation: Taking 20% off leaves 80%, so the amount to pay is the price times 0.8.

grade9-ict.question: An algorithm reads three marks and outputs the average. Which line is correct?
grade9-ict.answer: average = (a + b + c) / 3
grade9-ict.hint: The three marks must be added before dividing.
grade9-ict.explanation: The brackets make the addition happen first; without them only c would be divided by 3.

grade9-ict.question: What does LAN stand for?
grade9-ict.answer: Local Area Network
grade9-ict.hint: The first word describes how far it reaches.
grade9-ict.explanation: LAN stands for Local Area Network - a network covering one building or site.

grade9-ict.question: What does WAN stand for?
grade9-ict.answer: Wide Area Network
grade9-ict.hint: It covers a much larger area than a LAN.
grade9-ict.explanation: WAN stands for Wide Area Network - one that spans towns, countries or the world.

grade9-ict.question: A school connects all the computers in one building. Which type of network is this?
grade9-ict.answer: LAN
grade9-ict.hint: One building, one site.
grade9-ict.explanation: A network confined to a single site is a Local Area Network.

grade9-ict.question: A bank links its branches in Mauritius, Rodrigues and London. Which type of network is this?
grade9-ict.answer: WAN
grade9-ict.hint: The branches are far apart.
grade9-ict.explanation: A network spanning large distances is a Wide Area Network.

grade9-ict.question: The internet is best described as:
options: The largest WAN in the world
grade9-ict.answer: The largest WAN in the world
acceptableAnswers: The largest WAN in the world
grade9-ict.hint: It spans the whole world.
grade9-ict.explanation: The internet is a global network of networks - the largest wide area network there is.

grade9-ict.question: A private network that only the staff of one company can use is called:
grade9-ict.answer: An intranet
grade9-ict.hint: The prefix means "inside".
grade9-ict.explanation: An intranet is a private network using internet technology, available only inside an organisation.

grade9-ict.question: A company lets trusted suppliers reach part of its private network. That extended network is called:
grade9-ict.answer: An extranet
grade9-ict.hint: The prefix means "outside".
grade9-ict.explanation: An extranet extends part of an intranet to selected outsiders such as suppliers or customers.

grade9-ict.question: In a star topology, every computer is connected to:
grade9-ict.answer: A central device
grade9-ict.hint: Think of the shape the cables make.
grade9-ict.explanation: In a star topology every device has its own cable to a central switch or hub.

grade9-ict.question: In a ring topology, the computers are connected:
grade9-ict.answer: In a closed loop
grade9-ict.hint: The name describes the shape.
grade9-ict.explanation: In a ring topology each device connects to two others, forming a closed loop.

grade9-ict.question: In a bus topology, all the computers share:
grade9-ict.answer: One main cable
grade9-ict.hint: Everything hangs off a single backbone.
grade9-ict.explanation: A bus topology connects every device to one shared backbone cable.

grade9-ict.question: What is the main disadvantage of a bus topology?
options: Each computer needs its own switch
It needs more cable than any other topology
It cannot be used with wireless devices
A fault in the main cable stops the whole network
grade9-ict.answer: A fault in the main cable stops the whole network
acceptableAnswers: A fault in the main cable stops the whole network
grade9-ict.hint: Everything depends on one shared cable.
grade9-ict.explanation: Because every device shares one backbone, a break in that cable brings the whole network down.

grade9-ict.question: What is an advantage of a star topology?
options: It uses the least cable of any topology
A fault in one cable affects only that computer
It works without any central device
grade9-ict.answer: A fault in one cable affects only that computer
acceptableAnswers: A fault in one cable affects only that computer
grade9-ict.hint: Each device has its own cable.
grade9-ict.explanation: In a star each device has its own link to the centre, so one broken cable affects only that machine.

grade9-ict.question: Which device connects a home network to the internet?
grade9-ict.answer: Router
grade9-ict.hint: It routes traffic between two networks.
grade9-ict.explanation: A router joins one network to another - typically a home LAN to the internet.

grade9-ict.question: Which device joins several computers together in a LAN and sends data only to the intended recipient?
grade9-ict.answer: Switch
grade9-ict.hint: It is cleverer than a hub.
grade9-ict.explanation: A switch learns which device is on which port and forwards data only to that port; a hub copies it to all.

grade9-ict.question: Which device converts a computer signal so it can travel over a telephone line, and back again?
grade9-ict.answer: Modem
grade9-ict.hint: The name is short for two words that describe both directions.
grade9-ict.explanation: A modem MOdulates and DEModulates - it converts between digital and analogue signals.

grade9-ict.question: Which device strengthens a weak signal so it can travel further along a network?
grade9-ict.answer: Repeater
grade9-ict.hint: It repeats what it receives, more strongly.
grade9-ict.explanation: A repeater regenerates a weakened signal so it can carry on over a longer distance.

grade9-ict.question: What is the main purpose of a firewall?
options: To control what traffic may enter or leave a network
To back up the files on the network automatically
To speed up the internet connection for every user
To share one printer between all the computers
grade9-ict.answer: To control what traffic may enter or leave a network
acceptableAnswers: To control what traffic may enter or leave a network
grade9-ict.hint: It is a barrier, not a booster.
grade9-ict.explanation: A firewall inspects traffic and blocks anything that breaks its rules, protecting the network.

grade9-ict.question: Which cable type carries data as pulses of light?
grade9-ict.answer: Fibre optic
grade9-ict.hint: The clue is in the word optic.
grade9-ict.explanation: Fibre optic cable carries data as light along a glass or plastic strand, giving very high speeds.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is a wireless way of connecting a device to a network?
grade9-ict.answer: Wi-Fi
grade9-ict.hint: Only one of these needs no cable.
grade9-ict.explanation: Wi-Fi connects devices using radio waves, with no cable at all.

grade9-ict.question: What is the main advantage of a wired connection over Wi-Fi?
options: It lets the device be carried around
It needs no hardware at all
It works over longer distances than any cable
It is usually faster and more reliable
grade9-ict.answer: It is usually faster and more reliable
acceptableAnswers: It is usually faster and more reliable
grade9-ict.hint: Think about interference and walls.
grade9-ict.explanation: A cable is not affected by walls, distance or radio interference, so it is usually faster and steadier.

grade9-ict.question: Write in full what LAN stands for.
grade9-ict.answer: Local Area Network
grade9-ict.hint: Three words.
grade9-ict.explanation: LAN stands for Local Area Network.

grade9-ict.question: Write in full what WAN stands for.
grade9-ict.answer: Wide Area Network
grade9-ict.hint: Three words.
grade9-ict.explanation: WAN stands for Wide Area Network.

grade9-ict.question: Name the device that connects a home network to the internet.
grade9-ict.answer: Router
grade9-ict.hint: It routes traffic between networks.
grade9-ict.explanation: A router connects one network to another.

grade9-ict.question: Name the topology in which every computer has its own cable to a central device.
grade9-ict.answer: Star
grade9-ict.hint: Think of the shape the cables make.
grade9-ict.explanation: A star topology gives each device its own link to a central switch or hub.

grade9-ict.question: Name the security device that controls which traffic may enter or leave a network.
grade9-ict.answer: Firewall
grade9-ict.hint: It is a barrier.
grade9-ict.explanation: A firewall filters traffic according to rules and blocks what is not allowed.

grade9-ict.question: What is a computer network?
options: A type of printer that several rooms can share
A program that edits pictures on several computers
Two or more computers connected so they can share data
A single computer with two screens and two keyboards
grade9-ict.answer: Two or more computers connected so they can share data
acceptableAnswers: Two or more computers connected so they can share data
grade9-ict.hint: The key word is connected.
grade9-ict.explanation: A network is two or more computers linked together so they can communicate and share resources.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is an advantage of putting a school’s computers on a network?
options: The computers work when the power is off
One printer can be shared by every computer
Files can no longer be copied
Each computer needs its own printer
grade9-ict.answer: One printer can be shared by every computer
acceptableAnswers: One printer can be shared by every computer
grade9-ict.hint: Think about what can now be shared.
grade9-ict.explanation: Networking lets hardware, files and an internet connection be shared instead of duplicated for every machine.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is a disadvantage of a network?
options: A virus can spread quickly from one computer to all the others
Printers can never be shared once a network is installed
Each computer must be bought twice over to be networked
Files can no longer be shared between any of the computers
grade9-ict.answer: A virus can spread quickly from one computer to all the others
acceptableAnswers: A virus can spread quickly from one computer to all the others
grade9-ict.hint: What else travels along the connection?
grade9-ict.explanation: The same links that carry files carry malicious software, so an infection on one machine can reach the rest.

grade9-ict.question: A school network stops working and no one can print or reach the internet. What does this illustrate?
options: Printers do not work on a network
A network creates a single point of failure
The internet is faster than a LAN
grade9-ict.answer: A network creates a single point of failure
acceptableAnswers: A network creates a single point of failure
grade9-ict.hint: What happened to every machine at once?
grade9-ict.explanation: When shared equipment fails, everything that depends on it stops - which is the cost of sharing.

grade9-ict.question: Which cable is most commonly used to connect a computer to a wired LAN?
grade9-ict.answer: Ethernet cable
grade9-ict.hint: It plugs into the network port.
grade9-ict.explanation: An Ethernet cable connects a computer’s network port to a switch or a router.

grade9-ict.question: What is the main advantage of a wireless connection over a wired one?
options: It is never affected by walls
It needs no equipment at all
Devices can be moved around freely
It is always faster than a cable
grade9-ict.answer: Devices can be moved around freely
acceptableAnswers: Devices can be moved around freely
grade9-ict.hint: Think about a laptop being carried between rooms.
grade9-ict.explanation: With no cable a device can move anywhere within range, which a wired connection cannot allow.

grade9-ict.question: A computer laboratory of 30 fixed machines needs the fastest, steadiest connection. Which should be chosen?
grade9-ict.answer: A wired connection
grade9-ict.hint: The machines never move.
grade9-ict.explanation: Fixed machines gain nothing from mobility, and cable gives higher, steadier speeds with no interference.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these can reduce the strength of a Wi-Fi signal?
options: Using a shorter password for the network
Sorting the files stored on the hard disk
Thick walls between the device and the router
Choosing a larger monitor for the computer
grade9-ict.answer: Thick walls between the device and the router
acceptableAnswers: Thick walls between the device and the router
grade9-ict.hint: Radio waves have to get through something.
grade9-ict.explanation: Walls, distance and other radio equipment all weaken a Wi-Fi signal; none of the other options touches it.

grade9-ict.question: An intranet is available to:
options: Only one single computer in the building
Anyone in the world with a browser
Only the people inside one organisation
grade9-ict.answer: Only the people inside one organisation
acceptableAnswers: Only the people inside one organisation
grade9-ict.hint: The prefix means inside.
grade9-ict.explanation: An intranet is private to one organisation, even though it uses the same technology as the internet.

grade9-ict.question: Which is the best example of something a school would put on its intranet rather than its public website?
options: The date of the open day
Internal staff notices and pupil records
grade9-ict.answer: Internal staff notices and pupil records
acceptableAnswers: Internal staff notices and pupil records
grade9-ict.hint: Which of these should the public not see?
grade9-ict.explanation: An intranet holds material meant only for people inside the organisation; public information belongs on the website.

grade9-ict.question: What is the difference between an intranet and an extranet?
options: An extranet also lets selected outsiders in, such as suppliers
There is no difference between them
An extranet is available to everyone in the whole world
grade9-ict.answer: An extranet also lets selected outsiders in, such as suppliers
acceptableAnswers: An extranet also lets selected outsiders in, such as suppliers
grade9-ict.hint: One of them reaches slightly further than the other.
grade9-ict.explanation: An extranet extends part of an organisation’s intranet to chosen outsiders, while the rest stays private.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is a web browser?
grade9-ict.answer: Google Chrome
grade9-ict.hint: A browser is the program you open web pages in.
grade9-ict.explanation: Chrome is a browser - the program that displays web pages. Search and Gmail are services you reach through one.

grade9-ict.question: What does URL stand for?
grade9-ict.answer: Uniform Resource Locator
grade9-ict.hint: It locates a resource on the web.
grade9-ict.explanation: A URL - Uniform Resource Locator - is the address of a page or file on the web.

grade9-ict.question: In the address https://www.mie.ac.mu/library, which part is the domain name?
grade9-ict.answer: www.mie.ac.mu
grade9-ict.hint: It is the part that names the site, before the first single slash.
grade9-ict.explanation: The domain name identifies the site; https is the protocol and /library is the path within it.

grade9-ict.question: What does the s in https indicate?
options: The page is stored on a server
The connection is secure and encrypted
The site is a search engine
The site is in a different country
grade9-ict.answer: The connection is secure and encrypted
acceptableAnswers: The connection is secure and encrypted
grade9-ict.hint: Look for the padlock in the address bar.
grade9-ict.explanation: The s means secure: data between the browser and the site is encrypted.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is a search engine?
grade9-ict.answer: Google
grade9-ict.hint: Three of these are browsers.
grade9-ict.explanation: Google is a search engine; Chrome, Firefox and Edge are browsers you use to reach it.

grade9-ict.question: Putting a phrase in "quotation marks" in a search engine makes it:
options: Ignore the words in the quotes
Look for those exact words together
grade9-ict.answer: Look for those exact words together
acceptableAnswers: Look for those exact words together
grade9-ict.hint: It makes the search stricter, not wider.
grade9-ict.explanation: Quotation marks ask for an exact phrase rather than the words in any order.

grade9-ict.question: Saving a web address in the browser so you can return to it quickly is called adding a:
grade9-ict.answer: Bookmark
grade9-ict.hint: The paper name for keeping your place.
grade9-ict.explanation: A bookmark (or favourite) stores a page address so it can be reopened with one click.

grade9-ict.question: Which symbol always appears in an email address?
grade9-ict.hint: It separates the user from the domain.
grade9-ict.explanation: An email address is always username@domain, so it always contains @.

grade9-ict.question: In an email, what is the Cc field used for?
options: Sending a visible copy to other people
Sending a hidden copy to other people
grade9-ict.answer: Sending a visible copy to other people
acceptableAnswers: Sending a visible copy to other people
grade9-ict.hint: Cc stands for carbon copy.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cc sends a copy to others, and every recipient can see who was copied.

grade9-ict.question: In an email, what is the Bcc field used for?
options: Sending a copy that every other recipient is able to see
Sending a copy without other recipients seeing that address
Marking the email as urgent so that it is opened first
Adding a signature block to the end of the message
grade9-ict.answer: Sending a copy without other recipients seeing that address
acceptableAnswers: Sending a copy without other recipients seeing that address
grade9-ict.hint: The extra B stands for blind.
grade9-ict.explanation: Bcc - blind carbon copy - sends a copy without revealing that address to the other recipients.

grade9-ict.question: Sending a photograph with an email is done by adding an:
grade9-ict.answer: Attachment
grade9-ict.hint: The file is attached to the message.
grade9-ict.explanation: A file sent with an email is called an attachment.

grade9-ict.question: A pupil must email one message to 40 people without any of them seeing the others' addresses. Which field should the addresses go in?
grade9-ict.answer: Bcc
grade9-ict.hint: The addresses must stay hidden from each other.
grade9-ict.explanation: Bcc hides the recipients from one another, which is the correct way to email a large list.

grade9-ict.question: What is the main advantage of email over ordinary post?
options: It arrives almost immediately and costs nothing to send
It does not need an internet connection at either end
It can carry heavier parcels than the post office will
It cannot be read by anyone else on the way there
grade9-ict.answer: It arrives almost immediately and costs nothing to send
acceptableAnswers: It arrives almost immediately and costs nothing to send
grade9-ict.hint: Think about speed and cost.
grade9-ict.explanation: Email is delivered in seconds at no per-message cost, unlike a posted letter.

grade9-ict.question: Buying goods over the internet is called:
grade9-ict.answer: E-commerce
grade9-ict.hint: Commerce means trade.
grade9-ict.explanation: E-commerce is buying and selling goods and services online.

grade9-ict.question: Checking your account balance on a bank's website is an example of:
grade9-ict.answer: E-banking
grade9-ict.hint: The clue is the word bank.
grade9-ict.explanation: E-banking lets a customer manage an account online instead of visiting a branch.

grade9-ict.question: Taking a course through a website with videos and quizzes is an example of:
grade9-ict.answer: E-learning
grade9-ict.hint: The clue is the word learning.
grade9-ict.explanation: E-learning delivers teaching and assessment online.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is a benefit of online shopping for the customer?
options: The shop is open at any hour
The customer can always try the goods on first
grade9-ict.answer: The shop is open at any hour
acceptableAnswers: The shop is open at any hour
grade9-ict.hint: Think about when you can use it, not how fast delivery is.
grade9-ict.explanation: An online shop can be used at any time of day, unlike a shop with opening hours.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is a drawback of online shopping?
options: You cannot examine the goods before buying
You can only shop during opening hours
It is never possible to compare prices
You must always pay in cash
grade9-ict.answer: You cannot examine the goods before buying
acceptableAnswers: You cannot examine the goods before buying
grade9-ict.hint: What can a shop do that a web page cannot?
grade9-ict.explanation: Online you cannot handle, try on or inspect the item before it arrives.

grade9-ict.question: Holding a meeting with people in another country using cameras and microphones is called:
grade9-ict.answer: Video conferencing
grade9-ict.hint: Everyone can see and hear each other, both ways.
grade9-ict.explanation: Video conferencing lets people in different places see and hear one another in real time.

grade9-ict.question: What is the main advantage of video conferencing for a business?
options: It saves the time and cost of travelling
It works without any internet connection
It removes the need for any equipment
grade9-ict.answer: It saves the time and cost of travelling
acceptableAnswers: It saves the time and cost of travelling
grade9-ict.hint: Compare it with flying to a meeting.
grade9-ict.explanation: A meeting held online avoids the cost and hours that travelling to it would take.

grade9-ict.question: Write in full what URL stands for.
grade9-ict.answer: Uniform Resource Locator
grade9-ict.hint: Three words.
grade9-ict.explanation: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator.

grade9-ict.question: Give the name of the email field used to send a copy that the other recipients cannot see.
grade9-ict.answer: Bcc
grade9-ict.hint: The extra letter stands for blind.
grade9-ict.explanation: Bcc - blind carbon copy - hides that recipient from the others.

grade9-ict.question: Give the term for buying and selling goods over the internet.
grade9-ict.answer: E-commerce
grade9-ict.hint: Commerce means trade.
grade9-ict.explanation: E-commerce is trade carried out online.

grade9-ict.question: Name the program used to view web pages.
grade9-ict.answer: Browser
grade9-ict.hint: Chrome and Firefox are examples.
grade9-ict.explanation: A web browser displays web pages.

grade9-ict.question: Give the term for a meeting held over the internet using cameras and microphones.
grade9-ict.answer: Video conferencing
grade9-ict.hint: Both sides can see and hear each other.
grade9-ict.explanation: Video conferencing links people in different places in real time.

grade9-ict.question: What is the Internet?
options: A single very large computer that stores every page
A program used to view web pages on a screen
A collection of linked web pages and nothing else
A worldwide network of connected computer networks
grade9-ict.answer: A worldwide network of connected computer networks
acceptableAnswers: A worldwide network of connected computer networks
grade9-ict.hint: It is the connection itself.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Internet is the global network infrastructure that links networks together.

grade9-ict.question: What is the World Wide Web?
options: Another name for the Internet and the cables it uses
A search engine that finds pages on the Internet
The linked pages and sites carried over the Internet
A type of network cable used to reach the Internet
grade9-ict.answer: The linked pages and sites carried over the Internet
acceptableAnswers: The linked pages and sites carried over the Internet
grade9-ict.hint: It is one of the services the Internet carries.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Web is the collection of linked pages and sites delivered over the Internet; email and file transfer are other services on the same network.

grade9-ict.question: Which statement is correct?
options: The Web is one of the services carried by the Internet
The Internet is one of the services carried by the Web
The Internet and the Web are exactly the same thing
Neither has anything to do with the other
grade9-ict.answer: The Web is one of the services carried by the Internet
acceptableAnswers: The Web is one of the services carried by the Internet
grade9-ict.hint: Which one is the road, and which the traffic?
grade9-ict.explanation: The Internet is the network; the Web is one service running on it.

grade9-ict.question: What does ISP stand for?
grade9-ict.answer: Internet Service Provider
grade9-ict.hint: It is the company you pay for a connection.
grade9-ict.explanation: An ISP - Internet Service Provider - is the company that connects a home or business to the Internet.

grade9-ict.question: A personal online journal, with entries shown newest first, is called a:
grade9-ict.answer: Blog
grade9-ict.hint: It is written by one person or a small group.
grade9-ict.explanation: A blog is a website of dated entries, usually written by one author and read by many.

grade9-ict.question: A website whose pages can be edited by many contributors is called a:
grade9-ict.answer: Wiki
grade9-ict.hint: Many people build it together.
grade9-ict.explanation: A wiki lets its readers edit and extend the pages, so the content is written collaboratively.

grade9-ict.question: An audio programme published on the internet for people to download or stream is a:
grade9-ict.answer: Podcast
grade9-ict.hint: You listen to it.
grade9-ict.explanation: A podcast is an audio episode published online to be downloaded or streamed.

grade9-ict.question: A class must discuss a topic over several days, with everyone able to read and reply to earlier messages. Which tool suits this best?
grade9-ict.answer: A discussion forum
grade9-ict.hint: The discussion must stay readable over time.
grade9-ict.explanation: A forum keeps the messages in threads that can be read and replied to at any time, unlike a live call that ends.

grade9-ict.question: Which is the best guide to how a web page should be laid out?
options: Hide the menu so that the page looks tidy and uncluttered
Use as many different fonts and colours as possible
Keep it simple and consistent so visitors can find things
Fill every empty space on the page with moving images
grade9-ict.answer: Keep it simple and consistent so visitors can find things
acceptableAnswers: Keep it simple and consistent so visitors can find things
grade9-ict.hint: The visitor must be able to use it.
grade9-ict.explanation: A user-friendly site is simple, consistent and predictable, so a visitor knows where to look.

grade9-ict.question: Why should the navigation menu appear in the same place on every page of a site?
options: It stops the site being searched by a search engine
It reduces the number of pages the site has to hold
It makes every page of the site load noticeably faster
Visitors learn where it is and can move around quickly
grade9-ict.answer: Visitors learn where it is and can move around quickly
acceptableAnswers: Visitors learn where it is and can move around quickly
grade9-ict.hint: Consistency is what makes a site learnable.
grade9-ict.explanation: A menu that moves forces the visitor to hunt for it on every page; keeping it still makes the site predictable.

grade9-ict.question: Why should a web page not use pale grey text on a white background?
options: Grey text cannot be printed on an ordinary office printer
Grey text loads more slowly than black text on the same page
Search engines refuse to list a page that uses grey text
It is hard to read, especially for visitors with poor eyesight
grade9-ict.answer: It is hard to read, especially for visitors with poor eyesight
acceptableAnswers: It is hard to read, especially for visitors with poor eyesight
grade9-ict.hint: Think about contrast.
grade9-ict.explanation: Text needs enough contrast against its background to be readable; pale grey on white fails that for many readers.

grade9-ict.question: In a database table, what is a single row called?
grade9-ict.answer: A record
grade9-ict.hint: It holds everything known about one person or thing.
grade9-ict.explanation: A row is a record: all the data about one item, such as one pupil.

grade9-ict.question: In a database table, what is a single column called?
grade9-ict.answer: A field
grade9-ict.hint: It holds one kind of information for every row.
grade9-ict.explanation: A column is a field: one item of information, such as Surname, held for every record.

grade9-ict.question: A table stores 200 pupils with 6 columns each. How many records does it hold?
grade9-ict.hint: One record per pupil.
grade9-ict.explanation: Each pupil is one record, so there are 200 records of 6 fields each.

grade9-ict.question: What is a primary key?
options: The password that opens up the database
The first field in the table
The field that is sorted first
A field whose value is different in every record
grade9-ict.answer: A field whose value is different in every record
acceptableAnswers: A field whose value is different in every record
grade9-ict.hint: It must identify one record and only one.
grade9-ict.explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies each record, so no two records may share its value.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these fields would make the best primary key for a table of pupils?
grade9-ict.answer: Admission number
grade9-ict.hint: Which one can never be repeated?
grade9-ict.explanation: Two pupils can share a surname, a class or a birthday; an admission number is issued once and never repeated.

grade9-ict.question: Which data type should be used for a field holding a pupil’s date of birth?
grade9-ict.answer: Date/Time
grade9-ict.hint: The field holds a calendar date.
grade9-ict.explanation: A Date/Time field stores dates properly, so they can be sorted and compared.

grade9-ict.question: Which data type should be used for a field holding a telephone number?
grade9-ict.answer: Text
grade9-ict.hint: Would you ever add two telephone numbers together?
grade9-ict.explanation: A telephone number is never calculated with and may begin with a zero, which a Number field would drop, so Text is correct.

grade9-ict.question: Which data type should be used for a field that records whether a fee has been paid?
grade9-ict.answer: Yes/No
grade9-ict.hint: There are only two possible answers.
grade9-ict.explanation: A Yes/No (Boolean) field stores one of exactly two states, which is what "paid or not" needs.

grade9-ict.question: Which data type should be used for a field holding the price of an item in rupees?
grade9-ict.answer: Currency
grade9-ict.hint: It is money.
grade9-ict.explanation: A Currency field stores an amount of money with the right number of decimal places and a currency symbol.

grade9-ict.question: Why is Number the wrong data type for a field holding a postcode that may start with 0?
options: A Number field cannot be searched
A Number field cannot be sorted
A Number field removes a leading zero
A Number field cannot hold five digits
grade9-ict.answer: A Number field removes a leading zero
acceptableAnswers: A Number field removes a leading zero
grade9-ict.hint: What happens to a 0 written in front of a number?
grade9-ict.explanation: A Number field stores a value, not the characters typed, so a leading zero is lost. Text keeps it.

grade9-ict.question: What is the name for the whole organised collection of related tables and the data in them?
grade9-ict.answer: A database
grade9-ict.hint: It is the largest of these four.
grade9-ict.explanation: A database is the whole organised collection of related data.

grade9-ict.question: A pupil moves house. What should be done to the database?
options: Delete the record and stop there
Add a second record for the same pupil
Edit the address field in that pupil’s record
grade9-ict.answer: Edit the address field in that pupil’s record
acceptableAnswers: Edit the address field in that pupil’s record
grade9-ict.hint: Only one thing about the pupil has changed.
grade9-ict.explanation: Editing the one field that changed keeps the record accurate without duplicating the pupil.

grade9-ict.question: What is the main problem with entering the same customer twice in a table?
options: The queries begin to run more slowly than usual
The data becomes inconsistent and reports are wrong
The table runs out of records
grade9-ict.answer: The data becomes inconsistent and reports are wrong
acceptableAnswers: The data becomes inconsistent and reports are wrong
grade9-ict.hint: Which of the two copies is the true one?
grade9-ict.explanation: Duplicate records can disagree with each other, so counts, searches and reports stop being reliable.

grade9-ict.question: What is a query used for?
options: To make a backup copy of the database
To print a neat summary of the data
To enter data one record at a time
To find the records that match a condition
grade9-ict.answer: To find the records that match a condition
acceptableAnswers: To find the records that match a condition
grade9-ict.hint: It asks a question of the data.
grade9-ict.explanation: A query searches the table and returns only the records that satisfy the criteria given.

grade9-ict.question: In a query design grid with the rows Field, Table, Sort, Show and Criteria, which row holds the condition a record must satisfy?
grade9-ict.answer: Criteria
grade9-ict.hint: The name of the row says what it holds.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Criteria row holds the condition; Field names the column, Sort orders it and Show decides whether it is displayed.

grade9-ict.question: In a query design grid, what does the Show row control?
options: Whether that field may be edited
Whether that field is the primary key
Whether that field appears in the results
grade9-ict.answer: Whether that field appears in the results
acceptableAnswers: Whether that field appears in the results
grade9-ict.hint: It is a tick box.
grade9-ict.explanation: Unticking Show lets a field be used in the criteria without appearing in the answer.

grade9-ict.question: A query on a Marks field has the criteria >50. Which records are returned?
options: Those with a mark of 50 or more
grade9-ict.answer: Those with a mark above 50
grade9-ict.hint: "Greater than" does not include equal to.
grade9-ict.explanation: The criteria >50 returns marks above 50 only; a mark of exactly 50 is excluded.

grade9-ict.question: A query must list pupils who are in Grade 9 and also in the netball club. Which operator joins the two conditions?
grade9-ict.answer: AND
grade9-ict.hint: Both conditions must be true at the same time.
grade9-ict.explanation: AND returns only the records that satisfy both conditions; OR would return those satisfying either.

grade9-ict.question: What is a database form mainly used for?
options: Entering and viewing one record at a time
Printing a summary for a meeting
Storing the data on the hard disk
grade9-ict.answer: Entering and viewing one record at a time
acceptableAnswers: Entering and viewing one record at a time
grade9-ict.hint: It is a screen a user types into.
grade9-ict.explanation: A form gives a friendly on-screen layout for entering and viewing records one at a time.

grade9-ict.question: What is a database report mainly used for?
options: Presenting selected data in a neat printable layout
Typing new records into the table
Protecting the whole database with a password
Setting the data type of each field
grade9-ict.answer: Presenting selected data in a neat printable layout
acceptableAnswers: Presenting selected data in a neat printable layout
grade9-ict.hint: It is the output, not the input.
grade9-ict.explanation: A report formats data - often grouped and totalled - so it can be printed or read as a summary.

grade9-ict.question: Give the database term for one row of a table.
grade9-ict.answer: Record
grade9-ict.hint: It holds all the data about one item.
grade9-ict.explanation: A row of a table is a record.

grade9-ict.question: Give the database term for one column of a table.
grade9-ict.answer: Field
grade9-ict.hint: It holds one item of information for every row.
grade9-ict.explanation: A column of a table is a field.

grade9-ict.question: Name the field whose value must be different in every record so that it identifies one record only.
grade9-ict.answer: Primary key
grade9-ict.hint: Two words.
grade9-ict.explanation: The primary key uniquely identifies each record.

grade9-ict.question: Name the data type that should be used for a field storing whether a library book has been returned.
grade9-ict.answer: Yes/No
grade9-ict.hint: There are only two possible values.
grade9-ict.explanation: A Yes/No (Boolean) field stores one of exactly two states.

grade9-ict.question: Name the row of a query design grid in which the condition is typed.
grade9-ict.answer: Criteria
grade9-ict.hint: The name of the row says what it holds.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Criteria row of the design grid holds the condition a record must satisfy.

grade9-ict.question: Which is the best way to let a clerk who knows nothing about databases add new customers?
options: Let them type into the table directly
grade9-ict.answer: Give them a form
grade9-ict.hint: It must be simple and hard to get wrong.
grade9-ict.explanation: A form shows one record at a time in a friendly layout, so data can be entered without touching the table design.

grade9-ict.question: A head teacher wants a printed list of pupils grouped by class with a total for each class. What should be produced?
grade9-ict.answer: A report
grade9-ict.hint: It is printed, grouped and totalled.
grade9-ict.explanation: A report presents selected data grouped and totalled in a layout designed to be printed.

grade9-ict.question: Where does the data shown on a form or a report come from?
options: The table or query it is based on
grade9-ict.answer: The table or query it is based on
acceptableAnswers: The table or query it is based on
grade9-ict.hint: Forms and reports display data; they do not store it.
grade9-ict.explanation: A form or report is a view of data held in a table or returned by a query.

grade9-ict.question: Why should data be checked as it is typed into a database?
options: It makes the database file smaller than it would otherwise be
A mistake entered once is repeated in every report that uses it
Typing is always faster when each entry is checked first
The primary key changes automatically whenever data is added
grade9-ict.answer: A mistake entered once is repeated in every report that uses it
acceptableAnswers: A mistake entered once is repeated in every report that uses it
grade9-ict.hint: Think about everything that reads the record afterwards.
grade9-ict.explanation: Wrong data spreads: every search, count and report built on it is wrong too, which is why entry is checked.

grade9-ict.question: A field is set to accept only values between 1 and 100. What is this check called?
grade9-ict.answer: A validation rule
grade9-ict.hint: It decides what may be entered.
grade9-ict.explanation: A validation rule refuses data outside the range allowed, catching errors at the point of entry.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is an operating system?
grade9-ict.answer: Windows
grade9-ict.hint: Three of these are programs that run on top of the fourth.
grade9-ict.explanation: Windows is an operating system; Word, Excel and Chrome are application programs that run on it.

grade9-ict.question: What is the main job of an operating system?
options: To type letters, reports and essays
To control the hardware and run the other programs
To connect the computer to a printer only
grade9-ict.answer: To control the hardware and run the other programs
acceptableAnswers: To control the hardware and run the other programs
grade9-ict.hint: It is the software everything else depends on.
grade9-ict.explanation: The operating system manages the hardware, the memory, the files and the running of every other program.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is not a task of an operating system?
grade9-ict.answer: Writing a business letter
grade9-ict.hint: Three are system tasks; one is what a user does with an application.
grade9-ict.explanation: Writing a letter is done in an application such as a word processor; the other three are operating-system tasks.

grade9-ict.question: Which part of the computer does the operating system load into when it starts?
grade9-ict.answer: RAM
grade9-ict.hint: It must be in the memory the processor works from.
grade9-ict.explanation: The operating system is loaded from storage into RAM at start-up so the processor can run it.

grade9-ict.question: Two programs are open at once. Which part of the computer decides how the processor time is shared between them?
grade9-ict.answer: The operating system
grade9-ict.hint: Only one piece of software is in charge of the machine.
grade9-ict.explanation: Scheduling processor time between running programs is one of the operating system’s core jobs.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is an operating system used on many mobile phones?
grade9-ict.answer: Android
grade9-ict.hint: Think about what runs on a phone.
grade9-ict.explanation: Android is a mobile operating system; the others are used on computers and servers.

grade9-ict.question: An operating system that a user controls by typing commands is described as having a:
grade9-ict.answer: Command line interface
grade9-ict.hint: The user types instead of clicking.
grade9-ict.explanation: A command line interface takes typed commands; a graphical user interface uses windows, icons and a pointer.

grade9-ict.question: What does GUI stand for?
grade9-ict.answer: Graphical User Interface
grade9-ict.hint: It is what windows and icons make.
grade9-ict.explanation: GUI stands for Graphical User Interface - the windows, icons, menus and pointer a user clicks on.

grade9-ict.question: What is the main advantage of a graphical user interface over a command line interface?
options: It always runs faster on old hardware than a command line does
It allows more commands to be typed at once than a command line
It is easier for a beginner because commands do not have to be memorised
It uses far less memory than a command line interface needs
grade9-ict.answer: It is easier for a beginner because commands do not have to be memorised
acceptableAnswers: It is easier for a beginner because commands do not have to be memorised
grade9-ict.hint: Think about what a new user has to know.
grade9-ict.explanation: A GUI shows the choices on screen, so the user recognises them instead of having to remember typed commands.

grade9-ict.question: Which type of operating system allows several users to work on one computer at the same time?
grade9-ict.answer: Multi-user
grade9-ict.hint: The name says how many people it serves.
grade9-ict.explanation: A multi-user operating system supports several users on the same machine at once.

grade9-ict.question: Software written to do a job for the user, such as a word processor, is called:
grade9-ict.answer: Application software
grade9-ict.hint: The user applies it to a task.
grade9-ict.explanation: Application software performs a task for the user; system software runs the machine.

grade9-ict.question: Software that runs and maintains the computer itself is called:
grade9-ict.answer: System software
grade9-ict.hint: It serves the machine, not the user’s task.
grade9-ict.explanation: System software - the operating system, drivers and utilities - keeps the computer running.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is a utility program?
grade9-ict.answer: Antivirus software
grade9-ict.hint: A utility looks after the computer rather than doing the user’s work.
grade9-ict.explanation: Antivirus is a utility: it maintains and protects the system. The other three are applications.

grade9-ict.question: Which utility makes a spare copy of files so they can be recovered if the original is lost?
grade9-ict.answer: Backup
grade9-ict.hint: The name says what it does.
grade9-ict.explanation: A backup utility copies files to another place so they can be restored after a loss.

grade9-ict.question: Which utility makes a file smaller so it takes less space or sends more quickly?
grade9-ict.answer: File compression
grade9-ict.hint: It squeezes the file.
grade9-ict.explanation: A compression utility reduces file size, which saves storage and speeds up transfer.

grade9-ict.question: Which utility deletes temporary and unwanted files to free space on a disk?
grade9-ict.answer: Disk cleanup
grade9-ict.hint: It removes files rather than rearranging them.
grade9-ict.explanation: Disk cleanup removes temporary and unneeded files; the defragmenter rearranges the files that remain.

grade9-ict.question: What does a disk defragmenter do?
options: Rearranges the parts of files so each one is stored together
Deletes the files that are no longer needed from the disk
Scans every file on the disk for viruses and removes them
Copies every file to a second disk for safe keeping
grade9-ict.answer: Rearranges the parts of files so each one is stored together
acceptableAnswers: Rearranges the parts of files so each one is stored together
grade9-ict.hint: It tidies where the pieces are, without deleting anything.
grade9-ict.explanation: Defragmenting gathers the scattered pieces of each file into one place so the disk reads it faster.

grade9-ict.question: Small software that lets the operating system work with a particular printer or scanner is called a:
grade9-ict.answer: Driver
grade9-ict.hint: It drives one device.
grade9-ict.explanation: A device driver translates between the operating system and one particular piece of hardware.

grade9-ict.question: Software that may be used free of charge and freely copied is described as:
grade9-ict.answer: Freeware
grade9-ict.hint: The clue is in the first half of the word.
grade9-ict.explanation: Freeware is distributed at no cost; shareware is free to try for a period and then must be paid for.

grade9-ict.question: Which operating-system feature lets a user organise files into a structure of folders?
grade9-ict.answer: File management
grade9-ict.hint: The name says what it manages.
grade9-ict.explanation: File management is the operating-system job of naming, storing, finding and organising files and folders.

grade9-ict.question: Give the name of the software that controls the hardware and runs all the other programs.
grade9-ict.answer: Operating system
grade9-ict.hint: Two words.
grade9-ict.explanation: The operating system controls the computer and runs every other program.

grade9-ict.question: Write in full what GUI stands for.
grade9-ict.answer: Graphical User Interface
grade9-ict.hint: Three words.
grade9-ict.explanation: GUI stands for Graphical User Interface.

grade9-ict.question: Give the term for software written to do a task for the user, such as a spreadsheet.
grade9-ict.answer: Application software
grade9-ict.hint: The user applies it to a job.
grade9-ict.explanation: Application software does a task for the user, as opposed to system software.

grade9-ict.question: Name the utility program that protects a computer against malicious software.
grade9-ict.answer: Antivirus
grade9-ict.hint: It scans for infections.
grade9-ict.explanation: Antivirus software detects and removes malicious programs.

grade9-ict.question: Name the small program that allows the operating system to work with one particular device, such as a printer.
grade9-ict.answer: Driver
grade9-ict.hint: It drives that one device.
grade9-ict.explanation: A device driver lets the operating system communicate with a particular piece of hardware.

grade9-ict.question: A program written to damage a computer or its data is called a:
grade9-ict.answer: Virus
grade9-ict.hint: It spreads from one machine to another.
grade9-ict.explanation: A virus is malicious software that damages data or the system and copies itself to other machines.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these makes the strongest password?
options: The user’s date of birth, written as six digits
The user’s first name, so that it is easy to remember
A mix of upper and lower case letters, digits and symbols
The word "password", which is short and quick to type
grade9-ict.answer: A mix of upper and lower case letters, digits and symbols
acceptableAnswers: A mix of upper and lower case letters, digits and symbols
grade9-ict.hint: Which one would be hardest for someone else to guess?
grade9-ict.explanation: A long password mixing cases, digits and symbols has far more possibilities and cannot be guessed from what people know about you.

grade9-ict.question: Gaining access to a computer system without permission is called:
grade9-ict.answer: Hacking
grade9-ict.hint: It is done without the owner’s permission.
grade9-ict.explanation: Hacking is gaining unauthorised access to a computer system or network.

grade9-ict.question: An email claims to be from a bank and asks the reader to type their password on a linked page. This is:
grade9-ict.answer: Phishing
grade9-ict.hint: It fishes for the reader’s details by pretending to be someone trusted.
grade9-ict.explanation: Phishing tries to trick a user into handing over passwords or bank details by imitating a trusted organisation.

grade9-ict.question: What should you do with an unexpected email attachment from someone you do not know?
options: Do not open it and delete the message
Forward it to your friends first
Open it to see what is inside
grade9-ict.answer: Do not open it and delete the message
acceptableAnswers: Do not open it and delete the message
grade9-ict.hint: The attachment is the risk.
grade9-ict.explanation: Unexpected attachments are a common way of spreading malicious software, so they should not be opened.

grade9-ict.question: What does encryption do to data?
options: Scrambles it so only someone with the key can read it
Deletes it permanently so that nobody can recover it
Copies it to a second disk kept in another building
Makes the file smaller so that it is quicker to send
grade9-ict.answer: Scrambles it so only someone with the key can read it
acceptableAnswers: Scrambles it so only someone with the key can read it
grade9-ict.hint: It protects the data even if it is stolen.
grade9-ict.explanation: Encryption converts data into a form that is unreadable without the correct key.

grade9-ict.question: A shop wants to protect customer data held on its network from outside attack. Which measure addresses that directly?
grade9-ict.answer: Installing a firewall
grade9-ict.hint: Something must stand between the network and the outside.
grade9-ict.explanation: A firewall controls which traffic may enter or leave the network, blocking unauthorised access.

grade9-ict.question: What is the main purpose of making a backup?
options: So the files open more quickly whenever they are next needed
So the data can be recovered if the original is lost or damaged
So the data cannot be read by anyone outside the company
So the disk has more free space for new work to be saved
grade9-ict.answer: So the data can be recovered if the original is lost or damaged
acceptableAnswers: So the data can be recovered if the original is lost or damaged
grade9-ict.hint: Think about what happens after a disaster.
grade9-ict.explanation: A backup is a spare copy kept so the data can be restored after loss, theft, fire or corruption.

grade9-ict.question: Where should a backup of a school’s data ideally be kept?
options: In a different building from the original
On the desk beside the computer
On the same hard disk as the original
In the same computer, in another folder
grade9-ict.answer: In a different building from the original
acceptableAnswers: In a different building from the original
grade9-ict.hint: What would a fire or a burglary destroy?
grade9-ict.explanation: A backup stored beside the original is lost to the same fire, flood or theft, so it should be kept elsewhere.

grade9-ict.question: A business backs up once a year. What is the main risk?
options: The backup would be too small to store
The computers would run more slowly
Up to a year of work could be lost
grade9-ict.answer: Up to a year of work could be lost
acceptableAnswers: Up to a year of work could be lost
grade9-ict.hint: How much work sits between two backups?
grade9-ict.explanation: Everything created since the last backup is unprotected, so a yearly backup risks losing a year of work.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is personal data?
options: The name of the capital city
A pupil’s name and date of birth
grade9-ict.answer: A pupil’s name and date of birth
acceptableAnswers: A pupil’s name and date of birth
grade9-ict.hint: It identifies one living person.
grade9-ict.explanation: Personal data is information that identifies a living individual, such as a name, address or date of birth.

grade9-ict.question: Why should you be careful about posting your home address on social media?
options: Strangers could use it to find or target you
The address would be spelled incorrectly
It would use too much storage
The post would take longer to load
grade9-ict.answer: Strangers could use it to find or target you
acceptableAnswers: Strangers could use it to find or target you
grade9-ict.hint: Who else can read a public post?
grade9-ict.explanation: A public post can be read by anyone, and an address lets a stranger locate you.

grade9-ict.question: A website collects customers’ addresses to deliver orders, then sells the list to advertisers without asking. Which principle has been broken?
options: Data must be used only for the purpose it was collected for
Data must always be printed on paper before it is deleted
Data must be stored on the fastest disk that is available
Data must be backed up on the same day of every week
grade9-ict.answer: Data must be used only for the purpose it was collected for
acceptableAnswers: Data must be used only for the purpose it was collected for
grade9-ict.hint: What were the addresses given for?
grade9-ict.explanation: Data protection requires that personal data is used only for the stated purpose, and not passed on without consent.

grade9-ict.question: Under data protection rules, personal data held about someone must be:
options: Accurate and kept up to date
grade9-ict.answer: Accurate and kept up to date
acceptableAnswers: Accurate and kept up to date
grade9-ict.hint: What harm does a wrong record do?
grade9-ict.explanation: Data protection principles require personal data to be accurate, kept up to date and held no longer than necessary.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is a right a person normally has over the personal data an organisation holds about them?
options: To be paid every time it is used
To read the data held about other customers
To ask to see it and have mistakes corrected
grade9-ict.answer: To ask to see it and have mistakes corrected
acceptableAnswers: To ask to see it and have mistakes corrected
grade9-ict.hint: It concerns their own record only.
grade9-ict.explanation: A person may ask what data is held about them and require inaccurate data to be corrected.

grade9-ict.question: Copying and selling software you did not pay for is called:
grade9-ict.answer: Software piracy
grade9-ict.hint: It is theft of someone’s work.
grade9-ict.explanation: Software piracy is copying, using or selling software without the licence to do so.

grade9-ict.question: A photograph found on a website is:
options: Never protected once it is published
Owned by whoever downloads it first
Usually protected by copyright and owned by its creator
Free for anyone at all to use because it is online
grade9-ict.answer: Usually protected by copyright and owned by its creator
acceptableAnswers: Usually protected by copyright and owned by its creator
grade9-ict.hint: Being visible is not the same as being free.
grade9-ict.explanation: Publishing something online does not give up copyright; the creator still owns the work.

grade9-ict.question: Copying a paragraph from a website into your project and presenting it as your own writing is:
grade9-ict.answer: Plagiarism
grade9-ict.hint: The source was not credited.
grade9-ict.explanation: Plagiarism is presenting someone else’s words or ideas as your own without acknowledging them.

grade9-ict.question: What is the correct way to use a sentence from a website in your project?
options: Use it as it is; websites are public
Quote it and state where it came from
Change two words and use it as your own
Translate it and use it as your own
grade9-ict.answer: Quote it and state where it came from
acceptableAnswers: Quote it and state where it came from
grade9-ict.hint: The reader must be able to see whose words they are.
grade9-ict.explanation: Acknowledging the source - quoting and referencing it - is what turns copying into legitimate use.

grade9-ict.question: A stranger online asks a pupil to meet alone. What should the pupil do?
options: Agree and take a friend’s phone
Refuse and tell a trusted adult
grade9-ict.answer: Refuse and tell a trusted adult
acceptableAnswers: Refuse and tell a trusted adult
grade9-ict.hint: The safest action involves an adult.
grade9-ict.explanation: Meeting an online stranger is unsafe; the right response is to refuse and tell a trusted adult.

grade9-ict.question: Give the term for gaining access to a computer system without permission.
grade9-ict.answer: Hacking
grade9-ict.hint: It is done without the owner’s consent.
grade9-ict.explanation: Hacking is unauthorised access to a computer system.

grade9-ict.question: Give the term for an email that pretends to come from a bank in order to obtain a password.
grade9-ict.answer: Phishing
grade9-ict.hint: It fishes for your details.
grade9-ict.explanation: Phishing imitates a trusted organisation to trick a user into revealing details.

grade9-ict.question: Give the term for scrambling data so that only someone with the key can read it.
grade9-ict.answer: Encryption
grade9-ict.hint: It protects data even if it is stolen.
grade9-ict.explanation: Encryption makes data unreadable without the correct key.

grade9-ict.question: Give the term for presenting someone else’s work as your own.
grade9-ict.answer: Plagiarism
grade9-ict.hint: The source was not credited.
grade9-ict.explanation: Plagiarism is using another person’s words or ideas without acknowledgement.

grade9-ict.question: Give the term for a spare copy of data kept so it can be restored after a loss.
grade9-ict.answer: Backup
grade9-ict.hint: One word.
grade9-ict.explanation: A backup is a spare copy from which data can be restored.

grade9-ict.question: Reading someone else’s messages on a computer they left signed in is:
options: Wrong, because it invades their privacy
Acceptable, because they left it open
