Wrong only if they find out
grade9-ict.answer: Wrong, because it invades their privacy
acceptableAnswers: Wrong, because it invades their privacy
grade9-ict.hint: Whose messages are they?
grade9-ict.explanation: Their carelessness does not transfer ownership of their private messages; reading them is an invasion of privacy.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these best describes computer ethics?
options: The law that sets the price software may be sold for
The rules of right and wrong behaviour when using computers
The speed at which a computer carries out its instructions
The manual of instructions that comes with a new computer
grade9-ict.answer: The rules of right and wrong behaviour when using computers
acceptableAnswers: The rules of right and wrong behaviour when using computers
grade9-ict.hint: It is about conduct, not equipment.
grade9-ict.explanation: Computer ethics is the study of how computers should and should not be used, and of the responsibilities of those who use them.

grade9-ict.question: A pupil finds a classmate’s password written on a desk. What is the right thing to do?
options: Write it somewhere safer for later
Tell the classmate so they can change it
Use it once to see if it works
grade9-ict.answer: Tell the classmate so they can change it
acceptableAnswers: Tell the classmate so they can change it
grade9-ict.hint: The account belongs to someone else.
grade9-ict.explanation: The password belongs to its owner; telling them lets it be changed before anyone misuses it.

grade9-ict.question: Repeatedly sending threatening or hurtful messages to someone online is called:
grade9-ict.answer: Cyberbullying
grade9-ict.hint: It is bullying carried out through a screen.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cyberbullying is using online messages or posts to threaten, humiliate or harass someone.

grade9-ict.question: What should a pupil do if they receive threatening messages online?
options: Keep the evidence and tell a trusted adult
Send their address so it can be sorted out
grade9-ict.answer: Keep the evidence and tell a trusted adult
acceptableAnswers: Keep the evidence and tell a trusted adult
grade9-ict.hint: The messages themselves are the proof.
grade9-ict.explanation: Saving the messages preserves evidence, and telling a trusted adult brings help; retaliating makes things worse.

grade9-ict.question: What is one effect of computers on employment?
options: No job is affected in any way by the use of computers
Some jobs disappear while new ICT jobs are created
Every job disappears completely within a few years
Only farming jobs are affected by the change
grade9-ict.answer: Some jobs disappear while new ICT jobs are created
acceptableAnswers: Some jobs disappear while new ICT jobs are created
grade9-ict.hint: The change works in both directions.
grade9-ict.explanation: Automation removes some routine jobs and creates others - support, programming, data work - so the effect is a shift, not simply a loss.

grade9-ict.question: What is one economic effect of widespread software piracy?
options: The internet becomes cheaper for everyone who uses it
Computers run faster everywhere the software is used
Developers lose income, so less new software is produced
Hardware prices are fixed by law in every country
grade9-ict.answer: Developers lose income, so less new software is produced
acceptableAnswers: Developers lose income, so less new software is produced
grade9-ict.hint: Who is not being paid?
grade9-ict.explanation: Piracy denies developers the income that funds their work, which reduces what gets written and supported.

grade9-ict.question: A village has no internet access while a nearby town has fast broadband. This difference is known as the:
grade9-ict.answer: Digital divide
grade9-ict.hint: It divides those with access from those without.
grade9-ict.explanation: The digital divide is the gap between people who have good access to ICT and those who do not.

grade9-ict.question: Give the term for information that identifies a living individual, such as a name and address.
grade9-ict.answer: Personal data
grade9-ict.hint: Two words.
grade9-ict.explanation: Personal data is information identifying a living person.

grade9-ict.question: Give the term for the legal right of a creator to control the copying of their work.
grade9-ict.answer: Copyright
grade9-ict.hint: One word.
grade9-ict.explanation: Copyright gives the creator control over how their work is copied and used.

grade9-ict.question: State one thing a data protection act requires an organisation to do with the personal data it holds.
grade9-ict.answer: Keep it accurate and secure
acceptableAnswers: use it only for the stated purpose
not keep it longer than necessary
grade9-ict.hint: Think about accuracy, purpose and security.
grade9-ict.explanation: Data protection principles require personal data to be accurate, kept securely, used only for its stated purpose and not kept longer than needed.

grade9-ict.question: Give the term for repeatedly sending threatening or hurtful messages to someone online.
grade9-ict.answer: Cyberbullying
grade9-ict.hint: One word, two halves.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cyberbullying is harassment carried out through online messages or posts.

grade9-ict.question: What is a single page of a presentation called?
grade9-ict.answer: A slide
grade9-ict.hint: It is shown one at a time on a screen.
grade9-ict.explanation: A presentation is made of slides, shown one after another.

grade9-ict.question: What does a design template give a presentation?
options: A printed copy of the slides for the audience
The words that will be written on every slide
A consistent set of colours, fonts and backgrounds
A recording of the speaker reading the slides
grade9-ict.answer: A consistent set of colours, fonts and backgrounds
acceptableAnswers: A consistent set of colours, fonts and backgrounds
grade9-ict.hint: It sets how the slides look, not what they say.
grade9-ict.explanation: A design template applies one coordinated look - colours, fonts and background - to every slide.

grade9-ict.question: Why should a presentation use the same design template throughout?
options: It removes the need for a title slide
It looks consistent and is easier to follow
It stops the slides from being printed
It makes the file smaller than any other option
grade9-ict.answer: It looks consistent and is easier to follow
acceptableAnswers: It looks consistent and is easier to follow
grade9-ict.hint: Think about the audience, not the file.
grade9-ict.explanation: A consistent look keeps the audience focused on the content instead of a changing appearance.

grade9-ict.question: What is a slide master used for?
options: To set formatting that applies to every slide at once
To lock the whole presentation with a password
To print the slides six to a page
grade9-ict.answer: To set formatting that applies to every slide at once
acceptableAnswers: To set formatting that applies to every slide at once
grade9-ict.hint: Change it once, and every slide changes.
grade9-ict.explanation: The slide master holds the formatting inherited by every slide, so one change updates them all.

grade9-ict.question: A school logo must appear in the same corner of all 30 slides. What is the most efficient way to do it?
options: Place it once on the slide master
Print it on the handouts only
Add it to the first slide and hope it repeats
Paste it separately onto each of the 30 slides
grade9-ict.answer: Place it once on the slide master
acceptableAnswers: Place it once on the slide master
grade9-ict.hint: One action should affect every slide.
grade9-ict.explanation: Anything placed on the slide master appears on every slide that uses it, so the logo is added once.

grade9-ict.question: Why might a presentation use more than one slide master?
options: It is required before a presentation can be printed
A presentation cannot have more than ten slides otherwise
Different sections need different layouts and looks
grade9-ict.answer: Different sections need different layouts and looks
acceptableAnswers: Different sections need different layouts and looks
grade9-ict.hint: Think of a long talk split into parts.
grade9-ict.explanation: Multiple masters let different sections of one presentation carry different designs while each stays internally consistent.

grade9-ict.question: What does an animation do in a presentation?
options: Controls how an item appears or moves on a slide
Sets the font of the whole presentation
grade9-ict.answer: Controls how an item appears or moves on a slide
acceptableAnswers: Controls how an item appears or moves on a slide
grade9-ict.hint: It affects one object on the slide.
grade9-ict.explanation: An animation controls how an object enters, moves or leaves a slide.

grade9-ict.question: What is a slide transition?
options: The time and date the presentation was first created
The order in which the slides will be printed out
The effect used when moving from one slide to the next
The movement of a single bullet point on one slide
grade9-ict.answer: The effect used when moving from one slide to the next
acceptableAnswers: The effect used when moving from one slide to the next
grade9-ict.hint: It happens between slides, not inside one.
grade9-ict.explanation: A transition is the visual effect shown as one slide is replaced by the next; an animation acts on objects within a slide.

grade9-ict.question: Why should animations be used sparingly in a presentation?
options: They make the slides impossible to edit
They use up the computer’s memory permanently
Too many distract the audience from the message
grade9-ict.answer: Too many distract the audience from the message
acceptableAnswers: Too many distract the audience from the message
grade9-ict.hint: Think about the audience again.
grade9-ict.explanation: Excessive movement draws attention away from the content the presentation exists to communicate.

grade9-ict.question: Which is the best way to show how sales changed over twelve months?
grade9-ict.answer: A line chart
grade9-ict.hint: The data changes over time.
grade9-ict.explanation: A line chart shows a trend over time far more clearly than the same figures written out.

grade9-ict.question: Which chart is best for showing each subject’s share of a class total?
grade9-ict.answer: A pie chart
grade9-ict.hint: The whole is divided into parts.
grade9-ict.explanation: A pie chart shows parts of a whole as slices, so shares of a total are read at a glance.

grade9-ict.question: Which is the best way to present exact figures that the audience must read precisely?
grade9-ict.answer: A table
grade9-ict.hint: Exact numbers must be readable.
grade9-ict.explanation: A table shows exact values; a chart shows a pattern but not precise figures.

grade9-ict.question: A chart is pasted onto a slide but nobody can tell what the axes mean. What is missing?
options: Axis titles and a chart title
A design template for the slide
A speaker note for the presenter
grade9-ict.answer: Axis titles and a chart title
acceptableAnswers: Axis titles and a chart title
grade9-ict.hint: A chart must label what it shows.
grade9-ict.explanation: Without a title and labelled axes a chart cannot be interpreted, however well it is drawn.

grade9-ict.question: What are speaker notes used for?
options: The title of the presentation, repeated on every slide
Reminders for the presenter that the audience does not see
Extra slides shown to the audience at the end of the talk
The list of animations used on each slide of the talk
grade9-ict.answer: Reminders for the presenter that the audience does not see
acceptableAnswers: Reminders for the presenter that the audience does not see
grade9-ict.hint: They are for the person talking.
grade9-ict.explanation: Speaker notes are prompts attached to a slide, visible to the presenter but not projected.

grade9-ict.question: What is a handout in a presentation program?
options: A slide with no text on it
Printed slides given to the audience
grade9-ict.answer: Printed slides given to the audience
acceptableAnswers: Printed slides given to the audience
grade9-ict.hint: It is something the audience takes away.
grade9-ict.explanation: A handout prints several slides to a page for the audience to keep and annotate.

grade9-ict.question: Which view shows one slide with its speaker notes underneath, ready to be printed?
grade9-ict.answer: Notes Page view
grade9-ict.hint: The name says what is on the page.
grade9-ict.explanation: Notes Page view shows a slide with its notes below it, which is the layout that prints.

grade9-ict.question: What is the purpose of Print Preview?
options: To record the presentation as it is being given
To change the order in which the animations will run
To see exactly how the pages will look before printing
To send the finished file to someone else by email
grade9-ict.answer: To see exactly how the pages will look before printing
acceptableAnswers: To see exactly how the pages will look before printing
grade9-ict.hint: It is used before paper is used.
grade9-ict.explanation: Print Preview shows the printed result on screen so mistakes are caught before paper and ink are spent.

grade9-ict.question: What is a storyboard used for?
options: Printing the slides for the audience to take away afterwards
Recording the narration that plays over the finished clip
Planning the order and content of scenes or slides before making them
Storing the finished video file once all the editing is done
grade9-ict.answer: Planning the order and content of scenes or slides before making them
acceptableAnswers: Planning the order and content of scenes or slides before making them
grade9-ict.hint: It comes before the work, not after.
grade9-ict.explanation: A storyboard sketches each scene or slide in order so the sequence can be planned before production starts.

grade9-ict.question: Why is a storyboard drawn before a video is filmed?
options: A video cannot be edited once the filming has been finished
The camera needs it before it will record anything at all
Mistakes in the plan are cheap to fix; mistakes in filming are not
It replaces the need for a script and for any narration
grade9-ict.answer: Mistakes in the plan are cheap to fix; mistakes in filming are not
acceptableAnswers: Mistakes in the plan are cheap to fix; mistakes in filming are not
grade9-ict.hint: Compare the cost of redrawing with the cost of refilming.
grade9-ict.explanation: Planning on paper lets the sequence be corrected before time, equipment and people are committed to filming.

grade9-ict.question: Which is the most suitable tool for assembling clips, adding recorded narration and overlaying text on a video?
grade9-ict.answer: Video editing software
grade9-ict.hint: Only one of these works with moving images.
grade9-ict.explanation: Video editing software sequences clips and adds narration, titles and overlay text.

grade9-ict.question: Name the feature that holds the formatting inherited by every slide, so one change updates them all.
grade9-ict.answer: Slide master
grade9-ict.hint: Two words.
grade9-ict.explanation: The slide master carries formatting shared by every slide.

grade9-ict.question: Give the term for the visual effect used when moving from one slide to the next.
grade9-ict.answer: Transition
grade9-ict.hint: It happens between slides.
grade9-ict.explanation: A transition is the effect shown as one slide replaces another.

grade9-ict.question: Give the term for printed slides given to the audience to keep.
grade9-ict.answer: Handout
grade9-ict.hint: The audience takes it away.
grade9-ict.explanation: A handout prints slides for the audience.

grade9-ict.question: Name the planning document that sketches each scene of a video in order before filming begins.
grade9-ict.answer: Storyboard
grade9-ict.hint: One word, two halves.
grade9-ict.explanation: A storyboard plans the sequence of scenes before production.

grade9-ict.question: Name the type of chart that shows each part as a slice of a whole.
grade9-ict.answer: Pie chart
grade9-ict.hint: It is round.
grade9-ict.explanation: A pie chart shows parts of a whole as slices.

grade9-ict.question: A presentation is to be printed with six slides on each sheet. Where is that chosen?
options: In the design template, as a page setting
In the print settings, as a handout layout
On the slide master, as a repeating layout
In the animation pane, as a timing setting
grade9-ict.answer: In the print settings, as a handout layout
acceptableAnswers: In the print settings, as a handout layout
grade9-ict.hint: It is a printing choice, not a design one.
grade9-ict.explanation: The number of slides per printed page is a handout setting chosen when printing.

grade9-ict.question: Print Preview shows the last slide printing almost empty on a page of its own. What is the best response?
options: Print it anyway and throw the page away
grade9-ict.answer: Adjust the layout before printing
grade9-ict.hint: That is what a preview is for.
grade9-ict.explanation: Preview exists so the layout can be corrected before paper and ink are used.

grade9-ict.question: Which tool is most suitable for assembling drawn panels with speech bubbles into an educational comic strip?
options: A spreadsheet with the gridlines hidden
A database of the characters and their lines
A web browser with a drawing add-on
grade9-ict.answer: Comic or graphics authoring software
grade9-ict.hint: It must place pictures and text together on a panel.
grade9-ict.explanation: Comic and graphics authoring tools lay out panels, artwork and speech bubbles in sequence.

grade9-ict.question: What should decide which authoring tool is chosen for a project?
options: Whichever tool produces files of the largest size
Whichever tool has the most buttons on its toolbar
The kind of media the project needs and who the audience is
Whichever tool was released most recently by its maker
grade9-ict.answer: The kind of media the project needs and who the audience is
acceptableAnswers: The kind of media the project needs and who the audience is
grade9-ict.hint: Fit the tool to the job.
grade9-ict.explanation: A tool is chosen for the media it handles and the audience it must reach, not for its novelty.

grade9-ict.question: An animation is made of a sequence of still pictures. What is each one called?
grade9-ict.answer: A frame
grade9-ict.hint: They are shown one after another, very quickly.
grade9-ict.explanation: Each still picture in an animation is a frame; playing them in quick succession creates movement.

grade9-ict.question: What creates the impression of movement in an animation?
options: Making the screen brighter for the length of the clip
Adding music to the clip while the pictures stay still
Printing the frames on paper in the order they were drawn
Showing slightly different frames quickly, one after another
grade9-ict.answer: Showing slightly different frames quickly, one after another
acceptableAnswers: Showing slightly different frames quickly, one after another
grade9-ict.hint: Each frame differs a little from the last.
grade9-ict.explanation: The eye blends rapidly shown frames that each differ slightly, which reads as movement.

grade9-ict.question: An animated clip plays jerkily. Which change is most likely to smooth it?
options: Play it on a bigger screen
Add more colours to each frame
grade9-ict.answer: Use more frames per second
grade9-ict.hint: The gap between frames is what is being seen.
grade9-ict.explanation: More frames per second means smaller changes between frames, so the movement looks continuous.

grade9-ict.question: What is narration in a video?
options: A recorded voice explaining what is shown
The list of people who made it
grade9-ict.answer: A recorded voice explaining what is shown
acceptableAnswers: A recorded voice explaining what is shown
grade9-ict.hint: Someone is speaking over the pictures.
grade9-ict.explanation: Narration is a recorded spoken commentary added to the video.

grade9-ict.question: Text placed on top of the picture in a video, such as a name or a caption, is called:
grade9-ict.answer: Overlay text
grade9-ict.hint: It lies over the image.
grade9-ict.explanation: Overlay text is placed on top of the video image to caption or label what is being shown.

grade9-ict.question: Why is narration usually recorded after the clips have been put in order?
options: So the words match the pictures and their timing
Because a microphone cannot be used earlier
So the video file is smaller
Because the camera must be switched off first
grade9-ict.answer: So the words match the pictures and their timing
acceptableAnswers: So the words match the pictures and their timing
grade9-ict.hint: The commentary has to fit what is on screen.
grade9-ict.explanation: Once the sequence and its timings are fixed, the narration can be written and recorded to match them.

grade9-ict.question: In a comic strip, what is each separate box of the story called?
grade9-ict.answer: A panel
grade9-ict.hint: The strip is read from one to the next.
grade9-ict.explanation: A comic strip is made of panels, each showing one moment of the story.

grade9-ict.question: In a comic strip, what does a speech bubble show?
options: The page number of the strip
The words a character is saying
The time of day in the story
grade9-ict.answer: The words a character is saying
acceptableAnswers: The words a character is saying
grade9-ict.hint: It points at whoever is talking.
grade9-ict.explanation: A speech bubble holds a character’s spoken words and its tail points to the speaker.

grade9-ict.question: Why is a comic strip a useful way of teaching a topic to younger pupils?
options: It removes the need for any words at all on the page
It takes far longer to read than the same page of a textbook
Pictures and short text together make the ideas easier to follow
It can only be read by adults who know the topic already
grade9-ict.answer: Pictures and short text together make the ideas easier to follow
acceptableAnswers: Pictures and short text together make the ideas easier to follow
grade9-ict.hint: Think about how much text a young reader can manage.
grade9-ict.explanation: Combining a picture with a short caption carries the idea with far less reading than a page of prose.

grade9-ict.question: Which health problem is most associated with staring at a screen for hours?
grade9-ict.answer: Eye strain
grade9-ict.hint: Which part of the body is working hardest?
grade9-ict.explanation: Long periods of close screen work tire the eye muscles, causing eye strain, headaches and blurred vision.

grade9-ict.question: Sitting badly at a computer for long periods most often causes:
grade9-ict.answer: Back and neck pain
grade9-ict.hint: Think about which parts hold you upright.
grade9-ict.explanation: Poor posture strains the muscles of the back and neck, which is why chair and screen height matter.

grade9-ict.question: What does RSI stand for?
grade9-ict.answer: Repetitive Strain Injury
grade9-ict.hint: It comes from doing the same movement over and over.
grade9-ict.explanation: RSI - Repetitive Strain Injury - affects the wrists, hands and arms after long periods of typing or mouse use.

grade9-ict.question: Which part of the body is most affected by Repetitive Strain Injury from typing?
grade9-ict.answer: The wrists and hands
grade9-ict.hint: Which part makes the repeated movement?
grade9-ict.explanation: Typing and mouse use repeat small movements of the wrists and fingers, which is where RSI appears.

grade9-ict.question: A pupil complains of headaches and dry eyes after two hours at a computer with no break. What is the most likely cause?
options: Too little RAM in the computer
Eye strain from continuous screen use
A fault in the hard disk
grade9-ict.answer: Eye strain from continuous screen use
acceptableAnswers: Eye strain from continuous screen use
grade9-ict.hint: The symptoms are in the eyes and head.
grade9-ict.explanation: Continuous close focus without breaks tires the eyes, producing headaches, dryness and blurred vision.

grade9-ict.question: What is the best way to reduce eye strain when working at a computer?
options: Sit as close to the screen as possible
Take regular breaks and look away from the screen
Work in a completely dark room
grade9-ict.answer: Take regular breaks and look away from the screen
acceptableAnswers: Take regular breaks and look away from the screen
grade9-ict.hint: The eyes need to refocus at a distance.
grade9-ict.explanation: Regular breaks let the eye muscles relax and refocus, which is the standard advice for screen work.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these helps prevent back pain at a computer?
options: A wireless mouse used with the other hand
An adjustable chair with good back support
A larger monitor set further back from the desk
A faster processor inside the computer itself
grade9-ict.answer: An adjustable chair with good back support
acceptableAnswers: An adjustable chair with good back support
grade9-ict.hint: Only one of these changes how you sit.
grade9-ict.explanation: An adjustable chair supporting the lower back keeps the spine in a natural position.

grade9-ict.question: How should a monitor be positioned to reduce neck strain?
options: At about eye level, an arm’s length away
As low as possible on the desk
Turned to face away from the user
Directly in front of a bright window
grade9-ict.answer: At about eye level, an arm’s length away
acceptableAnswers: At about eye level, an arm’s length away
grade9-ict.hint: The head should not have to tilt.
grade9-ict.explanation: A screen at eye level and roughly an arm’s length away keeps the neck straight and the eyes comfortable.

grade9-ict.question: Which measure most directly reduces Repetitive Strain Injury?
options: A brighter monitor placed on the desk
A larger hard disk inside the computer
A faster internet connection to the room
A wrist rest and regular breaks from typing
grade9-ict.answer: A wrist rest and regular breaks from typing
acceptableAnswers: A wrist rest and regular breaks from typing
grade9-ict.hint: It must change how the hands work.
grade9-ict.explanation: Supporting the wrists and pausing regularly breaks the repetition that causes RSI.

grade9-ict.question: A computer room has bright sunlight reflecting off every screen. What is the best solution?
grade9-ict.answer: Fit blinds at the windows
grade9-ict.hint: Deal with the light, not the computers.
grade9-ict.explanation: Blinds control the light that causes glare, which is what makes the screens hard to read.

grade9-ict.question: Why should food and drink be kept away from computers?
options: A spill can damage the equipment and cause a shock
Crumbs make the processor run much faster
grade9-ict.answer: A spill can damage the equipment and cause a shock
acceptableAnswers: A spill can damage the equipment and cause a shock
grade9-ict.hint: Think about liquid and electricity.
grade9-ict.explanation: Liquid spilled into a keyboard or a socket damages equipment and creates a risk of electric shock.

grade9-ict.question: Trailing cables across the floor of a computer room are mainly a:
grade9-ict.answer: Trip hazard
grade9-ict.hint: What happens when someone walks past?
grade9-ict.explanation: Loose cables across a walkway cause trips and falls, and should be secured or routed away.

grade9-ict.question: What should be done if a power cable is frayed or damaged?
options: Use it only for short periods
Report it and stop using that equipment
Pull it out by the cable
Wrap it in paper and carry on
grade9-ict.answer: Report it and stop using that equipment
acceptableAnswers: Report it and stop using that equipment
grade9-ict.hint: A damaged cable is an electrical risk.
grade9-ict.explanation: A damaged cable can cause a shock or a fire; it must be reported and the equipment taken out of use.

grade9-ict.question: Why should too many devices not be plugged into one socket?
options: It can overload the circuit and start a fire
It reduces the screen resolution slightly
grade9-ict.answer: It can overload the circuit and start a fire
acceptableAnswers: It can overload the circuit and start a fire
grade9-ict.hint: Think about the current in one wire.
grade9-ict.explanation: Overloading a socket draws more current than the circuit is rated for, which causes overheating and fire.

grade9-ict.question: A computer room must be kept ventilated mainly because:
options: Equipment generates heat that must escape
Cool air makes the software run correctly
Fresh air cleans the hard disks
grade9-ict.answer: Equipment generates heat that must escape
acceptableAnswers: Equipment generates heat that must escape
grade9-ict.hint: What do many machines produce in one room?
grade9-ict.explanation: Computers give off heat; without ventilation the room and the equipment overheat.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is a normal rule in a computer laboratory?
options: Do not eat or drink at the computers
Move the computers whenever you like
grade9-ict.answer: Do not eat or drink at the computers
acceptableAnswers: Do not eat or drink at the computers
grade9-ict.hint: Three of these would cause a problem.
grade9-ict.explanation: No food or drink is a standard laboratory rule because a spill damages equipment.

grade9-ict.question: Why should a pupil log off rather than just walk away from a computer?
options: The files would be deleted automatically
Someone else could use their account
grade9-ict.answer: Someone else could use their account
acceptableAnswers: Someone else could use their account
grade9-ict.hint: The account is still open.
grade9-ict.explanation: An account left signed in can be used by anyone, and whatever they do is recorded as the owner’s work.

grade9-ict.question: What should be done before leaving the computer laboratory at the end of a lesson?
options: Turn the monitor to face the wall
Shut down the computer and push in the chair
Unplug the network cable at the back
grade9-ict.answer: Shut down the computer and push in the chair
acceptableAnswers: Shut down the computer and push in the chair
grade9-ict.hint: Leave the place safe and tidy for the next class.
grade9-ict.explanation: Shutting down properly protects the equipment and data, and a pushed-in chair keeps the walkway clear.

grade9-ict.question: How should a screen be cleaned?
options: With a soft dry cloth made for screens
With plenty of water poured onto it
grade9-ict.answer: With a soft dry cloth made for screens
acceptableAnswers: With a soft dry cloth made for screens
grade9-ict.hint: The surface scratches easily and hates liquid.
grade9-ict.explanation: A soft cloth removes dust without scratching the surface or letting liquid into the equipment.

grade9-ict.question: Why should a USB flash drive be removed using "safely remove hardware" rather than simply pulled out?
options: Data still being written could be lost or corrupted
The drive would lose the label printed on its case
The computer would restart as soon as it was removed
The USB port would be scratched by the metal casing
grade9-ict.answer: Data still being written could be lost or corrupted
acceptableAnswers: Data still being written could be lost or corrupted
grade9-ict.hint: The computer may not have finished writing.
grade9-ict.explanation: Ejecting safely tells the operating system to finish writing, so no file is left half-written and unreadable.

grade9-ict.question: Write in full what RSI stands for.
grade9-ict.answer: Repetitive Strain Injury
grade9-ict.hint: Three words.
grade9-ict.explanation: RSI stands for Repetitive Strain Injury.

grade9-ict.question: Name the eye problem caused by staring at a screen for long periods without a break.
grade9-ict.answer: Eye strain
grade9-ict.hint: Two words.
grade9-ict.explanation: Continuous screen work causes eye strain.

grade9-ict.question: State one way of reducing back pain when working at a computer.
grade9-ict.answer: Use an adjustable chair with back support
acceptableAnswers: Use an adjustable chair with back support
use a chair with back support
grade9-ict.hint: It concerns how you sit.
grade9-ict.explanation: An adjustable chair supporting the lower back keeps the spine in a natural position.

grade9-ict.question: State one reason why food and drink are not allowed near computers.
grade9-ict.answer: A spill can damage the equipment
acceptableAnswers: A spill can damage the equipment
liquid can cause an electric shock
a spill can cause a shock
grade9-ict.hint: Think about liquid and electricity.
grade9-ict.explanation: Spilled liquid damages equipment and creates a risk of electric shock.

grade9-ict.question: State what a pupil should do to their account before leaving a shared computer.
grade9-ict.answer: Log off
grade9-ict.hint: Two words.
grade9-ict.explanation: Logging off stops anyone else using the account that is still open.

grade9-ict.question: How should a computer be switched off at the end of the day?
options: By closing the lid and walking away from the machine
Using Shut down, so the operating system closes properly
By pulling the power plug out of the wall socket
By switching off the monitor and leaving the rest on
grade9-ict.answer: Using Shut down, so the operating system closes properly
acceptableAnswers: Using Shut down, so the operating system closes properly
grade9-ict.hint: The software must finish what it is doing.
grade9-ict.explanation: Shut down lets the operating system close its files first; cutting the power can corrupt them.

grade9-ict.question: Why should the vents on a computer case not be blocked?
grade9-ict.answer: The machine would overheat
grade9-ict.hint: Air must be able to move through it.
grade9-ict.explanation: Vents let hot air escape; blocking them traps the heat the components produce.

grade9-ict.question: How should a laptop be carried between classrooms?
options: Closed, in a padded bag, held with both hands
Balanced on top of a pile of books
By the power cable hanging down
Open, carried by the screen alone
grade9-ict.answer: Closed, in a padded bag, held with both hands
acceptableAnswers: Closed, in a padded bag, held with both hands
grade9-ict.hint: Protect the screen and the hinges.
grade9-ict.explanation: A padded bag protects it from knocks, and carrying it by the screen or the cable damages the hinge and the socket.

grade9-ict.question: A monitor shows nothing at all. What should be checked first?
options: That a new monitor is bought
That the hard disk is replaced
That it is switched on and plugged in
That the operating system is reinstalled
grade9-ict.answer: That it is switched on and plugged in
acceptableAnswers: That it is switched on and plugged in
grade9-ict.hint: Start with the simplest possible cause.
grade9-ict.explanation: Troubleshooting begins with the cheapest and simplest check - power and connections - before anything is replaced.

grade9-ict.question: A keyboard types nothing. What is the first thing to check?
options: That the mouse battery is new
That the monitor brightness is correct
That the cable is properly connected
grade9-ict.answer: That the cable is properly connected
acceptableAnswers: That the cable is properly connected
grade9-ict.hint: A loose connection is the commonest cause.
grade9-ict.explanation: Checking the connection costs nothing and explains most dead peripherals.

grade9-ict.question: What is the correct order of the first steps in troubleshooting?
options: Reinstall the operating system, then look at the cables
Identify the problem, check the simple causes, then test the fix
Call the supplier before looking at anything
Replace the parts, then identify the problem
grade9-ict.answer: Identify the problem, check the simple causes, then test the fix
acceptableAnswers: Identify the problem, check the simple causes, then test the fix
grade9-ict.hint: Understand it before changing anything.
grade9-ict.explanation: Troubleshooting is: identify the problem, check the simplest causes, apply a fix, then test that it worked.

grade9-ict.question: Why should only one change be made at a time when solving a fault?
options: So the warranty stays valid for longer
So you know which change actually fixed it
grade9-ict.answer: So you know which change actually fixed it
acceptableAnswers: So you know which change actually fixed it
grade9-ict.hint: Two changes at once tell you nothing.
grade9-ict.explanation: Changing one thing at a time is what makes the result meaningful - otherwise the real cause is never known.

grade9-ict.question: After a fault has been fixed, what should be done last?
options: Test that the system works and record what was done
Switch the computer off at once and say nothing
grade9-ict.answer: Test that the system works and record what was done
acceptableAnswers: Test that the system works and record what was done
grade9-ict.hint: The job is not finished until it is proved and written down.
grade9-ict.explanation: Testing confirms the fix and a record helps whoever meets the same fault next time.

grade9-ict.question: A program has stopped responding. What is the usual first action?
options: Close it using the task manager
Switch the computer off at the wall
grade9-ict.answer: Close it using the task manager
acceptableAnswers: Close it using the task manager
grade9-ict.hint: Deal with the one program before the whole machine.
grade9-ict.explanation: Ending the unresponsive task closes it without risking the data in every other program.

grade9-ict.question: Why is switching a computer off at the wall a poor way to close a frozen program?
options: It deletes the operating system and everything stored with it
It takes far longer than any other way of closing a program
It permanently damages the keyboard and the mouse together
Unsaved work in other programs is lost and files can be corrupted
grade9-ict.answer: Unsaved work in other programs is lost and files can be corrupted
acceptableAnswers: Unsaved work in other programs is lost and files can be corrupted
grade9-ict.hint: Think about everything else that was open.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cutting power stops every program mid-write, losing unsaved work and risking corrupted files.

grade9-ict.question: A document has been deleted by mistake. Where should you look first?
options: The Downloads page of a browser
grade9-ict.answer: The Recycle Bin
grade9-ict.hint: Deleted files are not gone immediately.
grade9-ict.explanation: A deleted file is normally moved to the Recycle Bin and can be restored from there.

grade9-ict.question: A file was deleted and the Recycle Bin has been emptied. What is the best chance of getting it back?
grade9-ict.answer: Restore it from a backup
grade9-ict.hint: This is the situation backups exist for.
grade9-ict.explanation: Once the Recycle Bin is emptied the file is no longer in it; a backup is the reliable way to recover it.

grade9-ict.question: A printer will not print and a queue of jobs is waiting. Which check is most likely to explain it?
options: Whether the printer is out of paper or offline
Whether the monitor is set too bright
grade9-ict.answer: Whether the printer is out of paper or offline
acceptableAnswers: Whether the printer is out of paper or offline
grade9-ict.hint: Look at the printer itself.
grade9-ict.explanation: A stalled queue is usually the printer being out of paper, out of ink, offline or unplugged.

grade9-ict.question: One computer in a laboratory cannot reach the internet while all the others can. What is the most sensible first check?
options: Every other computer in the room
That machine’s own network cable and settings
The electricity supply to the building
grade9-ict.answer: That machine’s own network cable and settings
acceptableAnswers: That machine’s own network cable and settings
grade9-ict.hint: What is different about that one machine?
grade9-ict.explanation: If the others work, the shared connection is fine, so the fault is almost certainly local to that machine.

grade9-ict.question: Every computer in the laboratory has lost internet access at the same moment. What is the most likely cause?
options: A broken keyboard on one of the twenty machines
A fault in the shared connection, router or service
A virus on one pupil’s account in the laboratory
Twenty separate cable faults happening at once
grade9-ict.answer: A fault in the shared connection, router or service
acceptableAnswers: A fault in the shared connection, router or service
grade9-ict.hint: What do all of them have in common?
grade9-ict.explanation: When every machine fails together the fault is in what they share: the router, the line or the provider.

grade9-ict.question: A computer has become very slow and shows unexpected pop-up messages. What should be done?
grade9-ict.answer: Run a full antivirus scan
grade9-ict.hint: The symptoms suggest an infection.
grade9-ict.explanation: Slowness with unexpected pop-ups is a classic sign of malicious software, so a full scan is the right response.

grade9-ict.question: A computer says the disk is full. Which action frees space?
options: Add more RAM so the computer has extra working memory
Change the desktop theme to one that uses fewer colours
Increase the screen resolution so more fits on the display
Delete files that are no longer needed and empty the Recycle Bin
grade9-ict.answer: Delete files that are no longer needed and empty the Recycle Bin
acceptableAnswers: Delete files that are no longer needed and empty the Recycle Bin
grade9-ict.hint: The problem is storage, not memory.
grade9-ict.explanation: Disk space is freed by removing unwanted files; adding RAM does not change storage at all.

grade9-ict.question: A newly connected printer is not recognised by the computer. Apart from the cable, what is the most likely cause?
options: The printer needs a bigger hard disk
The driver has not been installed
The monitor is the wrong size
grade9-ict.answer: The driver has not been installed
acceptableAnswers: The driver has not been installed
grade9-ict.hint: The operating system needs software for that model.
grade9-ict.explanation: Without the correct device driver the operating system cannot communicate with the printer.

grade9-ict.question: The screen image is there but very dim and hard to read. What should be checked?
grade9-ict.answer: The brightness setting
grade9-ict.hint: The picture is present, only faint.
grade9-ict.explanation: An image that is present but dim points to the brightness or backlight setting, not to a dead connection.

grade9-ict.question: A pupil cannot sign in and is sure the password is correct. Which is worth checking before anything else?
grade9-ict.answer: Whether Caps Lock is on
grade9-ict.hint: Passwords are case sensitive.
grade9-ict.explanation: Caps Lock changes every letter typed, and passwords are case sensitive, so it is the first thing to rule out.

grade9-ict.question: Why is it useful to ask the user exactly what happened before the fault appeared?
options: It makes the computer restart faster
It frees space on the disk
It narrows down the possible causes
It is required before switching on
grade9-ict.answer: It narrows down the possible causes
acceptableAnswers: It narrows down the possible causes
grade9-ict.hint: Information comes before action.
grade9-ict.explanation: What changed just before the fault usually points straight at the cause, which is why identification comes first.

grade9-ict.question: A fault cannot be solved after the simple checks have all been made. What should be done next?
options: Report it to the technician with a note of what was already tried
Ignore it and use another machine without telling anyone
Open the computer case and remove parts at random
grade9-ict.answer: Report it to the technician with a note of what was already tried
acceptableAnswers: Report it to the technician with a note of what was already tried
grade9-ict.hint: Escalate, and pass on what you learned.
grade9-ict.explanation: Reporting the fault with the checks already made saves the technician repeating them and gets the machine fixed properly.

grade9-ict.question: Which keyboard shortcut normally undoes the last action?
grade9-ict.answer: Ctrl + Z
grade9-ict.hint: It is at the bottom left of the keyboard.
grade9-ict.explanation: Ctrl + Z undoes the last action, which is often the quickest recovery from a mistake.

grade9-ict.question: A monitor is blank. State the first thing that should be checked.
grade9-ict.answer: That it is switched on and plugged in
acceptableAnswers: That it is switched on and plugged in
grade9-ict.hint: Start with the simplest possible cause.
grade9-ict.explanation: Power and connections are checked before anything is replaced.

grade9-ict.question: Name the place a deleted file is normally moved to, from which it can be restored.
grade9-ict.answer: Recycle Bin
grade9-ict.hint: Two words.
grade9-ict.explanation: A deleted file is moved to the Recycle Bin and can be restored from there.

grade9-ict.question: Give the keyboard shortcut that undoes the last action.
grade9-ict.answer: Ctrl + Z
grade9-ict.hint: Z is at the bottom left.
grade9-ict.explanation: Ctrl + Z undoes the last action.

grade9-ict.question: State why only one change should be made at a time when solving a fault.
grade9-ict.answer: So you know which change fixed it
acceptableAnswers: So you know which change fixed it
so you know what fixed the problem
grade9-ict.hint: Two changes at once tell you nothing.
grade9-ict.explanation: One change at a time is what makes the result meaningful.

grade9-ict.question: Name the software that must be installed before the operating system can use a newly connected printer.
grade9-ict.answer: Driver
grade9-ict.hint: It drives that one device.
grade9-ict.explanation: A device driver lets the operating system communicate with that model of printer.

grade9-ict.question: A database is best described as:
options: a word-processed document with a table
a single spreadsheet containing one table
an organised collection of related data stored so it can be easily accessed, managed and updated
a program that draws charts from numbers
grade9-ict.answer: an organised collection of related data stored so it can be easily accessed, managed and updated
acceptableAnswers: an organised collection of related data stored so it can be easily accessed, managed and updated
grade9-ict.hint: Think of a school register: many records, organised.
grade9-ict.explanation: A database stores structured data in a way that makes it easy to search, retrieve and update.

grade9-ict.question: In a database, a field is:
options: a query used to search the database
a single item of data stored for each record, such as a surname or date of birth
a collection of all the records in the database
a complete set of data about one person or thing
grade9-ict.answer: a single item of data stored for each record, such as a surname or date of birth
acceptableAnswers: a single item of data stored for each record, such as a surname or date of birth
grade9-ict.hint: One column heading = one field.
grade9-ict.explanation: A field is the smallest unit of data — one category of information, like First Name or Phone Number.

grade9-ict.question: In a database, a record is:
options: a complete set of related fields for one entity, such as all the details of one student
grade9-ict.answer: a complete set of related fields for one entity, such as all the details of one student
acceptableAnswers: a complete set of related fields for one entity, such as all the details of one student
grade9-ict.hint: One row in the table = one record.
grade9-ict.explanation: A record is one complete row in a table, grouping all the fields that describe a single entity.

grade9-ict.question: A primary key in a database table is a field that:
options: uniquely identifies each record in the table
stores the most important data in each record
grade9-ict.answer: uniquely identifies each record in the table
acceptableAnswers: uniquely identifies each record in the table
grade9-ict.hint: No two records can share the same primary key value.
grade9-ict.explanation: A primary key is a field (or combination of fields) whose value is unique for every record, ensuring each row can be identified without ambiguity.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following would be a suitable primary key for a student database?
grade9-ict.answer: Student ID number
grade9-ict.hint: It must be unique for every student.
grade9-ict.explanation: A student ID number is unique to each student. Names, dates of birth and classes can be shared by more than one student.

grade9-ict.question: A flat-file database stores all data in:
options: one table only, with no links to other tables
grade9-ict.answer: one table only, with no links to other tables
acceptableAnswers: one table only, with no links to other tables
grade9-ict.hint: Flat = one level, one table.
grade9-ict.explanation: A flat-file database is a single table; it cannot handle complex relationships and can lead to data redundancy.

grade9-ict.question: A relational database stores data in:
options: multiple related tables linked by key fields
a series of plain text files
a single form that users fill in
grade9-ict.answer: multiple related tables linked by key fields
acceptableAnswers: multiple related tables linked by key fields
grade9-ict.hint: Related tables = relational.
grade9-ict.explanation: A relational database organises data into separate tables, each representing one entity type, linked by key fields to avoid duplication.

grade9-ict.question: Data redundancy in a flat-file database means:
options: all data is backed up twice
the same data is stored more than once, wasting space and risking inconsistency
records are sorted in alphabetical order
the database uses two primary keys
grade9-ict.answer: the same data is stored more than once, wasting space and risking inconsistency
acceptableAnswers: the same data is stored more than once, wasting space and risking inconsistency
grade9-ict.hint: Repeating data unnecessarily.
grade9-ict.explanation: Redundancy occurs when the same information appears in multiple records; updating one copy without the others causes inconsistency.

grade9-ict.question: A foreign key in a database table is a field that:
options: identifies each record uniquely within its own table
matches the primary key of another table, creating a link between the two tables
grade9-ict.answer: matches the primary key of another table, creating a link between the two tables
acceptableAnswers: matches the primary key of another table, creating a link between the two tables
grade9-ict.hint: It is a primary key "borrowed" from another table.
grade9-ict.explanation: A foreign key references the primary key of a related table, enforcing the link between records in different tables.

grade9-ict.question: Data validation in a database ensures that:
options: data is automatically backed up every hour
all records are sorted before they are saved
only data of the correct type, range or format can be entered into a field
only the database administrator can edit records
grade9-ict.answer: only data of the correct type, range or format can be entered into a field
acceptableAnswers: only data of the correct type, range or format can be entered into a field
grade9-ict.hint: It checks data when it is entered.
grade9-ict.explanation: Validation rules (data type, range, format, presence) prevent incorrect data from being stored by rejecting entries that fail the checks.

grade9-ict.question: The data type "Text" (or "Short Text") in a database field is used for:
options: values that will be added or multiplied
any combination of letters, numbers and symbols that will not be used in calculations
grade9-ict.answer: any combination of letters, numbers and symbols that will not be used in calculations
acceptableAnswers: any combination of letters, numbers and symbols that will not be used in calculations
grade9-ict.hint: Names and codes are text — not calculated.
grade9-ict.explanation: Text fields store alphanumeric data. A phone number stored as Text cannot be averaged, which is correct — you never add phone numbers together.

grade9-ict.question: In a database table, columns represent:
grade9-ict.answer: fields (the categories of data stored)
grade9-ict.hint: Each column heading is one field name.
grade9-ict.explanation: Each column in a table is one field, defining a category of information (e.g., Surname, Email, Date of Birth).

grade9-ict.question: In a database table, rows represent:
grade9-ict.answer: records (individual entries about one entity)
grade9-ict.hint: Each row describes one person, product or event.
grade9-ict.explanation: Each row in a table is one record — all the information collected about a single instance of the entity.

grade9-ict.question: A database field with the data type "Number" should be used when:
options: the values are names or codes
the values are either Yes or No
the values will be used in calculations such as addition or averaging
grade9-ict.answer: the values will be used in calculations such as addition or averaging
acceptableAnswers: the values will be used in calculations such as addition or averaging
grade9-ict.hint: Only use Number if you plan to calculate with it.
grade9-ict.explanation: Number data type stores numerical values that can be used in arithmetic. Codes like student numbers are stored as Text even though they look like numbers.

grade9-ict.question: A "Date/Time" data type in a database is used to:
options: store dates and times so they can be sorted chronologically and used in date calculations
grade9-ict.answer: store dates and times so they can be sorted chronologically and used in date calculations
acceptableAnswers: store dates and times so they can be sorted chronologically and used in date calculations
grade9-ict.hint: Dates need their own type to be sorted correctly.
grade9-ict.explanation: A Date/Time field stores dates and times in a standard format, enabling correct sorting and age/duration calculations.

grade9-ict.question: A "Yes/No" (or Boolean) data type is used for:
options: fields that can only be True/False, Yes/No, or 1/0
fields storing large amounts of text
grade9-ict.answer: fields that can only be True/False, Yes/No, or 1/0
acceptableAnswers: fields that can only be True/False, Yes/No, or 1/0
grade9-ict.hint: Two possible values only.
grade9-ict.explanation: A Boolean field stores a binary value — True or False — used for things like "Is the subscription active?" or "Is the student a prefect?".

grade9-ict.question: Adding a new field to an existing database table means:
options: adding a new column to the table structure
adding a new row of data
grade9-ict.answer: adding a new column to the table structure
acceptableAnswers: adding a new column to the table structure
grade9-ict.hint: A field is a column.
grade9-ict.explanation: Adding a field extends the table structure with a new category of data, adding a column that appears in every existing and future record.

grade9-ict.question: Sorting records in a database by surname in ascending (A–Z) order will:
options: arrange the records alphabetically from A to Z by surname
remove any records without a surname
arrange the records from newest to oldest
grade9-ict.answer: arrange the records alphabetically from A to Z by surname
acceptableAnswers: arrange the records alphabetically from A to Z by surname
grade9-ict.hint: Ascending = A to Z for text.
grade9-ict.explanation: Sorting text fields in ascending order arranges records alphabetically A–Z; descending would be Z–A.

grade9-ict.question: Which data type should be used for the "Price" field in a products table?
grade9-ict.answer: Currency
grade9-ict.hint: Prices are money values.
grade9-ict.explanation: A Currency data type stores monetary values and formats them with the appropriate currency symbol and decimal places.

grade9-ict.question: An "AutoNumber" (or AutoIncrement) field is useful as a primary key because:
options: it stores the number of records in the table
the database automatically assigns a unique number to each new record
the user can choose any number they like
it restricts the table to 100 records
grade9-ict.answer: the database automatically assigns a unique number to each new record
acceptableAnswers: the database automatically assigns a unique number to each new record
grade9-ict.hint: It is generated automatically.
grade9-ict.explanation: An AutoNumber primary key is generated by the database for each new record, ensuring uniqueness without requiring the user to enter a value.

grade9-ict.question: A lookup field in a database:
options: lets the user pick a value from a predefined list, reducing data-entry errors
searches the internet for data to fill the field
copies data from another table automatically
automatically calculates the average of the field
grade9-ict.answer: lets the user pick a value from a predefined list, reducing data-entry errors
acceptableAnswers: lets the user pick a value from a predefined list, reducing data-entry errors
grade9-ict.hint: A dropdown list in a field.
grade9-ict.explanation: A lookup field presents a dropdown list of allowed values, ensuring consistency and reducing the chance of typing errors.

grade9-ict.question: A relationship between two database tables is typically created by:
options: copying all the records from one table into the other
sorting both tables in alphabetical order
matching the primary key of one table to a foreign key in the other table
grade9-ict.answer: matching the primary key of one table to a foreign key in the other table
acceptableAnswers: matching the primary key of one table to a foreign key in the other table
grade9-ict.hint: Primary key meets foreign key.
grade9-ict.explanation: A relationship links two tables through a primary key–foreign key pair, allowing data from both tables to be combined in queries and reports.

grade9-ict.question: A data entry form in a database is used to:
options: provide a user-friendly interface for entering and viewing records one at a time
search the database with complex criteria
print a summary report of all records
grade9-ict.answer: provide a user-friendly interface for entering and viewing records one at a time
acceptableAnswers: provide a user-friendly interface for entering and viewing records one at a time
grade9-ict.hint: It is the on-screen version of a paper form.
grade9-ict.explanation: A form presents one record at a time in a neat layout, making data entry easier and reducing mistakes compared to entering data directly into the table.

grade9-ict.question: A validation rule that allows only values between 1 and 100 in a "Score" field is an example of:
grade9-ict.answer: range check
grade9-ict.hint: It checks that the value falls within an allowed range.
grade9-ict.explanation: A range check validation rule rejects any entry outside the specified minimum and maximum — here, any score below 1 or above 100.

grade9-ict.question: A presence check validation rule ensures that:
options: the value is within an acceptable range
a field is not left blank when saving a record
the value is in the correct format
the value matches one from a list
grade9-ict.answer: a field is not left blank when saving a record
acceptableAnswers: a field is not left blank when saving a record
grade9-ict.hint: It checks that something is present.
grade9-ict.explanation: A presence check makes a field mandatory — the record cannot be saved unless that field contains a value.

grade9-ict.question: Data verification in a database differs from validation because verification:
options: checks that the data is the correct type or range
checks that data was entered correctly as intended, for example by comparing two entries of the same data
grade9-ict.answer: checks that data was entered correctly as intended, for example by comparing two entries of the same data
acceptableAnswers: checks that data was entered correctly as intended, for example by comparing two entries of the same data
grade9-ict.hint: Typing the email address twice to confirm is verification.
grade9-ict.explanation: Verification confirms that entered data matches what was intended (e.g., re-entering a password); validation checks that the data meets a set of rules.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is an example of a format check?
options: Rejecting a date entered as "30-13-2025" because the month value (13) is invalid
Rejecting a name containing a number
Rejecting a score of 150 in a field limited to 0–100
grade9-ict.answer: Rejecting a date entered as "30-13-2025" because the month value (13) is invalid
acceptableAnswers: Rejecting a date entered as "30-13-2025" because the month value (13) is invalid
grade9-ict.hint: The format must match the expected pattern.
grade9-ict.explanation: A format check ensures the data matches the required pattern — for dates, the month must be 1–12; 13 violates the format.

grade9-ict.question: Importing data into a database from a CSV file means:
options: exporting the database as a printed report
bringing data from a comma-separated text file into a database table automatically
copying one table to another within the same database
creating a new form for data entry
grade9-ict.answer: bringing data from a comma-separated text file into a database table automatically
acceptableAnswers: bringing data from a comma-separated text file into a database table automatically
grade9-ict.hint: CSV = Comma-Separated Values — a common data exchange format.
grade9-ict.explanation: A CSV import reads each row of the text file and creates a corresponding database record, allowing bulk data entry.

grade9-ict.question: The "Undo" function in a database is used to:
options: reverse the last action, such as a mistaken data entry
grade9-ict.answer: reverse the last action, such as a mistaken data entry
acceptableAnswers: reverse the last action, such as a mistaken data entry
grade9-ict.hint: It cancels the most recent change.
grade9-ict.explanation: Undo reverts the last action performed, allowing users to correct mistakes without manually re-entering old data.

grade9-ict.question: A list-box or drop-down field on a data entry form helps to:
options: ensure consistent, valid data by restricting choices to a predefined list
allow the user to enter any text they wish
grade9-ict.answer: ensure consistent, valid data by restricting choices to a predefined list
acceptableAnswers: ensure consistent, valid data by restricting choices to a predefined list
grade9-ict.hint: Choose from a list, not free text.
grade9-ict.explanation: Drop-down lists limit the user to approved values, eliminating spelling variations and ensuring data consistency.

grade9-ict.question: A check-digit is a type of validation that:
options: limits the length of text in a field
ensures the field is not blank
checks that the data type is correct
adds an extra calculated digit to a code and recalculates it on entry to detect transcription errors
grade9-ict.answer: adds an extra calculated digit to a code and recalculates it on entry to detect transcription errors
acceptableAnswers: adds an extra calculated digit to a code and recalculates it on entry to detect transcription errors
grade9-ict.hint: Barcodes and ISBNs use check digits.
grade9-ict.explanation: A check digit is computed from the other digits in a code; when the code is entered, the computer recalculates and compares — a mismatch reveals an error.

grade9-ict.question: Why should a "Phone Number" field be stored as Text rather than Number in a database?
options: Phone numbers must be sorted numerically
Phone numbers may start with a leading zero that would be lost if stored as a number, and they are never used in calculations
grade9-ict.answer: Phone numbers may start with a leading zero that would be lost if stored as a number, and they are never used in calculations
acceptableAnswers: Phone numbers may start with a leading zero that would be lost if stored as a number, and they are never used in calculations
grade9-ict.hint: You never add two phone numbers together.
grade9-ict.explanation: Storing a phone number as a Number field removes any leading zeros and allows arithmetic, which is meaningless for phone numbers. Text is correct.

grade9-ict.question: Duplicate records in a database can be prevented by:
options: removing all fields that might be duplicated
sorting all records alphabetically before saving
only allowing one user to access the database at a time
setting the primary key field so that no two records can share the same value
grade9-ict.answer: setting the primary key field so that no two records can share the same value
acceptableAnswers: setting the primary key field so that no two records can share the same value
grade9-ict.hint: A primary key is always unique.
grade9-ict.explanation: The primary key uniqueness constraint prevents a second record from being entered with the same key value, rejecting true duplicates.

grade9-ict.question: A database query is used to:
options: design the layout of a data entry form
search for and retrieve records that match specific criteria
print a formatted report of all records
grade9-ict.answer: search for and retrieve records that match specific criteria
acceptableAnswers: search for and retrieve records that match specific criteria
grade9-ict.hint: Ask the database a question.
grade9-ict.explanation: A query lets the user specify criteria and retrieves only the matching records, hiding the rest.

grade9-ict.question: In Microsoft Access, a QBE (Query By Example) grid allows users to:
options: design a query by filling in criteria rows for each field without writing SQL code
grade9-ict.answer: design a query by filling in criteria rows for each field without writing SQL code
acceptableAnswers: design a query by filling in criteria rows for each field without writing SQL code
grade9-ict.hint: QBE is a visual approach to querying.
grade9-ict.explanation: The QBE grid in Access lets users choose fields and type criteria into a visual grid; the application generates the underlying SQL automatically.

grade9-ict.question: In a database query, the criterion >"50" in a "Mark" field would return records where:
grade9-ict.answer: the mark is greater than 50
grade9-ict.hint: The > operator means "greater than".
grade9-ict.explanation: The > operator selects records where the field value exceeds the specified number — here, any mark above 50.

grade9-ict.question: The query criterion "Like *son*" applied to a "Surname" field would return:
options: records where the surname ends with "son"
all records where the surname contains "son" anywhere in the word
only records where the surname is exactly "son"
records where the surname starts with "son"
grade9-ict.answer: all records where the surname contains "son" anywhere in the word
acceptableAnswers: all records where the surname contains "son" anywhere in the word
grade9-ict.hint: The asterisk (*) is a wildcard meaning "any characters".
grade9-ict.explanation: The wildcard * means zero or more characters; *son* matches any surname containing "son" — e.g., Jackson, Sonia, Wilson.

grade9-ict.question: Using AND between two criteria in a query means:
options: all records are returned regardless of the criteria
records matching neither criterion are returned
records that satisfy either criterion are returned
only records that satisfy BOTH criteria are returned
grade9-ict.answer: only records that satisfy BOTH criteria are returned
acceptableAnswers: only records that satisfy BOTH criteria are returned
grade9-ict.hint: AND = both must be true.
grade9-ict.explanation: An AND query is more restrictive — a record must match criterion A AND criterion B to be included in the results.

grade9-ict.question: Using OR between two criteria in a query means:
options: records that satisfy at least one of the criteria are returned
only records satisfying both criteria are returned
grade9-ict.answer: records that satisfy at least one of the criteria are returned
acceptableAnswers: records that satisfy at least one of the criteria are returned
grade9-ict.hint: OR = either is enough.
grade9-ict.explanation: An OR query is less restrictive — a record matching criterion A OR criterion B (or both) is included.

grade9-ict.question: A query that shows only selected fields (columns) rather than all fields is called a:
grade9-ict.answer: projection
grade9-ict.hint: Choosing which columns to show.
grade9-ict.explanation: A projection picks specific fields to display in the query result, hiding others that are not relevant.

grade9-ict.question: An action query in a database can:
options: change the font used in forms
update, delete or append records based on criteria, making permanent changes to the data
only display records without changing them
grade9-ict.answer: update, delete or append records based on criteria, making permanent changes to the data
acceptableAnswers: update, delete or append records based on criteria, making permanent changes to the data
grade9-ict.hint: Action queries change the data, not just display it.
grade9-ict.explanation: Unlike a select query (which only reads data), an action query modifies records — for example, updating all prices by 10%, or deleting expired records.

grade9-ict.question: In a query, the "Sort" row is used to:
options: specify whether the results should be ordered ascending or descending by a particular field
grade9-ict.answer: specify whether the results should be ordered ascending or descending by a particular field
acceptableAnswers: specify whether the results should be ordered ascending or descending by a particular field
grade9-ict.hint: It determines the order of results.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Sort row in the QBE grid lets you set the field to sort by and the order (Ascending A–Z or Descending Z–A) for the query results.

grade9-ict.question: A query that draws data from two or more related tables is called a:
grade9-ict.answer: multi-table query (or join query)
grade9-ict.hint: It joins tables together.
grade9-ict.explanation: A join query links two or more tables through a shared key field, allowing data from multiple tables to be combined in the results.

grade9-ict.question: The criterion "Between 1 And 5" applied to an "Age" field would return records where:
options: the age is exactly between 1 and 5 (i.e., 3)
grade9-ict.answer: the age is 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5
grade9-ict.hint: Between is inclusive of both boundary values.
grade9-ict.explanation: The BETWEEN operator includes both boundary values, so Between 1 And 5 returns records with age values of 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5.

grade9-ict.question: The main purpose of a database report is to:
options: present selected data from the database in a formatted, printable layout
enter new records into the database
grade9-ict.answer: present selected data from the database in a formatted, printable layout
acceptableAnswers: present selected data from the database in a formatted, printable layout
grade9-ict.hint: Reports are for presenting, not editing.
grade9-ict.explanation: A report formats query results or table data for printing or display, often grouping and summarising data.

grade9-ict.question: Grouping in a database report means:
options: organising records with the same value in a field together, and optionally showing a subtotal for each group
adding a chart to the report
grade9-ict.answer: organising records with the same value in a field together, and optionally showing a subtotal for each group
acceptableAnswers: organising records with the same value in a field together, and optionally showing a subtotal for each group
grade9-ict.hint: Group by Department shows all records in each department together.
grade9-ict.explanation: Grouping in a report collects records sharing a common field value, making it easy to see subtotals (e.g., total sales per department).

grade9-ict.question: A report based on a query will show:
options: only the record with the highest value
only the records that matched the query criteria, formatted for printing
all records in the database regardless of the criteria
grade9-ict.answer: only the records that matched the query criteria, formatted for printing
acceptableAnswers: only the records that matched the query criteria, formatted for printing
grade9-ict.hint: The report shows whatever the underlying query returned.
grade9-ict.explanation: A report presents the results of its underlying query or table; basing it on a query applies filter criteria before the data is formatted.

grade9-ict.question: A form in a database is different from a report because a form:
options: can only be created by an administrator
cannot show data from the database
is used to enter and edit data, while a report is used to display and print data
grade9-ict.answer: is used to enter and edit data, while a report is used to display and print data
acceptableAnswers: is used to enter and edit data, while a report is used to display and print data
grade9-ict.hint: Forms are for input; reports are for output.
grade9-ict.explanation: Forms provide an interactive screen for data entry and editing; reports provide a formatted, non-editable view of data for output.

grade9-ict.question: A subform in a database is:
options: a form embedded inside another form, used to show related records from a linked table
a form that is much smaller than the main form
a read-only version of the main form
a form that connects to the internet
grade9-ict.answer: a form embedded inside another form, used to show related records from a linked table
acceptableAnswers: a form embedded inside another form, used to show related records from a linked table
grade9-ict.hint: It appears inside the main form.
grade9-ict.explanation: A subform typically shows the "many" side of a one-to-many relationship — for example, a customer form with a subform listing all their orders.

grade9-ict.question: Adding a total (Sum) at the footer of a report group allows:
options: the report to be exported to a spreadsheet
the report to sort records descending
the report to display the sum of a numeric field for all records in that group
the report to print the total number of pages
grade9-ict.answer: the report to display the sum of a numeric field for all records in that group
acceptableAnswers: the report to display the sum of a numeric field for all records in that group
grade9-ict.hint: A subtotal in the group footer.
grade9-ict.explanation: A Sum aggregate function in a group footer adds up the numeric field values for all records in that group, displaying a subtotal.

grade9-ict.question: The Report Wizard in Access helps users to:
options: create a formatted report by following step-by-step prompts to choose fields, grouping and layout
import data from a CSV file
grade9-ict.answer: create a formatted report by following step-by-step prompts to choose fields, grouping and layout
acceptableAnswers: create a formatted report by following step-by-step prompts to choose fields, grouping and layout
grade9-ict.hint: Wizard = guided, step-by-step.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Report Wizard asks a series of questions about which fields to include, how to group and sort, and which layout to use, then generates the report automatically.

grade9-ict.question: Conditional formatting in a report changes:
options: the font size of every field in the report
the order in which records are printed
the primary key of the table
the appearance of a field value (e.g., colour, bold) automatically based on the value, such as highlighting failing grades in red
grade9-ict.answer: the appearance of a field value (e.g., colour, bold) automatically based on the value, such as highlighting failing grades in red
acceptableAnswers: the appearance of a field value (e.g., colour, bold) automatically based on the value, such as highlighting failing grades in red
grade9-ict.hint: Format depends on the value.
grade9-ict.explanation: Conditional formatting applies different fonts, colours or styles to field values that meet a specified condition, drawing attention to important data.

grade9-ict.question: A mailing-label report is a special report layout used to:
options: send emails to all contacts in the database
show a pivot chart of sales data
print address labels, one per record, in a format that fits on label sheets
list all records in a single column
grade9-ict.answer: print address labels, one per record, in a format that fits on label sheets
acceptableAnswers: print address labels, one per record, in a format that fits on label sheets
grade9-ict.hint: Stickers for envelopes.
grade9-ict.explanation: A mailing-label report formats address data so each record prints on one peel-and-stick label, arranged in columns to match commercial label sheets.

grade9-ict.question: Exporting a database report as a PDF file allows:
options: the report to be shared and printed by anyone without needing the database software
the report layout to be changed by recipients
the data to be automatically updated when the database changes
the data to be imported back into the database
grade9-ict.answer: the report to be shared and printed by anyone without needing the database software
acceptableAnswers: the report to be shared and printed by anyone without needing the database software
grade9-ict.hint: PDF is a universal, read-only format.
grade9-ict.explanation: PDF preserves the report layout and can be opened by any device with a PDF reader, making it ideal for sharing final reports.

grade9-ict.question: Which section of a database report typically displays the column headings?
options: The Page Header or Report Header
grade9-ict.answer: The Page Header or Report Header
acceptableAnswers: The Page Header or Report Header
grade9-ict.hint: Headings appear at the top.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Page Header (or Report Header) section appears at the top of each page (or once at the top of the report), displaying field labels and titles.

grade9-ict.question: Before using the school computer laboratory, students should:
options: run straight to the nearest computer and switch it on immediately
leave their bags across the pathway between desks
wait for the teacher's permission, sign in if required, and check that their work area is clean and safe
bring food and drinks to eat while working
grade9-ict.answer: wait for the teacher's permission, sign in if required, and check that their work area is clean and safe
acceptableAnswers: wait for the teacher's permission, sign in if required, and check that their work area is clean and safe
grade9-ict.hint: Lab rules must be followed before starting.
grade9-ict.explanation: Orderly entry and a safe, tidy workspace protect equipment and prevent accidents in the lab.

grade9-ict.question: Food and drinks are not allowed in a computer laboratory because:
options: spills can damage keyboards, circuit boards and other components, and crumbs attract pests
computers work better when the room smells of food
the rule is set only to stop students enjoying themselves
grade9-ict.answer: spills can damage keyboards, circuit boards and other components, and crumbs attract pests
acceptableAnswers: spills can damage keyboards, circuit boards and other components, and crumbs attract pests
grade9-ict.hint: Liquid and electronics do not mix.
grade9-ict.explanation: A liquid spill on a keyboard or into a computer case can short-circuit components and destroy the equipment.

grade9-ict.question: Students should log off or shut down the computer when they finish using it because:
options: it is faster to start a computer that was shut down correctly
it allows the teacher to delete all student work
it protects their files and the school's data from unauthorised access and saves energy
the computer will break if left on overnight
