grade9-ict.answer: it protects their files and the school's data from unauthorised access and saves energy
acceptableAnswers: it protects their files and the school's data from unauthorised access and saves energy
grade9-ict.hint: Leaving a session open is a security risk.
grade9-ict.explanation: Logging off ends the user's session, preventing others from accessing their files; shutting down also conserves electricity.

grade9-ict.question: In a computer laboratory, power cables should be:
options: kept tidy and out of walkways to prevent people from tripping over them
left loose on the floor to allow air circulation
removed when not in use and stored in a drawer
grade9-ict.answer: kept tidy and out of walkways to prevent people from tripping over them
acceptableAnswers: kept tidy and out of walkways to prevent people from tripping over them
grade9-ict.hint: Trailing cables are a trip hazard.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cables on the floor in busy areas are a serious tripping hazard that can injure users and pull equipment off desks.

grade9-ict.question: If a student notices a damaged power cable on a computer in the lab, they should:
options: unplug all computers in the room
continue using the computer and hope nothing happens
repair the cable themselves using tape
report it immediately to the teacher and not use that computer
grade9-ict.answer: report it immediately to the teacher and not use that computer
acceptableAnswers: report it immediately to the teacher and not use that computer
grade9-ict.hint: Damaged electrical cables are dangerous.
grade9-ict.explanation: A frayed or damaged cable is an electrocution and fire risk; only a qualified person should carry out repairs.

grade9-ict.question: Students should never touch the back of a desktop computer or the inside of the case because:
options: it will make the computer run faster
it is impolite to touch school property
the inside is too hot to touch
some components carry dangerous voltages even when the computer is switched off, and components can be damaged by static electricity
grade9-ict.answer: some components carry dangerous voltages even when the computer is switched off, and components can be damaged by static electricity
acceptableAnswers: some components carry dangerous voltages even when the computer is switched off, and components can be damaged by static electricity
grade9-ict.hint: Danger from electricity and static.
grade9-ict.explanation: Components like the power supply unit retain charge after being switched off. Static from your hands can also destroy sensitive chips.

grade9-ict.question: The correct procedure when there is a fire in the computer laboratory is to:
options: grab the nearest computer and carry it out first
hide under the desk until the fire goes out
alert everyone, leave the room calmly without taking any equipment, and raise the fire alarm
use water to put out any burning electrical equipment
grade9-ict.answer: alert everyone, leave the room calmly without taking any equipment, and raise the fire alarm
acceptableAnswers: alert everyone, leave the room calmly without taking any equipment, and raise the fire alarm
grade9-ict.hint: People first, always.
grade9-ict.explanation: In a fire emergency, the priority is to evacuate all people safely; never use water on electrical fires — use a CO₂ extinguisher if trained.

grade9-ict.question: Software in a school lab should only be installed by:
options: the student whose computer it is
an authorised technician or network administrator
any student who knows how to do it
grade9-ict.answer: an authorised technician or network administrator
acceptableAnswers: an authorised technician or network administrator
grade9-ict.hint: Installing software requires admin rights.
grade9-ict.explanation: Unauthorised software installations can introduce malware, violate licensing and disrupt the network; only authorised staff should perform them.

grade9-ict.question: Students should not share their network login password because:
options: another person could access their files, and any misuse would be traced back to the original account holder
sharing passwords makes the network faster
the network administrator already knows all passwords
passwords are too long to remember anyway
grade9-ict.answer: another person could access their files, and any misuse would be traced back to the original account holder
acceptableAnswers: another person could access their files, and any misuse would be traced back to the original account holder
grade9-ict.hint: Your account, your responsibility.
grade9-ict.explanation: A shared password means a third party can access personal files and carry out actions that will be logged under your name.

grade9-ict.question: Bags and personal belongings should be stored under the desk or at the side of the room in a computer lab because:
options: the teacher needs to inspect all bags
bags contain magnetic materials that damage hard drives
the computers work better when the desk is tidy
bags in the aisle are a tripping hazard and can block emergency exits
grade9-ict.answer: bags in the aisle are a tripping hazard and can block emergency exits
acceptableAnswers: bags in the aisle are a tripping hazard and can block emergency exits
grade9-ict.hint: Clear aisles for safety.
grade9-ict.explanation: Bags and coats on the floor between desks create a tripping hazard and can impede quick evacuation in an emergency.

grade9-ict.question: Students should save their work regularly while in the computer lab because:
options: the network automatically deletes unsaved files
saving sends a copy to the teacher automatically
unexpected power cuts or program crashes can lose unsaved work permanently
grade9-ict.answer: unexpected power cuts or program crashes can lose unsaved work permanently
acceptableAnswers: unexpected power cuts or program crashes can lose unsaved work permanently
grade9-ict.hint: Unsaved work exists only in RAM.
grade9-ict.explanation: RAM is volatile — a power failure or crash erases everything in memory. Frequent saves to disk protect against data loss.

grade9-ict.question: In a computer laboratory, students should use the equipment only for:
options: connecting personal USB drives without scanning them for viruses
downloading software for use at home
any personal purpose, including gaming and social media, if they finish early
the educational tasks set by the teacher, in accordance with the school's acceptable use policy
grade9-ict.answer: the educational tasks set by the teacher, in accordance with the school's acceptable use policy
acceptableAnswers: the educational tasks set by the teacher, in accordance with the school's acceptable use policy
grade9-ict.hint: School equipment is for school use.
grade9-ict.explanation: Acceptable use policies restrict school computers to educational activities, protecting resources and ensuring equitable access for all students.

grade9-ict.question: Before plugging a USB drive from home into a school computer, students should:
options: format the USB drive to remove all files
have it scanned for viruses by the network administrator or use the lab's up-to-date antivirus software
plug it in immediately without any checks
break the USB drive to prevent any risk
grade9-ict.answer: have it scanned for viruses by the network administrator or use the lab's up-to-date antivirus software
acceptableAnswers: have it scanned for viruses by the network administrator or use the lab's up-to-date antivirus software
grade9-ict.hint: Foreign drives can carry malware.
grade9-ict.explanation: A USB drive used on other computers may carry malware; scanning it before use prevents infection spreading to the school network.

grade9-ict.question: Electrical equipment in the computer lab should be connected to:
options: any available socket without checking the voltage
extension leads that are coiled up while in use
properly earthed, grounded sockets with the correct voltage rating
the mains supply without using a plug
grade9-ict.answer: properly earthed, grounded sockets with the correct voltage rating
acceptableAnswers: properly earthed, grounded sockets with the correct voltage rating
grade9-ict.hint: Earthing and correct voltage prevent shocks and fires.
grade9-ict.explanation: Earthed sockets and the correct voltage protect against electric shock and prevent overloading that could start a fire.

grade9-ict.question: An anti-static wrist strap is worn when handling computer components to:
options: protect the wrist from cuts on sharp edges
safely discharge static electricity from the person's body to earth, preventing damage to sensitive chips
grade9-ict.answer: safely discharge static electricity from the person's body to earth, preventing damage to sensitive chips
acceptableAnswers: safely discharge static electricity from the person's body to earth, preventing damage to sensitive chips
grade9-ict.hint: Static can destroy electronic components.
grade9-ict.explanation: A wrist strap bonds the technician to the earth, equalising charge and preventing the discharge of built-up static into sensitive components.

grade9-ict.question: Extension leads should not be overloaded in a computer lab because:
options: computers work faster when connected directly to the wall
extension leads are only safe in offices, not schools
too many appliances on one lead can exceed its current rating, causing it to overheat and potentially start a fire
grade9-ict.answer: too many appliances on one lead can exceed its current rating, causing it to overheat and potentially start a fire
acceptableAnswers: too many appliances on one lead can exceed its current rating, causing it to overheat and potentially start a fire
grade9-ict.hint: Too much current = heat.
grade9-ict.explanation: Each extension lead is rated for a maximum current; exceeding this causes overheating of the cable insulation, which can ignite.

grade9-ict.question: A Residual Current Device (RCD) in the lab is there to:
options: cut the power instantly if a fault is detected, protecting users from electric shock
record which computers are switched on
grade9-ict.answer: cut the power instantly if a fault is detected, protecting users from electric shock
acceptableAnswers: cut the power instantly if a fault is detected, protecting users from electric shock
grade9-ict.hint: It detects earth faults and trips the circuit.
grade9-ict.explanation: An RCD monitors the current in a circuit and trips the supply within milliseconds if it detects a leakage to earth, preventing a potentially fatal shock.

grade9-ict.question: Monitors and towers should not be placed near water sources such as open windows during rain because:
options: rain creates a magnetic field that erases hard drives
water conducts electricity and can cause a short circuit or electrocution
grade9-ict.answer: water conducts electricity and can cause a short circuit or electrocution
acceptableAnswers: water conducts electricity and can cause a short circuit or electrocution
grade9-ict.hint: Water and electricity are a deadly combination.
grade9-ict.explanation: Water is a conductor; if it enters a powered device it can short-circuit it and electrocute the user.

grade9-ict.question: A surge protector (or UPS — Uninterruptible Power Supply) protects computers from:
options: sudden voltage spikes and power cuts that can damage hardware and corrupt data
grade9-ict.answer: sudden voltage spikes and power cuts that can damage hardware and corrupt data
acceptableAnswers: sudden voltage spikes and power cuts that can damage hardware and corrupt data
grade9-ict.hint: It keeps the power supply stable.
grade9-ict.explanation: A UPS provides clean, regulated power and battery backup, preventing voltage spikes and giving users time to save and shut down gracefully during a power cut.

grade9-ict.question: The correct way to clean a computer screen is with:
options: a soft, lint-free cloth, slightly dampened with a screen-cleaning solution
a hard brush to scrub off dust
a wet cloth soaked in tap water
grade9-ict.answer: a soft, lint-free cloth, slightly dampened with a screen-cleaning solution
acceptableAnswers: a soft, lint-free cloth, slightly dampened with a screen-cleaning solution
grade9-ict.hint: Gentle cleaning only.
grade9-ict.explanation: Harsh chemicals can damage anti-glare coatings; excess liquid near electronic components is dangerous; a microfibre cloth and screen cleaner are safest.

grade9-ict.question: When carrying a laptop, students should:
options: carry it open so they can see what is on the screen
carry it by the screen in one hand
hold it closed with both hands, keep the lid closed, and never hold it by the screen
swing it by the charging cable
grade9-ict.answer: hold it closed with both hands, keep the lid closed, and never hold it by the screen
acceptableAnswers: hold it closed with both hands, keep the lid closed, and never hold it by the screen
grade9-ict.hint: Screens are fragile.
grade9-ict.explanation: The screen is the most fragile part of a laptop; holding it by the screen can crack the panel. Two hands and a closed lid protect the device.

grade9-ict.question: Computers should not be placed in direct sunlight because:
options: screen colours look better in bright light
the computer will charge its battery from solar energy
overheating can damage the processor, battery and other components, and screen glare makes it hard to see
grade9-ict.answer: overheating can damage the processor, battery and other components, and screen glare makes it hard to see
acceptableAnswers: overheating can damage the processor, battery and other components, and screen glare makes it hard to see
grade9-ict.hint: Heat is a computer's enemy.
grade9-ict.explanation: Sustained high temperatures shorten the life of processors, RAM and batteries; screen glare also makes the display unusable.

grade9-ict.question: Students should wash their hands before using shared keyboards because:
options: keyboards charge faster when hands are clean
greasy or dirty hands can damage keyboard surfaces and spread germs to the next user
the keyboard detects fingerprints to log in
grade9-ict.answer: greasy or dirty hands can damage keyboard surfaces and spread germs to the next user
acceptableAnswers: greasy or dirty hands can damage keyboard surfaces and spread germs to the next user
grade9-ict.hint: Hygiene and equipment care.
grade9-ict.explanation: Oils and dirt from hands build up on keys and can degrade the legends; shared keyboards are also a vector for spreading illness.

grade9-ict.question: In the event of an electric shock to a person in the lab, the first action should be to:
options: pour water on the equipment to extinguish any sparks
switch off the power at the mains before touching the victim, then call for help
pull the victim away from the equipment immediately using your hands
leave the room and wait for help to arrive
grade9-ict.answer: switch off the power at the mains before touching the victim, then call for help
acceptableAnswers: switch off the power at the mains before touching the victim, then call for help
grade9-ict.hint: Never touch someone being electrocuted with the power still on.
grade9-ict.explanation: Touching a person still in contact with live electricity will electrocute the rescuer too; cutting the power first makes rescue safe.

grade9-ict.question: To keep a desktop computer cool and prevent overheating, you should:
options: put the computer in a sealed cupboard
ensure ventilation slots are not blocked and the room is adequately ventilated
cover the computer with a blanket when not in use
run as many programs as possible to keep the fan working
grade9-ict.answer: ensure ventilation slots are not blocked and the room is adequately ventilated
acceptableAnswers: ensure ventilation slots are not blocked and the room is adequately ventilated
grade9-ict.hint: Airflow keeps components cool.
grade9-ict.explanation: Processors, GPUs and PSUs produce heat; clear ventilation slots and adequate room airflow allow the cooling fans to dissipate heat effectively.

grade9-ict.question: Compressed air cans are used for computer maintenance to:
options: blow dust out of keyboards, fans and case vents
grade9-ict.answer: blow dust out of keyboards, fans and case vents
acceptableAnswers: blow dust out of keyboards, fans and case vents
grade9-ict.hint: Blow out the dust.
grade9-ict.explanation: Compressed air safely dislodges dust from components without contact, preventing heat build-up caused by dust-clogged vents and fans.

grade9-ict.question: Magnets should be kept away from traditional hard disk drives (HDDs) because:
options: strong magnetic fields can corrupt or erase the data stored on the magnetic platters
magnets cause the screen to flicker
magnets slow down the read/write heads
grade9-ict.answer: strong magnetic fields can corrupt or erase the data stored on the magnetic platters
acceptableAnswers: strong magnetic fields can corrupt or erase the data stored on the magnetic platters
grade9-ict.hint: HDD data is stored magnetically.
grade9-ict.explanation: HDDs record data by magnetising tiny regions of their platters; an external magnetic field can randomly flip those regions, corrupting or erasing data.

grade9-ict.question: Why should computers be shut down properly rather than just switching off the power at the wall?
options: switching off at the wall uses less electricity
a proper shutdown charges the battery faster
a proper shutdown updates the antivirus automatically
a proper shutdown closes files correctly, writes any cached data to disk and prevents file system corruption
grade9-ict.answer: a proper shutdown closes files correctly, writes any cached data to disk and prevents file system corruption
acceptableAnswers: a proper shutdown closes files correctly, writes any cached data to disk and prevents file system corruption
grade9-ict.hint: Abrupt power loss can corrupt the file system.
grade9-ict.explanation: The operating system needs time to write buffered data, close open files and update file system structures; cutting power mid-process can corrupt data.

grade9-ict.question: A protective screen cover or filter is used on a monitor to:
options: reduce glare and protect the screen surface from dust and scratches
grade9-ict.answer: reduce glare and protect the screen surface from dust and scratches
acceptableAnswers: reduce glare and protect the screen surface from dust and scratches
grade9-ict.hint: Protection and comfort.
grade9-ict.explanation: Screen protectors reduce reflections that cause eye strain and add a physical barrier against dust and accidental scratching.

grade9-ict.question: Regularly defragmenting a traditional HDD (hard disk drive) is done to:
options: reorganise fragmented files so they are stored contiguously, improving access speed
grade9-ict.answer: reorganise fragmented files so they are stored contiguously, improving access speed
acceptableAnswers: reorganise fragmented files so they are stored contiguously, improving access speed
grade9-ict.hint: Fragmented files make the read head travel further.
grade9-ict.explanation: Over time, files become scattered across the disk; defragmentation rearranges them into contiguous blocks, reducing the distance the read/write head must travel.

grade9-ict.question: Portable storage devices such as USB drives should be safely ejected before being physically removed from the computer because:
options: the drive needs to cool down before removal
the USB port breaks if the drive is removed without ejecting
the operating system may still be writing data to the drive, and unsafe removal can corrupt files
grade9-ict.answer: the operating system may still be writing data to the drive, and unsafe removal can corrupt files
acceptableAnswers: the operating system may still be writing data to the drive, and unsafe removal can corrupt files
grade9-ict.hint: The OS may have buffered writes pending.
grade9-ict.explanation: The OS caches writes; a safe eject flushes the cache to the drive. Removing the drive with pending writes leaves the file system in an inconsistent state.

grade9-ict.question: Printers in a lab should be maintained by:
options: pouring water into the paper tray to moisten the paper
replacing ink or toner when low, clearing paper jams carefully and keeping them dust-free
leaving them running 24 hours a day regardless of use
grade9-ict.answer: replacing ink or toner when low, clearing paper jams carefully and keeping them dust-free
acceptableAnswers: replacing ink or toner when low, clearing paper jams carefully and keeping them dust-free
grade9-ict.hint: Regular, gentle maintenance.
grade9-ict.explanation: Correct maintenance — replacing consumables, carefully clearing jams and keeping the device clean — extends printer life and print quality.

grade9-ict.question: To protect a laptop's battery health, users should:
options: only ever use the laptop plugged into the mains
remove the battery when not in use every day
charge it for exactly two hours every day
avoid regularly allowing the battery to completely drain to 0% or leaving it permanently at 100% while always plugged in
grade9-ict.answer: avoid regularly allowing the battery to completely drain to 0% or leaving it permanently at 100% while always plugged in
acceptableAnswers: avoid regularly allowing the battery to completely drain to 0% or leaving it permanently at 100% while always plugged in
grade9-ict.hint: Extremes of charge level stress lithium batteries.
grade9-ict.explanation: Lithium-ion batteries degrade fastest at the extremes; keeping charge between about 20% and 80% extends battery lifespan significantly.

grade9-ict.question: Network cables should not be bent sharply or run under heavy furniture because:
options: cables work faster when they are straight
cables must always be in plain sight for safety
sharp bends and physical pressure damage the internal conductors, causing intermittent faults or complete failures
grade9-ict.answer: sharp bends and physical pressure damage the internal conductors, causing intermittent faults or complete failures
acceptableAnswers: sharp bends and physical pressure damage the internal conductors, causing intermittent faults or complete failures
grade9-ict.hint: Cables have bend-radius limits.
grade9-ict.explanation: The copper conductors inside a cable can break or make poor contact if bent beyond their minimum bend radius or crushed, causing network faults.

grade9-ict.question: Which type of fire extinguisher should be used on an electrical fire in the computer lab?
options: Dry powder extinguisher (only if CO₂ is unavailable — it damages equipment)
grade9-ict.answer: CO₂ (carbon dioxide) extinguisher
grade9-ict.hint: CO₂ is safe on electrical fires.
grade9-ict.explanation: CO₂ extinguishers discharge non-conductive gas, smothering the fire without damaging electrical equipment or leaving a messy residue.

grade9-ict.question: RSI (Repetitive Strain Injury) in computer users is caused by:
options: sitting too close to the screen
performing the same hand and wrist movements repetitively over long periods, especially with a keyboard and mouse
staring at a bright screen in a dark room
grade9-ict.answer: performing the same hand and wrist movements repetitively over long periods, especially with a keyboard and mouse
acceptableAnswers: performing the same hand and wrist movements repetitively over long periods, especially with a keyboard and mouse
grade9-ict.hint: Repetition + poor posture = RSI.
grade9-ict.explanation: RSI is an umbrella term for pain and inflammation in tendons and muscles caused by repeated awkward movements without adequate rest.

grade9-ict.question: Eye strain from prolonged computer use can be reduced by:
options: increasing the screen brightness to maximum
sitting as close to the screen as possible
looking away from the screen at a distant object for 20 seconds every 20 minutes (the 20-20-20 rule), and adjusting screen brightness
using the computer in a completely darkened room
grade9-ict.answer: looking away from the screen at a distant object for 20 seconds every 20 minutes (the 20-20-20 rule), and adjusting screen brightness
acceptableAnswers: looking away from the screen at a distant object for 20 seconds every 20 minutes (the 20-20-20 rule), and adjusting screen brightness
grade9-ict.hint: Regular breaks and correct brightness.
grade9-ict.explanation: The 20-20-20 rule gives the eye muscles a rest; matching screen brightness to room light prevents both squinting and glare.

grade9-ict.question: Back pain is a common health problem for computer users who:
options: use a wireless mouse instead of a wired one
work in a brightly lit room
type with more than two fingers
sit in a poorly adjusted chair with no lumbar support and hunch over the keyboard for hours without breaks
grade9-ict.answer: sit in a poorly adjusted chair with no lumbar support and hunch over the keyboard for hours without breaks
acceptableAnswers: sit in a poorly adjusted chair with no lumbar support and hunch over the keyboard for hours without breaks
grade9-ict.hint: Posture and prolonged sitting are the causes.
grade9-ict.explanation: Poor seating posture with no lumbar support places excessive stress on the spinal discs and back muscles, leading to chronic pain.

grade9-ict.question: Carpal tunnel syndrome is a health hazard associated with computer use that affects:
options: the wrist and hand, causing pain, tingling and numbness due to compression of the median nerve
grade9-ict.answer: the wrist and hand, causing pain, tingling and numbness due to compression of the median nerve
acceptableAnswers: the wrist and hand, causing pain, tingling and numbness due to compression of the median nerve
grade9-ict.hint: It affects the wrist.
grade9-ict.explanation: Prolonged, repetitive wrist movements and poor wrist angle compress the median nerve in the carpal tunnel, causing pain, numbness and weakness in the hand.

grade9-ict.question: Neck pain in computer users is often caused by:
options: a monitor that is too high or too low, forcing the user to crane or bow their neck for long periods
using a laptop without a case
grade9-ict.answer: a monitor that is too high or too low, forcing the user to crane or bow their neck for long periods
acceptableAnswers: a monitor that is too high or too low, forcing the user to crane or bow their neck for long periods
grade9-ict.hint: The monitor height should be at eye level.
grade9-ict.explanation: If the screen is not at eye level, the user must hold their head in an awkward position, straining the neck muscles.

grade9-ict.question: Photosensitive epilepsy can be triggered in susceptible users by:
options: rapidly flashing images or lights on a screen
the colour of the desktop background
grade9-ict.answer: rapidly flashing images or lights on a screen
acceptableAnswers: rapidly flashing images or lights on a screen
grade9-ict.hint: Flashing lights can trigger seizures.
grade9-ict.explanation: In people with photosensitive epilepsy, flashing images at certain frequencies (typically 3–50 Hz) can trigger a seizure; content with rapid flashes should carry a warning.

grade9-ict.question: Prolonged exposure to noise from loud headphones or speakers can cause:
options: permanent hearing loss or tinnitus (ringing in the ears)
grade9-ict.answer: permanent hearing loss or tinnitus (ringing in the ears)
acceptableAnswers: permanent hearing loss or tinnitus (ringing in the ears)
grade9-ict.hint: Loud sound damages hair cells in the inner ear.
grade9-ict.explanation: The hair cells in the cochlea that detect sound cannot regenerate; sustained exposure to loud audio permanently reduces hearing ability.

grade9-ict.question: Sedentary behaviour (sitting for many hours without movement) associated with heavy computer use increases the risk of:
options: obesity, cardiovascular disease and deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
grade9-ict.answer: obesity, cardiovascular disease and deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
acceptableAnswers: obesity, cardiovascular disease and deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
grade9-ict.hint: Lack of movement has serious health consequences.
grade9-ict.explanation: Extended sitting without movement slows the metabolism, contributes to weight gain, and increases the risk of blood clots forming in the legs.

grade9-ict.question: Blue light emitted by screens may contribute to:
options: disrupted sleep patterns, particularly if screens are used close to bedtime
grade9-ict.answer: disrupted sleep patterns, particularly if screens are used close to bedtime
acceptableAnswers: disrupted sleep patterns, particularly if screens are used close to bedtime
grade9-ict.hint: Blue light suppresses melatonin.
grade9-ict.explanation: Blue light inhibits the production of melatonin, the hormone that induces sleep; using screens in the evening can delay sleep onset and reduce sleep quality.

grade9-ict.question: Stress and anxiety can be health hazards associated with computer use because:
options: cyberbullying, information overload and the pressure to always be available online can increase stress levels
grade9-ict.answer: cyberbullying, information overload and the pressure to always be available online can increase stress levels
acceptableAnswers: cyberbullying, information overload and the pressure to always be available online can increase stress levels
grade9-ict.hint: Social and psychological effects of being always connected.
grade9-ict.explanation: Constant connectivity, exposure to negative online content and cyberbullying are recognised causes of stress and poor mental health in young people.

grade9-ict.question: Computer addiction is characterised by:
options: compulsive, excessive use of computers or the internet that interferes with daily life, sleep, schoolwork and relationships
using a computer for more than one hour per day
preferring to use a laptop instead of a desktop
grade9-ict.answer: compulsive, excessive use of computers or the internet that interferes with daily life, sleep, schoolwork and relationships
acceptableAnswers: compulsive, excessive use of computers or the internet that interferes with daily life, sleep, schoolwork and relationships
grade9-ict.hint: When it takes over other aspects of life.
grade9-ict.explanation: Computer or internet addiction is a behavioural disorder where the compulsion to use screens disrupts sleep, school performance and real-world social relationships.

grade9-ict.question: Dry eyes in computer users are caused by:
options: blinking less frequently than normal while concentrating on a screen, reducing moisture across the eye surface
using the computer in bright light
grade9-ict.answer: blinking less frequently than normal while concentrating on a screen, reducing moisture across the eye surface
acceptableAnswers: blinking less frequently than normal while concentrating on a screen, reducing moisture across the eye surface
grade9-ict.hint: Screen focus reduces blink rate.
grade9-ict.explanation: The average person blinks far less frequently when concentrating on a screen, reducing the spread of tear film and causing dry, irritated eyes.

grade9-ict.question: Poor posture while using a laptop on a bed or sofa can cause:
options: back, neck and shoulder strain because the spine is not properly supported
grade9-ict.answer: back, neck and shoulder strain because the spine is not properly supported
acceptableAnswers: back, neck and shoulder strain because the spine is not properly supported
grade9-ict.hint: Soft surfaces and low screens cause you to slouch.
grade9-ict.explanation: Using a laptop on a bed usually means looking down at a low screen while the spine is unsupported, creating forward-head posture and muscle strain.

grade9-ict.question: The recommended distance between a user's eyes and a computer monitor is approximately:
grade9-ict.answer: 50 to 70 cm (about arm's length)
grade9-ict.hint: About arm's length.
grade9-ict.explanation: Sitting about 50–70 cm from the screen gives a comfortable viewing angle, reduces eye strain and limits exposure to any electromagnetic emissions.

grade9-ict.question: An ergonomic chair should be adjusted so that:
options: both feet rest flat on the floor, knees are at a right angle and the lower back is supported by the lumbar rest
the user must stretch to reach the keyboard
the seat is as high as possible
grade9-ict.answer: both feet rest flat on the floor, knees are at a right angle and the lower back is supported by the lumbar rest
acceptableAnswers: both feet rest flat on the floor, knees are at a right angle and the lower back is supported by the lumbar rest
grade9-ict.hint: Feet flat, knees 90°, lumbar support.
grade9-ict.explanation: Correct chair adjustment maintains the natural curve of the spine, keeps blood flowing to the legs and reduces pressure on the lumbar discs.

grade9-ict.question: The top of a monitor should be positioned at or just below eye level so that:
options: the user looks slightly downward at the screen, keeping the neck in a neutral position
the user must look up to see the screen, strengthening neck muscles
the screen is tilted away from the user
the screen is as far from the user as possible
grade9-ict.answer: the user looks slightly downward at the screen, keeping the neck in a neutral position
acceptableAnswers: the user looks slightly downward at the screen, keeping the neck in a neutral position
grade9-ict.hint: Slight downward gaze is most comfortable.
grade9-ict.explanation: A screen positioned at or slightly below eye level allows the head to rest in its natural forward position, reducing neck and shoulder strain.

grade9-ict.question: Using a wrist rest while typing helps to:
options: keep the wrists in a neutral, flat position and reduce the risk of carpal tunnel syndrome and RSI
grade9-ict.answer: keep the wrists in a neutral, flat position and reduce the risk of carpal tunnel syndrome and RSI
acceptableAnswers: keep the wrists in a neutral, flat position and reduce the risk of carpal tunnel syndrome and RSI
grade9-ict.hint: Neutral wrist position reduces nerve and tendon stress.
grade9-ict.explanation: A wrist rest allows the user to rest their wrists between bursts of typing with the wrists in a neutral position, reducing strain on tendons and the median nerve.

grade9-ict.question: Taking regular breaks from the computer every 30–60 minutes helps to:
options: reduce eye strain, prevent RSI, ease back and neck tension and improve overall concentration
grade9-ict.answer: reduce eye strain, prevent RSI, ease back and neck tension and improve overall concentration
acceptableAnswers: reduce eye strain, prevent RSI, ease back and neck tension and improve overall concentration
grade9-ict.hint: Movement breaks counteract the effects of prolonged static posture.
grade9-ict.explanation: Regular micro-breaks allow the eyes to refocus, muscles to relax and blood to circulate, reducing the cumulative strain of long computer sessions.

grade9-ict.question: An anti-glare screen filter reduces:
options: reflections from windows and lights that cause eye strain when viewing the monitor
grade9-ict.answer: reflections from windows and lights that cause eye strain when viewing the monitor
acceptableAnswers: reflections from windows and lights that cause eye strain when viewing the monitor
grade9-ict.hint: Glare = reflected light on the screen.
grade9-ict.explanation: An anti-glare filter has a matte surface that diffuses reflected light, reducing the brightness contrast between the screen content and reflections.

grade9-ict.question: Cable management trunking in a computer lab is used to:
options: speed up the data transfer rate of network cables
route cables neatly along walls or under desks to eliminate trip hazards and keep the workspace tidy
grade9-ict.answer: route cables neatly along walls or under desks to eliminate trip hazards and keep the workspace tidy
acceptableAnswers: route cables neatly along walls or under desks to eliminate trip hazards and keep the workspace tidy
grade9-ict.hint: Trunking = neat cable channels.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cable trunking channels guide cables safely along walls or under desk surfaces, eliminating trailing cables that are a trip and safety hazard.

grade9-ict.question: The keyboard and mouse should be placed so that:
options: the mouse is on the opposite side of the room from the keyboard
the keyboard is directly on the floor
the keyboard is as high as possible
the elbows are at or slightly above desk height, upper arms hang vertically and wrists are flat
grade9-ict.answer: the elbows are at or slightly above desk height, upper arms hang vertically and wrists are flat
acceptableAnswers: the elbows are at or slightly above desk height, upper arms hang vertically and wrists are flat
grade9-ict.hint: Elbows at desk height, shoulders relaxed.
grade9-ict.explanation: Correct keyboard and mouse placement allows the arms to hang naturally from the shoulders, reducing strain on the elbows, wrists and shoulders.

grade9-ict.question: Adequate lighting in a computer lab should:
options: be bright enough to see documents clearly without causing screen glare, and avoid direct light hitting the screen
be as dark as possible to make the screen easier to see
be bright enough to prevent anyone from sleeping but no more
use only natural sunlight directed at the screen
grade9-ict.answer: be bright enough to see documents clearly without causing screen glare, and avoid direct light hitting the screen
acceptableAnswers: be bright enough to see documents clearly without causing screen glare, and avoid direct light hitting the screen
grade9-ict.hint: Balance between document visibility and screen glare.
grade9-ict.explanation: Room lighting must illuminate work surfaces and printed documents but should not reflect on the screen; indirect, diffuse lighting is best.

grade9-ict.question: Regular software updates and antivirus scans help to prevent:
options: malware infections, security vulnerabilities and data loss caused by viruses and ransomware
grade9-ict.answer: malware infections, security vulnerabilities and data loss caused by viruses and ransomware
acceptableAnswers: malware infections, security vulnerabilities and data loss caused by viruses and ransomware
grade9-ict.hint: Updated software = patched vulnerabilities.
grade9-ict.explanation: Updates patch known security flaws; antivirus scans detect and remove malicious software before it can cause data loss or system damage.

grade9-ict.question: A screen saver that activates after a few minutes of inactivity helps to:
options: increase battery life of desktop computers
prevent a static image from being permanently burned into older CRT and plasma screens, and obscures the screen for privacy
grade9-ict.answer: prevent a static image from being permanently burned into older CRT and plasma screens, and obscures the screen for privacy
acceptableAnswers: prevent a static image from being permanently burned into older CRT and plasma screens, and obscures the screen for privacy
grade9-ict.hint: Screen savers were invented for screen burn.
grade9-ict.explanation: On older CRT and plasma screens, a static image displayed for long periods can permanently "burn" into the phosphor; screen savers also obscure the user's work.

grade9-ict.question: Parental controls and content filters on school computers help to:
options: prevent students from accessing inappropriate or harmful online content during school hours
improve the graphics quality of the screen
allow students to install any software they choose
grade9-ict.answer: prevent students from accessing inappropriate or harmful online content during school hours
acceptableAnswers: prevent students from accessing inappropriate or harmful online content during school hours
grade9-ict.hint: Filtering keeps content safe.
grade9-ict.explanation: Content filters block websites categorised as inappropriate, protecting students from exposure to harmful material while using school resources.

grade9-ict.question: A footrest in an ergonomic workstation setup is used by:
options: anyone who wants to use the computer standing up
users who want to raise their monitors higher
users who want to reduce glare on the screen
users whose feet do not reach the floor comfortably when the chair is at the correct height, to support the legs and improve circulation
grade9-ict.answer: users whose feet do not reach the floor comfortably when the chair is at the correct height, to support the legs and improve circulation
acceptableAnswers: users whose feet do not reach the floor comfortably when the chair is at the correct height, to support the legs and improve circulation
grade9-ict.hint: Feet must be supported.
grade9-ict.explanation: If a chair adjusted to the correct height for the desk leaves the user's feet dangling, a footrest supports them in the correct position.

grade9-ict.question: Clear exit routes and emergency exits in a computer laboratory must always be:
options: kept completely unobstructed so everyone can evacuate quickly in an emergency
used as extra storage for computer boxes
marked with a red cross sign
locked during class to prevent interruptions
grade9-ict.answer: kept completely unobstructed so everyone can evacuate quickly in an emergency
acceptableAnswers: kept completely unobstructed so everyone can evacuate quickly in an emergency
grade9-ict.hint: Blocked exits are dangerous and illegal.
grade9-ict.explanation: Emergency regulations require clear, unobstructed exit routes; cluttered aisles or locked emergency doors can prevent safe evacuation during a fire or other emergency.

grade9-ict.question: Students should be taught to recognise phishing emails and suspicious links to:
options: teach them to create their own websites
protect personal data and prevent malware from being downloaded onto school computers
grade9-ict.answer: protect personal data and prevent malware from being downloaded onto school computers
acceptableAnswers: protect personal data and prevent malware from being downloaded onto school computers
grade9-ict.hint: Awareness prevents phishing attacks.
grade9-ict.explanation: Phishing emails trick users into revealing credentials or clicking malicious links; educating students to recognise the signs prevents data breaches and malware infections.

grade9-ict.question: Proper disposal of old computer equipment (e-waste) is important because:
options: old computers can be reused as door stops
throwing computers in the bin is the fastest method
electronic devices contain toxic materials such as lead, mercury and cadmium that can harm the environment and human health if sent to landfill
grade9-ict.answer: electronic devices contain toxic materials such as lead, mercury and cadmium that can harm the environment and human health if sent to landfill
acceptableAnswers: electronic devices contain toxic materials such as lead, mercury and cadmium that can harm the environment and human health if sent to landfill
grade9-ict.hint: Electronics contain hazardous substances.
grade9-ict.explanation: Computers and monitors contain heavy metals and other hazardous materials; responsible recycling through certified e-waste facilities prevents these from entering soil and water.

grade9-ict.question: Computer ethics refers to:
options: the moral principles that guide the use of computers and technology
the technical rules for writing computer programs
the standards for computer hardware design
the laws about how computers are manufactured
grade9-ict.answer: the moral principles that guide the use of computers and technology
acceptableAnswers: the moral principles that guide the use of computers and technology
grade9-ict.hint: Ethics is about right and wrong behaviour.
grade9-ict.explanation: Computer ethics is the study of moral principles that guide responsible use of computers and information technology.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is an example of unethical computer use?
options: Saving your own files to a USB drive
Changing the desktop background on your own computer
Using a spell checker in a word processor
Accessing someone else's email account without permission
grade9-ict.answer: Accessing someone else's email account without permission
acceptableAnswers: Accessing someone else's email account without permission
grade9-ict.hint: Accessing an account that is not yours is wrong.
grade9-ict.explanation: Accessing another person's account without their permission violates their privacy and is both unethical and illegal.

grade9-ict.question: Hacking into a computer system without authorisation is:
options: perfectly acceptable if no data is changed
grade9-ict.answer: both unethical and illegal
grade9-ict.hint: Unauthorised access breaks both moral rules and the law.
grade9-ict.explanation: Hacking without permission is both ethically wrong (it violates others' rights) and illegal under computer misuse laws.

grade9-ict.question: Which principle of computer ethics says that technology should be used without harming others?
grade9-ict.answer: The principle of non-maleficence
grade9-ict.hint: Non-maleficence means "do no harm".
grade9-ict.explanation: Non-maleficence is the principle that technology should not be used in ways that cause harm to other people.

grade9-ict.question: Using a school computer to play games instead of completing the set task is an example of:
grade9-ict.answer: misuse of school resources
grade9-ict.hint: School computers are provided for educational use.
grade9-ict.explanation: Using school computers for personal entertainment rather than educational work is a misuse of shared resources.

grade9-ict.question: Sharing false information about a person on social media is:
options: a good use of social media
always protected by freedom of speech
grade9-ict.answer: unethical and potentially illegal
grade9-ict.hint: False information can harm a person's reputation.
grade9-ict.explanation: Sharing deliberately false information is unethical and may be illegal under defamation or harassment laws.

grade9-ict.question: A computer professional has an ethical duty to:
options: protect the privacy and security of users' data
share all data with any interested party
sell users' data to the highest bidder
grade9-ict.answer: protect the privacy and security of users' data
acceptableAnswers: protect the privacy and security of users' data
grade9-ict.hint: Professionals are trusted with others' data.
grade9-ict.explanation: Computer professionals are trusted with sensitive data and have an ethical obligation to protect it from misuse.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following actions demonstrates ethical computer use?
options: Citing the source of an image you use in a presentation
Installing software on a school computer without permission
Sharing your login password with a friend
Copying a classmate's project and submitting it as your own
grade9-ict.answer: Citing the source of an image you use in a presentation
acceptableAnswers: Citing the source of an image you use in a presentation
grade9-ict.hint: Giving credit for others' work is ethical.
grade9-ict.explanation: Acknowledging the source of images and other content respects copyright and is an example of ethical computing.

grade9-ict.question: The digital divide refers to:
options: the speed difference between two computers
the gap between old and new software versions
the gap between people who have access to technology and those who do not
the difference between hardware and software
grade9-ict.answer: the gap between people who have access to technology and those who do not
acceptableAnswers: the gap between people who have access to technology and those who do not
grade9-ict.hint: Not everyone has equal access to ICT.
grade9-ict.explanation: The digital divide is the inequality between those with ready access to computers and the internet and those without.

grade9-ict.question: Installing unauthorised software on a school computer is wrong because:
options: it helps other students learn new programs
it is required for some subjects
it makes the computer run faster
it could introduce viruses and violates the school's acceptable use policy
grade9-ict.answer: it could introduce viruses and violates the school's acceptable use policy
acceptableAnswers: it could introduce viruses and violates the school's acceptable use policy
grade9-ict.hint: Schools have policies about software installation.
grade9-ict.explanation: Unauthorised software may contain malware, slows the system and breaks the terms of the school's acceptable use policy.

grade9-ict.question: An acceptable use policy (AUP) is a document that:
options: controls the speed of an internet connection
sets out the rules for using an organisation's computer systems
grade9-ict.answer: sets out the rules for using an organisation's computer systems
acceptableAnswers: sets out the rules for using an organisation's computer systems
grade9-ict.hint: It is a set of guidelines users must agree to follow.
grade9-ict.explanation: An AUP defines what users may and may not do on an organisation's computers and network, to promote ethical use.

grade9-ict.question: Why is it unethical to use someone else's creative work without giving credit?
options: It makes the document too long
It denies the creator recognition and may violate copyright law
grade9-ict.answer: It denies the creator recognition and may violate copyright law
acceptableAnswers: It denies the creator recognition and may violate copyright law
grade9-ict.hint: Creators deserve acknowledgement for their work.
grade9-ict.explanation: Using another's work without credit steals the recognition they deserve and may break copyright law.

grade9-ict.question: Which statement about computer ethics is true?
options: Ethical rules for computers are based on the same values as ethical rules for everyday life
Anything done online has no ethical implications
Ethics do not apply if you are using a personal computer
Computer ethics only applies to professional programmers
grade9-ict.answer: Ethical rules for computers are based on the same values as ethical rules for everyday life
acceptableAnswers: Ethical rules for computers are based on the same values as ethical rules for everyday life
grade9-ict.hint: Honesty and respect apply online as well as offline.
grade9-ict.explanation: Computer ethics extends general ethical values — honesty, respect, fairness — to the specific context of computing.

grade9-ict.question: Personal data is information that:
options: is always available to the public
is used only by the police
can be used to identify a specific individual
grade9-ict.answer: can be used to identify a specific individual
acceptableAnswers: can be used to identify a specific individual
grade9-ict.hint: A name or an ID number links to one person.
grade9-ict.explanation: Personal data is any information that, alone or combined, can identify a specific person, such as a name, address or ID number.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is an example of personal data?
options: The price of a loaf of bread
The name of the country's president
grade9-ict.answer: A person's date of birth
grade9-ict.hint: This information relates to a specific individual.
grade9-ict.explanation: A date of birth can help identify a specific person, making it personal data.

grade9-ict.question: Information privacy means that individuals have the right to:
options: make all personal data publicly available
control how their personal information is collected and used
access anyone else's personal data freely
delete all data held anywhere on the internet
grade9-ict.answer: control how their personal information is collected and used
acceptableAnswers: control how their personal information is collected and used
grade9-ict.hint: Privacy is about control over your own data.
grade9-ict.explanation: Information privacy is the right of individuals to decide who can collect their personal data and how it can be used.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of sensitive personal data?
options: The name of a country's capital city
grade9-ict.answer: The name of a country's capital city
acceptableAnswers: The name of a country's capital city
grade9-ict.hint: This fact does not relate to any individual.
grade9-ict.explanation: The name of a capital city is general knowledge, not information about a person. Medical records, finances and beliefs are sensitive personal data.

grade9-ict.question: Cookies stored by a website on your browser are used mainly to:
options: remember your preferences and track your browsing activity
grade9-ict.answer: remember your preferences and track your browsing activity
acceptableAnswers: remember your preferences and track your browsing activity
grade9-ict.hint: They are small files that remember information.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cookies store data about your preferences and activity so websites can personalise your experience and track visits.

grade9-ict.question: To protect your privacy when using social media, you should:
options: review your privacy settings and limit who can see your posts
share your home address and phone number publicly
use the same simple password on all platforms
accept every friend or follow request you receive
grade9-ict.answer: review your privacy settings and limit who can see your posts
acceptableAnswers: review your privacy settings and limit who can see your posts
grade9-ict.hint: Control who can see your information.
grade9-ict.explanation: Adjusting privacy settings so only trusted people see your posts reduces the risk of strangers accessing your personal information.

grade9-ict.question: An organisation collects your email address when you register on their website. Under good privacy practice, they should:
options: share it publicly on their website
store it forever even after you delete your account
sell it to any company that pays
use it only for the purpose stated at the time of collection
grade9-ict.answer: use it only for the purpose stated at the time of collection
acceptableAnswers: use it only for the purpose stated at the time of collection
grade9-ict.hint: Data should only be used for the reason it was collected.
grade9-ict.explanation: Good privacy practice requires using personal data only for the specific purpose explained to the user when the data was collected.

grade9-ict.question: The right to be forgotten (right to erasure) means that a person can:
options: remove all data from the internet instantly
request that an organisation deletes their personal data
prevent anyone from creating a website about them
stop companies from using any computers
grade9-ict.answer: request that an organisation deletes their personal data
acceptableAnswers: request that an organisation deletes their personal data
grade9-ict.hint: Under data protection laws, you can ask for your data to be removed.
grade9-ict.explanation: The right to be forgotten allows individuals to request that organisations delete their personal data when there is no longer a valid reason to keep it.

grade9-ict.question: Which action best protects your privacy when using a public computer?
options: Logging out of all accounts before leaving the computer
Saving your passwords in the browser
grade9-ict.answer: Logging out of all accounts before leaving the computer
acceptableAnswers: Logging out of all accounts before leaving the computer
grade9-ict.hint: The next user could access your accounts if you stay logged in.
grade9-ict.explanation: Logging out before leaving a shared computer prevents the next user from accessing your accounts and personal data.

grade9-ict.question: Sharing a friend's private photos on social media without their permission is:
options: an example of good computer ethics
a legal requirement in some countries
grade9-ict.answer: a violation of their privacy
grade9-ict.hint: Their photos belong to them.
grade9-ict.explanation: Sharing someone's private photos without consent violates their privacy and may constitute harassment or a breach of data protection law.

grade9-ict.question: Two-factor authentication protects your privacy by:
options: doubling the length of your password automatically
storing your password in two separate databases
requiring a second form of verification in addition to the password
making your password visible only to yourself
grade9-ict.answer: requiring a second form of verification in addition to the password
acceptableAnswers: requiring a second form of verification in addition to the password
grade9-ict.hint: A second step means a stolen password alone is not enough.
grade9-ict.explanation: Two-factor authentication adds a second check (such as a code sent to your phone) so a stolen password alone cannot unlock your account.

grade9-ict.question: A privacy policy on a website explains:
options: how to change the website's background colour
the technical specifications of the web server
the price of the products sold on the site
how the site collects, uses and protects visitors' personal data
grade9-ict.answer: how the site collects, uses and protects visitors' personal data
acceptableAnswers: how the site collects, uses and protects visitors' personal data
grade9-ict.hint: It tells you what the website does with your information.
grade9-ict.explanation: A privacy policy is a legal statement that discloses how a website collects, uses, stores and protects personal data.

grade9-ict.question: Entering personal details into a form on an unsecured (http, not https) website is risky because:
options: the website will delete your details immediately
the form will not submit at all
the data could be intercepted in transit
the browser will print the form automatically
grade9-ict.answer: the data could be intercepted in transit
acceptableAnswers: the data could be intercepted in transit
grade9-ict.hint: Without encryption, data travels in plain text.
grade9-ict.explanation: An unsecured http connection sends data without encryption, so it could be read by anyone who intercepts it on the network.

grade9-ict.question: The main aim of data security is to:
options: make data available to everyone on the internet
delete data that is no longer needed
reduce the speed of data transmission
protect data from unauthorised access, loss or damage
grade9-ict.answer: protect data from unauthorised access, loss or damage
acceptableAnswers: protect data from unauthorised access, loss or damage
grade9-ict.hint: Security keeps data safe.
grade9-ict.explanation: Data security covers all the measures taken to protect data from being accessed without permission, corrupted, or lost.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following makes a password strong?
options: A mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers and symbols
Using only your date of birth
grade9-ict.answer: A mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers and symbols
acceptableAnswers: A mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers and symbols
grade9-ict.hint: Complexity makes a password hard to guess.
grade9-ict.explanation: A strong password uses a variety of character types to increase the number of possible combinations, making it much harder to guess.

grade9-ict.question: A firewall helps protect a network by:
options: storing backup copies of all data
monitoring and filtering traffic entering and leaving the network
grade9-ict.answer: monitoring and filtering traffic entering and leaving the network
acceptableAnswers: monitoring and filtering traffic entering and leaving the network
grade9-ict.hint: It checks what is allowed to pass.
grade9-ict.explanation: A firewall inspects data packets and blocks any traffic that does not meet the security rules defined by the network administrator.

grade9-ict.question: Encryption protects data by:
options: converting it into an unreadable code that requires a key to decode
deleting it from the server after it is sent
compressing it to save storage space
making it available to all users on the network
grade9-ict.answer: converting it into an unreadable code that requires a key to decode
acceptableAnswers: converting it into an unreadable code that requires a key to decode
grade9-ict.hint: Without the key, the data looks like nonsense.
grade9-ict.explanation: Encryption scrambles data into ciphertext; only someone with the correct decryption key can read the original data.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is a physical security measure for protecting data?
grade9-ict.answer: Locking the server room
grade9-ict.hint: This prevents physical access to the hardware.
grade9-ict.explanation: Locking the server room prevents unauthorised people from physically accessing and stealing or damaging the servers.

grade9-ict.question: Antivirus software protects a computer by:
grade9-ict.answer: detecting and removing malicious software
grade9-ict.hint: Its job is to find and destroy malware.
grade9-ict.explanation: Antivirus software scans files and programs for known malicious code and removes or quarantines anything it finds.

grade9-ict.question: What should you do if you receive a suspicious email with an attachment from an unknown sender?
options: Forward it to all your contacts
Open it to find out what it contains
Delete it without opening the attachment
grade9-ict.answer: Delete it without opening the attachment
acceptableAnswers: Delete it without opening the attachment
grade9-ict.hint: An attachment may contain malware.
grade9-ict.explanation: Email attachments from unknown senders may carry viruses or ransomware; the safest action is to delete the email without opening the attachment.

grade9-ict.question: Two-factor authentication is more secure than a password alone because:
options: it removes the need for any password
even if the password is stolen, the attacker still needs the second factor
it makes the password twice as long
it stores two copies of the password
grade9-ict.answer: even if the password is stolen, the attacker still needs the second factor
acceptableAnswers: even if the password is stolen, the attacker still needs the second factor
grade9-ict.hint: Two steps are better than one.
grade9-ict.explanation: With 2FA, a stolen password is not enough; the attacker also needs the second verification (such as a phone code).

grade9-ict.question: Access control in data security means:
options: preventing anyone from using the computer
limiting who can read, write or delete specific data
allowing everyone to see all data
grade9-ict.answer: limiting who can read, write or delete specific data
acceptableAnswers: limiting who can read, write or delete specific data
grade9-ict.hint: Not everyone needs to see everything.
grade9-ict.explanation: Access control restricts which users can view, change or delete data, ensuring only authorised people can work with sensitive information.

grade9-ict.question: Ransomware is a type of malicious software that:
options: improves the quality of internet connections
encrypts the victim's files and demands payment for the decryption key
grade9-ict.answer: encrypts the victim's files and demands payment for the decryption key
acceptableAnswers: encrypts the victim's files and demands payment for the decryption key
grade9-ict.hint: It holds your files hostage.
grade9-ict.explanation: Ransomware encrypts a victim's files, making them inaccessible, and demands a ransom payment in exchange for the decryption key.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is the best practice for password management?
options: Use a different password for each account and change passwords regularly
Use the same simple password on all accounts
Write all passwords on a sticky note attached to the monitor
Share passwords with colleagues so they can help in emergencies
grade9-ict.answer: Use a different password for each account and change passwords regularly
acceptableAnswers: Use a different password for each account and change passwords regularly
grade9-ict.hint: Different passwords limit the damage if one is compromised.
grade9-ict.explanation: Using unique passwords for each account means that if one is stolen, attackers cannot use it to access other accounts.

grade9-ict.question: A biometric security measure uses:
options: a physical characteristic such as a fingerprint or retina scan to verify identity
a hardware key plugged into a USB port
a long random string of characters as a password
a code sent by text message
grade9-ict.answer: a physical characteristic such as a fingerprint or retina scan to verify identity
acceptableAnswers: a physical characteristic such as a fingerprint or retina scan to verify identity
grade9-ict.hint: It uses part of your body.
grade9-ict.explanation: Biometric authentication verifies identity using unique physical characteristics such as fingerprints, retina patterns or facial recognition.

grade9-ict.question: SSL/TLS in a web address shows that:
options: the website does not use any cookies
the page has been approved by a government authority
the connection between the browser and the server is encrypted
the website is free to use
grade9-ict.answer: the connection between the browser and the server is encrypted
acceptableAnswers: the connection between the browser and the server is encrypted
grade9-ict.hint: The padlock symbol indicates encrypted communication.
grade9-ict.explanation: SSL/TLS encrypts the data sent between a browser and a web server, indicated by "https" and a padlock icon.

grade9-ict.question: Why should antivirus software be updated regularly?
options: Updates remove the need for a firewall
Regular updates make the computer run faster
New threats appear constantly, and updates add definitions to detect them
Older antivirus programs delete all your files
grade9-ict.answer: New threats appear constantly, and updates add definitions to detect them
acceptableAnswers: New threats appear constantly, and updates add definitions to detect them
grade9-ict.hint: Malware evolves quickly.
grade9-ict.explanation: New viruses and malware appear every day; antivirus updates add the signatures needed to detect and remove the latest threats.

grade9-ict.question: A data backup is:
options: a copy of data kept separately so it can be restored if the original is lost
a program that speeds up the hard disk
grade9-ict.answer: a copy of data kept separately so it can be restored if the original is lost
acceptableAnswers: a copy of data kept separately so it can be restored if the original is lost
grade9-ict.hint: A backup is a spare copy.
grade9-ict.explanation: A backup is a copy of data stored separately from the original so it can be used to restore data if the original is lost, damaged or corrupted.

grade9-ict.question: Which backup method copies only the files that have changed since the last full backup?
grade9-ict.answer: Incremental backup
grade9-ict.hint: It only copies new or changed files.
grade9-ict.explanation: An incremental backup copies only the data that has changed since the previous backup (full or incremental), saving time and storage space.

grade9-ict.question: A full backup:
options: copies only files changed since the last backup
copies all selected data, regardless of whether it has changed
runs only when the computer is idle
makes a copy only when the disk is nearly full
grade9-ict.answer: copies all selected data, regardless of whether it has changed
acceptableAnswers: copies all selected data, regardless of whether it has changed
grade9-ict.hint: It does a complete copy every time.
grade9-ict.explanation: A full backup copies every selected file each time it runs, creating a complete independent copy of all the data.

grade9-ict.question: Why should a backup be stored in a different location from the original data?
options: So that the backup runs faster on a second computer
So that a disaster such as a fire or flood that destroys the original cannot also destroy the backup
So that no password is needed to access the backup
So that the backup takes up less disk space
grade9-ict.answer: So that a disaster such as a fire or flood that destroys the original cannot also destroy the backup
acceptableAnswers: So that a disaster such as a fire or flood that destroys the original cannot also destroy the backup
grade9-ict.hint: Two copies in the same room can both be lost at once.
grade9-ict.explanation: Storing backups off-site or in the cloud means a local disaster cannot destroy both the original and the backup at the same time.

grade9-ict.question: Cloud backup means storing backup copies:
options: on a CD-ROM kept in the same room
on remote servers accessed over the internet
on the second hard disk inside the computer
on a USB drive attached to the computer
grade9-ict.answer: on remote servers accessed over the internet
acceptableAnswers: on remote servers accessed over the internet
grade9-ict.hint: The cloud is a network of remote servers.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cloud backup stores copies of data on remote servers managed by an online service provider, accessible from anywhere with an internet connection.

grade9-ict.question: How often should critical business data be backed up?
options: Only when the computer breaks down
Once a year is usually enough
Only when a virus is detected
As frequently as possible — daily or more often
grade9-ict.answer: As frequently as possible — daily or more often
acceptableAnswers: As frequently as possible — daily or more often
grade9-ict.hint: The more often you back up, the less data you can lose.
grade9-ict.explanation: Critical data should be backed up as frequently as possible; the longer the gap between backups, the more data can be lost if something goes wrong.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is a suitable medium for backing up large amounts of data?
options: External hard disk or cloud storage
A printed copy of the screen
grade9-ict.answer: External hard disk or cloud storage
acceptableAnswers: External hard disk or cloud storage
grade9-ict.hint: Large backups need large, persistent storage.
grade9-ict.explanation: External hard disks and cloud storage offer large capacity and persistent storage, making them suitable for backing up significant amounts of data.

grade9-ict.question: What is a backup rotation scheme?
options: A way of spinning hard disk platters faster
A method for changing passwords automatically
A plan for cycling through multiple sets of backup media so older backups are retained
A schedule for rotating staff who do the backups
grade9-ict.answer: A plan for cycling through multiple sets of backup media so older backups are retained
acceptableAnswers: A plan for cycling through multiple sets of backup media so older backups are retained
grade9-ict.hint: It keeps several generations of backups.
grade9-ict.explanation: A rotation scheme uses multiple sets of backup media in sequence so you can restore data from several different points in the past.

grade9-ict.question: A backup is useless unless:
options: it is stored on a magnetic tape
it is printed and stored in a filing cabinet
it is encrypted with a 256-bit key
it has been tested and confirmed to restore correctly
grade9-ict.answer: it has been tested and confirmed to restore correctly
acceptableAnswers: it has been tested and confirmed to restore correctly
grade9-ict.hint: A backup you cannot restore from is worthless.
grade9-ict.explanation: Backups must be tested by actually restoring data from them; a backup that cannot be restored is no protection at all.

grade9-ict.question: Ransomware attacks highlight the importance of backups because:
options: a recent backup allows the victim to restore files without paying the ransom
backups alert you when ransomware arrives
backups prevent ransomware from being installed
backups contain the decryption key for ransomware
grade9-ict.answer: a recent backup allows the victim to restore files without paying the ransom
acceptableAnswers: a recent backup allows the victim to restore files without paying the ransom
grade9-ict.hint: A backup gives you a clean copy to return to.
grade9-ict.explanation: If files are encrypted by ransomware, a recent backup means the victim can restore their data without paying the criminals.

grade9-ict.question: What does the 3-2-1 backup rule recommend?
options: 3 copies of data, on 2 different media types, with 1 stored off-site
Use 3 passwords, 2 antivirus programs and 1 firewall
Delete old backups after 3 weeks using 2 computers and 1 server
Back up 3 times a day using 2 hard drives, 1 inside the computer
grade9-ict.answer: 3 copies of data, on 2 different media types, with 1 stored off-site
acceptableAnswers: 3 copies of data, on 2 different media types, with 1 stored off-site
grade9-ict.hint: The numbers refer to copies, media types and off-site copies.
grade9-ict.explanation: The 3-2-1 rule means keep 3 copies of data, store on 2 different types of media, and keep 1 copy off-site for disaster recovery.

grade9-ict.question: Which device provides automatic real-time backup of files as they change?
options: A NAS (Network Attached Storage) with continuous backup software
grade9-ict.answer: A NAS (Network Attached Storage) with continuous backup software
acceptableAnswers: A NAS (Network Attached Storage) with continuous backup software
grade9-ict.hint: Some backup systems work continuously, not just at scheduled times.
grade9-ict.explanation: A NAS device with continuous backup software can copy changes to files in real time, minimising the amount of data that could be lost.

grade9-ict.question: One advantage of cloud backup over a local external hard disk is that cloud backup:
options: can be accessed from any location with an internet connection
is always faster than a local disk
grade9-ict.answer: can be accessed from any location with an internet connection
acceptableAnswers: can be accessed from any location with an internet connection
grade9-ict.hint: Cloud storage is remote.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cloud backup is stored on remote servers, so it can be accessed and restored from any device with an internet connection.

grade9-ict.question: The main purpose of a Data Protection Act is to:
options: protect individuals by regulating how organisations collect and use personal data
ban the use of computers in government offices
prevent computers from being connected to the internet
make all personal data freely available to the public
grade9-ict.answer: protect individuals by regulating how organisations collect and use personal data
acceptableAnswers: protect individuals by regulating how organisations collect and use personal data
grade9-ict.hint: It gives people rights over their own data.
grade9-ict.explanation: A Data Protection Act sets rules for how organisations collect, store, use and share personal data, protecting individuals' privacy.

grade9-ict.question: Under a Data Protection Act, personal data must be:
options: stored only on paper, not on computers
accurate and kept up to date
shared freely with all other organisations
grade9-ict.answer: accurate and kept up to date
acceptableAnswers: accurate and kept up to date
grade9-ict.hint: Incorrect data is not allowed.
grade9-ict.explanation: Data protection legislation requires that personal data held about an individual is accurate and current; inaccurate data must be corrected.

grade9-ict.question: An individual's right of access under data protection law allows them to:
options: delete any data they do not like from any website
access data held about other people
request a copy of the personal data an organisation holds about them
grade9-ict.answer: request a copy of the personal data an organisation holds about them
acceptableAnswers: request a copy of the personal data an organisation holds about them
grade9-ict.hint: You can ask to see what is held about you.
grade9-ict.explanation: The right of access (subject access request) allows a person to ask an organisation for a copy of the personal data it holds about them.

grade9-ict.question: Data protection law says personal data should be kept:
options: until the individual requests more be collected
at least 100 years for legal purposes
only for as long as it is necessary
forever, to build a complete history
grade9-ict.answer: only for as long as it is necessary
acceptableAnswers: only for as long as it is necessary
grade9-ict.hint: Unnecessary data is a risk.
grade9-ict.explanation: Data must not be kept longer than the purpose requires; once the purpose is fulfilled, the data should be deleted.

grade9-ict.question: Who is responsible for ensuring that an organisation complies with data protection laws?
options: The individual whose data is held
The organisation that collects and processes the data
grade9-ict.answer: The organisation that collects and processes the data
acceptableAnswers: The organisation that collects and processes the data
grade9-ict.hint: Responsibility sits with whoever holds the data.
grade9-ict.explanation: The data controller — the organisation that collects and processes personal data — is legally responsible for complying with data protection legislation.

grade9-ict.question: Data collected for one purpose may NOT be used for:
options: a different purpose without the individual's consent
the original purpose after one week
grade9-ict.answer: a different purpose without the individual's consent
acceptableAnswers: a different purpose without the individual's consent
grade9-ict.hint: Purpose limitation is a core data protection principle.
grade9-ict.explanation: The principle of purpose limitation requires that data is used only for the specific purpose for which it was collected, unless further consent is obtained.

grade9-ict.question: Under data protection law, "consent" means:
options: the individual has freely and clearly agreed to the collection and use of their data
the data has been automatically gathered from the internet
the government has authorised the collection
the company has agreed to pay the individual for their data
grade9-ict.answer: the individual has freely and clearly agreed to the collection and use of their data
acceptableAnswers: the individual has freely and clearly agreed to the collection and use of their data
grade9-ict.hint: Consent must be given by the data subject.
grade9-ict.explanation: Consent is a legal basis for processing data; it requires a clear, freely given, and informed agreement from the individual.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is a breach of data protection law?
options: Deleting personal data when it is no longer needed
Allowing customers to view their own records
Storing customer data in an encrypted database
Selling customers' email addresses to a marketing company without their consent
grade9-ict.answer: Selling customers' email addresses to a marketing company without their consent
acceptableAnswers: Selling customers' email addresses to a marketing company without their consent
grade9-ict.hint: Using data without consent for a different purpose is a breach.
grade9-ict.explanation: Selling personal data without consent violates the principle of purpose limitation and other data protection requirements.

grade9-ict.question: What is a data breach?
options: A scheduled update of the data protection policy
An incident in which personal data is accessed, disclosed or lost without authorisation
A routine backup of the database
A request by an individual to see their own data
grade9-ict.answer: An incident in which personal data is accessed, disclosed or lost without authorisation
acceptableAnswers: An incident in which personal data is accessed, disclosed or lost without authorisation
grade9-ict.hint: Something went wrong with the security of the data.
