grade9-ict.explanation: A data breach occurs when personal data is accessed, altered, disclosed or lost in an unauthorised or unlawful way.

grade9-ict.question: Under GDPR and similar data protection laws, organisations must report certain data breaches to:
options: the relevant data protection authority within a specified time limit
the individuals affected before doing anything else
every other company in the country
grade9-ict.answer: the relevant data protection authority within a specified time limit
acceptableAnswers: the relevant data protection authority within a specified time limit
grade9-ict.hint: There is a regulatory body that oversees compliance.
grade9-ict.explanation: Organisations must notify the data protection authority of serious breaches, usually within 72 hours under GDPR.

grade9-ict.question: The principle of data minimisation in data protection law means:
options: all data must be stored in the smallest file format possible
data should be deleted every month
the organisation should have as few computers as possible
only the minimum amount of personal data necessary for the purpose should be collected
grade9-ict.answer: only the minimum amount of personal data necessary for the purpose should be collected
acceptableAnswers: only the minimum amount of personal data necessary for the purpose should be collected
grade9-ict.hint: Collect only what you need.
grade9-ict.explanation: Data minimisation means collecting only the personal data that is strictly necessary for the stated purpose, not more.

grade9-ict.question: Children's personal data is given extra protection under data protection laws because:
options: children may not understand the implications of sharing their data
children give stronger consent than adults
children use the internet more than adults
children's data is always more accurate
grade9-ict.answer: children may not understand the implications of sharing their data
acceptableAnswers: children may not understand the implications of sharing their data
grade9-ict.hint: Young people need more protection.
grade9-ict.explanation: Children may not fully understand how their data will be used, so laws give their data additional protection and often require parental consent.

grade9-ict.question: An organisation that fails to comply with data protection law can face:
options: a warning letter only, with no further consequences
automatic data deletion by the regulator
grade9-ict.answer: significant fines and legal action
grade9-ict.hint: Non-compliance is a serious offence.
grade9-ict.explanation: Breaches of data protection law can result in heavy financial penalties and legal proceedings against the organisation.

grade9-ict.question: A data controller differs from a data processor because the data controller:
options: builds the hardware that stores the data
decides the purpose and means of processing personal data
only carries out processing on behalf of another organisation
grade9-ict.answer: decides the purpose and means of processing personal data
acceptableAnswers: decides the purpose and means of processing personal data
grade9-ict.hint: The controller is in charge of how and why data is used.
grade9-ict.explanation: The data controller determines why data is collected and how it is processed; the data processor carries out processing as instructed by the controller.

grade9-ict.question: Copyright law protects:
options: original creative works such as music, text, images and software
physical objects like computers and monitors
grade9-ict.answer: original creative works such as music, text, images and software
acceptableAnswers: original creative works such as music, text, images and software
grade9-ict.hint: It covers intellectual creations.
grade9-ict.explanation: Copyright automatically protects original creative works — including writing, music, images and software — from being copied without permission.

grade9-ict.question: Downloading a music track from the internet without paying for it or obtaining permission is:
options: acceptable for personal use in all countries
a form of creative sharing encouraged by artists
legal if the song is more than five years old
grade9-ict.answer: an infringement of copyright
grade9-ict.hint: The creator has the right to decide how their work is distributed.
grade9-ict.explanation: Downloading copyrighted music without paying for it or having permission from the rights holder is copyright infringement.

grade9-ict.question: A Creative Commons (CC) licence allows:
options: the government to own all rights to the work
others to use the work under conditions set by the creator
anyone to modify and sell the work commercially without restriction
grade9-ict.answer: others to use the work under conditions set by the creator
acceptableAnswers: others to use the work under conditions set by the creator
grade9-ict.hint: The creator sets the terms under a CC licence.
grade9-ict.explanation: A Creative Commons licence lets creators choose conditions under which others may use their work, such as requiring attribution or prohibiting commercial use.

grade9-ict.question: Software that can be used and distributed freely without any charge is called:
grade9-ict.answer: freeware
grade9-ict.hint: The name says it is free.
grade9-ict.explanation: Freeware is software distributed at no cost; the developer retains copyright but allows free use and distribution.

grade9-ict.question: Open source software means:
options: the software can only be used by government organisations
the software is only available on open networks
the source code is made available so anyone can view, modify and distribute it
the software costs more than commercial software
grade9-ict.answer: the source code is made available so anyone can view, modify and distribute it
acceptableAnswers: the source code is made available so anyone can view, modify and distribute it
grade9-ict.hint: The source code is open — you can see exactly how it works.
grade9-ict.explanation: Open source software provides public access to its source code, allowing anyone to inspect, change and redistribute it under the terms of its licence.

grade9-ict.question: A software licence is a legal agreement that:
options: proves the computer was manufactured correctly
defines how the software may be used
shows the software is free from viruses
grade9-ict.answer: defines how the software may be used
acceptableAnswers: defines how the software may be used
grade9-ict.hint: It sets the terms of use.
grade9-ict.explanation: A software licence is a legal document granting the user permission to use the software and setting conditions on how it may be used.

grade9-ict.question: Using a single-user software licence on five computers simultaneously is:
options: acceptable if the computers are in the same building
a breach of the licence agreement
grade9-ict.answer: a breach of the licence agreement
acceptableAnswers: a breach of the licence agreement
grade9-ict.hint: A single-user licence covers only one computer.
grade9-ict.explanation: A single-user licence permits installation and use on only one computer; installing it on multiple computers violates the licence.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is an example of intellectual property?
options: A song written by a musician
A chair made in a factory
A river flowing through a town
grade9-ict.answer: A song written by a musician
acceptableAnswers: A song written by a musician
grade9-ict.hint: Intellectual property is a creation of the mind.
grade9-ict.explanation: A song is a creative work — intellectual property owned by the musician who created it.

grade9-ict.question: Shareware differs from freeware because shareware:
options: can only be used by businesses
is completely free with no conditions
requires a monthly subscription from the first day
is distributed free to try, but payment is required for continued or full use
grade9-ict.answer: is distributed free to try, but payment is required for continued or full use
acceptableAnswers: is distributed free to try, but payment is required for continued or full use
grade9-ict.hint: Try before you buy.
grade9-ict.explanation: Shareware is a try-before-you-buy model; the software is free to evaluate but must be purchased for ongoing or unrestricted use.

grade9-ict.question: A patent protects:
options: an original piece of creative writing
an invention or process that is new and non-obvious
the colour scheme used by a company
the name or logo of a brand
grade9-ict.answer: an invention or process that is new and non-obvious
acceptableAnswers: an invention or process that is new and non-obvious
grade9-ict.hint: Patents cover technical inventions.
grade9-ict.explanation: A patent grants exclusive rights to an inventor for a new and non-obvious invention or process, preventing others from making or selling it without permission.

grade9-ict.question: When copyright expires, the work enters the:
options: renewal period, meaning copyright is extended automatically
public domain, meaning anyone can use it freely
restricted zone, meaning no one can use it
private domain, meaning it is owned by the government
grade9-ict.answer: public domain, meaning anyone can use it freely
acceptableAnswers: public domain, meaning anyone can use it freely
grade9-ict.hint: After a long time, works can be used by everyone.
grade9-ict.explanation: When copyright expires, the work enters the public domain and can be used, reproduced or adapted by anyone without permission.

grade9-ict.question: Using an image found on a Google Images search in a school project is only legal if:
options: the image was uploaded before the current year
the image is larger than 500 × 500 pixels
the image is licensed for reuse, or you obtain the owner's permission
the search result shows the image on the first page
grade9-ict.answer: the image is licensed for reuse, or you obtain the owner's permission
acceptableAnswers: the image is licensed for reuse, or you obtain the owner's permission
grade9-ict.hint: Appearing in a search result does not mean the image is free to use.
grade9-ict.explanation: Most images online are copyright-protected; you must have a licence that allows reuse or obtain explicit permission from the copyright holder.

grade9-ict.question: A trademark protects:
options: a brand name, logo or symbol used to identify goods or services
a new invention or technical process
an original piece of music or writing
personal data held in a database
grade9-ict.answer: a brand name, logo or symbol used to identify goods or services
acceptableAnswers: a brand name, logo or symbol used to identify goods or services
grade9-ict.hint: It distinguishes one company's products from another's.
grade9-ict.explanation: A trademark is a registered symbol, name or slogan that identifies and distinguishes a company's products or services.

grade9-ict.question: The owner of a copyright is usually:
options: the person or company that created the work
the government of the country where the work is read
the internet service provider that hosts the work
the first person to download the work
grade9-ict.answer: the person or company that created the work
acceptableAnswers: the person or company that created the work
grade9-ict.hint: Creators own what they make.
grade9-ict.explanation: Copyright belongs to the creator of the work — the author, artist or developer — or the company they created it for.

grade9-ict.question: Plagiarism in ICT means:
options: sharing files legally with Creative Commons permission
citing every source you used in a bibliography
downloading licensed software for personal use
using someone else's work and presenting it as your own without giving credit
grade9-ict.answer: using someone else's work and presenting it as your own without giving credit
acceptableAnswers: using someone else's work and presenting it as your own without giving credit
grade9-ict.hint: It is about claiming ownership of work you did not create.
grade9-ict.explanation: Plagiarism is the act of taking another person's work — text, code, images, ideas — and presenting it as your own without acknowledgement.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is an example of plagiarism?
options: Copying a paragraph from a website and pasting it into a report without quoting it
Quoting a short passage and citing the author
Paraphrasing an idea and naming the original source
Summarising an article in your own words and referencing it
grade9-ict.answer: Copying a paragraph from a website and pasting it into a report without quoting it
acceptableAnswers: Copying a paragraph from a website and pasting it into a report without quoting it
grade9-ict.hint: No credit is given for the copied words.
grade9-ict.explanation: Copying text verbatim without quotation marks or a citation is plagiarism because it presents the original author's words as your own.

grade9-ict.question: Software used to detect plagiarism in students' work compares:
options: the submitted text against a large database of existing documents
the student's typing speed against a standard
the font size of the document against the allowed size
the file size against an expected maximum
grade9-ict.answer: the submitted text against a large database of existing documents
acceptableAnswers: the submitted text against a large database of existing documents
grade9-ict.hint: It looks for matching text in other sources.
grade9-ict.explanation: Plagiarism detection software checks a document against millions of web pages and academic papers to find matching text.

grade9-ict.question: To avoid plagiarism when using information from a website, you should:
options: use only the images, not the text
copy the text but change the font colour
paraphrase the information in your own words and cite the source
print the page without reading it
grade9-ict.answer: paraphrase the information in your own words and cite the source
acceptableAnswers: paraphrase the information in your own words and cite the source
grade9-ict.hint: Rewrite it and give credit.
grade9-ict.explanation: Paraphrasing puts the ideas in your own words, and a citation gives credit to the original source — together they avoid plagiarism.

grade9-ict.question: Self-plagiarism means:
options: submitting your own previous work as if it is new original work for a different assignment
using the same font as another student
printing more than one copy of your work
copying text from a famous author
grade9-ict.answer: submitting your own previous work as if it is new original work for a different assignment
acceptableAnswers: submitting your own previous work as if it is new original work for a different assignment
grade9-ict.hint: Even your own old work must be acknowledged.
grade9-ict.explanation: Self-plagiarism occurs when a student resubmits work they have already submitted elsewhere without disclosing that they have done so.

grade9-ict.question: Turnitin and similar tools are used in schools to:
grade9-ict.answer: detect plagiarism in submitted assignments
grade9-ict.hint: They are plagiarism-checking services.
grade9-ict.explanation: Turnitin and similar plagiarism detection services compare submitted text against databases of published work and student papers to find copied content.

grade9-ict.question: Plagiarism is harmful in schools because it:
options: reduces the time needed to complete assignments
helps teachers mark work more quickly
prevents students from developing their own skills and is unfair to other students
grade9-ict.answer: prevents students from developing their own skills and is unfair to other students
acceptableAnswers: prevents students from developing their own skills and is unfair to other students
grade9-ict.hint: It harms both the plagiarist and honest students.
grade9-ict.explanation: Plagiarism prevents learning and is unfair because it gives plagiarists an advantage over students who did their own work.

grade9-ict.question: A bibliography at the end of a report is used to:
options: list all the sources that were consulted in preparing the report
show the word count of the report
store backup copies of all images used
describe the contents of each chapter
grade9-ict.answer: list all the sources that were consulted in preparing the report
acceptableAnswers: list all the sources that were consulted in preparing the report
grade9-ict.hint: It credits the sources used.
grade9-ict.explanation: A bibliography or reference list gives full details of every source consulted, allowing readers to find and verify them.

grade9-ict.question: In addition to being academically dishonest, plagiarism may also be:
options: harmless if only a few sentences are copied
a legal requirement in some countries
grade9-ict.answer: a breach of copyright law
grade9-ict.hint: Using someone else's writing without permission may also be illegal.
grade9-ict.explanation: Plagiarism can also constitute copyright infringement if the copied material is protected by copyright.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following best describes academic integrity?
options: Submitting work on time no matter what
Completing your own work honestly and taking responsibility for it
Using as many sources as possible
Getting the highest mark in the class
grade9-ict.answer: Completing your own work honestly and taking responsibility for it
acceptableAnswers: Completing your own work honestly and taking responsibility for it
grade9-ict.hint: Integrity means honesty and responsibility.
grade9-ict.explanation: Academic integrity means doing your own work honestly, citing sources correctly, and taking responsibility for what you submit.

grade9-ict.question: Paraphrasing means:
options: rewriting someone else's idea in your own words while retaining the meaning
summarising a source in a single sentence
copying text word for word from a source
translating a document into another language
grade9-ict.answer: rewriting someone else's idea in your own words while retaining the meaning
acceptableAnswers: rewriting someone else's idea in your own words while retaining the meaning
grade9-ict.hint: Same idea, different words.
grade9-ict.explanation: Paraphrasing rewrites an idea using your own vocabulary and sentence structure while keeping the original meaning, and still requires a citation.

grade9-ict.question: Using an AI tool to write your whole assignment and submitting it as your own work is:
options: a form of academic dishonesty equivalent to plagiarism
grade9-ict.answer: a form of academic dishonesty equivalent to plagiarism
acceptableAnswers: a form of academic dishonesty equivalent to plagiarism
grade9-ict.hint: You are passing off work produced by another (the AI) as your own.
grade9-ict.explanation: Submitting AI-generated work as your own is academic dishonesty because you are presenting work you did not produce as your own effort.

grade9-ict.question: When must you provide a citation for information used in a report?
options: Every time you use a fact, idea or quotation taken from another source
Only when the source is a printed book
Only when the teacher specifically asks for it
grade9-ict.answer: Every time you use a fact, idea or quotation taken from another source
acceptableAnswers: Every time you use a fact, idea or quotation taken from another source
grade9-ict.hint: All borrowed ideas need a credit.
grade9-ict.explanation: Any time you use someone else's information — whether quoted or paraphrased — a citation must be provided to acknowledge the source.

grade9-ict.question: Phishing is an online attack in which criminals:
options: install useful software on your computer without asking
speed up the internet connection for their own use
pretend to be a trustworthy organisation to trick people into revealing personal information
create new websites to sell goods cheaply
grade9-ict.answer: pretend to be a trustworthy organisation to trick people into revealing personal information
acceptableAnswers: pretend to be a trustworthy organisation to trick people into revealing personal information
grade9-ict.hint: They pretend to be your bank or a trusted service.
grade9-ict.explanation: Phishing uses fake emails or websites that appear to come from a trusted source to trick people into handing over passwords or financial details.

grade9-ict.question: Cyber-bullying is defined as:
options: the use of digital technology to repeatedly harass, threaten or humiliate another person
sharing your own embarrassing photos online
downloading files without paying for them
grade9-ict.answer: the use of digital technology to repeatedly harass, threaten or humiliate another person
acceptableAnswers: the use of digital technology to repeatedly harass, threaten or humiliate another person
grade9-ict.hint: Bullying done through technology.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cyber-bullying uses digital channels — social media, messaging, gaming — to repeatedly intimidate, embarrass or harm another person.

grade9-ict.question: A computer virus is a program that:
options: speeds up the computer by removing old software
connects a computer to the internet automatically
cleans up unwanted files from the disk
copies itself and spreads to other files or computers, often causing damage
grade9-ict.answer: copies itself and spreads to other files or computers, often causing damage
acceptableAnswers: copies itself and spreads to other files or computers, often causing damage
grade9-ict.hint: Like a biological virus, it spreads and harms.
grade9-ict.explanation: A computer virus is malicious software that replicates itself by attaching to other files and can corrupt data, slow the system or enable further attacks.

grade9-ict.question: Spam email is best described as:
options: an official communication from your internet provider
unsolicited bulk messages, often advertising goods or carrying malware
a program for organising your inbox
grade9-ict.answer: unsolicited bulk messages, often advertising goods or carrying malware
acceptableAnswers: unsolicited bulk messages, often advertising goods or carrying malware
grade9-ict.hint: Unwanted bulk email you did not ask for.
grade9-ict.explanation: Spam is mass unsolicited email, typically used for advertising, phishing or distributing malware.

grade9-ict.question: A Trojan horse in computing is:
options: malicious software disguised as a legitimate program
a method for speeding up downloads
a tool for recovering deleted files
grade9-ict.answer: malicious software disguised as a legitimate program
acceptableAnswers: malicious software disguised as a legitimate program
grade9-ict.hint: It looks helpful but is actually harmful.
grade9-ict.explanation: A Trojan horse appears to be useful software but secretly carries malicious code that runs when the program is installed.

grade9-ict.question: Spyware is malicious software designed to:
options: organise files on the hard disk
secretly collect information about a user and send it to a third party
improve the speed of the internet connection
grade9-ict.answer: secretly collect information about a user and send it to a third party
acceptableAnswers: secretly collect information about a user and send it to a third party
grade9-ict.hint: It spies on you without your knowledge.
grade9-ict.explanation: Spyware silently monitors a user's activities — browsing, keystrokes, passwords — and transmits the data to criminals without the user's knowledge.

grade9-ict.question: Online grooming refers to:
options: an adult building a relationship with a child online in order to exploit them
tidying up your social media profile
updating your privacy settings on a social network
removing unwanted software from your computer
grade9-ict.answer: an adult building a relationship with a child online in order to exploit them
acceptableAnswers: an adult building a relationship with a child online in order to exploit them
grade9-ict.hint: This is a serious safeguarding issue.
grade9-ict.explanation: Online grooming is when an adult builds a relationship of trust with a child online with the intention of exploiting or abusing them.

grade9-ict.question: If you receive a message online from a stranger that makes you feel uncomfortable, you should:
options: reply to find out what they want
forward it to all your friends
tell a trusted adult and report or block the sender
grade9-ict.answer: tell a trusted adult and report or block the sender
acceptableAnswers: tell a trusted adult and report or block the sender
grade9-ict.hint: Always report uncomfortable online contact to an adult.
grade9-ict.explanation: Telling a trusted adult ensures the right people are informed; reporting and blocking the sender stops further contact.

grade9-ict.question: Identity theft online involves:
options: someone using another person's personal information without their knowledge to commit fraud
changing the username on a social network
grade9-ict.answer: someone using another person's personal information without their knowledge to commit fraud
acceptableAnswers: someone using another person's personal information without their knowledge to commit fraud
grade9-ict.hint: Someone steals who you are to commit crimes in your name.
grade9-ict.explanation: Identity theft occurs when criminals obtain personal details and use them fraudulently — to open bank accounts, apply for loans or make purchases.

grade9-ict.question: A keylogger records:
options: the speed of the internet connection
the number of files on the hard disk
every key pressed on the keyboard, capturing passwords and messages
grade9-ict.answer: every key pressed on the keyboard, capturing passwords and messages
acceptableAnswers: every key pressed on the keyboard, capturing passwords and messages
grade9-ict.hint: It watches every keystroke.
grade9-ict.explanation: A keylogger is malware that silently records all keystrokes, allowing criminals to capture passwords, bank details and private messages.

grade9-ict.question: Social engineering attacks exploit:
options: human psychology and trust rather than technical vulnerabilities
grade9-ict.answer: human psychology and trust rather than technical vulnerabilities
acceptableAnswers: human psychology and trust rather than technical vulnerabilities
grade9-ict.hint: They trick people, not machines.
grade9-ict.explanation: Social engineering manipulates people into revealing information or taking actions, exploiting trust, fear or urgency rather than hacking technology.

grade9-ict.question: The safest way to connect to online banking is:
options: using a shared school computer without logging out
on any public Wi-Fi network in a café
on your own device using a trusted private network with https
by typing the bank's address into a link from an email
grade9-ict.answer: on your own device using a trusted private network with https
acceptableAnswers: on your own device using a trusted private network with https
grade9-ict.hint: Use your own device on a trusted connection.
grade9-ict.explanation: Your own device on a private, trusted network with an https connection minimises the risk of interception or keylogging.

grade9-ict.question: A DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) attack works by:
options: inserting a virus into every file on the server
flooding a server with so many requests that it becomes unable to respond to legitimate users
grade9-ict.answer: flooding a server with so many requests that it becomes unable to respond to legitimate users
acceptableAnswers: flooding a server with so many requests that it becomes unable to respond to legitimate users
grade9-ict.hint: It overwhelms the server with traffic.
grade9-ict.explanation: A DDoS attack uses many compromised computers to send huge volumes of requests to a server, overloading it so legitimate users cannot access the service.

grade9-ict.question: Fake news online is dangerous because it:
options: spreads quickly and can mislead many people before it is corrected
is only shared by young people
grade9-ict.answer: spreads quickly and can mislead many people before it is corrected
acceptableAnswers: spreads quickly and can mislead many people before it is corrected
grade9-ict.hint: It travels far before the truth catches up.
grade9-ict.explanation: Fake news spreads rapidly on social media, influencing opinions and behaviour before fact-checkers or media organisations can correct it.

grade9-ict.question: One positive social effect of the internet is that:
options: people can communicate and share information across the world instantly
it removes all forms of inequality
it eliminates the need for face-to-face interaction entirely
grade9-ict.answer: people can communicate and share information across the world instantly
acceptableAnswers: people can communicate and share information across the world instantly
grade9-ict.hint: Global communication is a major benefit.
grade9-ict.explanation: The internet enables instant global communication and information sharing, connecting people and organisations regardless of distance.

grade9-ict.question: Automation in industry can lead to:
options: computer viruses spreading to all machines
some jobs being replaced by machines, reducing employment in those roles
grade9-ict.answer: some jobs being replaced by machines, reducing employment in those roles
acceptableAnswers: some jobs being replaced by machines, reducing employment in those roles
grade9-ict.hint: Machines can do some jobs that people used to do.
grade9-ict.explanation: Automation replaces repetitive manual tasks with machines or software, which can reduce the number of workers needed in those roles.

grade9-ict.question: E-commerce has changed shopping by allowing:
options: prices to be set by the customer
goods to be sent for free to any address
shops to stop employing any staff at all
goods to be bought and sold over the internet without visiting a physical store
grade9-ict.answer: goods to be bought and sold over the internet without visiting a physical store
acceptableAnswers: goods to be bought and sold over the internet without visiting a physical store
grade9-ict.hint: You can buy things online.
grade9-ict.explanation: E-commerce enables consumers and businesses to buy and sell goods and services online, transforming retail and business models.

grade9-ict.question: One negative social effect of spending too much time on social media is:
options: reduced face-to-face social skills and increased feelings of isolation
grade9-ict.answer: reduced face-to-face social skills and increased feelings of isolation
acceptableAnswers: reduced face-to-face social skills and increased feelings of isolation
grade9-ict.hint: Online time can replace real-world interaction.
grade9-ict.explanation: Excessive social media use is linked to reduced face-to-face social interaction, loneliness, and mental health issues in young people.

grade9-ict.question: Teleworking (working from home using ICT) benefits employees by:
options: eliminating the need for a computer
reducing commuting time and offering greater flexibility
removing the need for any meetings
grade9-ict.answer: reducing commuting time and offering greater flexibility
acceptableAnswers: reducing commuting time and offering greater flexibility
grade9-ict.hint: No travel to the office is needed.
grade9-ict.explanation: Teleworking saves the time and cost of commuting and allows employees to arrange their working day more flexibly.

grade9-ict.question: One environmental benefit of using computers in business is:
options: more packaging waste from online shopping
reduced paper use through digital documents and email
greater carbon emissions from data centres
grade9-ict.answer: reduced paper use through digital documents and email
acceptableAnswers: reduced paper use through digital documents and email
grade9-ict.hint: Digital documents replace printed ones.
grade9-ict.explanation: Digital communication reduces the volume of paper documents that need to be printed, saving trees and reducing waste.

grade9-ict.question: The use of ICT in health care has led to:
options: faster diagnosis, better patient record management and remote consultations
the disappearance of all hospital staff
the elimination of all medical errors
patients diagnosing themselves without any medical guidance
grade9-ict.answer: faster diagnosis, better patient record management and remote consultations
acceptableAnswers: faster diagnosis, better patient record management and remote consultations
grade9-ict.hint: ICT helps doctors and patients.
grade9-ict.explanation: ICT in health care enables electronic patient records, computer-aided diagnosis, telemedicine and improved information sharing among medical staff.

grade9-ict.question: One concern about the widespread use of social media is:
options: the spread of misinformation and the erosion of privacy
that it prevents children from reading books
that it reduces the cost of phone calls
that it makes computers run more slowly
grade9-ict.answer: the spread of misinformation and the erosion of privacy
acceptableAnswers: the spread of misinformation and the erosion of privacy
grade9-ict.hint: False information travels fast on social platforms.
grade9-ict.explanation: Social media can spread false or misleading information rapidly, and platforms collect large amounts of personal data, raising privacy concerns.

grade9-ict.question: Online banking has created an economic benefit by:
options: reducing the cost of financial transactions and making banking available 24 hours a day
requiring every customer to own a smartphone
grade9-ict.answer: reducing the cost of financial transactions and making banking available 24 hours a day
acceptableAnswers: reducing the cost of financial transactions and making banking available 24 hours a day
grade9-ict.hint: Banking is cheaper and always available.
grade9-ict.explanation: Online banking reduces processing costs for banks and offers customers round-the-clock access to their accounts without visiting a branch.

grade9-ict.question: Digital entertainment (streaming music and video) has economically impacted:
options: the traditional music and DVD retail industry, causing many physical stores to close
grade9-ict.answer: the traditional music and DVD retail industry, causing many physical stores to close
acceptableAnswers: the traditional music and DVD retail industry, causing many physical stores to close
grade9-ict.hint: Streaming replaced buying physical media.
grade9-ict.explanation: Streaming services reduced demand for CDs and DVDs, causing many music and video rental shops to close and transforming how entertainment is sold.

grade9-ict.question: ICT in education provides the benefit of:
options: preventing students from doing their own research
access to a vast range of learning resources from anywhere with internet access
eliminating the role of teachers entirely
grade9-ict.answer: access to a vast range of learning resources from anywhere with internet access
acceptableAnswers: access to a vast range of learning resources from anywhere with internet access
grade9-ict.hint: The internet is a huge library.
grade9-ict.explanation: ICT gives students access to online courses, research papers, videos and interactive tools that would be impossible to provide in a physical classroom alone.

grade9-ict.question: One risk of society becoming too dependent on computer systems is:
options: a widespread system failure could disrupt essential services
people forget how to communicate in any language
computers learn to make all decisions for humans
all data is instantly shared with other countries
grade9-ict.answer: a widespread system failure could disrupt essential services
acceptableAnswers: a widespread system failure could disrupt essential services
grade9-ict.hint: If the computers fail, everything that depends on them stops.
grade9-ict.explanation: Overdependence on computer systems means that a hardware failure, software bug or cyberattack could disable banking, utilities, transport and communications.

grade9-ict.question: The use of computers has created jobs in areas such as:
options: vehicle manufacture using only hand tools
software development, network administration, cybersecurity and data analysis
grade9-ict.answer: software development, network administration, cybersecurity and data analysis
acceptableAnswers: software development, network administration, cybersecurity and data analysis
grade9-ict.hint: New technology creates new types of jobs.
grade9-ict.explanation: The computing industry has created millions of new jobs in programming, IT support, data science, cybersecurity and digital marketing.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is an input device?
grade9-ict.answer: Scanner
grade9-ict.hint: Data must travel INTO the computer.
grade9-ict.explanation: A scanner sends an image of a document into the computer, so it is an input device.

grade9-ict.question: Which input device is used to read the barcode on a tin of food at a supermarket till?
grade9-ict.answer: Barcode reader
grade9-ict.hint: The name says what it reads.
grade9-ict.explanation: A barcode reader scans the striped code and sends the product number to the computer.

grade9-ict.question: Which input device is best for entering a hand-drawn design directly into a computer?
grade9-ict.answer: A graphics tablet
grade9-ict.hint: The other three all send data OUT.
grade9-ict.explanation: A graphics tablet lets the user draw with a stylus, and the strokes go straight into the computer.

grade9-ict.question: Which device reads the marks made in pencil on a multiple-choice answer sheet?
grade9-ict.answer: Optical mark reader
grade9-ict.hint: It reads marks, not characters.
grade9-ict.explanation: An optical mark reader (OMR) detects pencil marks in fixed positions, which is how answer sheets are marked automatically.

grade9-ict.question: A shop must record which items are sold without anyone typing a product code. Which input device suits this best?
grade9-ict.answer: A barcode reader
grade9-ict.hint: Nothing may be typed.
grade9-ict.explanation: Scanning the barcode enters the product code with no typing, which is faster and avoids typing mistakes.

grade9-ict.question: A touch screen is unusual because it is:
options: Both an input and an output device
Neither an input nor an output device
grade9-ict.answer: Both an input and an output device
acceptableAnswers: Both an input and an output device
grade9-ict.hint: It shows and it receives.
grade9-ict.explanation: A touch screen displays the picture (output) and senses where it is touched (input), so it does both jobs.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is an output device?
grade9-ict.answer: Printer
grade9-ict.hint: Data must travel OUT of the computer.
grade9-ict.explanation: A printer takes data from the computer and produces it on paper, so it is an output device.

grade9-ict.question: Which output device produces large, accurate technical drawings?
grade9-ict.answer: Plotter
grade9-ict.hint: It draws with a pen on large paper.
grade9-ict.explanation: A plotter draws precise lines on large sheets, which is what engineering and architectural drawings need.

grade9-ict.question: Which type of printer is best for printing hundreds of pages of text quickly and cheaply?
grade9-ict.answer: Laser printer
grade9-ict.hint: Think about speed and cost per page.
grade9-ict.explanation: A laser printer prints whole pages at high speed with a low cost per page, which suits large text jobs.

grade9-ict.question: Which output device is most suitable for showing a presentation to a hall of two hundred people?
grade9-ict.answer: A projector
grade9-ict.hint: Everyone in the hall must see it at once.
grade9-ict.explanation: A projector throws the image onto a large screen so a whole audience can see it.

grade9-ict.question: A monitor’s picture is made of tiny dots. What is one of those dots called?
grade9-ict.answer: A pixel
grade9-ict.hint: Short for picture element.
grade9-ict.explanation: A pixel is one of the tiny dots that together make up the image on a screen.

grade9-ict.question: Which storage device is built into most desktop computers and holds the operating system?
grade9-ict.answer: Hard disk
grade9-ict.hint: It is inside the machine and holds everything permanently.
grade9-ict.explanation: The hard disk is the main internal storage, holding the operating system, programs and files.

grade9-ict.question: Which small storage device plugs into a USB port and is carried in a pocket?
grade9-ict.answer: Flash drive
grade9-ict.hint: It is the one you carry.
grade9-ict.explanation: A USB flash drive is small, removable solid-state storage used to carry files between machines.

grade9-ict.question: Which storage medium is read using a laser?
grade9-ict.answer: A DVD
grade9-ict.hint: It is an optical disc.
grade9-ict.explanation: Optical media such as CDs and DVDs are read by a laser reflecting off the surface of the disc.

grade9-ict.question: What is the main advantage of a solid-state drive over a traditional hard disk?
options: It has no moving parts, so it is faster and harder to damage
It always holds more data than a hard disk of the same price
It needs no power at all, even while it is being written to
It can never be erased once data has been written to it
grade9-ict.answer: It has no moving parts, so it is faster and harder to damage
acceptableAnswers: It has no moving parts, so it is faster and harder to damage
grade9-ict.hint: Think about what spins inside a hard disk.
grade9-ict.explanation: A solid-state drive stores data in memory chips rather than on spinning platters, so it reads faster and survives knocks better.

grade9-ict.question: A school must keep a copy of its records off the premises without buying any hardware. Which storage suits this best?
options: A DVD left in the office
A second hard disk in the same server
grade9-ict.answer: Cloud storage
grade9-ict.hint: It must be somewhere else, with nothing to buy.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cloud storage keeps the data on a provider’s servers elsewhere, which is off-site by definition and needs no hardware of the school’s own.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these storage capacities is the largest?
grade9-ict.answer: 1 terabyte
grade9-ict.hint: Work up the ladder of units.
grade9-ict.explanation: The order is kilobyte, megabyte, gigabyte, terabyte, so a terabyte is the largest of the four.

grade9-ict.question: What does CPU stand for?
grade9-ict.answer: Central Processing Unit
grade9-ict.hint: It is the part that does the processing.
grade9-ict.explanation: CPU stands for Central Processing Unit, the part of the computer that carries out the instructions.

grade9-ict.question: Which type of memory loses its contents when the computer is switched off?
grade9-ict.answer: RAM
grade9-ict.hint: It is the working memory.
grade9-ict.explanation: RAM is volatile: it holds the programs and data in use and is emptied when the power goes.

grade9-ict.question: Which type of memory keeps its contents permanently and cannot normally be written to?
grade9-ict.answer: ROM
grade9-ict.hint: Read Only Memory.
grade9-ict.explanation: ROM holds instructions such as the start-up routine; it is non-volatile and normally read only.

grade9-ict.question: A computer runs slowly whenever several programs are open at once. Which upgrade helps most directly?
grade9-ict.answer: More RAM
grade9-ict.hint: Where do open programs live?
grade9-ict.explanation: Open programs occupy RAM; when it runs short the computer swaps to disk, which is far slower, so more RAM is the direct fix.

grade9-ict.question: The speed of a processor is measured in:
grade9-ict.answer: Gigahertz
grade9-ict.hint: It measures cycles per second, not storage.
grade9-ict.explanation: Processor speed is a frequency, measured in gigahertz; gigabytes measure storage.

grade9-ict.question: How many bits are there in one byte?
grade9-ict.hint: It is a power of two.
grade9-ict.explanation: One byte is 8 bits.

grade9-ict.question: Which unit is the smallest?
grade9-ict.answer: Bit
grade9-ict.hint: Everything else is built from it.
grade9-ict.explanation: A bit is a single 0 or 1 and is the smallest unit of data; eight of them make a byte.

grade9-ict.question: Roughly how many bytes are there in one kilobyte?
grade9-ict.answer: About a thousand
grade9-ict.hint: The prefix kilo means a thousand.
grade9-ict.explanation: A kilobyte is about a thousand bytes (1024 exactly), a megabyte about a million and a gigabyte about a thousand million.

grade9-ict.question: A photograph is 4 megabytes. Roughly how many such photographs fit on a 2 gigabyte flash drive?
grade9-ict.answer: About 500
grade9-ict.hint: 1 gigabyte is about 1000 megabytes.
grade9-ict.explanation: 2 GB is about 2000 MB, and 2000 divided by 4 is about 500 photographs.

grade9-ict.question: Which flowchart symbol would be used for the step "DISPLAY total"?
grade9-ict.answer: A parallelogram
grade9-ict.hint: Something is being shown to the user.
grade9-ict.explanation: Displaying a value is an output step, and input/output is drawn as a parallelogram.

grade9-ict.question: How many arrows normally leave a process symbol?
grade9-ict.hint: Only a decision has a choice of paths.
grade9-ict.explanation: A process step has one way in and one way out; only a decision splits the flow.

grade9-ict.question: A flowchart has a diamond with only ONE arrow leaving it. What is wrong?
options: A diamond must have three exits
A diamond may not appear in a flowchart at all
A decision must have two exits, one for each answer
grade9-ict.answer: A decision must have two exits, one for each answer
acceptableAnswers: A decision must have two exits, one for each answer
grade9-ict.hint: What does a question have?
grade9-ict.explanation: A decision asks a yes/no question, so it needs a path for each answer; one exit means one answer has nowhere to go.

grade9-ict.question: A flowchart reads: START, INPUT x, y = x * 3, y = y - 2, OUTPUT y, STOP. With x = 5, what is output?
grade9-ict.hint: Do the two process steps in order.

grade9-ict.question: An algorithm reads: count = 0; repeat 5 times: count = count + 2. What is count at the end?
grade9-ict.hint: Add 2 five times, starting from 0.
grade9-ict.explanation: Five additions of 2 give 10.

grade9-ict.question: A flowchart asks "Is n less than 10?" and adds 1 to n each time the answer is Yes. If n starts at 7, how many times is 1 added?
grade9-ict.hint: Follow n: 7, 8, 9, then test again.
grade9-ict.explanation: n goes 7 to 8, 8 to 9, 9 to 10 - three additions - and at 10 the condition is false, so the loop stops.

grade9-ict.question: An algorithm reads: total = 0; for each of 3 prices, total = total + price. The prices are 120, 85 and 45. What is total?
grade9-ict.hint: Add them one at a time from zero.

grade9-ict.question: Which keyword begins a loop that repeats while a condition stays true?
grade9-ict.answer: WHILE
grade9-ict.hint: It keeps going as long as something holds.
grade9-ict.explanation: WHILE repeats its steps for as long as the condition is true.

grade9-ict.question: In an IF ... ELSE structure, when are the ELSE steps carried out?
grade9-ict.answer: When the condition is false
grade9-ict.hint: ELSE is the other path.
grade9-ict.explanation: The IF steps run when the condition is true; the ELSE steps run when it is false.

grade9-ict.question: A program must keep asking for a password until the correct one is typed. Which structure suits this best?
grade9-ict.answer: A WHILE loop
grade9-ict.hint: You do not know how many attempts it will take.
grade9-ict.explanation: The number of repetitions is unknown in advance, which is exactly what a condition-controlled WHILE loop is for.

grade9-ict.question: What happens if the condition of a WHILE loop never becomes false?
options: The program prints an error and stops
grade9-ict.answer: The loop runs forever
grade9-ict.hint: Nothing ever tells it to stop.
grade9-ict.explanation: A condition that is never made false gives an infinite loop; something inside the loop must eventually change it.

grade9-ict.question:
What does this Python code display?
a = 7
b = 2
print(a - b)
grade9-ict.hint: The subtraction is worked out first.
grade9-ict.explanation: 7 - 2 = 5, so 5 is displayed.

grade9-ict.question: In Python, which symbol is used to multiply?
grade9-ict.hint: The same symbol a spreadsheet uses.
grade9-ict.explanation: Python uses the asterisk * for multiplication.

grade9-ict.question:
What does this Python code display?
n = 3
if n > 5:
    print("High")
else:
    print("Low")
grade9-ict.answer: Low
grade9-ict.hint: Is 3 greater than 5?
grade9-ict.explanation: 3 is not greater than 5, so the condition is false and the else branch runs.

grade9-ict.question:
How many times does this loop print?
for i in range(5):
    print(i)
grade9-ict.hint: range(5) produces 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.
grade9-ict.explanation: range(5) gives five values, so print runs five times.

grade9-ict.question: An algorithm must output a message when a mark is 50 or more. Which two symbols does that need, in order?
grade9-ict.answer: A diamond, then a parallelogram
grade9-ict.hint: Test first, then show the message.
grade9-ict.explanation: The mark is tested in a decision (diamond), and the message is shown in an output step (parallelogram).

grade9-ict.question: A pupil is paid Rs 60 an hour. An algorithm reads the hours worked into h. Which line gives the pay?
grade9-ict.answer: pay = h * 60
grade9-ict.hint: Each hour is worth 60 rupees.
grade9-ict.explanation: The pay is the hourly rate multiplied by the number of hours, so pay = h * 60.

grade9-ict.question: What is the name of the whole spreadsheet file, containing several sheets?
grade9-ict.answer: A workbook
grade9-ict.hint: Each page inside it is a worksheet.
grade9-ict.explanation: The file is the workbook; each page within it is a worksheet.

grade9-ict.question: How many cells are there in the range B2:D4?
grade9-ict.hint: Count the columns and the rows, then multiply.
grade9-ict.explanation: Columns B, C and D by rows 2, 3 and 4 gives 3 x 3 = 9 cells.

grade9-ict.question: Which cell reference does not exist in a spreadsheet?
grade9-ict.hint: Which way round is a reference written?
grade9-ict.explanation: A reference is always the column letter followed by the row number, so 12B is not a valid reference.

grade9-ict.question: Cell A1 holds 8, A2 holds 2. What does =A1/A2 display?
grade9-ict.hint: The slash means divide.
grade9-ict.explanation: 8 divided by 2 is 4.

grade9-ict.question: Which formula adds 15 to whatever is in cell C4?
grade9-ict.hint: It must begin with an equals sign.
grade9-ict.explanation: =C4+15 starts with the equals sign and adds 15 to the value in C4.

grade9-ict.question: Cell A1 holds 4, A2 holds 6. What does =A1*2+A2 display?
grade9-ict.hint: Multiplication happens before addition.
grade9-ict.explanation: 4 * 2 = 8 first, then 8 + 6 = 14.

grade9-ict.question: What is displayed if a cell contains A1+A2 with no equals sign?
options: The sum of A1 and A2
grade9-ict.answer: The text A1+A2
grade9-ict.hint: Without the equals sign it is not a calculation.
grade9-ict.explanation: A cell entry that does not begin with = is stored as ordinary text and displayed exactly as typed.

grade9-ict.question: Which function returns the smallest value in a range?
grade9-ict.answer: MIN
grade9-ict.hint: Short for minimum.
grade9-ict.explanation: =MIN(A1:A20) returns the smallest value in the range.

grade9-ict.question: What is displayed by =AVERAGE(A1:A4) when the cells hold 4, 6, 8 and 2?
grade9-ict.hint: Add them and divide by how many there are.
grade9-ict.explanation: 4 + 6 + 8 + 2 = 20, and 20 divided by 4 is 5.

grade9-ict.question: What is displayed by =MAX(B1:B4) when the cells hold 12, 45, 7 and 30?
grade9-ict.hint: MAX returns one of the values, not a total.
grade9-ict.explanation: The largest of 12, 45, 7 and 30 is 45.

grade9-ict.question: A column holds 20 marks, but 3 of the cells are empty. What does =COUNT of that range return?
grade9-ict.hint: COUNT counts only cells holding numbers.
grade9-ict.explanation: COUNT ignores empty cells, so it returns 17.

grade9-ict.question: A list is sorted by Surname and then the filter "Class = 9A" is applied. What is on screen?
options: Only the 9A pupils, in the order originally typed
Only the 9A pupils, still in surname order
grade9-ict.answer: Only the 9A pupils, still in surname order
acceptableAnswers: Only the 9A pupils, still in surname order
grade9-ict.hint: A filter hides rows; it does not reorder them.
grade9-ict.explanation: Sorting set the order and filtering hides the non-matching rows, so what remains is the 9A pupils in surname order.

grade9-ict.question: Conditional formatting is set to colour any mark below 40 in red. A mark of 40 is entered. What happens?
options: It is coloured red, because the rule includes 40
It is not coloured, because 40 is not below 40
An error message is shown in place of the mark
The cell is emptied and the mark must be typed again
grade9-ict.answer: It is not coloured, because 40 is not below 40
acceptableAnswers: It is not coloured, because 40 is not below 40
grade9-ict.hint: "Below" does not include equal to.
grade9-ict.explanation: The rule tests for marks strictly below 40, so exactly 40 does not match it.

grade9-ict.question: A chart is made from a range, and then one of the numbers in that range is changed. What happens to the chart?
options: It stays exactly as it was
grade9-ict.answer: It updates automatically
grade9-ict.hint: The chart is linked to the cells.
grade9-ict.explanation: A chart is a view of its source range, so changing the data redraws the chart at once.

grade9-ict.question: Which feature draws a line under a word?
grade9-ict.answer: Underline
grade9-ict.hint: The name says where the line goes.
grade9-ict.explanation: Underline draws a line beneath the selected text.

grade9-ict.question: Which alignment places a heading exactly in the middle of the line?
grade9-ict.answer: Centre
grade9-ict.hint: Equal space on both sides.
grade9-ict.explanation: Centre alignment puts equal space either side of the text, which is how a heading is centred.

grade9-ict.question: Which paper size is normally used for a school letter?
grade9-ict.answer: A4
grade9-ict.hint: It is the everyday office size.
grade9-ict.explanation: A4 is the standard paper size for letters and reports.

grade9-ict.question: Which keyboard shortcut is normally used to cut the selected text?
grade9-ict.answer: Ctrl + X
grade9-ict.hint: X looks like a pair of scissors closing.
grade9-ict.explanation: Ctrl + X cuts, Ctrl + C copies and Ctrl + V pastes.

grade9-ict.question: Which keyboard shortcut normally opens the print dialog?
grade9-ict.answer: Ctrl + P
grade9-ict.hint: P for print.
grade9-ict.explanation: Ctrl + P opens the print dialog.

grade9-ict.question: A picture must sit behind the text of a page as a watermark. Which setting achieves that?
options: Changing the margins so the text starts lower down
Adding a page break immediately above the picture
Increasing the font size until the text covers it
A text wrapping option that places it behind the text
grade9-ict.answer: A text wrapping option that places it behind the text
acceptableAnswers: A text wrapping option that places it behind the text
grade9-ict.hint: It is a wrapping choice.
grade9-ict.explanation: Text wrapping decides how text and picture share the space, including placing the picture behind the text.

grade9-ict.question: What does NIC stand for?
grade9-ict.answer: Network Interface Card
grade9-ict.hint: It is the card that connects a computer to a network.
grade9-ict.explanation: A NIC - Network Interface Card - is the hardware that lets a computer join a network.

grade9-ict.question: What does ISP stand for?
grade9-ict.answer: Internet Service Provider
grade9-ict.hint: It is the company you buy a connection from.
grade9-ict.explanation: An ISP - Internet Service Provider - supplies a home or business with its internet connection.

grade9-ict.question: In which topology does a break in one cable affect the fewest other computers?
grade9-ict.answer: Star
grade9-ict.hint: Each machine has its own cable to the centre.
grade9-ict.explanation: In a star only the machine on the broken cable is cut off; in a bus or a ring the whole network is disrupted.

grade9-ict.question: Which topology needs the most cable, because every device has its own link to the centre?
grade9-ict.answer: Star
grade9-ict.hint: Count the cables in each shape.
grade9-ict.explanation: A star needs one cable per device back to the central switch, which is more cable than one shared backbone.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is a reason a school might NOT want its computers networked?
options: One printer could serve several rooms
Files could then be shared between classrooms
A problem with the shared server stops everyone working
grade9-ict.answer: A problem with the shared server stops everyone working
acceptableAnswers: A problem with the shared server stops everyone working
grade9-ict.hint: Three of these are advantages.
grade9-ict.explanation: Sharing brings a single point of failure: when the shared equipment fails, everyone depending on it stops.

grade9-ict.question: What is the Subject line of an email for?
options: To attach a file to the message
To set the font used in the message
To tell the reader what the message is about
grade9-ict.answer: To tell the reader what the message is about
acceptableAnswers: To tell the reader what the message is about
grade9-ict.hint: It is the first thing the reader sees in their inbox.
grade9-ict.explanation: The subject line summarises the message so the reader can see what it concerns before opening it.

grade9-ict.question: A pupil receives an email offering a prize and asking for their bank details. What should they do?
options: Forward it to the whole class
Reply with the details quickly before the offer ends
Delete it and tell an adult; it is almost certainly a scam
Click the link to check whether it is genuine
grade9-ict.answer: Delete it and tell an adult; it is almost certainly a scam
acceptableAnswers: Delete it and tell an adult; it is almost certainly a scam
grade9-ict.hint: Genuine organisations do not ask for bank details this way.
grade9-ict.explanation: An unexpected prize that asks for bank details is a classic scam; the safe action is to delete it and tell an adult.

grade9-ict.question: What is the browser’s history?
options: A list of the pages visited recently
The list of downloaded files only
grade9-ict.answer: A list of the pages visited recently
acceptableAnswers: A list of the pages visited recently
grade9-ict.hint: It records where you have been.
grade9-ict.explanation: The history records the pages visited, so one can be found again without remembering its address.

grade9-ict.question: A search returns thousands of unrelated results. Which is the best way to narrow it?
options: Add more specific words to the search
Search for a single very common word
grade9-ict.answer: Add more specific words to the search
acceptableAnswers: Add more specific words to the search
grade9-ict.hint: Make the question narrower, not wider.
grade9-ict.explanation: More specific search terms exclude the unrelated pages; a shorter, vaguer query returns more of them.

grade9-ict.question: Which is a drawback of e-learning compared with a classroom?
options: It always costs a family more than classroom teaching does
It can only be used at one fixed time of the school day
It cannot include videos, only written text and pictures
There is less face-to-face contact with a teacher and classmates
grade9-ict.answer: There is less face-to-face contact with a teacher and classmates
acceptableAnswers: There is less face-to-face contact with a teacher and classmates
grade9-ict.hint: What does a classroom give that a screen does not?
grade9-ict.explanation: E-learning is flexible but loses the immediate personal contact and discussion a classroom provides.

grade9-ict.question: Four shapes used in flowcharts are shown below. Which shape represents a PROCESS?
grade9-ict.answer: D — Rectangle
grade9-ict.hint: The process box is the most common shape in a flowchart — it contains an action or calculation.
grade9-ict.explanation: Shape D (Rectangle) represents a process — an action, calculation or instruction (e.g. "Calculate total", "Add 1 to counter"). Shape A (Diamond) = decision; Shape B (Oval/Ellipse) = start/end (terminal); Shape C (Parallelogram) = input or output.

grade9-ict.question: A PowerPoint print layout is shown. The page displays a small slide image in the upper half and lines for speaker notes in the lower half, both on the same page. Which type of print layout is this?
grade9-ict.answer: Notes pages
grade9-ict.hint: This layout is designed to help the presenter remember what to say during each slide.
grade9-ict.explanation: Notes pages print each slide as a smaller image with the speaker's notes printed below it on the same page. Handouts print multiple slides per page without notes. Outline shows only the text content in hierarchical form. Full page slides prints one slide per full page without notes.

grade9-ict.question:
The spreadsheet below shows student marks.
Which cell shows the marks scored by Malini in ICT?
grade9-ict.answer: B5
grade9-ict.hint: Cell reference = column letter + row number. Malini is in row 5, marks are in column B.
grade9-ict.explanation: Malini's name is in cell A5 and her marks (56) are in cell B5. Cell references combine the column letter first and the row number second. Column B contains the marks; row 5 contains Malini's data.

grade9-ict.question:
A network diagram is shown below. Computers are arranged in layers: a root node at the top, connecting to two nodes in the middle, each of which connects to further nodes below.
Which network topology is shown?
grade9-ict.answer: Tree
grade9-ict.hint: The devices branch outward from a single root node, like branches of a tree.
grade9-ict.explanation: The diagram shows a tree topology — a hierarchical network where nodes branch outward from a central root node. It is a combination of star and bus topologies. Advantages: easy to expand by adding branches. Disadvantage: if the root fails, the whole network is affected. Bus = single backbone cable; Star = central hub; Mesh = every device connected to every other.

grade9-ict.question: A speech balloon shape is shown with a dashed (dotted) outline forming an oval, with a small dashed tail pointing downward. Which type of speech balloon is this?
grade9-ict.answer: Whisper balloon
grade9-ict.hint: The dashed/dotted outline suggests something soft or quiet rather than a loud statement.
grade9-ict.explanation: A whisper balloon has a dashed or dotted outline to indicate that something is being said quietly or whispered. A general speech balloon has a solid oval outline with a pointed tail. A thought balloon has a cloud-like bumpy outline with small circles forming the tail. An exclamation/emphasis callout has jagged, spiky edges.

grade9-ict.question: A picture shows a hardware device with a long, flexible neck on a base and a capsule-shaped head at the top — designed to capture sound and convert it to an electrical signal. Which hardware device is shown?
grade9-ict.answer: Microphone
grade9-ict.hint: This device is used to record voice or sound — it is an input device.
grade9-ict.explanation: The device described is a microphone — an input device that converts sound waves into electrical signals. It is used for voice recording, video calls, dictation and podcasts. A router routes network data; a printer produces hard-copy output; a compact disc is a round optical storage medium.

grade9-ict.question: Four network topology diagrams are shown below. Which diagram represents a bus topology?
grade9-ict.answer: A
grade9-ict.hint: In a bus topology, all devices share a single backbone cable — they connect off the same straight line.
grade9-ict.explanation: Diagram A is a bus topology: all devices connect to a single shared backbone cable (the horizontal line). B = star (central hub), C = ring (circular loop), D = mesh (every device connects to every other).

grade9-ict.question: In a star topology, if the central device (hub or switch) fails, what happens to the other computers on the network?
options: Only computers next to the failed hub are affected
The network continues to operate normally
All computers lose their network connection
Computers reconnect automatically through a different path
grade9-ict.answer: All computers lose their network connection
acceptableAnswers: All computers lose their network connection
grade9-ict.hint: Every device on a star network depends on the central device to communicate.
grade9-ict.explanation: In a star topology, every device communicates only through the central hub or switch. If the central device fails, all connections are lost — this is the main disadvantage of star topology. Bus topology continues with the backbone; ring topology can reroute.

grade9-ict.question: In a word-processing or presentation document, a jagged, star-burst-shaped balloon (with spiky edges pointing outward) is used to represent which type of text?
grade9-ict.answer: An exclamation or emphasis callout
grade9-ict.hint: The spiky, burst shape is designed to grab attention and signal something dramatic or important.
grade9-ict.explanation: A jagged star-burst (explosion) shape is an emphasis or exclamation callout — used in presentations and documents to highlight a dramatic statement or draw the reader's eye. A smooth oval is a thought bubble; a rounded rectangle with a pointer is a speech balloon.

grade9-ict.question: Which device is used to produce a hard copy of a document?
grade9-ict.answer: Printer
grade9-ict.explanation: A printer produces a physical (hard) copy of a document on paper. A monitor displays a soft copy on screen; a scanner converts paper to digital.

grade9-ict.question: A small rectangular device that is plugged into a USB port to store files is called a:
grade9-ict.answer: Pendrive
grade9-ict.explanation: A pendrive (also called a USB flash drive) connects via a USB port and uses flash memory to store data portably. It is a secondary storage device.

grade9-ict.question: How many bits are there in one byte?
grade9-ict.explanation: 1 byte = 8 bits. A bit is the smallest unit of data (0 or 1); 8 bits grouped together form one byte, which can represent values from 0 to 255.

grade9-ict.question: Which type of computer is a laptop?
grade9-ict.answer: Microcomputer
grade9-ict.explanation: Laptops, desktops, tablets and smartphones are all microcomputers — personal computers built around a single microprocessor. Mainframes and supercomputers are far larger and more powerful.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following operating systems is designed for use on smartphones?
grade9-ict.answer: Android
grade9-ict.explanation: Android (Google) is the most widely used mobile OS, designed for smartphones and tablets. Windows 10 and Mac OS are desktop operating systems; Linux has mobile variants but Android dominates.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is a function of an operating system?
options: Manage the computer's hardware and software resources
grade9-ict.answer: Manage the computer's hardware and software resources
acceptableAnswers: Manage the computer's hardware and software resources
grade9-ict.explanation: The OS acts as an interface between hardware and software. Its key functions include memory management, processor scheduling, file management and device control.

grade9-ict.question: Which OS function prevents unauthorised access to a computer by requiring a username and password?
grade9-ict.answer: System Security Management
grade9-ict.explanation: System Security Management controls who can access the computer and its resources. It enforces logins, permissions and access rights to protect data.

grade9-ict.question: A computer freezes completely and does not respond to any input. What should the user do first?
grade9-ict.answer: Switch off the power
grade9-ict.explanation: When a computer freezes and is unresponsive, switching it off and restarting is the standard first step. This clears the memory and allows the system to restart cleanly.

grade9-ict.question: A student accidentally deletes a file. What is the correct sequence of steps to restore it?
options: 1. Click Restore → 2. Open Recycle Bin → 3. Right-click the file
1. Right-click the file → 2. Open Recycle Bin → 3. Click Restore
1. Open Recycle Bin → 2. Right-click the file → 3. Click Restore
1. Open Recycle Bin → 2. Click Restore → 3. Right-click the file
grade9-ict.answer: 1. Open Recycle Bin → 2. Right-click the file → 3. Click Restore
acceptableAnswers: 1. Open Recycle Bin → 2. Right-click the file → 3. Click Restore
grade9-ict.explanation: To restore a deleted file: first open the Recycle Bin, then right-click the file to see options, then select Restore to return it to its original location.

grade9-ict.question: A paper jam inside a printer will:
options: Cause the monitor to go blank
Prevent the printer from working properly
grade9-ict.answer: Prevent the printer from working properly
acceptableAnswers: Prevent the printer from working properly
grade9-ict.explanation: A paper jam blocks the paper path inside the printer and stops it from printing. The jam must be carefully removed before printing can resume.

grade9-ict.question: In the date "29 March 2022", the word March appears in bold and is underlined. Which formatting combination has been applied?
grade9-ict.answer: Bold and underline
grade9-ict.explanation: Bold makes text heavier/darker; underline adds a line beneath the text. Both have been applied here. Italic would slant the letters.

grade9-ict.question: A button on the title bar shows an X inside a rectangle. What does clicking this button do?
grade9-ict.answer: Close the window
grade9-ict.explanation: The X button (Close) on the title bar closes the application window. Minimise hides it to the taskbar; Maximise/Restore changes its size.

grade9-ict.question: A page break in a word-processed document is used to:
options: Change the page orientation from portrait to landscape
Divide a page into sections with different formatting
Insert a table of contents automatically
grade9-ict.answer: Separate contents between pages
grade9-ict.explanation: A page break forces the cursor to the top of the next page, keeping sections of content on separate pages. It is different from a section break, which allows different formatting.

grade9-ict.question: Which tab in Microsoft Word is used to insert a table of contents?
grade9-ict.answer: References
grade9-ict.explanation: The References tab contains the Table of Contents tool. Word generates the TOC automatically from headings already formatted in the document.

grade9-ict.question: In a spreadsheet, column B holds cost prices and column C holds selling prices. Which formula calculates the profit per item in cell D3?
grade9-ict.explanation: Profit = Selling price − Cost price, so the formula is =C3−B3. Division or MIN would not give profit; addition would give the sum, not the difference.

grade9-ict.question: Profit per item values are in cells D3 to D7. Which formula in cell D8 calculates the total profit?
grade9-ict.answer: =SUM(D3:D7)
grade9-ict.explanation: SUM adds all values in the specified range. =SUM(D3:D7) adds the five profit values in D3 through D7 to give the total profit.

grade9-ict.question: Column E contains the number of items in stock. Items with fewer than 50 need reordering. Which formula in cell F3 shows "YES" if reorder is needed and "NO" if not?
grade9-ict.explanation: The IF function checks a condition: if E3 is less than 50 the result is "YES" (reorder needed); otherwise "NO". The comparison operator < means "less than".

grade9-ict.question: Column F shows "YES" or "NO" for whether each item needs reordering. Two items show "YES". What does =COUNTIF(F3:F7,"YES") return?
grade9-ict.explanation: COUNTIF counts cells in the range F3:F7 that contain "YES". With two items marked YES, the result is 2.

grade9-ict.question: A primary key in a database table is a field that:
options: Links two tables together (a foreign key)
Contains the most recently entered data
Stores the largest value in the table
Uniquely identifies each record in the table
grade9-ict.answer: Uniquely identifies each record in the table
acceptableAnswers: Uniquely identifies each record in the table
grade9-ict.explanation: A primary key is a field (or combination of fields) whose value is unique for every row in the table. It is used to identify and locate individual records without ambiguity.

grade9-ict.question: In a database table, each row represents a:
grade9-ict.answer: Record
grade9-ict.explanation: A row in a database table is a record — all the information about one entity (e.g. one flight, one student). A column is a field (one attribute of that entity).

grade9-ict.question: The FLIGHTS table has columns: FLIGHT_ID, FLIGHT_NAME, DEPARTURE, LOCATION, DESTINATION. How many fields does the table have?
grade9-ict.explanation: Each column in a database table is a field. The FLIGHTS table has five columns: FLIGHT_ID, FLIGHT_NAME, DEPARTURE, LOCATION and DESTINATION.

grade9-ict.question: A query selects all records from the FLIGHTS table where DEPARTURE = 23:00, sorted by FLIGHT_ID ascending. The table has flights SP-205 (23:00) and EM-234 (23:00). What is the output?
grade9-ict.explanation: Sorted ascending by FLIGHT_ID: EM-234 comes before SP-205 alphabetically (E before S). Both match DEPARTURE = 23:00 so both appear, in that order.

grade9-ict.question: A network topology in which all computers are connected to a central device (such as a switch or hub) is called a:
grade9-ict.answer: Star topology
grade9-ict.explanation: In a star topology, each device connects individually to a central hub or switch. If one connection fails, only that device is affected — the rest of the network continues.

grade9-ict.question: An Intranet is best described as:
options: A private network for use within an organisation
The global public network connecting billions of computers
A network that uses satellite links
A network that connects computers across a city
grade9-ict.answer: A private network for use within an organisation
acceptableAnswers: A private network for use within an organisation
grade9-ict.explanation: An intranet uses the same technology as the Internet but is restricted to authorised users within a company or institution. It is not accessible to the general public.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following best describes the Internet?
options: A private company network accessible only to staff
A single computer that stores all web pages
Software used to browse web pages
A global network that connects millions of computers worldwide
grade9-ict.answer: A global network that connects millions of computers worldwide
acceptableAnswers: A global network that connects millions of computers worldwide
grade9-ict.explanation: The Internet is a worldwide system of interconnected networks. Web browsers are software used to access its resources; websites live on servers connected to this network.

grade9-ict.question: A computer virus is best described as:
options: A software program that can damage or disrupt a computer
A hardware fault that slows down the processor
grade9-ict.answer: A software program that can damage or disrupt a computer
acceptableAnswers: A software program that can damage or disrupt a computer
grade9-ict.explanation: A virus is malicious software (malware) that can copy itself, corrupt files, slow the system, or give unauthorised access. It is combated with antivirus software.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is a search engine?
grade9-ict.answer: Google
grade9-ict.explanation: Google is a search engine — it indexes billions of web pages and returns results matching a user's query. Skype and WhatsApp are communication apps; Gmail is an email service.

grade9-ict.question: An online forum is a website used for:
grade9-ict.answer: Online discussions and debates
grade9-ict.explanation: Online forums are platforms where users post messages, reply to each other and discuss topics. Examples include Reddit and specialised community boards.

grade9-ict.question: A mailing list is a collection of:
options: Spam messages blocked by the mail filter
Folders used to organise received emails
Names, email addresses and contact details used to send group messages
Deleted emails stored in the trash folder
grade9-ict.answer: Names, email addresses and contact details used to send group messages
acceptableAnswers: Names, email addresses and contact details used to send group messages
grade9-ict.explanation: A mailing list stores contact information so that one message can be sent to many recipients at once — used for newsletters, announcements and group communications.

grade9-ict.question: In programming, a loop is a control structure in which:
options: Statements are executed only if a condition is met
Statements are executed in the order they appear
grade9-ict.answer: Statements are executed multiple times
grade9-ict.explanation: A loop (repetition) repeats a block of statements a set number of times or until a condition changes. Examples include FOR loops and WHILE loops.

grade9-ict.question: In programming, a selection structure means:
options: Statements are executed only if a certain condition is met
Statements are always run from top to bottom
Statements that are never run in any program
Statements are repeated a fixed number of times
grade9-ict.answer: Statements are executed only if a certain condition is met
acceptableAnswers: Statements are executed only if a certain condition is met
grade9-ict.explanation: Selection (IF-THEN-ELSE) checks a condition and executes different code depending on whether the condition is true or false.

grade9-ict.question: A flowchart inputs values P and Q, then asks: "Is P < Q?" If YES it outputs "P is small"; if NO it outputs "P is large". If P = 3 and Q = 5, what is the output?
grade9-ict.answer: "P is small"
grade9-ict.explanation: Is 3 < 5? Yes. The YES branch outputs "P is small". The NO branch would output "P is large" only if P ≥ Q.

grade9-ict.question: Which control structure describes executing instructions in the order in which they appear, one after another?
grade9-ict.answer: Sequence
grade9-ict.explanation: Sequence is the simplest control structure: instructions are carried out one at a time, from top to bottom, in the order they are written.

grade9-ict.question: A handout in a presentation is:
options: A video clip embedded in the presentation
A digital animation added to each slide
A printed copy of the presentation slides
grade9-ict.answer: A printed copy of the presentation slides
acceptableAnswers: A printed copy of the presentation slides
grade9-ict.explanation: Handouts are paper copies of the presentation given to the audience. They can show one, two, three, four, six or nine slides per page.

grade9-ict.question: Applying a design template to a presentation will:
options: Change the colours, fonts and background design of all slides at once
Delete all text from the slides
Add new slides to the presentation automatically
Convert the presentation to a video file
grade9-ict.answer: Change the colours, fonts and background design of all slides at once
acceptableAnswers: Change the colours, fonts and background design of all slides at once
grade9-ict.explanation: A design template (theme) applies a consistent colour scheme, font set and background to every slide, giving the presentation a professional and uniform appearance.
