grade9-ict.question: Is it ethical to use someone else's password to log into a computer system?
options: Yes — if you need access urgently
No — but only if the computer belongs to a company
Yes — as long as you do not change any files
No — it violates privacy and is a form of unauthorised access
grade9-ict.answer: No — it violates privacy and is a form of unauthorised access
acceptableAnswers: No — it violates privacy and is a form of unauthorised access
grade9-ict.explanation: Using another person's password without permission is unethical and often illegal. It breaches privacy and may constitute unauthorised access under data protection laws.

grade9-ict.question: Backup means to:
options: Keep a copy of an original document in case the original is lost or damaged
Delete an original document after sending it
Modify a document and save it under a new name
grade9-ict.answer: Keep a copy of an original document in case the original is lost or damaged
acceptableAnswers: Keep a copy of an original document in case the original is lost or damaged
grade9-ict.explanation: A backup is a duplicate of data stored separately. If the original is lost, corrupted or accidentally deleted, the backup can be used to restore it.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is an example of a computer crime?
options: Saving a file to a USB drive
grade9-ict.answer: Hacking into a computer system
grade9-ict.explanation: Hacking (gaining unauthorised access to a system) is a criminal offence. Other computer crimes include spreading viruses, phishing and software piracy.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is a correct rule for a computer laboratory?
options: No food or drinks are allowed near the computers
Multiple users can share one login account
Mobile phones should be left on the desk during lessons
Students may play music through the lab speakers
grade9-ict.answer: No food or drinks are allowed near the computers
acceptableAnswers: No food or drinks are allowed near the computers
grade9-ict.explanation: Food and drinks can spill onto keyboards and components, causing damage or electric shock. Keeping them out of the lab protects the equipment and users.

grade9-ict.question: Staring at a computer screen for long hours without breaks can lead to:
grade9-ict.answer: Eye strain
grade9-ict.explanation: Prolonged screen use causes eye fatigue, dryness and blurred vision — collectively called eye strain. RSI affects wrists/hands from repetitive movements; back pain comes from poor posture.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is an input device?
grade9-ict.answer: Keyboard
grade9-ict.explanation: A keyboard is an input device. Data is typed into the computer through it. Monitors, printers, and speakers are all output devices.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is an output device?
grade9-ict.answer: Monitor
grade9-ict.explanation: A monitor displays information from the computer to the user, making it an output device. A mouse, webcam, and barcode reader are all input devices.

grade9-ict.question: What is the purpose of the motherboard in a computer?
options: It displays the visual output of the computer
It is the main circuit board that all other components connect to
It stores all programs and files when the computer is switched off
It carries out all arithmetic and logical operations
grade9-ict.answer: It is the main circuit board that all other components connect to
acceptableAnswers: It is the main circuit board that all other components connect to
grade9-ict.explanation: The motherboard is the main circuit board of a computer. Components such as the CPU, RAM, and expansion cards all connect to it, allowing them to communicate.

grade9-ict.question: Which input device captures live video and transmits it to the computer?
grade9-ict.answer: Webcam
grade9-ict.explanation: A webcam is an input device that captures live images and video and sends them to the computer in real time.

grade9-ict.question: What does CPU stand for?
grade9-ict.answer: Central Processing Unit
grade9-ict.explanation: CPU stands for Central Processing Unit. It is often called the brain of the computer because it processes all instructions.

grade9-ict.question: What is the main purpose of RAM in a computer?
options: To convert data into images on the screen
To carry out all arithmetic and comparison operations
To store data and programs temporarily while the computer is in use
To store data permanently even when the computer is switched off
grade9-ict.answer: To store data and programs temporarily while the computer is in use
acceptableAnswers: To store data and programs temporarily while the computer is in use
grade9-ict.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) holds data and programs that the CPU is currently using. Its contents are lost as soon as the computer is switched off.

grade9-ict.question: Which component enables a computer to use a microphone and speakers?
grade9-ict.answer: Sound card
grade9-ict.explanation: A sound card processes audio signals, allowing the computer to accept input from a microphone and produce output through speakers or headphones.

grade9-ict.question: How many bits make up one byte?
grade9-ict.explanation: One byte consists of 8 bits. A bit is the smallest unit of data in a computer, represented as either 0 or 1.

grade9-ict.question: How many bytes make up one kilobyte?
grade9-ict.explanation: One kilobyte equals 1 024 bytes. Computers work in powers of 2, and 2¹⁰ = 1 024.

grade9-ict.question: A file is 3 MB in size. How many kilobytes is this?
grade9-ict.explanation: One megabyte equals 1 024 kilobytes. Therefore 3 MB = 3 × 1 024 = 3 072 KB.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following correctly describes a Solid State Drive (SSD)?
options: It loses its contents as soon as the computer is switched off
It is the least expensive form of permanent storage
It uses spinning magnetic platters to read and write data
It has no moving parts and is faster than a traditional hard disk drive
grade9-ict.answer: It has no moving parts and is faster than a traditional hard disk drive
acceptableAnswers: It has no moving parts and is faster than a traditional hard disk drive
grade9-ict.explanation: An SSD stores data on flash memory chips. Because it has no moving parts, it is faster and less fragile than a Hard Disk Drive (HDD).

grade9-ict.question: Which storage device uses spinning magnetic platters and a read/write head?
grade9-ict.answer: Hard Disk Drive (HDD)
grade9-ict.explanation: A Hard Disk Drive (HDD) stores data on spinning magnetic platters. It is generally slower than an SSD but offers more storage capacity for the same cost.

grade9-ict.question: A teacher wants to display her slides on a large screen for the whole class. Which output device should she use?
grade9-ict.answer: Projector
grade9-ict.explanation: A projector is an output device that displays an enlarged image on a screen or wall, making it suitable for classroom presentations.

grade9-ict.question: Which input device is used at supermarket checkouts to read product codes?
grade9-ict.answer: Barcode reader
grade9-ict.explanation: A barcode reader is an input device that uses light to scan the pattern of lines in a barcode and sends the product information to the computer.

grade9-ict.question: What is the difference between RAM and ROM?
options: RAM is temporary and loses its data when power is off; ROM is permanent and retains its data when power is off
RAM and ROM are both permanent but ROM is faster
RAM stores the BIOS; ROM stores user files and programs
ROM is temporary and loses its data when power is off; RAM is permanent and retains data when power is off
grade9-ict.answer: RAM is temporary and loses its data when power is off; ROM is permanent and retains its data when power is off
acceptableAnswers: RAM is temporary and loses its data when power is off; ROM is permanent and retains its data when power is off
grade9-ict.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile — its contents disappear when the computer is switched off. ROM (Read Only Memory) is non-volatile and permanently stores instructions such as the BIOS that the computer needs to start up.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is an example of system software?
grade9-ict.answer: Operating system
grade9-ict.explanation: An operating system is system software that manages the computer's hardware and provides services for application programs. Word processors, spreadsheets, and web browsers are application software.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of an operating system?
grade9-ict.answer: Creating spreadsheets and formatting data
grade9-ict.explanation: Creating spreadsheets is done by application software such as Microsoft Excel. The operating system manages hardware resources, files, memory, and provides the interface between the user and the computer.

grade9-ict.question: Which type of user interface uses icons, windows, and a pointing device?
grade9-ict.answer: Graphical User Interface (GUI)
grade9-ict.explanation: A Graphical User Interface (GUI) lets users interact with the computer through visual elements such as icons, windows, and menus, typically controlled with a mouse.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is an example of application software?
grade9-ict.answer: Microsoft Word
grade9-ict.explanation: Microsoft Word is application software used for word processing. Windows 10, Linux, and macOS are all operating systems, which are system software.

grade9-ict.question: A school wants software that can be freely used and distributed, but whose source code cannot be modified. Which type best fits?
grade9-ict.answer: Freeware
grade9-ict.explanation: Freeware is software available at no charge that can be freely used and distributed, but the source code is not provided for modification. Open source software allows the source code to be viewed and changed.

grade9-ict.question: Which keyboard shortcut applies bold formatting to selected text?
grade9-ict.answer: Ctrl+B
grade9-ict.explanation: Ctrl+B toggles bold formatting on the selected text. Ctrl+I applies italic, Ctrl+U applies underline, and Ctrl+S saves the document.

grade9-ict.question: A student presses a key and the cursor moves to a new line, starting a new paragraph. Which key did she press?
grade9-ict.answer: Enter
grade9-ict.explanation: Pressing Enter begins a new paragraph. The Tab key indents text or moves between table cells, but it does not start a new paragraph.

grade9-ict.question: Which keyboard shortcut opens the Find and Replace dialog box?
grade9-ict.answer: Ctrl+H
grade9-ict.explanation: Ctrl+H opens the Find and Replace dialog box, which lets the user find specific text and replace it with different text throughout the document.

grade9-ict.question: Which function key starts the spelling and grammar check in most word processors?
grade9-ict.answer: F7
grade9-ict.explanation: The F7 key opens the spelling and grammar check tool in most word processing applications, including Microsoft Word.

grade9-ict.question: A student wants each line of her paragraph to be neatly aligned at both the left and right margins. Which alignment should she choose?
grade9-ict.answer: Justified
grade9-ict.explanation: Justified alignment stretches each line so that text touches both the left and right margins, creating a neat block shape on both sides of the page.

grade9-ict.question: What is the purpose of mail merge?
options: To combine a template document with a data source to produce personalised copies
To send emails directly from the word processor
To combine two open documents into a single file
To apply a master style to all paragraphs at once
grade9-ict.answer: To combine a template document with a data source to produce personalised copies
acceptableAnswers: To combine a template document with a data source to produce personalised copies
grade9-ict.explanation: Mail merge joins a main document (such as a letter template containing merge fields) with a data source (such as a list of names and addresses) to automatically produce personalised copies.

grade9-ict.question: Where does a header appear in a word processed document?
options: At the top of every page
In the left margin of each page
At the bottom of every page
grade9-ict.answer: At the top of every page
acceptableAnswers: At the top of every page
grade9-ict.explanation: A header is text or information (such as a title or page number) that is repeated at the top of every page. A footer appears at the bottom of every page.

grade9-ict.question: In a word processing table, which key moves the cursor to the next cell?
grade9-ict.answer: Tab
grade9-ict.explanation: Pressing Tab moves the cursor to the next cell in a table. Pressing Enter within a cell creates a new line inside the same cell.

grade9-ict.question: A student has formatted a report with specific headings, fonts, and spacing. She wants every new document she creates to use those same settings automatically. What should she save?
grade9-ict.answer: A document template
grade9-ict.explanation: A template is a pre-formatted document used as the starting point for new documents. All formatting settings are stored in it and applied automatically each time it is used.

grade9-ict.question: During a mail merge a student notices that the same name appears on every letter. What is the most likely cause?
options: The page margins prevent the field from updating
The merge fields are not correctly linked to the data source columns
The spell checker has overwritten the field names
The document has been saved in the wrong file format
grade9-ict.answer: The merge fields are not correctly linked to the data source columns
acceptableAnswers: The merge fields are not correctly linked to the data source columns
grade9-ict.explanation: In a mail merge, each merge field in the main document must be linked to the correct column in the data source. An incorrect link causes the same value to repeat instead of changing for each record.

grade9-ict.question: Which character must appear at the start of every spreadsheet formula?
grade9-ict.explanation: Every formula in a spreadsheet must begin with an equals sign (=). This tells the application that what follows is a calculation to be performed.

grade9-ict.question: Which spreadsheet function returns the smallest value in a range of cells?
grade9-ict.answer: MIN
grade9-ict.explanation: The MIN function returns the lowest value in the specified range of cells.

grade9-ict.question: A student wants to count how many cells in the range B2:B20 contain numbers. Which function should she use?
grade9-ict.answer: COUNT
grade9-ict.explanation: The COUNT function counts the number of cells in a range that contain numerical values. COUNTA counts cells that are not empty, regardless of data type.

grade9-ict.question: In a spreadsheet, what does the cell reference B3 represent?
options: The third cell in the workbook
grade9-ict.answer: Column B, Row 3
grade9-ict.explanation: In spreadsheet notation, letters identify columns and numbers identify rows. B3 refers to the cell at column B, row 3.

grade9-ict.question: What is the fill handle in a spreadsheet used for?
options: Inserting a new row or column into the sheet
Applying a colour fill to a range of cells
Copying a cell's content or formula to adjacent cells by dragging
grade9-ict.answer: Copying a cell's content or formula to adjacent cells by dragging
acceptableAnswers: Copying a cell's content or formula to adjacent cells by dragging
grade9-ict.explanation: The fill handle is the small square at the bottom-right corner of a selected cell. Dragging it copies the cell's content or formula into the cells in the direction you drag.

grade9-ict.question: A student enters =B2*C2 in cell D2 and drags the fill handle down to D3. What formula appears in D3?
grade9-ict.explanation: Relative cell references adjust automatically when a formula is copied. Moving one row down increases all row numbers by one, so =B2*C2 becomes =B3*C3 in D3.

grade9-ict.question: Which type of chart is most suitable for showing how a student's test scores have changed over six months?
grade9-ict.answer: Line chart
grade9-ict.explanation: A line chart is designed to show trends over time. Points are plotted for each time period and connected by a line, making it easy to see rises and falls.

grade9-ict.question: A student enters =SUM($A$1:$A$5) in cell B1 and copies it to cell C1. What formula appears in C1?
grade9-ict.explanation: The dollar signs create absolute references that do not change when a formula is copied. C1 will still contain =SUM($A$1:$A$5), pointing to exactly the same cells.

grade9-ict.question: A teacher has a spreadsheet of student marks and wants to arrange them from highest to lowest. Which option should she choose?
grade9-ict.answer: Sort descending
grade9-ict.explanation: Sort descending arranges numerical data from the largest value to the smallest (highest to lowest). Sort ascending would arrange from lowest to highest.

grade9-ict.question: A student needs to look up a student ID in the first column of a table and return the mark from the fourth column. Which function should she use?
grade9-ict.answer: VLOOKUP
grade9-ict.explanation: VLOOKUP (Vertical Lookup) searches the first column of a table range for a value and returns data from a specified column in the same row. It is ideal for looking up values in a vertical list.

grade9-ict.question: What is a storyboard used for when planning a multimedia video?
options: To plan the sequence of scenes using sketches and notes
To record the audio narration for the video
To apply transitions between video clips
To compress the finished video for uploading
grade9-ict.answer: To plan the sequence of scenes using sketches and notes
acceptableAnswers: To plan the sequence of scenes using sketches and notes
grade9-ict.explanation: A storyboard is a planning tool that shows the intended sequence of scenes, together with images, descriptions, and instructions, before production begins.

grade9-ict.question: What is a slide master in a presentation application?
options: A slide that contains the presenter's notes
The title slide at the start of a presentation
The slide with the most animations applied to it
A template that controls the default formatting of all slides
grade9-ict.answer: A template that controls the default formatting of all slides
acceptableAnswers: A template that controls the default formatting of all slides
grade9-ict.explanation: The slide master controls the default fonts, colours, backgrounds, and layouts for every slide. Changes made to the slide master are applied to all slides automatically.

grade9-ict.question: In a presentation, what is an animation?
options: The speed setting for the whole slideshow
The visual effect that plays when moving from one slide to the next
A video clip inserted into a slide
A movement or appearance effect applied to an object on a slide
grade9-ict.answer: A movement or appearance effect applied to an object on a slide
acceptableAnswers: A movement or appearance effect applied to an object on a slide
grade9-ict.explanation: An animation controls how a specific object (such as a text box or image) enters, moves, or exits on a slide during the presentation.

grade9-ict.question: What is a slide transition in a presentation?
options: A movement effect applied to text or images on a single slide
The timer that controls how long each slide is shown
The visual effect that plays when moving from one slide to the next
The background colour that changes between slides
grade9-ict.answer: The visual effect that plays when moving from one slide to the next
acceptableAnswers: The visual effect that plays when moving from one slide to the next
grade9-ict.explanation: A transition is the animated effect (such as a fade, wipe, or dissolve) that plays as the presentation moves from one slide to the next.

grade9-ict.question: A student wants to add notes that she can read while presenting, but that the audience cannot see. Which feature should she use?
grade9-ict.answer: Speaker notes
grade9-ict.explanation: Speaker notes are typed in the notes panel below each slide. In Presenter View they are visible only to the presenter, not to the audience viewing the main screen.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following best describes a multimedia presentation?
options: One that consists of images on a white background
One that uses only bullet points and text
One that is delivered through a projector
One that combines text, images, audio, video, and animations
grade9-ict.answer: One that combines text, images, audio, video, and animations
acceptableAnswers: One that combines text, images, audio, video, and animations
grade9-ict.explanation: Multimedia refers to the combination of different media types — text, still images, audio, video, and animations — in a single product.

grade9-ict.question: A student applies an entrance animation and then an exit animation to the same text box. In which order will the animations play?
options: The animations play in reverse alphabetical order
Both animations play at the same time
The entrance animation plays first, then the exit animation
The exit animation plays first, then the entrance animation
grade9-ict.answer: The entrance animation plays first, then the exit animation
acceptableAnswers: The entrance animation plays first, then the exit animation
grade9-ict.explanation: Entrance animations control how an object appears on the slide; exit animations control how it disappears. By default, entrance effects play before exit effects for the same object.

grade9-ict.question: A student embeds a video in her presentation and saves the file. On another computer the video does not play. What is the most likely reason?
options: The video file format is not supported anywhere
The slide transition setting has disabled the video
The video was linked rather than embedded, so the file is missing on the new computer
The presentation software version is different
grade9-ict.answer: The video was linked rather than embedded, so the file is missing on the new computer
acceptableAnswers: The video was linked rather than embedded, so the file is missing on the new computer
grade9-ict.explanation: A linked video is stored separately; the presentation holds only a path to it. When the file is moved to another computer without the video, the link breaks. Embedding stores the video inside the presentation file.

grade9-ict.question: In a database, what is a record?
options: One complete set of data about a single item
One category of data stored across all items
A unique identifier for each entry
grade9-ict.answer: One complete set of data about a single item
acceptableAnswers: One complete set of data about a single item
grade9-ict.explanation: A record is one row in a database table. It holds all the data about one particular item or person, such as all the details for a single student.

grade9-ict.question: What is a field in a database table?
options: A unique identifier that links two tables
One category of data stored for every record in the table
A condition used to filter which records are shown
One complete set of data about a single item
grade9-ict.answer: One category of data stored for every record in the table
acceptableAnswers: One category of data stored for every record in the table
grade9-ict.explanation: A field is one column in a database table. It stores one category of data — such as Name, Date of Birth, or Grade — for every record.

grade9-ict.question: What is a primary key in a database?
options: The field used to sort records in alphabetical order
The first record entered into a table
A field shared between two related tables
A field that uniquely identifies each record in a table
grade9-ict.answer: A field that uniquely identifies each record in a table
acceptableAnswers: A field that uniquely identifies each record in a table
grade9-ict.explanation: A primary key is a field whose value is unique for every record. No two records can share the same primary key value, so each record can always be found individually.

grade9-ict.question: A student chooses "Book Title" as the primary key for a library database. Why might this cause a problem?
options: Two different books could share the same title, so records would not be unique
Titles cannot be searched using a query
Book titles are too long to store in a database field
Titles may change when a new edition is published, making queries fail
grade9-ict.answer: Two different books could share the same title, so records would not be unique
acceptableAnswers: Two different books could share the same title, so records would not be unique
grade9-ict.explanation: A primary key must be unique for every record. If two books have the same title, the uniqueness rule is broken. A unique Book ID number would be a safer choice.

grade9-ict.question: What is the purpose of a query in a database?
options: To enter new records through a screen form
To search and display records that match specific criteria
To print database records in a formatted layout
To link the columns of two tables together
grade9-ict.answer: To search and display records that match specific criteria
acceptableAnswers: To search and display records that match specific criteria
grade9-ict.explanation: A query retrieves specific records from a database based on conditions set by the user. For example, a query might find all students who scored above 70%.

grade9-ict.question: What is the purpose of a form in a database?
options: To search for records that match a condition
To print a formatted summary of the database
To create a link between two database tables
To provide a user-friendly screen for entering and viewing records
grade9-ict.answer: To provide a user-friendly screen for entering and viewing records
acceptableAnswers: To provide a user-friendly screen for entering and viewing records
grade9-ict.explanation: A form provides a structured, easy-to-use interface for entering, viewing, and editing records, making the process more straightforward than typing directly into the table.

grade9-ict.question: A school wants to print a neat, formatted summary of all exam results from a database. Which database object should they use?
grade9-ict.answer: Report
grade9-ict.explanation: A report is a database object designed to display and print data in a formatted layout, often with headings, grouped data, and totals.

grade9-ict.question: Why does each table in a relational database need a primary key?
options: So that two tables can share the same column name
So that the table can be sorted in ascending order automatically
So that the database file size stays small
So that every record can be uniquely identified and retrieved
grade9-ict.answer: So that every record can be uniquely identified and retrieved
acceptableAnswers: So that every record can be uniquely identified and retrieved
grade9-ict.explanation: A primary key guarantees that no two records are identical in their key value. This makes it possible to find, update, or delete exactly the right record without confusion.

grade9-ict.question: A query is set with the criterion: Age > 14 AND Grade = "Form 3". What will it return?
options: Only Form 3 students who are also older than 14
All students older than 14, regardless of grade
All students who are older than 14 or in Form 3
All Form 3 students, regardless of age
grade9-ict.answer: Only Form 3 students who are also older than 14
acceptableAnswers: Only Form 3 students who are also older than 14
grade9-ict.explanation: When conditions are joined with AND, both must be true for a record to be included. The query returns records where the student is simultaneously older than 14 and in Form 3.

grade9-ict.question: A Students table uses StudentID as its primary key. An Enrolments table holds StudentID as a foreign key. What does this enforce?
options: Each student can be enrolled in no more than one subject
Only StudentID values that exist in Students can appear in Enrolments
Every student must have at least one enrolment record
The Enrolments table updates automatically when a student is added
grade9-ict.answer: Only StudentID values that exist in Students can appear in Enrolments
acceptableAnswers: Only StudentID values that exist in Students can appear in Enrolments
grade9-ict.explanation: Referential integrity ensures that a foreign key value must match an existing primary key in the parent table. This prevents enrolment records from being created for students who do not exist.

grade9-ict.question: In a bus topology, how are the computers connected?
options: Each computer connects to every other computer
Computers are joined in a closed circle
All computers share a single central cable
All computers connect to a central hub or switch
grade9-ict.answer: All computers share a single central cable
acceptableAnswers: All computers share a single central cable
grade9-ict.explanation: In a bus topology, all devices are connected to one main cable called the backbone. Data travels along this shared cable to reach its destination.

grade9-ict.question: Which network topology connects every computer to a central hub or switch?
grade9-ict.answer: Star topology
grade9-ict.explanation: In a star topology, each device has its own cable connecting it to a central hub or switch. If one device fails, the rest of the network continues to work.

grade9-ict.question: What is one disadvantage of a bus topology?
options: It requires an expensive central switch to operate
Computers cannot share files with each other
If the main cable fails, the entire network stops working
New computers are difficult to add to the network
grade9-ict.answer: If the main cable fails, the entire network stops working
acceptableAnswers: If the main cable fails, the entire network stops working
grade9-ict.explanation: In a bus topology all devices share the one backbone cable. A break anywhere in that cable stops all communication on the network.

grade9-ict.question: A company has offices in three different countries and needs one network linking all of them. Which network type is most appropriate?
grade9-ict.answer: Wide Area Network (WAN)
grade9-ict.explanation: A WAN spans large geographical distances such as different cities or countries. A LAN covers only a small area such as a single building and is not suitable for connecting offices across different countries.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is a web browser?
grade9-ict.answer: Google Chrome
grade9-ict.explanation: Google Chrome is a web browser — software used to access and display web pages. Google Search is a search engine, Gmail is an email service, and Google Drive is cloud storage.

grade9-ict.question: What is the difference between a web browser and a search engine?
options: A browser finds web pages; a search engine displays them
A search engine requires an internet connection; a browser does not
A browser displays web pages; a search engine finds web pages
They are different names for exactly the same tool
grade9-ict.answer: A browser displays web pages; a search engine finds web pages
acceptableAnswers: A browser displays web pages; a search engine finds web pages
grade9-ict.explanation: A web browser (such as Chrome or Firefox) is software that renders and displays websites. A search engine (such as Google or Bing) is a service used to locate web pages by keyword.

grade9-ict.question: What is an email attachment?
options: An email saved in the Drafts folder
A copy of an email forwarded to another person
A file sent along with an email message
A reply sent back to the original sender
grade9-ict.answer: A file sent along with an email message
acceptableAnswers: A file sent along with an email message
grade9-ict.explanation: An email attachment is a file — such as a document, image, or spreadsheet — that is added to and sent together with an email message.

grade9-ict.question: What is the difference between HTTP and HTTPS?
options: HTTPS encrypts the data transmitted, making it more secure than HTTP
HTTP is for mobile devices while HTTPS is for desktop computers
HTTP is faster because it uses fewer packets than HTTPS
HTTPS is used for email while HTTP is used for web pages
grade9-ict.answer: HTTPS encrypts the data transmitted, making it more secure than HTTP
acceptableAnswers: HTTPS encrypts the data transmitted, making it more secure than HTTP
grade9-ict.explanation: Both are protocols for transferring web pages. HTTPS (HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure) encrypts data using TLS, protecting it from being read if intercepted. HTTP sends data without encryption.

grade9-ict.question: A student receives an email from her bank asking her to click a link and confirm her password immediately. What type of cybercrime is this most likely to be?
grade9-ict.answer: Phishing
grade9-ict.explanation: Phishing uses fake emails or websites that impersonate trusted organisations to trick people into revealing personal data such as passwords or bank details.

grade9-ict.question: A home user pays a monthly fee to a company for access to the internet. What is that company called?
grade9-ict.answer: Internet Service Provider (ISP)
grade9-ict.explanation: An Internet Service Provider (ISP) is a company that sells internet access to homes and businesses, usually for a recurring fee.

grade9-ict.question: What is computer ethics?
options: A code of conduct that applies only to professional programmers
The legal protection given to software creators
The study of how to prevent computer crimes
A set of moral principles that guides the responsible use of computers
grade9-ict.answer: A set of moral principles that guides the responsible use of computers
acceptableAnswers: A set of moral principles that guides the responsible use of computers
grade9-ict.explanation: Computer ethics refers to the moral principles and guidelines that govern how computers and technology should be used responsibly in everyday life.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is an example of a cybercrime?
options: Downloading a free app from an official store
Using a search engine to look up information
Posting a photo of yourself on a social media profile
Hacking into someone's computer without permission
grade9-ict.answer: Hacking into someone's computer without permission
acceptableAnswers: Hacking into someone's computer without permission
grade9-ict.explanation: Hacking — gaining unauthorised access to a computer or network — is a criminal offence. The other options are all legal activities.

grade9-ict.question: What is software piracy?
options: Illegally copying or distributing copyrighted software
Sending large volumes of unwanted email
Stealing personal data from a website
grade9-ict.answer: Illegally copying or distributing copyrighted software
acceptableAnswers: Illegally copying or distributing copyrighted software
grade9-ict.explanation: Software piracy is the illegal copying, distribution, or use of software without permission from the copyright holder. It is a violation of copyright law.

grade9-ict.question: A student shares another student's personal contact details online without permission. Which principle has been violated?
grade9-ict.answer: Information privacy
grade9-ict.explanation: Information privacy is the right of individuals to keep their personal data confidential. Sharing someone's details without consent violates that right.

grade9-ict.question: A person creates a fake online profile using someone else's identity in order to deceive others for financial gain. Which cybercrime is this?
grade9-ict.answer: Identity fraud
grade9-ict.explanation: Identity fraud involves pretending to be another person by using their name, photo, or personal details, often to gain money or deceive others.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following shows responsible use of a computer?
options: Sharing your password with a close friend for convenience
Downloading software only from trusted, official sources
Visiting websites that the school network has blocked
Copying a classmate's work and submitting it as your own
grade9-ict.answer: Downloading software only from trusted, official sources
acceptableAnswers: Downloading software only from trusted, official sources
grade9-ict.explanation: Using only trusted, official sources reduces the risk of installing malware or pirated software. Sharing passwords, copying work, and bypassing restrictions are all unethical behaviours.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following best describes cyberbullying?
options: Using technology to repeatedly harass or intimidate another person
Copying software without the copyright holder's permission
Sending advertising messages to thousands of email addresses
Gaining unauthorised access to a school's database
grade9-ict.answer: Using technology to repeatedly harass or intimidate another person
acceptableAnswers: Using technology to repeatedly harass or intimidate another person
grade9-ict.explanation: Cyberbullying is the use of digital technology — social media, messaging, email — to bully, threaten, or humiliate someone repeatedly.

grade9-ict.question: What is ergonomics?
options: The study of designing a safe and comfortable working environment
A method of encrypting data to protect it from unauthorised access
The study of computer networks and how they operate
The legal framework that governs the use of technology
grade9-ict.answer: The study of designing a safe and comfortable working environment
acceptableAnswers: The study of designing a safe and comfortable working environment
grade9-ict.explanation: Ergonomics is the science of arranging a workstation — screen height, chair position, lighting, and so on — to suit the physical needs of the user and reduce the risk of injury.

grade9-ict.question: A student types for several hours without a break and develops pain in her wrists and hands. Which health problem is most likely?
grade9-ict.answer: Repetitive strain injury (RSI)
grade9-ict.explanation: Repetitive strain injury (RSI) is caused by repeating the same movements — such as typing or using a mouse — for long periods. It causes pain and stiffness in the wrists, hands, and arms.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is a correct safety rule for a computer laboratory?
options: Keep drinks and food away from all computer equipment
Leave cables on the floor so they are easy to unplug when needed
Turn computers off by unplugging them from the wall socket
Place monitors as close to the face as possible for a clear view
grade9-ict.answer: Keep drinks and food away from all computer equipment
acceptableAnswers: Keep drinks and food away from all computer equipment
grade9-ict.explanation: Liquids and food can cause short circuits, electric shock, or permanent damage to equipment. Keeping them away from computers is a basic safety rule in any computer laboratory.

grade9-ict.question: A student in a rural village has no internet access, while students in the city use online resources daily for schoolwork. Which concept does this illustrate?
grade9-ict.answer: The digital divide
grade9-ict.explanation: The digital divide is the gap between people who have ready access to computers and the internet and those who do not, often because of location, income, or infrastructure.

grade9-ict.question: A user works at a computer for eight hours a day. Which combination of measures best reduces health risks?
options: Taking regular screen breaks, positioning the monitor at eye level, and using a wrist rest
Alternating between two computers so that each device is used for four hours
Standing at a standing desk for the entire working day without any sitting
Working in a dark room, maximising screen brightness, and sitting as close to the screen as possible
grade9-ict.answer: Taking regular screen breaks, positioning the monitor at eye level, and using a wrist rest
acceptableAnswers: Taking regular screen breaks, positioning the monitor at eye level, and using a wrist rest
grade9-ict.explanation: Regular breaks reduce eye strain and RSI, positioning the monitor at eye level prevents neck strain, and a wrist rest reduces wrist fatigue. Together these measures significantly lower the health risks of prolonged computer use.

grade9-ict.intro: For each device below, tick whether it is an input, output or storage device.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A barcode scanner at a supermarket checkout.
parts.hint: It reads data into the computer.
parts.explanation: A barcode scanner captures the barcode pattern and sends the data to the computer, so it is an input device.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: An inkjet printer connected to a laptop.
parts.hint: It produces a physical copy of the document.
parts.explanation: A printer takes data from the computer and produces a hard copy, making it an output device.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A Blu-ray disc inserted in a drive.
parts.hint: It holds data even when removed from the drive.
parts.explanation: A Blu-ray disc stores data persistently, so it is a storage medium.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A digital camera connected to a computer via USB to transfer photos.
parts.hint: Photos are being transferred into the computer.
parts.explanation: In this context the camera sends data to the computer, acting as an input device.

grade9-ict.intro:
Use words from the list to complete the sentences. One word is not used.
RAM  ·  ROM  ·  CPU  ·  volatile  ·  permanent  ·  cache

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Complete each sentence with the correct word.
(i) The … carries out all the instructions and calculations in a computer.
(ii) … is temporary memory that loses its contents when the power is switched off.
(iii) Memory that keeps its contents without power is described as … storage.
(iv) Very fast memory built close to the processor that holds frequently used data is called …
(v) The BIOS program that runs when a computer starts is stored in …
parts.hint: One word in the list is not needed.
parts.explanation: The CPU processes instructions; RAM is volatile working memory; permanent/non-volatile storage survives power loss; cache is ultra-fast processor-side memory; BIOS lives in ROM.

grade9-ict.intro: For each statement, tick True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: An operating system manages how RAM is shared between running programs.
parts.hint: Memory management is a core OS function.
parts.explanation: The OS allocates and deallocates RAM to processes, ensuring each program gets the memory it needs without clashing with others.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Microsoft Word is an example of an operating system.
parts.hint: Word is used to create documents.
parts.explanation: Microsoft Word is an application program, not an operating system. Windows and Linux are examples of operating systems.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A device driver allows the operating system to control a specific hardware device.
parts.hint: Drivers translate OS commands for the device.
parts.explanation: A device driver provides the OS with the instructions needed to communicate with a particular hardware component.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Virtual memory uses part of the hard disk when RAM is full.
parts.hint: The disk acts as slower, extra RAM.
parts.explanation: When RAM is full, the OS swaps less-used pages to a disk swap file, extending the available memory at the cost of speed.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: A graphical user interface (GUI) requires the user to type commands into a terminal.
parts.hint: A GUI uses icons and a mouse.
parts.explanation: A GUI uses windows, icons and a pointing device; typing commands describes a Command Line Interface (CLI).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Give one reason why antivirus software should be kept up to date.

answer: new viruses are created all the time
virus definitions must be updated to recognise new threats

parts.hint: Think about how often new threats appear.
parts.explanation: New malware is released constantly; updating ensures the antivirus has the latest virus definitions to recognise and stop new threats.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: What is the purpose of a file compression utility?

options: To reduce the size of files so they take up less space and transfer more quickly
To encrypt files so they cannot be read without a password
response.answer: To reduce the size of files so they take up less space and transfer more quickly

parts.hint: Think about making a zip file.
parts.explanation: Compression reduces file size by encoding repeated patterns more efficiently, saving disk space and reducing download time.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: State two tasks that a disk cleanup utility can perform.
parts.hint: Think about files that accumulate without being needed.
parts.explanation: Disk cleanup deletes temporary files, clears cached data, empties the recycle bin and removes old system log files to free up disk space.

grade9-ict.intro:
Use words from the list to complete the sentences. There is one extra word.
LAN  ·  WAN  ·  MAN  ·  PAN  ·  WLAN  ·  VPN

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the correct abbreviation for each description.
(i) A network that connects devices in a single school building. …
(ii) A network that connects two offices in different countries. …
(iii) A secure, encrypted connection made over the public internet. …
(iv) A network covering a city, larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN. …
(v) A network that connects personal devices such as a phone and a headset within a few metres. …
parts.hint: Match the geographic scale or purpose of each description to its acronym.
parts.explanation: LAN = local (one building); WAN = wide area (different countries); VPN = secure tunnel over the internet; MAN = metropolitan area (city); PAN = personal area (a few metres).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a star topology, all computers connect to a central …
parts.hint: All cables meet at one central point.
parts.explanation: In a star topology, each device has its own cable running to a central switch or hub.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: State one advantage and one disadvantage of a star topology.

answer: a fault in one cable only affects that computer
adding a new computer is straightforward
if the switch fails the whole network fails
the switch is a single point of failure
more cable is used than in a bus topology

parts.hint: Think about what happens when one cable breaks vs when the central device breaks.
parts.explanation: Advantage: isolating a faulty cable is easy. Disadvantage: the central switch is a single point of failure.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: In a bus topology, a break in the main cable:

options: stops all communication on the entire network
only affects the nearest two computers
has no effect because traffic is rerouted
slows the network but does not stop it
response.answer: stops all communication on the entire network

parts.hint: Every device shares the same backbone.
parts.explanation: All devices share one bus cable; a break anywhere makes the whole network unusable.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the letter of the correct description for each network device.
A  Converts digital signals to analogue for transmission over a phone line and back again.
B  Forwards packets between different networks, choosing the best path.
C  Sends data only to the port where the destination device is connected.
(i) Router    (ii) Modem    (iii) Switch
parts.hint: Router = between networks; Modem = digital/analogue; Switch = within a LAN.
parts.explanation: Router → B (forwards between networks); Modem → A (digital↔analogue conversion); Switch → C (targeted delivery within the LAN).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: What device allows wireless devices to connect to a wired LAN?
parts.hint: It bridges the wireless and wired worlds.
parts.explanation: A WAP provides a Wi-Fi connection and bridges it to the wired LAN infrastructure.

grade9-ict.intro: For each statement, tick True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A wired Ethernet connection is generally faster and more reliable than Wi-Fi.
parts.hint: A cable provides a dedicated path.
parts.explanation: Ethernet cables deliver a stable, interference-free connection with consistently higher speeds than wireless.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: An open (unsecured) Wi-Fi network encrypts all data automatically.
parts.hint: Open means no security.
parts.explanation: An open network has no encryption, so any nearby device can intercept the unencrypted traffic.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The 5 GHz Wi-Fi band has a longer range than the 2.4 GHz band.
parts.hint: Higher frequency = shorter range.
parts.explanation: Higher frequency radio waves are absorbed more readily by walls and obstacles; the 5 GHz band has a shorter range than 2.4 GHz.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: WPA2 is a security protocol used to protect Wi-Fi communications.
parts.hint: WPA2 encrypts Wi-Fi traffic.
parts.explanation: WPA2 (Wi-Fi Protected Access 2) uses AES encryption to protect the data travelling over a wireless network.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: An intranet is best described as:

options: A private network within an organisation that uses web technologies but is not publicly accessible
The global public internet restricted to one country
A wireless network available in cafés and public spaces
A backup copy of the public internet
response.answer: A private network within an organisation that uses web technologies but is not publicly accessible

parts.hint: Intra = inside.
parts.explanation: An intranet uses browser-based technology but is accessible only to authorised users within the organisation.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: What is the main difference between an intranet and an extranet?

options: An extranet extends controlled access to trusted external parties such as suppliers, whereas an intranet is restricted to employees only
An extranet is faster than an intranet
An intranet uses wireless technology and an extranet uses cables
An extranet has no security controls, unlike an intranet
response.answer: An extranet extends controlled access to trusted external parties such as suppliers, whereas an intranet is restricted to employees only

parts.hint: Extra = outside (but limited).
parts.explanation: An extranet gives selected external users — suppliers, partners, clients — access to parts of the intranet that are relevant to them.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Give two features a school intranet might provide for its pupils.
parts.hint: Think about what a school website only for students would contain.
parts.explanation: A school intranet typically provides timetables, learning resources, homework assignments, notices and staff contact details to pupils and staff.

grade9-ict.intro:
Use words from the list to complete the sentences. One word is not used.
DNS  ·  HTTP  ·  HTTPS  ·  URL  ·  HTML  ·  ISP

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the correct abbreviation for each description.
(i) The protocol used to transfer web pages between a server and a browser. …
(ii) The secure version of the web protocol that encrypts data in transit. …
(iii) The system that translates domain names into IP addresses. …
(iv) The unique web address used to locate a specific page on the internet. …
(v) The markup language used to structure and create web pages. …
parts.hint: ISP is the unused word — it stands for Internet Service Provider.
parts.explanation: HTTP transfers pages; HTTPS does so securely; DNS resolves domain names; URL is the web address; HTML is the page markup language. ISP is the extra word.

grade9-ict.intro: For each statement, tick True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The BCC field hides the recipient's address from all other recipients.
parts.hint: BCC = Blind Carbon Copy.
parts.explanation: BCC (Blind Carbon Copy) adds a recipient whose email address is invisible to all other recipients.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: SMTP is the protocol used to download emails from a server to a client.
parts.hint: SMTP is for sending, not receiving.
parts.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) sends and routes email between servers; IMAP or POP3 are used to retrieve email.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: An advantage of email over a posted letter is that email arrives almost instantly.
parts.hint: Speed is the primary advantage.
parts.explanation: Email is delivered in seconds worldwide; a letter can take days or weeks.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Webmail requires dedicated email software to be installed on the user's computer.
parts.hint: Webmail works through a browser.
parts.explanation: Webmail provides access to email through any web browser; no separate email client is needed.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Give one advantage of online shopping compared with visiting a physical shop.
parts.hint: Think about convenience.
parts.explanation: Online shops are available around the clock and can be accessed from any location, offering convenience that physical stores cannot always match.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Give one disadvantage of online shopping.

answer: cannot handle the product before buying
items may not match their description
may need to pay delivery charges

parts.hint: Think about the risks of not seeing the item.
parts.explanation: Online shoppers cannot inspect products physically; they also face risks of fraud, delivery issues and items that differ from their descriptions.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: When paying online, the presence of https and a padlock symbol in the address bar indicates:

options: The connection is encrypted and the site has a valid security certificate
The purchase is free of charge
The website is operated by a government
The goods will be delivered the next day
response.answer: The connection is encrypted and the site has a valid security certificate

parts.hint: HTTPS = secure and encrypted.
parts.explanation: HTTPS with a padlock means the connection uses TLS encryption, protecting payment details from interception.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the letter of the correct definition for each browser term.
A  A stored web address that the user can click to return to a page quickly.
B  A record of all the web pages visited in recent sessions.
C  A local copy of recently visited pages saved to speed up future visits.
(i) Bookmark    (ii) History    (iii) Cache
parts.hint: Bookmark = saved; History = past visits; Cache = saved copy of pages.
parts.explanation: Bookmark → A (saved address); History → B (list of visited pages); Cache → C (local stored copies).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Enclosing a search phrase in quotation marks (e.g., "climate change") tells the search engine to:

options: Find pages containing that exact phrase
Translate the search into another language
response.answer: Find pages containing that exact phrase

parts.hint: Quotes lock in the exact sequence of words.
parts.explanation: Quotation marks instruct the search engine to return only pages where those words appear together in that exact order.

grade9-ict.intro:
Use words from the list to complete the sentences. One word is not used.
field  ·  record  ·  primary key  ·  foreign key  ·  flat-file  ·  relational

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the correct term for each description.
(i) A single category of data, such as Surname or Date of Birth. …
(ii) All the data stored about one person or item. …
(iii) A field whose value is unique for every record, identifying each row. …
(iv) A database that stores all data in one table only. …
(v) A database made up of several linked tables. …
parts.hint: Foreign key is the unused term.
parts.explanation: Field = one column; record = one row; primary key = unique identifier; flat-file = single table; relational = multiple linked tables. Foreign key is not used here.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A database query criterion of >"2024-01-01" in a "DateJoined" field would return records where:
parts.hint: > means "greater than" (later in time for dates).
parts.explanation: The > operator on a date field selects records where the date is later than the specified value.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Using the AND operator between two criteria in a query:

options: Returns only records that satisfy BOTH criteria simultaneously
Returns records that satisfy either criterion
response.answer: Returns only records that satisfy BOTH criteria simultaneously

parts.hint: AND = both must be true.
parts.explanation: AND is more restrictive; both conditions must be met for a record to appear in the results.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt:
A student database has fields: StudentID, Surname, FirstName, Class, Mark.
Write the criteria you would use to find all students in class 9A with a mark greater than 60.
parts.hint: One criterion for class, one for mark.
parts.explanation: Class = "9A" (or equals 9A) AND Mark > 60 would return all students in class 9A who scored more than 60.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What is the main purpose of a form in a database application?

options: To provide a user-friendly screen for entering and editing records one at a time
To print a formatted summary of all records
To search the database with complex criteria
response.answer: To provide a user-friendly screen for entering and editing records one at a time

parts.hint: Forms are for data entry.
parts.explanation: A form displays one record at a time in a neat layout, making data entry and editing easier and less error-prone than working directly in the table.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Grouping records in a report allows:

options: Records with the same value in a field to be collected together, with optional subtotals for each group
All records to be displayed in a single column
The report to be sorted in reverse order
Images to be added to the report
response.answer: Records with the same value in a field to be collected together, with optional subtotals for each group

parts.hint: Group by Department, then total each group.
parts.explanation: Grouping collects records sharing a common value — e.g., all records for Department = "Science" — and can calculate group subtotals.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Exporting a report as a PDF is useful because:

options: The formatted report can be shared and printed by anyone without the database software
PDF files are automatically updated when the database changes
response.answer: The formatted report can be shared and printed by anyone without the database software

parts.hint: PDF is a universal, read-only format.
parts.explanation: PDF preserves the layout and can be opened on any device with a PDF reader, making it ideal for distributing finalised reports.

grade9-ict.intro: For each statement, tick True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A presence check ensures that a required field is not left blank.
parts.hint: Presence = must contain something.
parts.explanation: A presence check validation rule prevents a record from being saved unless the mandatory field contains a value.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A range check validates that a value falls within an acceptable minimum and maximum.
parts.hint: Range = between two limits.
parts.explanation: A range check rejects entries outside the allowed bounds — for example, a score field that only accepts values from 0 to 100.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Data verification checks that entered data is of the correct type or within a valid range.
parts.hint: Verification checks accuracy; validation checks rules.
parts.explanation: Verification checks that data was entered as intended (e.g., re-typing an email to confirm it was copied correctly). Validation checks rules like type and range.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A lookup field in a database presents the user with a list of approved values to select from.
parts.hint: A dropdown list restricts entries.
parts.explanation: A lookup (or drop-down) field limits input to a predefined list, preventing typing errors and ensuring data consistency.

grade9-ict.intro: For each statement, tick True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: RSI (Repetitive Strain Injury) is caused by performing the same hand movements repeatedly over a long period.
parts.hint: Repetition is in the name.
parts.explanation: RSI develops from repeated, often awkward movements without adequate rest, damaging tendons and muscles.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Eye strain from computer use can be reduced by increasing the screen brightness to its maximum setting.
parts.hint: Extreme brightness causes glare.
parts.explanation: Eye strain is reduced by matching screen brightness to room lighting and taking regular breaks, not by maximising brightness.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The 20-20-20 rule recommends looking at an object 20 metres away for 20 seconds every 20 minutes.
parts.hint: 20-20-20: metres, seconds, minutes.
parts.explanation: The 20-20-20 rule gives the eye muscles a rest and helps prevent eye strain and dryness from prolonged screen use.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Prolonged sitting at a computer can contribute to obesity and cardiovascular disease.
parts.hint: Sedentary behaviour has serious health risks.
parts.explanation: Extended sitting slows the metabolism and reduces circulation, increasing the long-term risk of obesity, cardiovascular disease and blood clots.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Blue light from screens has no effect on sleep quality.
parts.hint: Blue light affects melatonin.
parts.explanation: Blue light suppresses melatonin production, delaying sleep onset and reducing sleep quality, especially when screens are used close to bedtime.

grade9-ict.intro:
Use words from the list to complete the sentences. One word is not used.
wrist rest  ·  footrest  ·  lumbar support  ·  anti-glare filter  ·  eye level  ·  surge protector

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the correct term for each ergonomic or safety measure.
(i) A device placed in front of the monitor to reduce reflections that cause eye strain. …
(ii) A padded support that keeps wrists in a neutral position while typing. …
(iii) A feature of an ergonomic chair that supports the natural curve of the lower spine. …
(iv) The top of the monitor should be placed at or just below … so the user looks slightly downward.
(v) A device that protects equipment from voltage spikes and power cuts. …
parts.hint: Footrest is the unused term.
parts.explanation: Anti-glare filter reduces reflections; wrist rest keeps wrists neutral; lumbar support supports the lower back; eye level is the correct monitor height; surge protector guards against voltage spikes. Footrest is not used here.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Why should food and drinks not be brought into a computer laboratory?

options: Spills can damage keyboards and circuit boards, and crumbs attract pests
The computer works faster without food nearby
It is considered impolite in all countries
Food improves the humidity which damages screens
response.answer: Spills can damage keyboards and circuit boards, and crumbs attract pests

parts.hint: Liquids and electronics are dangerous together.
parts.explanation: A spill on a keyboard or into a computer can cause a short circuit, destroying the equipment.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Before plugging a personal USB drive into a school computer, a student should:

options: Have the drive scanned for viruses first
Format the drive to remove all files
Ask their teacher to break the USB drive
Ignore any warnings and proceed immediately
response.answer: Have the drive scanned for viruses first

parts.hint: External drives can carry malware.
parts.explanation: USB drives from other computers may contain malware; scanning before use prevents spreading infection to the school network.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Give two reasons why students should save their work regularly while in the computer lab.

answer: power cuts could lose unsaved work
unexpected program crashes may cause data loss
RAM is volatile and loses data without power
unsaved work is lost if the computer freezes
power cuts could lose unsaved work
unexpected program crashes may cause data loss
RAM is volatile and loses data without power
unsaved work is lost if the computer freezes

parts.hint: Think about what can happen unexpectedly.
parts.explanation: Unsaved work lives only in volatile RAM; a power cut or program crash immediately destroys it. Regular saves to disk protect against this.

grade9-ict.intro: For each statement, tick True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A strong password should contain at least eight characters including uppercase letters, numbers and symbols.
parts.hint: Complexity makes passwords harder to crack.
parts.explanation: A strong password mixes character types and length, making brute-force and dictionary attacks much harder.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A firewall prevents all computer viruses from entering a system.
parts.hint: Firewalls filter network traffic, not file contents.
parts.explanation: A firewall filters network connections but cannot detect viruses in legitimate files; antivirus software is needed for that.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Phishing is an attack that tricks users into revealing personal information through a fake message or website.
parts.hint: Phishing = fishing for credentials.
parts.explanation: Phishing uses deceptive emails or websites disguised as legitimate ones to steal passwords, bank details or personal information.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Two-factor authentication (2FA) is less secure than a password alone because it adds complexity.
parts.hint: Two factors = two barriers to overcome.
parts.explanation: 2FA adds a second verification step (e.g., a one-time code sent to a phone) so an attacker who has the password still cannot log in without the second factor.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Copyright law gives the creator of an original work the exclusive right to:

options: Reproduce, distribute and adapt the work, and to authorise others to do so
Allow anyone to copy the work freely
Use the work only for personal purposes
Share the work on social media without restriction
response.answer: Reproduce, distribute and adapt the work, and to authorise others to do so

parts.hint: It gives the creator control.
parts.explanation: Copyright is the legal right that protects original works; only the creator (or someone they authorise) can legally copy, distribute or adapt the work.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Using someone else's image from the internet in your presentation without permission or acknowledgement is an example of:
parts.hint: You are using their work without the right to do so.
parts.explanation: Images on the internet are normally protected by copyright; using them without permission or credit infringes the creator's rights.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: "Creative Commons" licence allows:

options: Others to use the work under specified conditions set by the creator, often including attribution
Anyone to use the work for any purpose with no conditions at all
Only the creator to view the work
The government to own the work
response.answer: Others to use the work under specified conditions set by the creator, often including attribution

parts.hint: Creative Commons = sharing with conditions.
parts.explanation: Creative Commons licences allow creators to specify how others may use their work — for example, with attribution, non-commercially or with no derivatives.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A full backup copies:

options: All selected data every time the backup runs, regardless of what has changed
Only files that have changed since the last backup
Only system files, not user data
Data to the same drive as the original
response.answer: All selected data every time the backup runs, regardless of what has changed

parts.hint: Full = everything, every time.
parts.explanation: A full backup copies all selected files each time it runs; it takes the most time and space but is the simplest to restore from.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: An incremental backup copies:

options: Only files that have changed since the last backup of any kind
A copy of the last full backup
response.answer: Only files that have changed since the last backup of any kind

parts.hint: It backs up only the new changes.
parts.explanation: An incremental backup stores only the files that changed since the previous backup (whether full or incremental), saving time and storage.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: State two reasons why backups should be stored in a different physical location from the original data.

answer: fire or flood could destroy both if in the same place
theft of the original also destroys the backup if they are together
physical disaster could affect both copies
a local fire could destroy the original and backup simultaneously
fire or flood could destroy both if in the same place
theft of the original also destroys the backup if they are together
physical disaster could affect both copies
a local fire could destroy the original and backup simultaneously

parts.hint: Think about what one disaster could destroy.
parts.explanation: If backups and originals are in the same location, a fire, flood or theft could destroy both simultaneously, defeating the purpose of the backup.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Mail merge is used to:

options: Create personalised letters or emails automatically by combining a template document with a data source
Merge two word-processed documents into one
Send emails without an internet connection
Print all documents in a folder at once
response.answer: Create personalised letters or emails automatically by combining a template document with a data source

parts.hint: Each letter is personalised with data from a list.
parts.explanation: Mail merge takes a standard template letter and inserts data (names, addresses, etc.) from a spreadsheet or database to produce individualised copies for each recipient.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: In a mail merge document, a merge field such as <<FirstName>> acts as a:

options: A placeholder that is replaced by the actual data value for each record during the merge
A formatting instruction for the font
A hyperlink to the data file
A formula that calculates a value
response.answer: A placeholder that is replaced by the actual data value for each record during the merge

parts.hint: It is a placeholder for real data.
parts.explanation: Merge fields are placeholders in double angle brackets; when the merge runs, each field is replaced by the corresponding value from the data source.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Name two items of information that are typically stored in the data source (recipient list) for a mail merge.
parts.hint: What details do you need to personalise a letter?
parts.explanation: The data source typically holds recipient details such as name, address, email address and other personalisation data.

grade9-ict.intro: For each statement, tick True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Applying a Heading 1 style to text automatically formats it according to the predefined style definition.
parts.hint: A style applies a complete set of formatting at once.
parts.explanation: A style applies all its defined formatting properties — font, size, colour, spacing — in one click.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Modifying the Heading 2 style in a document updates every paragraph tagged with that style automatically.
parts.hint: Changing the style changes all instances.
parts.explanation: Because all Heading 2 paragraphs reference the same style definition, changing the style updates every one of them simultaneously.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Styles can be used to automatically generate a Table of Contents because headings are tagged.
parts.hint: The TOC collects heading-styled text.
parts.explanation: A Table of Contents is built by collecting all paragraphs formatted with Heading styles; they provide the text and page number for each TOC entry.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Using styles makes documents harder to format consistently across many pages.
parts.hint: Styles make consistency easy.
parts.explanation: Styles ensure every heading, body paragraph and caption in the document looks identical, making consistent formatting across a long document straightforward.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the letter of the correct function for each task.
A  Adds together all the numbers in a range of cells.
B  Returns the highest value in a range of cells.
C  Displays one of two values depending on whether a condition is true or false.
(i) =MAX(A1:A20)    (ii) =IF(B2>50,"Pass","Fail")    (iii) =SUM(A1:A20)
parts.hint: SUM = total; MAX = largest; IF = conditional.
parts.explanation: MAX → B (largest value); IF → C (conditional choice); SUM → A (total).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The function =AVERAGE(C1:C10) returns:

options: The arithmetic mean of all values in C1 to C10
The largest value in C1 to C10
The total of all values in C1 to C10
The number of cells containing data in C1 to C10
response.answer: The arithmetic mean of all values in C1 to C10

parts.hint: AVERAGE = mean.
parts.explanation: AVERAGE sums the values and divides by the count to give the arithmetic mean.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the letter of the chart type that best suits each purpose.
A  To show how parts contribute to a total (percentages of a whole).
B  To compare values across different categories side by side.
C  To show how a value changes over a continuous period of time.
(i) Line graph    (ii) Pie chart    (iii) Bar/column chart
parts.hint: Pie = parts of a whole; Bar = comparison; Line = trend over time.
parts.explanation: Line graph → C (trends over time); Pie chart → A (parts of a whole); Bar chart → B (category comparison).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: If the data values in a spreadsheet are changed after a chart has been created, the chart will:

options: Update automatically to reflect the new values
Need to be deleted and redrawn
response.answer: Update automatically to reflect the new values

parts.hint: Charts are linked to their source data.
parts.explanation: A spreadsheet chart is dynamically linked to its data range; any change to source data immediately updates the chart.

grade9-ict.intro:
Use words from the list to complete the sentences. One word is not used.
oval  ·  rectangle  ·  diamond  ·  parallelogram  ·  arrow  ·  connector

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the correct flowchart symbol name for each description.
(i) Used to mark the START or END of an algorithm. …
(ii) Represents a process, action or calculation. …
(iii) Represents a decision with a Yes or No exit path. …
(iv) Represents an input or output operation. …
(v) Shows the direction and sequence of flow between symbols. …
parts.hint: Connector is the unused symbol.
parts.explanation: Oval = START/END; Rectangle = process; Diamond = decision; Parallelogram = input/output; Arrow = flow direction. The connector circle links distant sections.

grade9-ict.intro: For each statement below, tick True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A hard disk keeps its contents when the computer is switched off.
parts.hint: Think about whether your saved work is still there tomorrow.
parts.explanation: A hard disk is secondary storage and is non-volatile, so what is saved on it survives being switched off.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A DVD holds more data than a CD of the same physical size.
parts.hint: Compare about 700 MB with about 4.7 GB.
parts.explanation: A single-layer DVD holds about 4.7 GB against about 700 MB on a CD, so the DVD holds much more.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A pen drive is an output device.
parts.hint: Data travels both ways with a pen drive.
parts.explanation: A pen drive is a storage device: data is written to it and read back from it, so it is not an output device.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: One gigabyte is smaller than one megabyte.
parts.hint: Put the units in order of size.
parts.explanation: One gigabyte is 1 024 megabytes, so a gigabyte is very much larger than a megabyte.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: The contents of a CD-ROM can be changed by the user each time it is used.
parts.hint: Look at what the letters ROM stand for.
parts.explanation: ROM stands for read-only memory, so a CD-ROM can be read as often as you like but cannot be written to again.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: A memory card used in a camera is a form of secondary storage.
parts.hint: The photographs are still there when the camera is off.
parts.explanation: A memory card keeps the photographs after the camera is switched off, which is exactly what secondary storage does.

grade9-ict.intro: For each device below, tick whether it is used mainly for input, for output or for storage.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A microphone plugged into a computer.
parts.hint: Which way does the sound travel?
parts.explanation: A microphone turns sound into data and sends it into the computer, so it is an input device.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A plotter attached to a design computer.
parts.hint: It puts something onto paper.
parts.explanation: A plotter draws the computer’s output onto large sheets of paper, so it is an output device.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A pen drive plugged into a USB port.
parts.hint: Files are both saved to it and opened from it.
parts.explanation: A pen drive holds files so they can be carried and opened later, which makes it a storage device.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A touchpad on a laptop computer.
parts.hint: It is used instead of a mouse.
parts.explanation: A touchpad sends the movement of the finger into the computer to move the pointer, so it is an input device.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: A pair of speakers on a desk.
parts.hint: The user hears the result.
parts.explanation: Speakers turn data from the computer into sound for the user, so they are output devices.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: An external hard disk connected by a cable.
parts.hint: It is used for backups.
parts.explanation: An external hard disk holds files outside the computer, usually for backup, so it is a storage device.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many bits make up one byte?
parts.hint: It is the number of bits needed for one character.
parts.explanation: One byte is 8 bits, which is enough to store a single character of text.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How many kilobytes make up one megabyte?
parts.hint: It is the same step as from a byte to a kilobyte.
parts.explanation: Each step up the units multiplies by 1 024, so one megabyte is 1 024 kilobytes. Manufacturers often round this to 1 000.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A photograph has a size of 3 072 kilobytes. Write its size in megabytes.
parts.hint: Divide by the number of kilobytes in a megabyte.
parts.explanation: 3 072 ÷ 1 024 = 3, so the photograph is 3 MB.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Write the four units below in order of size, starting with the smallest: gigabyte, kilobyte, megabyte, terabyte.
parts.hint: Each unit is about a thousand times the one before it.
parts.explanation: The order is kilobyte, megabyte, gigabyte, terabyte - each about 1 024 times the one before it. The mark is given only when all four are in the right order.

grade9-ict.intro:
Use words from the list to complete the sentences. There is one extra word in the list.
booting  ·  driver  ·  multitasking  ·  operating system  ·  spreadsheet

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the missing word for each sentence.
(i) Switching a computer on and loading the software that controls it is called …
(ii) Running a browser and a word processor at the same time is called …
(iii) The small program that lets the computer control a printer is called a …
(iv) Windows, Linux and Android are each an example of an …
