parts.hint: One word in the list belongs to application software and is not used at all.
parts.explanation: Booting is the start-up process; multitasking is running several programs at once; a driver lets the system control a particular device; and Windows, Linux and Android are operating systems. "Spreadsheet" is the extra word.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Which one of the following is system software?
parts.hint: System software runs the machine; application software does a job for the user.
parts.explanation: The operating system runs the machine itself. A word processor, a spreadsheet and a browser are all application software.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Which of these tasks is carried out by the operating system?

options: Managing the files stored on the disk
Writing the text of a letter
Drawing the pictures on a poster
Choosing the words for an email
response.answer: Managing the files stored on the disk

parts.hint: Three of these are jobs the user does with an application.
parts.explanation: Managing files and folders on the disk is an operating system job. The other three are done by the user in an application program.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the letter of the description that matches each utility programme.
A  Removes files that are no longer needed so that disk space is freed.
B  Makes files smaller so that they take up less space.
C  Searches for malicious software and removes what it finds.
(i) Antivirus    (ii) File compression    (iii) Disk clean-up
parts.hint: Read what each description does, not what it is called.
parts.explanation: Antivirus matches C, file compression matches B and disk clean-up matches A.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A utility programme is a kind of:
parts.hint: It looks after the machine rather than doing a job for the user.
parts.explanation: Utility programmes look after the computer itself - the disk, the files and the security - so they are system software.

grade9-ict.intro: For each statement below, tick True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A password made only of your date of birth is a strong password.
parts.hint: How easily could someone else find that out?
parts.explanation: A date of birth is short, is made only of digits and is easy for other people to find, so it makes a weak password.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Keeping a backup on a separate device protects the data if the computer is stolen.
parts.hint: Where is the second copy kept?
parts.explanation: A backup on a separate device is not lost with the computer, so the data can be restored.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Antivirus software should be updated regularly.
parts.hint: New threats appear all the time.
parts.explanation: New viruses appear constantly, so antivirus software can only recognise them once it has been updated.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: It is safe to open an attachment sent by someone you do not know.
parts.hint: An attachment can carry a program.
parts.explanation: An attachment from an unknown sender may carry a virus or other malicious software, so it should not be opened.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: A firewall helps to control the traffic entering and leaving a network.
parts.hint: Its name describes a barrier.
parts.explanation: A firewall inspects the traffic crossing the edge of a network and blocks whatever is not allowed.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: Sharing your password with a classmate keeps your account safer.
parts.hint: How many people can now use the account?
parts.explanation: Every extra person who knows a password is another way for the account to be misused, so sharing it makes the account less safe.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the letter of the description that matches each term.
A  Pretending to be a bank in order to obtain someone’s password.
B  Unwanted advertising email sent to very many addresses at once.
C  A program that copies itself and damages the files it reaches.
D  Sending repeated unkind messages to another person online.
(i) Phishing    (ii) Virus    (iii) Spam    (iv) Cyber-bullying
parts.hint: Two of the four are about people and two are about programs.
parts.explanation: Phishing matches A, a virus matches C, spam matches B and cyber-bullying matches D.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A message arrives asking you to confirm your bank password by clicking a link. What should you do?

options: Delete the message and do not click the link
Click the link and type in the password
Forward the message to all your friends
Reply to the message with the password
response.answer: Delete the message and do not click the link

parts.hint: A bank never asks for a password by email.
parts.explanation: This is phishing. The message should be deleted without clicking the link, and the password must never be sent to anyone.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Which one of these makes a password stronger?

options: Using the name of your favourite pet
Using the date of your own birthday
Repeating one short word twice over

parts.hint: The harder it is to guess, the better.
parts.explanation: A mixture of letters, digits and symbols gives far more possible passwords, so it is much harder to guess or to break.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A data protection act gives a person the right to:

options: see the personal data held about them
choose the price of any service offered
use any software at all without paying
copy any picture found on the Internet
response.answer: see the personal data held about them

parts.hint: The act protects the person the data is about.
parts.explanation: A data protection act gives people the right to see the personal data an organisation holds about them and to have mistakes corrected.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Personal data collected for one purpose may:

options: not be used for a different purpose
be sold to anyone who asks to buy it
be published on any public website
be kept for ever without any reason
response.answer: not be used for a different purpose

parts.hint: The reason for collecting it is part of the promise made.
parts.explanation: Data must be used only for the purpose it was collected for; using it for something else breaks that promise.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Who is responsible for keeping personal data accurate and up to date?

options: The postman who delivers the letters
Any visitor who reads the website
The company that made the computer

parts.hint: Responsibility sits with whoever holds the data.
parts.explanation: The organisation that collects and holds personal data is responsible for keeping it accurate and up to date.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A data protection act says that personal data should be kept:

options: only for as long as it is needed
for at least twenty-five whole years
on paper rather than on a computer
in a language chosen by the owner
response.answer: only for as long as it is needed

parts.hint: Old data that is no longer needed is a risk, not an asset.
parts.explanation: Data must not be kept longer than the purpose requires; once it is no longer needed it should be deleted.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the letter of the action that helps to prevent each health problem.
A  Look away at something distant for a moment and take a short break.
B  Use a chair with back support and sit upright with both feet flat.
C  Fit a screen filter or lower the brightness of the display.
D  Rest the wrists on a support and change position regularly.
(i) Eye strain    (ii) Back ache    (iii) Wrist injury    (iv) Glare from the screen
parts.hint: Match the part of the body to the thing that supports or rests it.
parts.explanation: Eye strain matches A, back ache matches B, a wrist injury matches D and glare matches C.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The top of the screen should be roughly level with:
parts.hint: The neck should stay straight.
parts.explanation: With the top of the screen at eye level the user looks slightly downwards and the neck stays in a natural position.

grade9-ict.intro: For each rule below, tick True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Food and drink may be taken to the computer table.
parts.hint: Think about what a spill would do.
parts.explanation: Food and drink are kept away from computers because a spill can destroy a keyboard or a whole machine.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Trailing cables on the floor should be covered or tied out of the way.
parts.hint: Someone has to walk past them.
parts.explanation: Loose cables across a floor are a trip hazard, so they are covered or fastened out of the walkway.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A computer should be shut down properly before the power is switched off.
parts.hint: Files may still be open.
parts.explanation: Shutting down closes open files and lets the operating system finish writing to the disk, so nothing is lost or damaged.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
The four troubleshooting steps below are in the wrong order. Write 1, 2, 3 or 4 against each one to show the correct order.
(i) Test that the problem has gone.
(ii) Identify exactly what the problem is.
(iii) Decide on the most likely cause.
(iv) Apply the fix.
parts.hint: Nothing can be fixed before it has been identified, and nothing is finished before it has been tested.
parts.explanation: The order is identify the problem, decide the likely cause, apply the fix, then test that it has gone - so (ii) is 1, (iii) is 2, (iv) is 3 and (i) is 4.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A monitor shows no picture although its power light is on. Which check should be made first?

options: The cable between monitor and computer
The free space left on the hard disk
The version of the word processor used
The number of files kept in the folder
response.answer: The cable between monitor and computer

parts.hint: Start with the simplest and most likely cause.
parts.explanation: Checking the video cable is the simplest and most likely cause; the other three have nothing to do with a blank display.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the letter of the first check to make for each fault.
A  Check that the paper tray is not empty.
B  Check that the network cable is plugged in.
C  Check that the speaker volume is not muted.
(i) No sound comes from the computer    (ii) The printer will not print    (iii) The school network cannot be reached
parts.hint: Match each fault to the part of the system it involves.
parts.explanation: No sound matches C, the printer fault matches A and the network fault matches B.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A file has been deleted by mistake. Where should the user look first?
parts.hint: Deleted files are not removed from the disk straight away.
parts.explanation: A deleted file is moved to the Recycle Bin first, so it can usually be restored from there.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
The four stages of making a short multimedia clip are listed in the wrong order. Write 1, 2, 3 or 4 against each one to show the correct order.
(i) Record the sound and take the photographs.
(ii) Decide what the message of the clip is.
(iii) Draw a storyboard of each scene in order.
(iv) Assemble the scenes in the authoring software.
parts.hint: Planning comes before recording, and recording before assembling.
parts.explanation: The message is decided first, then the storyboard is drawn, then the material is recorded, and finally the scenes are assembled - so (ii) is 1, (iii) is 2, (i) is 3 and (iv) is 4.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: What is the main purpose of a storyboard?

options: To plan the order of the scenes beforehand
To record the sound track of the finished clip
To print out the handouts for the audience
To choose the colours used on the slide master
response.answer: To plan the order of the scenes beforehand

parts.hint: It is drawn before any recording is done.
parts.explanation: A storyboard sets out what each scene shows and the order the scenes come in, so problems are found on paper rather than after filming.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A change made on the slide master will:

options: appear on every slide that uses it
appear on the very first slide only
delete the text written on every slide
print the slides out as audience handouts
response.answer: appear on every slide that uses it

parts.hint: That is the whole reason a master exists.
parts.explanation: The slide master holds the settings shared by the slides, so one change there is applied to all of them at once.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Which view shows the notes the speaker will use?
parts.hint: The name says what it holds.
parts.explanation: Notes Page view shows each slide with the speaker’s notes beneath it, ready to be printed for the presenter.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A design template is used to:

options: give every slide the same look
change the order of the slides
add narration to the slide show
count the words on each slide
response.answer: give every slide the same look

parts.hint: It is about appearance, not content.
parts.explanation: A design template applies one set of colours, fonts and backgrounds so the whole presentation looks consistent.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the letter of the network type that fits each situation.
A  LAN
B  WAN
C  PAN
D  VPN
(i) The computers in one school laboratory joined together.
(ii) The branches of a bank in Mauritius, Rodrigues and France joined together.
(iii) A phone joined to a wireless headset one metre away.
(iv) A secure private link to an office network made across the Internet.
parts.hint: Sort them by the distance each one covers, then deal with the secure one.
parts.explanation: One laboratory is a LAN (A); branches in different countries need a WAN (B); a phone and a headset a metre apart make a PAN (C); a secure private tunnel across the Internet is a VPN (D).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: What do the letters LAN stand for?
parts.hint: It describes how much ground the network covers.
parts.explanation: LAN stands for Local Area Network - a network covering one building or one site.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Which one of these is an advantage of joining computers in a network?

options: A printer can be shared between users
Each computer needs its own printer
Files cannot be copied between users
Software must be installed twice over
response.answer: A printer can be shared between users

parts.hint: Think about what only has to be bought once.
parts.explanation: On a network one printer can serve many users, which saves both money and space.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the letter of the job done by each network component.
A  Joins one network to another and directs traffic between them.
B  Checks the traffic crossing the edge of a network and blocks what is not allowed.
C  Lets a single computer join a network, by cable or wirelessly.
(i) Router    (ii) Network interface card    (iii) Firewall
parts.hint: One joins networks, one joins a computer, one guards the edge.
parts.explanation: A router matches A, a network interface card matches C and a firewall matches B.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A company that provides a home with its Internet connection is called:
parts.hint: Its name says exactly what it supplies.
parts.explanation: An Internet Service Provider (ISP) sells the connection that links a home or a school to the Internet.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the letter of the description that matches each online tool.
A  A personal online diary that readers may add comments to.
B  A website that many people may edit to build one shared page.
C  A meeting held with sound and moving pictures over the Internet.
(i) Blog    (ii) Video conference    (iii) Wiki
parts.hint: One is written by a single person and one is written by many.
parts.explanation: A blog matches A, a video conference matches C and a wiki matches B.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A podcast is best described as:

options: a sound recording published on the Internet
a printed copy of a page from a website
a folder of photographs kept on a disk
a short message sent to a mobile phone
response.answer: a sound recording published on the Internet

parts.hint: It is something you listen to.
parts.explanation: A podcast is an audio programme published on the Internet so that listeners can play or download it whenever they wish.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the keyboard shortcut used for each action. Give each answer in the form Ctrl + letter.
(i) Copy the selected text    (ii) Paste the copied text    (iii) Make the selected text bold
parts.hint: Two of the three letters are the first letter of the action.
parts.explanation: Ctrl + C copies, Ctrl + V pastes and Ctrl + B makes text bold. V is used for paste because it sits next to C on the keyboard.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Which formatting makes text lean over to the right?
parts.hint: It is often used for the title of a book.
parts.explanation: Italic text slopes to the right and is used for emphasis and for titles.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Text that is level at both the left and the right margin is said to be:
parts.hint: Newspaper columns are set this way.
parts.explanation: Justified text is spaced so that it lines up at both margins, which is how newspaper columns are set.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Carrying out steps one after another in the order written is called:
parts.hint: Nothing is skipped and nothing is repeated.
parts.explanation: Sequence means the steps are carried out one after another in the order they are written.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Choosing between two different paths using IF is called:
parts.hint: A decision is being made.
parts.explanation: Selection means the program tests a condition and then chooses which path to follow.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt:
A program must print the word HELLO twenty times.
(i) Name the control structure that should be used.
(ii) Name the flowchart symbol that holds the test deciding when to stop.
parts.hint: One word describes doing something over and over; the other names a shape.
parts.explanation: Repetition (a loop) is used to run the same step many times, and the test that decides when to stop is held in a decision symbol, drawn as a diamond.

grade9-ict.intro: The panel below was opened on a computer in the school laboratory.

stimulus.html:
System information
Device nameLAB-PC-07
ProcessorIntel Core i5   2.40 GHz
Installed memory8.00 GB
System type64-bit operating system
EditionWindows 11 Pro
Storage500 GB hard disk
stimulus.altText: A system information panel listing the device name, the processor, the installed memory, the system type, the edition of the operating system and the storage fitted.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write down the amount of installed memory shown on the panel.
parts.hint: Read it straight off the row labelled Installed memory.
parts.explanation: The panel gives the installed memory as 8.00 GB.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write down the edition of the operating system on this computer.
parts.hint: It is on the row labelled Edition.
parts.explanation: The Edition row reads Windows 11 Pro.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The system type of this computer is:
parts.hint: Read the row labelled System type.
parts.explanation: The panel shows a 64-bit operating system, which means the processor handles data 64 bits at a time.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Write down the speed of the processor, in GHz.
parts.hint: It is printed after the name of the processor.
parts.explanation: The processor row reads 2.40 GHz, so the speed is 2.4 GHz.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Which component holds the programs that are running at this moment?
parts.hint: It is the memory that is emptied when the power goes off.
parts.explanation: RAM holds the programs and data in use right now; the hard disk keeps them when the machine is off, and ROM holds the start-up instructions.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: The user wants to run several large programs at the same time without the computer slowing down. Which upgrade would help most?
parts.hint: Which part runs out of room when many programs are open?
parts.explanation: Running many programs at once fills the RAM, so adding more RAM is the upgrade that helps. The other three change what the user sees or hears, not the speed.

parts.label: g
parts.prompt: State two things the processor does in a computer.
parts.rubric: 1 mark each, to a maximum of 2: carries out the instructions of a program; performs arithmetic and logical operations on data; controls and coordinates the other parts of the computer; fetches, decodes and executes instructions in turn.

grade9-ict.intro: A school sends the same letter to the parents of three pupils. The list of names is stored in one file and the letter in another.

stimulus.html:
TitleSurnameClass
1TitleSurnameClass
2MrRamdin9A
3MissCoret9B
4MrsPayen9C
Dear «Title» «Surname»,

Your child in class «Class» is invited to the prize-giving on Friday.

Yours sincerely,
The Rector
stimulus.altText: A table of titles, surnames and classes, and below it a letter whose greeting and first sentence contain field names written between chevrons.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The file holding the titles, surnames and classes is called the:
parts.hint: It is the file the values are taken from.
parts.explanation: The list of names and classes is the data source; the letter itself is the main document.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write the words that will appear in place of «Title» and «Surname» in the letter sent to the parent of the pupil in class 9B.
parts.hint: Find the row of the table whose class is 9B.
parts.explanation: The 9B row holds Miss and Coret, so that letter begins "Dear Miss Coret,".

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: How many letters will be produced when the merge is completed?
parts.hint: Count the rows of data, not the heading row.
parts.explanation: There are three rows of data below the heading row, so three letters are produced - one for each row.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Name the part of a mail merge that holds the text repeated in every letter.
parts.hint: It is the other of the two files.
parts.explanation: The main document holds the wording that is the same in every letter, together with the merge fields.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: In the main document a merge field is shown as:

options: a red wavy underline below it
a page break above the line

parts.hint: Look at how Title, Surname and Class are printed in the letter.
parts.explanation: A merge field is printed as the field name between chevrons, for example «Surname», and is replaced by the value from the data source.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: Give two advantages of using mail merge instead of typing each letter separately.
parts.rubric: 1 mark each, to a maximum of 2: it is much faster for a large number of letters; the wording cannot be typed differently by mistake from one letter to the next; a correction has to be made in one place only; the same list can be reused for another letter.

grade9-ict.intro: A pupil has written a long project and wants the word processor to build the contents page for it.

stimulus.html:
Introduction1
Method3
Results7
Conclusion11
stimulus.altText: A contents list of four section names, each with a page number beside it.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
The four steps below are in the wrong order. Write 1, 2, 3 or 4 against each one to show the correct order.
(i) Click at the place where the contents are to appear.
(ii) Apply heading styles to each section heading.
(iii) Choose Table of Contents from the References tab.
(iv) Update the table after the text has been changed.
parts.hint: The word processor can only find headings that have already been marked as headings.
parts.explanation: The headings must be styled first, then the cursor is placed, then the table is inserted, and it is updated last - so (ii) is 1, (i) is 2, (iii) is 3 and (iv) is 4.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: An automatic table of contents can be built because the headings carry:
parts.hint: The word processor has to be able to recognise a heading.
parts.explanation: Heading styles mark which lines are headings, and the word processor collects exactly those lines into the table of contents.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The page numbers in an automatic table of contents are:

options: worked out by the word processor
typed in by the user each time
the same number on every page
response.answer: worked out by the word processor

parts.hint: That is why the table has to be updated.
parts.explanation: The word processor works the page numbers out itself, which is why the table must be updated after the text changes.

grade9-ict.intro: The print settings below were chosen before a document was sent to the printer.

stimulus.html:
Print
PrinterHP LaserJet 1020
Copies3
Pages2 - 5
OrientationPortrait
Print on both sidesOff
stimulus.altText: A print dialog listing the printer, the number of copies, the range of pages, the orientation and whether both sides of the sheet are used.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many copies will be printed?
parts.hint: Read the row labelled Copies.
parts.explanation: The Copies box is set to 3.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How many pages are printed in each copy?
parts.hint: Count both ends of the range.
parts.explanation: Pages 2 to 5 is four pages - 2, 3, 4 and 5.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: How many sheets of paper are used altogether?
parts.hint: Multiply the pages in one copy by the number of copies.
parts.explanation: 4 pages × 3 copies = 12 sheets, because printing on both sides is switched off.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: The orientation shown prints each page:

options: on both sides of a sheet

parts.hint: Portrait is the way a face is usually painted.
parts.explanation: Portrait orientation makes the page taller than it is wide; landscape is the other way round.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Name the setting that would print on both sides of each sheet.
parts.hint: It is the last row of the panel.
parts.explanation: Printing on both sides of a sheet is called duplex printing; here it is switched off.

grade9-ict.intro: The spreadsheet below is used to work out the cost of the stationery bought for a class.

stimulus.html:
ABCD
1ItemPriceQtyTotal
2Exercise book254
3Pen156
4Ruler202
5Total
stimulus.altText: A spreadsheet with lettered columns and numbered rows holding an item name, a price and a quantity on each of three rows, and an empty Total column.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the formula that should be typed in cell D2 to work out the total cost of the exercise books.
parts.hint: A formula begins with an equals sign.
parts.explanation: The total is the price multiplied by the quantity, so the formula is =B2*C2.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write the formula that should be typed in cell D3.
parts.hint: It is the same formula one row further down.
parts.explanation: On row 3 the price is in B3 and the quantity in C3, so the formula is =B3*C3.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Write the formula that should be typed in cell D5 to add the three totals together.
parts.hint: A range is written with a colon between the two ends.
parts.explanation: =SUM(D2:D4) adds every cell from D2 through to D4. Writing =D2+D3+D4 gives the same answer.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: What value will appear in cell D4?
parts.hint: Multiply the price of a ruler by how many were bought.
parts.explanation: Two rulers at 20 each give 20 × 2 = 40.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: The formula in D2 is copied down into D3. The references B2 and C2 become B3 and C3. This is called:
parts.hint: The references move with the formula.
parts.explanation: A relative reference changes as the formula is copied, so a formula written once can be reused down a whole column.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: Write the cell reference of the cell holding the price of a pen.
parts.hint: Give the column letter first, then the row number.
parts.explanation: The pen is on row 3 and the prices are in column B, so the reference is B3.

parts.label: g
parts.prompt: Explain why a formula is used in D5 rather than typing the answer in.
parts.rubric: 1 mark each, to a maximum of 2: the total is worked out again by itself whenever a price or a quantity is changed; it removes the risk of an arithmetic mistake; the same formula can be copied and reused elsewhere.

grade9-ict.intro: The spreadsheet below holds the test marks of five pupils.

stimulus.html:
AB
1PupilMark
2Anil72
3Bibi55
4Chan88
5Devi41
6Emma64
stimulus.altText: A spreadsheet with a column of five pupil names and a column of the mark each of them scored.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the function that finds the highest mark in the range B2:B6.
parts.hint: Its name is the first three letters of the word maximum.
parts.explanation: =MAX(B2:B6) returns the largest value in the range, which is 88.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write the function that finds the average mark of the five pupils.
parts.hint: It adds the values and divides by how many there are.
parts.explanation: =AVERAGE(B2:B6) gives (72 + 55 + 88 + 41 + 64) ÷ 5 = 64.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: What value is returned by =MIN(B2:B6)?
parts.hint: Look for the smallest mark in the column.
parts.explanation: MIN returns the smallest value in the range, which is Devi’s 41.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: What value is returned by =COUNT(B2:B6)?
parts.hint: COUNT counts how many cells hold a number.
parts.explanation: Five cells in B2:B6 hold a number, so COUNT returns 5. It counts the marks, it does not add them.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: What value is returned by =COUNTIF(B2:B6,">60")?
parts.hint: Count only the marks above sixty.
parts.explanation: The marks above 60 are 72, 88 and 64, so COUNTIF returns 3.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: Every function typed into a cell must begin with:
parts.hint: Without it the entry is stored as ordinary text.
parts.explanation: A function begins with an equals sign; without it the spreadsheet stores what was typed as text.

parts.label: g
parts.prompt: The part written inside the brackets of a function is called the:
parts.hint: It is what the function is given to work on.
parts.explanation: The value or range inside the brackets is the argument - what the function is asked to work on.

grade9-ict.intro: The chart below was drawn from a spreadsheet holding the number of pupils in four classes.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Name the topology marked P and the topology marked Q.
parts.hint: One is named after a shape in the sky and one after a single shared line.
parts.explanation: P is a star topology, because every computer runs its own cable to one central point. Q is a bus topology, because all the computers share one main cable.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: In topology P, every computer is connected to a central:
parts.hint: It is the box drawn in the middle of the star.
parts.explanation: A star topology joins every computer to a central switch (or hub), which passes the data on to the right machine.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: In topology Q, a break in the main cable will:

options: affect only one computer on it
make the network run much faster
have no effect on the network

parts.hint: Every computer shares that one cable.
parts.explanation: All the traffic in a bus network travels along the one main cable, so a break in it cuts the whole network.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Name the device that joins a school network to the Internet.
parts.hint: It directs traffic between two different networks.
parts.explanation: A router joins one network to another and directs the traffic between them, so it is what connects a school network to the Internet.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: A network covering the computers in a single building is a:
parts.hint: Local means nearby.
parts.explanation: A Local Area Network covers one building or one site; a WAN spans towns or countries.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: Give two advantages of connecting the computers in a school in a network.
parts.rubric: 1 mark each, to a maximum of 2: hardware such as a printer can be shared; files can be shared between users; software can be installed and updated from one place; users can send messages to each other; access to data can be controlled centrally; work can be backed up centrally.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which one of these does Mrs Appadu need in order to use Internet banking?
parts.hint: The clue is in the name of the service.
parts.explanation: Internet banking needs a device and a connection to the Internet; none of the other three is required.

parts.prompt:
Before she can sign in, the bank asks for two things.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The padlock symbol and the letters https in the address bar show that the connection is:
parts.hint: The extra letter s stands for secure.
parts.explanation: https means the data travelling between the phone and the bank is encrypted, so it cannot be read if it is intercepted.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A one-time code is sent to her phone before the payment is accepted. This adds:

options: a discount on the amount paid
more storage space on the phone
a faster connection to the bank

parts.explanation: The code is a second factor: a thief who knew the password would still need the phone as well.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: She pays three bills of Rs 450, Rs 620 and Rs 930. What total amount leaves her account?
parts.hint: Add the three amounts together.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: Give one advantage and one drawback of paying bills over the Internet.

parts.prompt: Write the Python keyword that begins the loop in this program.
parts.hint: It is the first word on the second line.
parts.explanation: The keyword for begins a loop that repeats once for each value in a range.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Write the name of the variable that holds the running total.
parts.hint: It is the name given a value on the first line.
parts.explanation: The variable total starts at 0 and has each number added to it in turn.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Complete the missing word so that the line displays HELLO on the screen: ………("HELLO")
parts.hint: The same word is used on the last line of the program above.
parts.explanation: print("HELLO") displays the word HELLO on the screen.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: In Python, the symbol = is used to:

options: give a value to a variable
mark the end of the program
print one line onto the screen
response.answer: give a value to a variable

parts.hint: A double equals sign is used for the other job.
parts.explanation: A single = stores a value in a variable; == is what tests whether two values are equal.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: The call range(1, 5) produces the numbers:
parts.hint: The second number says where to stop, and is not itself included.
parts.explanation: range(1, 5) starts at 1 and stops before 5, so it gives 1, 2, 3 and 4.

grade9-ict.question: A computer network is:
options: a single computer with two monitors
a program for browsing the internet
two or more computers connected together to share resources and communicate
grade9-ict.answer: two or more computers connected together to share resources and communicate
acceptableAnswers: two or more computers connected together to share resources and communicate
grade9-ict.hint: At least two computers must be connected.
grade9-ict.explanation: A network consists of two or more connected devices that can share data, software and hardware resources.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is an advantage of connecting computers in a network?
options: Hardware such as printers can be shared between users
Each user must buy their own copy of every program
Each computer works more slowly on a network
Data cannot be transferred between computers
grade9-ict.answer: Hardware such as printers can be shared between users
acceptableAnswers: Hardware such as printers can be shared between users
grade9-ict.hint: Sharing is the key benefit.
grade9-ict.explanation: One printer can serve every computer on the network, reducing costs and the number of devices needed.

grade9-ict.question: A disadvantage of networking computers is that:
options: a virus on one computer can spread to others on the network
all computers must run the same application at the same time
network computers cannot be switched off
every computer must have a colour printer
grade9-ict.answer: a virus on one computer can spread to others on the network
acceptableAnswers: a virus on one computer can spread to others on the network
grade9-ict.hint: Connected computers share risks.
grade9-ict.explanation: Once a virus infects one machine on a network, it can spread to every connected computer, making security more critical.

grade9-ict.question: In a client-server network, the server is:
options: any wireless device on the network
the computer of the network administrator
a powerful computer that provides services and resources to the client computers
any computer connected to the internet
grade9-ict.answer: a powerful computer that provides services and resources to the client computers
acceptableAnswers: a powerful computer that provides services and resources to the client computers
grade9-ict.hint: It serves the other machines.
grade9-ict.explanation: The server is a dedicated, powerful machine that stores files, manages accounts and provides shared resources to client computers.

grade9-ict.question: In a peer-to-peer (P2P) network:
options: one computer controls all the others
all data is stored on a central server
all computers have equal status and can share resources with each other
only one computer can access the internet at a time
grade9-ict.answer: all computers have equal status and can share resources with each other
acceptableAnswers: all computers have equal status and can share resources with each other
grade9-ict.hint: No hierarchy — each computer is both a client and a server.
grade9-ict.explanation: In a P2P network, every computer can act as both a client (requesting resources) and a server (providing them) without a central server.

grade9-ict.question: Bandwidth in a network refers to:
options: the number of computers on the network
the distance between two network devices
the physical width of the network cable
the maximum amount of data that can be transmitted per second
grade9-ict.answer: the maximum amount of data that can be transmitted per second
acceptableAnswers: the maximum amount of data that can be transmitted per second
grade9-ict.hint: It is like the width of a pipe — wider means more water.
grade9-ict.explanation: Bandwidth is the maximum data transfer rate of a network, measured in bits per second (bps, Mbps, Gbps).

grade9-ict.question: Latency in a network is:
options: the speed at which data is encrypted
the maximum number of users allowed on the network
the cost of the network hardware
the delay between sending a signal and receiving it
grade9-ict.answer: the delay between sending a signal and receiving it
acceptableAnswers: the delay between sending a signal and receiving it
grade9-ict.hint: It is the lag in the network.
grade9-ict.explanation: Latency is the time it takes for data to travel from the sender to the receiver; low latency is important for real-time applications like video calls.

grade9-ict.question: A network protocol is:
options: a set of rules that govern how data is transmitted between devices on a network
a program for filtering spam emails
the physical layout of the network
grade9-ict.answer: a set of rules that govern how data is transmitted between devices on a network
acceptableAnswers: a set of rules that govern how data is transmitted between devices on a network
grade9-ict.hint: Rules for communication.
grade9-ict.explanation: A protocol is an agreed set of rules that all devices follow to communicate, ensuring that data is sent, received and understood correctly.

grade9-ict.question: The most common protocol used to transmit data over the internet is:
grade9-ict.answer: TCP/IP
grade9-ict.hint: Every device connected to the internet uses this.
grade9-ict.explanation: TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) is the fundamental communication protocol of the internet.

grade9-ict.question: An IP address is used to:
options: uniquely identify a device on a network so data can be routed to it
set the speed of the network
store the password for a Wi-Fi network
determine the physical size of the network
grade9-ict.answer: uniquely identify a device on a network so data can be routed to it
acceptableAnswers: uniquely identify a device on a network so data can be routed to it
grade9-ict.hint: Like a postal address for a computer.
grade9-ict.explanation: An IP address is a unique numerical label assigned to each device, enabling routers to direct data to the correct destination.

grade9-ict.question: LAN stands for:
grade9-ict.answer: Local Area Network
grade9-ict.hint: The first word describes how much area it covers.
grade9-ict.explanation: A Local Area Network (LAN) covers a small geographic area, such as a single building or campus.

grade9-ict.question: WAN stands for:
grade9-ict.answer: Wide Area Network
grade9-ict.hint: It covers a wide geographic area.
grade9-ict.explanation: A Wide Area Network (WAN) spans large geographic areas, connecting networks in different cities or countries. The internet is the largest WAN.

grade9-ict.question: A MAN (Metropolitan Area Network) covers:
options: a city or large campus, larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN
grade9-ict.answer: a city or large campus, larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN
acceptableAnswers: a city or large campus, larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN
grade9-ict.hint: It is city-sized.
grade9-ict.explanation: A MAN covers a metropolitan area such as a city, connecting multiple buildings or campuses — larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN.

grade9-ict.question: A PAN (Personal Area Network) typically covers:
options: a very short range, such as within a few metres of a person
grade9-ict.answer: a very short range, such as within a few metres of a person
acceptableAnswers: a very short range, such as within a few metres of a person
grade9-ict.hint: It is for your personal devices only.
grade9-ict.explanation: A PAN covers the area immediately surrounding one person, typically connecting personal devices such as a phone, laptop and headset via Bluetooth.

grade9-ict.question: Which type of network connects the computers in a single school laboratory?
grade9-ict.answer: LAN
grade9-ict.hint: One room in one building.
grade9-ict.explanation: A single laboratory is a small, localised area, so the network connecting its computers is a Local Area Network (LAN).

grade9-ict.question: A VPN (Virtual Private Network) creates:
options: a secure, encrypted connection over a public network such as the internet
a physical private cable between two offices
a new type of wireless signal
grade9-ict.answer: a secure, encrypted connection over a public network such as the internet
acceptableAnswers: a secure, encrypted connection over a public network such as the internet
grade9-ict.hint: Private inside the public internet.
grade9-ict.explanation: A VPN encrypts data and tunnels it through the public internet so it is as secure as if the two ends were connected by a private cable.

grade9-ict.question: The internet is best described as:
options: a single large computer in a data centre
a wireless LAN covering one country
a global wide area network of interconnected networks
grade9-ict.answer: a global wide area network of interconnected networks
acceptableAnswers: a global wide area network of interconnected networks
grade9-ict.hint: It connects millions of networks worldwide.
grade9-ict.explanation: The internet is a global system of interconnected computer networks, forming the largest WAN in existence.

grade9-ict.question: Which network type is most commonly used by a business with offices in different countries?
grade9-ict.answer: WAN
grade9-ict.hint: Country-to-country needs a wide area connection.
grade9-ict.explanation: A WAN connects geographically dispersed sites — such as international offices — over long distances using leased lines, the internet or satellite links.

grade9-ict.question: WLAN stands for:
grade9-ict.answer: Wireless Local Area Network
grade9-ict.hint: A LAN that uses radio waves instead of cables.
grade9-ict.explanation: A WLAN is a Local Area Network that uses Wi-Fi (radio waves) instead of physical cables to connect devices.

grade9-ict.question: Bluetooth is typically used to create which type of network?
grade9-ict.answer: PAN
grade9-ict.hint: Bluetooth connects personal devices over a very short range.
grade9-ict.explanation: Bluetooth is the technology most commonly used for Personal Area Networks (PANs), connecting devices within a few metres of each other.

grade9-ict.question: The main advantage of a WAN over a LAN is that a WAN:
options: is cheaper to build than a LAN
can connect devices and networks that are geographically far apart
is always faster than a LAN
requires no hardware to set up
grade9-ict.answer: can connect devices and networks that are geographically far apart
acceptableAnswers: can connect devices and networks that are geographically far apart
grade9-ict.hint: Distance is the defining feature of a WAN.
grade9-ict.explanation: A WAN covers large distances, enabling communication between offices, cities or countries that a LAN could never reach.

grade9-ict.question: Network topology refers to:
options: the number of users on the network
the speed of the network connection
the physical or logical arrangement of devices on a network
the brand of network cable used
grade9-ict.answer: the physical or logical arrangement of devices on a network
acceptableAnswers: the physical or logical arrangement of devices on a network
grade9-ict.hint: It is the layout or shape of the network.
grade9-ict.explanation: Topology describes how the nodes and links of a network are arranged relative to each other.

grade9-ict.question: In a star topology, every computer is connected to:
grade9-ict.answer: a central switch or hub
grade9-ict.hint: All cables meet at one central point.
grade9-ict.explanation: In a star topology, each device has its own cable running to a central switch or hub that manages all communication.

grade9-ict.question: The advantage of a star topology over a bus topology is that in a star topology:
options: all computers share one cable, making it cheaper
a fault in one cable only affects that one computer, not the whole network
grade9-ict.answer: a fault in one cable only affects that one computer, not the whole network
acceptableAnswers: a fault in one cable only affects that one computer, not the whole network
grade9-ict.hint: One broken cable does not break everything.
grade9-ict.explanation: In a star, each device has its own cable, so a cable fault isolates only that device. In a bus, a cable break stops the whole network.

grade9-ict.question: In a bus topology, all computers are connected to:
grade9-ict.answer: one main cable (the backbone)
grade9-ict.hint: One shared cable for everyone.
grade9-ict.explanation: A bus topology uses a single shared cable along which all devices are connected at different points.

grade9-ict.question: A disadvantage of bus topology is:
options: each computer must have its own switch
a break anywhere in the main cable stops all communication on the network
it requires the most cable of any topology
grade9-ict.answer: a break anywhere in the main cable stops all communication on the network
acceptableAnswers: a break anywhere in the main cable stops all communication on the network
grade9-ict.hint: Everybody shares one cable.
grade9-ict.explanation: Because every device depends on the same backbone cable, a single cable fault brings the entire bus network down.

grade9-ict.question: In a ring topology, data travels:
options: along a single main cable to all devices at once
in one direction around the ring, passing through each device in turn
through a central hub to its destination
from any device directly to any other device
grade9-ict.answer: in one direction around the ring, passing through each device in turn
acceptableAnswers: in one direction around the ring, passing through each device in turn
grade9-ict.hint: Think of a roundabout — traffic flows in one direction.
grade9-ict.explanation: In a ring topology, data packets are passed from one device to the next around the ring until they reach the intended recipient.

grade9-ict.question: In a mesh topology, each device is connected to:
options: only the device next to it
every other device in the network, giving multiple paths for data
grade9-ict.answer: every other device in the network, giving multiple paths for data
acceptableAnswers: every other device in the network, giving multiple paths for data
grade9-ict.hint: Many connections, many routes.
grade9-ict.explanation: A full mesh topology connects every node to every other node, providing many redundant paths so the network continues working even if several links fail.

grade9-ict.question: The main disadvantage of a star topology is that:
options: if the central switch fails, the whole network goes down
it is impossible to add new computers
each computer must connect to every other computer
it uses no cables at all
grade9-ict.answer: if the central switch fails, the whole network goes down
acceptableAnswers: if the central switch fails, the whole network goes down
grade9-ict.hint: The switch is a single point of failure.
grade9-ict.explanation: In a star topology, all communication passes through the central switch; if it fails, every device loses its connection.

grade9-ict.question: A hybrid topology is:
options: a topology that uses only wireless connections
a ring network with no central device
a combination of two or more different topologies within one network
a bus topology with a wireless extension
grade9-ict.answer: a combination of two or more different topologies within one network
acceptableAnswers: a combination of two or more different topologies within one network
grade9-ict.hint: Mix and match.
grade9-ict.explanation: A hybrid topology combines two or more basic topologies — for example, a star-bus or star-ring — to take advantage of the strengths of each.

grade9-ict.question: Which topology is most commonly used in modern office LANs?
grade9-ict.answer: Star
grade9-ict.hint: Most networks use a central switch.
grade9-ict.explanation: Star topology is the most widely used in modern LANs because it is easy to manage, faults are isolated to individual links, and it is straightforward to expand.

grade9-ict.question: A router is a network device that:
options: stores shared files for all network users
amplifies the signal on a cable
connects two or more networks and forwards data between them
grade9-ict.answer: connects two or more networks and forwards data between them
acceptableAnswers: connects two or more networks and forwards data between them
grade9-ict.hint: It routes traffic between networks.
grade9-ict.explanation: A router reads each packet's destination address and forwards it along the best available path between networks.

grade9-ict.question: A switch is a network device that:
options: connects devices within a LAN and forwards data only to the intended destination device
amplifies and extends a network signal
provides wireless access to the internet
grade9-ict.answer: connects devices within a LAN and forwards data only to the intended destination device
acceptableAnswers: connects devices within a LAN and forwards data only to the intended destination device
grade9-ict.hint: It is smarter than a hub.
grade9-ict.explanation: A switch forwards each data frame only to the specific port where the destination device is connected, unlike a hub which broadcasts to all ports.

grade9-ict.question: A hub differs from a switch because a hub:
options: sends data to all connected devices regardless of the intended recipient
sends data only to the intended device
grade9-ict.answer: sends data to all connected devices regardless of the intended recipient
acceptableAnswers: sends data to all connected devices regardless of the intended recipient
grade9-ict.hint: A hub broadcasts; a switch targets.
grade9-ict.explanation: A hub broadcasts every data frame to all connected ports, wasting bandwidth; a switch learns which device is on which port and sends data only where needed.

grade9-ict.question: A Network Interface Card (NIC) is:
options: a hardware component that allows a computer to connect to a network
a device that boosts the Wi-Fi signal
a program that monitors network traffic
grade9-ict.answer: a hardware component that allows a computer to connect to a network
acceptableAnswers: a hardware component that allows a computer to connect to a network
grade9-ict.hint: Every networked computer has one.
grade9-ict.explanation: A NIC is the physical adapter inside (or attached to) a computer that provides the electrical or wireless interface to the network.

grade9-ict.question: A wireless access point (WAP) is used to:
options: store backup copies of network data
allow wireless devices to connect to a wired LAN
grade9-ict.answer: allow wireless devices to connect to a wired LAN
acceptableAnswers: allow wireless devices to connect to a wired LAN
grade9-ict.hint: It bridges wireless and wired networks.
grade9-ict.explanation: A WAP provides a Wi-Fi connection for wireless devices and bridges them to the wired network infrastructure.

grade9-ict.question: A modem is a device that:
options: stores shared files for a LAN
converts digital computer signals to signals suitable for transmission over a telephone line, and vice versa
amplifies the Wi-Fi signal across a large building
provides a firewall between the LAN and the internet
grade9-ict.answer: converts digital computer signals to signals suitable for transmission over a telephone line, and vice versa
acceptableAnswers: converts digital computer signals to signals suitable for transmission over a telephone line, and vice versa
grade9-ict.hint: Modem = MOdulator-DEModulator.
grade9-ict.explanation: A modem modulates digital data into analogue signals for transmission and demodulates incoming signals back into digital data.

grade9-ict.question: A repeater in a network is used to:
options: regenerate and amplify a signal so it can travel further
grade9-ict.answer: regenerate and amplify a signal so it can travel further
acceptableAnswers: regenerate and amplify a signal so it can travel further
grade9-ict.hint: Signals weaken over distance.
grade9-ict.explanation: A repeater receives a weakened signal and re-transmits it at full strength, extending the effective range of the network.

grade9-ict.question: A network cable made of glass or plastic that transmits data as pulses of light is called:
grade9-ict.answer: fibre optic cable
grade9-ict.hint: Light, not electricity.
grade9-ict.explanation: Fibre optic cables carry data as pulses of light, offering very high bandwidth and immunity to electrical interference.

grade9-ict.question: The MAC address of a network device is:
options: the wireless frequency of the device
the IP address assigned by the router
the serial number of the computer
a unique physical address assigned to its network interface card by the manufacturer
grade9-ict.answer: a unique physical address assigned to its network interface card by the manufacturer
acceptableAnswers: a unique physical address assigned to its network interface card by the manufacturer
grade9-ict.hint: It is built in at the factory.
grade9-ict.explanation: A MAC (Media Access Control) address is a unique 48-bit hardware identifier permanently assigned to a NIC by its manufacturer.

grade9-ict.question: An Internet Service Provider (ISP) is:
options: a program that measures network speed
a government department that controls internet content
a company that provides access to the internet for a fee
grade9-ict.answer: a company that provides access to the internet for a fee
acceptableAnswers: a company that provides access to the internet for a fee
grade9-ict.hint: They sell the internet connection.
grade9-ict.explanation: An ISP (such as a telecoms company) sells internet connectivity services to homes, schools and businesses.

grade9-ict.question: One advantage of a wired network connection over a wireless one is that it:
options: allows users to move freely around the building
can connect more devices than Wi-Fi
is generally faster and more reliable with less interference
grade9-ict.answer: is generally faster and more reliable with less interference
acceptableAnswers: is generally faster and more reliable with less interference
grade9-ict.hint: Cables provide a dedicated, stable path.
grade9-ict.explanation: A wired Ethernet connection provides a dedicated channel with no radio interference, giving more consistent speeds and reliability than Wi-Fi.

grade9-ict.question: One advantage of a wireless (Wi-Fi) network over a wired one is:
options: users can move around freely and connect without cables
it is always faster than wired connections
it is more secure than wired connections
it requires no access point or router
grade9-ict.answer: users can move around freely and connect without cables
acceptableAnswers: users can move around freely and connect without cables
grade9-ict.hint: No cable means mobility.
grade9-ict.explanation: Wi-Fi allows devices such as laptops and phones to connect from anywhere within range without the constraint of a physical cable.

grade9-ict.question: Wi-Fi uses which type of signal to transmit data?
options: Electrical pulses in a copper wire
grade9-ict.answer: Radio waves
grade9-ict.hint: It is a form of wireless radio communication.
grade9-ict.explanation: Wi-Fi transmits data using radio frequency waves, typically in the 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz bands.

grade9-ict.question: An SSID is:
options: the name of a Wi-Fi network that devices see when they search for networks
the frequency band used by the network
the password used to join a Wi-Fi network
the IP address of the wireless router
grade9-ict.answer: the name of a Wi-Fi network that devices see when they search for networks
acceptableAnswers: the name of a Wi-Fi network that devices see when they search for networks
grade9-ict.hint: It is what you see in the list of available Wi-Fi networks.
grade9-ict.explanation: SSID (Service Set Identifier) is the human-readable name assigned to a Wi-Fi network, displayed to users when they scan for networks.

grade9-ict.question: WPA2 is a:
options: security protocol used to protect wireless network communication
grade9-ict.answer: security protocol used to protect wireless network communication
acceptableAnswers: security protocol used to protect wireless network communication
grade9-ict.hint: It encrypts Wi-Fi traffic.
grade9-ict.explanation: WPA2 (Wi-Fi Protected Access 2) encrypts data transmitted over a Wi-Fi network, protecting it from unauthorised interception.

grade9-ict.question: One security risk of an open (unsecured) Wi-Fi network is:
options: anyone within range can connect and potentially intercept data
all devices must use the same password
the network runs faster than it should
grade9-ict.answer: anyone within range can connect and potentially intercept data
acceptableAnswers: anyone within range can connect and potentially intercept data
grade9-ict.hint: No password, no protection.
grade9-ict.explanation: An open Wi-Fi network has no encryption or password, so anyone nearby can connect and eavesdrop on unencrypted traffic.

grade9-ict.question: The twisted pair cable most commonly used in wired Ethernet LANs is:
grade9-ict.answer: Cat5e or Cat6 UTP cable
grade9-ict.hint: UTP stands for Unshielded Twisted Pair.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cat5e and Cat6 UTP (Unshielded Twisted Pair) cables are the standard wired connections in Ethernet LANs, supporting speeds of 100 Mbps to 10 Gbps.

grade9-ict.question: Which standard connector is used at each end of a UTP Ethernet cable?
grade9-ict.answer: RJ-45
grade9-ict.hint: It looks like a wide telephone plug.
grade9-ict.explanation: RJ-45 is the 8-pin connector used on Ethernet cables to plug into network switches, routers and computers.

grade9-ict.question: The signal range of a typical 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network indoors is approximately:
grade9-ict.answer: 30 to 50 metres
grade9-ict.hint: Walls reduce the range considerably.
grade9-ict.explanation: A 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi signal typically reaches 30–50 metres indoors before it weakens too much; walls and interference reduce this further.

grade9-ict.question: The 5 GHz Wi-Fi band compared to 2.4 GHz offers:
options: faster speeds but a shorter range
slower speeds but a longer range
grade9-ict.answer: faster speeds but a shorter range
acceptableAnswers: faster speeds but a shorter range
grade9-ict.hint: Higher frequency = faster but shorter.
grade9-ict.explanation: The 5 GHz band provides higher bandwidth and less interference than 2.4 GHz but has a shorter effective range because higher frequencies are absorbed more quickly by obstacles.

grade9-ict.question: An intranet is:
options: a network that only allows email
a private network within an organisation that uses internet technologies but is not publicly accessible
grade9-ict.answer: a private network within an organisation that uses internet technologies but is not publicly accessible
acceptableAnswers: a private network within an organisation that uses internet technologies but is not publicly accessible
grade9-ict.hint: Like the internet but private.
grade9-ict.explanation: An intranet uses web technologies (browsers, pages, servers) but is restricted to authorised users within the organisation.

grade9-ict.question: An extranet is:
options: a backup of the company's intranet
the public internet restricted to one country
an extension of an organisation's intranet that allows authorised external parties such as suppliers to access certain parts of it
a wireless network for customers only
grade9-ict.answer: an extension of an organisation's intranet that allows authorised external parties such as suppliers to access certain parts of it
acceptableAnswers: an extension of an organisation's intranet that allows authorised external parties such as suppliers to access certain parts of it
grade9-ict.hint: Intranet extended outward to selected partners.
grade9-ict.explanation: An extranet gives controlled access to selected parts of an intranet to trusted external users such as suppliers, customers or business partners.

grade9-ict.question: A school intranet might be used to:
options: allow any member of the public to access school files
replace all physical books in the library
share timetables, notices and learning resources with staff and pupils
grade9-ict.answer: share timetables, notices and learning resources with staff and pupils
acceptableAnswers: share timetables, notices and learning resources with staff and pupils
grade9-ict.hint: It is internal to the school.
grade9-ict.explanation: A school intranet provides a secure internal web portal where staff and students can access timetables, homework, announcements and resources.

grade9-ict.question: What prevents unauthorised users from accessing an intranet from outside the organisation?
options: The physical size of the building
The colour of the cable used
grade9-ict.answer: A firewall and login credentials
grade9-ict.hint: Security controls are needed.
grade9-ict.explanation: A firewall blocks external access, and login authentication ensures only authorised users can connect to the intranet.

grade9-ict.question: The main difference between an intranet and the internet is:
options: an intranet can only send emails
an intranet is private and restricted to one organisation; the internet is public and open to everyone
an intranet is always wireless and the internet is always wired
the internet can only be accessed from a desktop computer
grade9-ict.answer: an intranet is private and restricted to one organisation; the internet is public and open to everyone
acceptableAnswers: an intranet is private and restricted to one organisation; the internet is public and open to everyone
grade9-ict.hint: Private versus public is the key distinction.
grade9-ict.explanation: An intranet is a closed network accessible only to those within the organisation; the internet is a public global network.

grade9-ict.question: A company uses an extranet to allow its suppliers to check stock levels. This is beneficial because:
options: suppliers can see what is needed without phoning or emailing the company
the company's employees can no longer see the stock levels
the data becomes available to the general public
the extranet automatically orders stock when it is low
grade9-ict.answer: suppliers can see what is needed without phoning or emailing the company
acceptableAnswers: suppliers can see what is needed without phoning or emailing the company
grade9-ict.hint: Direct access saves time for both parties.
grade9-ict.explanation: Giving suppliers controlled access to stock data reduces the time spent on phone calls and emails, streamlining the supply chain.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following technologies is typically used to build both intranets and extranets?
options: Web browsers, web servers and HTTP/HTTPS protocols
grade9-ict.answer: Web browsers, web servers and HTTP/HTTPS protocols
acceptableAnswers: Web browsers, web servers and HTTP/HTTPS protocols
grade9-ict.hint: They use the same technology as the public internet.
grade9-ict.explanation: Intranets and extranets use standard web technologies — browsers, HTTP/HTTPS, web servers — but restrict access through authentication and firewalls.

grade9-ict.question: An intranet helps a large organisation by:
options: making all company data available to the press
providing a central place for internal communication, document sharing and collaboration
replacing the internet for all employees
grade9-ict.answer: providing a central place for internal communication, document sharing and collaboration
acceptableAnswers: providing a central place for internal communication, document sharing and collaboration
grade9-ict.hint: It is the company's internal web.
grade9-ict.explanation: An intranet gives employees a shared platform for news, policies, forms, project documents and internal communication.

grade9-ict.question: An extranet improves upon a simple intranet by:
options: giving every person in the world an account
making all data publicly available on the internet
allowing selective access to trusted outside parties without exposing the whole internal network
grade9-ict.answer: allowing selective access to trusted outside parties without exposing the whole internal network
acceptableAnswers: allowing selective access to trusted outside parties without exposing the whole internal network
grade9-ict.hint: Controlled external access is what makes it an extranet.
grade9-ict.explanation: An extranet extends intranet access to specific external users with their own login credentials, without making the whole intranet public.

grade9-ict.question: A hospital uses an extranet to allow a patient's GP to view test results. This is an example of:
options: giving a trusted external partner controlled access to specific internal data
connecting two hospitals with a LAN
making medical records available to the public
grade9-ict.answer: giving a trusted external partner controlled access to specific internal data
acceptableAnswers: giving a trusted external partner controlled access to specific internal data
grade9-ict.hint: The GP is an external but trusted party.
grade9-ict.explanation: The hospital extranet lets the GP access specific patient data securely without being a hospital employee or gaining access to the full internal system.

grade9-ict.question: The World Wide Web (WWW) is:
options: the same thing as the internet
a system of interlinked web pages accessed via the internet using a browser
grade9-ict.answer: a system of interlinked web pages accessed via the internet using a browser
acceptableAnswers: a system of interlinked web pages accessed via the internet using a browser
grade9-ict.hint: The web is one service that runs on the internet.
grade9-ict.explanation: The World Wide Web is a collection of web pages and sites connected by hyperlinks, hosted on servers and accessed via a web browser over the internet.

grade9-ict.question: HTTP stands for:
grade9-ict.answer: HyperText Transfer Protocol
grade9-ict.hint: It is the protocol for transmitting web pages.
grade9-ict.explanation: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) defines how web pages are requested by browsers and delivered by web servers.

grade9-ict.question: HTTPS differs from HTTP because HTTPS:
options: is faster but less secure than HTTP
can only be used for email
encrypts the data exchanged between the browser and the web server
grade9-ict.answer: encrypts the data exchanged between the browser and the web server
acceptableAnswers: encrypts the data exchanged between the browser and the web server
grade9-ict.hint: The S stands for Secure.
grade9-ict.explanation: HTTPS uses SSL/TLS encryption to secure the connection, protecting data in transit from interception.

grade9-ict.question: A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is:
options: the name of the web browser
the unique web address used to locate a specific resource on the internet
grade9-ict.answer: the unique web address used to locate a specific resource on the internet
acceptableAnswers: the unique web address used to locate a specific resource on the internet
grade9-ict.hint: It is what you type in the address bar.
grade9-ict.explanation: A URL is the complete address of a resource on the web, including the protocol (https://), the domain name and the path.

grade9-ict.question: DNS (Domain Name System) converts:
options: images into text for faster loading
web pages into audio for visually impaired users
human-readable domain names like www.school.mu into IP addresses computers can use
grade9-ict.answer: human-readable domain names like www.school.mu into IP addresses computers can use
acceptableAnswers: human-readable domain names like www.school.mu into IP addresses computers can use
grade9-ict.hint: It is the internet's phone book.
grade9-ict.explanation: DNS translates domain names into the numerical IP addresses needed to route traffic to the correct server.

grade9-ict.question: A web server is a computer that:
options: connects the LAN to the telephone network
stores only the images used on websites
is used by one person to browse the internet
stores and delivers web pages to browsers on request
grade9-ict.answer: stores and delivers web pages to browsers on request
acceptableAnswers: stores and delivers web pages to browsers on request
grade9-ict.hint: It serves the pages to your browser.
grade9-ict.explanation: A web server stores website files and responds to HTTP/HTTPS requests by sending the requested pages to the client browser.

grade9-ict.question: A hyperlink on a web page is:
options: a type of image embedded in a page
a menu bar at the top of the browser
a clickable element that takes the user to another page or resource
a form of encryption used on secure sites
grade9-ict.answer: a clickable element that takes the user to another page or resource
acceptableAnswers: a clickable element that takes the user to another page or resource
grade9-ict.hint: Click it and you go somewhere.
grade9-ict.explanation: A hyperlink (link) is a clickable word, phrase or image that navigates the user to another URL when clicked.

grade9-ict.question: The domain extension ".edu" in a web address indicates:
grade9-ict.answer: an educational institution
grade9-ict.hint: edu = education.
grade9-ict.explanation: The .edu top-level domain is used by educational institutions such as schools and universities, mainly in the United States.

grade9-ict.question: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is used to:
options: define the structure and content of web pages
grade9-ict.answer: define the structure and content of web pages
acceptableAnswers: define the structure and content of web pages
grade9-ict.hint: Web pages are written in HTML.
grade9-ict.explanation: HTML is the markup language used to create web pages; it uses tags to define headings, paragraphs, links, images and other elements.

grade9-ict.question: Hosting a website means:
options: designing the visual appearance of the website
registering a domain name for the site
writing the HTML code for each page
storing the website's files on a web server that is connected to the internet
grade9-ict.answer: storing the website's files on a web server that is connected to the internet
acceptableAnswers: storing the website's files on a web server that is connected to the internet
grade9-ict.hint: The files must live on a server permanently.
grade9-ict.explanation: Web hosting provides server space and an internet connection to store website files so they can be accessed by visitors 24 hours a day.

grade9-ict.question: An email address has the format:
grade9-ict.answer: username@domain.extension
grade9-ict.hint: The @ symbol separates the user from the domain.
grade9-ict.explanation: Email addresses follow the format: a local part (username), an @ symbol, and the domain (such as gmail.com).

grade9-ict.question: SMTP is the protocol used to:
options: send email from a client to a mail server, or between mail servers
receive email from a server to a client
grade9-ict.answer: send email from a client to a mail server, or between mail servers
acceptableAnswers: send email from a client to a mail server, or between mail servers
grade9-ict.hint: SMTP = Simple Mail Transfer Protocol — for sending.
grade9-ict.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) handles the sending and routing of email between mail servers.

grade9-ict.question: The CC field in an email is used to:
options: attach a file to the email
set the priority of the message
send a copy of the email to additional recipients who can all see each other's addresses
send a hidden copy that the main recipient cannot see
grade9-ict.answer: send a copy of the email to additional recipients who can all see each other's addresses
acceptableAnswers: send a copy of the email to additional recipients who can all see each other's addresses
grade9-ict.hint: CC = Carbon Copy — visible to all.
grade9-ict.explanation: CC (Carbon Copy) sends a copy to extra recipients; all recipients can see the CC addresses. BCC hides the copy recipient.

grade9-ict.question: The BCC field in an email is used to:
options: send a blind copy to a recipient whose address is hidden from all other recipients
set a read receipt for the email
attach a file to the message
mark the message as high priority
grade9-ict.answer: send a blind copy to a recipient whose address is hidden from all other recipients
acceptableAnswers: send a blind copy to a recipient whose address is hidden from all other recipients
grade9-ict.hint: BCC = Blind Carbon Copy.
grade9-ict.explanation: BCC (Blind Carbon Copy) adds a recipient whose address is invisible to all other recipients, protecting their privacy.

grade9-ict.question: An email attachment is:
options: the subject line of the email
a link within the body of the email
a file sent along with an email message
the email address of the sender
grade9-ict.answer: a file sent along with an email message
acceptableAnswers: a file sent along with an email message
grade9-ict.hint: A document or image sent with the email.
grade9-ict.explanation: An attachment is a file (document, image, spreadsheet, etc.) included with an email message.

grade9-ict.question: Forwarding an email means:
options: sending a received message on to another recipient
deleting the message from the inbox
moving the message to a folder
sending your own reply to the original sender
grade9-ict.answer: sending a received message on to another recipient
acceptableAnswers: sending a received message on to another recipient
grade9-ict.hint: Pass it on to someone else.
grade9-ict.explanation: Forwarding sends a copy of a received email to a new recipient who was not in the original correspondence.

grade9-ict.question: An email signature is:
options: a block of text automatically added to the end of outgoing messages, usually containing contact details
the subject line repeated at the end
a watermark image on the email
a digital certificate that proves the email was not altered in transit
grade9-ict.answer: a block of text automatically added to the end of outgoing messages, usually containing contact details
acceptableAnswers: a block of text automatically added to the end of outgoing messages, usually containing contact details
grade9-ict.hint: It is your auto-added sign-off.
grade9-ict.explanation: An email signature is a personalised block of text — name, title, phone, website — appended automatically to messages.

grade9-ict.question: An advantage of email over sending a printed letter is that email:
options: arrives almost instantly anywhere in the world
grade9-ict.answer: arrives almost instantly anywhere in the world
acceptableAnswers: arrives almost instantly anywhere in the world
grade9-ict.hint: Speed is the biggest advantage.
grade9-ict.explanation: Email is delivered in seconds regardless of the recipient's location, whereas a posted letter may take days or weeks.

grade9-ict.question: A junk mail or spam filter moves suspected spam to:
options: the Junk or Spam folder so the inbox stays uncluttered
grade9-ict.answer: the Junk or Spam folder so the inbox stays uncluttered
acceptableAnswers: the Junk or Spam folder so the inbox stays uncluttered
grade9-ict.hint: Spam goes to a separate folder.
grade9-ict.explanation: Spam filters analyse incoming messages and move those suspected of being unwanted bulk email to a dedicated Junk/Spam folder.

grade9-ict.question: Webmail allows a user to:
options: send email without an internet connection
send email only from one specific computer
send email that is always encrypted
access their email account through a browser from any internet-connected device
grade9-ict.answer: access their email account through a browser from any internet-connected device
acceptableAnswers: access their email account through a browser from any internet-connected device
grade9-ict.hint: No software to install — just a browser.
grade9-ict.explanation: Webmail stores messages on a server and provides access through a browser, so the user can read and send email from any device with internet access.

grade9-ict.question: A web browser is software used to:
options: access and display web pages from the internet
grade9-ict.answer: access and display web pages from the internet
acceptableAnswers: access and display web pages from the internet
grade9-ict.hint: It is what you use to visit websites.
grade9-ict.explanation: A web browser (such as Chrome, Firefox, Edge or Safari) renders web pages by interpreting HTML and displaying the content.

grade9-ict.question: A search engine is used to:
options: find web pages matching keywords entered by the user
grade9-ict.answer: find web pages matching keywords entered by the user
acceptableAnswers: find web pages matching keywords entered by the user
grade9-ict.hint: Type a word and it finds relevant pages.
grade9-ict.explanation: A search engine (such as Google, Bing or Yahoo) indexes billions of web pages and returns a ranked list matching the user's search terms.

grade9-ict.question: The browser's address bar is used to:
options: show the file size of the current page
show the history of pages visited
type a web address (URL) to navigate directly to a site
grade9-ict.answer: type a web address (URL) to navigate directly to a site
acceptableAnswers: type a web address (URL) to navigate directly to a site
