grade9-ict.hint: Type the full URL there.
grade9-ict.explanation: The address bar displays the current URL and allows the user to type any web address to navigate directly to that page.

grade9-ict.question: Browser bookmarks (or favourites) are used to:
options: report a website to the authorities
save the address of a web page for easy return visits
speed up the loading of web pages
grade9-ict.answer: save the address of a web page for easy return visits
acceptableAnswers: save the address of a web page for easy return visits
grade9-ict.hint: Mark a page you want to find again.
grade9-ict.explanation: Bookmarks store a URL so the user can return to a page quickly without having to retype or search for the address.

grade9-ict.question: Browser history shows:
options: the contents of the browser's cache
a list of websites the user has visited recently
grade9-ict.answer: a list of websites the user has visited recently
acceptableAnswers: a list of websites the user has visited recently
grade9-ict.hint: It records where you have been.
grade9-ict.explanation: Browser history is a chronological list of all web pages visited in recent sessions, allowing the user to revisit them easily.

grade9-ict.question: Using quotation marks around a search term (e.g., "World Cup") in a search engine:
options: finds pages containing that exact phrase rather than pages with the words in any order
translates the search into another language
grade9-ict.answer: finds pages containing that exact phrase rather than pages with the words in any order
acceptableAnswers: finds pages containing that exact phrase rather than pages with the words in any order
grade9-ict.hint: Quotes lock in the exact phrase.
grade9-ict.explanation: Enclosing a phrase in quotation marks tells the search engine to find only pages where those words appear together in that exact order.

grade9-ict.question: The browser cache stores:
options: copies of recently visited web pages and resources so they load faster on a repeat visit
grade9-ict.answer: copies of recently visited web pages and resources so they load faster on a repeat visit
acceptableAnswers: copies of recently visited web pages and resources so they load faster on a repeat visit
grade9-ict.hint: Local copies save downloading the same files again.
grade9-ict.explanation: The cache saves web page images, scripts and CSS files locally; on a return visit, the browser loads these from the cache rather than re-downloading them, speeding up the page.

grade9-ict.question: Browsing the web in private or incognito mode means:
options: the browser does not save history, cookies or form data on the device after the session ends
no one on the internet can see what the user is doing
the user is completely anonymous to all websites
grade9-ict.answer: the browser does not save history, cookies or form data on the device after the session ends
acceptableAnswers: the browser does not save history, cookies or form data on the device after the session ends
grade9-ict.hint: Local privacy only — the website and ISP can still see you.
grade9-ict.explanation: Private/incognito mode prevents the browser from saving history, cookies and form data locally, but the user's activity is still visible to the website and ISP.

grade9-ict.question: Evaluating the reliability of information found on a website involves checking:
options: how many images the page contains
the colour scheme and font used
who wrote it, when it was last updated, and whether it cites its sources
grade9-ict.answer: who wrote it, when it was last updated, and whether it cites its sources
acceptableAnswers: who wrote it, when it was last updated, and whether it cites its sources
grade9-ict.hint: Author, date and sources are key signs of reliability.
grade9-ict.explanation: Reliable web information comes from identifiable authors, is current, and supports its claims with references to other trustworthy sources.

grade9-ict.question: A pop-up blocker in a browser is used to:
options: translate web pages into another language
prevent unwanted new windows from opening automatically while browsing
grade9-ict.answer: prevent unwanted new windows from opening automatically while browsing
acceptableAnswers: prevent unwanted new windows from opening automatically while browsing
grade9-ict.hint: It blocks new windows that open without the user asking.
grade9-ict.explanation: A pop-up blocker stops websites from automatically opening new browser windows or tabs, which are often used for advertising or phishing.

grade9-ict.question: E-commerce refers to:
options: buying and selling goods and services over the internet
grade9-ict.answer: buying and selling goods and services over the internet
acceptableAnswers: buying and selling goods and services over the internet
grade9-ict.hint: Electronic commerce.
grade9-ict.explanation: E-commerce covers all commercial transactions conducted online, including retail, business-to-business and consumer-to-consumer sales.

grade9-ict.question: Internet banking allows customers to:
options: open a new account without any personal details
print their bank statements in a branch
manage their bank accounts, make payments and transfer money online
buy shares on the stock market directly
grade9-ict.answer: manage their bank accounts, make payments and transfer money online
acceptableAnswers: manage their bank accounts, make payments and transfer money online
grade9-ict.hint: All your banking, online.
grade9-ict.explanation: Internet banking provides secure online access to account information, balance checks, transfers, bill payments and other banking services.

grade9-ict.question: An advantage of online shopping compared to visiting a physical store is:
options: there is no risk of receiving a wrong item
you can shop at any time of day without leaving home
grade9-ict.answer: you can shop at any time of day without leaving home
acceptableAnswers: you can shop at any time of day without leaving home
grade9-ict.hint: 24/7 availability.
grade9-ict.explanation: Online stores are open around the clock, allowing customers to browse and buy at any hour without travelling to a shop.

grade9-ict.question: A disadvantage of online shopping is:
options: the website is available only during shop opening hours
delivery always takes less than one hour
you cannot physically handle the product before buying it
you must always pay in cash
grade9-ict.answer: you cannot physically handle the product before buying it
acceptableAnswers: you cannot physically handle the product before buying it
grade9-ict.hint: You cannot try it before you buy.
grade9-ict.explanation: Online shopping means customers cannot touch, try on or fully inspect products before purchasing, leading to a higher rate of returns.

grade9-ict.question: E-government services allow citizens to:
options: speak directly with the head of state
access government services and submit forms online without visiting a government office
vote in elections by playing a video game
grade9-ict.answer: access government services and submit forms online without visiting a government office
acceptableAnswers: access government services and submit forms online without visiting a government office
grade9-ict.hint: Government services delivered electronically.
grade9-ict.explanation: E-government provides online access to services such as tax filing, passport applications, licence renewals and benefit claims.

grade9-ict.question: Video conferencing allows:
options: users to send very large files by email
groups of people in different locations to meet face-to-face over the internet using cameras and microphones
computers to be controlled remotely without video
people to watch recorded videos on demand
grade9-ict.answer: groups of people in different locations to meet face-to-face over the internet using cameras and microphones
acceptableAnswers: groups of people in different locations to meet face-to-face over the internet using cameras and microphones
grade9-ict.hint: Real-time audio and video between remote participants.
grade9-ict.explanation: Video conferencing (Zoom, Teams, Google Meet) enables live audio and video meetings between participants anywhere in the world.

grade9-ict.question: Online learning (e-learning) benefits students by:
options: guaranteeing a qualification without any tests
requiring no computer or internet connection
allowing them to study at their own pace and from any location with internet access
replacing all written assignments with video games
grade9-ict.answer: allowing them to study at their own pace and from any location with internet access
acceptableAnswers: allowing them to study at their own pace and from any location with internet access
grade9-ict.hint: Flexibility is the key benefit.
grade9-ict.explanation: E-learning lets students access course materials and complete activities whenever and wherever they have internet access.

grade9-ict.question: When paying online, the padlock symbol and https in the address bar mean:
options: the connection is encrypted and the site has a valid security certificate
the website has been approved by the government
grade9-ict.answer: the connection is encrypted and the site has a valid security certificate
acceptableAnswers: the connection is encrypted and the site has a valid security certificate
grade9-ict.hint: https and a padlock = secure connection.
grade9-ict.explanation: The padlock and https indicate that the connection is secured with TLS encryption, protecting payment details in transit.

grade9-ict.question: Streaming a film online differs from downloading it because streaming:
options: plays the content as it is received without storing a permanent copy on the device
takes longer before the content can begin playing
saves a permanent file on the hard disk
grade9-ict.answer: plays the content as it is received without storing a permanent copy on the device
acceptableAnswers: plays the content as it is received without storing a permanent copy on the device
grade9-ict.hint: Stream now, not saved for later.
grade9-ict.explanation: Streaming plays content in real time as it arrives; downloading saves the complete file for repeated local playback.

grade9-ict.question: Cloud storage (such as Google Drive or OneDrive) allows users to:
options: store files on remote servers and access them from any device with an internet connection
send emails without an email address
store files only on a USB drive
grade9-ict.answer: store files on remote servers and access them from any device with an internet connection
acceptableAnswers: store files on remote servers and access them from any device with an internet connection
grade9-ict.hint: Files in the cloud are accessible from anywhere.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cloud storage saves files on remote servers managed by a provider, making them accessible from any device with internet access.

grade9-ict.question: A blog is best described as:
options: a regularly updated personal website or online journal with entries displayed newest first
a hardware device that connects to the internet
grade9-ict.answer: a regularly updated personal website or online journal with entries displayed newest first
acceptableAnswers: a regularly updated personal website or online journal with entries displayed newest first
grade9-ict.hint: Blog = web log.
grade9-ict.explanation: A blog is an online journal or informational website where the author posts regular entries (articles); readers can usually add comments.

grade9-ict.question: A wiki is a website that:
options: can only be read by one person at a time
is used only by scientists and researchers
can be edited and built collaboratively by multiple users through the browser
grade9-ict.answer: can be edited and built collaboratively by multiple users through the browser
acceptableAnswers: can be edited and built collaboratively by multiple users through the browser
grade9-ict.hint: Wikipedia is the most famous example.
grade9-ict.explanation: A wiki is a web platform that allows any authorised user to create, edit and delete pages, building a collaborative knowledge base.

grade9-ict.question: Social networking sites (such as Facebook or Instagram) allow users to:
options: create profiles, share content and communicate with others in an online community
store large files securely in the cloud
grade9-ict.answer: create profiles, share content and communicate with others in an online community
acceptableAnswers: create profiles, share content and communicate with others in an online community
grade9-ict.hint: They connect people socially online.
grade9-ict.explanation: Social networks provide platforms for users to share updates, photos and messages, and to interact with friends, family and groups.

grade9-ict.question: A podcast is:
options: a video call between two people
a type of social media post containing only text
a digital audio programme published on the internet that users can subscribe to and download
grade9-ict.answer: a digital audio programme published on the internet that users can subscribe to and download
acceptableAnswers: a digital audio programme published on the internet that users can subscribe to and download
grade9-ict.hint: You listen to a podcast.
grade9-ict.explanation: A podcast is an audio file (or series of audio files) published online; subscribers are notified when new episodes are released.

grade9-ict.question: Instant messaging (IM) allows users to:
options: schedule a video call for a later time
post a message visible to all internet users
send an email that arrives within one hour
exchange text messages in real time over the internet
grade9-ict.answer: exchange text messages in real time over the internet
acceptableAnswers: exchange text messages in real time over the internet
grade9-ict.hint: Messages appear instantly.
grade9-ict.explanation: Instant messaging allows real-time text communication between users who are online at the same time.

grade9-ict.question: RSS (Really Simple Syndication) allows users to:
options: subscribe to content updates from multiple websites and receive them in one news reader application
grade9-ict.answer: subscribe to content updates from multiple websites and receive them in one news reader application
acceptableAnswers: subscribe to content updates from multiple websites and receive them in one news reader application
grade9-ict.hint: Subscribe once and updates come to you.
grade9-ict.explanation: An RSS feed delivers new articles or posts from subscribed websites directly to the user's feed reader, without needing to visit each site.

grade9-ict.question: An online forum is a place where:
options: users post questions and replies on a topic in a public discussion thread
grade9-ict.answer: users post questions and replies on a topic in a public discussion thread
acceptableAnswers: users post questions and replies on a topic in a public discussion thread
grade9-ict.hint: A discussion board.
grade9-ict.explanation: An online forum is a community discussion platform where users post messages, ask questions and reply in threaded conversations on specific topics.

grade9-ict.question: VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) allows:
options: data to be compressed for faster download
websites to be translated into any language
voice telephone calls to be made over an internet connection instead of a traditional phone line
video to be streamed in very high definition
grade9-ict.answer: voice telephone calls to be made over an internet connection instead of a traditional phone line
acceptableAnswers: voice telephone calls to be made over an internet connection instead of a traditional phone line
grade9-ict.hint: Internet telephone calls.
grade9-ict.explanation: VoIP converts voice into digital data packets and transmits them over the internet, enabling free or low-cost calls anywhere in the world.

grade9-ict.question: Uploading content to a video-sharing site (such as YouTube) allows:
options: the video to play without an internet connection
anyone with access to the site to watch the video
only the uploader to watch the video
other users to edit the video directly
grade9-ict.answer: anyone with access to the site to watch the video
acceptableAnswers: anyone with access to the site to watch the video
grade9-ict.hint: Shared content can be watched by others.
grade9-ict.explanation: Uploading a video to a public video-sharing platform makes it accessible to any viewer with internet access and the site's address.

grade9-ict.question: Navigation on a website should be:
options: placed only at the very bottom of the page
different on every page of the site
hidden until the user clicks a special button
consistent, clear and easy to use so visitors can find information quickly
grade9-ict.answer: consistent, clear and easy to use so visitors can find information quickly
acceptableAnswers: consistent, clear and easy to use so visitors can find information quickly
grade9-ict.hint: Easy navigation keeps visitors on the site.
grade9-ict.explanation: Consistent, clear navigation helps users locate content efficiently; inconsistent menus confuse visitors and increase the likelihood they leave the site.

grade9-ict.question: A website with good readability uses:
options: multiple different fonts on each page
very small text to fit more content on the page
a dark green font on a black background
sufficient contrast between text and background, an appropriate font size and adequate spacing
grade9-ict.answer: sufficient contrast between text and background, an appropriate font size and adequate spacing
acceptableAnswers: sufficient contrast between text and background, an appropriate font size and adequate spacing
grade9-ict.hint: Contrast, size and spacing all affect readability.
grade9-ict.explanation: Good readability requires a font large enough to read comfortably, clear contrast between text and its background, and enough white space between lines and paragraphs.

grade9-ict.question: A responsive website is one that:
options: loads instantly regardless of connection speed
adapts its layout automatically to display correctly on different screen sizes (desktop, tablet, phone)
grade9-ict.answer: adapts its layout automatically to display correctly on different screen sizes (desktop, tablet, phone)
acceptableAnswers: adapts its layout automatically to display correctly on different screen sizes (desktop, tablet, phone)
grade9-ict.hint: It responds to the screen size.
grade9-ict.explanation: A responsive design uses flexible grids and CSS media queries to rearrange content so it looks good on any device, from a large monitor to a small phone.

grade9-ict.question: Accessibility in web design means:
options: ensuring the website can be used by people with disabilities, for example by providing alt text for images
removing all images from the site
allowing only registered users to view the content
grade9-ict.answer: ensuring the website can be used by people with disabilities, for example by providing alt text for images
acceptableAnswers: ensuring the website can be used by people with disabilities, for example by providing alt text for images
grade9-ict.hint: Everyone should be able to use the site.
grade9-ict.explanation: Web accessibility ensures people with visual, hearing, motor or cognitive disabilities can access and use the site, for example through screen readers, captions and keyboard navigation.

grade9-ict.question: The purpose of white space (negative space) in web design is to:
options: make the site load more slowly
make the content easier to read by preventing a cluttered, overwhelming appearance
hide parts of the page from certain users
grade9-ict.answer: make the content easier to read by preventing a cluttered, overwhelming appearance
acceptableAnswers: make the content easier to read by preventing a cluttered, overwhelming appearance
grade9-ict.hint: Space lets the eye rest.
grade9-ict.explanation: White space around text and images reduces visual noise, making the layout cleaner and the content easier to read.

grade9-ict.question: Web pages should load quickly because:
options: slow loading is required by privacy laws
images look better when the page is slow
users leave pages that take too long to load, increasing the bounce rate
a slow page is always more secure
grade9-ict.answer: users leave pages that take too long to load, increasing the bounce rate
acceptableAnswers: users leave pages that take too long to load, increasing the bounce rate
grade9-ict.hint: People are impatient online.
grade9-ict.explanation: Studies show that many users abandon a page that takes more than a few seconds to load, so fast load times are critical for keeping visitors.

grade9-ict.question: Using too many different fonts on a website makes it look:
grade9-ict.answer: unprofessional and difficult to read
grade9-ict.hint: Consistency in typography is important.
grade9-ict.explanation: Mixing many fonts creates visual confusion; professional sites typically use two fonts at most — one for headings and one for body text.

grade9-ict.question: A sitemap is:
options: a style sheet controlling the layout of each page
the history of all visits to the site
a map of the physical location of the web server
a list or diagram showing all the pages of a website and how they are linked together
grade9-ict.answer: a list or diagram showing all the pages of a website and how they are linked together
acceptableAnswers: a list or diagram showing all the pages of a website and how they are linked together
grade9-ict.hint: It is the architecture plan of the site.
grade9-ict.explanation: A sitemap is an organised list (or visual diagram) of all the pages in a website, showing the hierarchy and links between them.

grade9-ict.question: A "call to action" button on a web page is designed to:
options: prompt the visitor to take a specific action such as signing up, buying or downloading
show the site owner's contact details
grade9-ict.answer: prompt the visitor to take a specific action such as signing up, buying or downloading
acceptableAnswers: prompt the visitor to take a specific action such as signing up, buying or downloading
grade9-ict.hint: Buy Now, Sign Up, Learn More are common examples.
grade9-ict.explanation: A call-to-action (CTA) button guides visitors towards a desired action; it should be visually prominent and clearly worded.

grade9-ict.question: Breadcrumb navigation on a website shows:
options: the number of images remaining on the page
a progress bar for file downloads
the path the user has taken through the site hierarchy, from the home page to the current page
a list of recently visited external websites
grade9-ict.answer: the path the user has taken through the site hierarchy, from the home page to the current page
acceptableAnswers: the path the user has taken through the site hierarchy, from the home page to the current page
grade9-ict.hint: Home > Products > Electronics > Phones is an example.
grade9-ict.explanation: Breadcrumb navigation displays the hierarchy of pages leading to the current location, letting users navigate back to any level easily.

grade9-ict.question: Which one of the following is an output device?
grade9-ict.answer: Plotter
grade9-ict.hint: An output device sends information OUT of the computer to the user.
grade9-ict.explanation: A plotter draws the computer’s output onto paper, so it is an output device. A touchpad, microphone and joystick all send data into the computer.

grade9-ict.question: How many bits make up a byte?
grade9-ict.answer: 8 bits
grade9-ict.hint: It is the number of bits needed to store one character.
grade9-ict.explanation: One byte is 8 bits. That is enough to hold a single character of text, which is why file sizes are measured in bytes.

grade9-ict.question: Which component prevents the CPU from overheating?
grade9-ict.answer: Fan
grade9-ict.hint: Which part moves air across the processor?
grade9-ict.explanation: A fan (with a heat sink) blows air across the CPU to carry heat away. Without it the processor would overheat and shut down.

grade9-ict.question: Which one of the following stores data temporarily?
grade9-ict.answer: RAM
grade9-ict.hint: Which memory loses its contents when the power goes off?
grade9-ict.explanation: RAM is volatile: it holds the programs and data in use right now and is emptied when the computer is switched off. ROM, a hard disk and a CD keep their contents.

grade9-ict.question: Which device is shown in the picture below?
grade9-ict.answer: Barcode reader
grade9-ict.hint: Look at what the device is being held over - those stripes are read at a supermarket till.
grade9-ict.explanation: The stripes are a barcode, and the hand-held unit reading them is a barcode reader - an input device that turns the pattern of bars into a product number.

grade9-ict.question: The spreadsheet below shows the marks obtained by Ravi in a test.In which cell do the marks for French appear?
grade9-ict.answer: B3
grade9-ict.hint: A cell address is its COLUMN letter followed by its ROW number.
grade9-ict.explanation: French is on row 3, and the marks are in column B, so the cell address is B3. A3 holds the word “French” itself, not the mark.

grade9-ict.question: Which speech balloon is used when you want your character to tell a secret?
grade9-ict.answer: Whisper Balloon
grade9-ict.hint: A secret is spoken quietly, not thought and not shouted.
grade9-ict.explanation: A whisper balloon (usually drawn with a dashed outline) shows words spoken quietly so other characters cannot hear. A thought balloon shows what a character thinks but does not say.

grade9-ict.question: Which component is used to connect two LANs?
grade9-ict.answer: Router
grade9-ict.hint: Which device passes traffic between two separate networks rather than within one?
grade9-ict.explanation: A router joins two networks together and decides which way to send traffic between them. A switch connects devices inside one LAN.

grade9-ict.question: Which hardware component is shown below?
grade9-ict.answer: Network Interface Card
grade9-ict.hint: Look at the socket on the metal bracket - what kind of cable plugs into that?
grade9-ict.explanation: The square RJ45 socket on the bracket takes a network cable, so this is a Network Interface Card. A wireless card would have an aerial rather than a cable socket.

grade9-ict.question: Which health problem may be caused when a mouse is used for a long time?
grade9-ict.answer: Repetitive strain injury
grade9-ict.hint: Think about the same small hand movement being made over and over.
grade9-ict.explanation: Gripping and clicking a mouse repeats the same small movement for hours, which damages tendons and nerves in the hand and wrist - repetitive strain injury. Eye strain comes from the screen, not the mouse.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is a popular videoconferencing software?
grade9-ict.answer: Skype
grade9-ict.hint: Which one is built for live audio and video calls?
grade9-ict.explanation: Skype is designed for live video and voice calls. The others are for posting or editing text and pictures, not for holding a meeting.

grade9-ict.question: Which one of the following is required for e-learning?
grade9-ict.answer: Laptop
grade9-ict.hint: E-learning means learning delivered electronically, over a network.
grade9-ict.explanation: E-learning needs a computing device that can connect to the internet, so a laptop is required. A book, calculator or ordinary whiteboard cannot deliver an online lesson.

grade9-ict.question: Which shape is used for a “Decision Box” in a flowchart?
grade9-ict.answer: A diamond
grade9-ict.hint: A decision has more than one way out, so the shape has corners for the branches.
grade9-ict.explanation: A decision box is a diamond, with a Yes branch and a No branch leaving it. A rectangle is a process, a parallelogram is input/output and an oval is start or stop.

grade9-ict.question: Which feature in MS Word allows the word “DRAFT” to be placed behind the text of a document, as shown below?
grade9-ict.answer: Watermark
grade9-ict.hint: The word sits faintly BEHIND the text, across the whole page.
grade9-ict.explanation: A watermark is faint text or an image placed behind the document text, used to mark a page as DRAFT or CONFIDENTIAL. Page Color would fill the whole background with one colour.

grade9-ict.question: In a .......... topology every node is connected to a single cable.
grade9-ict.answer: bus
grade9-ict.hint: Picture one long backbone cable with every machine tapping into it.
grade9-ict.explanation: A bus topology runs one backbone cable and every node connects to it. If that single cable breaks, the whole network goes down - which is the weakness of the design.

grade9-ict.question: An example of a free operating system is ...........
grade9-ict.answer: Linux
grade9-ict.hint: Which one can be downloaded and used without paying a licence fee?
grade9-ict.explanation: Linux is free and open source - anyone may download, use and modify it. Windows and macOS are commercial products.

grade9-ict.question: Mobile phones can be connected to the internet using ...........
grade9-ict.answer: Wifi
grade9-ict.hint: Which of these is a way of connecting without a cable?
grade9-ict.explanation: Wifi connects a phone to a network over radio waves, with no cable. The others are a network layout, an operating system and a way of protecting data.

grade9-ict.question: A .......... is a software that can slow down a computer.
grade9-ict.answer: virus
grade9-ict.hint: Which one is malicious software that a computer catches?
grade9-ict.explanation: A virus is malicious software that copies itself and consumes memory and processor time, which is why an infected machine runs slowly.

grade9-ict.question: The purpose of a .......... is to keep data secure in case the original is lost.
grade9-ict.answer: backup
grade9-ict.hint: What do you make so that losing the original does not lose the data?
grade9-ict.explanation: A backup is a second copy of the data kept somewhere else, so the information survives a deletion, a hardware failure, a fire or a flood.

grade9-ict.question: A laser printer is slower than an inkjet printer.
grade9-ict.answer: False
grade9-ict.hint: Which type is used in busy offices for long print runs?
grade9-ict.explanation: False. A laser printer is faster - it forms a whole page at a time, which is why offices use them for large jobs. An inkjet builds the page line by line.

grade9-ict.question: A page break helps to separate content between pages.
grade9-ict.answer: True
grade9-ict.hint: What does inserting one do to the text after it?
grade9-ict.explanation: True. A page break forces everything after it onto a new page, which keeps sections apart no matter how the text above is edited.

grade9-ict.question: A conditional formatting rule cannot be removed in Excel.
grade9-ict.answer: False
grade9-ict.hint: Is formatting ever permanent in a spreadsheet?
grade9-ict.explanation: False. Conditional formatting rules can be edited or deleted at any time through Manage Rules. Nothing about a spreadsheet’s formatting is permanent.

grade9-ict.question: In a PowerPoint presentation, you cannot use more than one slide master.
grade9-ict.answer: False
grade9-ict.hint: Could one presentation need two different section designs?
grade9-ict.explanation: False. A presentation may contain several slide masters, so different sections can carry different designs while each section stays internally consistent.

grade9-ict.question: In a star topology, nodes are connected to a central computer.
grade9-ict.answer: True
grade9-ict.hint: Picture the shape the cables make.
grade9-ict.explanation: True. Every node has its own cable to a central device, forming a star. One node’s cable failing therefore affects only that node - unlike a bus.

grade9-ict.question: A firewall can be a hardware or a software.
grade9-ict.answer: True
grade9-ict.hint: Does it have to be a physical box?
grade9-ict.explanation: True. A firewall may be a dedicated hardware device on the edge of a network, or a program running on the computer itself. Both filter traffic against a set of rules.

grade9-ict.question: Personal information should be shared with everybody.
grade9-ict.answer: False
grade9-ict.hint: Think about who could use your address or ID number, and how.
grade9-ict.explanation: False. Personal information should be shared only with people who need it and can be trusted. Sharing it openly invites identity theft, fraud and unwanted contact.

grade9-ict.question: In a flowchart, flowlines indicate the movement of data.
grade9-ict.answer: True
grade9-ict.hint: What do the arrows between the boxes tell you?
grade9-ict.explanation: True. Flowlines are the arrows joining the symbols; they show the order the steps run in and how data moves from one step to the next.

grade9-ict.question: The Report Wizard is located in the Home Tab in MS Access.
grade9-ict.answer: False
grade9-ict.hint: Which tab do you use to make a new object in Access?
grade9-ict.explanation: False. The Report Wizard is on the Create tab, along with the other tools that make new tables, queries, forms and reports. The Home tab holds views, clipboard and formatting.

grade9-ict.question: Python is an example of a database software.
grade9-ict.answer: False
grade9-ict.hint: Is Python something you store data in, or something you write instructions in?
grade9-ict.explanation: False. Python is a programming language. Database software - MS Access, MySQL - stores and queries data; a Python program may talk to a database but is not one.

grade9-ict.question: Which hardware device stores pictures in digital cameras?
grade9-ict.answer: Memory Card
grade9-ict.hint: It is small, removable, and slots into the camera.
grade9-ict.explanation: A memory card is removable flash storage small enough for a camera, and it can be taken out and read on a computer.

grade9-ict.question: Which hardware device creates real world objects from a computer design?
grade9-ict.answer: 3D Printer
grade9-ict.hint: Which one builds something you can hold?
grade9-ict.explanation: A 3D printer builds a solid object layer by layer from a digital model, so the output is a physical thing rather than an image or a page.

grade9-ict.question: Which hardware device magnifies images generated by a computer?
grade9-ict.answer: Projector
grade9-ict.hint: Which one throws the screen onto a wall so a whole class can see?
grade9-ict.explanation: A projector enlarges the computer’s display onto a screen or wall, so a large audience can see it at once.

grade9-ict.question: Which term is used to perform mail merge in a word document?
grade9-ict.answer: Mailing list
grade9-ict.hint: Mail merge needs a document AND a source of names and addresses.
grade9-ict.explanation: A mailing list supplies the names, addresses and other fields that mail merge drops into each copy of the letter.

grade9-ict.question: Which term deals with the loading and running of application software?
grade9-ict.answer: Memory Management
grade9-ict.hint: Which one is a job the operating system does?
grade9-ict.explanation: Memory management is the operating system function that allocates memory to each program, loads it and reclaims the space when it closes.

grade9-ict.question: Which term refers to gaining unauthorised access to a computer system?
grade9-ict.answer: Hacking
grade9-ict.hint: Access that was never permitted in the first place.
grade9-ict.explanation: Hacking is gaining access to a system without permission. It is a criminal offence whether or not any data is changed.

grade9-ict.question: Which device produces digital images of hardcopy documents?
grade9-ict.answer: Scanner
grade9-ict.hint: It turns something printed on paper into a file.
grade9-ict.explanation: A scanner reads a printed page and produces a digital image of it - the reverse of what a printer does.

grade9-ict.question: Which term describes an online journal that displays the latest posts first?
grade9-ict.answer: Blog
grade9-ict.hint: A personal site of dated entries, newest at the top.
grade9-ict.explanation: A blog is an online journal whose entries are shown newest first, so a returning reader sees what has changed since their last visit.

grade9-ict.question: Google is an example of a ...........
grade9-ict.answer: search engine
grade9-ict.hint: What do you use it to do?
grade9-ict.explanation: Google is a search engine: it indexes web pages and returns the ones matching the words you type.

grade9-ict.question: Which of these is a threat to data security?
options: Accidental loss of data by deletion
grade9-ict.answer: Accidental loss of data by deletion
acceptableAnswers: Accidental loss of data by deletion
grade9-ict.hint: Three of these protect data. One destroys it.
grade9-ict.explanation: Accidental deletion loses the data, so it is a threat. Strong passwords, updated anti-virus software and regular backups are all protections against threats.

grade9-ict.question: The specifications of a computer system are shown below.What is the installed memory (RAM) of this computer?
grade9-ict.answer: 8 GB
grade9-ict.hint: Find the line labelled “Installed memory (RAM)”.
grade9-ict.explanation: The window reports 8.00 GB of installed memory (7.87 GB usable - some is reserved by the hardware). “64-bit” on the line below is the system type, not the memory size.

grade9-ict.question: Using the system information window below, give the operating system installed on the computer.
grade9-ict.answer: Windows 10 Home Single Language
grade9-ict.hint: Look under the heading “Windows edition”.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Windows edition line at the top of the window reads Windows 10 Home Single Language. Every option here is a real Windows edition, so the version number and the edition name both have to be read off the screen.

grade9-ict.question: Using the system information window below, give the speed of the processor.
grade9-ict.answer: 2.50 GHz
grade9-ict.hint: The speed is the figure after the @ sign on the Processor line.
grade9-ict.explanation: The processor line ends “@ 2.50GHz”, which is the clock speed. i5-7200U is the model number, not a speed.

grade9-ict.question: The spreadsheet below shows sales of perfume bottles in a duty-free shop.Which cell contains the sales of Chanel perfume bottles in January?
grade9-ict.answer: B4
grade9-ict.hint: Find the Chanel row, then the January column.
grade9-ict.explanation: Chanel is on row 4 and January is column B, so the cell is B4. B3 is Dior’s January sales and A4 holds the word “Chanel”.

grade9-ict.question: In the spreadsheet below, which cell contains the Average Sales of Gucci perfume bottles?
grade9-ict.answer: E6
grade9-ict.hint: Average Sales is a column heading; Gucci is a row.
grade9-ict.explanation: Average Sales is column E and Gucci is row 6, so the cell is E6. F6 holds the Below/Above label, not the average.

grade9-ict.question: In the spreadsheet below, which formula was used in cell C8 to calculate the Total Sales for February?
grade9-ict.answer: = SUM(C3:C7)
grade9-ict.hint: A total adds every brand’s February figure, from row 3 to row 7.
grade9-ict.explanation: = SUM(C3:C7) adds the five February values in column C. Multiplying or subtracting two of them would not give a total, and AVERAGE would give the mean.

grade9-ict.question: In the spreadsheet below, which formula in cell E3 finds the Average Sales of Dior perfume bottles across the three months?
grade9-ict.answer: = AVERAGE(B3:D3)
grade9-ict.hint: Dior’s three monthly figures run ACROSS row 3, from column B to column D.
grade9-ict.explanation: Dior’s January, February and March sales are B3, C3 and D3, so the mean is = AVERAGE(B3:D3). B3:B7 would average one month down the column instead.

grade9-ict.question: The Shop Average Sales is $2500. In cell F3, “Below” must appear when the Average Sales is less than $2500, and “Above” otherwise. Which formula does this?
grade9-ict.answer: = IF(E3 < 2500, "Below", "Above")
grade9-ict.hint: IF(test, value when true, value when false) - so the FIRST result is the one for a true test.
grade9-ict.explanation: The test is “less than 2500”, and when that is true the answer is “Below”, so it goes in the true slot: = IF(E3 < 2500, "Below", "Above"). Swapping the two results reverses every label.

grade9-ict.question: In the spreadsheet below, the formula = COUNTIF(F3:F7, "Above") is used in cell F8. What is the output?
grade9-ict.hint: Count how many rows in the last column say Above - do not add anything up.
grade9-ict.explanation: COUNTIF counts the cells in F3:F7 whose contents are “Above”. Dior and Yves Saint Laurent are Above; Chanel, Gucci and Dolce are Below - so the answer is 2.

grade9-ict.question: In a database table of games, the field RATING holds values such as 5, 4 and 3. Which data type is used for this field?
grade9-ict.answer: Number
grade9-ict.hint: Could you sort these values, or work out an average of them?
grade9-ict.explanation: The ratings are whole numbers that can be compared, sorted and averaged, so the field is a Number. Storing them as Text would sort 10 before 2.

grade9-ict.question: In a database, which object is used to organise and display data for printing?
grade9-ict.answer: Report
grade9-ict.hint: Which one is designed to be read on paper?
grade9-ict.explanation: A report arranges selected data into a formatted, printable layout with headings, grouping and totals.

grade9-ict.question: A .......... is a diagram that shows the steps to solve a problem.
grade9-ict.answer: flowchart
grade9-ict.hint: It is the whole diagram, not one part of it.
grade9-ict.explanation: A flowchart is the complete diagram of an algorithm. A flowline is one arrow inside it, and a sequence is one way of ordering its steps.

grade9-ict.question: A .......... connects one symbol to another in a flowchart.
grade9-ict.answer: flowline
grade9-ict.hint: It is the arrow between two boxes.
grade9-ict.explanation: A flowline is the arrow joining two symbols; it shows which step follows which.

grade9-ict.question: Steps in a .......... are executed one after the other, from first to last.
grade9-ict.answer: sequence
grade9-ict.hint: No repeating and no branching - just straight through.
grade9-ict.explanation: In a sequence each step runs once, in order. A loop repeats steps and a decision chooses between them.

grade9-ict.question:
This Python program must display a sentence seven times.
count = 0
while count < ___ :
  print("The weather is windy.")
  count = count + 1
Which number completes the while line?
grade9-ict.hint: count starts at 0 and goes up by 1. List the values for which the test is still true.
grade9-ict.explanation: With count starting at 0 and rising by 1, the test count < 7 is true for 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 - seven passes. Using 6 would print six times.

grade9-ict.question: In a Python while loop that must run a fixed number of times, what happens if the line count = count + 1 is left out?
grade9-ict.answer: The loop never ends
grade9-ict.hint: The condition is tested against count. What changes count?
grade9-ict.explanation: Without that line count stays at 0, so the condition is true forever and the loop never ends - an infinite loop. Changing the counter is what eventually makes the test false.

grade9-ict.question: Which type of chart is best for comparing the number of pupils in four separate classes?
grade9-ict.answer: Bar chart
grade9-ict.hint: Which chart places groups side by side so heights can be compared?
grade9-ict.explanation: A bar chart sets categories side by side so their sizes can be compared at a glance.

grade9-ict.question: Which chart type is best for showing how one quantity changes over a period of time?
grade9-ict.answer: Line graph
grade9-ict.hint: Think about which chart joins points with a continuous line.
grade9-ict.explanation: A line graph connects data points in order, making trends over time easy to see.

grade9-ict.question: Which chart type best shows how a whole is divided into parts?
grade9-ict.answer: Pie chart
grade9-ict.hint: This chart is circular and divided into slices.
grade9-ict.explanation: A pie chart shows each part as a slice of one whole circle, making proportions easy to read.

grade9-ict.question: In a table, a row runs:
options: from left to right across the table
from top to bottom down the table
grade9-ict.answer: from left to right across the table
acceptableAnswers: from left to right across the table
grade9-ict.hint: Think about how you read a single row of data.
grade9-ict.explanation: A row is a horizontal line of cells running left to right; a column is vertical.

grade9-ict.question: The key that identifies what each colour or pattern on a chart represents is called the:
grade9-ict.answer: legend
grade9-ict.hint: It is usually placed beside or below the chart area.
grade9-ict.explanation: The legend (or key) tells the reader which colour or pattern belongs to which data series.

grade9-ict.question: Which type of chart shows data as individual dots and is used to find relationships between two sets of values?
grade9-ict.answer: Scatter graph
grade9-ict.hint: Each dot represents one pair of measurements.
grade9-ict.explanation: A scatter graph plots pairs of values as dots, making it easy to spot correlations.

grade9-ict.question: When would a table be more useful than a chart in a presentation?
options: When showing a trend over many years
When making the slide more colourful
When the data has only two items
When exact values need to be compared
grade9-ict.answer: When exact values need to be compared
acceptableAnswers: When exact values need to be compared
grade9-ict.hint: Charts show patterns; tables show precise figures.
grade9-ict.explanation: A table allows the audience to read exact numbers; a chart is better for seeing trends or proportions.

grade9-ict.question: The numbers running along the side of a bar chart are placed on the:
grade9-ict.answer: y-axis
grade9-ict.hint: The vertical line is usually where the scale of values appears.
grade9-ict.explanation: The y-axis is the vertical axis and usually carries the scale of values.

grade9-ict.question: Gridlines on a chart help the reader to:
grade9-ict.answer: read values more accurately
grade9-ict.hint: They extend from the axis across the plot area.
grade9-ict.explanation: Gridlines extend from the axis across the chart, making it easier to read the value of each bar or point.

grade9-ict.question: What is the heading row of a table used for?
options: To apply a border to the whole table
grade9-ict.answer: To label each column
grade9-ict.hint: It sits at the top and tells the reader what is in each column.
grade9-ict.explanation: The heading row contains the column names so readers know what data each column holds.

grade9-ict.question: A stacked bar chart is used to show:
options: how data changes over time as a line
only one data series at a time
the total and the contribution of each part
grade9-ict.answer: the total and the contribution of each part
acceptableAnswers: the total and the contribution of each part
grade9-ict.hint: Each bar is divided into segments.
grade9-ict.explanation: A stacked bar chart divides each bar into coloured segments, showing both the total and how parts contribute to it.

grade9-ict.question: To edit the data used to draw a chart in a presentation, you would:
options: move the chart to a new slide
open the chart and edit the linked data table
delete the chart and draw a new one
grade9-ict.answer: open the chart and edit the linked data table
acceptableAnswers: open the chart and edit the linked data table
grade9-ict.hint: The chart is linked to a set of data.
grade9-ict.explanation: Double-clicking or right-clicking the chart opens the data table, which you edit to update the chart.

grade9-ict.question: Which tab in a presentation application is used to insert a chart?
grade9-ict.answer: Insert
grade9-ict.hint: You insert new objects such as charts, tables and pictures from this tab.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Insert tab provides commands to add new objects — including charts, tables, images and shapes — to a slide.

grade9-ict.question: A data table added below a chart in a presentation:
options: prints the slide as a handout
removes the legend from the chart
shows the exact numbers the chart is drawn from
changes the colours used in the chart
grade9-ict.answer: shows the exact numbers the chart is drawn from
acceptableAnswers: shows the exact numbers the chart is drawn from
grade9-ict.hint: It is a grid of figures placed beneath the chart area.
grade9-ict.explanation: A data table displays the underlying numbers beneath the chart so the audience can check the exact values.

grade9-ict.question: A presenter wants to show what percentage of a school budget is spent on each subject. Which chart is most appropriate?
grade9-ict.answer: Pie chart
grade9-ict.hint: Each subject is one slice of the total budget.
grade9-ict.explanation: A pie chart shows parts of a whole as slices; because the spending adds up to 100 %, it is ideal here.

grade9-ict.question: What does the chart title tell the audience?
options: Which slide the chart is on
The highest value in the data
How many data series are plotted
grade9-ict.answer: What the chart is about
grade9-ict.hint: It is displayed above or below the chart area.
grade9-ict.explanation: The chart title describes the subject of the chart so the audience immediately understands what it shows.

grade9-ict.question: An animation applied to an object on a slide makes the object:
options: appear, move or disappear in a chosen way
change the background of the slide
appear on every slide at once
grade9-ict.answer: appear, move or disappear in a chosen way
acceptableAnswers: appear, move or disappear in a chosen way
grade9-ict.hint: Animations are visual effects applied to individual objects.
grade9-ict.explanation: Animations control how individual objects enter, are emphasised, or leave the slide during a presentation.

grade9-ict.question: A slide transition is different from an animation because a transition:
options: is the effect used when moving from one slide to the next
is applied to a single object on one slide
plays a sound when a picture is clicked
makes text appear one letter at a time
grade9-ict.answer: is the effect used when moving from one slide to the next
acceptableAnswers: is the effect used when moving from one slide to the next
grade9-ict.hint: A transition affects the change between two slides, not the objects on a single slide.
grade9-ict.explanation: A transition is the visual effect that plays as one slide replaces another; animations affect objects within a slide.

grade9-ict.question: Which animation category makes an object leave the slide?
grade9-ict.answer: Exit
grade9-ict.hint: This animation removes the object from view.
grade9-ict.explanation: Exit animations cause an object to disappear from the slide, for example by fading out or flying off screen.

grade9-ict.question: An Emphasis animation is used to:
options: move an object along a path
remove an object from the slide
draw attention to an object that is already on the slide
bring an object onto the slide for the first time
grade9-ict.answer: draw attention to an object that is already on the slide
acceptableAnswers: draw attention to an object that is already on the slide
grade9-ict.hint: It does not add or remove the object.
grade9-ict.explanation: Emphasis animations highlight or draw attention to objects that are already visible, for example by spinning or changing colour.

grade9-ict.question: Where are all the animations for a slide listed in order?
grade9-ict.answer: The Animation Pane
grade9-ict.hint: It opens on the right side of the window and shows a numbered list.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Animation Pane shows every animation on the selected slide in the order they will play.

grade9-ict.question: An animation set to "Start On Click" will play:
options: at the same time as the previous animation
when the presenter clicks the mouse
after a set number of seconds
as soon as the slide appears
grade9-ict.answer: when the presenter clicks the mouse
acceptableAnswers: when the presenter clicks the mouse
grade9-ict.hint: The presenter controls when it plays.
grade9-ict.explanation: "On Click" means the animation waits until the presenter clicks the mouse or presses a key.

grade9-ict.question: The "Fly In" animation makes an object:
options: spin in place on the slide
slide in from the edge of the slide
grade9-ict.answer: slide in from the edge of the slide
acceptableAnswers: slide in from the edge of the slide
grade9-ict.hint: The object moves across the slide into its final position.
grade9-ict.explanation: "Fly In" is an entrance effect where an object moves in from one edge of the slide until it reaches its position.

grade9-ict.question: Using too many different animations in a single presentation will:
options: always make the presentation more professional
distract the audience from the content
reduce the file size of the presentation
prevent the slides from being printed
grade9-ict.answer: distract the audience from the content
acceptableAnswers: distract the audience from the content
grade9-ict.hint: Animations should support the message, not compete with it.
grade9-ict.explanation: Too many animations draw attention to the effects rather than the content, making the presentation harder to follow.

grade9-ict.question: To preview the animations on a slide without starting the full slide show, you click:
grade9-ict.answer: Preview in the Animations tab
grade9-ict.hint: It plays the animations in the editing window.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Preview button in the Animations tab plays all animations on the current slide in the editing view.

grade9-ict.question: The duration of an animation controls:
options: how long the animation takes to complete
the colour the object changes to
how many times the animation repeats
grade9-ict.answer: how long the animation takes to complete
acceptableAnswers: how long the animation takes to complete
grade9-ict.hint: A longer duration means a slower effect.
grade9-ict.explanation: Duration is the time in seconds from when the animation starts to when it finishes; a longer value gives a slower effect.

grade9-ict.question: A Motion Path animation makes an object:
options: follow a drawn path around the slide
fade in from transparent to opaque
bounce up and down on the spot
shrink and disappear from the slide
grade9-ict.answer: follow a drawn path around the slide
acceptableAnswers: follow a drawn path around the slide
grade9-ict.hint: The path is drawn by the user or chosen from a list.
grade9-ict.explanation: A motion path lets the user draw or select a route across the slide that the object will follow.

grade9-ict.question: Which animation effect makes an object appear gradually from invisible to fully visible?
grade9-ict.answer: Fade
grade9-ict.hint: The object grows from 0 % to 100 % opacity.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Fade entrance animation makes the object increase gradually from transparent to fully opaque.

grade9-ict.question: An animation set to "Start With Previous" will play:
options: at the same time as the animation before it
after all other animations have finished
grade9-ict.answer: at the same time as the animation before it
acceptableAnswers: at the same time as the animation before it
grade9-ict.hint: Several animations can play together.
grade9-ict.explanation: "With Previous" starts the animation at the same moment as the animation listed before it in the pane.

grade9-ict.question: A teacher wants to reveal bullet points one at a time as she speaks. Which setting should she apply to the text box?
options: Entrance animation with "On Click" trigger for each paragraph
Exit animation applied to the whole slide
grade9-ict.answer: Entrance animation with "On Click" trigger for each paragraph
acceptableAnswers: Entrance animation with "On Click" trigger for each paragraph
grade9-ict.hint: Each paragraph needs to appear separately when she clicks.
grade9-ict.explanation: Applying an entrance animation to the text box and setting it to appear by first-level paragraph reveals one bullet at a time on each click.

grade9-ict.question: The Bounce animation is placed in which animation category?
grade9-ict.answer: Entrance
grade9-ict.hint: The object arrives on the slide with a bouncing motion.
grade9-ict.explanation: Bounce is an entrance effect — the object bounces as it arrives on the slide for the first time.

grade9-ict.question: The "Spin" animation is an example of which animation category?
grade9-ict.answer: Emphasis
grade9-ict.hint: The object is already visible and spins in place.
grade9-ict.explanation: Spin is an emphasis animation: it rotates an object that is already on the slide to draw attention to it.

grade9-ict.question: Speaker notes in a presentation are intended for:
options: the audience to read during the talk
the projector to set the brightness
the presenter to use as a reminder
the printer to decide paper size
grade9-ict.answer: the presenter to use as a reminder
acceptableAnswers: the presenter to use as a reminder
grade9-ict.hint: They are not shown to the audience on the screen.
grade9-ict.explanation: Speaker notes are reminders for the presenter and are not displayed to the audience during the slide show.

grade9-ict.question: The notes pane in Normal view appears:
options: to the right of the ribbon
grade9-ict.answer: below the current slide
grade9-ict.hint: You type notes there while looking at the slide.
grade9-ict.explanation: In Normal view the notes pane is positioned directly below the slide editing area.

grade9-ict.question: A handout printed with three slides per page includes:
options: only the title of each slide
a copy of the full script
the speaker notes for each slide
lines for the audience to write their own notes
grade9-ict.answer: lines for the audience to write their own notes
acceptableAnswers: lines for the audience to write their own notes
grade9-ict.hint: The three-slides layout leaves ruled lines beside each thumbnail.
grade9-ict.explanation: The three-slides-per-page handout layout places lines next to each slide thumbnail so the audience can write notes.

grade9-ict.question: Which view shows each slide with its speaker notes below it, ready to be printed?
grade9-ict.answer: Notes Page view
grade9-ict.hint: Its name says what it contains.
grade9-ict.explanation: Notes Page view shows a reduced image of each slide above its speaker notes, making it easy to print for the presenter.

grade9-ict.question: Which print layout fits the most slides on one sheet of paper?
grade9-ict.answer: 9 slides per page
grade9-ict.hint: The more slides per page, the smaller each thumbnail is.
grade9-ict.explanation: Printing 9 slides per page places 9 small thumbnails on a single sheet, fitting the most slides on one page.

grade9-ict.question: The Handout Master allows you to:
options: set a consistent layout for all printed handout pages
add new slides to the presentation
change the animation on every slide
grade9-ict.answer: set a consistent layout for all printed handout pages
acceptableAnswers: set a consistent layout for all printed handout pages
grade9-ict.hint: It is the equivalent of the Slide Master but for printouts.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Handout Master controls the header, footer, page number and layout that appear on every printed handout page.

grade9-ict.question: Speaker notes are visible to the audience:
options: only when the presenter clicks a button
never — they appear only on the presenter's screen
always — they scroll at the bottom of the display
grade9-ict.answer: never — they appear only on the presenter's screen
acceptableAnswers: never — they appear only on the presenter's screen
grade9-ict.hint: The presenter view keeps notes private.
grade9-ict.explanation: In Presenter View, notes appear only on the presenter's monitor; the audience screen shows only the slide.

grade9-ict.question: To add speaker notes to a slide, the presenter types in the:
grade9-ict.answer: notes pane below the slide
grade9-ict.hint: It is the text area at the bottom of Normal view.
grade9-ict.explanation: The notes pane below the slide in Normal view is where speaker notes are typed.

grade9-ict.question: A handout is given to the audience so they can:
options: choose the order of the slides
follow the presentation and have a record to keep
see the animations that were used
grade9-ict.answer: follow the presentation and have a record to keep
acceptableAnswers: follow the presentation and have a record to keep
grade9-ict.hint: It is a printout for the audience.
grade9-ict.explanation: Handouts give the audience a printed copy of the slides to follow during the presentation and refer to afterwards.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following can be included in a handout header?
grade9-ict.answer: A title and a date
grade9-ict.hint: Headers and footers contain text information.
grade9-ict.explanation: The handout header can include a title, date, or other text that prints at the top of every handout page.

grade9-ict.question: Printing a presentation in Outline view produces:
options: the speaker notes without the slides
text only, with no slide images
grade9-ict.answer: text only, with no slide images
acceptableAnswers: text only, with no slide images
grade9-ict.hint: Outline view shows only text content.
grade9-ict.explanation: Printing in Outline view produces only the text from each slide in a hierarchical list, without any images.

grade9-ict.question: Which view allows a presenter to see their notes, the current slide and the next slide all at once?
grade9-ict.answer: Presenter View
grade9-ict.hint: It is designed for a two-screen setup.
grade9-ict.explanation: Presenter View is displayed on the presenter's monitor and shows the current slide, the next slide and the speaker notes together.

grade9-ict.question: The main advantage of providing handouts is that:
options: the presenter does not need to prepare notes
the animations still play on the printed page
the audience does not need to copy everything down
the file size of the presentation is reduced
grade9-ict.answer: the audience does not need to copy everything down
acceptableAnswers: the audience does not need to copy everything down
grade9-ict.hint: Handouts let the audience focus on listening.
grade9-ict.explanation: With a handout the audience can concentrate on what the presenter is saying rather than spending time copying information.

grade9-ict.question: To print six slide thumbnails on one sheet without note lines, you choose:
options: 6 slides per page from the Handouts section
Notes Pages from the print settings
grade9-ict.answer: 6 slides per page from the Handouts section
acceptableAnswers: 6 slides per page from the Handouts section
grade9-ict.hint: The Handouts section has options for different numbers of slides per page.
grade9-ict.explanation: Choosing 6 slides per page under Handouts prints six small slide images with no note lines beside them.

grade9-ict.question: Notes added in the notes pane are:
options: visible to the audience during the slide show
grade9-ict.answer: saved with the presentation file
grade9-ict.hint: They are part of the same file as the slides.
grade9-ict.explanation: Speaker notes are stored inside the presentation file and can be printed or viewed through Presenter View.

grade9-ict.question: Print Preview is used to:
options: check how a document will look before printing
change the font size on all slides
grade9-ict.answer: check how a document will look before printing
acceptableAnswers: check how a document will look before printing
grade9-ict.hint: It lets you see the output before using any paper.
grade9-ict.explanation: Print Preview shows an on-screen image of the printed output so you can spot problems before wasting paper.

grade9-ict.question: Printing a presentation in greyscale instead of colour:
options: makes the animations visible on paper
grade9-ict.answer: saves ink or toner
grade9-ict.hint: Colour cartridges are more expensive to use.
grade9-ict.explanation: Greyscale printing uses only the black cartridge, which saves the colour toner or ink.

grade9-ict.question: To print only slides 3 to 7 of a presentation, you would type in the page range box:
grade9-ict.hint: A hyphen between two numbers specifies a range.
grade9-ict.explanation: Most print dialogs accept a range like 3-7 meaning all slides from 3 through to 7 inclusive.

grade9-ict.question: Collated printing means:
options: slides are printed in reverse order
the page numbers are removed from the output
each complete copy is printed before the next begins
all copies of page 1 are printed first, then all of page 2
grade9-ict.answer: each complete copy is printed before the next begins
acceptableAnswers: each complete copy is printed before the next begins
grade9-ict.hint: Collated keeps sets together — 1,2,3 — 1,2,3.
grade9-ict.explanation: Collated prints a full set of pages (1, 2, 3) for one copy before starting the next, so the copies do not need to be sorted.

grade9-ict.question: Portrait orientation prints each page:
options: on both sides of the paper
grade9-ict.answer: taller than it is wide
grade9-ict.hint: Think of how a portrait painting is usually displayed.
grade9-ict.explanation: Portrait orientation makes the page taller than it is wide, like a standing person.

grade9-ict.question: Landscape orientation prints each page:
grade9-ict.answer: wider than it is tall
grade9-ict.hint: Think of a landscape painting viewed on its side.
grade9-ict.explanation: Landscape orientation rotates the page so it is wider than tall, useful for slides and wide tables.

grade9-ict.question: "Print Current Slide" prints:
options: only the slide that is currently selected
all the slides in the presentation
grade9-ict.answer: only the slide that is currently selected
acceptableAnswers: only the slide that is currently selected
grade9-ict.hint: It is a quick way to print just one slide.
grade9-ict.explanation: "Print Current Slide" prints whichever slide is highlighted or open at the time the print command is given.

grade9-ict.question: A presentation has 10 slides. If 3 copies are printed on "Full Page Slides", how many sheets of paper are used?
grade9-ict.hint: Each slide is on one sheet, and there are 3 copies.
grade9-ict.explanation: 10 slides × 3 copies = 30 sheets of paper.

grade9-ict.question: Which print setting places four slide thumbnails on a single sheet?
grade9-ict.answer: 4 slides per page (Handouts)
grade9-ict.hint: The Handouts section offers 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, or 9 per page.
grade9-ict.explanation: Choosing 4 slides per page under Handouts prints four small thumbnail images on one sheet.

grade9-ict.question: The Page Setup dialog in a presentation application is used to set:
options: the speed of the slide transition
the font used in the slide master
the colour scheme of the theme
the size and orientation of the slides
grade9-ict.answer: the size and orientation of the slides
acceptableAnswers: the size and orientation of the slides
grade9-ict.hint: It controls how large each slide is and how it is oriented.
grade9-ict.explanation: Page Setup controls the width, height and orientation of slides — settings that affect both display and printing.

grade9-ict.question: Pure Black and White print mode differs from Greyscale because it:
options: adds a black border around every slide
prints text only and omits all images
removes shading and prints all non-white areas as solid black
uses colour for text but grey for images
grade9-ict.answer: removes shading and prints all non-white areas as solid black
acceptableAnswers: removes shading and prints all non-white areas as solid black
grade9-ict.hint: There are no grey shades — only black and white.
grade9-ict.explanation: Pure Black and White converts all content to solid black or white with no intermediate grey shades.

grade9-ict.question: Before clicking Print, a presenter should use Print Preview to check:
options: that the font is installed on the printer
that all animations will still play
that the correct slides are selected and the layout looks right
that the Internet connection is working
grade9-ict.answer: that the correct slides are selected and the layout looks right
acceptableAnswers: that the correct slides are selected and the layout looks right
grade9-ict.hint: Preview catches layout problems before wasting paper.
grade9-ict.explanation: Print Preview lets you confirm the correct slides, the correct layout and that nothing is cut off at the edges.

grade9-ict.question: The number of copies to be printed is set in the:
options: Copies box in the Print dialog
grade9-ict.answer: Copies box in the Print dialog
acceptableAnswers: Copies box in the Print dialog
grade9-ict.hint: It is a numbered box in the print settings.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Copies box in the Print dialog lets you type how many complete sets of the slides you want to print.

grade9-ict.question: Duplex printing means:
options: printing on both sides of each sheet
printing twice as fast as normal
printing two slides on the same page
grade9-ict.answer: printing on both sides of each sheet
acceptableAnswers: printing on both sides of each sheet
grade9-ict.hint: It halves the number of sheets used.
grade9-ict.explanation: Duplex (double-sided) printing uses both sides of each sheet, which reduces paper consumption.

grade9-ict.question: Which option would you choose to print every slide that is currently selected in Slide Sorter view?
grade9-ict.answer: Selection
grade9-ict.hint: It prints only the highlighted items.
grade9-ict.explanation: "Selection" prints only the slides that have been highlighted/selected, rather than the whole presentation.

grade9-ict.question: A design template in a presentation application sets:
options: the colours, fonts and background for all slides
the order in which slides are shown
the speed at which transitions play
grade9-ict.answer: the colours, fonts and background for all slides
acceptableAnswers: the colours, fonts and background for all slides
grade9-ict.hint: It controls the visual look of the whole presentation.
grade9-ict.explanation: A design template applies a consistent set of colours, fonts and backgrounds to every slide in the presentation.

grade9-ict.question: Applying a theme to a presentation changes:
options: the colours, fonts and visual effects
grade9-ict.answer: the colours, fonts and visual effects
acceptableAnswers: the colours, fonts and visual effects
grade9-ict.hint: A theme is a coordinated set of visual settings.
grade9-ict.explanation: A theme is a preset collection of colours, fonts and graphic effects that is applied to all slides at once.

grade9-ict.question: Themes and design templates are found under which tab?
grade9-ict.answer: Design
grade9-ict.hint: The tab name describes what it controls.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Design tab contains all the available themes, colour variants and background options for a presentation.

grade9-ict.question: Applying a new theme to a presentation does NOT change:
options: the text written on each slide
the colour of the slide title
grade9-ict.answer: the text written on each slide
acceptableAnswers: the text written on each slide
grade9-ict.hint: A theme controls appearance, not content.
grade9-ict.explanation: A theme changes visual settings such as colours and fonts but does not alter the words or data on any slide.

grade9-ict.question: The main reason to use a design template rather than formatting each slide separately is:
options: to make all slides look consistent with less effort
to record narration for the slide show
to add more slides to the presentation
to convert the file into a PDF
grade9-ict.answer: to make all slides look consistent with less effort
acceptableAnswers: to make all slides look consistent with less effort
grade9-ict.hint: One setting change updates every slide.
grade9-ict.explanation: A template applies the same look to every slide instantly, keeping the presentation consistent without formatting each slide individually.

grade9-ict.question: A blank presentation has:
options: a plain white background and no preset colours or fonts
a background image on each slide
grade9-ict.answer: a plain white background and no preset colours or fonts
acceptableAnswers: a plain white background and no preset colours or fonts
grade9-ict.hint: Nothing is applied — you start from scratch.
grade9-ict.explanation: A blank presentation opens with a plain white background and default fonts so you can design it from scratch.

grade9-ict.question: Theme colours can be customised by:
options: editing the colour palette in the Theme Colors dialog
deleting and retyping all the text
grade9-ict.answer: editing the colour palette in the Theme Colors dialog
acceptableAnswers: editing the colour palette in the Theme Colors dialog
grade9-ict.hint: You can replace the preset colours with your own.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Theme Colors dialog lets you swap each colour in the palette for a custom choice, updating all slides that use those colours.

grade9-ict.question: A custom design template is saved with the file extension:
grade9-ict.answer: .potx
grade9-ict.hint: The "t" in the extension stands for template.
grade9-ict.explanation: .potx is the file extension for a PowerPoint Open XML template file.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is a benefit of using a design template for a school project?
options: Animations are added without any effort
Every pupil's work looks professional and consistent
The file is automatically sent to the teacher
The presentation is protected from editing
grade9-ict.answer: Every pupil's work looks professional and consistent
acceptableAnswers: Every pupil's work looks professional and consistent
grade9-ict.hint: Templates provide a ready-made professional look.
grade9-ict.explanation: A template gives an instant professional appearance and ensures all slides share the same visual style.

grade9-ict.question: The background of a slide can be set to:
options: a video that plays on every slide
a solid colour, a gradient, a texture or an image
grade9-ict.answer: a solid colour, a gradient, a texture or an image
acceptableAnswers: a solid colour, a gradient, a texture or an image
grade9-ict.hint: There are several background fill types.
grade9-ict.explanation: Slide backgrounds can use a solid fill, a gradient, a pattern, a texture or a picture.

grade9-ict.question: Applying a theme variant changes:
options: the colour scheme while keeping the same font and layout
the number of slides in the presentation
grade9-ict.answer: the colour scheme while keeping the same font and layout
acceptableAnswers: the colour scheme while keeping the same font and layout
grade9-ict.hint: A variant is a colour alternative within the same theme.
grade9-ict.explanation: Theme variants offer alternative colour palettes within the same theme, so the layout and fonts stay the same.

grade9-ict.question: Which option applies the chosen background only to the currently selected slide, not to all slides?
grade9-ict.answer: Apply to Selected Slides
grade9-ict.hint: There are two apply buttons in the background dialog.
grade9-ict.explanation: "Apply to Selected Slides" changes the background only on the highlighted slide; "Apply to All" changes every slide.

grade9-ict.question: A company wants every presentation made by its staff to use the same logo, colours and fonts. The best approach is to:
options: use only blank presentations with no colours
ask each person to format their own slides manually
delete the Design tab from all computers
create a custom template and distribute it to all staff
grade9-ict.answer: create a custom template and distribute it to all staff
acceptableAnswers: create a custom template and distribute it to all staff
grade9-ict.hint: A template enforces a consistent look automatically.
grade9-ict.explanation: A custom template ensures that all staff start from the same design without needing to format each slide themselves.

grade9-ict.question: Which element is NOT typically set by a design template?
options: The content of the speaker notes
grade9-ict.answer: The content of the speaker notes
acceptableAnswers: The content of the speaker notes
grade9-ict.hint: Templates control appearance, not the words you type.
grade9-ict.explanation: A design template sets visual properties such as colours, fonts and backgrounds, but not the text typed into notes or slides.

grade9-ict.question: A dark background with light-coloured text is best used in a:
options: presentation viewed on a small phone screen
darkened room where the projector is bright
brightly lit room with natural light
grade9-ict.answer: darkened room where the projector is bright
acceptableAnswers: darkened room where the projector is bright
grade9-ict.hint: High contrast between background and text aids readability in low light.
grade9-ict.explanation: A dark background makes text stand out clearly when projected in a darkened room, but can look washed out in bright daylight.

grade9-ict.question: Theme fonts control:
options: the font used for headings and body text throughout the presentation
the number of words allowed on each slide
the speed at which text animates onto the slide
the size of the slide thumbnails in the panel
grade9-ict.answer: the font used for headings and body text throughout the presentation
acceptableAnswers: the font used for headings and body text throughout the presentation
grade9-ict.hint: Changing the theme font updates all text at once.
grade9-ict.explanation: Theme fonts define one font for headings and one for body text, applied consistently across all slides.

grade9-ict.question: The slide master controls:
options: the speed of the slide show
the layout and appearance shared by all slides that use it
the number of slides in the presentation
grade9-ict.answer: the layout and appearance shared by all slides that use it
acceptableAnswers: the layout and appearance shared by all slides that use it
grade9-ict.hint: It is the template for all slides.
grade9-ict.explanation: The slide master holds the background, fonts, colours and placeholders that every slide based on it inherits.

grade9-ict.question: Editing the slide master affects:
options: only slides that have no animations
all slides that are based on that master
grade9-ict.answer: all slides that are based on that master
acceptableAnswers: all slides that are based on that master
grade9-ict.hint: That is the whole purpose of a master.
grade9-ict.explanation: Any change made on the slide master is immediately applied to every slide that inherits from it.

grade9-ict.question: To open Slide Master view, you click on:
options: the Insert tab and then Slide
the Design tab and then Edit Master
the Slide Show tab and then Master
the View tab and then Slide Master
grade9-ict.answer: the View tab and then Slide Master
acceptableAnswers: the View tab and then Slide Master
grade9-ict.hint: Views are changed from the View tab.
grade9-ict.explanation: Slide Master view is accessed through the View tab by clicking the Slide Master button.

grade9-ict.question: A logo placed on the slide master will appear:
options: on every slide that uses that master
only when the show is printed
grade9-ict.answer: on every slide that uses that master
acceptableAnswers: on every slide that uses that master
grade9-ict.hint: Everything on the master is inherited by all its slides.
