grade9-ict.explanation: Objects placed on the slide master appear on every slide based on it, which is useful for logos and watermarks.

grade9-ict.question: After editing the slide master, to return to Normal view you:
options: drag the master off the screen
grade9-ict.answer: click Close Master View
grade9-ict.hint: There is a button for this in the Slide Master tab.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Slide Master tab contains a "Close Master View" button that returns you to Normal view.

grade9-ict.question: Layout slides in the Slide Master view control:
options: the arrangement of placeholders for a specific type of slide
the sound played at the start of the show
the colour of the presentation background
the number of words allowed per slide
grade9-ict.answer: the arrangement of placeholders for a specific type of slide
acceptableAnswers: the arrangement of placeholders for a specific type of slide
grade9-ict.hint: A title-only layout is different from a two-content layout.
grade9-ict.explanation: Layout slides define where title, content, picture and other placeholders sit for a particular slide type.

grade9-ict.question: A footer added in the slide master will appear:
options: at the bottom of every slide
at the top of the first slide only
grade9-ict.answer: at the bottom of every slide
acceptableAnswers: at the bottom of every slide
grade9-ict.hint: The footer placeholder in the master is at the bottom.
grade9-ict.explanation: A footer placed on the slide master appears in the footer area at the bottom of every slide that inherits the master.

grade9-ict.question: Which of the following is a benefit of using a slide master?
options: The presentation cannot be saved as a PDF
Changing the font everywhere only requires one edit
Animations are removed from all slides
Every slide must have a different background
grade9-ict.answer: Changing the font everywhere only requires one edit
acceptableAnswers: Changing the font everywhere only requires one edit
grade9-ict.hint: One change propagates to every slide.
grade9-ict.explanation: Editing the master font updates every slide at once, saving the time of reformatting each slide separately.

grade9-ict.question: The top slide in Slide Master view (the largest one) is the:
grade9-ict.answer: slide master itself
grade9-ict.hint: The individual layout slides sit beneath it.
grade9-ict.explanation: The topmost, largest slide in the master view is the slide master; the smaller slides below it are the layout variations.

grade9-ict.question: A date placeholder on the slide master inserts:
options: the current or a fixed date on every slide
a link to an online calendar
grade9-ict.answer: the current or a fixed date on every slide
acceptableAnswers: the current or a fixed date on every slide
grade9-ict.hint: It can update automatically or be set to a fixed value.
grade9-ict.explanation: The date placeholder can show either today's date (updating automatically) or a fixed date, on every slide.

grade9-ict.question: A slide number placeholder in the master shows:
options: the number of words on each slide
the total number of slides only
the version number of the software
the number of each slide automatically
grade9-ict.answer: the number of each slide automatically
acceptableAnswers: the number of each slide automatically
grade9-ict.hint: It counts upward from slide 1.
grade9-ict.explanation: The slide number placeholder inserts the page number of each slide automatically, incrementing for each slide.

grade9-ict.question: A Title Slide layout in the master is used for:

grade9-ict.explanation: A CLI (also called a terminal or console) accepts typed commands; it is faster for experienced users and uses fewer system resources than a GUI.

grade9-ict.question: A multi-user operating system allows:
options: multiple computers to share one keyboard
only one user at a time but with many accounts
a user to run multiple programs simultaneously
two or more users to use the system simultaneously, each with their own secure session
grade9-ict.answer: two or more users to use the system simultaneously, each with their own secure session
acceptableAnswers: two or more users to use the system simultaneously, each with their own secure session
grade9-ict.hint: Multiple users at the same time.
grade9-ict.explanation: Multi-user OS designs (common on servers and mainframes) isolate each user's session so they can all work concurrently without interfering with each other.

grade9-ict.question: Antivirus software is a utility program that:
options: compresses files to save disk space
scans the computer for malware and removes or quarantines threats
backs up user data to an external drive
grade9-ict.answer: scans the computer for malware and removes or quarantines threats
acceptableAnswers: scans the computer for malware and removes or quarantines threats
grade9-ict.hint: Antivirus detects and removes malicious software.
grade9-ict.explanation: Antivirus software uses signature databases and heuristic analysis to detect viruses, trojans, spyware and other malware, then neutralises them.

grade9-ict.question: A file compression utility (such as WinZip or 7-Zip) is used to:
options: reduce the file size of one or more files to save disk space and speed up transfer
convert files from one format to another
encrypt files so they cannot be read by others
back up files to a network server
grade9-ict.answer: reduce the file size of one or more files to save disk space and speed up transfer
acceptableAnswers: reduce the file size of one or more files to save disk space and speed up transfer
grade9-ict.hint: Compression makes files smaller.
grade9-ict.explanation: File compression algorithms (ZIP, RAR, 7z) reduce file size by encoding repeated data patterns more efficiently, saving storage and reducing download times.

grade9-ict.question: Disk cleanup is a utility that:
options: deletes temporary files, cached web pages and other unnecessary files to free up hard disk space
formats the disk and erases all data
grade9-ict.answer: deletes temporary files, cached web pages and other unnecessary files to free up hard disk space
acceptableAnswers: deletes temporary files, cached web pages and other unnecessary files to free up hard disk space
grade9-ict.hint: Clean up junk files.
grade9-ict.explanation: Disk cleanup scans for and removes temporary files, system cache, emptied recycle bin contents and other redundant files to recover disk space.

grade9-ict.question: Backup software is a utility that:
options: copies selected files or the entire system to a separate location so they can be restored if the originals are lost or corrupted
connects the computer to the internet
grade9-ict.answer: copies selected files or the entire system to a separate location so they can be restored if the originals are lost or corrupted
acceptableAnswers: copies selected files or the entire system to a separate location so they can be restored if the originals are lost or corrupted
grade9-ict.hint: Backups are copies for disaster recovery.
grade9-ict.explanation: Backup software automates the process of copying data to an external drive, NAS or cloud, enabling recovery after hardware failure, ransomware or accidental deletion.

grade9-ict.question: A firewall utility monitors:
options: the battery level of a laptop
incoming and outgoing network traffic and blocks connections that violate the security rules
the number of programs currently running
grade9-ict.answer: incoming and outgoing network traffic and blocks connections that violate the security rules
acceptableAnswers: incoming and outgoing network traffic and blocks connections that violate the security rules
grade9-ict.hint: A firewall is a traffic filter for the network.
grade9-ict.explanation: A software firewall inspects each packet of network data and allows or blocks it based on rules — for example, blocking unsolicited incoming connections.

grade9-ict.question: Screen-reader software is an accessibility utility that:
options: captures screenshots and saves them as files
translates web pages into different languages
reads the contents of the hard disk aloud to speed up backup
converts on-screen text and UI elements to speech or Braille output for visually impaired users
grade9-ict.answer: converts on-screen text and UI elements to speech or Braille output for visually impaired users
acceptableAnswers: converts on-screen text and UI elements to speech or Braille output for visually impaired users
grade9-ict.hint: For visually impaired computer users.
grade9-ict.explanation: Screen readers (e.g., JAWS, NVDA) narrate what is displayed on screen — text, menus, buttons — enabling visually impaired users to operate a computer without a monitor.

grade9-ict.question: A task manager utility allows users to:
options: view running processes and their resource use, and end unresponsive programs
grade9-ict.answer: view running processes and their resource use, and end unresponsive programs
acceptableAnswers: view running processes and their resource use, and end unresponsive programs
grade9-ict.hint: Ctrl+Alt+Del → Task Manager on Windows.
grade9-ict.explanation: Task Manager shows all running processes, their CPU and memory usage, and allows users to force-quit programs that have stopped responding.

grade9-ict.question: Encryption software protects data by:
options: converting it into a coded form that can only be read by someone with the correct decryption key
grade9-ict.answer: converting it into a coded form that can only be read by someone with the correct decryption key
acceptableAnswers: converting it into a coded form that can only be read by someone with the correct decryption key
grade9-ict.hint: Encrypted data is unreadable without the key.
grade9-ict.explanation: Encryption scrambles data using a mathematical algorithm; without the key, the ciphertext is meaningless — protecting confidentiality even if the device is stolen.

grade9-ict.question: A scanner is an input device used to:
options: convert a physical document or image into a digital format that the computer can process
grade9-ict.answer: convert a physical document or image into a digital format that the computer can process
acceptableAnswers: convert a physical document or image into a digital format that the computer can process
grade9-ict.hint: It digitises paper documents.
grade9-ict.explanation: A scanner reads a physical page using a light source and sensor array, converting it into a digital image or text file.

grade9-ict.question: A microphone is an input device that:
options: converts sound waves into electrical signals that the computer can record or process
grade9-ict.answer: converts sound waves into electrical signals that the computer can record or process
acceptableAnswers: converts sound waves into electrical signals that the computer can record or process
grade9-ict.hint: Sound in → electrical signal → computer.
grade9-ict.explanation: A microphone is a transducer that converts the pressure variations of sound waves into electrical signals, enabling voice recording, VoIP and speech recognition.

grade9-ict.question: A touch screen is an input device because:
options: it displays the output from the computer
it detects where the user touches the screen and sends that positional information to the computer as input
grade9-ict.answer: it detects where the user touches the screen and sends that positional information to the computer as input
acceptableAnswers: it detects where the user touches the screen and sends that positional information to the computer as input
grade9-ict.hint: It accepts finger/stylus input.
grade9-ict.explanation: A touch screen combines a display (output) with a touch-sensitive layer (input) that detects the position and gesture of touches, sending this data to the processor.

grade9-ict.question: A projector is an output device used to:
options: display images or video from a computer onto a large screen or wall for an audience
accept typed input from the user
grade9-ict.answer: display images or video from a computer onto a large screen or wall for an audience
acceptableAnswers: display images or video from a computer onto a large screen or wall for an audience
grade9-ict.hint: It projects the screen image onto a larger surface.
grade9-ict.explanation: A projector receives a video signal from the computer and uses a light source and lens to project it onto a screen, enabling presentations to large groups.

grade9-ict.question: Speakers are output devices that:
options: convert electrical audio signals from the computer into sound waves heard by the user
grade9-ict.answer: convert electrical audio signals from the computer into sound waves heard by the user
acceptableAnswers: convert electrical audio signals from the computer into sound waves heard by the user
grade9-ict.hint: Electrical signal → sound.
grade9-ict.explanation: Speakers (and headphones) are transducers that convert the analogue audio signal from the sound card into vibrating air — sound.

grade9-ict.question: A 3D printer is an output device that:
options: displays 3D images on a flat screen
builds physical three-dimensional objects layer by layer from a digital design file
prints text and images on flat paper
grade9-ict.answer: builds physical three-dimensional objects layer by layer from a digital design file
acceptableAnswers: builds physical three-dimensional objects layer by layer from a digital design file
grade9-ict.hint: It prints in three dimensions.
grade9-ict.explanation: A 3D printer extrudes (or cures) material layer by layer according to a digital 3D model (STL file), creating physical objects from plastic, resin or other materials.

grade9-ict.question: An SSD (Solid State Drive) compared to an HDD (Hard Disk Drive) is:
options: only used for storing music files
faster, more silent, more shock-resistant, and uses less power because it has no moving parts
grade9-ict.answer: faster, more silent, more shock-resistant, and uses less power because it has no moving parts
acceptableAnswers: faster, more silent, more shock-resistant, and uses less power because it has no moving parts
grade9-ict.hint: No spinning parts = faster and quieter.
grade9-ict.explanation: SSDs use flash memory chips with no mechanical parts, giving faster read/write speeds, silent operation and greater resilience to physical shock compared to HDDs.

grade9-ict.question: Cloud storage is a form of storage where data is:
options: stored on remote servers over the internet, accessible from any device with internet connectivity
stored on a USB drive inserted in the computer
grade9-ict.answer: stored on remote servers over the internet, accessible from any device with internet connectivity
acceptableAnswers: stored on remote servers over the internet, accessible from any device with internet connectivity
grade9-ict.hint: Files in the cloud, not on your device.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cloud storage (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox) saves files on provider-managed servers; users access them via the internet from any device.

grade9-ict.question: Optical storage media such as CDs and DVDs store data using:
options: microscopic pits and lands on a reflective disc surface, read by a laser
magnetic particles on a spinning platter
grade9-ict.answer: microscopic pits and lands on a reflective disc surface, read by a laser
acceptableAnswers: microscopic pits and lands on a reflective disc surface, read by a laser
grade9-ict.hint: A laser reads the pits and lands.
grade9-ict.explanation: Optical discs store data as physical variations (pits = binary 0, lands = binary 1) on a reflective surface; a laser detects these variations by measuring reflected light.

grade9-ict.question: RAM (Random Access Memory) is:
options: permanent storage that retains data when the power is off
volatile temporary memory used by the CPU to hold currently running programs and data — contents are lost when power is cut
the central processing unit's arithmetic unit
grade9-ict.answer: volatile temporary memory used by the CPU to hold currently running programs and data — contents are lost when power is cut
acceptableAnswers: volatile temporary memory used by the CPU to hold currently running programs and data — contents are lost when power is cut
grade9-ict.hint: RAM = fast but temporary.
grade9-ict.explanation: RAM holds the OS, running applications and working data for the CPU to access instantly; it is volatile, meaning all data is lost on power loss.

grade9-ict.question: The CPU's clock speed is measured in:
options: GHz (gigahertz), which represents the number of instruction cycles per second
grade9-ict.answer: GHz (gigahertz), which represents the number of instruction cycles per second
acceptableAnswers: GHz (gigahertz), which represents the number of instruction cycles per second
grade9-ict.hint: Clock speed tells you how many cycles per second.
grade9-ict.explanation: Clock speed (in MHz or GHz) is the number of instruction cycles a CPU can perform per second; a higher clock speed generally means faster processing.

grade9-ict.question: 1 kilobyte (KB) is approximately equal to:
grade9-ict.answer: 1,024 bytes
grade9-ict.hint: Binary kilo = 2¹⁰ = 1024.
grade9-ict.explanation: In computing, 1 KB = 2¹⁰ bytes = 1,024 bytes (though some contexts use the decimal approximation of 1,000 bytes).

grade9-ict.question: The smallest unit of data in a computer is a:
grade9-ict.answer: bit (a binary digit, either 0 or 1)
grade9-ict.hint: bit = binary digit.
grade9-ict.explanation: A bit is the most fundamental unit of data: a single binary value, either 0 or 1. Eight bits make one byte.

grade9-ict.question: The first step in troubleshooting a computer problem is:
options: call a technician before doing anything
clearly identify and define what the problem is before attempting any fix
grade9-ict.answer: clearly identify and define what the problem is before attempting any fix
acceptableAnswers: clearly identify and define what the problem is before attempting any fix
grade9-ict.hint: Understand the problem first.
grade9-ict.explanation: Effective troubleshooting begins by gathering information: what are the symptoms, when did they start, what changed recently? Jumping straight to a solution wastes time.

grade9-ict.question: "Try the simplest fix first" is a troubleshooting principle because:
options: it saves time to start with the most difficult possible solution
simple fixes never work and are only tried to waste time
complex fixes are always needed for any fault
most computer problems have simple causes such as a loose cable, a need to restart or a simple setting change
grade9-ict.answer: most computer problems have simple causes such as a loose cable, a need to restart or a simple setting change
acceptableAnswers: most computer problems have simple causes such as a loose cable, a need to restart or a simple setting change
grade9-ict.hint: Occam's razor — simplest explanation first.
grade9-ict.explanation: Statistics show that most user-reported issues are caused by simple oversights (unplugged cable, frozen process, low battery); checking simple fixes first saves time and reduces disruption.

grade9-ict.question: Restarting a computer often fixes minor software problems because:
options: it reinstalls the operating system from scratch
it clears RAM, reloads the operating system and closes any frozen or corrupt processes
it deletes all temporary files permanently
grade9-ict.answer: it clears RAM, reloads the operating system and closes any frozen or corrupt processes
acceptableAnswers: it clears RAM, reloads the operating system and closes any frozen or corrupt processes
grade9-ict.hint: A fresh start clears memory and resets processes.
grade9-ict.explanation: Restarting flushes RAM, restarts system services and allows pending OS updates to apply, resolving many issues caused by memory leaks or frozen processes.

grade9-ict.question: When a computer produces an error message, the user should:
options: immediately turn the computer off at the wall
read the message carefully, note it down or take a screenshot, and use it to guide the troubleshooting process
click OK as quickly as possible to dismiss it
grade9-ict.answer: read the message carefully, note it down or take a screenshot, and use it to guide the troubleshooting process
acceptableAnswers: read the message carefully, note it down or take a screenshot, and use it to guide the troubleshooting process
grade9-ict.hint: Error messages contain diagnostic information.
grade9-ict.explanation: Error codes and messages identify the fault; noting them down allows the user or technician to search for the specific solution online or in documentation.

grade9-ict.question: Checking cable connections is an important first step in troubleshooting hardware problems because:
options: internal components cannot be connected by cables
a loose or disconnected cable is one of the most common causes of hardware faults
cables never cause problems in modern computers
grade9-ict.answer: a loose or disconnected cable is one of the most common causes of hardware faults
acceptableAnswers: a loose or disconnected cable is one of the most common causes of hardware faults
grade9-ict.hint: Always check the physical connections first.
grade9-ict.explanation: Power cables, data cables and peripheral connections can come loose from vibration or movement; a disconnected cable is a quick and free fix that should always be checked first.

grade9-ict.question: After identifying a possible solution to a computer problem, the next step is to:
options: test the solution carefully, one change at a time, to see whether it resolves the problem
make all possible changes simultaneously to save time
grade9-ict.answer: test the solution carefully, one change at a time, to see whether it resolves the problem
acceptableAnswers: test the solution carefully, one change at a time, to see whether it resolves the problem
grade9-ict.hint: Test one change at a time.
grade9-ict.explanation: Making one change at a time and testing after each change reveals which fix actually solved the problem; making multiple changes simultaneously makes it impossible to know which worked.

grade9-ict.question: Documenting a troubleshooting process means:
options: printing every screen you see during troubleshooting
backing up the hard drive before starting
recording the problem, the steps taken, and the solution found so the same issue can be resolved faster in the future
grade9-ict.answer: recording the problem, the steps taken, and the solution found so the same issue can be resolved faster in the future
acceptableAnswers: recording the problem, the steps taken, and the solution found so the same issue can be resolved faster in the future
grade9-ict.hint: Write it down for future reference.
grade9-ict.explanation: Documentation creates a knowledge base; the next time the same fault occurs, the technician can consult the record rather than re-investigating from scratch.

grade9-ict.question: If an internet connection stops working, a logical first troubleshooting step is:
options: check that the router is powered on, all cables are connected, and try another device to see if the problem is with the device or the network
assume the problem cannot be fixed
grade9-ict.answer: check that the router is powered on, all cables are connected, and try another device to see if the problem is with the device or the network
acceptableAnswers: check that the router is powered on, all cables are connected, and try another device to see if the problem is with the device or the network
grade9-ict.hint: Isolate whether the fault is the device, the router or the ISP.
grade9-ict.explanation: Checking another device determines whether the fault is with the specific computer or with the network infrastructure, narrowing the troubleshooting scope significantly.

grade9-ict.question: Updating software and device drivers is a troubleshooting step that can resolve:
options: compatibility issues, crashes and security vulnerabilities caused by outdated software interacting poorly with newer systems
physical hardware damage such as broken keyboards
grade9-ict.answer: compatibility issues, crashes and security vulnerabilities caused by outdated software interacting poorly with newer systems
acceptableAnswers: compatibility issues, crashes and security vulnerabilities caused by outdated software interacting poorly with newer systems
grade9-ict.hint: Updates fix bugs and compatibility problems.
grade9-ict.explanation: Software vendors release updates to patch bugs, improve compatibility with new hardware/OS versions and fix security vulnerabilities; updating often resolves mysterious crashes and errors.

grade9-ict.question: Which keyboard shortcut makes selected text bold?
grade9-ict.answer: Ctrl + B
grade9-ict.hint: B for Bold.
grade9-ict.explanation: Ctrl + B applies bold formatting to selected text in most word processors.

grade9-ict.question: Which keyboard shortcut underlines selected text?
grade9-ict.answer: Ctrl + U
grade9-ict.hint: U for Underline.
grade9-ict.explanation: Ctrl + U applies an underline to selected text.

grade9-ict.question: Text that slopes to the right is formatted as:
grade9-ict.answer: Italic
grade9-ict.hint: It leans like a slanted letter i.
grade9-ict.explanation: Italic formatting makes text slope to the right and is used for emphasis or titles.

grade9-ict.question: Text that is level at both the left and right margins is:
grade9-ict.answer: Justified
grade9-ict.hint: Newspaper columns are usually set this way.
grade9-ict.explanation: Justified alignment spaces words so that text lines up neatly at both the left and the right margin.

grade9-ict.question: Which option changes the size of the text characters?
grade9-ict.answer: Font size
grade9-ict.hint: It is measured in points.
grade9-ict.explanation: Font size controls how large or small the characters appear, measured in points (pt).

grade9-ict.question: The font face (typeface) controls:
options: the design or style of the characters
the colour of the page background
the line spacing of the document
grade9-ict.answer: the design or style of the characters
acceptableAnswers: the design or style of the characters
grade9-ict.hint: Arial, Times New Roman and Calibri are all different fonts.
grade9-ict.explanation: The font face determines the visual design of the letters — for example, whether they have serifs or not.

grade9-ict.question: Superscript text appears:
options: slightly above the normal text line and in a smaller size
in bold on its own line
grade9-ict.answer: slightly above the normal text line and in a smaller size
acceptableAnswers: slightly above the normal text line and in a smaller size
grade9-ict.hint: Think of the "2" in cm².
grade9-ict.explanation: Superscript raises the text above the normal baseline and reduces its size, used for powers and footnote numbers.

grade9-ict.question: Strikethrough formatting is used to:
options: draw a line through text to show it has been deleted or is no longer valid
grade9-ict.answer: draw a line through text to show it has been deleted or is no longer valid
acceptableAnswers: draw a line through text to show it has been deleted or is no longer valid
grade9-ict.hint: A line goes through the middle of the text.
grade9-ict.explanation: Strikethrough draws a horizontal line through text, commonly used when revising documents to mark removed content.

grade9-ict.question: Line spacing in a word processor controls:
options: the number of characters per line
the vertical space between lines of text
grade9-ict.answer: the vertical space between lines of text
acceptableAnswers: the vertical space between lines of text
grade9-ict.hint: Double spacing leaves a gap between each line.
grade9-ict.explanation: Line spacing sets how much vertical space appears between successive lines in a paragraph.

grade9-ict.question: The Format Painter tool is used to:
options: change the background colour of the page
copy formatting from one piece of text and apply it to another
draw a border around a paragraph
insert a picture into the document
grade9-ict.answer: copy formatting from one piece of text and apply it to another
acceptableAnswers: copy formatting from one piece of text and apply it to another
grade9-ict.hint: It copies the look, not the content.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Format Painter copies all formatting settings (font, size, colour, bold, etc.) from selected text and applies them elsewhere.

grade9-ict.question: Which keyboard shortcut selects all text in a document?
grade9-ict.answer: Ctrl + A
grade9-ict.hint: A for All.
grade9-ict.explanation: Ctrl + A selects all content in the document, allowing formatting or copying in one step.

grade9-ict.question: Changing text to ALL CAPS using the Change Case option is different from holding Caps Lock because:
options: Caps Lock only works on the first letter
Change Case always underlines the text
Change Case can be removed without retyping the text, while Caps Lock requires retyping
grade9-ict.answer: Change Case can be removed without retyping the text, while Caps Lock requires retyping
acceptableAnswers: Change Case can be removed without retyping the text, while Caps Lock requires retyping
grade9-ict.hint: Change Case is a formatting toggle.
grade9-ict.explanation: Change Case applies an appearance change that can be reversed; Caps Lock physically changes the characters, requiring retyping to undo.

grade9-ict.question: The margin of a document is:
options: the gap between two columns of text
the coloured band at the top of the screen
the blank space between the text and the edge of the page
grade9-ict.answer: the blank space between the text and the edge of the page
acceptableAnswers: the blank space between the text and the edge of the page
grade9-ict.hint: It frames the text on the page.
grade9-ict.explanation: Margins are the areas of white space that surround the text area on all four sides of a page.

grade9-ict.question: A header in a word-processed document appears:
options: in the middle of the first page only
at the top of every page
at the bottom of every page
grade9-ict.answer: at the top of every page
acceptableAnswers: at the top of every page
grade9-ict.hint: The name tells you where it is.
grade9-ict.explanation: A header is an area at the very top of the page that can contain text such as a title, page number or date, repeated on every page.

grade9-ict.question: A footer in a word-processed document appears:
options: at the top of every page
at the bottom of every page
grade9-ict.answer: at the bottom of every page
acceptableAnswers: at the bottom of every page
grade9-ict.hint: It is the opposite of a header.
grade9-ict.explanation: A footer is an area at the bottom of every page, often used for page numbers, dates or document titles.

grade9-ict.question: To print a document with the page wider than it is tall, the orientation should be set to:
grade9-ict.answer: Landscape
grade9-ict.hint: Like a landscape painting viewed sideways.
grade9-ict.explanation: Landscape orientation rotates the page so it is wider than it is tall, useful for wide tables or certificates.

grade9-ict.question: Page break is used to:
options: delete the header on one page
remove a blank page from the middle of a document
force the text after it to begin on a new page
grade9-ict.answer: force the text after it to begin on a new page
acceptableAnswers: force the text after it to begin on a new page
grade9-ict.hint: It starts a fresh page at that point.
grade9-ict.explanation: A manual page break forces whatever follows it to start at the top of the next page regardless of how much text is on the current page.

grade9-ict.question: Gutter margin in a document is:
options: the top margin on odd pages
the space at the bottom of the page
extra space added on the binding edge so text is not hidden when the document is bound
grade9-ict.answer: extra space added on the binding edge so text is not hidden when the document is bound
acceptableAnswers: extra space added on the binding edge so text is not hidden when the document is bound
grade9-ict.hint: It is the inner edge margin for a booklet.
grade9-ict.explanation: A gutter margin adds extra blank space along the edge where pages will be bound, preventing text from disappearing into the spine.

grade9-ict.question: Which feature breaks a document into two or more side-by-side vertical sections of text on the same page?
grade9-ict.answer: Columns
grade9-ict.hint: Newspaper-style layout.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Columns feature divides the page into vertical strips so text flows from the bottom of one column to the top of the next.

grade9-ict.question: The paper size most commonly used in schools and offices is:
grade9-ict.answer: A4
grade9-ict.explanation: A4 (210 mm × 297 mm) is the standard paper size in most countries and the default for most office documents.

grade9-ict.question: Indentation in a word processor moves:
options: the paragraph to the next page
the text to the centre of the page
the line spacing of the paragraph
the left or right edge of a paragraph inward from the margin
grade9-ict.answer: the left or right edge of a paragraph inward from the margin
acceptableAnswers: the left or right edge of a paragraph inward from the margin
grade9-ict.hint: It pulls the paragraph in from the margin.
grade9-ict.explanation: An indent sets how far the paragraph's left or right edge sits from the page margin.

grade9-ict.question: A page border is applied using:
options: the Borders and Shading dialog under the Design or Page Layout tab
grade9-ict.answer: the Borders and Shading dialog under the Design or Page Layout tab
acceptableAnswers: the Borders and Shading dialog under the Design or Page Layout tab
grade9-ict.hint: It is a page-level setting, not a text setting.
grade9-ict.explanation: Page borders are applied through the Borders and Shading dialog, which lets you choose a style, colour and width for the border on each edge of the page.

grade9-ict.question: Section breaks in a document allow:
options: columns to be formatted as a table
different parts of the document to have different formatting, such as different page orientations
the document to be split into separate files
grade9-ict.answer: different parts of the document to have different formatting, such as different page orientations
acceptableAnswers: different parts of the document to have different formatting, such as different page orientations
grade9-ict.hint: Each section can have its own layout.
grade9-ict.explanation: Section breaks divide a document into sections that can each have their own margins, orientation, headers and columns.

grade9-ict.question: The ruler at the top of a document in a word processor is used to:
options: measure the weight of the paper
set tabs, indents and margins visually
grade9-ict.answer: set tabs, indents and margins visually
acceptableAnswers: set tabs, indents and margins visually
grade9-ict.hint: You drag the markers on it.
grade9-ict.explanation: The ruler displays tab stops and indent markers that can be dragged to adjust the layout of the paragraph or document.

grade9-ict.question: The icon that looks like a floppy disk in a word processor is used to:
grade9-ict.answer: save the document
grade9-ict.hint: It is the traditional symbol for saving.
grade9-ict.explanation: The floppy disk icon is the universally recognised symbol for the Save command, even though floppy disks are no longer commonly used.

grade9-ict.question: The icon showing a magnifying glass in a word processor represents:
grade9-ict.answer: Find and Replace or Search
grade9-ict.hint: A magnifying glass means search.
grade9-ict.explanation: A magnifying glass icon typically opens the Find (and Replace) function, used to search for words or phrases in the document.

grade9-ict.question: The Undo icon (usually a curved arrow pointing left) is used to:
grade9-ict.answer: reverse the last action taken
grade9-ict.hint: It takes you back one step.
grade9-ict.explanation: Undo reverses the most recent action; pressing it repeatedly undoes multiple actions in sequence.

grade9-ict.question: The Redo icon (usually a curved arrow pointing right) is used to:
options: reapply an action that was previously undone
grade9-ict.answer: reapply an action that was previously undone
acceptableAnswers: reapply an action that was previously undone
grade9-ict.hint: It is the opposite of Undo.
grade9-ict.explanation: Redo reapplies an action that was just reversed with Undo.

grade9-ict.question: Which icon in the toolbar represents Cut?
grade9-ict.answer: A pair of scissors
grade9-ict.hint: Cutting with scissors is the metaphor.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Cut command is represented by scissors, reflecting the idea of cutting text out of a document.

grade9-ict.question: The icon showing two overlapping sheets of paper represents:
grade9-ict.answer: Copy
grade9-ict.hint: Two copies of the same sheet.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Copy icon is depicted as two overlapping document sheets, representing duplicating the selected content.

grade9-ict.question: The icon showing a clipboard with a page on it represents:
grade9-ict.answer: Paste
grade9-ict.hint: You paste from a clipboard.
grade9-ict.explanation: Paste is represented by a clipboard, reflecting the act of transferring content from the clipboard into the document.

grade9-ict.question: The ABC icon with a red wavy underline represents:
grade9-ict.answer: Spell Check
grade9-ict.hint: A wavy red line marks spelling errors.
grade9-ict.explanation: The spell check icon uses the red wavy underline that word processors use to mark spelling mistakes.

grade9-ict.question: The paragraph symbol (¶) icon in a word processor is used to:
options: show or hide non-printing formatting marks such as spaces, tabs and paragraph returns
grade9-ict.answer: show or hide non-printing formatting marks such as spaces, tabs and paragraph returns
acceptableAnswers: show or hide non-printing formatting marks such as spaces, tabs and paragraph returns
grade9-ict.hint: Toggle the display of invisible formatting marks.
grade9-ict.explanation: Clicking the ¶ icon toggles the display of non-printing characters, making spaces, tabs and paragraph marks visible for editing.

grade9-ict.question: The printer icon in the toolbar is used to:
grade9-ict.answer: open the Print dialog
grade9-ict.hint: A printer picture means print.
grade9-ict.explanation: Clicking the printer icon opens the Print dialog where you choose the printer, number of copies and page range.

grade9-ict.question: The zoom slider at the bottom-right of the screen is used to:
options: increase or decrease the magnification of the document on screen
change the font size of the selected text
grade9-ict.answer: increase or decrease the magnification of the document on screen
acceptableAnswers: increase or decrease the magnification of the document on screen
grade9-ict.hint: Drag it left to shrink, right to enlarge the view.
grade9-ict.explanation: The zoom slider adjusts how large the document appears on screen; it does not change the actual font size or page size.

grade9-ict.question: To insert a picture into a word-processed document, you use:
grade9-ict.answer: Insert > Pictures
grade9-ict.hint: Pictures are inserted from the Insert tab.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Insert tab contains the Pictures command, which opens a dialog to locate and insert an image file.

grade9-ict.question: Text wrapping around an image is controlled by:
options: the Wrap Text option in the image tools
grade9-ict.answer: the Wrap Text option in the image tools
acceptableAnswers: the Wrap Text option in the image tools
grade9-ict.hint: You choose how text flows around the picture.
grade9-ict.explanation: Wrap Text settings determine how the document's text flows in relation to an inserted image — for example, square, tight or through.

grade9-ict.question: Setting the image wrap to "In Line with Text" means:
options: the text flows over the image
the image is treated as a character and moves with the surrounding text
the image appears behind the text
the image is fixed to the page regardless of text changes
grade9-ict.answer: the image is treated as a character and moves with the surrounding text
acceptableAnswers: the image is treated as a character and moves with the surrounding text
grade9-ict.hint: It behaves like a large letter in the text flow.
grade9-ict.explanation: "In Line with Text" inserts the image as if it were a text character, so it moves when text above it is added or deleted.

grade9-ict.question: To maintain the proportions of an image while resizing it, you should:
grade9-ict.answer: drag a corner handle
grade9-ict.hint: Corners resize both dimensions at the same time.
grade9-ict.explanation: Dragging a corner handle scales both width and height equally, keeping the image's original proportions. Side handles change only one dimension.

grade9-ict.question: Cropping an image in a document:
options: trims away the unwanted parts of the image
converts the image to black and white
grade9-ict.answer: trims away the unwanted parts of the image
acceptableAnswers: trims away the unwanted parts of the image
grade9-ict.hint: Cut away what you do not want to show.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cropping removes the outer edges of an image so only the desired portion is displayed.

grade9-ict.question: Drawing shapes such as rectangles and arrows in a word processor is done through:
grade9-ict.answer: Insert > Shapes
grade9-ict.hint: Shapes are in the Insert menu.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Shapes gallery in the Insert tab provides a library of shapes — lines, rectangles, arrows, callouts — that can be drawn on the page.

grade9-ict.question: A text box in a word-processed document allows you to:
options: create a spreadsheet inside the document
add a border around the entire document
position text independently of the main text flow, anywhere on the page
grade9-ict.answer: position text independently of the main text flow, anywhere on the page
acceptableAnswers: position text independently of the main text flow, anywhere on the page
grade9-ict.hint: Text inside a box can be placed anywhere.
grade9-ict.explanation: A text box is a container that can be dragged to any position on the page, allowing text placement independent of the main document flow.

grade9-ict.question: Alt text (alternative text) added to an image in a document is used to:
options: convert the image to a drawing
describe the image for screen readers used by visually impaired users
grade9-ict.answer: describe the image for screen readers used by visually impaired users
acceptableAnswers: describe the image for screen readers used by visually impaired users
grade9-ict.hint: It makes images accessible.
grade9-ict.explanation: Alt text provides a text description of an image so screen readers can convey its content to users who cannot see the image.

grade9-ict.question: SmartArt graphics in a word processor are used to create:
options: video clips embedded in the document
visually formatted diagrams such as process flows, hierarchies and lists
grade9-ict.answer: visually formatted diagrams such as process flows, hierarchies and lists
acceptableAnswers: visually formatted diagrams such as process flows, hierarchies and lists
grade9-ict.hint: They turn text into professional-looking diagrams.
grade9-ict.explanation: SmartArt provides templates for creating diagrams — cycle, hierarchy, relationship, process — with formatted shapes and text.

grade9-ict.question: To group several shapes together so they move as one object, you:
options: select all shapes and use Group from the Format or right-click menu
convert them to a single text box
copy the shapes into a table cell
save each shape as a separate file
grade9-ict.answer: select all shapes and use Group from the Format or right-click menu
acceptableAnswers: select all shapes and use Group from the Format or right-click menu
grade9-ict.hint: Grouping locks them together.
grade9-ict.explanation: Selecting all the shapes and choosing Group combines them into one object that can be moved and resized together.

grade9-ict.question: A watermark in a word-processed document is:
options: faded text or an image placed behind the main content on every page
a border around the edge of each page
a header applied to odd-numbered pages only
a hyperlink inserted in the body text
grade9-ict.answer: faded text or an image placed behind the main content on every page
acceptableAnswers: faded text or an image placed behind the main content on every page
grade9-ict.hint: DRAFT and CONFIDENTIAL stamps are common examples.
grade9-ict.explanation: A watermark is a semi-transparent image or text placed behind the document content, often used to mark documents as DRAFT or CONFIDENTIAL.

grade9-ict.question: The Picture Format tab (or Format Picture pane) allows you to:
options: add a footnote to the document
adjust brightness, contrast, colour and apply artistic effects to an image
grade9-ict.answer: adjust brightness, contrast, colour and apply artistic effects to an image
acceptableAnswers: adjust brightness, contrast, colour and apply artistic effects to an image
grade9-ict.hint: It is the formatting tool specifically for pictures.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Picture Format tab provides controls for adjusting image brightness, contrast, sharpness, colour mode and applying visual effects.

grade9-ict.question: A cell in a word-processed table is the intersection of:
grade9-ict.answer: a row and a column
grade9-ict.hint: It is the box formed where a row meets a column.
grade9-ict.explanation: Each cell is the rectangular box formed at the intersection of one row and one column in a table.

grade9-ict.question: To move to the next cell in a table using only the keyboard, you press:
grade9-ict.answer: Tab
grade9-ict.hint: Tab moves through cells one at a time.
grade9-ict.explanation: Pressing Tab moves the cursor to the next cell in the table; Shift + Tab moves to the previous cell.

grade9-ict.question: Merging cells in a table means:
options: splitting one cell into two smaller cells
combining two or more adjacent cells into one larger cell
changing the background colour of the cell
adding a border to selected cells
grade9-ict.answer: combining two or more adjacent cells into one larger cell
acceptableAnswers: combining two or more adjacent cells into one larger cell
grade9-ict.hint: Many cells become one.
grade9-ict.explanation: Merge Cells joins adjacent selected cells into a single cell, useful for table headings that span multiple columns.

grade9-ict.question: Splitting a cell in a table means:
options: adding a new column at the edge
removing a row from the table
dividing one cell into two or more smaller cells
grade9-ict.answer: dividing one cell into two or more smaller cells
acceptableAnswers: dividing one cell into two or more smaller cells
grade9-ict.hint: One cell becomes several.
grade9-ict.explanation: Split Cells divides a cell into a specified number of rows or columns.

grade9-ict.question: To add a new row at the bottom of a table, the simplest method is:
options: drag the bottom border of the table
press Tab when the cursor is in the last cell
grade9-ict.answer: press Tab when the cursor is in the last cell
acceptableAnswers: press Tab when the cursor is in the last cell
grade9-ict.hint: Tab at the end creates a new row.
grade9-ict.explanation: Pressing Tab when you are in the last cell of a table automatically adds a new row below it.

grade9-ict.question: Text alignment inside a table cell can be set to:
options: top-left, top-centre, top-right, middle-left, middle-centre, middle-right, and so on
none — tables always use the default
grade9-ict.answer: top-left, top-centre, top-right, middle-left, middle-centre, middle-right, and so on
acceptableAnswers: top-left, top-centre, top-right, middle-left, middle-centre, middle-right, and so on
grade9-ict.hint: There are nine alignment positions for cells.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cell content can be aligned both horizontally (left, centre, right) and vertically (top, middle, bottom) within the cell.

grade9-ict.question: The header row of a table should be formatted to:
options: stand out from the data rows, for example in bold or with shading
grade9-ict.answer: stand out from the data rows, for example in bold or with shading
acceptableAnswers: stand out from the data rows, for example in bold or with shading
grade9-ict.hint: It identifies the column contents.
grade9-ict.explanation: Formatting the header row differently — bold, coloured background — makes it visually distinct so readers can immediately identify each column.

grade9-ict.question: To delete an entire row from a table, you:
options: drag the row off the page
change the row colour to white
select the row and choose Delete Rows from the Table menu or right-click menu
press the Delete key on the keyboard
grade9-ict.answer: select the row and choose Delete Rows from the Table menu or right-click menu
acceptableAnswers: select the row and choose Delete Rows from the Table menu or right-click menu
grade9-ict.hint: Select it first, then delete.
grade9-ict.explanation: Selecting the row and using Delete Rows removes the entire row and its content from the table.

grade9-ict.question: AutoFit in a table automatically adjusts:
options: the font size to fit the cell
the page margins to match the table
column widths to fit the contents or the window
the table style to match the document theme
grade9-ict.answer: column widths to fit the contents or the window
acceptableAnswers: column widths to fit the contents or the window
grade9-ict.hint: It makes columns just wide enough for their content.
grade9-ict.explanation: AutoFit adjusts column widths automatically, either to fit the content in each column or to distribute columns evenly across the page.

grade9-ict.question: Sorting data in a table by a column means:
options: rearranging the rows into alphabetical or numerical order based on that column's values
removing rows that do not match the column
grade9-ict.answer: rearranging the rows into alphabetical or numerical order based on that column's values
acceptableAnswers: rearranging the rows into alphabetical or numerical order based on that column's values
grade9-ict.hint: Sort puts the rows in order.
grade9-ict.explanation: Sorting a table rearranges all rows based on the chosen column, either A to Z, Z to A, or smallest to largest.

grade9-ict.question: A table style in a word processor applies:
options: a set of colours, borders and shading to the whole table at once
a border only around the first row
a new page layout to the document
a new font to all text in the document
grade9-ict.answer: a set of colours, borders and shading to the whole table at once
acceptableAnswers: a set of colours, borders and shading to the whole table at once
grade9-ict.hint: Like a theme for the table.
grade9-ict.explanation: Table styles apply a coordinated combination of colours, fonts and borders to the entire table in one click.

grade9-ict.question: Which feature converts existing tabbed text into a formatted table?
options: Insert > Table > Convert Text to Table
grade9-ict.answer: Insert > Table > Convert Text to Table
acceptableAnswers: Insert > Table > Convert Text to Table
grade9-ict.hint: Text separated by tabs or commas can be converted automatically.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Convert Text to Table option reads separator characters (tabs, commas, etc.) in selected text and creates a table from them.

grade9-ict.question: To open more than one document at the same time in a word processor, you:
options: close the first file before opening the next
merge both files into one before opening
open each file separately — they appear in different windows or tabs
save the first file as a template first
grade9-ict.answer: open each file separately — they appear in different windows or tabs
acceptableAnswers: open each file separately — they appear in different windows or tabs
grade9-ict.hint: Word processors support multiple open files.
grade9-ict.explanation: Most word processors allow several documents to be open simultaneously, each in its own window or tab.

grade9-ict.question: The View Side by Side feature in a word processor is used to:
options: display two documents next to each other for comparison
place two tables next to each other
show the header on the left and the footer on the right
grade9-ict.answer: display two documents next to each other for comparison
acceptableAnswers: display two documents next to each other for comparison
grade9-ict.hint: It is useful for comparing two versions of a document.
grade9-ict.explanation: View Side by Side opens two documents in adjacent windows so their content can be compared or copied between them.

grade9-ict.question: To copy text from one document and paste it into another, you would use:
options: Save both documents and then merge them
Ctrl + C to copy, switch to the other document, and then Ctrl + V to paste
Use Insert > File to transfer the text
Use Print to print and retype the text
grade9-ict.answer: Ctrl + C to copy, switch to the other document, and then Ctrl + V to paste
acceptableAnswers: Ctrl + C to copy, switch to the other document, and then Ctrl + V to paste
grade9-ict.hint: The clipboard holds copied content across windows.
grade9-ict.explanation: The clipboard retains copied content even when you switch between document windows, allowing a quick copy and paste.

grade9-ict.question: Track Changes in a word processor is used to:
options: track how many words are typed each session
automatically back up the document every minute
record all edits made to a document so they can be accepted or rejected later
record the document's edit history in a separate file
grade9-ict.answer: record all edits made to a document so they can be accepted or rejected later
acceptableAnswers: record all edits made to a document so they can be accepted or rejected later
grade9-ict.hint: Editors use it to suggest changes.
grade9-ict.explanation: Track Changes marks every insertion, deletion and formatting change so the document's author can review and accept or reject each one.

grade9-ict.question: The Compare Documents feature is used to:
options: merge two documents into one combined file
show the differences between two versions of the same document highlighted as tracked changes
check the spelling of two documents simultaneously
print two documents at the same time
grade9-ict.answer: show the differences between two versions of the same document highlighted as tracked changes
acceptableAnswers: show the differences between two versions of the same document highlighted as tracked changes
grade9-ict.hint: It finds what has changed between two versions.
grade9-ict.explanation: Compare Documents generates a new document showing all differences between two versions as tracked changes.

grade9-ict.question: A master document in a word processor is used to:
options: organise and link a long document that is split into several sub-documents
convert the document to PDF automatically
make a copy of the document in a new folder
apply the same style to all open documents
grade9-ict.answer: organise and link a long document that is split into several sub-documents
acceptableAnswers: organise and link a long document that is split into several sub-documents
grade9-ict.hint: Long reports or books are often split into chapters.
grade9-ict.explanation: A master document contains links to several sub-documents, allowing a long work to be edited in sections while maintaining a single table of contents.

grade9-ict.question: Inserting a file into an open document using Insert > Object (or Text from File) places:
options: a link that opens the file in a separate window
a footnote referencing the other document
the complete content of another file into the current document at the cursor position
a thumbnail image of the other document
grade9-ict.answer: the complete content of another file into the current document at the cursor position
acceptableAnswers: the complete content of another file into the current document at the cursor position
grade9-ict.hint: It imports the entire file content.
grade9-ict.explanation: Insert Text from File inserts all the content of a chosen file into the current document at the cursor position.

grade9-ict.question: When multiple authors edit the same document using a cloud-based word processor, this is called:
grade9-ict.answer: real-time collaboration
grade9-ict.hint: Everyone works on the same file at the same time.
grade9-ict.explanation: Cloud-based word processors allow several users to edit the same document simultaneously, with each person's changes visible to others in real time.

grade9-ict.question: Saving a document as a PDF means:
options: the document can be viewed on any device without the need for word processor software
the file can only be opened in one specific application
grade9-ict.answer: the document can be viewed on any device without the need for word processor software
acceptableAnswers: the document can be viewed on any device without the need for word processor software
grade9-ict.hint: PDF is a universal format.
grade9-ict.explanation: PDF (Portable Document Format) can be opened on any device with a PDF reader, preserving the layout exactly without needing the original software.

grade9-ict.question: The Spelling and Grammar checker in a word processor:
options: guarantees that the document is completely error-free
translates the document into another language
identifies possible spelling mistakes and grammatical errors but may miss context-based errors
deletes all grammatical errors automatically without prompting
grade9-ict.answer: identifies possible spelling mistakes and grammatical errors but may miss context-based errors
acceptableAnswers: identifies possible spelling mistakes and grammatical errors but may miss context-based errors
grade9-ict.hint: It is helpful but not infallible.
grade9-ict.explanation: Spell checkers catch many errors but can miss correctly-spelt words used in the wrong context, so human proofreading is still necessary.

grade9-ict.question: The word count feature in a word processor shows:
options: the font size of the longest word
the maximum number of words allowed
the number of formatting errors found
the total number of words, characters, paragraphs and pages in the document
grade9-ict.answer: the total number of words, characters, paragraphs and pages in the document
acceptableAnswers: the total number of words, characters, paragraphs and pages in the document
grade9-ict.hint: It provides statistics about the document.
grade9-ict.explanation: Word Count (found under the Review tab or on the status bar) displays statistics including word count, character count, paragraph count and page count.

grade9-ict.question: A style in a word processor is:
options: a named set of formatting settings that can be applied with a single click
a type of border applied to paragraphs
a shortcut for printing the document
grade9-ict.answer: a named set of formatting settings that can be applied with a single click
acceptableAnswers: a named set of formatting settings that can be applied with a single click
grade9-ict.hint: One click applies many formats at once.
grade9-ict.explanation: A style saves multiple formatting settings (font, size, spacing, colour) under one name, allowing consistent formatting in a single click.

grade9-ict.question: Applying the Heading 1 style to text in a long document allows the word processor to:
options: save the text in a separate file
include that text in an automatic Table of Contents
send the text to a different document
print that text in a larger font only
grade9-ict.answer: include that text in an automatic Table of Contents
acceptableAnswers: include that text in an automatic Table of Contents
grade9-ict.hint: Heading styles are recognised by the TOC generator.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Table of Contents tool collects all text marked with Heading styles and builds a contents page automatically.

grade9-ict.question: Modifying a style in a document changes:
options: only text added after the modification
all text in the document that uses that style at once
grade9-ict.answer: all text in the document that uses that style at once
acceptableAnswers: all text in the document that uses that style at once
grade9-ict.hint: One change updates every instance.
grade9-ict.explanation: If you modify a style, every paragraph formatted with that style updates immediately throughout the entire document.

grade9-ict.question: The Normal style in a word processor applies to:
options: body text that has no other specific style applied
only the first paragraph of the document
grade9-ict.answer: body text that has no other specific style applied
acceptableAnswers: body text that has no other specific style applied
grade9-ict.hint: Normal is the default paragraph style.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Normal style is the default applied to ordinary body text when no other style has been chosen.

grade9-ict.question: A character style differs from a paragraph style because a character style:
options: can only be used on the first character of each word
removes all previous formatting from the paragraph
applies formatting only to selected characters within a paragraph, not to the whole paragraph
applies to the whole document at once
grade9-ict.answer: applies formatting only to selected characters within a paragraph, not to the whole paragraph
acceptableAnswers: applies formatting only to selected characters within a paragraph, not to the whole paragraph
grade9-ict.hint: It works at the character level, not the paragraph level.
grade9-ict.explanation: Character styles apply formatting (bold, colour, font size) to selected characters only, while paragraph styles apply to the entire paragraph.

grade9-ict.question: The Styles gallery or Styles pane in a word processor shows:
options: all recent changes made by Track Changes
all the named styles available in the current document or template
grade9-ict.answer: all the named styles available in the current document or template
acceptableAnswers: all the named styles available in the current document or template
grade9-ict.hint: It lists your formatting options.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Styles pane lists every style defined in the document or its template, allowing you to apply, modify or create styles.

grade9-ict.question: Using consistent heading styles throughout a long document helps because:
options: it removes the need for spell checking
it creates a uniform structure, allows automatic TOC generation and aids navigation
grade9-ict.answer: it creates a uniform structure, allows automatic TOC generation and aids navigation
acceptableAnswers: it creates a uniform structure, allows automatic TOC generation and aids navigation
grade9-ict.hint: Structure and navigation are the key benefits.
grade9-ict.explanation: Consistent heading styles give the document clear visual structure, enable automatic table-of-contents generation, and allow quick navigation using the Document Map.

grade9-ict.question: A Quick Style set is a collection of:
options: coordinated styles for headings, body text and other elements that work well together visually
recent documents opened in the word processor
grade9-ict.answer: coordinated styles for headings, body text and other elements that work well together visually
acceptableAnswers: coordinated styles for headings, body text and other elements that work well together visually
grade9-ict.hint: All the styles match each other.
grade9-ict.explanation: A Quick Style set provides a complete, visually coordinated set of styles for an entire document, making it easy to change the overall look.

grade9-ict.question: To create a new style based on existing text formatting, you:
options: type the style name into the font size box
print the document and write the style name on it
save the document under a new file name
select the formatted text and click New Style in the Styles pane
grade9-ict.answer: select the formatted text and click New Style in the Styles pane
acceptableAnswers: select the formatted text and click New Style in the Styles pane
grade9-ict.hint: Use the formatted text as the template for the new style.
grade9-ict.explanation: Selecting formatted text and choosing New Style creates a named style with all the formatting of the selected text.

grade9-ict.question: The difference between Heading 1 and Heading 2 styles is that:
options: Heading 1 is always blue and Heading 2 is always red
Heading 1 is used for main headings and Heading 2 for subheadings, creating a hierarchy
Heading 2 can only be used once per document
Heading 1 cannot include any bold text
grade9-ict.answer: Heading 1 is used for main headings and Heading 2 for subheadings, creating a hierarchy
acceptableAnswers: Heading 1 is used for main headings and Heading 2 for subheadings, creating a hierarchy
grade9-ict.hint: They form a hierarchy of heading levels.
grade9-ict.explanation: Heading styles are numbered to show hierarchy: Heading 1 for chapter titles, Heading 2 for sections within a chapter, and so on.

grade9-ict.question: Clearing all formatting from selected text restores it to:
grade9-ict.answer: the Normal (default paragraph) style
grade9-ict.hint: Clearing formatting resets to the base style.
grade9-ict.explanation: The Clear Formatting command removes all manually applied and style-based formatting, returning the text to the default Normal style.

grade9-ict.question: Styles improve consistency in a document by ensuring:
options: each paragraph uses a different font
the same type of text always looks the same throughout the document
every page has a different colour scheme
grade9-ict.answer: the same type of text always looks the same throughout the document
acceptableAnswers: the same type of text always looks the same throughout the document
grade9-ict.hint: One style definition means uniform appearance.
grade9-ict.explanation: Styles guarantee consistency because all text using a given style is formatted identically, removing the risk of accidental formatting variation.

grade9-ict.question: Mail merge is used to:
options: check the spelling of a mailing list
produce multiple personalised copies of a letter or document from one template and a list of data
grade9-ict.answer: produce multiple personalised copies of a letter or document from one template and a list of data
acceptableAnswers: produce multiple personalised copies of a letter or document from one template and a list of data
grade9-ict.hint: One template, many personalised letters.
grade9-ict.explanation: Mail merge creates a personalised copy of the main document for every record in the data source, inserting individual details automatically.

grade9-ict.question: In mail merge, the main document contains:
options: the fixed text and merge field placeholders used in every copy
the list of names and addresses
a copy of the data source
grade9-ict.answer: the fixed text and merge field placeholders used in every copy
acceptableAnswers: the fixed text and merge field placeholders used in every copy
grade9-ict.hint: It is the letter template.
grade9-ict.explanation: The main document has the wording common to all copies and contains merge field markers that will be replaced by individual data.

grade9-ict.question: In mail merge, the data source is:
options: the main document with the letter text
the printer used to print the letters
the file containing the records of names, addresses and other personal information
grade9-ict.answer: the file containing the records of names, addresses and other personal information
acceptableAnswers: the file containing the records of names, addresses and other personal information
grade9-ict.hint: It holds the variable information.
grade9-ict.explanation: The data source (often a spreadsheet or database table) contains the individual records whose fields are inserted into each merged copy.

grade9-ict.question: A merge field in a main document appears as:
options: a field name inside chevrons, such as «FirstName»
a footnote at the bottom of the page
a small image of the field
grade9-ict.answer: a field name inside chevrons, such as «FirstName»
acceptableAnswers: a field name inside chevrons, such as «FirstName»
grade9-ict.hint: Look at how they appear in the letter template.
grade9-ict.explanation: Merge fields are displayed between chevron marks (« ») in the main document and are replaced by the corresponding data values during the merge.

grade9-ict.question: If a data source has 50 records, a completed mail merge produces:
grade9-ict.answer: 50 personalised copies of the document
grade9-ict.hint: One copy is produced per record.
grade9-ict.explanation: Mail merge creates one personalised copy of the main document for each record in the data source, so 50 records produce 50 letters.

grade9-ict.question: One advantage of using mail merge rather than typing each letter individually is:
options: it checks the spelling for every letter individually
each letter is saved as a separate file automatically
it selects a different font for each recipient
the same wording is guaranteed in every letter and the process is much faster for large numbers
grade9-ict.answer: the same wording is guaranteed in every letter and the process is much faster for large numbers
acceptableAnswers: the same wording is guaranteed in every letter and the process is much faster for large numbers
grade9-ict.hint: One template, consistent wording, automated.
grade9-ict.explanation: Mail merge produces consistent wording in every copy and is extremely fast for large mailings compared to typing each letter separately.

grade9-ict.question: The mail merge wizard in a word processor guides you through:
options: drawing a chart of the data
converting the data source into a PDF
selecting the document type, data source, and fields, then completing the merge step by step

grade9-ict.question: Personal data collected for one purpose may:

be published on any public website
not be used for a different purpose
be kept for ever without any reason
grade9-ict.answer: not be used for a different purpose

grade9-ict.question: Who is responsible for keeping personal data accurate and up to date?

grade9-ict.explanation: The organisation that collects and holds personal data is responsible for keeping it accurate and up to date.

The postman who delivers the letters
grade9-ict.answer: The organisation that collects it

grade9-ict.question: A data protection act says that personal data should be kept:
grade9-ict.hint: Old data that is no longer needed is a risk, not an asset.
grade9-ict.explanation: Data must not be kept longer than the purpose requires; once it is no longer needed it should be deleted.
options: for at least twenty-five whole years
only for as long as it is needed
on paper rather than on a computer
in a language chosen by the owner
grade9-ict.answer: only for as long as it is needed
acceptableAnswers: only for as long as it is needed

grade9-ict.question:

D  Rest the wrists on a support and change position regularly.
(i) Eye strain    (ii) Back ache    (iii) Wrist injury    (iv) Glare from the screen
grade9-ict.hint: Match the part of the body to the thing that supports or rests it.
grade9-ict.explanation: Eye strain matches A, back ache matches B, a wrist injury matches D and glare matches C.
grade9-ict.answer: A, B, D, C

grade9-ict.question: The top of the screen should be roughly level with:

grade9-ict.question: For each rule below, tick True or False. Food and drink may be taken to the computer table.

grade9-ict.explanation: Food and drink are kept away from computers because a spill can destroy a keyboard or a whole machine.
grade9-ict.answer: False

grade9-ict.question: For each rule below, tick True or False. Trailing cables on the floor should be covered or tied out of the way.

grade9-ict.hint: Files may still be open.

grade9-ict.answer: True

grade9-ict.question:

(i) Test that the problem has gone.
(ii) Identify exactly what the problem is.
(iii) Decide on the most likely cause.
(iv) Apply the fix.
grade9-ict.hint: Nothing can be fixed before it has been identified, and nothing is finished before it has been tested.
grade9-ict.explanation: The order is identify the problem, decide the likely cause, apply the fix, then test that it has gone - so (ii) is 1, (iii) is 2, (iv) is 3 and (i) is 4.

grade9-ict.question: A monitor shows no picture although its power light is on. Which check should be made first?

The free space left on the hard disk
The version of the word processor used
grade9-ict.answer: The cable between monitor and computer
acceptableAnswers: The cable between monitor and computer

grade9-ict.question:

grade9-ict.hint: Match each fault to the part of the system it involves.
grade9-ict.explanation: No sound matches C, the printer fault matches A and the network fault matches B.
grade9-ict.answer: C, A, B

grade9-ict.question: A file has been deleted by mistake. Where should the user look first?
grade9-ict.hint: Deleted files are not removed from the disk straight away.

grade9-ict.answer: In the Recycle Bin

grade9-ict.question:

grade9-ict.question:

(iv) A secure private link to an office network made across the Internet.

grade9-ict.explanation: One laboratory is a LAN (A); branches in different countries need a WAN (B); a phone and a headset a metre apart make a PAN (C); a secure private tunnel across the Internet is a VPN (D).

grade9-ict.question: What do the letters LAN stand for?

grade9-ict.question: Which one of these is an advantage of joining computers in a network?

grade9-ict.explanation: On a network one printer can serve many users, which saves both money and space.
options: Files cannot be copied between users

Each computer needs its own printer
A printer can be shared between users
grade9-ict.answer: A printer can be shared between users
acceptableAnswers: A printer can be shared between users

grade9-ict.question:

grade9-ict.explanation: A router matches A, a network interface card matches C and a firewall matches B.

grade9-ict.explanation: A blog matches A, a video conference matches C and a wiki matches B.

a short message sent to a mobile phone

acceptableAnswers: a sound recording published on the Internet

grade9-ict.question:

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE body questions. Written as non-visual counterparts at mark sizes where a chapter held only figures.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE body questions. Written as non-visual counterparts at mark sizes where a chapter held only figures.
