parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the value of n, if 64 = 2n.
parts.hint: Keep multiplying 2 by itself until you reach 64.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE 2025 Q10, Q17 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the value of k, if 125 = 5k.
parts.hint: Write 125 as a power of 5.
parts.explanation: 5 × 5 × 5 = 125, so 125 = 5<sup>3</sup> and k = 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE 2025 Q10, Q17 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Simplify 3p2 × 4p3.
parts.hint: Multiply the numbers, then add the indices of p.
parts.explanation: 3 × 4 = 12 and p<sup>2</sup> × p<sup>3</sup> = p<sup>5</sup>, so the answer is 12p<sup>5</sup>.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE 2025 Q10, Q17 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Simplify 15x5 ÷ 5x2.
parts.hint: Divide the numbers, then subtract the indices of x.
parts.explanation: 15 ÷ 5 = 3 and x<sup>5</sup> ÷ x<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>3</sup>, so the answer is 3x<sup>3</sup>.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE 2025 Q10, Q17 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Simplify (5a2)3.
parts.hint: The index outside the bracket applies to the 5 as well as to a<sup>2</sup>.
parts.explanation: (5a<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3</sup> = 5<sup>3</sup> × a<sup>2×3</sup> = 125a<sup>6</sup>.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE 2025 Q10, Q17 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write 6<sup>−2</sup> as a fraction.
parts.hint: Work out 6 squared first, then put 1 over the result.
parts.explanation: 6<sup>2</sup> = 36, so 6<sup>−2</sup> = 1/36.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE 2025 Q10, Q17 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Evaluate 3<sup>−3</sup>.
parts.hint: Work out 3 cubed first, then take its reciprocal.
parts.explanation: 3<sup>3</sup> = 27, so 3<sup>−3</sup> = 1/27.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE 2025 Q10, Q17 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>8</sub> as a power of 2.
parts.hint: Write 8 as a power of 2, then use the negative index rule.
parts.explanation: 8 = 2<sup>3</sup>, so <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>8</sub> = 1 ÷ 2<sup>3</sup> = 2<sup>−3</sup>.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE 2025 Q10, Q17 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Simplify a2 × a−6.
parts.hint: Add the indices, keeping the minus sign.
parts.explanation: a<sup>2</sup> × a<sup>−6</sup> = a<sup>2+(−6)</sup> = a<sup>−4</sup>.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE 2025 Q10, Q17 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Evaluate (1⁄4)−2.
parts.hint: A negative index turns the fraction upside down first.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which of the following is equal to a3 × a4?
parts.hint: Multiplying powers of the same letter adds the indices.
parts.explanation: a<sup>3</sup> × a<sup>4</sup> = a<sup>3+4</sup> = a<sup>7</sup>. a<sup>12</sup> comes from multiplying the indices instead of adding; a<sup>1</sup> from subtracting; 2a<sup>7</sup> from also adding the invisible coefficients.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What is the value of 4<sup>0</sup>?
parts.hint: Think about what happens to 4<sup>2</sup> ÷ 4<sup>2</sup>.
parts.explanation: 4<sup>0</sup> = 1. The common mistake is to answer 0 because the index is 0, but 4<sup>2</sup> ÷ 4<sup>2</sup> = 4<sup>0</sup> and any number divided by itself is 1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which of the following is equal to 2<sup>−3</sup>?
parts.hint: A negative index does not make the answer negative.
parts.explanation: 2<sup>−3</sup> = 1 ÷ 2<sup>3</sup> = 1/8. −8 comes from reading the minus as a sign on the answer; −6 and 1/6 come from multiplying 2 by 3 instead of cubing it.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Simplify (x2)5.
parts.hint: A power of a power multiplies the indices.
parts.explanation: (x<sup>2</sup>)<sup>5</sup> = x<sup>2×5</sup> = x<sup>10</sup>. x<sup>7</sup> comes from adding the indices, x<sup>25</sup> from squaring the 5, and x<sup>3</sup> from subtracting.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What is the value of n if 3n = 27?
parts.hint: Write 27 as a power of 3.
parts.explanation: 27 = 3<sup>3</sup>, so n = 3. n = 9 comes from thinking 3 × 9 = 27; n = 6 from adding six 3s; n = 27 from confusing the base and the result.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which of the following is equal to 5<sup>−2</sup>?
parts.hint: A negative index never makes the result negative.
parts.explanation: 5<sup>−2</sup> = 1 ÷ 5<sup>2</sup> = 1/25. −25 comes from treating the − as negating the whole result; 1/10 and −10 come from multiplying 5 × 2 instead of squaring.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Indices, "solve simple equations involving indices"; NCE 2025 Q17 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the value of m, if 81 = 3m.
parts.hint: Keep multiplying 3 by itself until you reach 81.
parts.explanation: 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81, so 81 = 3<sup>4</sup> and m = 4.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Hence, solve 32x ÷ 3x−1 = 81.
parts.hint: Subtract the indices on the left, then compare with your answer to part (a).
parts.explanation: Dividing subtracts the indices: 3<sup>2x−(x−1)</sup> = 3<sup>x+1</sup>. From part (a), 81 = 3<sup>4</sup>, so 3<sup>x+1</sup> = 3<sup>4</sup>. Comparing indices: x + 1 = 4, giving x = 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Indices; NCE 2025 Q17.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the value of m, if 27 = 3m.
parts.hint: Keep multiplying 3 by itself until you reach 27.
parts.explanation: 3 × 3 × 3 = 27, so 27 = 3<sup>3</sup> and m = 3.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Hence, solve 36x ÷ 34x = 27.
parts.hint: Subtract the indices on the left, then compare with your answer to part (a).
parts.explanation: Subtracting the indices: 3<sup>6x−4x</sup> = 3<sup>2x</sup>. From part (a), 27 = 3<sup>3</sup>, so 3<sup>2x</sup> = 3<sup>3</sup>. Comparing indices: 2x = 3, giving x = 3/2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE past-paper level (difficulty 3–4).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve 4x+1 = 64.
parts.hint: Write 64 as a power of 4, then compare the indices.
parts.explanation: 64 = 4<sup>3</sup>, so 4<sup>x+1</sup> = 4<sup>3</sup>. Comparing indices: x + 1 = 3, giving x = 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE past-paper level (difficulty 3–4).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve 23x ÷ 2x = 16.
parts.hint: Subtract the indices on the left first.
parts.explanation: 2<sup>3x</sup> ÷ 2<sup>x</sup> = 2<sup>3x−x</sup> = 2<sup>2x</sup>. Since 16 = 2<sup>4</sup>, we get 2x = 4, so x = 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE past-paper level (difficulty 3–4).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Simplify (2x3)4 ÷ (4x2)2.
parts.hint: Expand each bracket first, then divide.
parts.explanation: (2x<sup>3</sup>)<sup>4</sup> = 16x<sup>12</sup> and (4x<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = 16x<sup>4</sup>. Dividing: 16 ÷ 16 = 1 and x<sup>12−4</sup> = x<sup>8</sup>.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE past-paper level (difficulty 3–4).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Simplify (3a2b)2 × 2a.
parts.hint: Square the bracket first, then multiply by 2a.
parts.explanation: (3a<sup>2</sup>b)<sup>2</sup> = 9a<sup>4</sup>b<sup>2</sup>. Multiplying by 2a: 9 × 2 = 18 and a<sup>4</sup> × a = a<sup>5</sup>, giving 18a<sup>5</sup>b<sup>2</sup>.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE past-paper level (difficulty 3–4).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve 5x−2 = 53x−8.
parts.hint: The bases are the same, so set the indices equal.
parts.explanation: x − 2 = 3x − 8. Rearranging: 6 = 2x, giving x = 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE past-paper level (difficulty 3–4).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Simplify 8a6 ÷ (2a2)2.
parts.hint: Expand (2a<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> first.
parts.explanation: (2a<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = 4a<sup>4</sup>. Then 8a<sup>6</sup> ÷ 4a<sup>4</sup> = 2a<sup>2</sup>.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE past-paper level (difficulty 3–4).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Evaluate 3<sup>−1</sup> + 3<sup>−2</sup>.
parts.hint: Write each term as a fraction, then find a common denominator.
parts.explanation: 3<sup>−1</sup> = 1/3 and 3<sup>−2</sup> = 1/9. Adding: 3/9 + 1/9 = 4/9.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE past-paper level (difficulty 3–4).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Simplify (2x−1y2)3, giving your answer as a fraction.
parts.hint: Cube every factor inside the bracket.
parts.explanation: (2x<sup>−1</sup>y<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3</sup> = 2<sup>3</sup>x<sup>−3</sup>y<sup>6</sup> = 8x<sup>−3</sup>y<sup>6</sup> = 8y<sup>6</sup>/x<sup>3</sup>.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE past-paper level (difficulty 3–4).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve 32−x = 1⁄9.
parts.hint: Write 1/9 as a power of 3, then compare the indices.
parts.explanation: 1/9 = 3<sup>−2</sup>, so 3<sup>2−x</sup> = 3<sup>−2</sup>. Comparing: 2 − x = −2, giving x = 4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE past-paper level (difficulty 3–4).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Simplify x−2 × x5 ÷ x−1.
parts.hint: Add then subtract the indices in order, remembering that dividing by x<sup>−1</sup> adds 1 to the index.
parts.explanation: x<sup>−2+5</sup> = x<sup>3</sup>, then x<sup>3</sup> ÷ x<sup>−1</sup> = x<sup>3−(−1)</sup> = x<sup>4</sup>.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Indices; NCE past-paper level (difficulty 3–4).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the value of p if 2p = 1⁄16.
parts.hint: Write 1/16 as a power of 2.
parts.explanation: 1/16 = 1/2<sup>4</sup> = 2<sup>−4</sup>, so p = −4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Indices; NCE Q17 "find m, hence solve" pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the value of m if 16 = 2m.
parts.hint: Write 16 as a product of 2s.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Hence, solve 23x+1 ÷ 2x+1 = 16.
parts.hint: Subtract the indices on the left, then compare with part (a).
parts.explanation: 2<sup>3x+1</sup> ÷ 2<sup>x+1</sup> = 2<sup>(3x+1)−(x+1)</sup> = 2<sup>2x</sup>. From part (a), 16 = 2<sup>4</sup>, so 2<sup>2x</sup> = 2<sup>4</sup>. Comparing: 2x = 4, giving x = 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Indices; NCE Q17 "find k, hence solve with negative index" pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the value of k if 8 = 2k.
parts.hint: 2 × 2 × 2 = ?
parts.explanation: 2<sup>3</sup> = 8, so k = 3.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Hence, solve 2x+1 = 1⁄8.
parts.hint: Write 1/8 as a power of 2 using your answer to part (a).
parts.explanation: 1/8 = 1/2<sup>3</sup> = 2<sup>−3</sup>. So 2<sup>x+1</sup> = 2<sup>−3</sup>. Comparing indices: x + 1 = −3, giving x = −4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line passes through the points A (0, 1) and B (3, 7). Find the gradient of the line AB.
parts.hint: Gradient is the change in y divided by the change in x.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (7 − 1) ÷ (3 − 0) = 6 ÷ 3 = 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining (1, 2) and (4, 11).
parts.hint: Subtract the y values, then the x values, in the same order.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (11 − 2) ÷ (4 − 1) = 9 ÷ 3 = 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What is the gradient of a horizontal line?
parts.hint: A horizontal line does not rise at all.
parts.explanation: The change in y is 0 for any change in x, so the gradient is 0 ÷ (change in x) = 0.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining (2, 5) and (6, 13).
parts.hint: Rise over run.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (13 − 5) ÷ (6 − 2) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining (−1, 4) and (3, −4).
parts.hint: Take care with the negative coordinates; subtract in the same order on both.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (−4 − 4) ÷ (3 − (−1)) = −8 ÷ 4 = −2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining (0, 0) and (5, 10).
parts.hint: Rise over run from the origin.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (10 − 0) ÷ (5 − 0) = 10 ÷ 5 = 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining (−2, −3) and (2, 5).
parts.hint: Subtracting a negative adds.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (5 − (−3)) ÷ (2 − (−2)) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write down the gradient of the line y = 3x + 5.
parts.hint: In y = mx + c, the gradient is m.
parts.explanation: Comparing with y = mx + c, the number multiplying x is 3, so the gradient is 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write down the gradient of the line y = −2x + 7.
parts.hint: The gradient is the number in front of x, including its sign.
parts.explanation: Comparing with y = mx + c gives m = −2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line 2y = 6x − 4.
parts.hint: Rearrange into the form y = mx + c first.
parts.explanation: Dividing every term by 2 gives y = 3x − 2, so the gradient is 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line is parallel to y = 4x − 1. Write down its gradient.
parts.hint: Parallel lines have equal gradients.
parts.explanation: Parallel lines have the same gradient, so this line also has gradient 4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining (3, 3) and (7, 3).
parts.hint: What do you notice about the two y values?
parts.explanation: The y values are equal, so the change in y is 0 and the gradient is 0 ÷ 4 = 0.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line 3x + y = 9.
parts.hint: Make y the subject.
parts.explanation: Rearranging gives y = −3x + 9, so the gradient is −3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining (−4, 2) and (0, 0).
parts.hint: Your answer will be a fraction.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (0 − 2) ÷ (0 − (−4)) = −2 ÷ 4 = −1/2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line 4y = 8x + 12.
parts.hint: Divide through by 4.
parts.explanation: Dividing every term by 4 gives y = 2x + 3, so the gradient is 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining (5, −2) and (1, 6).
parts.hint: Keep the points in the same order top and bottom.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (6 − (−2)) ÷ (1 − 5) = 8 ÷ (−4) = −2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The lines y = 5x + 2 and y = kx − 3 are parallel. Find the value of k.
parts.hint: Parallel means the gradients match.
parts.explanation: Parallel lines have equal gradients, so k = 5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining (0, 7) and (2, 1).
parts.hint: The line falls, so expect a negative answer.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (1 − 7) ÷ (2 − 0) = −6 ÷ 2 = −3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining (−3, 1) and (1, 9).
parts.hint: Rise over run.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (9 − 1) ÷ (1 − (−3)) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining (6, 4) and (2, 4).
parts.hint: Look at the y values before calculating.
parts.explanation: Both points have y = 4, so the line is horizontal and its gradient is 0.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line has gradient 2 and cuts the y-axis at 1. Write down its equation.
parts.hint: Substitute m and c into y = mx + c.
parts.explanation: With m = 2 and c = 1, the equation is y = 2x + 1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line passes through A (0, 1) and B (3, 7). State the equation of the line AB.
parts.hint: Find the gradient first; the point (0, 1) gives c straight away.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (7 − 1) ÷ 3 = 2. The line crosses the y-axis at (0, 1), so c = 1 and the equation is y = 2x + 1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the equation of the line with gradient 3 passing through (0, −4).
parts.hint: The point (0, c) gives the intercept directly.
parts.explanation: With m = 3 and c = −4, the equation is y = 3x − 4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the equation of the line with gradient −1 passing through (0, 5).
parts.hint: A gradient of −1 is written as −x, not −1x.
parts.explanation: With m = −1 and c = 5, the equation is y = −x + 5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the equation of the line with gradient 4 passing through the origin.
parts.hint: Through the origin means c = 0.
parts.explanation: The origin is (0, 0), so c = 0 and the equation is y = 4x.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line has gradient 2 and passes through (1, 5). Find its equation.
parts.hint: Substitute the point into y = 2x + c to find c.
parts.explanation: Substituting: 5 = 2(1) + c, so c = 3 and the equation is y = 2x + 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line has gradient 3 and passes through (2, 7). Find its equation.
parts.hint: Put the point into y = 3x + c.
parts.explanation: Substituting: 7 = 3(2) + c = 6 + c, so c = 1 and the equation is y = 3x + 1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line has gradient −2 and passes through (−1, 4). Find its equation.
parts.hint: Take care with the two negatives when you substitute.
parts.explanation: Substituting: 4 = −2(−1) + c = 2 + c, so c = 2 and the equation is y = −2x + 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line passing through (2, 3) and (4, 7).
parts.hint: Find the gradient first, then use one of the points to find c.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (7 − 3) ÷ (4 − 2) = 2. Substituting (2, 3): 3 = 2(2) + c, so c = −1 and the equation is y = 2x − 1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line passing through (0, 6) and (3, 0).
parts.hint: One of the points is on the y-axis.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (0 − 6) ÷ (3 − 0) = −2. The point (0, 6) gives c = 6, so the equation is y = −2x + 6.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write down the equation of the x-axis.
parts.hint: Every point on it has the same y value.
parts.explanation: Every point on the x-axis has y = 0, so its equation is y = 0.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write down the equation of the y-axis.
parts.hint: Every point on it has the same x value.
parts.explanation: Every point on the y-axis has x = 0, so its equation is x = 0.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the equation of the horizontal line through (2, 5).
parts.hint: A horizontal line keeps y constant.
parts.explanation: A horizontal line through (2, 5) has y = 5 everywhere, so its equation is y = 5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the equation of the vertical line through (3, −1).
parts.hint: A vertical line keeps x constant.
parts.explanation: A vertical line through (3, −1) has x = 3 everywhere, so its equation is x = 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line is parallel to y = 2x + 7 and passes through (0, −3). Find its equation.
parts.hint: Parallel lines share a gradient; the point gives c.
parts.explanation: Parallel means m = 2. The point (0, −3) gives c = −3, so the equation is y = 2x − 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line is parallel to y = −3x + 1 and passes through (1, 2). Find its equation.
parts.hint: Use m = −3 and substitute the point.
parts.explanation: Parallel gives m = −3. Substituting (1, 2): 2 = −3(1) + c, so c = 5 and the equation is y = −3x + 5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line passing through (−2, 1) and (2, 9).
parts.hint: Watch the signs in the gradient calculation.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (9 − 1) ÷ (2 − (−2)) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2. Substituting (2, 9): 9 = 4 + c, so c = 5 and the equation is y = 2x + 5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write down the y-intercept of the line y = 5x − 8.
parts.hint: In y = mx + c, the intercept is c.
parts.explanation: Comparing with y = mx + c gives c = −8.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line passing through (1, 1) and (3, 7).
parts.hint: Gradient first, then substitute either point.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (7 − 1) ÷ (3 − 1) = 3. Substituting (1, 1): 1 = 3 + c, so c = −2 and the equation is y = 3x − 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line is parallel to 2y = 4x + 6 and passes through (0, 1). Find its equation.
parts.hint: Rearrange the given line before comparing gradients.
parts.explanation: 2y = 4x + 6 gives y = 2x + 3, so the gradient is 2. With c = 1, the equation is y = 2x + 1.

stimulus.altText: A squared coordinate grid with the x-axis and y-axis drawn and numbered from minus one to eight.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Coordinates, straight-line graphs; NCE 2025 Q29 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: On the grid above, draw the graph of y = x + 2.
parts.rubric: One mark for a straight line with gradient 1. One mark for the line passing through (0, 2) and (4, 6). Accept any correctly drawn straight line through those points, extended across the grid.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write down the coordinates of the point where your line crosses the y-axis.
parts.hint: Read off the value of y where the line meets the vertical axis.
parts.explanation: The line y = x + 2 meets the y-axis where x = 0, giving y = 2. The point is (0, 2).

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q11 MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What is the gradient of the line y = 7 − 2x?
parts.hint: Rewrite it as y = mx + c before reading off m.
parts.explanation: y = 7 − 2x is y = −2x + 7, so the gradient is −2. Answering 7 reads the intercept instead; answering 2 drops the minus sign.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q11 MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which of these lines is parallel to y = 3x − 4?
parts.hint: Parallel lines have the same gradient.
parts.explanation: Parallel means the gradient must also be 3, so y = 3x + 9. The second answer flips the sign; the third swaps the gradient and intercept; the fourth is the perpendicular gradient.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q11 MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A straight line has a gradient of 0. Which statement describes the line?
parts.hint: A gradient of 0 means no change in y.
parts.explanation: Gradient 0 means y does not change as x changes, so the line is horizontal. A vertical line has no gradient at all, because the change in x is 0 and division by 0 is undefined.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 extended to a three-part problem.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line passes through P (−2, −5) and Q (4, 7). Find the gradient of PQ.
parts.hint: Subtract the y values and the x values in the same order.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (7 − (−5)) ÷ (4 − (−2)) = 12 ÷ 6 = 2.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line PQ.
parts.hint: Put one of the two points into y = mx + c.
parts.explanation: With m = 2, substituting Q (4, 7): 7 = 2(4) + c = 8 + c, so c = −1 and the equation is y = 2x − 1.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The point R (1, k) lies on the line PQ. Find the value of k.
parts.hint: Substitute x = 1 into your equation.
parts.explanation: Substituting x = 1 into y = 2x − 1 gives y = 2(1) − 1 = 1, so k = 1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Coordinates, gradient of parallel lines; NCE 2024 Q26 pattern.

parts.label: a.i
parts.prompt: A line L has equation 2y = 6x − 8. Find the gradient of L.
parts.hint: Divide every term by 2 to reach the form y = mx + c.
parts.explanation: Dividing throughout by 2 gives y = 3x − 4, so the gradient is 3.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.prompt: Write down the y-intercept of L.
parts.hint: It is the constant term once y is the subject.
parts.explanation: From y = 3x − 4, the y-intercept is −4.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line parallel to L that passes through (0, 5).
parts.hint: Parallel lines share a gradient, and the point given is on the y-axis.
parts.explanation: Parallel to L means the gradient is also 3. The point (0, 5) is the y-intercept, so c = 5 and the equation is y = 3x + 5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE past-paper level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining (2, 1) and (6, 9).
parts.hint: Rise divided by run.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (9 − 1) ÷ (6 − 2) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE past-paper level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining (−1, 3) and (5, −3).
parts.hint: The line falls — expect a negative answer.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (−3 − 3) ÷ (5 − (−1)) = −6 ÷ 6 = −1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE past-paper level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line 2x − 3y = 6.
parts.hint: Make y the subject first.
parts.explanation: Rearranging: 3y = 2x − 6, so y = <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub>x − 2. The gradient is <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub>.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE past-paper level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line x + 2y = 8.
parts.hint: Make y the subject first.
parts.explanation: Rearranging: 2y = −x + 8, so y = −<sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub>x + 4. The gradient is −<sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub>.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE past-paper level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining (4, −1) and (−2, −4).
parts.hint: Subtract in the same order; dividing two negatives gives a positive.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (−4 − (−1)) ÷ (−2 − 4) = −3 ÷ −6 = <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub>.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE past-paper level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line 3y = 6x − 9.
parts.hint: Divide every term by 3.
parts.explanation: Dividing throughout by 3 gives y = 2x − 3, so the gradient is 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE past-paper level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining (0, −3) and (5, 7).
parts.hint: One point is on the y-axis.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (7 − (−3)) ÷ (5 − 0) = 10 ÷ 5 = 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE past-paper level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the x-intercept of the line y = 2x − 6.
parts.hint: Set y = 0 and solve for x.
parts.explanation: Setting y = 0: 0 = 2x − 6, so x = 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE past-paper level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the x-intercept of the line y = −x + 5.
parts.hint: Set y = 0 and solve for x.
parts.explanation: Setting y = 0: 0 = −x + 5, so x = 5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE past-paper level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The point (3, k) lies on the line y = 2x − 1. Find the value of k.
parts.hint: Substitute x = 3 into the equation.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE past-paper level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The point (k, 3) lies on the line y = −x + 7. Find the value of k.
parts.hint: Substitute y = 3 and solve for x.
parts.explanation: 3 = −k + 7, so k = 4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE past-paper level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line passing through (1, 4) and (3, −2).
parts.hint: Find the gradient first, then substitute one point to find c.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (−2 − 4) ÷ (3 − 1) = −3. Substituting (1, 4): 4 = −3 + c, so c = 7 and the equation is y = −3x + 7.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE past-paper level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line has gradient −1 and passes through (3, 2). Find its equation.
parts.hint: Substitute m = −1 and the point into y = mx + c.
parts.explanation: Using y = −x + c with (3, 2): 2 = −3 + c, so c = 5 and the equation is y = −x + 5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE past-paper level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line has gradient −3 and passes through (−1, 5). Find its equation.
parts.hint: Take care with the double negative when you substitute.
parts.explanation: Substituting: 5 = −3(−1) + c = 3 + c, so c = 2 and the equation is y = −3x + 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE past-paper level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line parallel to y = 4x − 1 that passes through (2, 3).
parts.hint: Parallel means the same gradient; substitute the point to find c.
parts.explanation: Gradient = 4. Substituting (2, 3): 3 = 4(2) + c = 8 + c, so c = −5 and the equation is y = 4x − 5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Coordinates; NCE past-paper level.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the y-intercept of the line passing through (2, 3) and (4, 7).
parts.hint: Find the gradient first, then find c.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (7 − 3) ÷ (4 − 2) = 2. Substituting (2, 3): 3 = 4 + c, so c = −1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 "gradient → equation → point on line" pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line passes through A (1, 2) and B (5, 10). Find the gradient of AB.
parts.hint: Subtract the y values and the x values in the same order.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (10 − 2) ÷ (5 − 1) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line AB.
parts.hint: Use y = 2x + c and substitute one of the two points.
parts.explanation: With m = 2, substituting A (1, 2): 2 = 2(1) + c = 2 + c, so c = 0 and the equation is y = 2x.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The point C (3, k) lies on the line AB. Find the value of k.
parts.hint: Substitute x = 3 into your equation.
parts.explanation: Substituting x = 3 into y = 2x: k = 2(3) = 6.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Coordinates; NCE 2024 Q26 "rearrange → gradient → parallel" pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line 2y = 4x + 10.
parts.hint: Divide every term by 2 to get the form y = mx + c.
parts.explanation: Dividing throughout by 2 gives y = 2x + 5, so the gradient is 2.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line parallel to 2y = 4x + 10 that passes through (1, −1).
parts.hint: Parallel lines share the same gradient; substitute the point to find c.
parts.explanation: Gradient = 2. Substituting (1, −1): −1 = 2(1) + c = 2 + c, so c = −3 and the equation is y = 2x − 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Coordinates; NCE 2025 Q18 pattern — gradient, equation, x-intercept.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line passes through A (0, 2) and B (4, 6). Find the gradient of AB.
parts.hint: One point is on the y-axis, so c is immediate.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (6 − 2) ÷ (4 − 0) = 4 ÷ 4 = 1.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line AB.
parts.hint: The point (0, 2) gives c = 2 straight away.
parts.explanation: With m = 1 and y-intercept 2, the equation is y = x + 2.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the point where AB crosses the x-axis.
parts.hint: Set y = 0 in your equation.
parts.explanation: Setting y = 0: 0 = x + 2, so x = −2. The line crosses the x-axis at (−2, 0).

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Straight-line graphs in practical situations; NCE 2025 Q29 applied pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A taxi charges a fixed amount plus a rate per kilometre. A 3 km journey costs Rs 150 and a 7 km journey costs Rs 290. Find the gradient of the cost–distance graph.
parts.hint: Treat the two journeys as the points (3, 150) and (7, 290) on a straight line.
parts.explanation: Gradient = (290 − 150) ÷ (7 − 3) = 140 ÷ 4 = 35. The taxi charges Rs 35 per km.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the cost C (in rupees) in terms of distance d (in km).
parts.hint: Use C = 35d + c and substitute one of the given journeys.
parts.explanation: Substituting (3, 150): 150 = 35(3) + c = 105 + c, so c = 45. The equation is C = 35d + 45.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Work out 632 + 157.
parts.hint: Add the units, then the tens, then the hundreds.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Work out 849 − 523.
parts.hint: Subtract column by column, starting from the units.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Evaluate <sup>5</sup>⁄<sub>13</sub> + <sup>3</sup>⁄<sub>13</sub>.
parts.hint: The denominators are the same, so only the numerators change.
parts.explanation: With a common denominator, add the numerators: (5 + 3)/13 = 8/13.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Evaluate <sup>9</sup>⁄<sub>17</sub> − <sup>3</sup>⁄<sub>17</sub>.
parts.hint: Subtract the numerators and keep the denominator.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Work out 2.1 + 0.5.
parts.hint: Line up the decimal points.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate 3.02 × 4.
parts.hint: Multiply as whole numbers, then place the decimal point.
parts.explanation: 302 × 4 = 1208, and there are two decimal places, so the answer is 12.08.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Express 13% as a fraction.
parts.hint: Per cent means "out of a hundred".
parts.explanation: 13% means 13 out of 100, so the fraction is 13/100.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Express 0.31 as a percentage.
parts.hint: Multiply by 100.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Evaluate <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub> + <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub>.
parts.hint: Find a common denominator first.
parts.explanation: The lowest common denominator of 2 and 3 is 6: 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Evaluate 3 + 5 − 9.
parts.hint: Work from left to right.
parts.explanation: 3 + 5 = 8, and 8 − 9 = −1.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Evaluate 3 × (4 − 2) + 5.
parts.hint: Brackets first, then multiply, then add.
parts.explanation: 4 − 2 = 2, then 3 × 2 = 6, and 6 + 5 = 11.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Express <sup>3</sup>⁄<sub>4</sub> as a percentage.
parts.hint: Turn the fraction into hundredths.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Express 0.4 as a fraction in its simplest form.
parts.hint: Start from tenths, then cancel.
parts.explanation: 0.4 = 4/10, and dividing top and bottom by 2 gives 2/5.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Work out <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> of 360.
parts.hint: Divide by the bottom, then multiply by the top.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find 15% of 200.

parts.prompt: Evaluate <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>4</sub> × <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub>, giving your answer in its simplest form.
parts.hint: Multiply the tops, multiply the bottoms, then cancel.
parts.explanation: (1 × 2)/(4 × 3) = 2/12, which cancels to 1/6.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: After a discount of 10%, a laptop costs Rs 27 900. Find the original price of the laptop.
parts.hint: The sale price is 90% of the original price.
parts.explanation: The price paid is 100% − 10% = 90% of the original. So 90% = Rs 27 900, giving 1% = Rs 310 and 100% = Rs 31 000.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.prompt: Mira has Rs 360. She gives <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>5</sub> of her money to Tim. How much money does Tim receive?
parts.hint: Find one fifth first.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A shirt costing Rs 800 is sold at a profit of 25%. Find the selling price.
parts.hint: Find 25% of 800, then add it on.
parts.explanation: 25% of 800 = 200, so the selling price is 800 + 200 = Rs 1 000.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a

parts.hint: There are 1 000 millilitres in a litre.

parts.prompt: Convert 2 kg 350 g into grams.
parts.hint: There are 1 000 grams in a kilogram.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many minutes are there in 2 hours 10 minutes?
parts.hint: There are 60 minutes in an hour.
parts.explanation: 2 × 60 = 120 minutes, plus 10 minutes, gives 130 minutes.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find 3√8.
parts.hint: Which number multiplied by itself three times gives 8?
parts.explanation: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, so the cube root of 8 is 2.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find 3√64.
parts.hint: Try small whole numbers cubed.
parts.explanation: 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, so the cube root of 64 is 4.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A bag of flour weighs 15 kg. What is the mass of 4 such bags?
parts.hint: Multiply the mass of one bag by the number of bags.
parts.explanation: 15 × 4 = 60 kg.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Convert 3.5 L into cL.
parts.hint: There are 100 centilitres in a litre.

parts.prompt: Convert 4.2 km into metres.
parts.hint: There are 1 000 metres in a kilometre.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Convert 2 500 mL into litres.
parts.hint: Divide by 1 000.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 7. The smaller number is 21. Find the larger number.
parts.hint: Work out what one part is worth first.
parts.explanation: 3 parts = 21, so 1 part = 7. The larger number is 7 parts = 7 × 7 = 49.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Rs 4 500 is shared between A and B in the ratio 2 : 3. How much does B receive?
parts.hint: There are 5 equal parts altogether.
parts.explanation: 2 + 3 = 5 parts, so 1 part = 4 500 ÷ 5 = Rs 900. B receives 3 parts = Rs 2 700.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A sum of money is shared between Shania and Mirella in the ratio 2 : 5. Mirella receives Rs 360 more than Shania. Calculate the total amount of money shared.
parts.hint: The difference between them is 3 parts.
parts.explanation: Mirella has 5 parts and Shania 2 parts, so the difference is 3 parts = Rs 360, giving 1 part = Rs 120. The total is 7 parts = 7 × 120 = Rs 840.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: 12 men take 20 days to build a house. How many days would it take 10 men to build a similar house? [Assume that the men work at the same rate.]
parts.hint: Fewer men means more days - this is inverse proportion.
parts.explanation: The work is 12 × 20 = 240 man-days. With 10 men, the time is 240 ÷ 10 = 24 days.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The plan of a house is drawn to a scale of 1 : 400. On the plan, a wall is represented by a line of 7.5 cm. Find the actual length of the wall, in metres.
parts.hint: Find the real length in centimetres first, then change to metres.
parts.explanation: 7.5 × 400 = 3 000 cm. Since 100 cm = 1 m, the wall is 3 000 ÷ 100 = 30 m.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the L.C.M. of 4x and 12y.
parts.hint: Take the lowest common multiple of the numbers, then include every letter.
parts.explanation: The L.C.M. of 4 and 12 is 12, and both x and y must appear, so the L.C.M. is 12xy.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the H.C.F. of 3x and 6x2.
parts.hint: Take the highest factor common to both numbers and the lowest power of x.
parts.explanation: The H.C.F. of 3 and 6 is 3, and the lowest power of x present in both is x, so the H.C.F. is 3x.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A car travels 150 km in 2 hours. Find its average speed.
parts.hint: Speed is distance divided by time.
parts.explanation: 150 ÷ 2 = 75 km/h.

grade9-maths.source: Grade 7-8 number work carried into the NCE paper; NCE 2025 Q1-Q10, 2024 Q1-Q11 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: 5 identical books cost Rs 850. Find the cost of 8 such books.
parts.hint: Find the cost of one book first.
parts.explanation: 850 ÷ 5 = Rs 170 for one book, so 8 books cost 170 × 8 = Rs 1 360.

parts.prompt: Circle the composite number in the list below.
parts.hint: A composite number has more factors than just 1 and itself.
parts.explanation: 27 = 3 × 9, so it has factors other than 1 and 27. The other three - 2, 13 and 41 - are prime.

grade9-maths.source: NCE 2025 Q6/Q12, 2024 Q6 "circle the ... in the list below" pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Circle the square number in the list below.
parts.hint: Which one is a whole number multiplied by itself?
parts.explanation: 36 = 6 × 6, so it is a square number. None of 15, 20 or 59 is a whole number squared.

grade9-maths.source: NCE 2025 Q6/Q12, 2024 Q6 "circle the ... in the list below" pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Circle the prime number in the list below.
parts.hint: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
parts.explanation: 23 has no factors except 1 and 23. 21 = 3 × 7, 25 = 5 × 5 and 27 = 3 × 9.

grade9-maths.source: NCE 2025 Q6/Q12, 2024 Q6 "circle the ... in the list below" pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A list of numbers is given below. Circle the smallest number.
parts.hint: Compare the digits after the decimal point one place at a time.
parts.explanation: Comparing tenths: 2.005 and 2.05 both have 0 tenths, but 2.005 has 0 hundredths against 5, so 2.005 is the smallest.

grade9-maths.source: NCE 2024 Q14(a) ordering pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Arrange the following numbers in ascending order.
5.62     5.06     5.23     5.65     5.006
parts.hint: Ascending means smallest first. Compare the tenths, then the hundredths.
parts.explanation: Writing each to three decimal places: 5.620, 5.060, 5.230, 5.650, 5.006. In order, smallest first: 5.006, 5.06, 5.23, 5.62, 5.65.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A pen costs Rs 40. Its price is increased by 15%. Find the new price.
parts.hint: Find 15% of Rs 40, then add it to the original price.
parts.explanation: 15% of 40 = Rs 6, so the new price is 40 + 6 = Rs 46.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: After a 25% increase, a bag costs Rs 500. Find the original price of the bag.
parts.hint: The new price represents 125% of the original.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A television was bought for Rs 8 000 and sold for Rs 6 800. Calculate the percentage loss.
parts.hint: Percentage loss = (loss ÷ cost price) × 100.
parts.explanation: Loss = 8 000 − 6 800 = Rs 1 200. Percentage loss = (1 200 ÷ 8 000) × 100 = 15%.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A shopkeeper buys 50 oranges for Rs 100 and sells them at Rs 3 each. Calculate the percentage profit.
parts.hint: Find the total selling price, then calculate profit as a percentage of the cost price.
parts.explanation: Total selling price = 50 × Rs 3 = Rs 150. Profit = 150 − 100 = Rs 50. Percentage profit = (50 ÷ 100) × 100 = 50%.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A class has 45 pupils. 60% of them are girls. Find the number of boys in the class.
parts.hint: Find the number of girls first, then subtract from the total.
parts.explanation: 60% of 45 = 27 girls. Boys = 45 − 27 = 18.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A television costs Rs 12 000 before VAT. VAT of 15% is added to the price. Find the total cost.
parts.hint: Find 15% of Rs 12 000 and add it to the original price.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Evaluate 3<sup>2</sup> × 2 − (5 + 3) ÷ 4.
parts.hint: Follow BODMAS: Brackets, then Orders (powers), then Divide/Multiply, then Add/Subtract.
parts.explanation: 3<sup>2</sup> = 9. Then 9 × 2 = 18. Brackets: (5 + 3) = 8, and 8 ÷ 4 = 2. Finally 18 − 2 = 16.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Work out 4 − 1<sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub>, giving your answer as a fraction.
parts.hint: Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction first.
parts.explanation: 1<sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> = <sup>5</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub>. Write 4 as <sup>12</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub>: <sup>12</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> − <sup>5</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> = <sup>7</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub>.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Asha earns Rs 3 600 per month. She spends 2⁄5 on rent and 1⁄4 on food. How much money does she have left?
parts.hint: Find the amount spent on rent and food separately, then subtract both from her earnings.
parts.explanation: Rent = <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>5</sub> × 3 600 = Rs 1 440. Food = <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>4</sub> × 3 600 = Rs 900. Left = 3 600 − 1 440 − 900 = Rs 1 260.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A car travels 240 km on 20 litres of petrol. How many litres of petrol are needed to travel 360 km?
parts.hint: Find the rate of petrol use per kilometre, then multiply.
parts.explanation: Petrol per km = 20 ÷ 240 = <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>12</sub> L. Petrol for 360 km = 360 ÷ 12 = 30 L.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Three friends share a prize of Rs 2 400 in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. Find the largest share.
parts.hint: Find the value of one part first.
parts.explanation: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 parts. One part = Rs 2 400 ÷ 6 = Rs 400. Largest share = 3 × Rs 400 = Rs 1 200.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A car travels at 80 km/h. How far does it travel in 1 hour 30 minutes?
parts.hint: Convert 1 hour 30 minutes into hours before applying distance = speed × time.
parts.explanation: 1 hour 30 minutes = 1.5 hours. Distance = 80 × 1.5 = 120 km.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A bus travels 90 km at a speed of 60 km/h. How many minutes does the journey take?
parts.hint: Find the time in hours first, then convert to minutes.
parts.explanation: Time = 90 ÷ 60 = 1.5 hours. 1.5 × 60 = 90 minutes.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Two bells ring at the same time. After that, one rings every 20 minutes and the other every 30 minutes. After how many minutes will they ring together again?
parts.hint: Find the LCM of 20 and 30.
parts.explanation: LCM(20, 30) = 60. The bells will ring together again after 60 minutes.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: 6 workers can complete a task in 10 days. How many workers are needed to complete the same task in 4 days? [Assume all workers work at the same rate.]
parts.hint: This is inverse proportion: fewer days means more workers are needed.
parts.explanation: Total work = 6 × 10 = 60 worker-days. Workers needed for 4 days = 60 ÷ 4 = 15.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The average of 4 numbers is 18. Three of the numbers are 12, 20 and 25. Find the fourth number.
parts.hint: The total sum of all 4 numbers = 4 × their average.
parts.explanation: Sum of 4 numbers = 4 × 18 = 72. Fourth number = 72 − (12 + 20 + 25) = 72 − 57 = 15.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Convert 3 hours 20 minutes into seconds.
parts.hint: Convert to minutes first, then multiply by 60.
parts.explanation: 3 hours 20 minutes = 200 minutes. 200 × 60 = 12 000 seconds.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a school, the ratio of boys to girls is 3 : 5. There are 240 boys. Find the total number of pupils in the school.
parts.hint: Find the value of one part first, then multiply by the total number of parts.
parts.explanation: 3 parts = 240 boys, so 1 part = 80. Total = (3 + 5) × 80 = 8 × 80 = 640.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Raju earns Rs 5 000 per month. He saves 20% of his earnings each month.
Find the amount Raju saves per month.
parts.hint: Find 20% of Rs 5 000.
parts.explanation: 20% of 5 000 = <sup>20</sup>⁄<sub>100</sub> × 5 000 = Rs 1 000.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How many months will it take Raju to save Rs 6 000?
parts.hint: Divide the target amount by the monthly savings you found in (a).
parts.explanation: Rs 6 000 ÷ Rs 1 000 = 6 months.

grade9-maths.source: NCE past-paper number revision practice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
A map has a scale of 1 : 50 000. A road is represented by a line of 8 cm on the map.
Find the actual length of the road, in kilometres.
parts.hint: Multiply the map length by 50 000, then convert centimetres to kilometres.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A forest is 15 km long. Find its length on the map, in centimetres.
parts.hint: Convert 15 km to centimetres first, then divide by 50 000.

parts.label: a

4). Find the coordinates of its image.
parts.hint: Add the vector to the coordinates of A.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
The point A (2, −1) is translated by the vector (−3
5). Find the coordinates of its image.
parts.hint: Add each component, watching the signs.
parts.explanation: Adding: (2 + (−3), −1 + 5) = (−1, 4).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
A point A is mapped onto B (5, 7) by the translation (2
3). Find the coordinates of A.
parts.hint: To go backwards, subtract the translation vector.
parts.explanation: A = B − the vector = (5 − 2, 7 − 3) = (3, 4).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The point A (1, 1) is mapped onto B (4, 5). Find the translation vector.
parts.hint: Subtract the coordinates of A from those of B.
parts.explanation: The vector is B − A = (4 − 1, 5 − 1) = (3, 4).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A translation moves every point 4 units to the right and 2 units down. Write this translation as a column vector.
parts.hint: Right is positive across; down is negative up the page.
parts.explanation: Moving right is a positive x component and moving down is a negative y component, so the vector is (4, −2).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The point P (4, 3) is mapped onto Q (1, 8). Find the translation vector.
parts.hint: Image minus object.
parts.explanation: The vector is Q − P = (1 − 4, 8 − 3) = (−3, 5).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
The point A (−2, −3) is translated by (5
1). Find the coordinates of its image.
parts.hint: Add the vector to A.
parts.explanation: Adding: (−2 + 5, −3 + 1) = (3, −2).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
A point A is mapped onto B (0, 0) by the translation (−4
6). Find the coordinates of A.
parts.hint: Subtract the vector from B.
parts.explanation: A = B − the vector = (0 − (−4), 0 − 6) = (4, −6).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
A translation is given by (0
0). Describe its effect on any point.
parts.hint: What happens when you add nothing to a point?
parts.explanation: Adding (0, 0) leaves every coordinate unchanged, so the point does not move.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The point M (7, −2) is mapped onto N (7, 5). Find the translation vector.
parts.hint: The x-coordinate does not change.
parts.explanation: The vector is N − M = (7 − 7, 5 − (−2)) = (0, 7).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
The point A (3, 1) is translated by the vector (2
−4). Find the coordinates of its image.
parts.hint: Add the vector to A, watching the negative.
parts.explanation: Adding: (3 + 2, 1 + (−4)) = (5, −3).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
The point A (−1, 0) is translated by the vector (0
6). Find the coordinates of its image.
parts.hint: The x-coordinate is unchanged.
parts.explanation: Adding: (−1 + 0, 0 + 6) = (−1, 6).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The point P (2, 2) is mapped onto Q (6, 2). Find the translation vector.
parts.hint: Only one coordinate has changed.
parts.explanation: The vector is Q − P = (6 − 2, 2 − 2) = (4, 0).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The point A (5, 5) is mapped onto B (1, 1). Find the translation vector.
parts.hint: The point has moved left and down, so expect two negatives.
parts.explanation: The vector is B − A = (1 − 5, 1 − 5) = (−4, −4).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
A point is mapped onto (3, 3) by the translation (1
1). Find the coordinates of the object.
parts.hint: To go backwards, subtract the vector.
parts.explanation: Object = image − vector = (3 − 1, 3 − 1) = (2, 2).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
A point is mapped onto (−2, 4) by the translation (3
−1). Find the coordinates of the object.
parts.hint: Subtract the vector from the image, watching both signs.
parts.explanation: Object = image − vector = (−2 − 3, 4 − (−1)) = (−5, 5).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
The point A (0, 4) is translated by the vector (6
−4). Find the coordinates of its image.
parts.hint: Add each component.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
A vertex of a triangle is at T (−3, 2). The triangle is translated by (5
3). Find the coordinates of the image of T.
parts.hint: Translate the vertex like any other point.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q16 and Q20 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The point A (7, 1) is mapped onto B (7, 9). Find the translation vector.
parts.hint: The point moves straight up.
parts.explanation: The vector is B − A = (7 − 7, 9 − 1) = (0, 8).

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Vectors, "distinguish between a scalar and a vector quantity".

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
parts.hint: A vector has a direction as well as a size.
parts.explanation: Force has both size and direction, so it is a vector. Mass, temperature and time have size only, so they are scalars.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Vectors, "distinguish between a scalar and a vector quantity".

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
parts.hint: A scalar has size but no direction.
parts.explanation: Speed tells you how fast, but not which way, so it is a scalar. Velocity, displacement and acceleration all carry a direction and are vectors.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Vectors and Translation; NCE 2025 Q20 grid + tick + magnitude.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Tick (✔) the box which correctly indicates T expressed as a column vector.
parts.hint: Count how far right, then how far up, the arrow goes.
parts.explanation: From A (1, 1) to B (4, 5) the arrow moves 3 to the right and 4 up, so T = (3, 4).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the magnitude of the column vector T.
parts.hint: Use Pythagoras on the two components of T.
parts.explanation: |T| = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Vectors; NCE 2025 Q31 three-level numbering pattern.

parts.label: a.i
parts.prompt: Find a + b.
parts.hint: Add the components in pairs.
parts.explanation: Top: 4 + (−2) = 2. Bottom: 3 + 1 = 4. So a + b = (2, 4).

parts.label: a.ii
parts.prompt: Find 2a − b.
parts.hint: Double a first, then subtract b.
parts.explanation: 2a = (8, 6). Subtracting b: top 8 − (−2) = 10, bottom 6 − 1 = 5, giving (10, 5).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the magnitude of a.
parts.hint: Use Pythagoras on the components of a.
parts.explanation: |a| = √(4² + 3²) = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the mean of 4, 6, 8 and 10.
parts.hint: Add them up, then divide by how many there are.
parts.explanation: The total is 4 + 6 + 8 + 10 = 28, and there are 4 numbers, so the mean is 28 ÷ 4 = 7.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the median of 3, 7, 5, 9 and 4.
parts.hint: Put them in order first.
parts.explanation: In order: 3, 4, 5, 7, 9. There are five numbers, so the median is the third one, 5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the mode of 2, 3, 3, 5, 7 and 3.
parts.hint: The mode is the value that appears most often.
parts.explanation: 3 appears three times and every other value appears once, so the mode is 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the range of 12, 5, 18 and 9.
parts.hint: Largest minus smallest.
parts.explanation: The largest is 18 and the smallest is 5, so the range is 18 − 5 = 13.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the mean of 5, 5, 7 and 11.
parts.hint: Total first, then divide by 4.
parts.explanation: The total is 5 + 5 + 7 + 11 = 28, so the mean is 28 ÷ 4 = 7.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the median of 6, 2, 9 and 4.
parts.hint: With an even number of values, the median is halfway between the middle two.
parts.explanation: In order: 2, 4, 6, 9. The middle two are 4 and 6, so the median is (4 + 6) ÷ 2 = 5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the mode of 1, 4, 4, 6, 6, 6 and 9.
parts.hint: Count how many times each value appears.
parts.explanation: 6 appears three times, more than any other value, so the mode is 6.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the mean of 12, 15 and 18.
parts.hint: Add the three numbers and divide by 3.
parts.explanation: The total is 12 + 15 + 18 = 45, so the mean is 45 ÷ 3 = 15.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the range of −3, 8, 0 and 5.
parts.hint: Take care: the smallest value is negative.
parts.explanation: The largest is 8 and the smallest is −3, so the range is 8 − (−3) = 11.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the median of 10, 2, 8, 6, 4 and 12.
parts.hint: Order them, then average the middle two.
parts.explanation: In order: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. The middle two are 6 and 8, so the median is (6 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The mean of four numbers is 9. Find their total.
parts.hint: Work the mean formula backwards.
parts.explanation: Mean = total ÷ how many, so total = mean × how many = 9 × 4 = 36.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The mean of 5, 8, x and 11 is 9. Find the value of x.
parts.hint: Find the total the four numbers must have.
parts.explanation: The total must be 9 × 4 = 36. Since 5 + 8 + 11 = 24, x = 36 − 24 = 12.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the mode of 7, 7, 8, 9, 9, 9 and 10.
parts.hint: Which value occurs most often?
parts.explanation: 9 appears three times, more than any other, so the mode is 9.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the mean of 2.5, 3.5 and 6.
parts.hint: Add the decimals carefully, then divide by 3.
parts.explanation: The total is 2.5 + 3.5 + 6 = 12, so the mean is 12 ÷ 3 = 4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the range of 4.5, 2.1, 7.8 and 3.3.
parts.hint: Largest minus smallest.
parts.explanation: The largest is 7.8 and the smallest is 2.1, so the range is 7.8 − 2.1 = 5.7.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a pie chart showing 36 pupils, one sector represents 9 pupils. Calculate the angle of that sector.
parts.hint: A full pie chart is 360°.
parts.explanation: Each pupil is worth 360 ÷ 36 = 10°, so 9 pupils are represented by 9 × 10 = 90°.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a pie chart showing 36 students, 10 chose fruits. Calculate the angle representing fruits.
parts.hint: Find the angle for one student first.
parts.explanation: 360 ÷ 36 = 10° per student, so 10 students are represented by 10 × 10 = 100°.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A frequency table records a value of 3 occurring 5 times. What is the total contributed by that row?
parts.hint: Multiply the value by its frequency.
parts.explanation: Each row of a frequency table contributes value × frequency = 3 × 5 = 15.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the mean of the first five whole numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5.
parts.hint: Add them, then divide by 5.
parts.explanation: The total is 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15, so the mean is 15 ÷ 5 = 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Statistics; NCE 2025 Q21 and 2024 Q28 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Six numbers have a mean of 7. When one more number is added, the mean becomes 8. Find the number added.
parts.hint: Compare the total before and the total after.
parts.explanation: Six numbers with mean 7 total 42. Seven numbers with mean 8 total 56. The number added is 56 − 42 = 14.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Statistics, mean from a frequency table; NCE 2025 Q21 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Using the information given in the bar chart, complete the table below.
Number of goals01234
Number of matches……4…………1
parts.hint: Read the height of each bar against the vertical scale.
parts.explanation: Reading the bars: 0 goals in 2 matches, 2 goals in 2 matches and 3 goals in 3 matches. Checking the total: 2 + 4 + 2 + 3 + 1 = 12 matches, as stated.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the mean number of goals scored per match.
parts.hint: Multiply each number of goals by how many matches, add those up, then divide by 12.
parts.explanation: Total goals = (0×2) + (1×4) + (2×2) + (3×3) + (4×1) = 0 + 4 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 21. The mean is 21 ÷ 12 = 1.75 goals per match.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Draw a bar chart on the grid above to represent this information.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Which fruit is the mode?
parts.hint: The mode is the one chosen by the most pupils.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, which ratio is opposite ÷ hypotenuse?
parts.hint: Remember SOH CAH TOA.
parts.explanation: SOH: Sine = Opposite ÷ Hypotenuse.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, which ratio is adjacent ÷ hypotenuse?
parts.hint: Remember SOH CAH TOA.
parts.explanation: CAH: Cosine = Adjacent ÷ Hypotenuse.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, which ratio is opposite ÷ adjacent?
parts.hint: Remember SOH CAH TOA.
parts.explanation: TOA: Tangent = Opposite ÷ Adjacent.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a right-angled triangle the side opposite angle θ is 6 cm and the hypotenuse is 10 cm. Find sin θ.
parts.hint: Sine is opposite over hypotenuse.
parts.explanation: sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse = 6/10 = 3/5 = 0.6.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a right-angled triangle the side adjacent to angle θ is 8 cm and the hypotenuse is 10 cm. Find cos θ.
parts.hint: Cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse.
parts.explanation: cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse = 8/10 = 4/5 = 0.8.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a right-angled triangle the side opposite angle θ is 3 cm and the side adjacent is 4 cm. Find tan θ.
parts.hint: Tangent is opposite over adjacent.
parts.explanation: tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent = 3/4 = 0.75.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The diagram shows a right-angled triangle. Find the length of AB. [Given cos 60° = 0.5]
parts.hint: The side you want lies next to the 60° angle, and the hypotenuse is given.
parts.explanation: cos 60° = AB ÷ 14, so AB = 14 × 0.5 = 7 cm.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, the side adjacent to a 45° angle is 5 cm. Find the length of the opposite side. [Given tan 45° = 1]
parts.hint: Tangent relates the opposite side to the adjacent side.
parts.explanation: tan 45° = opposite ÷ 5, so opposite = 5 × 1 = 5 cm.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A ladder 10 m long leans against a wall, making an angle of 60° with the ground. Find the height it reaches up the wall, to the nearest whole number. [Given sin 60° = 0.87]
parts.hint: The wall is opposite the 60° angle and the ladder is the hypotenuse.
parts.explanation: sin 60° = height ÷ 10, so height = 10 × 0.87 = 8.7 m, which is 9 m to the nearest whole number.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is 20 cm and one angle is 30°. Find the side opposite that angle. [Given sin 30° = 0.5]
parts.hint: Opposite and hypotenuse means sine.
parts.explanation: sin 30° = opposite ÷ 20, so opposite = 20 × 0.5 = 10 cm.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The diagram shows a right-angled triangle. Find the length of AC, giving your answer to the nearest whole number. [Given sin 60° = 0.87, cos 60° = 0.5, tan 60° = 1.73]
parts.hint: Decide first which two sides the 60° angle connects: you have the hypotenuse and want the opposite side.
parts.explanation: AC is opposite the 60° angle and 14 cm is the hypotenuse, so sin 60° = AC ÷ 14. AC = 14 × 0.87 = 12.18 cm, which is 12 cm to the nearest whole number.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A right-angled triangle has sides 5 cm, 12 cm and 13 cm, with 13 cm as the hypotenuse. Find the sine of the angle opposite the 5 cm side.
parts.hint: Sine is opposite over hypotenuse.
parts.explanation: The side opposite is 5 cm and the hypotenuse is 13 cm, so the sine is 5/13.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A right-angled triangle has sides 5 cm, 12 cm and 13 cm, with 13 cm as the hypotenuse. Find the tangent of the angle opposite the 12 cm side.
parts.hint: Tangent is opposite over adjacent, and the adjacent side here is 5 cm.
parts.explanation: The side opposite is 12 cm and the adjacent side is 5 cm, so the tangent is 12/5 = 2.4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, tan θ = 1. Find the size of angle θ.
parts.hint: A tangent of 1 means the opposite and adjacent sides are equal.
parts.explanation: tan θ = 1 means opposite = adjacent, so the triangle is isosceles and θ = 45°.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, sin θ = 0.5. Find the size of angle θ.
parts.hint: This is one of the angles worth knowing by heart.
parts.explanation: sin 30° = 0.5, so θ = 30°.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A right-angled triangle has a base of 8 cm and a height of 8 cm. Find the size of the angle between the base and the hypotenuse.
parts.hint: Work out the tangent of the angle first.
parts.explanation: tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent = 8/8 = 1, and tan 45° = 1, so the angle is 45°.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, the side adjacent to a 60° angle is 9 cm. Find the length of the opposite side, to the nearest whole number. [Given tan 60° = 1.73]
parts.hint: Adjacent and opposite means tangent.
parts.explanation: tan 60° = opposite ÷ 9, so opposite = 9 × 1.73 = 15.57 cm, which is 16 cm to the nearest whole number.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The diagram shows a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse 20 cm. Find the length of PQ. [Given cos 30° = 0.87]
parts.hint: PQ lies next to the 30° angle, so use cosine.
parts.explanation: cos 30° = PQ ÷ 20, so PQ = 20 × 0.87 = 17.4 cm.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Geometry: Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 pattern (ratios supplied in the stem).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of 25 cm and one side of 15 cm. Find the sine of the angle opposite the 15 cm side, and hence the size of that angle.
parts.hint: Find the sine first, then recall which common angle it belongs to.
parts.explanation: sin θ = 15/25 = 0.6. The angle whose sine is 0.6 is approximately 37°.
