grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Trigonometry; NCE 2025 Q30 three-part dependent structure.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the length of BC.
parts.hint: BC lies next to the 60° angle and AC is the hypotenuse.
parts.explanation: cos 60° = BC ÷ 12, so BC = 12 × 0.5 = 6 cm.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the length of AB, to the nearest whole number.
parts.hint: AB is opposite the 60° angle.
parts.explanation: sin 60° = AB ÷ 12, so AB = 12 × 0.87 = 10.44 cm, which is 10 cm to the nearest whole number.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Using your answers to part (a) and part (b), find the perimeter of triangle ABC.
parts.hint: Add all three sides, including the hypotenuse you were given.
parts.explanation: Perimeter = AB + BC + AC = 10 + 6 + 12 = 28 cm. Follow-through applies: a candidate who found different values in (a) and (b) still earns both marks for adding their own three sides correctly.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A fair six-sided die is thrown once. Find the probability of getting an even number.
parts.hint: Three of the six faces are even.
parts.explanation: The even faces are 2, 4 and 6, so the probability is 3/6 = 1/2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A fair six-sided die is thrown once. Find the probability of getting a 3.
parts.hint: There is one face showing 3.
parts.explanation: One of the six equally likely faces is a 3, so the probability is 1/6.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A fair six-sided die is thrown once. Find the probability of getting a number greater than 4.
parts.hint: Which faces are greater than 4?
parts.explanation: The faces greater than 4 are 5 and 6, so the probability is 2/6 = 1/3.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The spinner shown is spun once. Find the probability that the arrow shows a number less than 5.
parts.hint: List the sectors below 5.
parts.explanation: The sectors below 5 are 2, 3 and 4 - three of eight - so the probability is 3/8.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The spinner shown is spun once. Find the probability that the arrow shows a prime number.
parts.hint: A prime has exactly two factors.
parts.explanation: The primes on the spinner are 2, 3, 5 and 7 - four of eight - so the probability is 4/8 = 1/2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A bag contains 5 red and 3 green marbles. One marble is taken at random. Find the probability that it is green.
parts.hint: How many marbles are there altogether?
parts.explanation: There are 5 + 3 = 8 marbles and 3 are green, so the probability is 3/8.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A bag contains 5 red and 3 green marbles. One marble is taken at random. Find the probability that it is not red.
parts.hint: The complement of "red" is "green" here.
parts.explanation: P(red) = 5/8, so P(not red) = 1 − 5/8 = 3/8.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A fair coin is tossed once. Find the probability of getting a head.
parts.hint: There are two equally likely outcomes.
parts.explanation: A coin has two equally likely outcomes, so P(head) = 1/2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The probability that it rains tomorrow is 0.3. Find the probability that it does not rain.
parts.hint: The two probabilities must add to 1.
parts.explanation: P(not rain) = 1 − 0.3 = 0.7.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A letter is chosen at random from the word MAURITIUS. Find the probability that it is a U.
parts.hint: Count the letters, then count the Us.
parts.explanation: MAURITIUS has 9 letters and two of them are U, so the probability is 2/9.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A letter is chosen at random from the word MAURITIUS. Find the probability that it is a vowel.
parts.hint: A, E, I, O and U are the vowels.
parts.explanation: The vowels in MAURITIUS are A, U, I, I and U - five of the nine letters - so the probability is 5/9.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A box holds 20 pens, of which 4 are faulty. One pen is taken at random. Find the probability that it is faulty.
parts.hint: Simplify the fraction.
parts.explanation: 4 out of 20 pens are faulty, so the probability is 4/20 = 1/5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A fair six-sided die is thrown once. Find the probability of getting a number that is both even and greater than 3.
parts.hint: List the faces that satisfy both conditions.
parts.explanation: The faces that are even AND greater than 3 are 4 and 6, so the probability is 2/6 = 1/3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What is the probability of an event that is certain to happen?
parts.hint: Probability runs from 0 to 1.
parts.explanation: A certain event has probability 1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What is the probability of an event that is impossible?
parts.hint: Probability runs from 0 to 1.
parts.explanation: An impossible event has probability 0.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A bag contains 7 blue and 5 yellow counters. Two more blue counters are added. Find the probability of drawing a yellow counter.
parts.hint: Recount the total after the counters are added.
parts.explanation: After adding 2 blue counters there are 9 blue and 5 yellow, so 14 altogether. P(yellow) = 5/14.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a class of 30 pupils, 18 study French. One pupil is chosen at random. Find the probability that the pupil does not study French, giving your answer in its simplest form.
parts.hint: Find how many do not study French first.
parts.explanation: 30 − 18 = 12 pupils do not study French, so the probability is 12/30 = 2/5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Probability; NCE 2024 Q23 and 2025 Q31 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A bag contains only red and blue balls. The probability of drawing a red ball is 2⁄7. There are 15 blue balls. Find the total number of balls.
parts.hint: If P(red) is 2/7 then P(blue) is 5/7.
parts.explanation: P(blue) = 1 − 2/7 = 5/7. If 5/7 of the total is 15 balls, then 1/7 of the total is 3, so the total is 21. Checking: 21 − 15 = 6 red, and 6/21 = 2/7 as required.

grade9-maths.intro:
Two fair coins are tossed together. The possibility diagram below shows all the outcomes, where H is a head and T is a tail.
HT
HHHHT
TTHTT
grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Probability, "construct and use simple possibility diagrams".

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write down the total number of possible outcomes.
parts.hint: Count the cells inside the table.
parts.explanation: The table has 2 rows and 2 columns, giving 2 × 2 = 4 possible outcomes.

parts.label: b.i
parts.prompt: Find the probability of getting two heads.
parts.hint: How many cells show HH?
parts.explanation: Only one of the four outcomes is HH, so the probability is 1/4.

parts.label: b.ii
parts.prompt: Find the probability of getting exactly one head.
parts.hint: Two of the outcomes have one head and one tail.
parts.explanation: The outcomes HT and TH each have exactly one head, so the probability is 2/4 = 1/2.

grade9-maths.intro: A bag contains 12 red balls and x blue balls. A ball is chosen at random from the bag.
grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Probability; NCE 2025 Q31 three-level algebraic structure.

parts.label: a.i
parts.prompt: Write down, in terms of x, the total number of balls in the bag.
parts.hint: Add the two amounts.
parts.explanation: There are 12 red and x blue, so the total is 12 + x balls.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.prompt: Find, in terms of x, the probability that a red ball is chosen.
parts.hint: Probability is the number of red balls over the total.
parts.explanation: P(red) = 12 ÷ (12 + x), which is written 12/(12 + x).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Given that the probability that a blue ball is chosen equals 3⁄5, find the value of x.
parts.hint: Write P(blue) as a fraction in terms of x, then set it equal to 3/5 and cross-multiply.
parts.explanation: P(blue) = x/(12 + x) = 3/5. Cross-multiplying gives 5x = 3(12 + x) = 36 + 3x, so 2x = 36 and x = 18.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Expand 4(x + 2).
parts.hint: Multiply the 4 by each term inside the bracket.
parts.explanation: 4 × x = 4x and 4 × 2 = 8, so the answer is 4x + 8.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise 6x − 15.
parts.hint: What is the highest number that divides both 6 and 15?
parts.explanation: The highest common factor of 6 and 15 is 3, so 6x − 15 = 3(2x − 5).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.hint: Multiply every term in the first bracket by every term in the second.
parts.explanation: x×x = x², x×2 = 2x, 3×x = 3x and 3×2 = 6. Collecting: x² + 5x + 6.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Expand (x + 5)(x − 2).
parts.hint: Take care with the minus sign in the second bracket.
parts.explanation: x² − 2x + 5x − 10 = x² + 3x − 10.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Expand (x + 4)2.
parts.hint: A square means the bracket multiplied by itself.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Expand (x − 3)2.
parts.hint: The middle term is negative; the last term is positive.
parts.explanation: (x − 3)² = x² − 3x − 3x + 9 = x² − 6x + 9. Note the last term is +9, because a negative times a negative is positive.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise x2 − 9.
parts.hint: This is a difference of two squares.
parts.explanation: x² − 9 = x² − 3² = (x + 3)(x − 3).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise x2 − 25.
parts.hint: Both terms are perfect squares with a minus between them.
parts.explanation: x² − 25 = x² − 5² = (x + 5)(x − 5).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise 2y2 − 50 completely.
parts.hint: Take out the common factor first, then look again.
parts.explanation: 2y² − 50 = 2(y² − 25) = 2(y + 5)(y − 5).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use the difference of two squares to evaluate 101<sup>2</sup> − 99<sup>2</sup>.
parts.hint: Write it as (a + b)(a − b) rather than squaring anything.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use perfect squares to evaluate 101<sup>2</sup>.
parts.hint: Write 101 as 100 + 1 and expand.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise 3x − 6.
parts.hint: Both terms share a factor of 3.
parts.explanation: 3x − 6 = 3(x − 2).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Simplify 6x⁄3.
parts.hint: Divide the number on the top by the number on the bottom.
parts.explanation: 6x ÷ 3 = 2x.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Simplify (2x + 4)⁄2.
parts.hint: Every term on the top must be divided by 2, not just the first.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.hint: Multiply all four pairs, then collect the x terms.
parts.explanation: 2x×x = 2x², 2x×3 = 6x, 1×x = x and 1×3 = 3. Collecting: 2x² + 7x + 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Expand (x − 1)(x − 4).
parts.hint: Two negatives multiply to give a positive.
parts.explanation: x² − 4x − x + 4 = x² − 5x + 4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise 4a + 8b.
parts.hint: The highest common factor of 4 and 8 is 4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Simplify 7x2 + 2x2.
parts.hint: These are like terms, so add the numbers in front.
parts.explanation: 7x² + 2x² = 9x².

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise x2 − 100.
parts.hint: Difference of two squares again.
parts.explanation: x² − 100 = x² − 10² = (x + 10)(x − 10).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Expressions; NCE 2025 Q9 and Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Expand (3x − 2)(x + 5).
parts.hint: Watch the signs on the two middle terms.
parts.explanation: 3x×x = 3x², 3x×5 = 15x, −2×x = −2x and −2×5 = −10. Collecting: 3x² + 13x − 10.

grade9-maths.intro: ABCD is a rectangle. It is given that DC = (3x + 1) cm and BC = (x + 1) cm. P is a point on AB, such that AP = (2 − x) cm.

stimulus.altText: A rectangle ABCD with a point P marked on the top side, and the lengths of the top part, the right side and the bottom side each given as an expression.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Expressions; NCE 2025 Q24 labelled-figure pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Giving your answer in its simplest form, find, in terms of x, an expression for PB.
parts.hint: AB is the same length as DC. PB is what is left of AB after AP.
parts.explanation: AB = DC = (3x + 1) cm. PB = AB − AP = (3x + 1) − (2 − x) = 3x + 1 − 2 + x = 4x − 1 cm.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Giving your answer in its simplest form, find, in terms of x, an expression for the area of rectangle ABCD.
parts.hint: Area is length times width; expand the brackets and collect terms.
parts.explanation: Area = DC × BC = (3x + 1)(x + 1) = 3x² + 3x + x + 1 = 3x² + 4x + 1 cm².

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise x2 + 5x + 6.
parts.hint: Find two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to 5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise x2 − 5x + 6.
parts.hint: The two numbers multiply to +6 and add to −5, so both are negative.
parts.explanation: (−2) × (−3) = 6 and (−2) + (−3) = −5, so the factors are (x − 2)(x − 3).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve x2 − 5x + 6 = 0.
parts.hint: Factorise first, then set each bracket to zero.
parts.explanation: (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0, so x − 2 = 0 or x − 3 = 0, giving x = 2 or x = 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve x2 + 7x + 12 = 0.
parts.hint: Two numbers multiplying to 12 and adding to 7.
parts.explanation: (x + 3)(x + 4) = 0, so x = −3 or x = −4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise x2 + 2x − 8.
parts.hint: The numbers multiply to −8 and add to +2, so one is negative.
parts.explanation: 4 × (−2) = −8 and 4 + (−2) = 2, so the factors are (x + 4)(x − 2).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve x2 − 9 = 0.
parts.hint: This is a difference of two squares.
parts.explanation: x² − 9 = (x + 3)(x − 3) = 0, so x = 3 or x = −3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve p2 − 10p + 10 = −14.
parts.hint: Move everything to one side so the equation equals zero first.
parts.explanation: Adding 14 to both sides: p² − 10p + 24 = 0. Two numbers multiplying to 24 and adding to −10 are −4 and −6, so (p − 4)(p − 6) = 0 and p = 4 or p = 6.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise x2 − 3x − 10.
parts.hint: Multiply to −10, add to −3.
parts.explanation: (−5) × 2 = −10 and (−5) + 2 = −3, so the factors are (x − 5)(x + 2).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve x2 + 6x = 0.
parts.hint: Take out the common factor of x.
parts.explanation: x(x + 6) = 0, so x = 0 or x + 6 = 0, giving x = 0 or x = −6. Dividing both sides by x would lose the root x = 0.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which of these is a quadratic expression?
parts.hint: A quadratic has a highest power of 2.
parts.explanation: A quadratic expression has x² as its highest power. 3x − 1 is linear, x³ + 2 is cubic, and 1/x is not a polynomial at all.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve x2 − 7x + 10 = 0.
parts.hint: Multiply to 10, add to −7.
parts.explanation: (x − 2)(x − 5) = 0, so x = 2 or x = 5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve x2 − 16 = 0.
parts.hint: Difference of two squares.
parts.explanation: (x + 4)(x − 4) = 0, so x = 4 or x = −4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise x2 + 8x + 15.
parts.hint: Multiply to 15, add to 8.
parts.explanation: 3 × 5 = 15 and 3 + 5 = 8, so the factors are (x + 3)(x + 5).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve x2 + 2x − 15 = 0.
parts.hint: Multiply to −15, add to +2.
parts.explanation: (x + 5)(x − 3) = 0, so x = −5 or x = 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which of these is a quadratic equation?
parts.hint: An equation has an equals sign, and a quadratic has x² as its highest power.
parts.explanation: x² − 4 = 0 is an equation whose highest power is 2. The others are linear, cubic, and a linear equation in two unknowns.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve x2 = 5x.
parts.hint: Bring everything to one side; do not divide by x.
parts.explanation: x² − 5x = 0, so x(x − 5) = 0 and x = 0 or x = 5. Dividing both sides by x at the start would lose the root x = 0.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve x2 − 11x + 24 = 0.
parts.hint: Multiply to 24, add to −11.
parts.explanation: (x − 3)(x − 8) = 0, so x = 3 or x = 8.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise x2 − 6x + 9.
parts.hint: Both numbers are the same here, which makes it a perfect square.
parts.explanation: (−3) × (−3) = 9 and (−3) + (−3) = −6, so the expression is (x − 3)(x − 3), or (x − 3)².

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Quadratics; NCE 2024 Q15(b) and 2025 Q22(b) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The length of a rectangle is 3 cm more than its width. Its area is 40 cm². Find the width of the rectangle.
parts.hint: Call the width x, write the area as an equation, then solve it.
parts.explanation: Let the width be x cm, so the length is (x + 3) cm and x(x + 3) = 40. This gives x² + 3x − 40 = 0, so (x + 8)(x − 5) = 0 and x = −8 or x = 5. A width cannot be negative, so the width is 5 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The length of each side of a square is increased by 8 cm. The area of the new square is 6 times its perimeter. Find the length of one side of the original square.
parts.hint: Let the original side be x. Write the new area and the new perimeter in terms of x.
parts.explanation: Let the original side be x cm, so the new side is (x + 8) cm. The new area is (x + 8)² and the new perimeter is 4(x + 8). So (x + 8)² = 6 × 4(x + 8) = 24(x + 8). Dividing both sides by (x + 8), which cannot be zero, gives x + 8 = 24, so x = 16 cm.

Find the total cost of 1 adult ticket and 4 child tickets.
parts.hint: Let a = cost of one adult ticket and c = cost of one child ticket. Form two equations, then solve.

grade9-maths.intro: At the school canteen, 3 portions of fried rice and 2 cups of juice cost Rs 85. 1 portion of fried rice and 4 cups of juice cost Rs 65.

parts.prompt: Find the cost of one portion of fried rice.
parts.hint: Multiply the first equation by 4 and the second by 2 so the juice terms cancel when you subtract.
parts.explanation: Let r = price of fried rice, j = price of juice. Multiplying 3r + 2j = 85 by 4: 12r + 8j = 340. Multiplying r + 4j = 65 by 2: 2r + 8j = 130. Subtracting: 10r = 210, so r = Rs 21.

parts.label: b

parts.explanation: Substituting r = 21 into r + 4j = 65: 21 + 4j = 65, so j = Rs 11.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
At a market stall, 3 mangoes and 2 pineapples cost Rs 65.
1 mango and 4 pineapples cost Rs 55.

Find the total cost of 2 mangoes and 3 pineapples.
parts.hint: Let m = cost of 1 mango and p = cost of 1 pineapple. Form two equations and solve.
parts.explanation: 3m + 2p = 65 and m + 4p = 55. From the second: m = 55 − 4p. Substituting: 3(55 − 4p) + 2p = 65, so 165 − 10p = 65, giving p = 10. Then m = 55 − 40 = 15. 2 mangoes + 3 pineapples = 2(15) + 3(10) = 30 + 30 = Rs 60.

grade9-maths.intro: Priya is x years old and her brother Dev is y years old. The sum of their ages is 27. In 3 years’ time, Priya will be twice as old as Dev.
grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Simultaneous Equations; ages word problem, multi-part.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the age of Priya.
parts.hint: Write one equation for the sum of ages, and one for "Priya's age in 3 years = twice Dev's age in 3 years".
parts.explanation: x + y = 27, and x + 3 = 2(y + 3), which gives x = 2y + 3. Substituting: 2y + 3 + y = 27, so 3y = 24, giving y = 8. Then x = 2(8) + 3 = 19. Priya is 19 years old.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How old will Dev be in 10 years’ time?
parts.hint: Use your answer from part (a) to find Dev's current age, then add 10.
parts.explanation: Dev is currently y = 8 years old. In 10 years he will be 8 + 10 = 18.

parts.hint: Area is πr².
parts.explanation: A = (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 22 × 7 = 154 cm².

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Surface area (nets, circle, cylinder, right prism).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the circumference of a circle of radius 14 cm. (Use π = 22⁄7)
parts.hint: Cancel the 7 in π against the radius.
parts.explanation: C = 2 × (22/7) × 14 = 2 × 22 × 2 = 88 cm.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Surface area (nets, circle, cylinder, right prism).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the area of a circle of radius 10 cm, leaving your answer in terms of π.
parts.hint: Do not replace π with a number.
parts.explanation: A = π × 10² = 100π cm².

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The net shown folds into a closed cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. Calculate its total surface area. (Use π = 22⁄7)
parts.hint: The net is two circles plus a rectangle whose width is the circumference.
parts.explanation: Curved surface = 2πrh = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 10 = 440 cm². Each circle = πr² = (22/7) × 49 = 154 cm², and there are two, giving 308 cm². Total = 440 + 308 = 748 cm².

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm is open at one end. Calculate its total surface area. (Use π = 22⁄7)
parts.hint: An open cylinder has only ONE circular face.
parts.explanation: Curved surface = 2πrh = 440 cm². One circle = πr² = 154 cm². Open at one end means only one circle, so the total is 440 + 154 = 594 cm².

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Surface area (nets, circle, cylinder, right prism).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A cylindrical pipe is hollow, that is open at both ends. It has radius 7 cm and length 20 cm. Calculate its curved surface area. (Use π = 22⁄7)
parts.hint: A hollow pipe has no circular faces at all.
parts.explanation: A pipe open at both ends is only the curved surface: 2πrh = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 20 = 880 cm².

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Surface area (nets, circle, cylinder, right prism).

parts.label: a

parts.hint: Add every face, remembering there are two triangles.

parts.hint: Three pairs of faces.
parts.explanation: The faces are 10×6 = 60, 10×5 = 50 and 6×5 = 30 cm², each twice: 2(60 + 50 + 30) = 2 × 140 = 280 cm².

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Surface area (nets, circle, cylinder, right prism).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A cube has a total surface area of 150 cm². Find the length of one edge.
parts.hint: Divide by 6 to get one face, then take the square root.
parts.explanation: One face has area 150 ÷ 6 = 25 cm², so each edge is √25 = 5 cm.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Surface area (nets, circle, cylinder, right prism).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the area of a circle of diameter 14 cm. (Use π = 22⁄7)
parts.hint: The formula needs the radius, not the diameter.
parts.explanation: The radius is 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm, so A = (22/7) × 49 = 154 cm².

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Surface area (nets, circle, cylinder, right prism).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The curved surface area of a cylinder is 176 cm² and its radius is 7 cm. Find its height. (Use π = 22⁄7)
parts.hint: Write down 2πrh and work backwards.
parts.explanation: 2πrh = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × h = 44h. Setting 44h = 176 gives h = 4 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A closed cylinder has radius 3.5 cm and height 6 cm. Calculate its total surface area. (Use π = 22⁄7)
parts.hint: Curved surface plus two circles.
parts.explanation: Curved surface = 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 6 = 132 cm². Each circle = (22/7) × 3.5 × 3.5 = 38.5 cm², so two give 77 cm². Total = 132 + 77 = 209 cm².

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A net of a cylinder is made of two circles and one rectangle. What does the length of that rectangle represent?
parts.hint: Imagine unrolling the curved surface.
parts.explanation: When the curved surface is unrolled it becomes a rectangle whose length wrapped once around the circle, so that length is the circumference.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Patterns and Sequences; NCE 2025 Q15(a) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write down the next term of the sequence 3, 7, 11, 15, …
parts.hint: What is added each time?
parts.explanation: Each term is 4 more than the one before, so the next term is 15 + 4 = 19.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Patterns and Sequences; NCE 2025 Q15(a) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the nth term of the sequence 3, 7, 11, 15, …
parts.hint: The common difference tells you what multiplies n.
parts.explanation: The terms go up by 4, so the nth term starts 4n. When n = 1, 4n = 4 but the term is 3, so the rule is 4n − 1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Patterns and Sequences; NCE 2025 Q15(a) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write down the next term of the sequence 2, 5, 8, 11, …
parts.hint: Look at the difference between terms.
parts.explanation: Each term is 3 more than the one before, so the next is 11 + 3 = 14.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Patterns and Sequences; NCE 2025 Q15(a) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the nth term of the sequence 2, 5, 8, 11, …
parts.hint: Difference 3, so start with 3n.
parts.explanation: The difference is 3, so the rule starts 3n. At n = 1 that gives 3 but the term is 2, so the nth term is 3n − 1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Patterns and Sequences; NCE 2025 Q15(a) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write down the next term of the sequence 20, 17, 14, 11, …
parts.hint: The sequence is going down.
parts.explanation: Each term is 3 less than the one before, so the next is 11 − 3 = 8.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Patterns and Sequences; NCE 2025 Q15(a) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the nth term of the sequence 20, 17, 14, 11, …
parts.hint: A falling sequence has a negative multiple of n.
parts.explanation: The difference is −3, so the rule starts −3n. At n = 1 that gives −3 but the term is 20, so the nth term is 23 − 3n.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Patterns and Sequences; NCE 2025 Q15(a) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write down the missing term in the following sequence of ordered pairs.
(2, 3), (3, 5), (4, 7), ( …… , …… )
parts.hint: Look at how the first number changes, then how the second changes.
parts.explanation: The first numbers go up by 1, so the next is 5. The second numbers go up by 2, so the next is 9. The missing pair is (5, 9). The rule is y = 2x − 1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Patterns and Sequences; NCE 2025 Q15(a) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: For the sequence of ordered pairs (1, 4), (2, 7), (3, 10), find the relation between x and y.
parts.hint: How much does y rise for each step in x?
parts.explanation: y increases by 3 each time x increases by 1, so y = 3x + c. Using (1, 4): 4 = 3 + c, so c = 1 and y = 3x + 1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Patterns and Sequences; NCE 2025 Q15(a) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: For the sequence of ordered pairs (1, −2), (2, −4), (3, −6), find the relation between x and y.
parts.hint: The y values are negative and doubling.
parts.explanation: Each y is −2 times its x, so y = −2x.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Patterns and Sequences; NCE 2025 Q15(a) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write down the next row of Pascal’s triangle after 1, 3, 3, 1.
parts.hint: Each number is the sum of the two above it, and every row starts and ends with 1.
parts.explanation: Adding neighbouring pairs of 1, 3, 3, 1 gives 4, 6, 4, and a 1 at each end: 1, 4, 6, 4, 1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Patterns and Sequences; NCE 2025 Q15(a) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In Pascal’s triangle, write down the missing number in the row 1, 5, ……, 10, 5, 1.
parts.hint: The row is symmetrical.
parts.explanation: Each row of Pascal’s triangle reads the same forwards and backwards, so the number matching the 10 near the end is also 10.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The dot patterns below form an L shape. Find an expression for the number of dots in Figure n.
parts.hint: The counts go up by 2 each time.
parts.explanation: The counts are 1, 3, 5, rising by 2, so the rule starts 2n. At n = 1 that gives 2 but the figure has 1 dot, so the number of dots in Figure n is 2n − 1.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The dot patterns below grow in a regular way. How many dots are in Figure 6?
parts.hint: Each figure is three rows deep.
parts.explanation: Each figure has 3 rows, with 1, 2 and 3 dots per row, giving 3, 6 and 9 dots. Figure 6 has 6 dots per row, so 3 × 6 = 18 dots.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Patterns and Sequences; NCE 2025 Q15(a) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Each of the dot patterns below has three rows. Find an expression for the number of dots in Figure n.
parts.hint: Three rows, each getting one longer.
parts.explanation: Each figure has 3 rows of n dots, so Figure n has 3n dots.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Patterns and Sequences; NCE 2025 Q15(a) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the 10th term of the sequence with nth term 5n + 2.
parts.hint: Substitute n = 10.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Patterns and Sequences; NCE 2025 Q15(a) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The nth term of a sequence is 2n2. Write down its first three terms.
parts.hint: Substitute n = 1, 2 and 3 in turn.
parts.explanation: 2(1)² = 2, 2(2)² = 8 and 2(3)² = 18, so the first three terms are 2, 8 and 18.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Patterns and Sequences; NCE 2025 Q15(a) pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The sequence 4, 9, 16, 25 continues in the same way. Find its nth term.
parts.hint: These are square numbers, but not starting from 1.
parts.explanation: The terms are 2², 3², 4², 5². The number being squared is one more than n, so the nth term is (n + 1)².

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality x + 3 > 7, giving your answer in set-builder notation.
parts.hint: Subtract 3 from both sides, as you would with an equation.
parts.explanation: x + 3 > 7 gives x > 4, written { x : x > 4 }.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality 2x < 10, giving your answer in set-builder notation.
parts.hint: Divide both sides by 2, which is positive, so the sign does not change.
parts.explanation: 2x < 10 gives x < 5, written { x : x < 5 }.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality 5x + 4 ≤ 24.
parts.hint: Subtract 4, then divide by 5.
parts.explanation: 5x + 4 ≤ 24 gives 5x ≤ 20, so x ≤ 4, written { x : x ≤ 4 }.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality −5x > 20.
parts.hint: Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign.
parts.explanation: Dividing both sides by −5 reverses the sign: x < −4, written { x : x < −4 }. Answering x > −4 is the common mistake - the sign must turn round.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality −3x ≤ 12.
parts.hint: Dividing by −3 turns ≤ into ≥.
parts.explanation: Dividing by −3 reverses the sign: x ≥ −4, written { x : x ≥ −4 }.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality 4x − 5 ≥ 7.
parts.hint: Add 5, then divide by 4.
parts.explanation: 4x − 5 ≥ 7 gives 4x ≥ 12, so x ≥ 3, written { x : x ≥ 3 }.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality x − 6 < −2.
parts.hint: Add 6 to both sides.
parts.explanation: x − 6 < −2 gives x < 4, written { x : x < 4 }.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality 3 − 2x > 9.
parts.hint: Move the 3 first, then divide by −2 and turn the sign round.
parts.explanation: Subtracting 3: −2x > 6. Dividing by −2 reverses the sign: x < −3, written { x : x < −3 }.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality 5x + 2 < 3x + 10.
parts.hint: Collect the x terms on one side first.
parts.explanation: Subtracting 3x: 2x + 2 < 10. Subtracting 2: 2x < 8, so x < 4, written { x : x < 4 }.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality x⁄3 ≥ 2.
parts.hint: Multiply both sides by 3.
parts.explanation: Multiplying by 3 gives x ≥ 6, written { x : x ≥ 6 }.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which inequality means “x is at least 5”?
parts.hint: “At least” means 5 itself is allowed.
parts.explanation: “At least 5” means 5 or more, so x ≥ 5. Using > would wrongly exclude 5 itself.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which inequality means “x is less than 8”?
parts.hint: “Less than” does not include the number itself.
parts.explanation: “Less than 8” excludes 8, so x < 8.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write down the smallest integer that satisfies x > 3.7.
parts.hint: The answer must be a whole number bigger than 3.7.
parts.explanation: The integers greater than 3.7 are 4, 5, 6, …, so the smallest is 4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write down the largest integer that satisfies x ≤ 6.2.
parts.hint: The answer must be a whole number no bigger than 6.2.
parts.explanation: The integers less than or equal to 6.2 are …, 5, 6, so the largest is 6.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality 2(x − 1) < 3x + 4.
parts.hint: Expand the bracket, then collect the x terms; watch the sign at the end.
parts.explanation: Expanding: 2x − 2 < 3x + 4. Subtracting 2x: −2 < x + 4. Subtracting 4: −6 < x, which is x > −6, written { x : x > −6 }.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which inequality is shown on the number line?
parts.hint: A filled circle includes its value; a hollow circle excludes it.
parts.explanation: The circle at −1 is filled, so −1 is included and the sign is ≤. The circle at 3 is hollow, so 3 is excluded and the sign is <. The inequality is −1 ≤ x < 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write down the inequality represented by the number line below.
parts.hint: Check each end separately.
parts.explanation: The circle at 0 is hollow, so 0 is excluded: 0 < x. The circle at 4 is filled, so 4 is included: x ≤ 4. Together, 0 < x ≤ 4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality −x⁄2 ≥ 3.
parts.hint: Multiplying by −2 reverses the sign.
parts.explanation: Multiplying both sides by −2 reverses the sign: x ≤ −6, written { x : x ≤ −6 }.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many integers satisfy −2 < x ≤ 3?
parts.hint: List them, remembering which end is included.
parts.explanation: −2 is excluded and 3 is included, so the integers are −1, 0, 1, 2, 3 - five of them.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Inequalities (set-builder notation); NCE 2025 Q14 and 2024 Q16 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality 7 − x ≤ 2.
parts.hint: Move the x across, or divide by −1 and turn the sign.
parts.explanation: Subtracting 7: −x ≤ −5. Multiplying by −1 reverses the sign: x ≥ 5, written { x : x ≥ 5 }.

grade9-maths.source: NCF §3.9 Inequalities; NCE 2024 Q16 solve-then-draw pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality 2x + 3 ≤ 11.
parts.hint: Subtract 3, then divide by 2.
parts.explanation: 2x + 3 ≤ 11 gives 2x ≤ 8, so x ≤ 4.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Draw a number line to represent the inequality in part (a).
parts.rubric: One mark for a number line with a FILLED circle at 4 and the line shaded to the left, with an arrow. Follow-through: accept a correct representation of the candidate's own answer to part (a). A hollow circle scores zero, because ≤ includes its endpoint.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Personal and Household Finance (CEB/CWA bills); NCE 2025 Q27 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A worker is paid Rs 450 per day. Find his pay for 6 days.
parts.hint: Multiply the daily rate by the number of days.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Personal and Household Finance (CEB/CWA bills); NCE 2025 Q27 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A clerk earns Rs 24 000 per month. Find her annual salary.
parts.hint: There are 12 months in a year.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Personal and Household Finance (CEB/CWA bills); NCE 2025 Q27 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A worker is paid Rs 150 per hour for overtime. Find his pay for 8 hours of overtime.
parts.hint: Multiply the hourly rate by the hours worked.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Personal and Household Finance (CEB/CWA bills); NCE 2025 Q27 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A basic salary is Rs 18 000. A bonus of 10% is added. Find the total pay.
parts.hint: Find 10% first, then add it on.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Personal and Household Finance (CEB/CWA bills); NCE 2025 Q27 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A salary of Rs 20 000 has 5% deducted for a pension. Find the net salary.
parts.hint: Work out the deduction, then subtract it.
parts.explanation: 5% of 20 000 = 1 000, so the net salary is 20 000 − 1 000 = Rs 19 000.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Personal and Household Finance (CEB/CWA bills); NCE 2025 Q27 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A television is bought on hire purchase with a deposit of Rs 5 000 and 12 monthly payments of Rs 1 500. Find the total amount paid.
parts.hint: Deposit plus all the monthly payments.
parts.explanation: The monthly payments come to 12 × 1 500 = Rs 18 000. Adding the deposit: 5 000 + 18 000 = Rs 23 000.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Personal and Household Finance (CEB/CWA bills); NCE 2025 Q27 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The cash price of a television is Rs 20 000. On hire purchase it costs a total of Rs 23 000. Find the extra amount paid for buying on hire purchase.
parts.hint: Compare the two totals.
parts.explanation: 23 000 − 20 000 = Rs 3 000 more than paying cash.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Personal and Household Finance (CEB/CWA bills); NCE 2025 Q27 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: John deposits Rs 200 000 for a period of 30 months in a bank. The rate of simple interest is 3% per annum. Find the total amount John will get when he withdraws all his money after 30 months.
parts.hint: Change 30 months into years before using the formula.
parts.explanation: 30 months = 2.5 years. Interest = 200 000 × 3/100 × 2.5 = Rs 15 000. The total is 200 000 + 15 000 = Rs 215 000.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Personal and Household Finance (CEB/CWA bills); NCE 2025 Q27 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A man invests Rs 300 000 for 5 years at 2% per annum. Calculate the simple interest he earns.
parts.hint: Interest = principal × rate × time.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Personal and Household Finance (CEB/CWA bills); NCE 2025 Q27 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the simple interest on Rs 50 000 at 4% per annum for 3 years.
parts.hint: Interest = P × R × T ÷ 100.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Personal and Household Finance (CEB/CWA bills); NCE 2025 Q27 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The simple interest on Rs 40 000 for 2 years is Rs 4 000. Find the rate per annum.
parts.hint: Rearrange the interest formula for the rate.
parts.explanation: Interest = P × R × T ÷ 100. Here 40 000 × 2 ÷ 100 = 800, so 4 000 = 800R and R = 4 000 ÷ 800 = 5% per annum.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Personal and Household Finance (CEB/CWA bills); NCE 2025 Q27 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A shopkeeper buys an article for Rs 800 and sells it for Rs 1 000. Find his profit.
parts.hint: Selling price minus cost price.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Personal and Household Finance (CEB/CWA bills); NCE 2025 Q27 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A shopkeeper buys an article for Rs 800 and sells it for Rs 1 000. Find his percentage profit.
parts.hint: Percentage profit is the profit over the COST price.
parts.explanation: The profit is Rs 200 on a cost of Rs 800, so the percentage profit is (200 ÷ 800) × 100 = 25%.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Using the electricity tariff shown, write down the rate per unit charged for the first 25 units.
parts.hint: Read straight off the first row of the table.
parts.explanation: The table gives Rs 3.50 per unit for the first 25 units.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Personal and Household Finance (CEB/CWA bills); NCE 2025 Q27 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A car is bought on hire purchase with a deposit of Rs 60 000 and 24 monthly payments of Rs 12 500. Find the total amount paid.
parts.hint: Deposit plus all the instalments.
parts.explanation: The instalments come to 24 × 12 500 = Rs 300 000. Adding the deposit: 60 000 + 300 000 = Rs 360 000.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Numbers: Personal and Household Finance (CEB/CWA bills); NCE 2025 Q27 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A worker’s basic pay is Rs 16 000 per month. He also works 20 hours of overtime at Rs 200 per hour, and 6% of his total pay is deducted. Find his net pay.
parts.hint: Add the overtime first, then take the deduction from the whole amount.
parts.explanation: Overtime = 20 × 200 = Rs 4 000, so the total pay is 16 000 + 4 000 = Rs 20 000. The deduction is 6% of 20 000 = Rs 1 200, so the net pay is 20 000 − 1 200 = Rs 18 800.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.prompt: Convert 3 L into mL.
parts.hint: There are 1 000 millilitres in a litre.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Convert 2 L into cL.
parts.hint: There are 100 centilitres in a litre.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Convert 500 mL into litres.
parts.hint: Divide by 1 000.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.prompt: Convert 75 cL into mL.
parts.hint: One centilitre is 10 millilitres.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Convert 1 250 mL into litres.
parts.hint: Divide by 1 000.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Convert 4.5 L into cL.
parts.hint: Multiply by 100.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which is larger, 600 mL or 0.6 L?
parts.hint: Put both into the same unit before comparing.
parts.explanation: 0.6 L = 0.6 × 1 000 = 600 mL, so the two are exactly equal.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A bottle holds 1.5 L of juice. How many 250 mL glasses can be filled from it?
parts.hint: Work in the same unit first.
parts.explanation: 1.5 L = 1 500 mL, and 1 500 ÷ 250 = 6 glasses.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A jug holds 2 L. It is filled from a 250 mL cup. How many cupfuls are needed?
parts.hint: Change the litres to millilitres.
parts.explanation: 2 L = 2 000 mL, and 2 000 ÷ 250 = 8 cupfuls.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A container has a volume of 1 000 cm³. Write down its capacity in litres.
parts.hint: 1 000 cm³ of space holds exactly one litre.
parts.explanation: 1 000 cm³ = 1 litre, so the capacity is 1 L.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A tank measures 20 cm by 10 cm by 5 cm. Find its capacity in millilitres.
parts.hint: Find the volume in cm³ first; 1 cm³ holds 1 mL.
parts.explanation: The volume is 20 × 10 × 5 = 1 000 cm³, and 1 cm³ holds 1 mL, so the capacity is 1 000 mL.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A tank measures 50 cm by 40 cm by 30 cm. Find its capacity in litres.
parts.hint: Volume in cm³ first, then divide by 1 000.
parts.explanation: The volume is 50 × 40 × 30 = 60 000 cm³. Since 1 000 cm³ = 1 L, the capacity is 60 000 ÷ 1 000 = 60 L.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A rectangular tank measures 30 cm by 20 cm by 25 cm. Water is poured in to a depth of 10 cm. Find the volume of water in litres.
parts.hint: Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank.
parts.explanation: The water forms a cuboid 30 × 20 × 10 = 6 000 cm³, which is 6 L.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Convert 0.25 L into mL.
parts.hint: Multiply by 1 000.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A bucket holds 12 L. A tap fills it at 2 L per minute. How long does it take to fill?
parts.hint: Divide the capacity by the rate.
parts.explanation: 12 ÷ 2 = 6 minutes.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Six identical bottles each hold 33 cL. Find the total in litres.
parts.hint: Add the centilitres first, then change to litres.
parts.explanation: 6 × 33 = 198 cL, and 198 ÷ 100 = 1.98 L.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A cubical container has edges of 10 cm. Find its capacity in litres.
parts.hint: Find the volume, then use 1 000 cm³ = 1 L.
parts.explanation: The volume is 10 × 10 × 10 = 1 000 cm³, which is 1 L.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A drum holds 25 L of water. 8 500 mL are used. How much water is left, in litres?
parts.hint: Change the millilitres to litres before subtracting.
parts.explanation: 8 500 mL = 8.5 L, so the water left is 25 − 8.5 = 16.5 L.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many centilitres are there in one litre?
parts.hint: The prefix "centi" means one hundredth.
parts.explanation: One litre is 100 centilitres.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Measurement: Capacity; NCE 2025 Q7 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A tank of capacity 90 L is 2⁄3 full. Find the volume of water in the tank, in litres.
parts.hint: Find one third first.
parts.explanation: 90 ÷ 3 = 30, so two thirds is 30 × 2 = 60 L.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
State the order of the matrix. (3
1)
parts.hint: Count the rows first, then the columns.
parts.explanation: The matrix has 2 rows and 1 column, so its order is 2 × 1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State the order of the matrix. (2  5  7)
parts.hint: Rows first, then columns.
parts.explanation: The matrix has 1 row and 3 columns, so its order is 1 × 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
State the order of the matrix. (1  2  3
4  5  6)
parts.hint: Two rows, three columns - and the rows come first.
parts.explanation: There are 2 rows and 3 columns, so the order is 2 × 3. Writing 3 × 2 is the usual mistake: the row count is always given first.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A matrix has order 3 × 4. How many elements does it contain?
parts.hint: Multiply the rows by the columns.
parts.explanation: 3 rows of 4 elements gives 3 × 4 = 12 elements.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which of these is a square matrix?
parts.hint: A square matrix has as many rows as columns.
parts.explanation: Only the 2 × 2 matrix has an equal number of rows and columns, so it is the square one.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which of these is the 2 × 2 identity matrix?
parts.hint: The identity has 1s down the leading diagonal and 0s elsewhere.
parts.explanation: The identity matrix has 1s on the leading diagonal, from top left to bottom right, and 0s everywhere else.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which of these is a null (zero) matrix?
parts.hint: Every element must be zero.
parts.explanation: A null matrix has 0 in every position.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which of these is a diagonal matrix?
parts.hint: Everything off the leading diagonal must be zero.
parts.explanation: A diagonal matrix has non-zero entries only on the leading diagonal and 0 everywhere else.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Find A + B, where A = (1  2
3  4) and B = (5  6
7  8).
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
parts.hint: Add the numbers in matching positions.
parts.explanation: Adding element by element: 1+5 = 6, 2+6 = 8, 3+7 = 10 and 4+8 = 12, giving (6 8; 10 12).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Find A − B, where A = (7  5
3  2) and B = (2  1
1  4).
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
parts.hint: Subtract element by element, keeping the positions.
parts.explanation: Subtracting: 7−2 = 5, 5−1 = 4, 3−1 = 2 and 2−4 = −2, giving (5 4; 2 −2).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Find 3A, where A = (1  -2
4  0).
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
parts.hint: Multiply every element by 3.
parts.explanation: Multiplying each element by 3: (3 −6; 12 0).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Find 2A − B, where A = (2  -3
0  5) and B = (-1  4
6  2).
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
parts.hint: Double A first, then subtract B element by element.
parts.explanation: 2A = (4 −6; 0 10). Subtracting B: 4−(−1) = 5, −6−4 = −10, 0−6 = −6 and 10−2 = 8, giving (5 −10; −6 8).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Find P + Q, where P = (8
-5) and Q = (3
2).
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
parts.hint: Add the top numbers, then the bottom numbers.
parts.explanation: 8+3 = 11 and −5+2 = −3, giving (11; −3).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Solve the matrix equation X + (1  2
3  4) = (5  7
9  11) for X.
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
parts.hint: Subtract the known matrix from both sides.
parts.explanation: X = (5 7; 9 11) − (1 2; 3 4). Subtracting element by element: (4 5; 6 7).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Solve the matrix equation Y − (2  0
1  3) = (1  4
2  2) for Y.
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
parts.hint: Add the known matrix to both sides.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Two matrices are equal. What must be true of them?

options: They have the same order and every matching element is equal
They have the same order only
They contain exactly the same numbers in any positions
They have the same number of elements
response.answer: They have the same order and every matching element is equal

parts.hint: Both the shape and every entry must match.
parts.explanation: Equal matrices must have the same order AND identical elements in matching positions. Two matrices holding the same numbers in different places are not equal.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Given that (x
3) + (2
y) = (7
10), find the values of x and y.
parts.hint: Matching positions must be equal, so write down two ordinary equations.
parts.explanation: The top entries give x + 2 = 7, so x = 5. The bottom entries give 3 + y = 10, so y = 7.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A shop records its sales in a matrix with 4 rows and 2 columns. State the order of the matrix.
parts.hint: Rows first.
parts.explanation: With 4 rows and 2 columns the order is 4 × 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Find 2Q, where Q = (3
2).
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
parts.hint: Multiply each element by 2.
parts.explanation: 2 × 3 = 6 and 2 × 2 = 4, giving (6; 4).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebra: Matrices; NCE 2025 Q4 and 2024 Q24 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Find A + 2B, where A = (1  0
2  1) and B = (3  1
0  4).
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
parts.hint: Work out 2B first, then add A.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebraic manipulation; NCE 2025 Q23 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Make x the subject of y = x + 5.
parts.hint: Subtract 5 from both sides.
parts.explanation: Subtracting 5 from both sides gives x = y − 5.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebraic manipulation; NCE 2025 Q23 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Make x the subject of y = 3x.
parts.hint: Divide both sides by 3.
parts.explanation: Dividing both sides by 3 gives x = y/3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebraic manipulation; NCE 2025 Q23 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Make x the subject of y = 2x + 7.
parts.hint: Undo the +7 first, then the ×2.
parts.explanation: Subtracting 7: y − 7 = 2x. Dividing by 2: x = (y − 7)/2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebraic manipulation; NCE 2025 Q23 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Make r the subject of C = 2πr.
parts.hint: Divide both sides by everything multiplying r.
parts.explanation: Dividing both sides by 2π gives r = C/(2π).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebraic manipulation; NCE 2025 Q23 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Make h the subject of V = lwh.
parts.hint: Divide both sides by the two lengths.
parts.explanation: Dividing both sides by lw gives h = V/(lw).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebraic manipulation; NCE 2025 Q23 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Make b the subject of A = 1⁄2bh.
parts.hint: Multiply by 2 first, then divide by h.
parts.explanation: Multiplying both sides by 2: 2A = bh. Dividing by h: b = 2A/h.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebraic manipulation; NCE 2025 Q23 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the value of y when x = 4, given y = 3x − 2.
parts.hint: Substitute 4 in place of x.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebraic manipulation; NCE 2025 Q23 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the value of A when l = 6 and w = 5, given A = lw.
parts.hint: Multiply the two values.
parts.explanation: A = 6 × 5 = 30.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebraic manipulation; NCE 2025 Q23 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the value of V when l = 4, w = 3 and h = 2, given V = lwh.
parts.hint: Multiply all three values.
parts.explanation: V = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebraic manipulation; NCE 2025 Q23 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the value of s when u = 5, t = 3 and a = 2, given s = ut + at2.
parts.hint: Work out each term separately, then add.
parts.explanation: ut = 5 × 3 = 15 and at² = 2 × 9 = 18, so s = 15 + 18 = 33.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebraic manipulation; NCE 2025 Q23 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the value of A when r = 7 and l = 4, given A = πr2 + πrl. Leave your answer in terms of π.
parts.hint: Work out each term with π kept as a symbol, then add.
parts.explanation: πr² = 49π and πrl = π × 7 × 4 = 28π. Adding: A = 49π + 28π = 77π.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebraic manipulation; NCE 2025 Q23 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Make l the subject of A = πr2 + πrl, leaving your answer in terms of π.
parts.hint: Get the term containing l on its own first.
parts.explanation: Subtracting πr² from both sides: A − πr² = πrl. Dividing by πr: l = (A − πr²)/(πr).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebraic manipulation; NCE 2025 Q23 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Make C the subject of F = 9⁄5C + 32.
parts.hint: Subtract 32 first, then undo the fraction.
parts.explanation: Subtracting 32: F − 32 = (9/5)C. Multiplying by 5 and dividing by 9: C = 5(F − 32)/9.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebraic manipulation; NCE 2025 Q23 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the value of P when l = 8 and w = 3, given P = 2(l + w).
parts.hint: Do the bracket first.
parts.explanation: l + w = 11, so P = 2 × 11 = 22.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9 Algebraic manipulation; NCE 2025 Q23 pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Make w the subject of P = 2(l + w).
parts.hint: Expand the bracket, or divide by 2 first.

parts.label: a

parts.hint: Move the term without l to the other side, then divide.
parts.explanation: Subtracting πr²: A − πr² = πrl. Dividing by πr: l = (A − πr²)/(πr).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A shopkeeper buys 40 shirts at Rs 250 each. He sells 30 of them at Rs 400 each and the remaining 10 at Rs 300 each. Calculate his total profit.
parts.hint: Work out the total cost, then the total money taken, then compare.

parts.label: a

parts.explanation: 18 000 ÷ 45 = 400 euros. After spending 240 she has 160 euros left. Changing back at 40 rupees to the euro gives 160 × 40 = Rs 6 400.

parts.prompt: The diagram shows a rectangular tank measuring 120 cm by 50 cm by 40 cm. Water flows into the empty tank at 8 litres per minute. How many minutes does it take to fill?

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A closed rectangular box measures 30 cm by 20 cm by 10 cm. It is to be covered with paper costing Rs 2 per 100 cm². Calculate the cost of the paper.
parts.hint: Find the total surface area first, then work out how many hundreds of square centimetres.
parts.explanation: The three different faces are 30×20 = 600, 30×10 = 300 and 20×10 = 200 cm². Each occurs twice, so the surface area is 2(600 + 300 + 200) = 2 200 cm². That is 22 lots of 100 cm², costing 22 × 2 = Rs 44.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In the right-angled triangle shown, AC = 20 cm and the angle at C is 30°. Calculate the perimeter of the triangle, giving your answer to the nearest whole number. [Given sin 30° = 0.5, cos 30° = 0.87]
parts.hint: Find each of the two shorter sides in turn, then add all three.
parts.explanation: AB is opposite the 30° angle: sin 30° = AB/20, so AB = 20 × 0.5 = 10 cm. BC is adjacent: cos 30° = BC/20, so BC = 20 × 0.87 = 17.4 cm. The perimeter is 10 + 17.4 + 20 = 47.4 cm, which is 47 cm to the nearest whole number.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The table shows the marks scored by 20 pupils in a test. Calculate the mean mark.
parts.hint: Multiply each mark by how many pupils scored it, add those up, then divide by 20.
parts.explanation: The total is (4×5) + (5×6) + (6×5) + (7×4) = 20 + 30 + 30 + 28 = 108. The mean is 108 ÷ 20 = 5.4 marks exactly.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A bag contains 4 red, 5 blue and 6 green marbles. One marble is drawn at random and NOT replaced. It is green. A second marble is then drawn. Find the probability that the second marble is also green.
parts.hint: Recount both the greens and the total after the first marble has gone.
parts.explanation: At the start there are 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 marbles, of which 6 are green. One green is removed and not replaced, leaving 14 marbles of which 5 are green. So the probability that the second is green is 5/14.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2024 Q31 (6 marks) and Q33 (7 marks) extended-tail pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line passes through A (−1, −3) and B (3, 5). A second line is parallel to AB and passes through (0, 4). Find the equation of the second line.
parts.hint: Find the gradient of AB first; parallel lines share it.
parts.explanation: The gradient of AB is (5 − (−3)) ÷ (3 − (−1)) = 8/4 = 2. The second line has the same gradient and passes through (0, 4), so its intercept is 4 and its equation is y = 2x + 4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2024 Q31 (6 marks) and Q33 (7 marks) extended-tail pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A rectangle has length (x + 5) cm and width (x − 2) cm. Show that its area is x2 + 3x − 10, then find the area when x = 6.
parts.hint: Expand the brackets first, then substitute.
parts.explanation: Area = (x + 5)(x − 2) = x² − 2x + 5x − 10 = x² + 3x − 10. Substituting x = 6: 36 + 18 − 10 = 44 cm².

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2024 Q31 (6 marks) and Q33 (7 marks) extended-tail pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: At a canteen, 3 rotis and 2 cups of tea cost Rs 85. 5 rotis and 4 cups of tea cost Rs 155. Find the cost of 2 rotis and 3 cups of tea.
parts.hint: Let r be a roti and t a cup of tea, write two equations, then answer the question asked.
parts.explanation: From 3r + 2t = 85 and 5r + 4t = 155. Doubling the first: 6r + 4t = 170. Subtracting the second: r = 15. Substituting back: 45 + 2t = 85, so t = 20. Then 2 rotis and 3 teas cost 2(15) + 3(20) = 30 + 60 = Rs 80.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2024 Q31 (6 marks) and Q33 (7 marks) extended-tail pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A rectangular garden is 4 m longer than it is wide. Its area is 96 m². Find the perimeter of the garden.
parts.hint: Call the width x, form a quadratic, solve it, then answer the question that was asked.
parts.explanation: Let the width be x m, so the length is (x + 4) m and x(x + 4) = 96. This gives x² + 4x − 96 = 0, so (x + 12)(x − 8) = 0 and x = −12 or x = 8. A width cannot be negative, so the width is 8 m and the length is 12 m. The perimeter is 2(8 + 12) = 40 m.

parts.label: b

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2024 Q31 (6 marks) and Q33 (7 marks) extended-tail pattern, and the 4-mark multi-part questions in the body.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Share Rs 4 200 between Aisha and Ben in the ratio 3 : 4. How much does Aisha get?
parts.hint: Find the value of one share first.
parts.explanation: 3 + 4 = 7 shares, and 4200 ÷ 7 = Rs 600 per share. Aisha gets 3 × 600 = Rs 1 800.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How much more than Aisha does Ben receive?
parts.hint: Ben has one more share than Aisha.
parts.explanation: Ben gets 4 × 600 = Rs 2 400, so he receives 2 400 − 1 800 = Rs 600 more.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2024 Q31 (6 marks) and Q33 (7 marks) extended-tail pattern, and the 4-mark multi-part questions in the body.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise x2 + 2x − 15.
parts.hint: Find two numbers that multiply to −15 and add to +2.
parts.explanation: +5 and −3 multiply to −15 and add to +2, so x² + 2x − 15 = (x + 5)(x − 3).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Hence solve x2 + 2x − 15 = 0, giving the positive root.
parts.hint: Each bracket can be zero.
parts.explanation: (x + 5)(x − 3) = 0 gives x = −5 or x = 3. The positive root is x = 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2024 Q31 (6 marks) and Q33 (7 marks) extended-tail pattern, and the 4-mark multi-part questions in the body.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining A (1, 3) and B (5, 11).
parts.hint: Gradient is the change in y divided by the change in x.
parts.explanation: (11 − 3) ÷ (5 − 1) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the y-intercept of the line AB.
parts.hint: Substitute one of the points into y = 2x + c.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A ladder leans against a wall as shown. Calculate the height it reaches up the wall, to 1 decimal place.
parts.hint: The height is opposite the 60° angle: use sin.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate how far the foot of the ladder is from the wall.
parts.hint: That distance is adjacent to the 60° angle: use cos.
parts.explanation: cos 60° = d ÷ 6, so d = 6 × 0.5 = 3 m.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The ladder slips so that it now makes 45° with the ground. Calculate the height it reaches up the wall, to 1 decimal place.
parts.hint: Use sin again, with the new angle.
parts.explanation: 6 × sin 45° = 6 × 0.7071 = 4.243, which is 4.2 m to 1 d.p. - lower than before, because sin 45° is less than sin 60°.

parts.label: a

parts.hint: Multiply the second equation so that one letter cancels.
parts.explanation: 2p + 3b = 235 and 4p + b = 195. Multiplying the second by 3 gives 12p + 3b = 585. Subtracting the first: 10p = 350, so p = Rs 35.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a class of 40 pupils, 22 study French and 18 study Spanish. 7 study both. How many study French only?
parts.hint: Take the overlap away from the French total.
parts.explanation: 22 − 7 = 15 pupils study French only.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How many study neither language?
parts.hint: Add the three regions inside the circles, then subtract from 40.
parts.explanation: French only 15, both 7, Spanish only 18 − 7 = 11. That is 15 + 7 + 11 = 33, so 40 − 33 = 7 pupils study neither.

parts.hint: Multiply each mark by its frequency and add.

parts.label: b.ii
parts.prompt: Calculate the mean mark, to 2 decimal places.
parts.hint: Total marks divided by number of pupils.
parts.explanation: 91 ÷ 30 = 3.033..., which is 3.03 to 2 d.p.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: How many pupils scored more than the mean?
parts.hint: Count everyone whose mark is above 3.03.
parts.explanation: Marks of 4 (7 pupils) and 5 (4 pupils) are above 3.03, so 7 + 4 = 11 pupils.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A shirt costs Rs 1 250. Its price is reduced by 12%. Calculate the reduction.
parts.hint: 12% means 12 out of every 100.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the new price of the shirt.
parts.hint: Take the reduction off the original price.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a.i
parts.prompt: Express 3⁄8 as a decimal.
parts.hint: Divide 3 by 8.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.prompt: Express 3⁄8 as a percentage.
parts.hint: Multiply the decimal by 100.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A tank holds 640 litres. Calculate <sup>3</sup>⁄<sub>8</sub> of its capacity.
parts.hint: Divide by 8, then multiply by 3.
parts.explanation: 640 ÷ 8 = 80, and 80 × 3 = 240 litres.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a.i
parts.prompt: A map has a scale of 1 : 50 000. Two towns are 8 cm apart on the map. Find the real distance in centimetres.
parts.hint: Multiply the map distance by the scale factor.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.prompt: Express that distance in kilometres.
parts.hint: There are 100 000 cm in a kilometre.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A third town is 11 km from the first. How far apart are they on the map?
parts.hint: Turn the kilometres into centimetres first, then divide by 50 000.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a.i
parts.prompt: Calculate <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> + <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>4</sub>, giving your answer as a fraction in its lowest terms.
parts.hint: Use a common denominator of 12.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.prompt: Calculate <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> − <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>4</sub>.
parts.hint: The same common denominator.

parts.label: a.iii
parts.prompt: Calculate <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> × <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>4</sub>, in its lowest terms.
parts.hint: Multiply the tops and the bottoms, then simplify.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A recipe for 4 people needs 600 g of rice. How much is needed for 6 people?
parts.hint: Find the amount for one person first.
parts.explanation: 600 ÷ 4 = 150 g each, so 6 people need 6 × 150 = 900 g.

parts.label: b.i
parts.prompt: Rice is sold in 2 kg bags. How many whole bags are needed for 6 people?
parts.hint: 900 g is less than 2 kg.
parts.explanation: 900 g is under 2 000 g, so one bag is enough.

parts.label: b.ii
parts.prompt: How many people could be fed from one 2 kg bag?
parts.hint: Divide 2 000 g by the amount one person needs, then round down.
parts.explanation: 2 000 ÷ 150 = 13.33, and you cannot feed a third of a person, so 13.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a.i
parts.prompt: A sum of Rs 25 000 is invested at 6% simple interest per year. Calculate the interest earned in one year.
parts.hint: 6% of the sum invested.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.prompt: Calculate the interest earned in 3 years.
parts.hint: Simple interest is the same every year.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write down the total amount after 3 years.
parts.hint: Add the interest to the original sum.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: For how many whole years must it be invested for the interest to exceed Rs 10 000?
parts.hint: Divide 10 000 by the yearly interest and round up.
parts.explanation: 10 000 ÷ 1 500 = 6.67, so after 6 years the interest is Rs 9 000 and after 7 it is Rs 10 500. The answer is 7 years.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a.i
parts.prompt: A car travels 210 km in 3 hours. Calculate its average speed.
parts.hint: Speed is distance divided by time.
parts.explanation: 210 ÷ 3 = 70 km/h.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.prompt: At the same speed, how far would it travel in 5 hours?
parts.hint: Speed multiplied by time.
parts.explanation: 70 × 5 = 350 km.

parts.label: b.i
parts.prompt: How long would a journey of 490 km take at that speed? Give your answer in hours.
parts.hint: Distance divided by speed.
parts.explanation: 490 ÷ 70 = 7 hours.

parts.label: b.ii
parts.prompt: The car uses 1 litre of fuel every 14 km. How many litres does the 490 km journey use?
parts.hint: Divide the distance by the distance per litre.
parts.explanation: 490 ÷ 14 = 35 litres.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The diagram shows the points A (1, 1) and B (5, 4). Write down the x-component of the vector AB.
parts.hint: Subtract the x of A from the x of B.
parts.explanation: 5 − 1 = 4.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write down the y-component of AB.
parts.hint: Subtract the y of A from the y of B.
parts.explanation: 4 − 1 = 3.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a.i
parts.prompt: Given a with components (3, 4), calculate its magnitude.
parts.hint: Use Pythagoras on the two components.
parts.explanation: √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.prompt: Given b with components (6, 8), calculate its magnitude.
parts.hint: The same method.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: b is a multiple of a. Write down the value of k for which b = ka.
parts.hint: Compare the components.
parts.explanation: 6 = 2 × 3 and 8 = 2 × 4, so k = 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a.i
parts.prompt: A point P (2, 3) is translated by the vector with components (4, −1). Write down the x-coordinate of the image.
parts.hint: Add the x-component to the x-coordinate.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.prompt: Write down the y-coordinate of the image.
parts.hint: Add the y-component, remembering it is negative.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The image is then translated back to P. Write down the x-component of that second translation.
parts.hint: It must undo the first translation.
parts.explanation: The reverse of (4, −1) is (−4, 1), so the x-component is −4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a.i
parts.prompt: Given a = (2, 5) and b = (3, −1), find the x-component of a + b.
parts.hint: Add the x parts.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.prompt: Find the y-component of a + b.
parts.hint: Add the y parts.

parts.label: b.i
parts.prompt: Find the x-component of 2a − b.
parts.hint: Double a first, then subtract b.
parts.explanation: 2 × 2 = 4, and 4 − 3 = 1.

parts.label: b.ii
parts.prompt: Find the y-component of 2a − b.
parts.hint: The same, taking care with the minus.
parts.explanation: 2 × 5 = 10, and 10 − (−1) = 11.
