parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line passes through A (0, 2) and B (4, 10). Find its gradient.
parts.hint: Change in y over change in x.
parts.explanation: (10 − 2) ÷ (4 − 0) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write down the y-intercept.
parts.hint: A has x = 0, so it is on the y-axis.
parts.explanation: A is (0, 2), so the y-intercept is 2.

parts.prompt: Find the value of y when x = 7.
parts.hint: Use y = 2x + 2.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the value of x when y = 0.
parts.hint: Set y to zero and solve.
parts.explanation: 0 = 2x + 2 gives x = −1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line through P (−2, 1) and Q (2, 9).
parts.hint: Take the differences in the same order.
parts.explanation: (9 − 1) ÷ (2 − (−2)) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

parts.label: b.i
parts.prompt: Find the midpoint of PQ. Write down its x-coordinate.
parts.hint: The midpoint x is the average of the two x values.
parts.explanation: (−2 + 2) ÷ 2 = 0.

parts.label: b.ii
parts.prompt: Write down the y-coordinate of the midpoint.
parts.hint: The average of the two y values.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a.i
parts.prompt: A line has equation y = 3x − 4. Write down its gradient.
parts.hint: The number in front of x.
parts.explanation: In y = mx + c the gradient m is 3.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.prompt: Write down its y-intercept.
parts.hint: The constant term.
parts.explanation: c = −4.

parts.label: b.i
parts.prompt: The point (5, k) lies on the line. Find k.
parts.hint: Substitute x = 5.

parts.label: b.ii
parts.prompt: A second line is parallel to the first and passes through (0, 6). Find y when x = 2.
parts.hint: Parallel lines share a gradient, so the second line is y = 3x + 6.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise x2 − 7x + 12.
parts.hint: Two numbers multiplying to 12 and adding to −7.
parts.explanation: −3 and −4 give (x − 3)(x − 4).

parts.label: b.i
parts.prompt: Hence write down the smaller root of x2 − 7x + 12 = 0.
parts.hint: Each bracket can be zero.
parts.explanation: x = 3 or x = 4; the smaller is 3.

parts.label: b.ii
parts.prompt: A rectangle has length (x − 3) cm and width (x − 4) cm. When x = 9, calculate its area.
parts.hint: Substitute x = 9 into both sides, then multiply.
parts.explanation: Length = 6 cm and width = 5 cm, so the area is 30 cm².

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise x2 + 9x + 20.
parts.hint: Two numbers multiplying to 20 and adding to 9.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write down the two roots of x2 + 9x + 20 = 0. Give the more negative one.
parts.hint: Each bracket can be zero.
parts.explanation: x = −4 or x = −5; the more negative is −5.

parts.label: c.i
parts.prompt: Find the sum of the two roots.
parts.hint: Add them.
parts.explanation: −4 + (−5) = −9.

parts.label: c.ii
parts.prompt: Find the product of the two roots.
parts.hint: Multiply them.
parts.explanation: (−4) × (−5) = 20.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a.i
parts.prompt: Simplify 2<sup>5</sup> × 2<sup>3</sup>, giving your answer as a power of 2. Write down the index.
parts.hint: When multiplying powers of the same base, add the indices.
parts.explanation: 5 + 3 = 8, so the answer is 2^8.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.prompt: Simplify 2<sup>9</sup> ÷ 2<sup>4</sup>. Write down the index.
parts.hint: When dividing, subtract the indices.
parts.explanation: 9 − 4 = 5, so the answer is 2^5.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Evaluate 2<sup>5</sup>.
parts.hint: Multiply 2 by itself five times.
parts.explanation: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Evaluate 3<sup>−2</sup>, giving your answer as a fraction.
parts.hint: A negative index means one over the positive power.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write down the value of 12<sup>0</sup> × 3<sup>0</sup>.
parts.hint: Anything raised to the power zero is 1.
parts.explanation: 12^0 = 1 and 3^0 = 1, so the product is 1 × 1 = 1.

parts.label: c.i
parts.prompt: Simplify 4<sup>3</sup> × 4<sup>−5</sup>. Write down the index of the answer as a power of 4.
parts.hint: Add the indices, keeping the sign.
parts.explanation: 3 + (−5) = −2, so the answer is 4^-2.

parts.label: c.ii
parts.prompt: Hence evaluate 4<sup>3</sup> × 4<sup>−5</sup> as a fraction.
parts.hint: Use your answer to (c).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a.i
parts.prompt: Expand (x + 6)(x − 2).
parts.hint: Multiply every term in the first bracket by every term in the second.
parts.explanation: x² − 2x + 6x − 12 = x² + 4x − 12.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.prompt: Hence find the value of the expression when x = 3.
parts.hint: Substitute into your expanded form, or into the brackets.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Factorise x2 − 36.
parts.hint: A difference of two squares.
parts.explanation: x² − 6² = (x + 6)(x − 6).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Expand (2x − 3)2.
parts.hint: A square means the bracket multiplied by itself; there are three terms in the answer.
parts.explanation: (2x − 3)(2x − 3) = 4x² − 6x − 6x + 9 = 4x² − 12x + 9.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the value of the expression when x = 5.
parts.hint: Substitute, or square (2×5 − 3) directly.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The formula for the perimeter of a rectangle is P = 2(l + w). Find P when l = 12 and w = 7.
parts.hint: Add first, then double.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Make w the subject and hence find w when P = 50 and l = 15.
parts.hint: Divide by 2, then subtract l.
parts.explanation: w = P/2 − l = 50/2 − 15 = 25 − 15 = 10.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE multi-part body questions. Written to give the heaviest chapters an alternative at 4-7 marks.

parts.label: a.i
parts.prompt: Solve 3x + 4 ≤ 19, giving your answer in the form x ≤ k. Write down k.
parts.hint: Subtract 4, then divide by 3.
parts.explanation: 3x ≤ 15, so x ≤ 5.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.prompt: Write down the largest integer that satisfies the inequality.
parts.hint: The sign allows equality.
parts.explanation: x ≤ 5 includes 5 itself.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Solve −2x > 8, giving your answer in the form x < k. Write down k.
parts.hint: Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign.
parts.explanation: Dividing both sides by −2 gives x < −4.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate: 8/11 − 5/11
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract the numerators; the denominator stays the same.
grade9-maths.explanation: 8/11 − 5/11 = 3/11 ≈ 0.2727. Fractions with the same denominator are subtracted by subtracting their numerators.

grade9-maths.question: Express 27/100 as a decimal.
grade9-maths.hint: Dividing by 100 moves the decimal point two places to the left.
grade9-maths.explanation: 27 ÷ 100 = 0.27. The digit 7 is in the hundredths place.

grade9-maths.question: Reduce 24/30 to its lowest terms.
grade9-maths.hint: Find the HCF of 24 and 30, then divide both by it.

grade9-maths.question: What is 35% of 200?
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply 200 by 35 and divide by 100.

grade9-maths.question: Convert 7 kg to grams.
Convert 350 cm to metres.
grade9-maths.hint: Divide by 100 to convert cm to m.

grade9-maths.question: China is 4 hours ahead of Mauritius. When it is 17:00 in Mauritius, what time is it in China?
grade9-maths.hint: Add 4 hours to the Mauritius time.
grade9-maths.explanation: 17:00 + 4 hours = 21:00 in China.

grade9-maths.question: A car travels at a constant speed of 80 km/h. How far does it travel in 2.5 hours? Give your answer in km.
grade9-maths.hint: Distance = speed × time.
grade9-maths.explanation: Distance = 80 × 2.5 = 200 km.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (a⁴)⁵.
grade9-maths.hint: Use the power law: (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ.

grade9-maths.question: Write 2 × 2 × 2 in index form.
grade9-maths.hint: Count how many times 2 appears as a factor.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2 appears as a factor 3 times, so 2 × 2 × 2 = 2³.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify a⁶ ÷ a².
grade9-maths.hint: Division law: subtract the exponents.

grade9-maths.question: Write 1/x³ using a negative index.
grade9-maths.hint: 1/xⁿ = x⁻ⁿ.
grade9-maths.explanation: By the negative index rule, 1/x³ = x⁻³.

grade9-maths.question: Complete the sequence: 3, 10, 17, 24, ___.
grade9-maths.hint: Find the common difference between consecutive terms.
grade9-maths.explanation: Each term increases by 7. So the next term is 24 + 7 = 31.

grade9-maths.question: The nth term of a sequence is 4n − 1. What is the 5th term?
grade9-maths.hint: Substitute n = 5 into the formula.

grade9-maths.question: One mobile phone costs Rs 9,000. What is the cost of 4 such phones?
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the cost of one by four.

grade9-maths.question: A worker earns Rs 18,000 per month. How much does she earn in a year?
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the monthly salary by 12.

grade9-maths.question: How many sides does a hexagon have?
grade9-maths.hint: Hex- means six in Greek.
grade9-maths.explanation: A hexagon has 6 sides. Pentagon = 5, heptagon = 7, octagon = 8.

grade9-maths.question: What is the sum of the interior angles of a triangle?
grade9-maths.hint: All three angles add up to a straight line.
grade9-maths.explanation: The interior angles of any triangle always sum to 180°.

grade9-maths.question: Two angles on a straight line are 65° and x°. What is x?
grade9-maths.hint: Angles on a straight line sum to 180°.

grade9-maths.question: A pie chart has four sectors. One sector represents 90°. What fraction of the whole does this sector represent?
grade9-maths.hint: A full circle = 360°. What fraction is 90° of 360°?
grade9-maths.explanation: 90° ÷ 360° = 1/4. A 90° sector is one quarter of the circle.

grade9-maths.question: In a right-angled triangle, the opposite side is 3 cm and the hypotenuse is 5 cm. What is sin θ? Give your answer as a decimal.
grade9-maths.hint: sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse.

grade9-maths.question: In a right-angled triangle, the adjacent side is 8 cm and the hypotenuse is 10 cm. What is angle θ in degrees? (Use cos⁻¹)
grade9-maths.hint: cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse = 8/10 = 0.8.

grade9-maths.question: What is the gradient of a line that passes through (0, 2) and (4, 10)?
grade9-maths.hint: Gradient = rise ÷ run = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁).

grade9-maths.question: A line has gradient 3 and passes through (0, −1). What is its equation?
grade9-maths.hint: Use y = mx + c, where m is the gradient and c is the y-intercept.
grade9-maths.explanation: m = 3, c = −1 → equation is y = 3x − 1.

grade9-maths.question: What is the magnitude of the vector (3, 4)?
grade9-maths.hint: Use Pythagoras: magnitude = √(x² + y²).

grade9-maths.question: Point A is at (1, 2). It is translated by vector (3, −4). What are the coordinates of the image A'?
grade9-maths.hint: Add the vector components to the coordinates.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify 4y + 9y.
grade9-maths.hint: Add the coefficients of the like terms.

grade9-maths.question: Factorise 2x + 4.
grade9-maths.hint: Take out the common factor of 2.

grade9-maths.question: Expand (x + 3)(x + 5).
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply each term in the first bracket by each term in the second.

grade9-maths.question: Factorise x² + 5x + 6.
grade9-maths.hint: Find two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to 5.

grade9-maths.question: Solve the simultaneous equations: x + y = 10 and x − y = 4. What is x?
grade9-maths.hint: Add the two equations to eliminate y.
grade9-maths.explanation: Adding: 2x = 14 → x = 7. Then y = 10 − 7 = 3.

grade9-maths.question: What is the order of a matrix with 3 rows and 2 columns?
grade9-maths.hint: Order = rows × columns (rows first).
grade9-maths.explanation: A matrix with 3 rows and 2 columns has order 3 × 2.

grade9-maths.question: What is the identity matrix for 2 × 2 matrices?
grade9-maths.hint: When multiplied by any 2×2 matrix, it leaves it unchanged.
grade9-maths.explanation: The 2×2 identity matrix is I = [[1,0],[0,1]]. It has 1s on the diagonal and 0s elsewhere.

grade9-maths.question: Find the circumference of a circle with diameter 10 cm. Use π = 3.14. Give your answer in cm.
grade9-maths.hint: Circumference = π × diameter.

grade9-maths.question: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. Use π = 3.14. Give your answer in cm³.
grade9-maths.hint: Volume of cylinder = π × r² × h.

grade9-maths.question: The ages of 5 students are: 13, 14, 14, 15, 14. What is the mode?
grade9-maths.hint: The mode is the value that appears most often.
grade9-maths.explanation: 14 appears three times; 13 and 15 appear once each. The mode is 14.

grade9-maths.question: Find the mean of the numbers: 8, 12, 15, 9, 6.
grade9-maths.hint: Mean = sum ÷ count.

grade9-maths.question: A bag contains 3 red balls and 7 blue balls. What is the probability of picking a red ball at random?
grade9-maths.hint: P(event) = favourable outcomes ÷ total outcomes.

grade9-maths.question: Solve: 2x + 3 > 11.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract 3 from both sides, then divide by 2.

grade9-maths.question: Make r the subject of the formula: A = πr².
grade9-maths.hint: Divide both sides by π, then take the square root.
grade9-maths.explanation: A = πr² → r² = A/π → r = √(A/π).

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What is the value of 3 in 21.03?
parts.hint: Count the places after the decimal point.
parts.explanation: The first place after the point is tenths and the second is hundredths, so the 3 is worth 3 hundredths. "3 tenths" reads the wrong column; the other two read to the left of the point.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which of the following is an irrational number?
parts.hint: An irrational number cannot be written as one whole number over another.
parts.explanation: √5 = 2.2360… never terminates or repeats, so it is irrational. √25 = 5 is a whole number; 22/7 is a fraction; 0.25 = 1/4. All three of those are rational. 22/7 is a common trap because it is used as an approximation for π, but it is itself rational.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Convert 3 kg 80 g into grams.
parts.hint: One kilogram is 1 000 grams - and 80 g is not 800 g.
parts.explanation: 3 kg = 3 000 g, so the total is 3 080 g. 380 g and 3 800 g both mis-place the 80; 3.080 g leaves the answer in kilograms.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: 130 minutes is the same as
parts.hint: There are 60 minutes in an hour, not 100.
parts.explanation: 130 = 120 + 10, and 120 minutes is 2 hours, so it is 2 h 10 min. "1 h 30 min" treats 130 as 1 hour and 30 minutes, which is the mistake of reading the digits rather than dividing by 60.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A crate holds 24 bottles. How many bottles are there in 7 crates?
parts.hint: Multiply the number in one crate by the number of crates.
parts.explanation: 24 × 7 = 168. 31 adds instead of multiplying; 17 subtracts; 148 is the slip of multiplying 20 × 7 and adding 4 × 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which of these is the largest?
parts.hint: Compare the first digit after the decimal point.
parts.explanation: 0.7 has 7 tenths; the others have 7 hundredths, thousandths and ten-thousandths. More digits after the point does not mean a bigger number.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Simplify x8 ÷ x2.
parts.hint: Division subtracts the indices.
parts.explanation: x<sup>8</sup> ÷ x<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>8−2</sup> = x<sup>6</sup>. x<sup>4</sup> comes from dividing the indices, x<sup>10</sup> from adding them and x<sup>16</sup> from multiplying them.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which of the following equals <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>16</sub>?
parts.hint: A negative index means one over the positive power.
parts.explanation: 2<sup>−4</sup> = 1/2<sup>4</sup> = 1/16. 2<sup>4</sup> = 16 and −2<sup>4</sup> = −16 both confuse a negative index with a negative answer, and 2<sup>−2</sup> = 1/4 halves the index instead of using it.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What is the next term of the sequence 1, 4, 9, 16, …?
parts.hint: Look at what kind of numbers these are.
parts.explanation: They are the square numbers 1², 2², 3², 4², so the next is 5² = 25. 20 and 24 come from assuming a constant difference; 32 from doubling.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The nth term of a sequence is 2n + 5. What is its 4th term?
parts.hint: Substitute n = 4.
parts.explanation: 2(4) + 5 = 13. 11 substitutes n = 3; 28 multiplies (2 + 5) by 4; 14 forgets to add the 5 and doubles 7.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In Pascal’s triangle, which row comes after 1, 2, 1?
parts.hint: Each entry is the sum of the two above it.
parts.explanation: Adding neighbouring pairs of 1, 2, 1 gives 3 and 3, with a 1 at each end: 1, 3, 3, 1. Every row of Pascal’s triangle begins and ends with 1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A worker earns Rs 500 a day. How much does he earn in 5 days?
parts.hint: Multiply the daily rate by the number of days.
parts.explanation: 500 × 5 = Rs 2 500. Rs 505 adds instead of multiplying; Rs 100 divides; Rs 1 000 doubles rather than multiplying by five.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The simple interest on Rs 10 000 at 5% per annum for 1 year is
parts.hint: 5% means 5 out of every 100.
parts.explanation: 5% of 10 000 = 500. Rs 50 divides by 100 twice; Rs 5 000 takes 50%; Rs 10 500 gives the total amount rather than the interest, which is what the question asked for.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: An item costs Rs 2 000 cash. On hire purchase it costs a deposit of Rs 500 plus 6 payments of Rs 280. How much MORE does hire purchase cost?
parts.hint: Work out the hire purchase total first, then compare.
parts.explanation: Hire purchase costs 500 + 6 × 280 = Rs 2 180, which is Rs 180 more than Rs 2 000. Rs 2 180 is the total rather than the difference; Rs 780 adds the deposit to one payment; Rs 1 680 is the instalments alone.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, cos θ is equal to
parts.hint: CAH in SOH CAH TOA.
parts.explanation: Cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse. Opposite over hypotenuse is sine, opposite over adjacent is tangent, and hypotenuse over adjacent is the cosine upside down.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A right-angled triangle has sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm. What is the sine of the angle opposite the 6 cm side?
parts.hint: The hypotenuse is the longest side.
parts.explanation: sin = opposite ÷ hypotenuse = 6/10 = 0.6. 0.8 is the cosine (8/10); 0.75 is the tangent (6/8); 1.25 turns the fraction upside down.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: If tan θ = 1, then θ equals
parts.hint: Tangent 1 means the two shorter sides are equal.
parts.explanation: tan 45° = 1, because opposite and adjacent are equal. tan 30° ≈ 0.58, tan 60° ≈ 1.73, and tan 90° is undefined.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which one of the following lines has a gradient of zero?
parts.hint: A gradient of zero means the line does not rise at all.
parts.explanation: y = 4 is horizontal, so its gradient is 0. x = 4 is vertical and has NO gradient (not zero - the division is by zero). y = 4x has gradient 4 and y = x + 4 has gradient 1.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What is the y-intercept of the line y = 2x − 3?
parts.hint: In y = mx + c, the intercept is c - with its sign.
parts.explanation: c = −3, so the line crosses the y-axis at −3. Answering 3 drops the minus sign; 2 gives the gradient instead of the intercept.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A line passes through (0, 0) and (2, 6). Its gradient is
parts.hint: Rise over run.
parts.explanation: Gradient = 6/2 = 3. Answering 2 or 6 uses only one coordinate; 1/3 puts the run over the rise.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The magnitude of the vector with components 3 and 4 is
parts.hint: Use Pythagoras, not addition.
parts.explanation: √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5. 7 adds the components; 12 multiplies them; 25 forgets to take the square root.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A translation moves a point 3 units left and 2 units up. As a column vector this is
parts.hint: Left is negative across; up is positive.
parts.explanation: Left is a negative x component and up is a positive y component, giving (−3, 2). (3, 2) misses the direction; (3, −2) reverses both; (2, −3) also swaps the order.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The surface area of a cube of side 3 cm is
parts.hint: A cube has six identical square faces.
parts.explanation: One face is 3 × 3 = 9 cm², and 6 × 9 = 54 cm². 27 cm² is the VOLUME; 9 cm² is one face only; 36 cm² uses four faces instead of six.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The net of a cylinder is made of
parts.hint: Think about unrolling a tin can.
parts.explanation: The two ends are circles and the curved surface unrolls into a rectangle.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm, using π = <sup>22</sup>⁄<sub>7</sub>, is
parts.hint: Circumference is 2πr, not πr².
parts.explanation: 2 × (22/7) × 7 = 44 cm. 154 cm is the AREA; 22 cm forgets the 2; 88 cm uses the diameter as the radius.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The volume of a cuboid measuring 4 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm is
parts.hint: Multiply all three dimensions.
parts.explanation: 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 cm³. 9 cm³ adds them; 52 cm³ is the surface area; 12 cm³ uses only two of the three dimensions.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The volume of a cylinder is given by
parts.hint: Volume is the area of the circular end times the height.
parts.explanation: The end has area πr², and multiplying by the height h gives πr²h. 2πrh is the curved surface area, πr² is the area of one end, and 2πr is the circumference.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A cube has a volume of 64 cm³. The length of one edge is
parts.hint: Which number cubed gives 64?
parts.explanation: 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, so each edge is 4 cm. 8 cm takes the square root instead of the cube root; 16 cm and 32 cm divide by 4 and by 2.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many millilitres are there in 2 litres?
parts.hint: One litre is 1 000 millilitres.
parts.explanation: 2 × 1 000 = 2 000 mL. 200 mL uses centilitres by mistake; the others move the decimal point the wrong way.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A container of volume 1 000 cm³ has a capacity of
parts.hint: 1 cm³ of space holds 1 mL.
parts.explanation: 1 000 cm³ holds 1 000 mL, which is 1 litre. The others shift the conversion by powers of ten.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Which of these is the same as 0.75 L?
parts.hint: One litre is 100 centilitres.
parts.explanation: 0.75 × 100 = 75 cL. 750 would be the millilitres; the others move the point wrongly.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Expand 3(x − 4).
parts.hint: The 3 multiplies BOTH terms in the bracket.
parts.explanation: 3 × x = 3x and 3 × (−4) = −12. "3x − 4" forgets to multiply the second term, which is the most common slip here.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Factorise x2 − 49.
parts.hint: Two squares with a minus between them.
parts.explanation: This is the difference of two squares: x² − 7² = (x + 7)(x − 7). (x − 7)² expands to x² − 14x + 49, which is not the same.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Expand (x + 2)2.
parts.hint: A square is the bracket multiplied by itself - there is a middle term.
parts.explanation: (x + 2)(x + 2) = x² + 2x + 2x + 4 = x² + 4x + 4. "x² + 4" squares each term separately and loses the middle term entirely, which is the classic error.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A matrix has 3 rows and 5 columns. Its order is
parts.hint: Rows are always given first.
parts.explanation: The order is written rows × columns, so 3 × 5. Writing 5 × 3 reverses them; 15 gives the number of elements; 8 adds the two.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Two matrices can be ADDED only when they have

options: the same number of rows only
the same number of columns only

parts.hint: Addition works element by element, position for position.
parts.explanation: Every element must have a partner in the same position, so both the rows and the columns must match - that is, the same order.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many elements are there in a matrix of order 4 × 3?
parts.hint: Multiply the rows by the columns.
parts.explanation: 4 × 3 = 12 elements. 7 adds the two numbers instead of multiplying them.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: One solution of (x − 3)(x + 5) = 0 is
parts.hint: Set each bracket equal to zero in turn.
parts.explanation: x − 3 = 0 gives x = 3, and x + 5 = 0 gives x = −5. The signs inside the brackets reverse when you solve: answering x = −3 or x = 5 is reading the brackets without solving them.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many solutions does the equation x2 − 4 = 0 have?
parts.hint: Factorise it and set each bracket to zero.
parts.explanation: x² − 4 = (x + 2)(x − 2) = 0, giving x = 2 and x = −2 - two solutions. Answering 1 forgets the negative root, which is the usual mistake.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Making x the subject of y = x − 7 gives
parts.hint: Do the opposite operation to both sides.
parts.explanation: Adding 7 to both sides gives x = y + 7. "x = y − 7" repeats the original rather than undoing it; "7 − y" subtracts the wrong way round.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: If A = lw, then w equals
parts.hint: The l is multiplying, so divide by it.
parts.explanation: Dividing both sides by l gives w = A/l. Subtracting l undoes the wrong operation; l/A turns the division upside down.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the value of P when l = 5 and w = 2, given P = 2(l + w).
parts.hint: Work out the bracket before multiplying.
parts.explanation: l + w = 7, so P = 2 × 7 = 14. Answering 12 multiplies only the l by 2 before adding; 10 multiplies l and w together; 7 forgets the 2 altogether.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Solving −2x > 6 gives
parts.hint: Dividing by a negative reverses the inequality sign.
parts.explanation: Dividing both sides by −2 turns > into <, giving x < −3. "x > −3" is the answer of someone who divided correctly but forgot to turn the sign round - the single most common mistake in this topic.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: On a number line, a hollow circle at 5 means
parts.hint: Filled means included; hollow means excluded.
parts.explanation: A hollow circle marks a strict inequality (< or >), so 5 itself is not part of the solution. A filled circle would mean ≤ or ≥.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: If x + y = 10 and x − y = 2, then x equals
parts.hint: Adding the two equations removes y.
parts.explanation: Adding gives 2x = 12, so x = 6 (and y = 4). Answering 4 gives y rather than x; 5 halves the 10 without using the second equation.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: To eliminate y from 3x + y = 9 and 2x − y = 1, you should
parts.hint: Look at the signs in front of the y terms.
parts.explanation: The y terms are +y and −y, so adding cancels them. Subtracting would give 2y, which keeps y in the equation.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The mode of 4, 5, 5, 6, 9 is
parts.hint: The mode is the most frequent value.
parts.explanation: 5 appears twice and everything else once, so the mode is 5. 6 is the median, 5.8 is the mean, and 9 is the largest value.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The median of 3, 8, 5, 1, 9 is
parts.hint: Put the numbers in order first.
parts.explanation: In order: 1, 3, 5, 8, 9. The middle value is 5. Answering 5 without ordering would be luck; answering 8 takes the middle of the list as written; 5.2 is the mean.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The range of 7, 2, 9, 4 is
parts.hint: Largest take away smallest.
parts.explanation: 9 − 2 = 7. Answering 5 subtracts the wrong pair; 11 adds them; 5.5 is the mean.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The probability of an event that is certain is
parts.hint: Probability runs from 0 to 1.
parts.explanation: A certain event has probability 1. 0 is impossible; 100 confuses a probability with a percentage; 1/2 is an even chance.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A fair die is thrown once. The probability of getting a number greater than 4 is
parts.hint: Which faces are greater than 4?
parts.explanation: The faces 5 and 6 are greater than 4, so the probability is 2/6 = 1/3. 1/6 counts only one face; 1/2 counts 4, 5 and 6, but 4 is not greater than 4.

grade9-maths.source: NCF Grades 7-9 §3.9; NCE 2025 Q11 / 2024 Q12 consolidated MCQ-block pattern.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The probability that it rains is 1⁄4. The probability that it does not rain is
parts.hint: The two probabilities must add up to 1.
parts.explanation: 1 − 1/4 = 3/4. A probability is never negative, so −1/4 cannot be right.

grade9-maths.question: Work out 632 + 157.
grade9-maths.hint: Add the units, then the tens, then the hundreds.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate 5/13 + 3/13.
grade9-maths.hint: The denominators are already the same.
grade9-maths.explanation: With a common denominator you add only the numerators: 5 + 3 = 8, so the answer is 8/13. The denominator does not change.

grade9-maths.question: Convert 5 kg 620 g into grams.
grade9-maths.hint: One kilogram is 1000 grams.

grade9-maths.question: Find the cube root of 64.
grade9-maths.hint: Which number multiplied by itself three times gives 64?
grade9-maths.explanation: 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, so the cube root of 64 is 4. (8 is the square root of 64.)

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (m3)5.
grade9-maths.hint: A power raised to a power: what do you do with the two indices?
grade9-maths.explanation: (ma)b = ma×b, so (m3)5 = m3×5 = m15. Adding the indices (giving m8) is the rule for multiplying powers, not raising one.

grade9-maths.question: Which of these is a square number: 15, 20, 36, 59, 80?
grade9-maths.hint: A square number is a whole number multiplied by itself.
grade9-maths.explanation: 6 × 6 = 36, so 36 is a square number. None of the others is a whole number times itself.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify 7x2 + 2x2.
grade9-maths.hint: These are like terms - the letter and its power match.
grade9-maths.explanation: Add the coefficients and keep the term: 7 + 2 = 9, so the answer is 9x2. The index does not change when you add like terms.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate 3 + 5 − 9.
grade9-maths.hint: Work from left to right.

grade9-maths.question: Express 0.31 as a percentage.
grade9-maths.hint: To turn a decimal into a percentage, multiply by 100.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate 3.02 × 4.
grade9-maths.hint: Work out 302 × 4, then put the decimal point back.
grade9-maths.explanation: 302 × 4 = 1208. There are two decimal places in 3.02, so the answer is 12.08.

grade9-maths.question: Factorise 3x − 6.
grade9-maths.hint: What is the highest factor common to 3x and 6?
grade9-maths.explanation: 3 divides both terms: 3x ÷ 3 = x and 6 ÷ 3 = 2, so 3x − 6 = 3(x − 2). Expanding it back gives 3x − 6, which is the check.

grade9-maths.question: How many right angles are there in a rectangle?
grade9-maths.hint: Count the corners of a rectangle.
grade9-maths.explanation: Every one of a rectangle’s four corners is a right angle, so there are 4.

grade9-maths.question: What is the value of the 2 in 502.6?
grade9-maths.hint: Read the columns: hundreds, tens, units, then the decimal point.
grade9-maths.explanation: In 502.6 the digits are 5 hundreds, 0 tens, 2 units and 6 tenths, so the 2 stands for 2 units.

grade9-maths.question: A clock shows 6.00 p.m. The clock is 20 minutes ahead of the correct time. What is the correct time?
grade9-maths.hint: If the clock is ahead, the real time is earlier than the clock shows.
grade9-maths.explanation: A clock that runs ahead shows a later time than it really is, so subtract: 6.00 p.m. − 20 min = 5.40 p.m.

grade9-maths.question: 130 minutes is the same as:
grade9-maths.hint: How many whole hours fit into 130 minutes?
grade9-maths.explanation: 120 minutes make 2 hours, and 130 − 120 = 10 minutes left over, so 130 minutes = 2 h 10 min.

grade9-maths.question: What is the highest common factor (H.C.F.) of 3x and 6x2?
grade9-maths.hint: Take the largest number that divides both, and the lowest power of x in both.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3 is the highest common factor of 3 and 6, and x is the lowest power of x present in both terms, so the H.C.F. is 3x. 6x would not divide 3x.

grade9-maths.question: Which of the following is a prime number: 21, 23, 25, 27?
grade9-maths.hint: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
grade9-maths.explanation: 21 = 3 × 7, 25 = 5 × 5 and 27 = 3 × 9, but 23 has no factors other than 1 and 23.

grade9-maths.question: Arrange in ascending order: 5.62, 5.06, 5.23, 5.65, 5.006
grade9-maths.hint: Compare the tenths first, then the hundredths, then the thousandths.
grade9-maths.explanation: Every number starts with 5, so compare the decimals: 0.006 < 0.06 < 0.23 < 0.62 < 0.65. Ascending means smallest first, so 5.006, 5.06, 5.23, 5.62, 5.65.

grade9-maths.question: After a discount of 10%, a laptop costs Rs 27 900. Find the original price of the laptop.
grade9-maths.hint: Rs 27 900 is not 100% of the price - it is what is left after 10% was taken off.
grade9-maths.explanation: After a 10% discount the customer pays 90% of the original price. So 90% = Rs 27 900, giving 1% = Rs 310 and 100% = Rs 31 000. Adding 10% to Rs 27 900 gives Rs 30 690, which is the common mistake - a percentage is always taken of the original amount.

grade9-maths.question: Solve x − 5 = -7.
grade9-maths.hint: Add 5 to both sides.
grade9-maths.explanation: x − 5 = -7, so x = -7 + 5 = -2. Check: -2 − 5 = -7.

grade9-maths.question: Solve x2 − 5x + 6 = 0.
grade9-maths.hint: Find two numbers that multiply to +6 and add to -5.
grade9-maths.explanation: -2 and -3 multiply to 6 and add to -5, so x2 − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0, giving x = 2 or x = 3. Note the signs: the factors are negative, so the roots are positive.

grade9-maths.question: Solve the inequality 2x + 3 ≤ 11.
grade9-maths.hint: Take 3 from both sides, then halve.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2x + 3 ≤ 11 gives 2x ≤ 8, so x ≤ 4. The inequality sign only flips when you multiply or divide by a negative number, which does not happen here.

grade9-maths.question: Given that the square root of 5 is 2.236 and the square root of 50 is 7.071, find the square root of 5000.
grade9-maths.hint: 5000 = 100 × 50, and the square root of 100 is exact.
grade9-maths.explanation: 5000 = 100 × 50, so the square root of 5000 = 10 × the square root of 50 = 10 × 7.071 = 70.71. Splitting off a perfect square is the whole technique here.

grade9-maths.question: Where must brackets be inserted to make this true? 50 ÷ 2 × 5 − 4 = 1
grade9-maths.hint: You need the division to happen last among the first three numbers - so make 2 × 5 into a single divisor.
grade9-maths.explanation: 50 ÷ (2 × 5) − 4 = 50 ÷ 10 − 4 = 5 − 4 = 1. Without brackets the left-to-right rule gives 50 ÷ 2 × 5 − 4 = 121.

grade9-maths.question: Kylie runs 1¾ km, then cycles 3500 m, then swims 2250 cm. What is the total distance she covers, in metres?
grade9-maths.hint: Convert all three distances to metres before adding anything.
grade9-maths.explanation: 1¾ km = 1750 m, the cycle is already 3500 m, and 2250 cm = 22.5 m. Total = 1750 + 3500 + 22.5 = 5272.5 m. The trap is adding before converting.

grade9-maths.question: A man invests Rs 300 000 for 5 years at 2% per annum simple interest. Calculate the interest he earns.
grade9-maths.hint: Simple interest = principal × rate × time.
grade9-maths.explanation: Interest = 300 000 × 2/100 × 5 = 6000 × 5 = Rs 30 000. Rs 6000 is one year only; Rs 330 000 is the total amount, not the interest.

grade9-maths.question: Make a the subject of the formula 3b = (2a − 1) / (4 − 5a).
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply both sides by (4 − 5a) first, then gather every term containing a on one side.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3b(4 − 5a) = 2a − 1, so 12b − 15ab = 2a − 1. Move the a terms together: 12b + 1 = 2a + 15ab = a(2 + 15b). Therefore a = (12b + 1) / (15b + 2).

grade9-maths.question: If A = 6m + 7n/100, find A when m = 2 and n = 3.
grade9-maths.hint: Work out 6m and 7n/100 separately, then add.

grade9-maths.question: A spinner numbered 2 to 9 is spun once. Find the probability that it shows an even number.
grade9-maths.hint: List 2 to 9 and count how many are even out of how many in total.
grade9-maths.explanation: The numbers 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 give 8 equally likely outcomes, of which 2, 4, 6 and 8 are even. So the probability is 4/8 = 1/2.

grade9-maths.question: A spinner numbered 2 to 9 is spun once. Find the probability that it does not show 7.
grade9-maths.hint: How many of the eight outcomes are not a 7?
grade9-maths.explanation: There are 8 outcomes and exactly one of them is a 7, so 7 are not. The probability is 7/8 - which is also 1 − 1/8.

grade9-maths.question: Given A = (2, -3; 0, 5) and B = (-1, 4; 6, 2), written row by row, find 2A − B.
grade9-maths.hint: Double every entry of A first, then subtract the matching entry of B.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2A = (4, -6; 0, 10). Subtracting B entry by entry: 4 − (-1) = 5, -6 − 4 = -10, 0 − 6 = -6, 10 − 2 = 8, giving (5, -10; -6, 8). The first entry is the one people get wrong - subtracting a negative adds.

grade9-maths.question: A line passes through S(-2, 3) and T(4, 5). Find the equation of the line through (-3, 1) that is parallel to ST.
grade9-maths.hint: Parallel lines share a gradient. Find the gradient of ST first.
grade9-maths.explanation: Gradient of ST = (5 − 3)/(4 − -2) = 2/6 = 1/3. A parallel line through (-3, 1) is y − 1 = (1/3)(x + 3), so y = x/3 + 1 + 1 = y = x/3 + 2.

grade9-maths.question: 12 men take 15 days to build a wall. How many more men are needed to build the same wall in 10 days? (All men work at the same rate.)
grade9-maths.hint: Work out the total man-days for the job first. Fewer days needs more men.
grade9-maths.explanation: The job is 12 × 15 = 180 man-days. In 10 days that needs 180 ÷ 10 = 18 men. The question asks how many more, so 18 − 12 = 6. Answering 18 is the trap.

grade9-maths.question: Matchstick figures use 3, 5, 7, ... matchsticks for Figures 1, 2, 3. How many matchsticks does Figure 5 use?
grade9-maths.hint: The pattern goes up by the same amount each time.
grade9-maths.explanation: The sequence 3, 5, 7 rises by 2 each figure, so Figure 4 uses 9 and Figure 5 uses 11.

grade9-maths.question: The matchstick pattern uses 3, 5, 7, ... matchsticks. Which figure uses 21 matchsticks?
grade9-maths.hint: The figure numbered n uses 2n + 1 matchsticks. Work backwards.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2n + 1 = 21 gives 2n = 20, so n = 10. Checking: Figure 10 uses 2(10) + 1 = 21 matchsticks.

grade9-maths.question: The matchstick pattern uses 3, 5, 7, ... matchsticks for Figures 1, 2, 3. Write the number used by Figure n.
grade9-maths.hint: It goes up by 2 each time, so the rule starts with 2n. What must be added to make Figure 1 give 3?
grade9-maths.explanation: A rise of 2 per figure means the rule contains 2n. For n = 1, 2n = 2 but the figure uses 3, so add 1: the rule is 2n + 1. Check n = 3: 2(3) + 1 = 7.

grade9-maths.question: 36 students named a favourite dessert: ice cream 13, fruits 10, rasmalai 7, donuts 6. On a pie chart, what angle represents fruits?
grade9-maths.hint: The whole pie is 360° and represents all 36 students.
grade9-maths.explanation: Fruits is 10 of 36 students, so the angle is 10/36 × 360° = 100°. (A useful shortcut here: 36 students in 360° means every student is worth exactly 10°.)

grade9-maths.question: ABCD is a trapezium with AB parallel to DC, AD = BC, AB = 8 cm and DC = 20 cm. X lies on DC so that AX is perpendicular to DC, and angle ADX = 40°. Calculate AX. [tan 40° = 0.84]
grade9-maths.hint: Because the trapezium is symmetrical, work out DX first: the two overhangs are equal.
grade9-maths.explanation: AD = BC makes the trapezium symmetrical, so the overhang at each end is (20 − 8) ÷ 2 = 6 cm, giving DX = 6 cm. In right-angled triangle ADX, tan 40° = AX / DX, so AX = 6 × 0.84 = 5.04 cm.

grade9-maths.question: A sum of money is shared between Shania and Mirella in the ratio 2 : 5. Mirella receives Rs 360 more than Shania. Calculate the total amount shared.
grade9-maths.hint: The difference between the two shares is 3 parts. What is one part worth?
grade9-maths.explanation: The shares differ by 5 − 2 = 3 parts, and that difference is Rs 360, so one part is Rs 120. The total is 2 + 5 = 7 parts = 7 × 120 = Rs 840.

grade9-maths.question: A pair of shoes and 3 T-shirts cost Rs 3750. Two pairs of the same shoes and 5 T-shirts cost Rs 6750. Find the cost of 1 pair of shoes and 4 T-shirts.
grade9-maths.hint: Call the shoes s and a T-shirt t, write both sentences as equations, and eliminate s.
grade9-maths.explanation: s + 3t = 3750 and 2s + 5t = 6750. Doubling the first gives 2s + 6t = 7500; subtracting the second leaves t = 750. Then s = 3750 − 3(750) = 1500. So 1 pair of shoes and 4 T-shirts cost 1500 + 4(750) = Rs 4500.

grade9-maths.question: A circle has radius 13 cm. Find its circumference, leaving your answer in terms of π.
grade9-maths.hint: Circumference = 2 × π × radius.
grade9-maths.explanation: C = 2πr = 2 × π × 13 = 26π cm. (169π would be the area, πr2.)

grade9-maths.question: A and B are points on a circle with centre O. What type of triangle is triangle AOB?
grade9-maths.hint: What can you say about OA and OB?
grade9-maths.explanation: OA and OB are both radii of the same circle, so they are equal in length. A triangle with two equal sides is isosceles.

grade9-maths.question: In a circle of centre O, chord AB = 10 cm and the radius OA = 13 cm. X is the point on AB where OX is perpendicular to AB. Calculate OX.
grade9-maths.hint: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so AX is half of AB. Then use Pythagoras.
grade9-maths.explanation: OX bisects AB, so AX = 5 cm. In right-angled triangle OXA, OX2 = OA2 − AX2 = 169 − 25 = 144, so OX = 12 cm.

grade9-maths.question: In a circle of centre O, chord AB = 10 cm and the perpendicular distance OX from O to AB is 12 cm. Calculate the area of triangle OAB.
grade9-maths.hint: Take AB as the base. Which length is the perpendicular height?
grade9-maths.explanation: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 12 = 60 cm2. OX is the height because it is perpendicular to AB.

grade9-maths.question: Each side of a square is increased by 8 cm. The area of the new square is 6 times its perimeter. Find the length of one side of the original square.
grade9-maths.hint: Let the new side be one letter. Write its area and its perimeter, then set area = 6 × perimeter.
grade9-maths.explanation: Let the new side be y, so y = original + 8. Area = y2 and perimeter = 4y, so y2 = 6(4y) = 24y. Dividing by y gives y = 24, so the new side is 24 cm and the original side is 24 − 8 = 16 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The number line shows a set of values. Write down the smallest value marked.
parts.hint: Read the left-hand end of the heavy bar.
parts.explanation: The heavy bar starts at −2 with a filled circle, so −2 is included.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write down the largest whole number in the marked set.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A regular hexagon has sides of length (x + 3) cm. Write an expression for its perimeter, expanded.
parts.hint: Six equal sides.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the perimeter when x = 4.
parts.hint: Substitute x = 4.

grade9-maths.question: The formula for converting degrees Celsius to Fahrenheit is F = 1.8C + 32. Find F when C = 25.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply first, then add.

grade9-maths.question: Make C the subject and hence find C when F = 68.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract 32, then divide by 1.8.
grade9-maths.explanation: C = (F − 32) ÷ 1.8 = 36 ÷ 1.8 = 20.

grade9-maths.question: The cost of hiring a van is C = 900 + 45d, where d is the number of days. Find the cost for 6 days. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Substitute d = 6.

grade9-maths.question: Make d the subject of the formula and hence find how many days a hire costing Rs 1 800 lasted. (answer in days)
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract 900, then divide by 45.
grade9-maths.explanation: d = (C − 900) ÷ 45 = 900 ÷ 45 = 20 days.

grade9-maths.question: Given v = u + at, find v when u = 5, a = 3 and t = 4.
grade9-maths.hint: Work out at first, then add u.

grade9-maths.question: Make a the subject and hence find a when v = 30, u = 6 and t = 8.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract u from both sides, then divide by t.
grade9-maths.explanation: a = (v − u) ÷ t = 24 ÷ 8 = 3.

grade9-maths.question: Given p with components (5, −3), write down the x-component of 3p.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply each component by 3.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the y-component of 3p.
grade9-maths.hint: The sign is kept.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3 × (−3) = −9.

grade9-maths.question: A translation moves (3, 7) to (8, 4). Write down the x-component of the translation vector.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract the starting x from the finishing x.
grade9-maths.explanation: 8 − 3 = 5.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the y-component.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract the starting y from the finishing y.
grade9-maths.explanation: 4 − 7 = −3.

grade9-maths.question: In a right-angled triangle the hypotenuse is 13 cm and one shorter side is 5 cm. Use Pythagoras to find the third side. (answer in cm)
grade9-maths.hint: The square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.
grade9-maths.explanation: 13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144, and √144 = 12 cm.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the area of that triangle. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: Half of the two shorter sides multiplied together.
grade9-maths.explanation: ½ × 5 × 12 = 30 cm².

grade9-maths.question: A cube has edges of 9 cm. Calculate its volume. (answer in cm³)
grade9-maths.hint: Edge cubed.
grade9-maths.explanation: 9 × 9 × 9 = 729 cm³.

grade9-maths.question: A second cube has twice the edge length. How many times bigger is its volume? (answer in times)
grade9-maths.hint: Doubling every edge multiplies the volume by 2 x 2 x 2.
grade9-maths.explanation: 18³ = 5 832, and 5 832 ÷ 729 = 8 times.

grade9-maths.question: In a survey of 50 people, 28 read the news online, 22 read a printed paper and 9 do both. How many read online only? (answer in people)
grade9-maths.hint: Take the overlap off the online total.
grade9-maths.explanation: 28 − 9 = 19 people.

grade9-maths.question: How many read a printed paper only? (answer in people)
grade9-maths.hint: Take the overlap off the printed total.
grade9-maths.explanation: 22 − 9 = 13 people.

grade9-maths.question: How many read neither? (answer in people)
grade9-maths.hint: Add the three regions, then subtract from 50.

grade9-maths.question: Three angles meet at a point on a straight line. Two of them are 47° and 68°. Find the third. (answer in °)
grade9-maths.hint: Angles on a straight line add to 180°.
grade9-maths.explanation: 180 − 47 − 68 = 65°.

grade9-maths.question: A fourth angle is added so that all four now meet at a point and fill a complete turn. Find that fourth angle. (answer in °)
grade9-maths.hint: A complete turn is 360°, and the first three already make 180°.

grade9-maths.question: A television costs Rs 18 000. In a sale the price falls by 15%. Calculate the sale price. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Find 15% and take it off, or find 85% directly.
grade9-maths.explanation: 15% of 18 000 = 2 700, so the sale price is 18 000 − 2 700 = Rs 15 300.

grade9-maths.question: After the sale the price is raised by 15% of the SALE price. Show that it does not return to Rs 18 000 by calculating the new price. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: 15% of 15 300 is smaller than 15% of 18 000.

grade9-maths.question: A recipe uses flour and sugar in the ratio 5 : 2. A baker uses 750 g of flour. How much sugar is needed? (answer in g)
grade9-maths.hint: Find what one part weighs first.
grade9-maths.explanation: 750 ÷ 5 = 150 g per part, so 2 × 150 = 300 g.

grade9-maths.question: What is the total weight of flour and sugar? (answer in g)
grade9-maths.hint: Add the two amounts.

grade9-maths.question: Expand and simplify (x + 4)(x + 7).
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply all four pairs, then collect the x terms.

grade9-maths.question: Hence find the value of the expression when x = 10.
grade9-maths.hint: Substitute into your expanded form, or into the brackets.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify a5 × a3.
grade9-maths.hint: When you multiply powers of the same letter, add the indices.
grade9-maths.explanation: a<sup>5</sup> × a<sup>3</sup> = a<sup>5+3</sup> = a<sup>8</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (m3)5.
grade9-maths.hint: A power raised to a power: multiply the indices.
grade9-maths.explanation: (m<sup>3</sup>)<sup>5</sup> = m<sup>3×5</sup> = m<sup>15</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify x7 ÷ x2.
grade9-maths.hint: When you divide powers of the same letter, subtract the indices.
grade9-maths.explanation: x<sup>7</sup> ÷ x<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>7−2</sup> = x<sup>5</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (a5)4.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the two indices.
grade9-maths.explanation: (a<sup>5</sup>)<sup>4</sup> = a<sup>5×4</sup> = a<sup>20</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify 2y3 × 5y4.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the numbers, then add the indices of y.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2 × 5 = 10 and y<sup>3</sup> × y<sup>4</sup> = y<sup>7</sup>, so the answer is 10y<sup>7</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify 12p6 ÷ 4p2.
grade9-maths.hint: Divide the numbers, then subtract the indices of p.
grade9-maths.explanation: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 and p<sup>6</sup> ÷ p<sup>2</sup> = p<sup>4</sup>, so the answer is 3p<sup>4</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate 5<sup>0</sup>.
grade9-maths.hint: Any number except 0, raised to the power zero, has the same value.
grade9-maths.explanation: By the zero index law, a<sup>0</sup> = 1 for any a ≠ 0. So 5<sup>0</sup> = 1.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (3x2)3.
grade9-maths.hint: The index outside the bracket applies to the 3 as well as to x².
grade9-maths.explanation: (3x<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3</sup> = 3<sup>3</sup> × x<sup>2×3</sup> = 27x<sup>6</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (2a3b)4.
grade9-maths.hint: Raise every factor inside the bracket to the power 4.
grade9-maths.explanation: (2a<sup>3</sup>b)<sup>4</sup> = 2<sup>4</sup> × a<sup>3×4</sup> × b<sup>4</sup> = 16a<sup>12</sup>b<sup>4</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify a6 × a0 ÷ a2.
grade9-maths.hint: Work left to right, remembering that a<sup>0</sup> = 1.
grade9-maths.explanation: a<sup>6</sup> × a<sup>0</sup> = a<sup>6+0</sup> = a<sup>6</sup>, then a<sup>6</sup> ÷ a<sup>2</sup> = a<sup>4</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate (7<sup>3</sup> × 7<sup>2</sup>) ÷ 7<sup>4</sup>.
grade9-maths.hint: Combine the indices before working out any value.
grade9-maths.explanation: 7<sup>3</sup> × 7<sup>2</sup> = 7<sup>5</sup>, and 7<sup>5</sup> ÷ 7<sup>4</sup> = 7<sup>1</sup> = 7.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (x4y3)2 × x.
grade9-maths.hint: Expand the bracket first, then multiply by x.
grade9-maths.explanation: (x<sup>4</sup>y<sup>3</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>8</sup>y<sup>6</sup>. Multiplying by x gives x<sup>8+1</sup>y<sup>6</sup> = x<sup>9</sup>y<sup>6</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate 3<sup>4</sup> ÷ 3<sup>2</sup>.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract the indices first.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3<sup>4</sup> ÷ 3<sup>2</sup> = 3<sup>2</sup> = 9.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (4m2n3)2 ÷ (2mn).
grade9-maths.hint: Square the bracket first, then divide each part.
grade9-maths.explanation: (4m<sup>2</sup>n<sup>3</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = 16m<sup>4</sup>n<sup>6</sup>. Dividing by 2mn: 16 ÷ 2 = 8, m<sup>4−1</sup> = m<sup>3</sup>, n<sup>6−1</sup> = n<sup>5</sup>, giving 8m<sup>3</sup>n<sup>5</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Given that 2x = 32, find the value of x.
grade9-maths.hint: Write 32 as a power of 2.
grade9-maths.explanation: 32 = 2<sup>5</sup>, so 2<sup>x</sup> = 2<sup>5</sup> and x = 5.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify 6a4 × 3a2 ÷ 9a3.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply first, then divide.
grade9-maths.explanation: 6a<sup>4</sup> × 3a<sup>2</sup> = 18a<sup>6</sup>. Then 18a<sup>6</sup> ÷ 9a<sup>3</sup> = 2a<sup>3</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate (5<sup>2</sup>)<sup>0</sup> + 4<sup>0</sup>.
grade9-maths.hint: Anything to the power zero is 1 - including a bracket.
grade9-maths.explanation: (5<sup>2</sup>)<sup>0</sup> = 1 and 4<sup>0</sup> = 1, so the sum is 1 + 1 = 2.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (p3q2)3.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply each index inside the bracket by 3.
grade9-maths.explanation: (p<sup>3</sup>q<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3</sup> = p<sup>3×3</sup>q<sup>2×3</sup> = p<sup>9</sup>q<sup>6</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify 20x8 ÷ 5x8.
grade9-maths.hint: What happens to x when the indices are equal?
grade9-maths.explanation: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 and x<sup>8</sup> ÷ x<sup>8</sup> = x<sup>0</sup> = 1, so the answer is simply 4.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate (2<sup>3</sup> × 2<sup>4</sup>) ÷ 2<sup>5</sup>.
grade9-maths.hint: Add the indices on the top, then subtract the one below.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2<sup>3</sup> × 2<sup>4</sup> = 2<sup>7</sup>, and 2<sup>7</sup> ÷ 2<sup>5</sup> = 2<sup>2</sup> = 4.

grade9-maths.question: Write 3<sup>−2</sup> as a fraction.
grade9-maths.hint: A negative index means one over the positive power.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3<sup>−2</sup> = 1 ÷ 3<sup>2</sup> = 1/9.

grade9-maths.question: Write <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>5<sup>3</sup></sub> as a power of 5.
grade9-maths.hint: Moving a power from the bottom of a fraction to the top changes the sign of the index.
grade9-maths.explanation: 1 ÷ 5<sup>3</sup> = 5<sup>−3</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate 2<sup>−4</sup>.
grade9-maths.hint: Work out the positive power first, then take one over it.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2<sup>4</sup> = 16, so 2<sup>−4</sup> = 1/16.

grade9-maths.question: Write 4<sup>−1</sup> as a fraction.
grade9-maths.hint: An index of −1 gives the reciprocal.
grade9-maths.explanation: 4<sup>−1</sup> = 1/4.

grade9-maths.question: Write x−3 as a fraction.
grade9-maths.hint: The letter moves to the bottom of the fraction.
grade9-maths.explanation: x<sup>−3</sup> = 1/x<sup>3</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate 10<sup>−3</sup>.
grade9-maths.hint: Ten cubed is a thousand.

grade9-maths.question: Write <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>2<sup>5</sup></sub> using a negative index.
grade9-maths.hint: Change the sign of the index as the power moves up.
grade9-maths.explanation: 1 ÷ 2<sup>5</sup> = 2<sup>−5</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate (1⁄3)−2.
grade9-maths.hint: A negative index turns the fraction upside down.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify a5 × a−3.
grade9-maths.hint: Add the indices, keeping the minus sign.
grade9-maths.explanation: a<sup>5</sup> × a<sup>−3</sup> = a<sup>5+(−3)</sup> = a<sup>2</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify m−2 ÷ m−5.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtracting a negative index is the same as adding.
grade9-maths.explanation: m<sup>−2</sup> ÷ m<sup>−5</sup> = m<sup>−2−(−5)</sup> = m<sup>3</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate 5<sup>−2</sup> × 5<sup>4</sup>.
grade9-maths.hint: Add the indices before working out the value.
grade9-maths.explanation: 5<sup>−2</sup> × 5<sup>4</sup> = 5<sup>2</sup> = 25.

grade9-maths.question: Write 2x−3 as a fraction.
grade9-maths.hint: Only the x carries the negative index, not the 2.
grade9-maths.explanation: The index −3 belongs to x alone, so 2x<sup>−3</sup> = 2/x<sup>3</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate 2<sup>−1</sup> + 2<sup>−2</sup>.
grade9-maths.hint: Write each term as a fraction, then add them.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2<sup>−1</sup> = 1/2 and 2<sup>−2</sup> = 1/4. Adding: 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (x−2)−3.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the two indices, watching both signs.
grade9-maths.explanation: (x<sup>−2</sup>)<sup>−3</sup> = x<sup>(−2)×(−3)</sup> = x<sup>6</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate 6<sup>0</sup> − 3<sup>−1</sup>.
grade9-maths.hint: Deal with the zero index first.
grade9-maths.explanation: 6<sup>0</sup> = 1 and 3<sup>−1</sup> = 1/3, so 1 − 1/3 = 2/3.

grade9-maths.question: Solve 2x = 1⁄8.
grade9-maths.hint: Write 1/8 as a power of 2.
grade9-maths.explanation: 1/8 = 1/2<sup>3</sup> = 2<sup>−3</sup>, so 2<sup>x</sup> = 2<sup>−3</sup> and x = −3.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (3a−2)2, giving your answer as a fraction.
grade9-maths.hint: Square the 3 and double the index of a.
grade9-maths.explanation: (3a<sup>−2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = 3<sup>2</sup>a<sup>−4</sup> = 9a<sup>−4</sup> = 9/a<sup>4</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate 4<sup>−2</sup> ÷ 4<sup>−3</sup>.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract the indices first.
grade9-maths.explanation: 4<sup>−2</sup> ÷ 4<sup>−3</sup> = 4<sup>−2−(−3)</sup> = 4<sup>1</sup> = 4.

grade9-maths.question: Write 0.001 as a power of 10.
grade9-maths.hint: How many places is the 1 after the decimal point?

grade9-maths.question: Solve 5x+1 = 1⁄25.
grade9-maths.hint: Make both sides a power of 5, then compare the indices.
grade9-maths.explanation: 1/25 = 1/5<sup>2</sup> = 5<sup>−2</sup>. So 5<sup>x+1</sup> = 5<sup>−2</sup>, giving x + 1 = −2 and x = −3.

grade9-maths.question: Write 2 × 2 × 2 in index form.
grade9-maths.hint: Count how many times 2 appears as a factor.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2 appears 3 times, so 2 × 2 × 2 = 2<sup>3</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Write 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 in index form.
grade9-maths.hint: Count how many times 5 is multiplied together.
grade9-maths.explanation: 5 appears 4 times, so 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 = 5<sup>4</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Write a × a × a × a × a in index form.
grade9-maths.hint: Count how many times a appears.
grade9-maths.explanation: a appears 5 times, so a × a × a × a × a = a<sup>5</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (a4)5.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the two indices.
grade9-maths.explanation: (a<sup>4</sup>)<sup>5</sup> = a<sup>4×5</sup> = a<sup>20</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of m, if 27 = 3m.
grade9-maths.hint: Write 27 as a power of 3.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3 × 3 × 3 = 27, so 27 = 3<sup>3</sup> and m = 3.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of n, if 64 = 2n.
grade9-maths.hint: Keep multiplying 2 by itself until you reach 64.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of k, if 125 = 5k.
grade9-maths.hint: Write 125 as a power of 5.
grade9-maths.explanation: 5 × 5 × 5 = 125, so 125 = 5<sup>3</sup> and k = 3.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify 3p2 × 4p3.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the numbers, then add the indices of p.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3 × 4 = 12 and p<sup>2</sup> × p<sup>3</sup> = p<sup>5</sup>, so the answer is 12p<sup>5</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify 15x5 ÷ 5x2.
grade9-maths.hint: Divide the numbers, then subtract the indices of x.
grade9-maths.explanation: 15 ÷ 5 = 3 and x<sup>5</sup> ÷ x<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>3</sup>, so the answer is 3x<sup>3</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (5a2)3.
grade9-maths.hint: The index outside the bracket applies to the 5 as well as to a<sup>2</sup>.
grade9-maths.explanation: (5a<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3</sup> = 5<sup>3</sup> × a<sup>2×3</sup> = 125a<sup>6</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Write 6<sup>−2</sup> as a fraction.
grade9-maths.hint: Work out 6 squared first, then put 1 over the result.
grade9-maths.explanation: 6<sup>2</sup> = 36, so 6<sup>−2</sup> = 1/36.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate 3<sup>−3</sup>.
grade9-maths.hint: Work out 3 cubed first, then take its reciprocal.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3<sup>3</sup> = 27, so 3<sup>−3</sup> = 1/27.

grade9-maths.question: Write <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>8</sub> as a power of 2.
grade9-maths.hint: Write 8 as a power of 2, then use the negative index rule.
grade9-maths.explanation: 8 = 2<sup>3</sup>, so <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>8</sub> = 1 ÷ 2<sup>3</sup> = 2<sup>−3</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify a2 × a−6.
grade9-maths.hint: Add the indices, keeping the minus sign.
grade9-maths.explanation: a<sup>2</sup> × a<sup>−6</sup> = a<sup>2+(−6)</sup> = a<sup>−4</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate (1⁄4)−2.
grade9-maths.hint: A negative index turns the fraction upside down first.

grade9-maths.question: Which of the following is equal to a3 × a4?
grade9-maths.hint: Multiplying powers of the same letter adds the indices.
grade9-maths.explanation: a<sup>3</sup> × a<sup>4</sup> = a<sup>3+4</sup> = a<sup>7</sup>. a<sup>12</sup> comes from multiplying the indices instead of adding; a<sup>1</sup> from subtracting; 2a<sup>7</sup> from also adding the invisible coefficients.

grade9-maths.question: What is the value of 4<sup>0</sup>?
grade9-maths.hint: Think about what happens to 4<sup>2</sup> ÷ 4<sup>2</sup>.
grade9-maths.explanation: 4<sup>0</sup> = 1. The common mistake is to answer 0 because the index is 0, but 4<sup>2</sup> ÷ 4<sup>2</sup> = 4<sup>0</sup> and any number divided by itself is 1.

grade9-maths.question: Which of the following is equal to 2<sup>−3</sup>?
grade9-maths.hint: A negative index does not make the answer negative.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2<sup>−3</sup> = 1 ÷ 2<sup>3</sup> = 1/8. −8 comes from reading the minus as a sign on the answer; −6 and 1/6 come from multiplying 2 by 3 instead of cubing it.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (x2)5.
grade9-maths.hint: A power of a power multiplies the indices.
grade9-maths.explanation: (x<sup>2</sup>)<sup>5</sup> = x<sup>2×5</sup> = x<sup>10</sup>. x<sup>7</sup> comes from adding the indices, x<sup>25</sup> from squaring the 5, and x<sup>3</sup> from subtracting.

grade9-maths.question: What is the value of n if 3n = 27?
grade9-maths.hint: Write 27 as a power of 3.
grade9-maths.explanation: 27 = 3<sup>3</sup>, so n = 3. n = 9 comes from thinking 3 × 9 = 27; n = 6 from adding six 3s; n = 27 from confusing the base and the result.

grade9-maths.question: Which of the following is equal to 5<sup>−2</sup>?
grade9-maths.hint: A negative index never makes the result negative.
grade9-maths.explanation: 5<sup>−2</sup> = 1 ÷ 5<sup>2</sup> = 1/25. −25 comes from treating the − as negating the whole result; 1/10 and −10 come from multiplying 5 × 2 instead of squaring.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of m, if 81 = 3m.
grade9-maths.hint: Keep multiplying 3 by itself until you reach 81.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81, so 81 = 3<sup>4</sup> and m = 4.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of m, if 27 = 3m.
grade9-maths.hint: Keep multiplying 3 by itself until you reach 27.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3 × 3 × 3 = 27, so 27 = 3<sup>3</sup> and m = 3.

grade9-maths.question: Solve 4x+1 = 64.
grade9-maths.hint: Write 64 as a power of 4, then compare the indices.
grade9-maths.explanation: 64 = 4<sup>3</sup>, so 4<sup>x+1</sup> = 4<sup>3</sup>. Comparing indices: x + 1 = 3, giving x = 2.

grade9-maths.question: Solve 23x ÷ 2x = 16.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract the indices on the left first.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2<sup>3x</sup> ÷ 2<sup>x</sup> = 2<sup>3x−x</sup> = 2<sup>2x</sup>. Since 16 = 2<sup>4</sup>, we get 2x = 4, so x = 2.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (2x3)4 ÷ (4x2)2.
grade9-maths.hint: Expand each bracket first, then divide.
grade9-maths.explanation: (2x<sup>3</sup>)<sup>4</sup> = 16x<sup>12</sup> and (4x<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = 16x<sup>4</sup>. Dividing: 16 ÷ 16 = 1 and x<sup>12−4</sup> = x<sup>8</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (3a2b)2 × 2a.
grade9-maths.hint: Square the bracket first, then multiply by 2a.
grade9-maths.explanation: (3a<sup>2</sup>b)<sup>2</sup> = 9a<sup>4</sup>b<sup>2</sup>. Multiplying by 2a: 9 × 2 = 18 and a<sup>4</sup> × a = a<sup>5</sup>, giving 18a<sup>5</sup>b<sup>2</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Solve 5x−2 = 53x−8.
grade9-maths.hint: The bases are the same, so set the indices equal.
grade9-maths.explanation: x − 2 = 3x − 8. Rearranging: 6 = 2x, giving x = 3.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify 8a6 ÷ (2a2)2.
grade9-maths.hint: Expand (2a<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> first.
grade9-maths.explanation: (2a<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = 4a<sup>4</sup>. Then 8a<sup>6</sup> ÷ 4a<sup>4</sup> = 2a<sup>2</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Evaluate 3<sup>−1</sup> + 3<sup>−2</sup>.
grade9-maths.hint: Write each term as a fraction, then find a common denominator.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3<sup>−1</sup> = 1/3 and 3<sup>−2</sup> = 1/9. Adding: 3/9 + 1/9 = 4/9.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify (2x−1y2)3, giving your answer as a fraction.
grade9-maths.hint: Cube every factor inside the bracket.
grade9-maths.explanation: (2x<sup>−1</sup>y<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3</sup> = 2<sup>3</sup>x<sup>−3</sup>y<sup>6</sup> = 8x<sup>−3</sup>y<sup>6</sup> = 8y<sup>6</sup>/x<sup>3</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Solve 32−x = 1⁄9.
grade9-maths.hint: Write 1/9 as a power of 3, then compare the indices.
grade9-maths.explanation: 1/9 = 3<sup>−2</sup>, so 3<sup>2−x</sup> = 3<sup>−2</sup>. Comparing: 2 − x = −2, giving x = 4.

grade9-maths.question: Simplify x−2 × x5 ÷ x−1.
grade9-maths.hint: Add then subtract the indices in order, remembering that dividing by x<sup>−1</sup> adds 1 to the index.
grade9-maths.explanation: x<sup>−2+5</sup> = x<sup>3</sup>, then x<sup>3</sup> ÷ x<sup>−1</sup> = x<sup>3−(−1)</sup> = x<sup>4</sup>.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of p if 2p = 1⁄16.
grade9-maths.hint: Write 1/16 as a power of 2.
grade9-maths.explanation: 1/16 = 1/2<sup>4</sup> = 2<sup>−4</sup>, so p = −4.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of m if 16 = 2m.
grade9-maths.hint: Write 16 as a product of 2s.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of k if 8 = 2k.
grade9-maths.hint: 2 × 2 × 2 = ?
grade9-maths.explanation: 2<sup>3</sup> = 8, so k = 3.

grade9-maths.question: A line passes through the points A (0, 1) and B (3, 7). Find the gradient of the line AB.
grade9-maths.hint: Gradient is the change in y divided by the change in x.
grade9-maths.explanation: Gradient = (7 − 1) ÷ (3 − 0) = 6 ÷ 3 = 2.

grade9-maths.question: Find the gradient of the line joining (1, 2) and (4, 11).
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract the y values, then the x values, in the same order.
grade9-maths.explanation: Gradient = (11 − 2) ÷ (4 − 1) = 9 ÷ 3 = 3.

grade9-maths.question: What is the gradient of a horizontal line?
grade9-maths.hint: A horizontal line does not rise at all.
grade9-maths.explanation: The change in y is 0 for any change in x, so the gradient is 0 ÷ (change in x) = 0.

grade9-maths.question: Find the gradient of the line joining (2, 5) and (6, 13).
grade9-maths.hint: Rise over run.
grade9-maths.explanation: Gradient = (13 − 5) ÷ (6 − 2) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

grade9-maths.question: Find the gradient of the line joining (−1, 4) and (3, −4).
grade9-maths.hint: Take care with the negative coordinates; subtract in the same order on both.
grade9-maths.explanation: Gradient = (−4 − 4) ÷ (3 − (−1)) = −8 ÷ 4 = −2.

grade9-maths.question: Find the gradient of the line joining (0, 0) and (5, 10).
grade9-maths.hint: Rise over run from the origin.
grade9-maths.explanation: Gradient = (10 − 0) ÷ (5 − 0) = 10 ÷ 5 = 2.

grade9-maths.question: Find the gradient of the line joining (−2, −3) and (2, 5).
grade9-maths.hint: Subtracting a negative adds.
grade9-maths.explanation: Gradient = (5 − (−3)) ÷ (2 − (−2)) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the gradient of the line y = 3x + 5.
grade9-maths.hint: In y = mx + c, the gradient is m.
grade9-maths.explanation: Comparing with y = mx + c, the number multiplying x is 3, so the gradient is 3.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the gradient of the line y = −2x + 7.
grade9-maths.hint: The gradient is the number in front of x, including its sign.
grade9-maths.explanation: Comparing with y = mx + c gives m = −2.

grade9-maths.question: Find the gradient of the line 2y = 6x − 4.
grade9-maths.hint: Rearrange into the form y = mx + c first.
grade9-maths.explanation: Dividing every term by 2 gives y = 3x − 2, so the gradient is 3.

grade9-maths.question: A line is parallel to y = 4x − 1. Write down its gradient.
grade9-maths.hint: Parallel lines have equal gradients.
grade9-maths.explanation: Parallel lines have the same gradient, so this line also has gradient 4.

grade9-maths.question: Find the gradient of the line joining (3, 3) and (7, 3).
grade9-maths.hint: What do you notice about the two y values?
grade9-maths.explanation: The y values are equal, so the change in y is 0 and the gradient is 0 ÷ 4 = 0.

grade9-maths.question: Find the gradient of the line 3x + y = 9.
grade9-maths.hint: Make y the subject.
grade9-maths.explanation: Rearranging gives y = −3x + 9, so the gradient is −3.

grade9-maths.question: Find the gradient of the line joining (−4, 2) and (0, 0).
grade9-maths.hint: Your answer will be a fraction.
grade9-maths.explanation: Gradient = (0 − 2) ÷ (0 − (−4)) = −2 ÷ 4 = −1/2.

grade9-maths.question: Find the gradient of the line 4y = 8x + 12.
grade9-maths.hint: Divide through by 4.
grade9-maths.explanation: Dividing every term by 4 gives y = 2x + 3, so the gradient is 2.

grade9-maths.question: Find the gradient of the line joining (5, −2) and (1, 6).
grade9-maths.hint: Keep the points in the same order top and bottom.
grade9-maths.explanation: Gradient = (6 − (−2)) ÷ (1 − 5) = 8 ÷ (−4) = −2.

grade9-maths.question: The lines y = 5x + 2 and y = kx − 3 are parallel. Find the value of k.
grade9-maths.hint: Parallel means the gradients match.
grade9-maths.explanation: Parallel lines have equal gradients, so k = 5.

grade9-maths.question: Find the gradient of the line joining (0, 7) and (2, 1).
grade9-maths.hint: The line falls, so expect a negative answer.
grade9-maths.explanation: Gradient = (1 − 7) ÷ (2 − 0) = −6 ÷ 2 = −3.

grade9-maths.question: Find the gradient of the line joining (−3, 1) and (1, 9).
grade9-maths.hint: Rise over run.
grade9-maths.explanation: Gradient = (9 − 1) ÷ (1 − (−3)) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

grade9-maths.question: Find the gradient of the line joining (6, 4) and (2, 4).
grade9-maths.hint: Look at the y values before calculating.
grade9-maths.explanation: Both points have y = 4, so the line is horizontal and its gradient is 0.

grade9-maths.question: A line has gradient 2 and cuts the y-axis at 1. Write down its equation.
grade9-maths.hint: Substitute m and c into y = mx + c.
grade9-maths.explanation: With m = 2 and c = 1, the equation is y = 2x + 1.

grade9-maths.question: A line passes through A (0, 1) and B (3, 7). State the equation of the line AB.
grade9-maths.hint: Find the gradient first; the point (0, 1) gives c straight away.
grade9-maths.explanation: Gradient = (7 − 1) ÷ 3 = 2. The line crosses the y-axis at (0, 1), so c = 1 and the equation is y = 2x + 1.

grade9-maths.question: Write the equation of the line with gradient 3 passing through (0, −4).
grade9-maths.hint: The point (0, c) gives the intercept directly.
grade9-maths.explanation: With m = 3 and c = −4, the equation is y = 3x − 4.

grade9-maths.question: Write the equation of the line with gradient −1 passing through (0, 5).
grade9-maths.hint: A gradient of −1 is written as −x, not −1x.
grade9-maths.explanation: With m = −1 and c = 5, the equation is y = −x + 5.

grade9-maths.question: Write the equation of the line with gradient 4 passing through the origin.
grade9-maths.hint: Through the origin means c = 0.
grade9-maths.explanation: The origin is (0, 0), so c = 0 and the equation is y = 4x.

grade9-maths.question: A line has gradient 2 and passes through (1, 5). Find its equation.
grade9-maths.hint: Substitute the point into y = 2x + c to find c.
grade9-maths.explanation: Substituting: 5 = 2(1) + c, so c = 3 and the equation is y = 2x + 3.

grade9-maths.question: A line has gradient 3 and passes through (2, 7). Find its equation.
grade9-maths.hint: Put the point into y = 3x + c.
grade9-maths.explanation: Substituting: 7 = 3(2) + c = 6 + c, so c = 1 and the equation is y = 3x + 1.

grade9-maths.question: A line has gradient −2 and passes through (−1, 4). Find its equation.
grade9-maths.hint: Take care with the two negatives when you substitute.
grade9-maths.explanation: Substituting: 4 = −2(−1) + c = 2 + c, so c = 2 and the equation is y = −2x + 2.

grade9-maths.question: Find the equation of the line passing through (2, 3) and (4, 7).
grade9-maths.hint: Find the gradient first, then use one of the points to find c.
grade9-maths.explanation: Gradient = (7 − 3) ÷ (4 − 2) = 2. Substituting (2, 3): 3 = 2(2) + c, so c = −1 and the equation is y = 2x − 1.

grade9-maths.question: Find the equation of the line passing through (0, 6) and (3, 0).
grade9-maths.hint: One of the points is on the y-axis.
grade9-maths.explanation: Gradient = (0 − 6) ÷ (3 − 0) = −2. The point (0, 6) gives c = 6, so the equation is y = −2x + 6.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the equation of the x-axis.
grade9-maths.hint: Every point on it has the same y value.
grade9-maths.explanation: Every point on the x-axis has y = 0, so its equation is y = 0.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the equation of the y-axis.
grade9-maths.hint: Every point on it has the same x value.
grade9-maths.explanation: Every point on the y-axis has x = 0, so its equation is x = 0.

grade9-maths.question: Write the equation of the horizontal line through (2, 5).
grade9-maths.hint: A horizontal line keeps y constant.
grade9-maths.explanation: A horizontal line through (2, 5) has y = 5 everywhere, so its equation is y = 5.

grade9-maths.question: Write the equation of the vertical line through (3, −1).
grade9-maths.hint: A vertical line keeps x constant.
grade9-maths.explanation: A vertical line through (3, −1) has x = 3 everywhere, so its equation is x = 3.

grade9-maths.question: A line is parallel to y = 2x + 7 and passes through (0, −3). Find its equation.
grade9-maths.hint: Parallel lines share a gradient; the point gives c.
grade9-maths.explanation: Parallel means m = 2. The point (0, −3) gives c = −3, so the equation is y = 2x − 3.

grade9-maths.question: A line is parallel to y = −3x + 1 and passes through (1, 2). Find its equation.
grade9-maths.hint: Use m = −3 and substitute the point.
grade9-maths.explanation: Parallel gives m = −3. Substituting (1, 2): 2 = −3(1) + c, so c = 5 and the equation is y = −3x + 5.

grade9-maths.question: Find the equation of the line passing through (−2, 1) and (2, 9).
grade9-maths.hint: Watch the signs in the gradient calculation.
grade9-maths.explanation: Gradient = (9 − 1) ÷ (2 − (−2)) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2. Substituting (2, 9): 9 = 4 + c, so c = 5 and the equation is y = 2x + 5.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the y-intercept of the line y = 5x − 8.
grade9-maths.hint: In y = mx + c, the intercept is c.
grade9-maths.explanation: Comparing with y = mx + c gives c = −8.
