How many faces does the net of a cuboid have?
grade9-maths.hint: Count the rectangles in the net.
grade9-maths.explanation: A cuboid has six faces, so its net is made of six rectangles.

grade9-maths.question: Find the surface area of a cube of side 4 cm. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: All six faces of a cube are identical squares.
grade9-maths.explanation: One face has area 4 × 4 = 16 cm², and there are six faces, so the total is 6 × 16 = 96 cm².

grade9-maths.question: Find the circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm. (Use π = 22⁄7) (answer in cm)
grade9-maths.hint: Circumference is 2πr.
grade9-maths.explanation: C = 2 × (22/7) × 7 = 2 × 22 = 44 cm.

grade9-maths.question: Find the area of a circle of radius 7 cm. (Use π = 22⁄7) (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: Area is πr².
grade9-maths.explanation: A = (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 22 × 7 = 154 cm².

grade9-maths.question: Find the circumference of a circle of radius 14 cm. (Use π = 22⁄7) (answer in cm)
grade9-maths.hint: Cancel the 7 in π against the radius.
grade9-maths.explanation: C = 2 × (22/7) × 14 = 2 × 22 × 2 = 88 cm.

grade9-maths.question: Find the area of a circle of radius 10 cm, leaving your answer in terms of π. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: Do not replace π with a number.
grade9-maths.explanation: A = π × 10² = 100π cm².

grade9-maths.question: The net shown folds into a closed cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. Calculate its total surface area. (Use π = 22⁄7) (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: The net is two circles plus a rectangle whose width is the circumference.
grade9-maths.explanation: Curved surface = 2πrh = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 10 = 440 cm². Each circle = πr² = (22/7) × 49 = 154 cm², and there are two, giving 308 cm². Total = 440 + 308 = 748 cm².

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the curved surface area of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 5 cm. (Use π = 22⁄7) (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: The curved surface unrolls into a rectangle of width 2πr.
grade9-maths.explanation: Curved surface = 2πrh = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 5 = 220 cm².

grade9-maths.question: A cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm is open at one end. Calculate its total surface area. (Use π = 22⁄7) (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: An open cylinder has only ONE circular face.
grade9-maths.explanation: Curved surface = 2πrh = 440 cm². One circle = πr² = 154 cm². Open at one end means only one circle, so the total is 440 + 154 = 594 cm².

grade9-maths.question: A cylindrical pipe is hollow, that is open at both ends. It has radius 7 cm and length 20 cm. Calculate its curved surface area. (Use π = 22⁄7) (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: A hollow pipe has no circular faces at all.
grade9-maths.explanation: A pipe open at both ends is only the curved surface: 2πrh = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 20 = 880 cm².

grade9-maths.question: A triangular prism has two triangular faces of area 6 cm² each and three rectangular faces of areas 20, 15 and 12 cm². Find its total surface area. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: Add every face, remembering there are two triangles.

grade9-maths.question: A cuboid measures 10 cm by 6 cm by 5 cm. Calculate its total surface area. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: Three pairs of faces.
grade9-maths.explanation: The faces are 10×6 = 60, 10×5 = 50 and 6×5 = 30 cm², each twice: 2(60 + 50 + 30) = 2 × 140 = 280 cm².

grade9-maths.question: A cube has a total surface area of 150 cm². Find the length of one edge. (answer in cm)
grade9-maths.hint: Divide by 6 to get one face, then take the square root.
grade9-maths.explanation: One face has area 150 ÷ 6 = 25 cm², so each edge is √25 = 5 cm.

grade9-maths.question: Find the area of a circle of diameter 14 cm. (Use π = 22⁄7) (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: The formula needs the radius, not the diameter.
grade9-maths.explanation: The radius is 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm, so A = (22/7) × 49 = 154 cm².

grade9-maths.question: The curved surface area of a cylinder is 176 cm² and its radius is 7 cm. Find its height. (Use π = 22⁄7) (answer in cm)
grade9-maths.hint: Write down 2πrh and work backwards.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2πrh = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × h = 44h. Setting 44h = 176 gives h = 4 cm.

grade9-maths.question: A cuboid measures 8 cm by 5 cm by 2 cm. Calculate its total surface area. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: Three pairs of faces.
grade9-maths.explanation: The faces are 8×5 = 40, 8×2 = 16 and 5×2 = 10 cm², each twice: 2(40 + 16 + 10) = 2 × 66 = 132 cm².

grade9-maths.question: A closed cylinder has radius 3.5 cm and height 6 cm. Calculate its total surface area. (Use π = 22⁄7) (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: Curved surface plus two circles.
grade9-maths.explanation: Curved surface = 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 6 = 132 cm². Each circle = (22/7) × 3.5 × 3.5 = 38.5 cm², so two give 77 cm². Total = 132 + 77 = 209 cm².

grade9-maths.question: A net of a cylinder is made of two circles and one rectangle. What does the length of that rectangle represent?
grade9-maths.hint: Imagine unrolling the curved surface.
grade9-maths.explanation: When the curved surface is unrolled it becomes a rectangle whose length wrapped once around the circle, so that length is the circumference.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the next term of the sequence 3, 7, 11, 15, …
grade9-maths.hint: What is added each time?
grade9-maths.explanation: Each term is 4 more than the one before, so the next term is 15 + 4 = 19.

grade9-maths.question: Find the nth term of the sequence 3, 7, 11, 15, …
grade9-maths.hint: The common difference tells you what multiplies n.
grade9-maths.explanation: The terms go up by 4, so the nth term starts 4n. When n = 1, 4n = 4 but the term is 3, so the rule is 4n − 1.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the next term of the sequence 2, 5, 8, 11, …
grade9-maths.hint: Look at the difference between terms.
grade9-maths.explanation: Each term is 3 more than the one before, so the next is 11 + 3 = 14.

grade9-maths.question: Find the nth term of the sequence 2, 5, 8, 11, …
grade9-maths.hint: Difference 3, so start with 3n.
grade9-maths.explanation: The difference is 3, so the rule starts 3n. At n = 1 that gives 3 but the term is 2, so the nth term is 3n − 1.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the next term of the sequence 20, 17, 14, 11, …
grade9-maths.hint: The sequence is going down.
grade9-maths.explanation: Each term is 3 less than the one before, so the next is 11 − 3 = 8.

grade9-maths.question: Find the nth term of the sequence 20, 17, 14, 11, …
grade9-maths.hint: A falling sequence has a negative multiple of n.
grade9-maths.explanation: The difference is −3, so the rule starts −3n. At n = 1 that gives −3 but the term is 20, so the nth term is 23 − 3n.

grade9-maths.question:
Write down the missing term in the following sequence of ordered pairs.
(2, 3), (3, 5), (4, 7), ( …… , …… )
grade9-maths.hint: Look at how the first number changes, then how the second changes.
grade9-maths.explanation: The first numbers go up by 1, so the next is 5. The second numbers go up by 2, so the next is 9. The missing pair is (5, 9). The rule is y = 2x − 1.

grade9-maths.question: For the sequence of ordered pairs (1, 4), (2, 7), (3, 10), find the relation between x and y.
grade9-maths.hint: How much does y rise for each step in x?
grade9-maths.explanation: y increases by 3 each time x increases by 1, so y = 3x + c. Using (1, 4): 4 = 3 + c, so c = 1 and y = 3x + 1.

grade9-maths.question: For the sequence of ordered pairs (1, −2), (2, −4), (3, −6), find the relation between x and y.
grade9-maths.hint: The y values are negative and doubling.
grade9-maths.explanation: Each y is −2 times its x, so y = −2x.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the next row of Pascal’s triangle after 1, 3, 3, 1.
grade9-maths.hint: Each number is the sum of the two above it, and every row starts and ends with 1.
grade9-maths.explanation: Adding neighbouring pairs of 1, 3, 3, 1 gives 4, 6, 4, and a 1 at each end: 1, 4, 6, 4, 1.

grade9-maths.question: In Pascal’s triangle, write down the missing number in the row 1, 5, ……, 10, 5, 1.
grade9-maths.hint: The row is symmetrical.
grade9-maths.explanation: Each row of Pascal’s triangle reads the same forwards and backwards, so the number matching the 10 near the end is also 10.

grade9-maths.question: The dot patterns below grow in a regular way. How many dots are in Figure 4? (answer in dots)
grade9-maths.hint: Count the dots in each figure and look for the rule.
grade9-maths.explanation: The figures hold 1, 4 and 9 dots - the square numbers - so Figure 4 has 4 × 4 = 16 dots.

grade9-maths.question: For the dot patterns below, find the number of dots in Figure n.
grade9-maths.hint: The counts are 1, 4, 9 …
grade9-maths.explanation: The numbers of dots are 1, 4 and 9, which are 1², 2² and 3², so Figure n has n² dots.

grade9-maths.question: The dot patterns below grow in a regular way. How many dots are in Figure 5? (answer in dots)
grade9-maths.hint: Each figure adds two dots to the one before.
grade9-maths.explanation: The figures hold 1, 3 and 5 dots, going up by 2 each time, so Figure 4 has 7 and Figure 5 has 9 dots.

grade9-maths.question: The dot patterns below form an L shape. Find an expression for the number of dots in Figure n.
grade9-maths.hint: The counts go up by 2 each time.
grade9-maths.explanation: The counts are 1, 3, 5, rising by 2, so the rule starts 2n. At n = 1 that gives 2 but the figure has 1 dot, so the number of dots in Figure n is 2n − 1.

grade9-maths.question: The dot patterns below grow in a regular way. How many dots are in Figure 6? (answer in dots)
grade9-maths.hint: Each figure is three rows deep.
grade9-maths.explanation: Each figure has 3 rows, with 1, 2 and 3 dots per row, giving 3, 6 and 9 dots. Figure 6 has 6 dots per row, so 3 × 6 = 18 dots.

grade9-maths.question: Each of the dot patterns below has three rows. Find an expression for the number of dots in Figure n.
grade9-maths.hint: Three rows, each getting one longer.
grade9-maths.explanation: Each figure has 3 rows of n dots, so Figure n has 3n dots.

grade9-maths.question: Find the 10th term of the sequence with nth term 5n + 2.
grade9-maths.hint: Substitute n = 10.

grade9-maths.question: The nth term of a sequence is 2n2. Write down its first three terms.
grade9-maths.hint: Substitute n = 1, 2 and 3 in turn.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2(1)² = 2, 2(2)² = 8 and 2(3)² = 18, so the first three terms are 2, 8 and 18.

grade9-maths.question: The sequence 4, 9, 16, 25 continues in the same way. Find its nth term.
grade9-maths.hint: These are square numbers, but not starting from 1.
grade9-maths.explanation: The terms are 2², 3², 4², 5². The number being squared is one more than n, so the nth term is (n + 1)².

grade9-maths.question: Solve the inequality x + 3 > 7, giving your answer in set-builder notation.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract 3 from both sides, as you would with an equation.
grade9-maths.explanation: x + 3 > 7 gives x > 4, written { x : x > 4 }.

grade9-maths.question: Solve the inequality 2x < 10, giving your answer in set-builder notation.
grade9-maths.hint: Divide both sides by 2, which is positive, so the sign does not change.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2x < 10 gives x < 5, written { x : x < 5 }.

grade9-maths.question: Solve the inequality 5x + 4 ≤ 24.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract 4, then divide by 5.
grade9-maths.explanation: 5x + 4 ≤ 24 gives 5x ≤ 20, so x ≤ 4, written { x : x ≤ 4 }.

grade9-maths.question: Solve the inequality −5x > 20.
grade9-maths.hint: Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality sign.
grade9-maths.explanation: Dividing both sides by −5 reverses the sign: x < −4, written { x : x < −4 }. Answering x > −4 is the common mistake - the sign must turn round.

grade9-maths.question: Solve the inequality −3x ≤ 12.
grade9-maths.hint: Dividing by −3 turns ≤ into ≥.
grade9-maths.explanation: Dividing by −3 reverses the sign: x ≥ −4, written { x : x ≥ −4 }.

grade9-maths.question: Solve the inequality 4x − 5 ≥ 7.
grade9-maths.hint: Add 5, then divide by 4.
grade9-maths.explanation: 4x − 5 ≥ 7 gives 4x ≥ 12, so x ≥ 3, written { x : x ≥ 3 }.

grade9-maths.question: Solve the inequality x − 6 < −2.
grade9-maths.hint: Add 6 to both sides.
grade9-maths.explanation: x − 6 < −2 gives x < 4, written { x : x < 4 }.

grade9-maths.question: Solve the inequality 3 − 2x > 9.
grade9-maths.hint: Move the 3 first, then divide by −2 and turn the sign round.
grade9-maths.explanation: Subtracting 3: −2x > 6. Dividing by −2 reverses the sign: x < −3, written { x : x < −3 }.

grade9-maths.question: Solve the inequality 5x + 2 < 3x + 10.
grade9-maths.hint: Collect the x terms on one side first.
grade9-maths.explanation: Subtracting 3x: 2x + 2 < 10. Subtracting 2: 2x < 8, so x < 4, written { x : x < 4 }.

grade9-maths.question: Solve the inequality x⁄3 ≥ 2.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply both sides by 3.
grade9-maths.explanation: Multiplying by 3 gives x ≥ 6, written { x : x ≥ 6 }.

grade9-maths.question: Which inequality means “x is at least 5”?
grade9-maths.hint: “At least” means 5 itself is allowed.
grade9-maths.explanation: “At least 5” means 5 or more, so x ≥ 5. Using > would wrongly exclude 5 itself.

grade9-maths.question: Which inequality means “x is less than 8”?
grade9-maths.hint: “Less than” does not include the number itself.
grade9-maths.explanation: “Less than 8” excludes 8, so x < 8.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the smallest integer that satisfies x > 3.7.
grade9-maths.hint: The answer must be a whole number bigger than 3.7.
grade9-maths.explanation: The integers greater than 3.7 are 4, 5, 6, …, so the smallest is 4.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the largest integer that satisfies x ≤ 6.2.
grade9-maths.hint: The answer must be a whole number no bigger than 6.2.
grade9-maths.explanation: The integers less than or equal to 6.2 are …, 5, 6, so the largest is 6.

grade9-maths.question: Solve the inequality 2(x − 1) < 3x + 4.
grade9-maths.hint: Expand the bracket, then collect the x terms; watch the sign at the end.
grade9-maths.explanation: Expanding: 2x − 2 < 3x + 4. Subtracting 2x: −2 < x + 4. Subtracting 4: −6 < x, which is x > −6, written { x : x > −6 }.

grade9-maths.question:
<svg viewBox="0 0 324 76" width="324" height="76" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img"><defs><marker id="nlA" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="7" refY="3.2" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L7,3.2 L0,6.4 z" fill="#000"/></marker></defs><line x1="12" y1="44" x2="312" y2="44" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" marker-end="url(#nlA)"/><line x1="12" y1="44" x2="22" y2="44" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5" marker-start="url(#nlA)"/><line x1="26" y1="38" x2="26" y2="50" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="26" y="66" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">-3</text><line x1="60" y1="38" x2="60" y2="50" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="60" y="66" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">-2</text><line x1="94" y1="38" x2="94" y2="50" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="94" y="66" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">-1</text><line x1="128" y1="38" x2="128" y2="50" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="128" y="66" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">0</text><line x1="162" y1="38" x2="162" y2="50" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="162" y="66" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">1</text><line x1="196" y1="38" x2="196" y2="50" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="196" y="66" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">2</text><line x1="230" y1="38" x2="230" y2="50" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="230" y="66" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">3</text><line x1="264" y1="38" x2="264" y2="50" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="264" y="66" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">4</text><line x1="298" y1="38" x2="298" y2="50" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.2"/><text x="298" y="66" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">5</text><line x1="94" y1="30" x2="230" y2="30" stroke="#000" stroke-width="2.6"/><circle cx="94" cy="30" r="5.4" fill="#000" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.8"/><circle cx="230" cy="30" r="5.4" fill="#fff" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.8"/></svg>
Which inequality is shown on the number line?
grade9-maths.hint: A filled circle includes its value; a hollow circle excludes it.
grade9-maths.explanation: The circle at −1 is filled, so −1 is included and the sign is ≤. The circle at 3 is hollow, so 3 is excluded and the sign is <. The inequality is −1 ≤ x < 3.

grade9-maths.question:

Write down the inequality represented by the number line below.
grade9-maths.hint: Check each end separately.
grade9-maths.explanation: The circle at 0 is hollow, so 0 is excluded: 0 < x. The circle at 4 is filled, so 4 is included: x ≤ 4. Together, 0 < x ≤ 4.

grade9-maths.question: Solve the inequality −x⁄2 ≥ 3.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiplying by −2 reverses the sign.
grade9-maths.explanation: Multiplying both sides by −2 reverses the sign: x ≤ −6, written { x : x ≤ −6 }.

grade9-maths.question: How many integers satisfy −2 < x ≤ 3?
grade9-maths.hint: List them, remembering which end is included.
grade9-maths.explanation: −2 is excluded and 3 is included, so the integers are −1, 0, 1, 2, 3 - five of them.

grade9-maths.question: Solve the inequality 7 − x ≤ 2.
grade9-maths.hint: Move the x across, or divide by −1 and turn the sign.
grade9-maths.explanation: Subtracting 7: −x ≤ −5. Multiplying by −1 reverses the sign: x ≥ 5, written { x : x ≥ 5 }.

grade9-maths.question: Solve the inequality 2x + 3 ≤ 11.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract 3, then divide by 2.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2x + 3 ≤ 11 gives 2x ≤ 8, so x ≤ 4.

grade9-maths.question: A worker is paid Rs 450 per day. Find his pay for 6 days.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the daily rate by the number of days.

grade9-maths.question: A clerk earns Rs 24 000 per month. Find her annual salary.
grade9-maths.hint: There are 12 months in a year.

grade9-maths.question: A worker is paid Rs 150 per hour for overtime. Find his pay for 8 hours of overtime.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the hourly rate by the hours worked.

grade9-maths.question: A basic salary is Rs 18 000. A bonus of 10% is added. Find the total pay.
grade9-maths.hint: Find 10% first, then add it on.

grade9-maths.question: A salary of Rs 20 000 has 5% deducted for a pension. Find the net salary.
grade9-maths.hint: Work out the deduction, then subtract it.
grade9-maths.explanation: 5% of 20 000 = 1 000, so the net salary is 20 000 − 1 000 = Rs 19 000.

grade9-maths.question: A television is bought on hire purchase with a deposit of Rs 5 000 and 12 monthly payments of Rs 1 500. Find the total amount paid.
grade9-maths.hint: Deposit plus all the monthly payments.
grade9-maths.explanation: The monthly payments come to 12 × 1 500 = Rs 18 000. Adding the deposit: 5 000 + 18 000 = Rs 23 000.

grade9-maths.question: The cash price of a television is Rs 20 000. On hire purchase it costs a total of Rs 23 000. Find the extra amount paid for buying on hire purchase.
grade9-maths.hint: Compare the two totals.
grade9-maths.explanation: 23 000 − 20 000 = Rs 3 000 more than paying cash.

grade9-maths.question: John deposits Rs 200 000 for a period of 30 months in a bank. The rate of simple interest is 3% per annum. Find the total amount John will get when he withdraws all his money after 30 months.
grade9-maths.hint: Change 30 months into years before using the formula.
grade9-maths.explanation: 30 months = 2.5 years. Interest = 200 000 × 3/100 × 2.5 = Rs 15 000. The total is 200 000 + 15 000 = Rs 215 000.

grade9-maths.question: A man invests Rs 300 000 for 5 years at 2% per annum. Calculate the simple interest he earns.
grade9-maths.hint: Interest = principal × rate × time.

grade9-maths.question: Find the simple interest on Rs 50 000 at 4% per annum for 3 years.
grade9-maths.hint: Interest = P × R × T ÷ 100.

grade9-maths.question: The simple interest on Rs 40 000 for 2 years is Rs 4 000. Find the rate per annum. (answer in %)
grade9-maths.hint: Rearrange the interest formula for the rate.
grade9-maths.explanation: Interest = P × R × T ÷ 100. Here 40 000 × 2 ÷ 100 = 800, so 4 000 = 800R and R = 4 000 ÷ 800 = 5% per annum.

grade9-maths.question: A shopkeeper buys an article for Rs 800 and sells it for Rs 1 000. Find his profit.
grade9-maths.hint: Selling price minus cost price.

grade9-maths.question: A shopkeeper buys an article for Rs 800 and sells it for Rs 1 000. Find his percentage profit. (answer in %)
grade9-maths.hint: Percentage profit is the profit over the COST price.
grade9-maths.explanation: The profit is Rs 200 on a cost of Rs 800, so the percentage profit is (200 ÷ 800) × 100 = 25%.

grade9-maths.question:
Electricity tariff

First 25 unitsRs 3.50

Above 75 unitsRs 6.50
A household uses 60 units of electricity in a month. Using the tariff shown, calculate the total cost.
grade9-maths.hint: Charge the first 25 units at one rate, then the rest at the next rate.
grade9-maths.explanation: First 25 units: 25 × 3.50 = Rs 87.50. The remaining 35 units fall in the next band: 35 × 5.00 = Rs 175. Total = 87.50 + 175 = Rs 262.50.

grade9-maths.question:
Electricity tariff
Units usedRate per unit
First 25 unitsRs 3.50
Next 50 unitsRs 5.00
Above 75 unitsRs 6.50
A household uses 90 units of electricity in a month. Using the tariff shown, calculate the total cost.
grade9-maths.hint: The bill crosses all three bands.
grade9-maths.explanation: First 25 units: 25 × 3.50 = Rs 87.50. Next 50 units: 50 × 5.00 = Rs 250. The last 15 units are above 75: 15 × 6.50 = Rs 97.50. Total = 87.50 + 250 + 97.50 = Rs 435.

grade9-maths.question:
Water tariff
Units usedRate per unit
First 10 m³Rs 8.00
Next 15 m³Rs 12.00
Above 25 m³Rs 20.00
A household uses 20 m³ of water in a month. Using the tariff shown, calculate the total cost.
grade9-maths.hint: The first 10 m³ are charged at the lower rate.
grade9-maths.explanation: First 10 m³: 10 × 8.00 = Rs 80. The remaining 10 m³ fall in the next band: 10 × 12.00 = Rs 120. Total = 80 + 120 = Rs 200.

grade9-maths.question:
Water tariff
Units usedRate per unit
First 10 m³Rs 8.00
Next 15 m³Rs 12.00
Above 25 m³Rs 20.00
A household uses 30 m³ of water in a month. Using the tariff shown, calculate the total cost.
grade9-maths.hint: The bill crosses all three bands.
grade9-maths.explanation: First 10 m³: 10 × 8.00 = Rs 80. Next 15 m³: 15 × 12.00 = Rs 180. The last 5 m³ are above 25: 5 × 20.00 = Rs 100. Total = 80 + 180 + 100 = Rs 360.

grade9-maths.question:
Electricity tariff
Units usedRate per unit
First 25 unitsRs 3.50
Next 50 unitsRs 5.00
Above 75 unitsRs 6.50
Using the electricity tariff shown, write down the rate per unit charged for the first 25 units.
grade9-maths.hint: Read straight off the first row of the table.
grade9-maths.explanation: The table gives Rs 3.50 per unit for the first 25 units.

grade9-maths.question: A car is bought on hire purchase with a deposit of Rs 60 000 and 24 monthly payments of Rs 12 500. Find the total amount paid.
grade9-maths.hint: Deposit plus all the instalments.
grade9-maths.explanation: The instalments come to 24 × 12 500 = Rs 300 000. Adding the deposit: 60 000 + 300 000 = Rs 360 000.

grade9-maths.question: A worker’s basic pay is Rs 16 000 per month. He also works 20 hours of overtime at Rs 200 per hour, and 6% of his total pay is deducted. Find his net pay.
grade9-maths.hint: Add the overtime first, then take the deduction from the whole amount.
grade9-maths.explanation: Overtime = 20 × 200 = Rs 4 000, so the total pay is 16 000 + 4 000 = Rs 20 000. The deduction is 6% of 20 000 = Rs 1 200, so the net pay is 20 000 − 1 200 = Rs 18 800.

grade9-maths.question: Convert 3 L into mL. (answer in mL)
grade9-maths.hint: There are 1 000 millilitres in a litre.

grade9-maths.question: Convert 2 L into cL. (answer in cL)
grade9-maths.hint: There are 100 centilitres in a litre.

grade9-maths.question: Convert 500 mL into litres. (answer in L)
grade9-maths.hint: Divide by 1 000.

grade9-maths.question: Convert 75 cL into mL. (answer in mL)
grade9-maths.hint: One centilitre is 10 millilitres.

grade9-maths.question: Convert 1 250 mL into litres. (answer in L)
grade9-maths.hint: Divide by 1 000.

grade9-maths.question: Convert 4.5 L into cL. (answer in cL)
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply by 100.

grade9-maths.question: Which is larger, 600 mL or 0.6 L?
grade9-maths.hint: Put both into the same unit before comparing.
grade9-maths.explanation: 0.6 L = 0.6 × 1 000 = 600 mL, so the two are exactly equal.

grade9-maths.question: A bottle holds 1.5 L of juice. How many 250 mL glasses can be filled from it? (answer in glasses)
grade9-maths.hint: Work in the same unit first.
grade9-maths.explanation: 1.5 L = 1 500 mL, and 1 500 ÷ 250 = 6 glasses.

grade9-maths.question: A jug holds 2 L. It is filled from a 250 mL cup. How many cupfuls are needed? (answer in cupfuls)
grade9-maths.hint: Change the litres to millilitres.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2 L = 2 000 mL, and 2 000 ÷ 250 = 8 cupfuls.

grade9-maths.question: A container has a volume of 1 000 cm³. Write down its capacity in litres. (answer in L)
grade9-maths.hint: 1 000 cm³ of space holds exactly one litre.
grade9-maths.explanation: 1 000 cm³ = 1 litre, so the capacity is 1 L.

grade9-maths.question: A tank measures 20 cm by 10 cm by 5 cm. Find its capacity in millilitres. (answer in mL)
grade9-maths.hint: Find the volume in cm³ first; 1 cm³ holds 1 mL.
grade9-maths.explanation: The volume is 20 × 10 × 5 = 1 000 cm³, and 1 cm³ holds 1 mL, so the capacity is 1 000 mL.

grade9-maths.question: A tank measures 50 cm by 40 cm by 30 cm. Find its capacity in litres. (answer in L)
grade9-maths.hint: Volume in cm³ first, then divide by 1 000.
grade9-maths.explanation: The volume is 50 × 40 × 30 = 60 000 cm³. Since 1 000 cm³ = 1 L, the capacity is 60 000 ÷ 1 000 = 60 L.

grade9-maths.question: A rectangular tank measures 30 cm by 20 cm by 25 cm. Water is poured in to a depth of 10 cm. Find the volume of water in litres. (answer in L)
grade9-maths.hint: Use the depth of the water, not the height of the tank.
grade9-maths.explanation: The water forms a cuboid 30 × 20 × 10 = 6 000 cm³, which is 6 L.

grade9-maths.question: Convert 0.25 L into mL. (answer in mL)
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply by 1 000.

grade9-maths.question: A bucket holds 12 L. A tap fills it at 2 L per minute. How long does it take to fill? (answer in minutes)
grade9-maths.hint: Divide the capacity by the rate.
grade9-maths.explanation: 12 ÷ 2 = 6 minutes.

grade9-maths.question: Six identical bottles each hold 33 cL. Find the total in litres. (answer in L)
grade9-maths.hint: Add the centilitres first, then change to litres.
grade9-maths.explanation: 6 × 33 = 198 cL, and 198 ÷ 100 = 1.98 L.

grade9-maths.question: A cubical container has edges of 10 cm. Find its capacity in litres. (answer in L)
grade9-maths.hint: Find the volume, then use 1 000 cm³ = 1 L.
grade9-maths.explanation: The volume is 10 × 10 × 10 = 1 000 cm³, which is 1 L.

grade9-maths.question: A drum holds 25 L of water. 8 500 mL are used. How much water is left, in litres? (answer in L)
grade9-maths.hint: Change the millilitres to litres before subtracting.
grade9-maths.explanation: 8 500 mL = 8.5 L, so the water left is 25 − 8.5 = 16.5 L.

grade9-maths.question: How many centilitres are there in one litre? (answer in cL)
grade9-maths.hint: The prefix "centi" means one hundredth.
grade9-maths.explanation: One litre is 100 centilitres.

grade9-maths.question: A tank of capacity 90 L is 2⁄3 full. Find the volume of water in the tank, in litres. (answer in L)
grade9-maths.hint: Find one third first.
grade9-maths.explanation: 90 ÷ 3 = 30, so two thirds is 30 × 2 = 60 L.

grade9-maths.question:
State the order of the matrix. (3
1)
grade9-maths.hint: Count the rows first, then the columns.
grade9-maths.explanation: The matrix has 2 rows and 1 column, so its order is 2 × 1.

grade9-maths.question: State the order of the matrix. (2  5  7)
grade9-maths.hint: Rows first, then columns.
grade9-maths.explanation: The matrix has 1 row and 3 columns, so its order is 1 × 3.

grade9-maths.question:
State the order of the matrix. (1  2  3
4  5  6)
grade9-maths.hint: Two rows, three columns - and the rows come first.
grade9-maths.explanation: There are 2 rows and 3 columns, so the order is 2 × 3. Writing 3 × 2 is the usual mistake: the row count is always given first.

grade9-maths.question: A matrix has order 3 × 4. How many elements does it contain?
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the rows by the columns.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3 rows of 4 elements gives 3 × 4 = 12 elements.

grade9-maths.question: Which of these is a square matrix?
grade9-maths.hint: A square matrix has as many rows as columns.
grade9-maths.explanation: Only the 2 × 2 matrix has an equal number of rows and columns, so it is the square one.

grade9-maths.question: Which of these is the 2 × 2 identity matrix?
grade9-maths.hint: The identity has 1s down the leading diagonal and 0s elsewhere.
grade9-maths.explanation: The identity matrix has 1s on the leading diagonal, from top left to bottom right, and 0s everywhere else.

grade9-maths.question: Which of these is a null (zero) matrix?
grade9-maths.hint: Every element must be zero.
grade9-maths.explanation: A null matrix has 0 in every position.

grade9-maths.question: Which of these is a diagonal matrix?
grade9-maths.hint: Everything off the leading diagonal must be zero.
grade9-maths.explanation: A diagonal matrix has non-zero entries only on the leading diagonal and 0 everywhere else.

grade9-maths.question:
Find A + B, where A = (1  2
3  4) and B = (5  6
7  8).
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
grade9-maths.hint: Add the numbers in matching positions.
grade9-maths.explanation: Adding element by element: 1+5 = 6, 2+6 = 8, 3+7 = 10 and 4+8 = 12, giving (6 8; 10 12).

grade9-maths.question:
Find A − B, where A = (7  5
3  2) and B = (2  1
1  4).
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract element by element, keeping the positions.
grade9-maths.explanation: Subtracting: 7−2 = 5, 5−1 = 4, 3−1 = 2 and 2−4 = −2, giving (5 4; 2 −2).

grade9-maths.question:
Find 3A, where A = (1  -2
4  0).
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply every element by 3.
grade9-maths.explanation: Multiplying each element by 3: (3 −6; 12 0).

grade9-maths.question:
Find 2A − B, where A = (2  -3
0  5) and B = (-1  4
6  2).
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
grade9-maths.hint: Double A first, then subtract B element by element.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2A = (4 −6; 0 10). Subtracting B: 4−(−1) = 5, −6−4 = −10, 0−6 = −6 and 10−2 = 8, giving (5 −10; −6 8).

grade9-maths.question:
Find P + Q, where P = (8
-5) and Q = (3
2).
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
grade9-maths.hint: Add the top numbers, then the bottom numbers.
grade9-maths.explanation: 8+3 = 11 and −5+2 = −3, giving (11; −3).

grade9-maths.question:
Solve the matrix equation X + (1  2
3  4) = (5  7
9  11) for X.
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract the known matrix from both sides.
grade9-maths.explanation: X = (5 7; 9 11) − (1 2; 3 4). Subtracting element by element: (4 5; 6 7).

grade9-maths.question:
Solve the matrix equation Y − (2  0
1  3) = (1  4
2  2) for Y.
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
grade9-maths.hint: Add the known matrix to both sides.

grade9-maths.question: Two matrices are equal. What must be true of them?
grade9-maths.hint: Both the shape and every entry must match.
grade9-maths.explanation: Equal matrices must have the same order AND identical elements in matching positions. Two matrices holding the same numbers in different places are not equal.
options: They have the same order only
They contain exactly the same numbers in any positions
They have the same order and every matching element is equal
They have the same number of elements
grade9-maths.answer: They have the same order and every matching element is equal
acceptableAnswers: They have the same order and every matching element is equal

grade9-maths.question:
Given that (x
3) + (2
y) = (7
10), find the values of x and y.
grade9-maths.hint: Matching positions must be equal, so write down two ordinary equations.
grade9-maths.explanation: The top entries give x + 2 = 7, so x = 5. The bottom entries give 3 + y = 10, so y = 7.

grade9-maths.question: A shop records its sales in a matrix with 4 rows and 2 columns. State the order of the matrix.
grade9-maths.hint: Rows first.
grade9-maths.explanation: With 4 rows and 2 columns the order is 4 × 2.

grade9-maths.question:
Find 2Q, where Q = (3
2).
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply each element by 2.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2 × 3 = 6 and 2 × 2 = 4, giving (6; 4).

grade9-maths.question:
Find A + 2B, where A = (1  0
2  1) and B = (3  1
0  4).
Write your answer with a semicolon between the rows, for example 1 2; 3 4.
grade9-maths.hint: Work out 2B first, then add A.

grade9-maths.question: Make x the subject of y = x + 5.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract 5 from both sides.
grade9-maths.explanation: Subtracting 5 from both sides gives x = y − 5.

grade9-maths.question: Make x the subject of y = 3x.
grade9-maths.hint: Divide both sides by 3.
grade9-maths.explanation: Dividing both sides by 3 gives x = y/3.

grade9-maths.question: Make x the subject of y = 2x + 7.
grade9-maths.hint: Undo the +7 first, then the ×2.
grade9-maths.explanation: Subtracting 7: y − 7 = 2x. Dividing by 2: x = (y − 7)/2.

grade9-maths.question: Make r the subject of C = 2πr.
grade9-maths.hint: Divide both sides by everything multiplying r.
grade9-maths.explanation: Dividing both sides by 2π gives r = C/(2π).

grade9-maths.question: Make h the subject of V = lwh.
grade9-maths.hint: Divide both sides by the two lengths.
grade9-maths.explanation: Dividing both sides by lw gives h = V/(lw).

grade9-maths.question: Make b the subject of A = 1⁄2bh.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply by 2 first, then divide by h.
grade9-maths.explanation: Multiplying both sides by 2: 2A = bh. Dividing by h: b = 2A/h.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of y when x = 4, given y = 3x − 2.
grade9-maths.hint: Substitute 4 in place of x.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of A when l = 6 and w = 5, given A = lw.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the two values.
grade9-maths.explanation: A = 6 × 5 = 30.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of V when l = 4, w = 3 and h = 2, given V = lwh.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply all three values.
grade9-maths.explanation: V = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of s when u = 5, t = 3 and a = 2, given s = ut + at2.
grade9-maths.hint: Work out each term separately, then add.
grade9-maths.explanation: ut = 5 × 3 = 15 and at² = 2 × 9 = 18, so s = 15 + 18 = 33.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of A when r = 7 and l = 4, given A = πr2 + πrl. Leave your answer in terms of π.
grade9-maths.hint: Work out each term with π kept as a symbol, then add.
grade9-maths.explanation: πr² = 49π and πrl = π × 7 × 4 = 28π. Adding: A = 49π + 28π = 77π.

grade9-maths.question: Make l the subject of A = πr2 + πrl, leaving your answer in terms of π.
grade9-maths.hint: Get the term containing l on its own first.
grade9-maths.explanation: Subtracting πr² from both sides: A − πr² = πrl. Dividing by πr: l = (A − πr²)/(πr).

grade9-maths.question: Make C the subject of F = 9⁄5C + 32.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract 32 first, then undo the fraction.
grade9-maths.explanation: Subtracting 32: F − 32 = (9/5)C. Multiplying by 5 and dividing by 9: C = 5(F − 32)/9.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of P when l = 8 and w = 3, given P = 2(l + w).
grade9-maths.hint: Do the bracket first.
grade9-maths.explanation: l + w = 11, so P = 2 × 11 = 22.

grade9-maths.question: Make w the subject of P = 2(l + w).
grade9-maths.hint: Expand the bracket, or divide by 2 first.
grade9-maths.explanation: Dividing by 2: P/2 = l + w. Subtracting l: w = P/2 − l, which is the same as (P − 2l)/2.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of x when y = 17, given y = 4x + 1.
grade9-maths.hint: Substitute, then solve the equation.

grade9-maths.question: Make r the subject of V = πr2h.
grade9-maths.hint: Isolate r² first, then take the square root.
grade9-maths.explanation: Dividing both sides by πh: r² = V/(πh). Taking the square root: r = √(V/(πh)).

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of a when v = 20, u = 4 and t = 8, given v = u + at.
grade9-maths.hint: Substitute the three values, then solve for a.

grade9-maths.question: Make t the subject of v = u + at.
grade9-maths.hint: Get the term with t alone, then divide.
grade9-maths.explanation: Subtracting u: v − u = at. Dividing by a: t = (v − u)/a.

grade9-maths.question: Make x the subject of y = (x + 3)⁄4.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply both sides by 4 first.
grade9-maths.explanation: Multiplying both sides by 4: 4y = x + 3. Subtracting 3: x = 4y − 3.

grade9-maths.question: A formula is given by A = πr2 + πrl. Calculate the value of A when r = 5 cm and l = 3 cm. Leave your answer in terms of π.
grade9-maths.hint: Work out each term with π kept as a symbol.
grade9-maths.explanation: πr² = 25π and πrl = π × 5 × 3 = 15π. Adding: A = 25π + 15π = 40π.

grade9-maths.question: A formula is given by A = πr2 + πrl. Make l the subject of the formula, leaving your answer in terms of π.
grade9-maths.hint: Move the term without l to the other side, then divide.
grade9-maths.explanation: Subtracting πr²: A − πr² = πrl. Dividing by πr: l = (A − πr²)/(πr).

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of angle x in the diagram. (answer in °)
grade9-maths.hint: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°, and the square marks a right angle.
grade9-maths.explanation: The square marks a right angle of 90° and the other marked angle is 55°, so x = 180 − 90 − 55 = 35°.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of angle y in the diagram. (answer in °)
grade9-maths.hint: The three angles sit on a straight line.
grade9-maths.explanation: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°, so y = 180 − 70 − 45 = 65°.

grade9-maths.question: Two angles on a straight line are 120° and p. Find p. (answer in °)
grade9-maths.hint: They must add to 180°.

grade9-maths.question: In the diagram the two horizontal lines are parallel. Find the value of angle a. (answer in °)
grade9-maths.hint: Angles in matching positions on parallel lines are equal.
grade9-maths.explanation: The marked 110° and a are corresponding angles on parallel lines, so they are equal and a = 110°.

grade9-maths.question: In the diagram the two horizontal lines are parallel. Find the value of angle b. (answer in °)
grade9-maths.hint: Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal.
grade9-maths.explanation: The 65° angle and b are alternate angles, on opposite sides of the slanting line, so b = 65°.

grade9-maths.question: The two horizontal lines are parallel. Given that the marked angle is 130°, find the co-interior angle c. (answer in °)
grade9-maths.hint: Co-interior angles on parallel lines add up to 180°.
grade9-maths.explanation: Co-interior angles between parallel lines are supplementary, so c = 180 − 130 = 50°.

grade9-maths.question: The angles of a triangle are 40°, 75° and t. Find t. (answer in °)
grade9-maths.hint: The angles of any triangle add up to 180°.
grade9-maths.explanation: t = 180 − 40 − 75 = 65°.

grade9-maths.question: Four angles meet at a point on a straight line. Three of them are 30°, 50° and 40°. Find the fourth angle q. (answer in °)
grade9-maths.hint: They still add to 180°.
grade9-maths.explanation: q = 180 − 30 − 50 − 40 = 60°.

grade9-maths.question:
<svg viewBox="0 0 300 168" width="300" height="168" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img"><circle cx="118" cy="88" r="50" fill="#d5d5d5"/><circle cx="182" cy="88" r="50" fill="#d5d5d5"/><rect x="34" y="22" width="232" height="132" fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.4"/><circle cx="118" cy="88" r="50" fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5"/><circle cx="182" cy="88" r="50" fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="250" y="40" font-size="13" font-style="italic">ξ</text><text x="88" y="34" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="212" y="34" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">B</text></svg>
The Venn diagram shows two sets. Which region is shaded?
grade9-maths.hint: Union means everything in either circle.
grade9-maths.explanation: Both circles are shaded completely, which is A union B - everything that is in A, in B, or in both.

grade9-maths.question:
<svg viewBox="0 0 300 168" width="300" height="168" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img"><defs><clipPath id="vclip"><circle cx="118" cy="88" r="50"/></clipPath></defs><circle cx="182" cy="88" r="50" fill="#c2c2c2" clip-path="url(#vclip)"/><rect x="34" y="22" width="232" height="132" fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.4"/><circle cx="118" cy="88" r="50" fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5"/><circle cx="182" cy="88" r="50" fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="250" y="40" font-size="13" font-style="italic">ξ</text><text x="88" y="34" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="212" y="34" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">B</text></svg>
Which region of the Venn diagram below has been shaded?
grade9-maths.hint: Only the overlap is shaded.
grade9-maths.explanation: The shaded part is the overlap alone, which is A intersection B - the members that are in both sets.

grade9-maths.question: The Venn diagram shows the numbers in each region. How many elements are in A ∪ B?
grade9-maths.hint: Add every region inside either circle - but count the overlap once.
grade9-maths.explanation: 9 + 5 + 9 = 23. The 4 outside both circles is not part of A union B, and the overlap of 5 must be counted once, not twice.

grade9-maths.question: The Venn diagram shows the numbers in each region. How many elements are in the universal set?
grade9-maths.hint: The universal set is everything inside the rectangle.
grade9-maths.explanation: 9 + 5 + 9 + 4 = 27, including the 4 that lie outside both circles.

grade9-maths.question: In a class of 30 students, 14 play football, 17 play volleyball, x play both and 6 play neither. Find the value of x.
grade9-maths.hint: Everything inside the rectangle adds to 30. Take care not to double-count the overlap.
grade9-maths.explanation: Football only is (14 − x), both is x, volleyball only is (17 − x), and 6 play neither. So (14 − x) + x + (17 − x) + 6 = 30, giving 37 − x = 30 and x = 7.

grade9-maths.question: In the same class of 30 students, 14 play football, 17 play volleyball, 7 play both and 6 play neither. How many play volleyball only? (answer in students)
grade9-maths.hint: Take the ones who play both away from the volleyball total.
grade9-maths.explanation: 17 − 7 = 10 students play volleyball but not football.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the area of the compound shape. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: Split it into two rectangles, or take a piece away from a big rectangle.
grade9-maths.explanation: The whole rectangle would be 10 × 10 = 100 cm². The piece cut away is 6 × 4 = 24 cm². So the area is 100 − 24 = 76 cm².

grade9-maths.question: A floor tile has the shape shown. Calculate its area. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: Work out the area of the full rectangle, then subtract the missing corner.
grade9-maths.explanation: The full rectangle is 12 × 8 = 96 cm² and the missing corner is 6 × 3 = 18 cm², so the area is 96 − 18 = 78 cm².

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the perimeter of the compound shape. (answer in cm)
grade9-maths.hint: Every side must be counted, including the two you are not told directly.
grade9-maths.explanation: Going round: 11 + 5 + 5 + 4 + 6 + 9 = 40 cm. The two sides that carry no label are found by subtraction: 9 − 5 = 4 and 11 − 5 = 6.

grade9-maths.question: A rectangle measures 9 cm by 5 cm. Calculate its area. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: Length times width.
grade9-maths.explanation: 9 × 5 = 45 cm².

grade9-maths.question: The pie chart shows how 36 pupils travel to school. The sector for bus is 120°. How many pupils travel by bus? (answer in pupils)
grade9-maths.hint: A whole pie chart is 360°, shared between 36 pupils.
grade9-maths.explanation: Each pupil is represented by 360 ÷ 36 = 10°. So 120° represents 120 ÷ 10 = 12 pupils.

grade9-maths.question: In a pie chart of 60 people, one sector represents 15 people. Calculate the angle of that sector. (answer in °)
grade9-maths.hint: Find the angle for one person first.
grade9-maths.explanation: 360 ÷ 60 = 6° per person, so 15 people are represented by 15 × 6 = 90°.

grade9-maths.question: A pie chart shows four sectors of 120°, 100°, 90° and x°. Find x. (answer in °)
grade9-maths.hint: The four sectors must make a complete turn.
grade9-maths.explanation: The angles round the centre add to 360°, so x = 360 − 120 − 100 − 90 = 50°.

grade9-maths.question: A pie chart of 72 families has a sector of 60° for “no car”. How many families have no car? (answer in families)
grade9-maths.hint: Work out how many degrees represent one family.
grade9-maths.explanation: 360 ÷ 72 = 5° per family, so 60° represents 60 ÷ 5 = 12 families.

grade9-maths.question: Three angles meet at a point. Two of them are 145° and 120°. Find the third angle m. (answer in °)
grade9-maths.hint: Angles that fill one complete turn add up to 360°.
grade9-maths.explanation: m = 360 − 145 − 120 = 95°.

grade9-maths.question: Four angles meet at a point. Three of them are 90°, 85° and 110°. Find the remaining angle n. (answer in °)
grade9-maths.hint: Add the three you are given, then take the total from a complete turn.

grade9-maths.question: The diagram shows an isosceles triangle. Two of its angles are 50° each. Find the third angle k. (answer in °)
grade9-maths.hint: The three angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
grade9-maths.explanation: k = 180 − 50 − 50 = 80°.

grade9-maths.question: In the triangle shown, one angle is 90° and another is 35°. Find the third angle h. (answer in °)
grade9-maths.hint: The angles of any triangle, right-angled or not, add up to 180°.
grade9-maths.explanation: h = 180 − 90 − 35 = 55°.

grade9-maths.question: The volume of a cone is 1⁄3πr2h. Taking π = 3.14, calculate the volume of the cone shown. (answer in cm³)
grade9-maths.hint: Square the radius, multiply by the height and by pi, then divide by 3.

grade9-maths.question: A cylinder has the same radius and height. How many times larger is its volume? (answer in times)
grade9-maths.hint: A cone is one third of the cylinder that contains it.
grade9-maths.explanation: The cylinder is πr²h and the cone is a third of that, so the cylinder is 3 times larger.

grade9-maths.question: The solid has an L-shaped end face. Calculate the area of that face. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: Split the L into two rectangles, or take a piece from a big one.
grade9-maths.explanation: The whole rectangle is 20 × 18 = 360 cm² and the missing corner is 11 × 8 = 88 cm², so the face is 360 − 88 = 272 cm².

grade9-maths.question: The solid is 9 cm deep. Calculate its volume. (answer in cm³)
grade9-maths.hint: Area of the end face multiplied by the depth.
grade9-maths.explanation: 272 × 9 = 2 448 cm³.

grade9-maths.question: The tank has a trapezium as its end face. Calculate the area of that face. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: ½ × (sum of the parallel sides) × depth.
grade9-maths.explanation: ½ × (24 + 12) × 40 = 18 × 40 = 720 cm².

grade9-maths.question: The tank is 50 cm long. Calculate its volume. (answer in cm³)
grade9-maths.hint: End area multiplied by length.

grade9-maths.question: Express that volume in litres (1 litre = 1 000 cm³). (answer in litres)
grade9-maths.hint: Divide by 1 000.
grade9-maths.explanation: 36 000 ÷ 1 000 = 36 litres.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the order of matrix A shown, in the form rows × columns. Give the number of rows.
grade9-maths.hint: Count the horizontal lines of numbers.
grade9-maths.explanation: There are 2 rows and 3 columns, so the order is 2 × 3.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the number of columns.
grade9-maths.hint: Count the vertical lines of numbers.
grade9-maths.explanation: There are 3 columns.

grade9-maths.question: Matrix B is shown. Write down the element in row 2, column 1.
grade9-maths.hint: Second row, first column.
grade9-maths.explanation: The element in row 2, column 1 is 7.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the sum of all four elements of B.
grade9-maths.hint: Add every number in the matrix.

grade9-maths.question: Three containers are shown with their capacities. What is their total capacity in litres? (answer in litres)
grade9-maths.hint: Add the three capacities.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 litres.

grade9-maths.question: Each is half full. How much liquid is there altogether? (answer in litres)
grade9-maths.hint: Half of the total capacity.
grade9-maths.explanation: ½ of 9 = 4.5 litres.

grade9-maths.question: Container C holds 4 litres when full and is shown three quarters full. How many litres does it contain? (answer in litres)
grade9-maths.hint: Three quarters of its capacity.
grade9-maths.explanation: ¾ of 4 = 3 litres.

grade9-maths.question: How many millilitres is that? (answer in ml)
grade9-maths.hint: 1 litre is 1 000 millilitres.

grade9-maths.question: The pattern is made of small squares. How many squares are in Figure 4? (answer in squares)
grade9-maths.hint: Each figure is a square of squares.
grade9-maths.explanation: The figures hold 1, 4, 9 squares - the square numbers - so Figure 4 holds 4² = 16.

grade9-maths.question: How many squares are in Figure 10? (answer in squares)
grade9-maths.hint: Square the figure number.
grade9-maths.explanation: 10² = 100 squares.

grade9-maths.question: The pattern grows as shown. Write down the number of squares in Figure 4. (answer in squares)
grade9-maths.hint: Look at how the side length grows.
grade9-maths.explanation: The sides are 2, 3, 4, so Figure 4 has side 5 and holds 5² = 25 squares.

grade9-maths.question: The nth figure has (n + 1)2 squares. How many squares are in Figure 12? (answer in squares)
grade9-maths.hint: Substitute n = 12 into the rule.

grade9-maths.question: A shopkeeper buys 40 shirts at Rs 250 each. He sells 30 of them at Rs 400 each and the remaining 10 at Rs 300 each. Calculate his total profit.
grade9-maths.hint: Work out the total cost, then the total money taken, then compare.
grade9-maths.explanation: The shirts cost 40 × 250 = Rs 10 000. He takes 30 × 400 = Rs 12 000 from the first batch and 10 × 300 = Rs 3 000 from the rest, giving Rs 15 000 in all. The profit is 15 000 − 10 000 = Rs 5 000.

grade9-maths.question: A tourist changes Rs 18 000 into euros at 45 rupees to the euro. She spends 240 euros and changes the rest back at 40 rupees to the euro. How many rupees does she get back?
grade9-maths.hint: Find the euros she starts with, then the euros left, then convert back at the NEW rate.
grade9-maths.explanation: 18 000 ÷ 45 = 400 euros. After spending 240 she has 160 euros left. Changing back at 40 rupees to the euro gives 160 × 40 = Rs 6 400.

grade9-maths.question: The diagram shows a rectangular tank measuring 120 cm by 50 cm by 40 cm. Water flows into the empty tank at 8 litres per minute. How many minutes does it take to fill? (answer in minutes)
grade9-maths.hint: Find the volume in cubic centimetres, change it to litres, then divide by the rate.
grade9-maths.explanation: The tank holds 120 × 50 × 40 = 240 000 cm³. Since 1 000 cm³ = 1 litre, that is 240 litres. At 8 litres a minute it takes 240 ÷ 8 = 30 minutes.

grade9-maths.question: The diagram shows a solid metal cuboid measuring 20 cm by 10 cm by 6 cm. It is melted down and recast as cubes of side 2 cm. How many cubes are made? (answer in cubes)
grade9-maths.hint: The metal keeps its volume; find the volume of one small cube.
grade9-maths.explanation: The cuboid has volume 20 × 10 × 6 = 1 200 cm³. Each small cube has volume 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 cm³. So 1 200 ÷ 8 = 150 cubes are made.

grade9-maths.question: A closed rectangular box measures 30 cm by 20 cm by 10 cm. It is to be covered with paper costing Rs 2 per 100 cm². Calculate the cost of the paper.
grade9-maths.hint: Find the total surface area first, then work out how many hundreds of square centimetres.
grade9-maths.explanation: The three different faces are 30×20 = 600, 30×10 = 300 and 20×10 = 200 cm². Each occurs twice, so the surface area is 2(600 + 300 + 200) = 2 200 cm². That is 22 lots of 100 cm², costing 22 × 2 = Rs 44.

grade9-maths.question: In the right-angled triangle shown, AC = 20 cm and the angle at C is 30°. Calculate the perimeter of the triangle, giving your answer to the nearest whole number. [Given sin 30° = 0.5, cos 30° = 0.87] (answer in cm)
grade9-maths.hint: Find each of the two shorter sides in turn, then add all three.
grade9-maths.explanation: AB is opposite the 30° angle: sin 30° = AB/20, so AB = 20 × 0.5 = 10 cm. BC is adjacent: cos 30° = BC/20, so BC = 20 × 0.87 = 17.4 cm. The perimeter is 10 + 17.4 + 20 = 47.4 cm, which is 47 cm to the nearest whole number.

grade9-maths.question:

The table shows the marks scored by 20 pupils in a test. Calculate the mean mark. (answer in marks)
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply each mark by how many pupils scored it, add those up, then divide by 20.
grade9-maths.explanation: The total is (4×5) + (5×6) + (6×5) + (7×4) = 20 + 30 + 30 + 28 = 108. The mean is 108 ÷ 20 = 5.4 marks exactly.

grade9-maths.question: A bag contains 4 red, 5 blue and 6 green marbles. One marble is drawn at random and NOT replaced. It is green. A second marble is then drawn. Find the probability that the second marble is also green.
grade9-maths.hint: Recount both the greens and the total after the first marble has gone.
grade9-maths.explanation: At the start there are 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 marbles, of which 6 are green. One green is removed and not replaced, leaving 14 marbles of which 5 are green. So the probability that the second is green is 5/14.

grade9-maths.question: A line passes through A (−1, −3) and B (3, 5). A second line is parallel to AB and passes through (0, 4). Find the equation of the second line.
grade9-maths.hint: Find the gradient of AB first; parallel lines share it.
grade9-maths.explanation: The gradient of AB is (5 − (−3)) ÷ (3 − (−1)) = 8/4 = 2. The second line has the same gradient and passes through (0, 4), so its intercept is 4 and its equation is y = 2x + 4.

grade9-maths.question: A rectangle has length (x + 5) cm and width (x − 2) cm. Show that its area is x2 + 3x − 10, then find the area when x = 6. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: Expand the brackets first, then substitute.
grade9-maths.explanation: Area = (x + 5)(x − 2) = x² − 2x + 5x − 10 = x² + 3x − 10. Substituting x = 6: 36 + 18 − 10 = 44 cm².

grade9-maths.question: At a canteen, 3 rotis and 2 cups of tea cost Rs 85. 5 rotis and 4 cups of tea cost Rs 155. Find the cost of 2 rotis and 3 cups of tea.
grade9-maths.hint: Let r be a roti and t a cup of tea, write two equations, then answer the question asked.
grade9-maths.explanation: From 3r + 2t = 85 and 5r + 4t = 155. Doubling the first: 6r + 4t = 170. Subtracting the second: r = 15. Substituting back: 45 + 2t = 85, so t = 20. Then 2 rotis and 3 teas cost 2(15) + 3(20) = 30 + 60 = Rs 80.

grade9-maths.question: A rectangular garden is 4 m longer than it is wide. Its area is 96 m². Find the perimeter of the garden. (answer in m)
grade9-maths.hint: Call the width x, form a quadratic, solve it, then answer the question that was asked.
grade9-maths.explanation: Let the width be x m, so the length is (x + 4) m and x(x + 4) = 96. This gives x² + 4x − 96 = 0, so (x + 12)(x − 8) = 0 and x = −12 or x = 8. A width cannot be negative, so the width is 8 m and the length is 12 m. The perimeter is 2(8 + 12) = 40 m.

grade9-maths.question: A tank holds 45 litres when full. It is 2⁄3 full. 12 litres are drawn off, then 5 litres are added. How many litres are in the tank now? (answer in L)
grade9-maths.hint: Work through the three steps in order.
grade9-maths.explanation: Two thirds of 45 is 30 litres. Drawing off 12 leaves 18 litres. Adding 5 gives 23 litres.

grade9-maths.question: The nth term of a sequence is 3n + 2. Find which term of the sequence is equal to 47.
grade9-maths.hint: Set the rule equal to 47 and solve for n.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3n + 2 = 47, so 3n = 45 and n = 15. The 15th term is 47. Checking: 3(15) + 2 = 47.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the volume of the cuboid. (answer in cm³)
grade9-maths.hint: Volume of a cuboid is length × width × height.
grade9-maths.explanation: 16 × 10 × 6 = 960 cm³.

grade9-maths.question: The cuboid is filled with water to three quarters of its height. Calculate the volume of water. (answer in cm³)
grade9-maths.hint: Three quarters of the volume you found in (a).
grade9-maths.explanation: ¾ of 960 = 720 cm³. (Or work with a height of 4.5 cm: 16 × 10 × 4.5 = 720.)

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the volume of the cylinder. Take π = 3.14. (answer in cm³)
grade9-maths.hint: Volume of a cylinder is π × r² × h.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3.14 × 10² × 5 = 3.14 × 100 × 5 = 1570 cm³.

grade9-maths.question: The cylinder is emptied into cups holding 157 cm³ each. How many cups can be filled? (answer in cups)
grade9-maths.hint: Divide the volume by the size of one cup.
grade9-maths.explanation: 1570 ÷ 157 = 10 cups.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the area of the trapezium. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: Area of a trapezium is ½ × (sum of the parallel sides) × height.
grade9-maths.explanation: ½ × (12 + 21) × 24 = ½ × 33 × 24 = 396 cm².

grade9-maths.question: A rectangle has the same area and a length of 33 cm. Find its width. (answer in cm)
grade9-maths.hint: Area divided by length gives the width.
grade9-maths.explanation: 396 ÷ 33 = 12 cm.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the length of the side opposite the 30° angle, to 1 decimal place. (answer in cm)
grade9-maths.hint: Use sin = opposite ÷ hypotenuse.
grade9-maths.explanation: sin 30° = opposite ÷ 10, so the side is 10 × sin 30° = 10 × 0.5 = 5.0 cm.

grade9-maths.question: Hence calculate the area of the triangle. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: Area of a triangle is ½ × base × perpendicular height, and the base is on the figure.
grade9-maths.explanation: The base is 8.7 cm and the perpendicular height is the 5.0 cm found in (a): ½ × 8.7 × 5.0 = 21.75 cm².

grade9-maths.question: How many pupils were asked altogether? (answer in pupils)
grade9-maths.hint: Add the height of every bar.

grade9-maths.question: Which sport is the mode?
grade9-maths.hint: The mode is the tallest bar.
grade9-maths.explanation: Football has the tallest bar, 8 pupils, so it is the mode.

grade9-maths.question: What percentage of the pupils chose swimming? (answer in %)
grade9-maths.hint: Write the swimming figure over the total, then multiply by 100.

grade9-maths.question:
Units usedRate per unit
First 50 unitsRs 7.50
Above 50 unitsRs 9.00
Calculate the cost of the first 50 units. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the number of units by the rate for that band.
grade9-maths.explanation: 50 × Rs 7.50 = Rs 375.

grade9-maths.question:
Units usedRate per unit
First 50 unitsRs 7.50
Above 50 unitsRs 9.00
A household uses 90 units in a month. Calculate the total cost. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: The first 50 units are charged at one rate and the remaining 40 at the other.
grade9-maths.explanation: First 50: Rs 375. Next 40: 40 × Rs 9.00 = Rs 360. Total = 375 + 360 = Rs 735.

grade9-maths.question: Share Rs 4 200 between Aisha and Ben in the ratio 3 : 4. How much does Aisha get? (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Find the value of one share first.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3 + 4 = 7 shares, and 4200 ÷ 7 = Rs 600 per share. Aisha gets 3 × 600 = Rs 1 800.

grade9-maths.question: How much more than Aisha does Ben receive? (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Ben has one more share than Aisha.
grade9-maths.explanation: Ben gets 4 × 600 = Rs 2 400, so he receives 2 400 − 1 800 = Rs 600 more.

grade9-maths.question: Factorise x2 + 2x − 15.
grade9-maths.hint: Find two numbers that multiply to −15 and add to +2.
grade9-maths.explanation: +5 and −3 multiply to −15 and add to +2, so x² + 2x − 15 = (x + 5)(x − 3).

grade9-maths.question: Hence solve x2 + 2x − 15 = 0, giving the positive root.
grade9-maths.hint: Each bracket can be zero.
grade9-maths.explanation: (x + 5)(x − 3) = 0 gives x = −5 or x = 3. The positive root is x = 3.

grade9-maths.question: Find the gradient of the line joining A (1, 3) and B (5, 11).
grade9-maths.hint: Gradient is the change in y divided by the change in x.
grade9-maths.explanation: (11 − 3) ÷ (5 − 1) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

grade9-maths.question: Find the y-intercept of the line AB.
grade9-maths.hint: Substitute one of the points into y = 2x + c.

grade9-maths.question: A bag holds 5 red, 7 blue and 8 green marbles. Find the probability of drawing a blue marble.
grade9-maths.hint: There are 20 marbles altogether.

grade9-maths.question: Find the probability that the marble is not green.
grade9-maths.hint: Either count the non-green marbles, or subtract from 1.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the total surface area of the cuboid. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: Three pairs of identical faces: 2(lw + lh + wh).

grade9-maths.question: The cuboid is painted at Rs 2 per cm². Find the cost, using your answer to (a). (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the surface area by the rate.

grade9-maths.question: Solve 5x − 3 > 12, giving your answer in the form x > k. Write down the value of k.
grade9-maths.hint: Add 3 to both sides, then divide by 5.
grade9-maths.explanation: 5x > 15, so x > 3.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the smallest integer that satisfies 5x − 3 > 12.
grade9-maths.hint: x > 3 does not include 3 itself.
grade9-maths.explanation: The inequality is strict, so x must be more than 3; the smallest integer is 4.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the volume of the tank. (answer in cm³)
grade9-maths.hint: Length × width × height.
grade9-maths.explanation: 60 × 30 × 30 = 54 000 cm³.

grade9-maths.question: Given that 1 litre = 1 000 cm³, express the volume in litres. (answer in litres)
grade9-maths.hint: Divide by 1 000.
grade9-maths.explanation: 54 000 ÷ 1 000 = 54 litres.

grade9-maths.question: Water flows in at 4.5 litres per minute. How long does the tank take to fill? (answer in minutes)
grade9-maths.hint: Divide the capacity by the rate.
grade9-maths.explanation: 54 ÷ 4.5 = 12 minutes.

grade9-maths.question: How many families were surveyed? (answer in families)
grade9-maths.hint: Add the bars.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the total number of children in all the families. (answer in children)
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply each number of children by how many families have that many, then add.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the mean number of children per family, to 2 decimal places.
grade9-maths.hint: Total children divided by number of families.
grade9-maths.explanation: 43 ÷ 25 = 1.72 children per family.

grade9-maths.question: A ladder leans against a wall as shown. Calculate the height it reaches up the wall, to 1 decimal place. (answer in m)
grade9-maths.hint: The height is opposite the 60° angle: use sin.
grade9-maths.explanation: sin 60° = h ÷ 6, so h = 6 × 0.866 = 5.196, which is 5.2 m to 1 d.p.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate how far the foot of the ladder is from the wall. (answer in m)
grade9-maths.hint: That distance is adjacent to the 60° angle: use cos.
grade9-maths.explanation: cos 60° = d ÷ 6, so d = 6 × 0.5 = 3 m.

grade9-maths.question: The ladder slips so that it now makes 45° with the ground. Calculate the height it reaches up the wall, to 1 decimal place. (answer in m)
grade9-maths.hint: Use sin again, with the new angle.
grade9-maths.explanation: 6 × sin 45° = 6 × 0.7071 = 4.243, which is 4.2 m to 1 d.p. - lower than before, because sin 45° is less than sin 60°.

grade9-maths.question:
Water usedRate per m³
First 20 m³Rs 12.50
Above 20 m³Rs 20.00
Calculate the charge for the first 20 m³ of water. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply by the first-band rate.

grade9-maths.question:
Water usedRate per m³
First 20 m³Rs 12.50
Above 20 m³Rs 20.00
A household uses 35 m³. Calculate the total charge before the fixed fee. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: The extra 15 m³ are charged at the higher rate.
grade9-maths.explanation: First 20: Rs 250. Next 15: 15 × Rs 20 = Rs 300. Total = Rs 550.

grade9-maths.question:
Water usedRate per m³
First 20 m³Rs 12.50
Above 20 m³Rs 20.00
A fixed service fee of Rs 90 is added. Calculate the final bill. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Add the fee to your answer for (b).

grade9-maths.question: Two pens and three books cost Rs 235; four pens and one book cost Rs 195. Taking p for the cost of a pen and b for a book, find p. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the second equation so that one letter cancels.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2p + 3b = 235 and 4p + b = 195. Multiplying the second by 3 gives 12p + 3b = 585. Subtracting the first: 10p = 350, so p = Rs 35.

grade9-maths.question: Find the cost of one book. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Substitute your value for a pen into either equation.

grade9-maths.question: In a class of 40 pupils, 22 study French and 18 study Spanish. 7 study both. How many study French only? (answer in pupils)
grade9-maths.hint: Take the overlap away from the French total.
grade9-maths.explanation: 22 − 7 = 15 pupils study French only.

grade9-maths.question: How many study neither language? (answer in pupils)
grade9-maths.hint: Add the three regions inside the circles, then subtract from 40.
grade9-maths.explanation: French only 15, both 7, Spanish only 18 − 7 = 11. That is 15 + 7 + 11 = 33, so 40 − 33 = 7 pupils study neither.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the volume of the cylindrical drum. Take π = 3.14. (answer in cm³)
grade9-maths.hint: π × r² × h.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3.14 × 10² × 15 = 4 710 cm³.

grade9-maths.question: Express the volume in litres, given 1 litre = 1 000 cm³. (answer in litres)
grade9-maths.hint: Divide by 1 000.
grade9-maths.explanation: 4 710 ÷ 1 000 = 4.71 litres.

grade9-maths.question: The drum is filled from a tap running at 0.3 litres per second. How long does it take, to the nearest second? (answer in seconds)
grade9-maths.hint: Capacity divided by rate.
grade9-maths.explanation: 4.71 ÷ 0.3 = 15.7, which is 16 seconds to the nearest second.

grade9-maths.question: Water costs Rs 4 per litre. Calculate the cost of one full drum, to the nearest rupee. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the capacity in litres by the rate.
grade9-maths.explanation: 4.71 × 4 = Rs 18.84, which is Rs 19 to the nearest rupee.

grade9-maths.question: How many matches were played? (answer in matches)
grade9-maths.hint: Add the bars.

grade9-maths.question: Find the modal number of goals. (answer in goals)
grade9-maths.hint: The tallest bar.
grade9-maths.explanation: 1 goal was scored in 6 matches, more than any other, so the mode is 1.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the total number of goals scored. (answer in goals)
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply each score by its frequency and add.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the mean number of goals per match. (answer in goals)
grade9-maths.hint: Total goals divided by number of matches.
grade9-maths.explanation: 40 ÷ 20 = 2 goals per match.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the area of the curved surface of the cylinder. Take π = 3.14. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: The curved surface is a rectangle 2πr long and h tall.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2 × 3.14 × 7 × 15 = 659.4 cm².

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the area of one circular end. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: π × r².

grade9-maths.question: Hence find the total surface area of the closed cylinder. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: The curved surface plus TWO ends.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the area of the trapezium-shaped garden. (answer in m²)
grade9-maths.hint: ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × height.
grade9-maths.explanation: ½ × (18 + 27) × 24 = ½ × 45 × 24 = 540 m².

grade9-maths.question: Grass seed covers 12 m² per bag. How many whole bags are needed? (answer in bags)
grade9-maths.hint: Divide the area by the coverage.
grade9-maths.explanation: 540 ÷ 12 = 45 bags exactly.

grade9-maths.question: Each bag costs Rs 185. Calculate the total cost. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the number of bags by the price.

grade9-maths.question: A worker earns Rs 285 per hour for a 40-hour week. Calculate the basic weekly pay. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Rate multiplied by hours.

grade9-maths.question: Overtime is paid at time and a half. Calculate the overtime rate per hour. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: One and a half times the basic rate.

grade9-maths.question: The worker does 6 hours of overtime. Calculate the overtime pay. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Overtime rate times overtime hours.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the total pay for the week. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Basic pay plus overtime pay.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the volume of the water tank. (answer in cm³)
grade9-maths.hint: Length × width × height.
grade9-maths.explanation: 80 × 60 × 30 = 144 000 cm³.

grade9-maths.question: Express its capacity in litres (1 litre = 1 000 cm³). (answer in litres)
grade9-maths.hint: Divide by 1 000.
grade9-maths.explanation: 144 000 ÷ 1 000 = 144 litres.

grade9-maths.question: The tank is two thirds full. Calculate the volume of water, in litres. (answer in litres)
grade9-maths.hint: Two thirds of the capacity.

grade9-maths.question: Water is drawn off at 8 litres per minute. How long until the tank is empty? (answer in minutes)
grade9-maths.hint: Divide the water present by the rate.
grade9-maths.explanation: 96 ÷ 8 = 12 minutes.

grade9-maths.question: How many pupils sat the test? (answer in pupils)
grade9-maths.hint: Add every bar.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the modal mark. (answer in marks)
grade9-maths.hint: The tallest bar.
grade9-maths.explanation: 3 marks was scored by 9 pupils, more than any other, so the mode is 3.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the total of all the marks. (answer in marks)
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply each mark by its frequency and add.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the mean mark, to 2 decimal places. (answer in marks)
grade9-maths.hint: Total marks divided by number of pupils.
grade9-maths.explanation: 91 ÷ 30 = 3.033..., which is 3.03 to 2 d.p.

grade9-maths.question: How many pupils scored more than the mean? (answer in pupils)
grade9-maths.hint: Count everyone whose mark is above 3.03.
grade9-maths.explanation: Marks of 4 (7 pupils) and 5 (4 pupils) are above 3.03, so 7 + 4 = 11 pupils.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the volume of the box. (answer in cm³)
grade9-maths.hint: Length × width × height.
grade9-maths.explanation: 20 × 15 × 12 = 3 600 cm³.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the total surface area of the box. (answer in cm²)
grade9-maths.hint: 2(lw + lh + wh).

grade9-maths.question: Card costs Rs 0.60 per cm². Calculate the cost of the card for one box. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the surface area by the price per cm².

grade9-maths.question: A shirt costs Rs 1 250. Its price is reduced by 12%. Calculate the reduction. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: 12% means 12 out of every 100.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the new price of the shirt. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Take the reduction off the original price.

grade9-maths.question: Express 3⁄8 as a decimal.
grade9-maths.hint: Divide 3 by 8.

grade9-maths.question: Express 3⁄8 as a percentage. (answer in %)
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the decimal by 100.

grade9-maths.question: A tank holds 640 litres. Calculate 3⁄8 of its capacity. (answer in litres)
grade9-maths.hint: Divide by 8, then multiply by 3.
grade9-maths.explanation: 640 ÷ 8 = 80, and 80 × 3 = 240 litres.

grade9-maths.question: A map has a scale of 1 : 50 000. Two towns are 8 cm apart on the map. Find the real distance in centimetres. (answer in cm)
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the map distance by the scale factor.

grade9-maths.question: Express that distance in kilometres. (answer in km)
grade9-maths.hint: There are 100 000 cm in a kilometre.

grade9-maths.question: A third town is 11 km from the first. How far apart are they on the map? (answer in cm)
grade9-maths.hint: Turn the kilometres into centimetres first, then divide by 50 000.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> + <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>4</sub>, giving your answer as a fraction in its lowest terms.
grade9-maths.hint: Use a common denominator of 12.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> − <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>4</sub>.
grade9-maths.hint: The same common denominator.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> × <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>4</sub>, in its lowest terms.
grade9-maths.hint: Multiply the tops and the bottoms, then simplify.

grade9-maths.question: A recipe for 4 people needs 600 g of rice. How much is needed for 6 people? (answer in g)
grade9-maths.hint: Find the amount for one person first.
grade9-maths.explanation: 600 ÷ 4 = 150 g each, so 6 people need 6 × 150 = 900 g.

grade9-maths.question: Rice is sold in 2 kg bags. How many whole bags are needed for 6 people? (answer in bag)
grade9-maths.hint: 900 g is less than 2 kg.
grade9-maths.explanation: 900 g is under 2 000 g, so one bag is enough.

grade9-maths.question: How many people could be fed from one 2 kg bag? (answer in people)
grade9-maths.hint: Divide 2 000 g by the amount one person needs, then round down.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2 000 ÷ 150 = 13.33, and you cannot feed a third of a person, so 13.

grade9-maths.question: A sum of Rs 25 000 is invested at 6% simple interest per year. Calculate the interest earned in one year. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: 6% of the sum invested.

grade9-maths.question: Calculate the interest earned in 3 years. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Simple interest is the same every year.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the total amount after 3 years. (answer in Rs)
grade9-maths.hint: Add the interest to the original sum.

grade9-maths.question: For how many whole years must it be invested for the interest to exceed Rs 10 000? (answer in years)
grade9-maths.hint: Divide 10 000 by the yearly interest and round up.
grade9-maths.explanation: 10 000 ÷ 1 500 = 6.67, so after 6 years the interest is Rs 9 000 and after 7 it is Rs 10 500. The answer is 7 years.

grade9-maths.question: A car travels 210 km in 3 hours. Calculate its average speed. (answer in km/h)
grade9-maths.hint: Speed is distance divided by time.
grade9-maths.explanation: 210 ÷ 3 = 70 km/h.

grade9-maths.question: At the same speed, how far would it travel in 5 hours? (answer in km)
grade9-maths.hint: Speed multiplied by time.
grade9-maths.explanation: 70 × 5 = 350 km.

grade9-maths.question: How long would a journey of 490 km take at that speed? Give your answer in hours. (answer in hours)
grade9-maths.hint: Distance divided by speed.
grade9-maths.explanation: 490 ÷ 70 = 7 hours.

grade9-maths.question: The car uses 1 litre of fuel every 14 km. How many litres does the 490 km journey use? (answer in litres)
grade9-maths.hint: Divide the distance by the distance per litre.
grade9-maths.explanation: 490 ÷ 14 = 35 litres.

grade9-maths.question: The diagram shows the points A (1, 1) and B (5, 4). Write down the x-component of the vector AB.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract the x of A from the x of B.
grade9-maths.explanation: 5 − 1 = 4.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the y-component of AB.
grade9-maths.hint: Subtract the y of A from the y of B.
grade9-maths.explanation: 4 − 1 = 3.

grade9-maths.question: Given a with components (3, 4), calculate its magnitude.
grade9-maths.hint: Use Pythagoras on the two components.
grade9-maths.explanation: √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5.

grade9-maths.question: Given b with components (6, 8), calculate its magnitude.
grade9-maths.hint: The same method.

grade9-maths.question: b is a multiple of a. Write down the value of k for which b = ka.
grade9-maths.hint: Compare the components.
grade9-maths.explanation: 6 = 2 × 3 and 8 = 2 × 4, so k = 2.

grade9-maths.question: A point P (2, 3) is translated by the vector with components (4, −1). Write down the x-coordinate of the image.
grade9-maths.hint: Add the x-component to the x-coordinate.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the y-coordinate of the image.
grade9-maths.hint: Add the y-component, remembering it is negative.

grade9-maths.question: The image is then translated back to P. Write down the x-component of that second translation.
grade9-maths.hint: It must undo the first translation.
grade9-maths.explanation: The reverse of (4, −1) is (−4, 1), so the x-component is −4.

grade9-maths.question: Given a = (2, 5) and b = (3, −1), find the x-component of a + b.
grade9-maths.hint: Add the x parts.

grade9-maths.question: Find the y-component of a + b.
grade9-maths.hint: Add the y parts.

grade9-maths.question: Find the x-component of 2a − b.
grade9-maths.hint: Double a first, then subtract b.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2 × 2 = 4, and 4 − 3 = 1.

grade9-maths.question: Find the y-component of 2a − b.
grade9-maths.hint: The same, taking care with the minus.
grade9-maths.explanation: 2 × 5 = 10, and 10 − (−1) = 11.

grade9-maths.question: A line passes through A (0, 2) and B (4, 10). Find its gradient.
grade9-maths.hint: Change in y over change in x.
grade9-maths.explanation: (10 − 2) ÷ (4 − 0) = 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

grade9-maths.question: Write down the y-intercept.
grade9-maths.hint: A has x = 0, so it is on the y-axis.
grade9-maths.explanation: A is (0, 2), so the y-intercept is 2.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of y when x = 7.
grade9-maths.hint: Use y = 2x + 2.

grade9-maths.question: Find the value of x when y = 0.
grade9-maths.hint: Set y to zero and solve.
grade9-maths.explanation: 0 = 2x + 2 gives x = −1.
