grade9-physics.hint: Not every location has a suitable river.
grade9-physics.explanation: Hydroelectric stations need a large river and suitable valley; solar panels can be installed on rooftops and flat land almost anywhere.

grade9-physics.question:
A table shows the carbon emissions of five electricity sources.
SourceCO₂ per kWh
Coal820 g
Gas490 g
Nuclear12 g
Wind11 g
Solar45 g
Which two sources produce the least CO₂ per kWh?
grade9-physics.hint: Find the two smallest values in the table.
grade9-physics.explanation: From the figures: wind (11 g) and nuclear (12 g) have the two lowest CO₂ emissions per kWh.

grade9-physics.question: Which of these is a vector quantity?
grade9-physics.hint: A vector needs a direction as well as a size.
grade9-physics.explanation: Velocity has both a size and a direction, so it is a vector. Speed, distance and time have size only.

grade9-physics.question: Which of these is a scalar quantity?
grade9-physics.hint: A scalar has size only, with no direction.
grade9-physics.explanation: Distance has a size but no direction, so it is a scalar. The other three all carry a direction.

grade9-physics.question: What is the difference between a scalar and a vector?
options: A vector has a direction as well as a size
A scalar is always measured in metres
A scalar can never be negative
A vector is always larger than a scalar
grade9-physics.answer: A vector has a direction as well as a size
acceptableAnswers: A vector has a direction as well as a size
grade9-physics.hint: Think about what extra information a vector carries.
grade9-physics.explanation: A scalar is fully described by a size; a vector needs a direction too.

grade9-physics.question: A pupil walks 40 m east, then 40 m back west to the starting point. What is the total distance travelled?
grade9-physics.hint: Distance counts every metre walked, whichever way.
grade9-physics.explanation: Distance is the whole path length: 40 + 40 = 80 m.

grade9-physics.question: A pupil walks 40 m east, then 40 m back west to the starting point. What is the displacement?
grade9-physics.hint: Displacement is measured from start to finish.
grade9-physics.explanation: Displacement is the straight line from start to finish; they end where they began, so it is zero.

grade9-physics.question: A car drives 300 m north and then 400 m east. Its distance travelled is 700 m. Why is its displacement smaller than that?
options: Displacement ignores the first part of a journey
Displacement is measured in different units
Displacement is the straight line from start to finish
Displacement is always half of the distance
grade9-physics.answer: Displacement is the straight line from start to finish
acceptableAnswers: Displacement is the straight line from start to finish
grade9-physics.hint: The path is bent; the displacement is not.
grade9-physics.explanation: Displacement is the direct line between the start and finish, which is shorter than a path that changes direction.

grade9-physics.question: What is the SI unit of speed?
grade9-physics.hint: Speed is a distance divided by a time.
grade9-physics.explanation: Speed is distance divided by time, so its unit is metres per second (m/s).

grade9-physics.question: What is the difference between speed and velocity?
options: Speed is measured over a longer time
Speed applies only to objects that are slowing down
Velocity states the direction as well as the size
Velocity is always the larger of the two
grade9-physics.answer: Velocity states the direction as well as the size
acceptableAnswers: Velocity states the direction as well as the size
grade9-physics.hint: One of them is a vector.
grade9-physics.explanation: Speed is a scalar; velocity is the same measurement with a direction attached.

grade9-physics.question: A car goes once round a circular track and returns to the start in 60 s. What is its average velocity?
options: The same as its average speed
It cannot be worked out without the radius
Zero, because the displacement is zero
grade9-physics.answer: Zero, because the displacement is zero
acceptableAnswers: Zero, because the displacement is zero
grade9-physics.hint: Average velocity uses displacement, not distance.
grade9-physics.explanation: The car finishes where it started, so its displacement is zero and its average velocity is zero - even though its speed was not.

grade9-physics.question: What is the SI unit of acceleration?
grade9-physics.hint: Acceleration is a change of speed divided by a time.
grade9-physics.explanation: Acceleration is measured in metres per second squared (m/s²).

grade9-physics.question: What does an acceleration of 3 m/s² mean?
options: The object travels 3 m in total
The speed increases by 3 m/s every second
The object travels 3 m every second
grade9-physics.answer: The speed increases by 3 m/s every second
acceptableAnswers: The speed increases by 3 m/s every second
grade9-physics.hint: Acceleration is a change of speed each second.
grade9-physics.explanation: An acceleration of 3 m/s² means the speed rises by 3 m/s in each second that passes.

grade9-physics.question: A car is slowing down. What can be said about its acceleration?
options: It is zero, because the car is still moving
It is negative, because the speed is decreasing
It cannot be worked out for a slowing car
It is positive, because the car is still moving forward
grade9-physics.answer: It is negative, because the speed is decreasing
acceptableAnswers: It is negative, because the speed is decreasing
grade9-physics.hint: A falling speed is a negative change of speed.
grade9-physics.explanation: Slowing down is a negative change of speed each second, which is a negative acceleration (a deceleration).

grade9-physics.question: What does the speed-time graph shown tell you about the motion?
options: The object is speeding up steadily
The object is not moving at all
The object moves at a constant speed
The object is slowing down quite steadily
grade9-physics.answer: The object moves at a constant speed
acceptableAnswers: The object moves at a constant speed
grade9-physics.hint: Look at whether the line rises, falls or stays level.
grade9-physics.explanation: A horizontal line on a speed-time graph means the speed does not change, so the object moves at a constant speed.

grade9-physics.question: What does the speed-time graph shown tell you about the motion?
options: The object stays at the same place
The object moves at a constant speed
The object is slowing down steadily
The object is speeding up steadily
grade9-physics.answer: The object is speeding up steadily
acceptableAnswers: The object is speeding up steadily
grade9-physics.hint: Look at whether the line rises, falls or stays level.
grade9-physics.explanation: A straight line rising to the right means the speed increases evenly, so the object accelerates steadily.

grade9-physics.question: What does the speed-time graph shown tell you about the motion?
options: The object is slowing down steadily
The object is speeding up steadily
The object moves at a constant speed
grade9-physics.answer: The object is slowing down steadily
acceptableAnswers: The object is slowing down steadily
grade9-physics.hint: Look at whether the line rises, falls or stays level.
grade9-physics.explanation: A straight line falling to the right means the speed drops evenly, so the object decelerates until it stops.

grade9-physics.question: Read the graph shown. What is the speed at 4 s?
grade9-physics.hint: Go up from 4 on the time axis to the line, then across.
grade9-physics.explanation: The line sits level at 8 on the speed axis, so at 4 s the speed is 8 m/s.

grade9-physics.question: Read the graph shown. What is happening between 2 s and 4 s?
grade9-physics.hint: Look only at the middle section of the line.
grade9-physics.explanation: Between 2 s and 4 s the line is horizontal, so the speed is unchanged over that interval.

grade9-physics.question: On the graph shown, which section describes the object slowing to a stop?
options: No section of this graph shows slowing down
The last section, from 4 s to 6 s
The middle section, from 2 s to 4 s
The first section, from 0 s to 2 s
grade9-physics.answer: The last section, from 4 s to 6 s
acceptableAnswers: The last section, from 4 s to 6 s
grade9-physics.hint: Find the part of the line that falls to zero.
grade9-physics.explanation: The final section falls from 8 m/s to 0 m/s, which is the object slowing to a stop.

grade9-physics.question: On a speed-time graph, what does a horizontal line lying on the time axis mean?
options: The object moves at a steady speed
grade9-physics.hint: The speed value being read off is zero.
grade9-physics.explanation: A line along the time axis means the speed is zero throughout, so the object is not moving.

grade9-physics.question: Which equation gives the speed of an object?
grade9-physics.hint: Metres per second is metres divided by seconds.
grade9-physics.explanation: Speed is the distance travelled divided by the time taken.

grade9-physics.question: A runner covers 100 m in 20 s. Calculate the average speed, in m/s.
grade9-physics.hint: Speed = distance ÷ time.

grade9-physics.question: A car travels 240 m in 12 s. Calculate the average speed, in m/s.
grade9-physics.hint: Speed = distance ÷ time.

grade9-physics.question: A cyclist travels at 6 m/s for 30 s. Calculate the distance covered, in metres.
grade9-physics.hint: Rearrange to distance = speed × time.

grade9-physics.question: A bus travels 900 m at an average speed of 15 m/s. Calculate the time taken, in seconds.
grade9-physics.hint: Rearrange to time = distance ÷ speed.

grade9-physics.question: A car speeds up from 4 m/s to 20 m/s in 8 s. Calculate its acceleration, in m/s².
grade9-physics.hint: Acceleration = change in speed ÷ time.

grade9-physics.question: A trolley starting from rest reaches 12 m/s in 4 s. Calculate its acceleration, in m/s².
grade9-physics.hint: Starting from rest means the first speed is 0.

grade9-physics.question: Read the graph shown. What is the speed, in m/s, at 3 s?
grade9-physics.hint: Go up from 3 on the time axis to the line, then across.
grade9-physics.explanation: The line rises evenly from 0 to 12 m/s over 6 s, so at 3 s it is halfway: 6 m/s.

grade9-physics.question: Read the graph shown. What is the acceleration, in m/s²?
grade9-physics.hint: Acceleration = change in speed ÷ time taken.
grade9-physics.explanation: The speed rises from 0 to 12 m/s in 6 s, so the acceleration is 12 / 6 = 2 m/s².

grade9-physics.question: A pupil walks 25 m north, then 25 m south back to the start. State the displacement, in metres.
grade9-physics.hint: Displacement is measured from start to finish.
grade9-physics.explanation: They finish where they started, so the displacement is 0 m.

grade9-physics.question: A train covers 3000 m in 150 s. Calculate its average speed, in m/s.
grade9-physics.hint: Speed = distance ÷ time.

grade9-physics.question: Give the term for a quantity that has a size but no direction.
grade9-physics.hint: The opposite of a vector.
grade9-physics.explanation: A scalar has magnitude only, with no direction.

grade9-physics.question: Give the term for a quantity that has both a size and a direction.
grade9-physics.hint: The opposite of a scalar.
grade9-physics.explanation: A vector has both magnitude and direction.

grade9-physics.question: Give the term for the straight-line separation of the finishing point from the starting point.
grade9-physics.hint: It is the vector partner of distance.
grade9-physics.explanation: Displacement is the straight line from start to finish, with a direction.

grade9-physics.question: Give the term for the rate at which the speed of an object changes.
grade9-physics.hint: It is measured in metres per second squared.
grade9-physics.explanation: Acceleration is the change of speed per second.

grade9-physics.question: State what a horizontal line on a speed-time graph tells you about the speed.
grade9-physics.hint: Look at whether the value being read off changes.
grade9-physics.explanation: A horizontal line means the speed stays the same throughout that interval.

grade9-physics.question: What is the difference between a scalar and a vector quantity?
options: A scalar has direction only; a vector has magnitude only
A scalar has magnitude only; a vector has both magnitude and direction
grade9-physics.answer: A scalar has magnitude only; a vector has both magnitude and direction
acceptableAnswers: A scalar has magnitude only; a vector has both magnitude and direction
grade9-physics.hint: Think about what information each type of quantity carries.
grade9-physics.explanation: A scalar is fully described by its magnitude (e.g. 5 kg, 30 °C); a vector also needs a direction (e.g. 10 m/s North).

grade9-physics.question: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
grade9-physics.hint: Scalar quantities have size but no direction.
grade9-physics.explanation: Distance is the total path length with no direction specified; it is a scalar. Displacement, velocity and acceleration are vectors.

grade9-physics.question: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
grade9-physics.hint: Vector quantities have both magnitude and direction.
grade9-physics.explanation: Velocity has both magnitude (speed) and direction (e.g. 30 m/s East); speed, time and temperature are scalars.

grade9-physics.question: A student writes: “The car travelled at 60 km/h.” Is this a speed or a velocity?
options: Speed, because no direction is given
Neither, because km/h is not an SI unit
Velocity, because it is a fast-moving object
grade9-physics.answer: Speed, because no direction is given
acceptableAnswers: Speed, because no direction is given
grade9-physics.hint: Velocity requires a direction.
grade9-physics.explanation: 60 km/h gives only the magnitude of motion, not a direction; it is therefore a speed (scalar), not a velocity (vector).

grade9-physics.question: Which set of quantities are ALL scalars?
grade9-physics.hint: Each one needs to be checked for direction.
grade9-physics.explanation: Mass, time, distance and speed are all scalars; they need no direction. Force, velocity, displacement and acceleration are vectors.

grade9-physics.question: Which set of quantities are ALL vectors?
grade9-physics.hint: All four must have both magnitude and direction.
grade9-physics.explanation: Force, velocity, acceleration and displacement each require a direction to be fully described; they are all vectors.

grade9-physics.question: A car drives at 50 km/h due North. What type of quantity is this 50 km/h North?
grade9-physics.hint: “Due North” provides the direction, making it a vector.
grade9-physics.explanation: Speed + direction = velocity. “50 km/h due North” is a velocity.

grade9-physics.question: A runner completes a circular track and returns to the starting point. They ran a total distance of 400 m. What is their displacement?
options: 400 m in the direction they ran
Zero, because they returned to the start
grade9-physics.answer: Zero, because they returned to the start
acceptableAnswers: Zero, because they returned to the start
grade9-physics.hint: Displacement is the straight-line distance from start to finish.
grade9-physics.explanation: Displacement is the change in position from start to finish. Since the runner is back at the start, the displacement is zero.

grade9-physics.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a vector quantity with its scalar equivalent?
grade9-physics.hint: A vector and its scalar pair measure the same physical concept but one includes direction.
grade9-physics.explanation: Velocity (vector) and speed (scalar) both measure how fast an object moves; velocity specifies direction, speed does not.

grade9-physics.question: A force of 5 N acts East and a force of 5 N acts West on an object. What is the resultant force?
grade9-physics.hint: Equal and opposite vectors cancel.
grade9-physics.explanation: Adding 5 N East and 5 N West: 5 − 5 = 0 N. The resultant force is zero.

grade9-physics.question: Temperature and mass are both scalar quantities. Which statement is correct?
options: They both have magnitude and direction
They have magnitude but no direction
Temperature is a vector because it increases in one direction
Mass is a vector because it describes weight
grade9-physics.answer: They have magnitude but no direction
acceptableAnswers: They have magnitude but no direction
grade9-physics.hint: Scalars need only a number and a unit.
grade9-physics.explanation: Temperature (e.g. 25 °C) and mass (e.g. 3 kg) are fully described by magnitude alone; no direction is needed.

grade9-physics.question: A person walks 3 m East and then 4 m North. What is the magnitude of their displacement?
grade9-physics.hint: Use Pythagoras’ theorem for perpendicular displacements.
grade9-physics.explanation: √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 m.

grade9-physics.question: Energy is measured in joules. Is energy a scalar or a vector?
options: Vector, because it is measured in joules
Vector, because it can be positive or negative
Scalar, because energy has no direction
Scalar, because it is always positive
grade9-physics.answer: Scalar, because energy has no direction
acceptableAnswers: Scalar, because energy has no direction
grade9-physics.hint: Energy has magnitude only; it does not point in any direction.
grade9-physics.explanation: Energy is a scalar quantity; 100 J of kinetic energy has no direction (though the velocity that produced it does).

grade9-physics.question: A student is asked whether acceleration is a scalar or vector. What is the correct answer?
options: Vector, because acceleration has both magnitude and direction
Scalar, because it is measured in m/s²
Vector, but only when the acceleration is negative (deceleration)
Scalar, because it only tells you how much faster an object is going
grade9-physics.answer: Vector, because acceleration has both magnitude and direction
acceptableAnswers: Vector, because acceleration has both magnitude and direction
grade9-physics.hint: Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time; since velocity is a vector, so is acceleration.
grade9-physics.explanation: Acceleration describes the rate of change of velocity (a vector), so it must also be a vector, with both magnitude and direction.

grade9-physics.question: What is distance?
options: The change in speed of an object
The total length of the path travelled, regardless of direction
The straight-line separation between start and finish
grade9-physics.answer: The total length of the path travelled, regardless of direction
acceptableAnswers: The total length of the path travelled, regardless of direction
grade9-physics.hint: Distance follows the path.
grade9-physics.explanation: Distance is the total path length; it is a scalar and includes every part of the route, no matter how curved.

grade9-physics.question: What is displacement?
options: The speed in a given direction
The total length of the path travelled
The straight-line distance from the starting point to the ending point, including direction
grade9-physics.answer: The straight-line distance from the starting point to the ending point, including direction
acceptableAnswers: The straight-line distance from the starting point to the ending point, including direction
grade9-physics.hint: Displacement is the shortest path from start to finish.
grade9-physics.explanation: Displacement is the vector from the initial position to the final position; it is the straight-line distance including direction.

grade9-physics.question: A student walks 8 m East, then 8 m West along a straight road. What is the distance travelled and the displacement?
grade9-physics.hint: Distance adds all paths; displacement is the net change in position.
grade9-physics.explanation: Total path = 8 + 8 = 16 m (distance). Start and finish are the same point, so displacement = 0 m.

grade9-physics.question: A car travels 60 km North and then 80 km East. What is its displacement from the start?
grade9-physics.hint: Use Pythagoras: √(60² + 80²) = 100 km.
grade9-physics.explanation: √(60² + 80²) = √(3 600 + 6 400) = √10 000 = 100 km, in a NE direction.

grade9-physics.question: A track is a rectangle 100 m by 60 m. A runner completes one full lap. What is the distance travelled and the displacement?
grade9-physics.hint: One full lap returns to the start.
grade9-physics.explanation: Perimeter = 2(100 + 60) = 320 m (distance). The runner returns to the starting point, so displacement = 0 m.

grade9-physics.question: A ship sails 50 km due South. What is the magnitude of its displacement?
grade9-physics.hint: Displacement = straight-line change in position.
grade9-physics.explanation: The ship moved 50 km in a straight line South; its displacement is 50 km South.

grade9-physics.question: A ball rolls 4 m North, then 3 m East. What is the magnitude of its displacement?
grade9-physics.hint: Pythagoras: √(4² + 3²).
grade9-physics.explanation: √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5 m.

grade9-physics.question: Why is distance always greater than or equal to displacement?
options: Displacement adds directions; distance subtracts them
Distance includes the full path length; displacement is only the shortest straight line between start and finish
Distance can be negative but displacement cannot
Distance is always measured in metres; displacement is measured in kilometres
grade9-physics.answer: Distance includes the full path length; displacement is only the shortest straight line between start and finish
acceptableAnswers: Distance includes the full path length; displacement is only the shortest straight line between start and finish
grade9-physics.hint: The straight line is the shortest possible path.
grade9-physics.explanation: The straight line (displacement) is never longer than the actual path (distance); they are equal only when the path is already a straight line.

grade9-physics.question: Which of the following is measured in metres AND is a vector?
grade9-physics.hint: Displacement has magnitude (metres) and direction.
grade9-physics.explanation: Displacement is measured in metres and has a direction; distance is in metres but is a scalar.

grade9-physics.question: A student walks 5 m East, then 5 m North, then 5 m West. What is their displacement from the start?
grade9-physics.hint: Work out the net East-West and net North-South components.
grade9-physics.explanation: East − West = 5 − 5 = 0 m; North = 5 m. Displacement = 5 m North.

grade9-physics.question: What is the SI unit of both distance and displacement?
grade9-physics.hint: Both measure length; the SI unit of length is the metre.
grade9-physics.explanation: Distance and displacement are both measured in metres (m) in the SI system.

grade9-physics.question: A car drives 300 km around a mountain road. The straight-line distance between start and finish is 100 km. What is its displacement?
options: 100 km in the direction from start to finish
0 km because it went around a mountain
grade9-physics.answer: 100 km in the direction from start to finish
acceptableAnswers: 100 km in the direction from start to finish
grade9-physics.hint: Displacement is the straight-line vector from start to finish.
grade9-physics.explanation: Regardless of the route, the displacement is 100 km from the start to the finish point.

grade9-physics.question: At the end of a race, the winner is 400 m from the starting line (straight-line). She ran 420 m on a curved track. What is the distance she ran?
grade9-physics.hint: Distance is the total path length, not the straight-line separation.
grade9-physics.explanation: The runner ran 420 m along the curved track; that is the distance. The 400 m is the magnitude of her displacement.

grade9-physics.question: A pendulum swings 12 cm to the right and 12 cm back to the centre. What is the total distance travelled and the displacement from the centre?
grade9-physics.hint: The pendulum returns to its starting position.
grade9-physics.explanation: The bob travels 12 cm out and 12 cm back = 24 cm total distance. It returns to the centre, so displacement = 0.

grade9-physics.question: What is the formula for average speed?
grade9-physics.hint: Average speed uses total distance and total time.
grade9-physics.explanation: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. (Average velocity = displacement ÷ time.)

grade9-physics.question: What is the SI unit of speed?
grade9-physics.hint: The SI unit of distance is m; the SI unit of time is s.
grade9-physics.explanation: The SI unit of speed is metres per second (m/s).

grade9-physics.question: A car travels 360 km in 4 hours. What is its average speed in km/h?
grade9-physics.hint: Average speed = distance ÷ time.
grade9-physics.explanation: 360 ÷ 4 = 90 km/h.

grade9-physics.question: A cyclist travels 1 500 m in 5 minutes. What is her average speed in m/s?
grade9-physics.hint: Convert minutes to seconds: 5 min = 300 s.

grade9-physics.question: A train travels at 54 km/h. Convert this speed to m/s.
grade9-physics.hint: Divide by 3.6 to convert km/h to m/s.

grade9-physics.question: How long does it take a bus to travel 2 400 m at an average speed of 12 m/s?
grade9-physics.hint: Time = distance ÷ speed.

grade9-physics.question: How far does a runner travel in 30 seconds at 8 m/s?
grade9-physics.hint: Distance = speed × time.

grade9-physics.question: A car has an average speed of 20 m/s for the first 100 s and 30 m/s for the next 50 s. What is the overall average speed for the whole journey?
grade9-physics.hint: Overall average speed = total distance ÷ total time.
grade9-physics.explanation: Distance 1 = 20 × 100 = 2 000 m. Distance 2 = 30 × 50 = 1 500 m. Total d = 3 500 m, total t = 150 s. Average = 3 500 ÷ 150 ≈ 23.3 m/s.

grade9-physics.question: A car's speedometer reads 100 km/h. The car is travelling in a straight line East. Express this as a velocity.
grade9-physics.hint: Velocity requires magnitude and direction.
grade9-physics.explanation: The velocity is 100 km/h East; the direction is essential. (100 ÷ 3.6 ≈ 27.8 m/s.)

grade9-physics.question: Two cars travel on the same road at the same speed of 30 m/s but in opposite directions. Do they have the same velocity?
options: No, because their masses are different
No, because their directions are different
Yes, because their speeds are the same
Yes, because they are on the same road
grade9-physics.answer: No, because their directions are different
acceptableAnswers: No, because their directions are different
grade9-physics.hint: Velocity = speed + direction. Same speed, different direction means different velocity.
grade9-physics.explanation: Velocity is a vector; the two cars have the same speed but opposite directions, so they have different velocities.

grade9-physics.question: A stone is dropped and falls 20 m in 2 s. What is its average speed?
grade9-physics.hint: Average speed = distance ÷ time.
grade9-physics.explanation: 20 ÷ 2 = 10 m/s.

grade9-physics.question: A car travels 300 m at 20 m/s, stops for 30 s, then travels 200 m at 25 m/s. What is the average speed for the whole journey?
grade9-physics.hint: Total distance ÷ total time.
grade9-physics.explanation: Time 1 = 300/20 = 15 s. Stop = 30 s. Time 3 = 200/25 = 8 s. Total t = 53 s. Total d = 500 m. Average = 500/53 ≈ 9.43 m/s ≈ 9.4 m/s. (Nearest option is 10 m/s.)

grade9-physics.question: A sound wave travels at 340 m/s. How long does it take to travel 1 700 m?
grade9-physics.hint: Time = distance ÷ speed.

grade9-physics.question: A satellite orbits Earth at 7 800 m/s. How far does it travel in 90 minutes?
grade9-physics.hint: Convert 90 min to seconds: 90 × 60 = 5 400 s.

grade9-physics.question: What is acceleration?
options: The total distance travelled per unit time
The rate of change of distance
The rate of change of velocity (or speed)
grade9-physics.answer: The rate of change of velocity (or speed)
acceptableAnswers: The rate of change of velocity (or speed)
grade9-physics.hint: Acceleration = (change in velocity) ÷ time.
grade9-physics.explanation: Acceleration is the change in velocity per unit time; a = Δv ÷ t.

grade9-physics.question: What is the formula for acceleration?
grade9-physics.hint: u = initial speed, v = final speed, t = time.
grade9-physics.explanation: Acceleration = (final velocity − initial velocity) ÷ time = (v − u) ÷ t.

grade9-physics.question: What is the SI unit of acceleration?
grade9-physics.hint: Acceleration = velocity ÷ time = (m/s) ÷ s = m/s².
grade9-physics.explanation: The SI unit of acceleration is metres per second squared (m/s²).

grade9-physics.question: A car increases its speed from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 5 s. What is its acceleration?
grade9-physics.hint: a = (v − u) ÷ t.
grade9-physics.explanation: a = (30 − 10) ÷ 5 = 20 ÷ 5 = 4 m/s².

grade9-physics.question: A train slows from 25 m/s to 5 m/s in 10 s. What is its deceleration?
grade9-physics.hint: Deceleration = (change in speed) ÷ time.
grade9-physics.explanation: Deceleration = (25 − 5) ÷ 10 = 20 ÷ 10 = 2 m/s².

grade9-physics.question: A motorcyclist starts from rest and reaches 18 m/s in 6 s. What is the acceleration?
grade9-physics.hint: a = (v − u) ÷ t; u = 0.
grade9-physics.explanation: a = (18 − 0) ÷ 6 = 3 m/s².

grade9-physics.question: A stone is dropped from rest. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is its speed after 3 s?
grade9-physics.hint: v = u + at; u = 0, a = 10 m/s², t = 3 s.

grade9-physics.question: A car decelerates from 20 m/s to rest in 4 s. What is the deceleration?
grade9-physics.hint: Deceleration = (u − v) ÷ t.
grade9-physics.explanation: (20 − 0) ÷ 4 = 5 m/s².

grade9-physics.question: An aeroplane accelerates at 3 m/s² for 20 s from rest. What speed does it reach?
grade9-physics.hint: v = u + at.

grade9-physics.question: A ball is thrown upward at 15 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s² (deceleration upward), how long does it take to stop?
grade9-physics.hint: Time to stop: a = 10 m/s² decelerating; t = u ÷ a.
grade9-physics.explanation: t = 15 ÷ 10 = 1.5 s.

grade9-physics.question: A car has a constant acceleration of 2.5 m/s². Starting from 8 m/s, what is its speed after 6 s?
grade9-physics.hint: v = u + at.

grade9-physics.question: What does a negative value of acceleration indicate?
options: The object is moving at constant speed
grade9-physics.hint: Negative acceleration is opposite to the direction of motion.
grade9-physics.explanation: A negative acceleration means the velocity is decreasing; the object is decelerating (slowing down).

grade9-physics.question: A racing car accelerates from 0 to 60 m/s in 3 s. What is its acceleration?
grade9-physics.hint: a = (v − u) ÷ t.
grade9-physics.explanation: (60 − 0) ÷ 3 = 20 m/s².

grade9-physics.question: An object moves at constant velocity. What is its acceleration?
grade9-physics.hint: Constant velocity means no change in velocity.
grade9-physics.explanation: Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time. If velocity is constant, the change is zero, so a = 0.

grade9-physics.question: A bus slows from 16 m/s to 4 m/s in 6 s. How far does it travel during this deceleration?
grade9-physics.hint: Use average speed × time, or the kinematic equation.
grade9-physics.explanation: Average speed = (16 + 4)/2 = 10 m/s. Distance = 10 × 6 = 60 m.

grade9-physics.question:
Look at the graph.
What does the shape of the line indicate about the object’s motion?
options: The object is moving at constant speed
The object is accelerating uniformly (constant acceleration)
grade9-physics.answer: The object is accelerating uniformly (constant acceleration)
acceptableAnswers: The object is accelerating uniformly (constant acceleration)
grade9-physics.hint: A straight line going upward on a speed-time graph means uniform acceleration.
grade9-physics.explanation: A straight line with a positive slope on a speed-time graph indicates constant (uniform) acceleration.

grade9-physics.question:
Look at the graph.
What does the line indicate?
options: The object is moving at constant speed (zero acceleration)
grade9-physics.answer: The object is moving at constant speed (zero acceleration)
acceptableAnswers: The object is moving at constant speed (zero acceleration)
grade9-physics.hint: A horizontal line means speed is not changing.
grade9-physics.explanation: A horizontal line on a speed-time graph means the speed is constant and acceleration is zero.

grade9-physics.question:
Look at the graph.
What does this line represent?
options: The object is moving at constant speed and then stopping
The object is accelerating and then slowing
The object is decelerating uniformly to rest
grade9-physics.answer: The object is decelerating uniformly to rest
acceptableAnswers: The object is decelerating uniformly to rest
grade9-physics.hint: A straight line going downward to the x-axis means deceleration.
grade9-physics.explanation: A straight line with a negative slope (falling to zero speed) on a speed-time graph represents uniform deceleration.

grade9-physics.question:
Look at the graph.
The object starts from rest and reaches 16 m/s in 8 s. What is its acceleration?
grade9-physics.hint: Acceleration = gradient = rise ÷ run.
grade9-physics.explanation: Gradient = (16 − 0) ÷ (8 − 0) = 16 ÷ 8 = 2 m/s².

grade9-physics.question:
Look at the graph.
What is the distance travelled in the first 8 s?
grade9-physics.hint: Distance = area under the speed-time graph (a triangle here).
grade9-physics.explanation: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 8 × 16 = 64 m.

grade9-physics.question:
Look at the graph.
What is the distance travelled in 10 s at 12 m/s?
grade9-physics.hint: Distance = area under the graph = rectangle area.
grade9-physics.explanation: Area = 12 × 10 = 120 m.

grade9-physics.question:
Look at the three-phase graph.
In which phase is the object stationary?
options: It is never stationary; but the third phase shows deceleration to 0
grade9-physics.answer: It is never stationary; but the third phase shows deceleration to 0
acceptableAnswers: It is never stationary; but the third phase shows deceleration to 0
grade9-physics.hint: Find the segment where the line is on the x-axis.
grade9-physics.explanation: The graph ends at zero speed after 10 s; the object decelerates to rest in the third phase. It is never at rest during the journey until t = 10 s.

grade9-physics.question: On a speed-time graph, what does the gradient (slope) of the line represent?
grade9-physics.hint: Gradient = rise over run = change in speed ÷ change in time.
grade9-physics.explanation: Gradient of a speed-time graph = (change in speed) ÷ (change in time) = acceleration.

grade9-physics.question: On a speed-time graph, what does the area under the line represent?
grade9-physics.hint: Area = height × width = speed × time = distance.
grade9-physics.explanation: Area under a speed-time graph = speed × time = distance; this is true for any shape of graph.

grade9-physics.question:
Look at the graph.
The object accelerates from 4 m/s to 16 m/s in 6 s. What is the distance covered?
grade9-physics.hint: Area = trapezium: ½ × (a + b) × h.
grade9-physics.explanation: Area = ½ × (4 + 16) × 6 = ½ × 20 × 6 = 60 m.

grade9-physics.question: A speed-time graph has a steep upward gradient. What does this indicate?
grade9-physics.hint: Steeper gradient = greater rate of change of speed.
grade9-physics.explanation: A steep upward gradient means speed is changing rapidly with time — a large acceleration.

grade9-physics.question: What does a horizontal line at zero speed on a speed-time graph represent?
options: The object is moving at constant speed
grade9-physics.hint: Zero speed means the object is not moving.
grade9-physics.explanation: A horizontal line on the x-axis (speed = 0) means the object is stationary.

grade9-physics.question:
Look at the graph.
Calculate the total distance travelled between 0 and 10 s.
grade9-physics.hint: Split the area into shapes: triangle + rectangle + triangle.
grade9-physics.explanation: Area 1 (0-4 s, triangle) = ½ × 4 × 8 = 16 m. Area 2 (4-8 s, rectangle) = 4 × 8 = 32 m. Area 3 (8-10 s, triangle) = ½ × 2 × 8 = 8 m. Total = 56 m.

grade9-physics.question: A speed-time graph shows a curve (not a straight line) going upward. What does a curve (as opposed to a straight line) indicate?
options: Non-uniform acceleration (the rate of acceleration is changing)
grade9-physics.answer: Non-uniform acceleration (the rate of acceleration is changing)
acceptableAnswers: Non-uniform acceleration (the rate of acceleration is changing)
grade9-physics.hint: A straight line = uniform acceleration; a curve = changing gradient = changing acceleration.
grade9-physics.explanation: A curved line on a speed-time graph means the gradient is changing, which means the acceleration is not constant (non-uniform acceleration).

grade9-physics.question: A car starts from rest and accelerates at 3 m/s². How far does it travel in 10 s?
grade9-physics.hint: d = ½at² (starts from rest).
grade9-physics.explanation: d = ½ × 3 × 100 = 150 m.

grade9-physics.question: A ball is dropped from rest. Taking g = 10 m/s², how far does it fall in 2 s?
grade9-physics.hint: d = ½gt².
grade9-physics.explanation: d = ½ × 10 × 4 = 20 m.

grade9-physics.question: A car travels at 25 m/s and brakes with a deceleration of 5 m/s². How long does it take to stop?
grade9-physics.hint: Time = initial speed ÷ deceleration.
grade9-physics.explanation: t = v ÷ a = 25 ÷ 5 = 5 s.

grade9-physics.question: A stone is thrown horizontally from a cliff at 10 m/s. It hits the sea 3 s later. Taking g = 10 m/s², how far does it fall vertically?
grade9-physics.hint: d = ½gt².
grade9-physics.explanation: d = ½ × 10 × 9 = 45 m.

grade9-physics.question: A vehicle travels 400 m in 20 s at constant speed. What is its speed?
grade9-physics.hint: Speed = distance ÷ time.
grade9-physics.explanation: 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m/s.

grade9-physics.question: A car decelerates uniformly from 30 m/s to 0 in 6 s. How far does it travel while braking?
grade9-physics.hint: Use average speed = (u + v)/2 or area under speed-time graph.
grade9-physics.explanation: Average speed = (30 + 0)/2 = 15 m/s. Distance = 15 × 6 = 90 m.

grade9-physics.question: A sprinter runs 100 m in 10 s from a standing start. What is her average speed?
grade9-physics.hint: Average speed = distance ÷ time.
grade9-physics.explanation: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 m/s.

grade9-physics.question: A car accelerates from 8 m/s to 20 m/s in 4 s. How far does it travel in those 4 s?
grade9-physics.hint: Use s = ½(u + v) × t.
grade9-physics.explanation: s = ½ × (8 + 20) × 4 = ½ × 28 × 4 = 56 m.

grade9-physics.question: A ball rolls at 4 m/s for 12 s. What distance does it cover?
grade9-physics.hint: Distance = speed × time.
grade9-physics.explanation: 4 × 12 = 48 m.

grade9-physics.question: A car traveling at 20 m/s accelerates at 2 m/s² for 5 s. What is the distance covered during the acceleration?
grade9-physics.hint: d = ut + ½at².
grade9-physics.explanation: d = 20 × 5 + ½ × 2 × 25 = 100 + 25 = 125 m.

grade9-physics.question: A lorry takes 12 s to travel 300 m. What is its average speed?
grade9-physics.hint: Average speed = distance ÷ time.
grade9-physics.explanation: 300 ÷ 12 = 25 m/s.

grade9-physics.question: Two cars set off from the same point at the same time. Car A travels at 20 m/s; Car B travels at 30 m/s. How far apart are they after 15 s?
grade9-physics.hint: Each car covers: d = vt. Distance apart = difference.
grade9-physics.explanation: Car A: 20 × 15 = 300 m. Car B: 30 × 15 = 450 m. Gap = 450 − 300 = 150 m.

grade9-physics.question: A cyclist decelerates from 12 m/s to 6 m/s in 3 s. What is the deceleration?
grade9-physics.hint: Deceleration = change in speed ÷ time.
grade9-physics.explanation: (12 − 6) ÷ 3 = 6 ÷ 3 = 2 m/s².

grade9-physics.question: A rocket accelerates from rest to 400 m/s in 16 s. What is the average speed during this acceleration?
grade9-physics.hint: Average speed = (u + v) ÷ 2 for uniform acceleration.
grade9-physics.explanation: Average speed = (0 + 400) ÷ 2 = 200 m/s.

grade9-physics.question: Which component does this symbol stand for?
grade9-physics.hint: One long line and one short line.
grade9-physics.explanation: A cell is drawn as a long thin line (the positive terminal) beside a short thick one (the negative terminal).

grade9-physics.question: Which component does this symbol stand for?
grade9-physics.hint: A circle with a cross drawn inside it.
grade9-physics.explanation: A lamp is a circle with a cross through it. A meter is a circle with a letter inside instead.

grade9-physics.question: Which component does this symbol stand for?
grade9-physics.hint: The line is lifted away from one of the two dots.
grade9-physics.explanation: An open switch is two contacts with the connecting arm lifted away from one of them.

grade9-physics.question: Which component does this symbol stand for?
grade9-physics.hint: A plain rectangle sitting in the wire.
grade9-physics.explanation: A resistor is drawn as a plain rectangle in the line of the wire.

grade9-physics.question: Which quantity does the meter shown by this symbol measure?
grade9-physics.hint: Read the letter inside the circle.
grade9-physics.explanation: A circle marked A is an ammeter, and an ammeter measures current in amperes.

grade9-physics.question: Which quantity does the meter shown by this symbol measure?
grade9-physics.hint: Read the letter inside the circle.
grade9-physics.explanation: A circle marked V is a voltmeter, and a voltmeter measures voltage in volts.

grade9-physics.question: In the circuit shown, what happens to the lamp when the switch is closed?
options: It stays off until a second cell is added
It lights only if the ammeter is removed first
It stays off, because the circuit is now broken
It lights, because the circuit is now complete
grade9-physics.answer: It lights, because the circuit is now complete
acceptableAnswers: It lights, because the circuit is now complete
grade9-physics.hint: A closed switch joins the two contacts.
grade9-physics.explanation: Closing the switch completes the loop, so charge can flow all the way round and the lamp lights.

grade9-physics.question: Three lamps are connected in series with one cell. One lamp is removed from its holder. What happens?
options: The other two stay lit as before
Only the removed lamp is affected
grade9-physics.hint: A series circuit is a single loop.
grade9-physics.explanation: In series there is only one path, so a break anywhere stops the current everywhere and every lamp goes out.

grade9-physics.question: A second identical cell is added in series to a circuit with one lamp. The lamp becomes:
options: Dimmer, because the cells share the current
Brighter, because the voltage across it is greater
Unlit, because two cells cancel each other out
Unchanged, because the lamp is the same lamp
grade9-physics.answer: Brighter, because the voltage across it is greater
acceptableAnswers: Brighter, because the voltage across it is greater
grade9-physics.hint: Cells in series add their voltages.
grade9-physics.explanation: Two cells in series give twice the voltage, so a larger current flows and the lamp is brighter.

grade9-physics.question: Why is a series circuit a poor choice for the lights in a house?
options: Series circuits cannot be switched off
The lights would all become far too bright
One broken lamp would switch off every other light
grade9-physics.answer: One broken lamp would switch off every other light
acceptableAnswers: One broken lamp would switch off every other light
grade9-physics.hint: Think about what one break does to a single loop.
grade9-physics.explanation: A house needs each light to work on its own; in series a single break cuts the current to all of them.

grade9-physics.question: In the circuit shown, how is the meter connected, and what does that tell you it is?
options: Across the lamp only, so it is an ammeter
In series in the loop, so it is a voltmeter
Across the lamp only, so it is a voltmeter
In series in the loop, so it is an ammeter
grade9-physics.answer: In series in the loop, so it is an ammeter
acceptableAnswers: In series in the loop, so it is an ammeter
grade9-physics.hint: Follow the wire: does the loop pass through the meter?
grade9-physics.explanation: The meter sits in the loop itself, so the whole current passes through it - that is how an ammeter is connected.

grade9-physics.question: In the circuit shown, how is the meter connected, and what does that tell you it is?
options: Across the lamp, so it is an ammeter
In series in the loop, so it is an ammeter
In series in the loop, so it is a voltmeter
Across the lamp, so it is a voltmeter
grade9-physics.answer: Across the lamp, so it is a voltmeter
acceptableAnswers: Across the lamp, so it is a voltmeter
grade9-physics.hint: Follow the wire: the meter is on its own branch beside the lamp.
grade9-physics.explanation: The meter is connected across the lamp, on a branch of its own - that is how a voltmeter is connected.

grade9-physics.question: An ammeter must always be connected:
grade9-physics.hint: The current being measured has to pass through it.
grade9-physics.explanation: An ammeter is placed in series so that the current it is measuring flows through it.

grade9-physics.question: A voltmeter must always be connected:
grade9-physics.hint: It compares two points, one on each side.
grade9-physics.explanation: A voltmeter is placed across (in parallel with) the component, because voltage is measured between two points.

grade9-physics.question: A pupil connects an ammeter across a lamp instead of in series with it. What is the main problem?
options: Almost all the current takes the meter instead of the lamp
The cell is unable to produce any voltage
The meter shows a reading of exactly zero every time
The lamp becomes brighter than it should be
grade9-physics.answer: Almost all the current takes the meter instead of the lamp
acceptableAnswers: Almost all the current takes the meter instead of the lamp
grade9-physics.hint: An ammeter has a very low resistance.
grade9-physics.explanation: An ammeter has almost no resistance, so connected across the lamp it short-circuits it and takes nearly all the current.

grade9-physics.question: What is the unit of electric current?
grade9-physics.hint: Its symbol is A.
grade9-physics.explanation: Current is measured in amperes (A).

grade9-physics.question: What is the unit of resistance?
grade9-physics.hint: Its symbol is the Greek letter omega.
grade9-physics.explanation: Resistance is measured in ohms.

grade9-physics.question: What does the resistance of a component tell you?
options: How much light it gives out
How much it opposes the flow of current
How much charge it stores for later
How much current it produces on its own
grade9-physics.answer: How much it opposes the flow of current
acceptableAnswers: How much it opposes the flow of current
grade9-physics.hint: A larger resistance lets less current through.
grade9-physics.explanation: Resistance measures how strongly a component opposes the current flowing through it.

grade9-physics.question: What does the electromotive force (emf) of a cell describe?
options: The charge stored on the cell casing
The current the cell always pushes out
The resistance inside the connecting wires
The energy the cell gives to each unit of charge
grade9-physics.answer: The energy the cell gives to each unit of charge
acceptableAnswers: The energy the cell gives to each unit of charge
grade9-physics.hint: It is about energy per unit charge, not about current.
grade9-physics.explanation: The emf of a cell is the energy it supplies to each coulomb of charge driven round the circuit.

grade9-physics.question: The voltage across a fixed resistor is doubled. What happens to the current through it?
grade9-physics.hint: For a fixed resistance, current and voltage rise together.
grade9-physics.explanation: With the resistance unchanged, doubling the voltage doubles the current through the resistor.

grade9-physics.question: What is the unit of electric charge?
grade9-physics.hint: Its symbol is C.
grade9-physics.explanation: Charge is measured in coulombs (C).

grade9-physics.question: Which statement describes electric current correctly?
options: It is the total charge stored in a cell
It is the opposition to the flow of charge
It is the rate of flow of charge
It is the energy carried by each charge
grade9-physics.answer: It is the rate of flow of charge
acceptableAnswers: It is the rate of flow of charge
grade9-physics.hint: Rate means "per second".
grade9-physics.explanation: Current is the charge passing a point each second, which is why Q = It.

grade9-physics.question: Which statement describes potential difference correctly?
options: It is the total charge moved round the circuit
It is the resistance between two points
It is the charge that flows in one second
It is the work done per unit charge between two points
grade9-physics.answer: It is the work done per unit charge between two points
acceptableAnswers: It is the work done per unit charge between two points
grade9-physics.hint: Per unit charge means "for each coulomb".
grade9-physics.explanation: Potential difference is the energy transferred per coulomb of charge, which is why W = QV.

grade9-physics.question: A charge moves through a lamp and the lamp gives out light and heat. Which quantity is the energy transferred divided by that charge?
options: The potential difference across the lamp
The current flowing through the lamp
grade9-physics.answer: The potential difference across the lamp
acceptableAnswers: The potential difference across the lamp
grade9-physics.hint: Energy per unit charge has a name.
grade9-physics.explanation: Energy transferred divided by charge is the potential difference across the component: V = W / Q.

grade9-physics.question: In a series circuit, the current is measured at three different points. What will the three readings be?
options: Each one is larger than the last
Each one is smaller than the last
The middle one is the largest
grade9-physics.hint: There is only one path for the charge.
grade9-physics.explanation: Current is the same everywhere in a series circuit, because charge has nowhere else to go.

grade9-physics.question: A current of 3 A flows for 5 s. Calculate the charge that passes, in coulombs.
grade9-physics.hint: Use Q = I × t.
grade9-physics.explanation: Q = It = 3 × 5 = 15 C.

grade9-physics.question: A current of 0.5 A flows for 60 s. Calculate the charge that passes, in coulombs.
grade9-physics.hint: Use Q = I × t.
grade9-physics.explanation: Q = It = 0.5 × 60 = 30 C.

grade9-physics.question: A charge of 24 C passes a point in 8 s. Calculate the current, in amperes.
grade9-physics.hint: Rearrange Q = It to I = Q ÷ t.

grade9-physics.question: A charge of 45 C flows when the current is 9 A. Calculate the time taken, in seconds.
grade9-physics.hint: Rearrange Q = It to t = Q ÷ I.

grade9-physics.question: A charge of 4 C moves through a potential difference of 6 V. Calculate the energy transferred, in joules.
grade9-physics.hint: Use W = Q × V.
grade9-physics.explanation: W = QV = 4 × 6 = 24 J.

grade9-physics.question: 36 J of energy is transferred when 3 C of charge flows through a lamp. Calculate the potential difference across the lamp, in volts.
grade9-physics.hint: Rearrange W = QV to V = W ÷ Q.

grade9-physics.question: 50 J of energy is transferred by a charge moving through 10 V. Calculate the charge, in coulombs.
grade9-physics.hint: Rearrange W = QV to Q = W ÷ V.

grade9-physics.question: Two cells of 1.5 V each are connected in series. Calculate the total voltage supplied, in volts.
grade9-physics.hint: Cells in series add.

grade9-physics.question: A 6 V supply is connected across a resistor and a current of 2 A flows. Calculate the resistance, in ohms.
grade9-physics.hint: Use R = V ÷ I.
grade9-physics.explanation: R = V / I = 6 / 2 = 3 ohms.

grade9-physics.question: A current of 0.4 A flows through a 20 ohm resistor. Calculate the voltage across it, in volts.
grade9-physics.hint: Use V = I × R.
grade9-physics.explanation: V = IR = 0.4 × 20 = 8 V.

grade9-physics.question: Two lamps in series each have 3 V across them. Calculate the supply voltage, in volts.
grade9-physics.hint: In series the voltages across the parts add to the supply voltage.

grade9-physics.question: An ammeter in a series circuit reads 0.25 A. What will a second ammeter placed elsewhere in the same loop read, in amperes?
grade9-physics.hint: Current is the same all the way round a series circuit.
grade9-physics.explanation: The current is the same at every point of a series circuit, so it also reads 0.25 A.

grade9-physics.question: Name the component drawn as a circle with a cross inside it.
grade9-physics.hint: It gives out light.
grade9-physics.explanation: A circle with a cross through it is the symbol for a lamp.

grade9-physics.question: Name the meter that is connected in series to measure current.
grade9-physics.hint: Its symbol is a circle marked A.
grade9-physics.explanation: An ammeter measures current and is connected in series.

grade9-physics.question: Name the meter that is connected across a component to measure voltage.
grade9-physics.hint: Its symbol is a circle marked V.
grade9-physics.explanation: A voltmeter measures voltage and is connected in parallel.

grade9-physics.question: Give the unit in which resistance is measured.
grade9-physics.hint: Its symbol is the Greek letter omega.
grade9-physics.explanation: Resistance is measured in ohms.

grade9-physics.question: Write the equation that links charge, current and time.
grade9-physics.hint: Charge equals current multiplied by time.
grade9-physics.explanation: Q = It: charge equals current multiplied by the time it flows for.

grade9-physics.question: What does this circuit symbol represent?
grade9-physics.hint: A long thin line and a short thick line — that is the cell symbol.
grade9-physics.explanation: A cell is represented by a long thin line (positive terminal) and a shorter thick line (negative terminal).

grade9-physics.question: What does this circuit symbol represent?
grade9-physics.hint: A circle with an X inside — the filament.
grade9-physics.explanation: A lamp is represented by a circle with two crossing lines (the filament symbol) inside it.

grade9-physics.question: What does this circuit symbol represent?
grade9-physics.hint: Two dots connected by a line at an angle — one end is lifted off.
grade9-physics.explanation: An open switch is shown as a lever lifted away from one of the contacts; closing the lever completes the circuit.

grade9-physics.question: What does this circuit symbol represent?
grade9-physics.hint: A rectangle is the international IEC symbol for a resistor.
grade9-physics.explanation: A resistor is represented by a rectangle in circuit diagrams.

grade9-physics.question: What does this circuit symbol represent?
grade9-physics.hint: A circle with the letter A inside.
grade9-physics.explanation: An ammeter (symbol: circle with A) is used to measure current; it is connected in series.

grade9-physics.question: What does this circuit symbol represent?
grade9-physics.hint: A circle with the letter V inside.
grade9-physics.explanation: A voltmeter (symbol: circle with V) is used to measure potential difference; it is connected in parallel.

grade9-physics.question: What does this symbol represent?
grade9-physics.hint: A short dashed line inside a rectangle — a thin wire that melts.
grade9-physics.explanation: A fuse is represented by a rectangle with a wire inside; when the current is too high the fuse wire melts and breaks the circuit.

grade9-physics.question: What does this symbol represent?
options: A battery (two or more cells in series)
grade9-physics.answer: A battery (two or more cells in series)
acceptableAnswers: A battery (two or more cells in series)
grade9-physics.hint: More than two pairs of lines — more than one cell.
grade9-physics.explanation: Two or more cell symbols in series represent a battery; more pairs of lines = more cells = higher e.m.f.

grade9-physics.question: In a circuit diagram, which of the following is always drawn as a straight line between components?
grade9-physics.hint: Connecting wires are shown as straight lines with corners.
grade9-physics.explanation: Ideal connecting wires are drawn as straight lines in circuit diagrams; they are assumed to have zero resistance.

grade9-physics.question: A student draws a circuit with a cell, switch, lamp and ammeter. The ammeter symbol (circle A) is drawn in parallel with the lamp. What is wrong?
options: An ammeter must be connected in series, not in parallel, with the component
An ammeter cannot be used in a circuit with a lamp
The switch should be inside the ammeter symbol
grade9-physics.answer: An ammeter must be connected in series, not in parallel, with the component
acceptableAnswers: An ammeter must be connected in series, not in parallel, with the component
grade9-physics.hint: An ammeter measures the current flowing through a branch.
grade9-physics.explanation: Ammeters have very low resistance and are connected in series so all the current flows through them; in parallel they would short-circuit the lamp.

grade9-physics.question: Why is a voltmeter connected in parallel with a component?
options: To measure the current flowing through the component
To measure the potential difference across the component without significantly changing the current
To reduce the resistance of the component
To increase the voltage supplied to the component
grade9-physics.answer: To measure the potential difference across the component without significantly changing the current
acceptableAnswers: To measure the potential difference across the component without significantly changing the current
grade9-physics.hint: Parallel connection shares the same voltage.
grade9-physics.explanation: A voltmeter is connected in parallel so it shares the potential difference across the component; its very high resistance means it draws negligible current.

grade9-physics.question: A student is given a circuit diagram showing a cell, a closed switch, a lamp and an ammeter in series. She adds a voltmeter across the lamp. How many separate loops does the circuit now have?
options: Two (the main loop and the voltmeter branch)
It depends on the cell voltage
grade9-physics.answer: Two (the main loop and the voltmeter branch)
acceptableAnswers: Two (the main loop and the voltmeter branch)
grade9-physics.hint: Adding a parallel branch creates a second loop.
grade9-physics.explanation: The original series loop is one loop. The voltmeter in parallel with the lamp creates a second, smaller loop.

grade9-physics.question: In a circuit diagram, what does a break (gap) in the line of a switch indicate?
options: The switch is closed and current flows
The switch is open and the circuit is broken
grade9-physics.answer: The switch is open and the circuit is broken
acceptableAnswers: The switch is open and the circuit is broken
grade9-physics.hint: A break in the conducting path means no current.
grade9-physics.explanation: An open switch has the lever lifted from one contact, showing a gap; no current flows when the circuit is open.

grade9-physics.question: Which component is specifically designed to protect a circuit by melting when the current is too large?
grade9-physics.hint: It is sacrificial — it breaks the circuit to save the rest.
grade9-physics.explanation: A fuse contains a fine wire that melts (blows) when the current exceeds a safe level, breaking the circuit and protecting other components.

grade9-physics.question: In a series circuit, what is true of the current?
options: The current is greatest near the positive terminal
The current is shared equally between the components
Each component has a different current flowing through it
The current is the same at every point in the circuit
grade9-physics.answer: The current is the same at every point in the circuit
acceptableAnswers: The current is the same at every point in the circuit
grade9-physics.hint: There is only one path for the current in a series circuit.
grade9-physics.explanation: In a series circuit there is only one path; the same current flows through every component.

grade9-physics.question: In a series circuit containing a cell, switch and two lamps, what happens when one lamp is removed?
options: The current doubles through the remaining lamp
The circuit breaks and both lamps go out
Only the removed lamp goes out; the other stays on
grade9-physics.answer: The circuit breaks and both lamps go out
acceptableAnswers: The circuit breaks and both lamps go out
grade9-physics.hint: In series, all components share the same path.
grade9-physics.explanation: In series, removing a lamp breaks the only conducting path; the circuit is incomplete and no current flows — both lamps go off.

grade9-physics.question: A series circuit has a 6 V cell and three resistors of 1 Ω, 2 Ω and 3 Ω. What is the total resistance?
grade9-physics.hint: Total resistance in series = sum of individual resistances.
grade9-physics.explanation: R⊂total; = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 Ω.

grade9-physics.question: A 12 V cell is connected in a series circuit with two identical lamps. Each lamp has a resistance of 4 Ω. What is the total current?
grade9-physics.hint: I = V ÷ R⊂total;. R⊂total; = 4 + 4 = 8 Ω.
grade9-physics.explanation: R⊂total; = 8 Ω; I = 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5 A.

grade9-physics.question: In a series circuit, a 9 V battery drives a current of 0.3 A. What is the total resistance of the circuit?
grade9-physics.hint: R = V ÷ I.
grade9-physics.explanation: R = 9 ÷ 0.3 = 30 Ω.

grade9-physics.question: In a series circuit the voltage across a 5 Ω resistor is 10 V. A second resistor in series with it is 3 Ω. What is the voltage across the 3 Ω resistor?
grade9-physics.hint: Find the current first; I = V/R = 10/5 = 2 A. Then V₂ = I × R₂.

grade9-physics.question: Two resistors of 6 Ω and 4 Ω are connected in series with a 20 V source. What is the current?
grade9-physics.hint: I = V ÷ R⊂total;.
grade9-physics.explanation: R⊂total; = 10 Ω. I = 20 ÷ 10 = 2 A.

grade9-physics.question: Three resistors of 4 Ω, 6 Ω and 10 Ω are in series with a 40 V supply. What is the voltage across the 6 Ω resistor?
grade9-physics.hint: Find total resistance, then I, then V = IR for the 6 Ω resistor.
grade9-physics.explanation: R⊂total; = 20 Ω. I = 40/20 = 2 A. V = 2 × 6 = 12 V.

grade9-physics.question: What is the sum of the voltages across all components in a series circuit compared to the e.m.f. of the source?
options: The voltages are all equal to each other
The voltages add up to equal the e.m.f.
grade9-physics.answer: The voltages add up to equal the e.m.f.
acceptableAnswers: The voltages add up to equal the e.m.f.
grade9-physics.hint: Kirchhoff’s voltage law.
grade9-physics.explanation: In a series circuit, the sum of the potential differences across all components equals the e.m.f. of the source (Kirchhoff’s voltage law).

grade9-physics.question: A series circuit has a 9 V battery and two resistors R₁ = 3 Ω and R₂ = 6 Ω. What is the voltage across R₁?
grade9-physics.hint: I = V / R⊂total; = 9 / 9 = 1 A. V₁ = I × R₁.
grade9-physics.explanation: R⊂total; = 9 Ω. I = 1 A. V₁ = 1 × 3 = 3 V.

grade9-physics.question: A switch is placed in series with a lamp. When the switch is opened, what happens?
options: The lamp goes out because the circuit is broken
The lamp stays on because the switch is not the power source
grade9-physics.answer: The lamp goes out because the circuit is broken
acceptableAnswers: The lamp goes out because the circuit is broken
grade9-physics.hint: An open switch breaks the only path.
grade9-physics.explanation: An open switch creates a gap in the series loop; no current flows and the lamp goes out.

grade9-physics.question: In a series circuit, a 12 V supply drives current through a lamp (resistance 3 Ω) and a resistor (5 Ω). What is the voltage across the lamp?
grade9-physics.explanation: I = 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5 A. V⊂lamp; = 1.5 × 3 = 4.5 V.

grade9-physics.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of connecting lamps in series in a household string of lights?
options: Each lamp receives too much current
The circuit cannot be switched off
If one lamp fails, all lamps go out
The total voltage across each lamp is too high
grade9-physics.answer: If one lamp fails, all lamps go out
acceptableAnswers: If one lamp fails, all lamps go out
grade9-physics.hint: Series circuits have a single path.
grade9-physics.explanation: In series, the path is broken when any lamp fails; all others go out, making fault-finding difficult.

grade9-physics.question: A student adds a third resistor (2 Ω) in series to a circuit that already has two resistors (4 Ω and 6 Ω) and a 12 V supply. How does the current change?
options: It stays the same because voltage is constant
It doubles because three resistors are more powerful
It increases (more resistors push more current)
grade9-physics.hint: More resistance in series means less current (I = V/R).
grade9-physics.explanation: Original R = 10 Ω; I = 1.2 A. New R = 12 Ω; I = 12 ÷ 12 = 1 A. Current decreases.

grade9-physics.question: Which instrument measures electric current?
grade9-physics.hint: It measures amps.
grade9-physics.explanation: An ammeter measures electric current in amperes (A); it is connected in series with the component.

grade9-physics.question: Which instrument measures potential difference (voltage)?
grade9-physics.hint: It measures volts.
grade9-physics.explanation: A voltmeter measures potential difference in volts (V); it is connected in parallel with the component.

grade9-physics.question: How should an ammeter be connected to measure the current through a lamp?
options: Between the switch and the battery only
In series with the lamp (in the same loop)
grade9-physics.answer: In series with the lamp (in the same loop)
acceptableAnswers: In series with the lamp (in the same loop)
grade9-physics.hint: Current through the lamp must flow through the ammeter.
grade9-physics.explanation: An ammeter must be in series so that the same current flowing through the lamp also flows through the ammeter.

grade9-physics.question: How should a voltmeter be connected to measure the voltage across a resistor?
grade9-physics.hint: Both connections share the same potential difference.
grade9-physics.explanation: A voltmeter is connected in parallel; both its terminals connect to the two ends of the resistor, so it measures the potential difference across it.

grade9-physics.question:
Look at the circuit.
Where would you connect the voltmeter to measure the voltage across the lamp?
options: In parallel with the lamp (across both ends of the lamp)
grade9-physics.answer: In parallel with the lamp (across both ends of the lamp)
acceptableAnswers: In parallel with the lamp (across both ends of the lamp)
grade9-physics.hint: The voltmeter must be directly across the component to measure its voltage.
grade9-physics.explanation: To measure the voltage across the lamp, connect the voltmeter in parallel with the lamp — one terminal to each end of the lamp.

grade9-physics.question: An ideal ammeter has a resistance of zero ohms. Why?
options: So that it can handle very large currents
So that it can be connected in parallel
So that inserting it in series does not reduce the current it is measuring
So that it measures voltage accurately
grade9-physics.answer: So that inserting it in series does not reduce the current it is measuring
acceptableAnswers: So that inserting it in series does not reduce the current it is measuring
grade9-physics.hint: Any resistance in series changes the current.
grade9-physics.explanation: If the ammeter had resistance, it would increase the total resistance of the circuit and reduce the current; zero resistance means no effect.

grade9-physics.question: An ideal voltmeter has infinite resistance. Why?
options: So that it measures current accurately
So that it can be placed in series
So that it draws no current from the circuit and does not change the voltage it measures
So that it can measure very large currents
grade9-physics.answer: So that it draws no current from the circuit and does not change the voltage it measures
acceptableAnswers: So that it draws no current from the circuit and does not change the voltage it measures
grade9-physics.hint: A voltmeter in parallel must not affect the circuit.
grade9-physics.explanation: Infinite resistance means no current flows through the voltmeter; it measures the voltage without disturbing the circuit.

grade9-physics.question: What is the unit of electric current?
grade9-physics.hint: Current is measured in amps.
grade9-physics.explanation: The SI unit of electric current is the ampere (A).

grade9-physics.question: What is the unit of potential difference (voltage)?
grade9-physics.hint: Voltage is measured in volts.
grade9-physics.explanation: The SI unit of potential difference is the volt (V).

grade9-physics.question: In a circuit, an ammeter reads 2.5 A and a voltmeter across a resistor reads 10 V. What is the resistance of the resistor?
grade9-physics.hint: R = V ÷ I.
grade9-physics.explanation: R = 10 ÷ 2.5 = 4 Ω.

grade9-physics.question: A student connects an ammeter in parallel with a lamp by mistake. What is likely to happen?
options: The circuit works normally because ammeters can be in parallel
The ammeter short-circuits the lamp; very large current may damage the ammeter
The ammeter accurately measures the lamp’s resistance
grade9-physics.answer: The ammeter short-circuits the lamp; very large current may damage the ammeter
acceptableAnswers: The ammeter short-circuits the lamp; very large current may damage the ammeter
grade9-physics.hint: An ammeter has very low (near zero) resistance.
grade9-physics.explanation: An ammeter in parallel with the lamp provides a near-zero-resistance path; almost all the current bypasses the lamp and flows through the ammeter, which may be damaged.

grade9-physics.question: A voltmeter reads 6 V when placed across a 3 Ω resistor in a circuit. What current flows through the resistor?
grade9-physics.hint: I = V ÷ R.
grade9-physics.explanation: I = 6 ÷ 3 = 2 A.

grade9-physics.question: Two ammeters are placed in a series circuit: one before and one after a lamp. What will their readings be?
options: The same, because current is the same everywhere in a series circuit
The one before the lamp reads higher
Different; the lamp uses some current
grade9-physics.answer: The same, because current is the same everywhere in a series circuit
acceptableAnswers: The same, because current is the same everywhere in a series circuit
grade9-physics.hint: Series circuits have the same current throughout.
grade9-physics.explanation: Current is conserved in a series circuit; both ammeters read the same value.

grade9-physics.question: A voltmeter across a cell reads 9 V with no other components connected. When a lamp is connected, the voltmeter reads 8.4 V. What does this show?
options: The cell e.m.f. has permanently dropped
The lamp has increased the resistance to infinity
The cell has internal resistance, so some voltage is “lost” inside the cell
grade9-physics.answer: The cell has internal resistance, so some voltage is “lost” inside the cell
acceptableAnswers: The cell has internal resistance, so some voltage is “lost” inside the cell
grade9-physics.hint: The terminal voltage drops when current flows due to the internal resistance of the cell.
grade9-physics.explanation: When current flows, the internal resistance of the cell causes a voltage drop inside it; the terminal voltage (8.4 V) is less than the open-circuit e.m.f. (9 V).

grade9-physics.question: State Ohm’s Law.
options: The voltage is inversely proportional to the current
Current equals resistance multiplied by temperature
The resistance is directly proportional to the length of the conductor
The current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it (at constant temperature)
grade9-physics.answer: The current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it (at constant temperature)
acceptableAnswers: The current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it (at constant temperature)
grade9-physics.hint: Ohm’s Law: V = IR.
grade9-physics.explanation: Ohm’s Law: V = IR, or equivalently, I is proportional to V at constant temperature.

grade9-physics.question: What is the formula linking voltage, current and resistance?
grade9-physics.hint: Ohm’s Law: Voltage = Current × Resistance.
grade9-physics.explanation: Ohm’s Law: V = IR. Current I = V/R; Resistance R = V/I.

grade9-physics.question: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
grade9-physics.hint: Named after Georg Ohm.
grade9-physics.explanation: The SI unit of resistance is the ohm (Ω).

grade9-physics.question: A resistor has a potential difference of 12 V across it and a current of 3 A through it. What is its resistance?
grade9-physics.hint: R = V ÷ I.
grade9-physics.explanation: R = 12 ÷ 3 = 4 Ω.

grade9-physics.question: A 6 Ω resistor has a current of 2 A through it. What is the potential difference across it?
grade9-physics.hint: V = IR.
grade9-physics.explanation: V = 2 × 6 = 12 V.

grade9-physics.question: A lamp has a resistance of 10 Ω and is connected to a 5 V supply. What current flows through it?
grade9-physics.hint: I = V ÷ R.
grade9-physics.explanation: I = 5 ÷ 10 = 0.5 A.

grade9-physics.question:
The circuit shows a 6 V cell, a 3 Ω resistor and an ammeter in series.
What does the ammeter read?
grade9-physics.hint: I = V ÷ R = 6 ÷ 3.
grade9-physics.explanation: I = 6 ÷ 3 = 2 A.

grade9-physics.question:
A 12 V source, a 4 Ω resistor and an ammeter are in series.
What does the ammeter read?
grade9-physics.hint: I = V ÷ R = 12 ÷ 4.
grade9-physics.explanation: I = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 A.

grade9-physics.question: Doubling the resistance in a circuit while keeping the voltage constant does what to the current?
options: Has no effect on the current
grade9-physics.hint: I = V/R; if R doubles and V is constant, I halves.
grade9-physics.explanation: I = V ÷ R. If R doubles, I = V ÷ (2R) = half the original current.

grade9-physics.question: Doubling the voltage while keeping the resistance constant does what to the current?
grade9-physics.hint: I = V/R; if V doubles and R is constant, I doubles.
grade9-physics.explanation: I = V ÷ R. If V doubles, I = (2V) ÷ R = twice the original current.

grade9-physics.question: A current of 0.4 A flows through a wire with a resistance of 15 Ω. What is the potential difference across the wire?
grade9-physics.hint: V = IR.

grade9-physics.question: A nichrome wire carries 1.5 A at 9 V. Calculate its resistance.
grade9-physics.hint: R = V ÷ I.
grade9-physics.explanation: R = 9 ÷ 1.5 = 6 Ω.

grade9-physics.question: A conductor obeys Ohm’s Law. A graph of V (y-axis) against I (x-axis) is plotted. What is the shape of the graph?
options: A straight line through the origin
grade9-physics.answer: A straight line through the origin
acceptableAnswers: A straight line through the origin
grade9-physics.hint: V = IR means V is directly proportional to I.
grade9-physics.explanation: V = IR is a linear equation; a graph of V vs I is a straight line through the origin with gradient = R.

grade9-physics.question: A student measures the current through a lamp at different voltages. At low voltages, the lamp follows Ohm’s Law but at high voltages the line curves. Why?
options: The resistance decreases at high temperature, increasing the current
Ohm’s Law only applies above 100 V
At high voltages the lamp gets hotter; its resistance increases with temperature, reducing the current below the Ohm’s Law prediction
The student made errors at high voltages
grade9-physics.answer: At high voltages the lamp gets hotter; its resistance increases with temperature, reducing the current below the Ohm’s Law prediction
acceptableAnswers: At high voltages the lamp gets hotter; its resistance increases with temperature, reducing the current below the Ohm’s Law prediction
grade9-physics.hint: The resistance of a metal increases with temperature.
grade9-physics.explanation: A lamp filament heats up at high voltages; its resistance rises, so the current is less than Ohm’s Law predicts for an ideal resistor at constant temperature.

grade9-physics.question: What is the relationship between charge, current and time?
grade9-physics.hint: Q in coulombs = I in amperes × t in seconds.
grade9-physics.explanation: Charge Q = current I × time t; Q is in coulombs (C), I in amperes (A), t in seconds (s).

grade9-physics.question: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
grade9-physics.hint: Named after Charles-Augustin de Coulomb.
grade9-physics.explanation: The SI unit of electric charge is the coulomb (C); 1 C = 1 A × 1 s.

grade9-physics.question: A current of 2 A flows for 30 s. How much charge passes?
grade9-physics.hint: Q = It.
grade9-physics.explanation: Q = 2 × 30 = 60 C.

grade9-physics.question: A charge of 90 C passes through a wire in 18 s. What is the current?
grade9-physics.hint: I = Q ÷ t.
grade9-physics.explanation: I = 90 ÷ 18 = 5 A.

grade9-physics.question: A current of 0.5 A flows. How long does it take for 10 C of charge to pass?
grade9-physics.hint: t = Q ÷ I.
grade9-physics.explanation: t = 10 ÷ 0.5 = 20 s.

grade9-physics.question: A torch draws 0.3 A from its battery. How much charge is supplied in 5 minutes?
grade9-physics.hint: Convert 5 min to seconds; then Q = It.

grade9-physics.question: A current of 4 A flows through a lamp for 10 s. How many coulombs of charge pass through the lamp?
grade9-physics.hint: Q = It.
grade9-physics.explanation: Q = 4 × 10 = 40 C.

grade9-physics.question: A battery delivers 360 C in 2 minutes. What is the average current?
grade9-physics.hint: t = 2 min = 120 s; I = Q ÷ t.
grade9-physics.explanation: I = 360 ÷ 120 = 3 A.

grade9-physics.question: Each electron carries a charge of 1.6 × 10²¹C. How many electrons pass a point when 4.8 × 10²¹C of charge passes?
grade9-physics.hint: Number = Q ÷ charge per electron.
grade9-physics.explanation: 4.8 × 10²¹C ÷ 1.6 × 10²¹C = 3 electrons.

grade9-physics.question: Current is defined as the rate of flow of which quantity?
grade9-physics.hint: Current = charge ÷ time.
grade9-physics.explanation: Current I = Q ÷ t; current is the rate of flow of charge past a point.

grade9-physics.question: A student charges a capacitor until it holds 0.005 C at 10 V. What current flowed during charging if it took 0.05 s?
grade9-physics.hint: I = Q ÷ t.

grade9-physics.question: A current of 250 mA flows through a circuit. Express this in amperes and calculate the charge after 2 minutes.
What is the current if 120 C pass through a wire in 1 minute?
grade9-physics.hint: 1 min = 60 s; I = Q ÷ t.
grade9-physics.explanation: I = 120 ÷ 60 = 2 A.

grade9-physics.question: A car starter motor draws 200 A for 4 s. How much charge is transferred from the battery?
grade9-physics.hint: Q = It.

grade9-physics.question: What is the formula linking work, charge and potential difference?
grade9-physics.hint: Work done (J) = charge (C) × potential difference (V).
grade9-physics.explanation: W = QV: the work done (in joules) when charge Q moves through a potential difference V.

grade9-physics.question: What is the potential difference if 10 J of work is done to move 2 C of charge?
grade9-physics.hint: V = W ÷ Q.
grade9-physics.explanation: V = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 V.

grade9-physics.question: A charge of 5 C moves through a potential difference of 12 V. How much work is done?
grade9-physics.hint: W = QV.
grade9-physics.explanation: W = 5 × 12 = 60 J.

grade9-physics.question: A 9 V battery transfers 18 J of energy. How many coulombs of charge move through it?
grade9-physics.hint: Q = W ÷ V.
grade9-physics.explanation: Q = 18 ÷ 9 = 2 C.
