grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Port Louis: 118,000 ÷ 43 ≈ 2,744/km². Savanne: 69,000 ÷ 244 ≈ 283/km². Port Louis is about ten times denser, as expected for a capital city.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: A population pyramid that looks like a rectangle (nearly the same width at all ages) indicates:
options: A rapidly growing population with very high birth rates
A population made up entirely of working-age adults
A stable population with low birth rates, low death rates and most people surviving to old age
A population devastated by war or disease
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: A stable population with low birth rates, low death rates and most people surviving to old age
acceptableAnswers: A stable population with low birth rates, low death rates and most people surviving to old age
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Rectangular means each age group is roughly the same size.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: A nearly rectangular pyramid shows low birth and death rates: about as many people are born each year as the number who die at the top end, so each age group is similar in size.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: In 2020, Mauritius had a birth rate of approximately 10 per 1,000 and a death rate of 9 per 1,000. What was its natural increase and what does this suggest about population growth?
options: The population is declining because the death rate is almost equal to the birth rate
19 per 1,000 — very rapid growth driven by births far exceeding deaths
1 per 1,000 — very slow natural increase, suggesting growth comes mainly from other factors
−1 per 1,000 — the population is shrinking rapidly due to high death rates
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: 1 per 1,000 — very slow natural increase, suggesting growth comes mainly from other factors
acceptableAnswers: 1 per 1,000 — very slow natural increase, suggesting growth comes mainly from other factors
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: 10 − 9 = 1; interpret what a tiny gap means.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: A natural increase of only 1 per 1,000 means the population is barely growing from births and deaths alone. Any significant growth would come from migration rather than natural increase.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Mauritius faces the challenge of an ageing population. Which combination of policies BEST addresses this challenge sustainably?
options: Investing in automation to maintain productivity, attracting skilled migrants, and gradually raising the retirement age
Banning all elderly people from using the health service to reduce costs
Reducing spending on education so more money is available for pensions
Encouraging the highest possible birth rate immediately to produce future workers
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Investing in automation to maintain productivity, attracting skilled migrants, and gradually raising the retirement age
acceptableAnswers: Investing in automation to maintain productivity, attracting skilled migrants, and gradually raising the retirement age
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Multiple policies working together are more sustainable than any single measure.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Automation keeps output high with fewer workers; skilled migrants supplement the workforce; raising the retirement age means more workers contribute longer. No single measure is sufficient alone.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Life expectancy at birth differs from life expectancy at age 60. Why?
options: A person who is 60 has a shorter life ahead regardless of their health
Life expectancy at 60 is always lower than at birth because people get older
A person who has already survived 60 years has avoided the risks (disease, accidents) that kill many people young, so their expected remaining years are different from the average at birth
Life expectancy figures are only calculated at birth and cannot be applied to older ages
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: A person who has already survived 60 years has avoided the risks (disease, accidents) that kill many people young, so their expected remaining years are different from the average at birth
acceptableAnswers: A person who has already survived 60 years has avoided the risks (disease, accidents) that kill many people young, so their expected remaining years are different from the average at birth
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Surviving to 60 means you have already beaten the odds of dying young.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Life expectancy at birth includes the risk of dying young. Someone who is already 60 has passed those risks, so their remaining life expectancy reflects only the risks faced by someone in their sixties — which can add up to many more years.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Why is the central plateau of Mauritius LESS densely populated than the coast, despite being cooler and green?
options: The plateau has been declared a national park and no one is allowed to live there
The soil on the plateau is too poor to support any human settlement
The plateau is harder to access, and economic activity (ports, hotels, factories) concentrates on the coast
The government has forbidden anyone from living above 100 m altitude
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: The plateau is harder to access, and economic activity (ports, hotels, factories) concentrates on the coast
acceptableAnswers: The plateau is harder to access, and economic activity (ports, hotels, factories) concentrates on the coast
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: People settle where jobs and transport are.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Despite its pleasant climate, the plateau is less accessible and has fewer economic opportunities than the coast. Ports, tourist hotels and EPZ factories are all coastal, drawing population toward the sea.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: A sudden notch (narrowing) in the 20–24 age group of a population pyramid could indicate that:
options: All people in that age group emigrated permanently
A famine, disease or war killed or displaced many people when that cohort was born 20–24 years ago
The data for that age group was accidentally lost
The government changed its education policy for that age group
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: A famine, disease or war killed or displaced many people when that cohort was born 20–24 years ago
acceptableAnswers: A famine, disease or war killed or displaced many people when that cohort was born 20–24 years ago
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: A smaller cohort means fewer people were born or survived — look 20–24 years into the past.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: A notch at 20–24 today means that cohort was smaller when born. This could result from a famine, epidemic or conflict about 20–24 years ago that reduced births or increased infant deaths.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What is a CRUDE birth rate?
options: The total number of babies born in a country in one year
The number of live births per 1,000 people in the total population per year
The percentage of women who give birth in any given decade
The number of births per 1,000 women of childbearing age
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: The number of live births per 1,000 people in the total population per year
acceptableAnswers: The number of live births per 1,000 people in the total population per year
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: The word "crude" means it uses the whole population, not just women.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The crude birth rate divides total births by the total population (not just women), giving a rate per 1,000 per year. It is "crude" because it does not account for the age structure of the population.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which of the following is a POSITIVE consequence of an ageing population for Mauritius?
options: There are more children in school, requiring more teachers and classrooms
Healthcare spending falls because older people are healthier than young people
Older people have accumulated skills and experience that can benefit businesses and communities
The military age population grows, strengthening national defence
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Older people have accumulated skills and experience that can benefit businesses and communities
acceptableAnswers: Older people have accumulated skills and experience that can benefit businesses and communities
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Ageing has challenges but also some advantages — think about what older people bring.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Experienced older workers (especially if kept in employment or volunteering) contribute valuable knowledge, mentorship and social capital. Many countries are exploring how to harness this rather than simply manage the costs of ageing.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: The graph shows that Mauritius's population density rose from around 350 per km² in 1970 to around 620 per km² in 2015. What caused this?
options: The population grew through natural increase while the land area of the island remained fixed
The government reduced the number of districts, making each one smaller
The land area of Mauritius shrank as the sea rose
Emigration brought millions of new people to the island
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: The population grew through natural increase while the land area of the island remained fixed
acceptableAnswers: The population grew through natural increase while the land area of the island remained fixed
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Density = people ÷ area. If the area stays the same and people increase, density rises.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Mauritius is a fixed-size island. As the population grew through natural increase and migration, the same amount of land had to support more people, raising density.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Mauritius's crude death rate was around 8 per 1,000 in 2020. Which factor MOST explains why this is higher than the crude death rate of some younger-population countries?
options: A higher crude death rate always means a less healthy population
Mauritius has worse healthcare than younger-population countries
Mauritius deliberately reduces healthcare spending to keep the death rate high
Mauritius has an older age structure, so more people are in the age groups where death is most common
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Mauritius has an older age structure, so more people are in the age groups where death is most common
acceptableAnswers: Mauritius has an older age structure, so more people are in the age groups where death is most common
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: A crude rate reflects the whole population; an older population has more deaths even with good healthcare.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: A crude death rate is affected by age structure: an older population has more people in age groups with naturally higher mortality, raising the crude rate even when healthcare is excellent. This is why crude rates must be interpreted alongside age structure.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which part of a population pyramid shows the number of people of WORKING AGE?
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: The middle section (roughly ages 15–64)
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: The working-age population is usually defined as 15–64.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The middle section of the pyramid (15–64 age groups) represents the working-age population — those contributing to the labour force and tax base that funds services for the young and elderly.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which statement correctly identifies a LIMITATION of life expectancy as a development indicator?
options: It is an average that can conceal large differences between rich and poor, urban and rural populations
It is always inaccurate because death cannot be measured
It measures only the health of children, not of adults
It only applies to countries with more than 10 million people
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: It is an average that can conceal large differences between rich and poor, urban and rural populations
acceptableAnswers: It is an average that can conceal large differences between rich and poor, urban and rural populations
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Think about what an average hides.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: A national average life expectancy can look healthy while hiding sharp inequalities: if wealthy urban residents live to 80 while poor rural communities average 60, the national figure of around 70 conceals this gap.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Mauritius is often cited as a success story for addressing the challenges of ageing. Which policy combination explains this?
options: Stopping all healthcare spending and letting the market decide who receives treatment
A universal pension, free healthcare for all ages, and investment in productive employment for older workers
Forcing all people over 65 to emigrate so the dependency ratio falls
Importing a large young workforce each year to replace retiring Mauritians
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: A universal pension, free healthcare for all ages, and investment in productive employment for older workers
acceptableAnswers: A universal pension, free healthcare for all ages, and investment in productive employment for older workers
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: The Mauritian welfare state plays a central role.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Mauritius has a universal Basic Retirement Pension, free healthcare and a culture of intergenerational support within families, all of which cushion the effects of ageing even as the fiscal pressure grows.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: A country has a birth rate of 12 per 1,000 and a death rate of 14 per 1,000. What is happening to its population (ignoring migration)?
options: It is growing — births exceed deaths by 2 per 1,000
It is declining — deaths exceed births by 2 per 1,000
It is stable — births and deaths are equal
It is growing rapidly because the total figure is 26 per 1,000
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: It is declining — deaths exceed births by 2 per 1,000
acceptableAnswers: It is declining — deaths exceed births by 2 per 1,000
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Natural increase = births − deaths. A negative result means decline.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: 12 − 14 = −2 per 1,000. The population is experiencing natural decrease: more people are dying than are being born. Migration is the only way the total population could still grow.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: A population pyramid for Mauritius in 2050 (projected) shows the widest bulge at the 50–70 age group. What does this tell us about the birth rate in approximately 1980–2000?
options: Birth rates were very low in that period, which is why the bulge appears at that age
The death rate was extremely high in that period, killing all other cohorts
Birth rates were relatively high in that period, producing the large cohort that will be 50–70 in 2050
The data for other age groups was lost and the bulge is an artefact
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Birth rates were relatively high in that period, producing the large cohort that will be 50–70 in 2050
acceptableAnswers: Birth rates were relatively high in that period, producing the large cohort that will be 50–70 in 2050
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: People who are 50–70 in 2050 were born in 1980–2000.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: A wide bulge at 50–70 in 2050 means many people were born in 1980–2000 — indicating that birth rates were higher in those decades than in more recent years.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Why do geographers distinguish between population DENSITY and population DISTRIBUTION?
options: Distribution measures only urban populations; density measures only rural ones
Distribution is calculated by dividing area by population; density by dividing population by area
Density measures how many people per unit area; distribution describes where within a country they are clustered
Density and distribution are two words for exactly the same concept
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Density measures how many people per unit area; distribution describes where within a country they are clustered
acceptableAnswers: Density measures how many people per unit area; distribution describes where within a country they are clustered
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: One gives a number; the other shows a pattern.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Density is a numerical measure (people per km²); distribution is a spatial concept showing where people are concentrated — along coasts, in valleys, in cities. Both are needed to understand population geography fully.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: A district has a population of 240 000 and covers 80 km². What is its population density?
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: 3 000 people/km²
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Divide population by area.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: 240 000 ÷ 80 = 3 000 people per km². Mauritius as a whole has one of the highest population densities in sub-Saharan Africa because a large population lives on a small island.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which part of Mauritius tends to have the highest population density?
options: Rodrigues, because it has fewer towns
The eastern coast, which is the driest part of the island
The northern coastal plain and the area around Port Louis
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: The northern coastal plain and the area around Port Louis
acceptableAnswers: The northern coastal plain and the area around Port Louis
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: People cluster near the capital city and on flat, accessible land.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The Port Louis area and the northern coastal plain are most densely populated because of proximity to the capital, economic opportunities and flat terrain. The forested plateau is less settled.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What does an uneven distribution of population across districts tell a geographer?
options: Governments set rules deciding exactly how many people live in each district
Some areas have more attractive conditions for living and working than others
Population density is always highest where rainfall is greatest
Every district has exactly the same resources and opportunities
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Some areas have more attractive conditions for living and working than others
acceptableAnswers: Some areas have more attractive conditions for living and working than others
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: People choose where to live based on available opportunities.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Uneven distribution reflects variations in economic opportunity, infrastructure, terrain and services. People concentrate where jobs, schools, hospitals and transport are most accessible.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Mauritius covers about 2 040 km² and had a population of roughly 1.3 million in 2020. Approximately what was its population density?
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: 637 people/km²
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: 1 300 000 ÷ 2 040 ≈ 637 people/km², making Mauritius one of the most densely populated countries in Africa, comparable to many European nations.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What shape of population pyramid would have been typical of Mauritius in the 1960s?
options: An inverted triangle with the oldest groups most numerous
A wide base narrowing quickly toward the top, showing many young people
A rectangular shape with equal numbers at every age
A narrow base widening toward the middle, showing few young people
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: A wide base narrowing quickly toward the top, showing many young people
acceptableAnswers: A wide base narrowing quickly toward the top, showing many young people
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: High birth rates in the past → many young people → wide base.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: High birth rates and relatively early death gave Mauritius a classic wide-based pyramid in the 1960s — lots of young people and relatively few elderly, typical of a developing country at that time.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which feature of a population pyramid shows that a country has recently experienced a "baby boom" followed by declining birth rates?
options: A very wide base that remains constant across all young age groups
A bulge in the middle age groups with a narrower base below it
An equal width at all age levels from 0 to 80
A complete absence of bars for any age group under 20
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: A bulge in the middle age groups with a narrower base below it
acceptableAnswers: A bulge in the middle age groups with a narrower base below it
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: The baby boom produced a large cohort; fewer births since then produced a narrower base.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: A bulge in the middle of the pyramid represents the large baby-boom cohort. The narrower base below them reflects the subsequent fall in birth rates — exactly the shape Mauritius's pyramid shows today.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What is the crude birth rate?
options: The number of live births per 1 000 of the total population per year
The total number of babies born in a country in any given century
The number of births minus the number of deaths in a single year
The percentage of women who have more than three children
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: The number of live births per 1 000 of the total population per year
acceptableAnswers: The number of live births per 1 000 of the total population per year
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: It is expressed per 1 000 people per year.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The crude birth rate is the number of live births per 1 000 of the total population in a year. "Crude" means it is not adjusted for the age structure of the population.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Mauritius's crude birth rate was approximately 34 per 1 000 in 1968 and 12 per 1 000 in 2020. Which factors best explain the fall?
options: Large-scale emigration of all women of childbearing age
A dramatic increase in the death rate that reduced the base population
Family planning, rising education levels and urbanisation
A government law limiting every family to one child
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Family planning, rising education levels and urbanisation
acceptableAnswers: Family planning, rising education levels and urbanisation
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: These are the standard demographic transition factors.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Family planning, rising female education, growing female employment and urbanisation all reduce birth rates — the mechanisms behind Mauritius's demographic transition from the 1960s onward.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: If Mauritius has a birth rate of 12 per 1 000 and a death rate of 8 per 1 000, what is the rate of natural increase?
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Natural increase = birth rate minus death rate.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: 12 − 8 = 4 per 1 000. This is a low natural increase, consistent with a country in the late stages of the demographic transition.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Life expectancy at birth for Mauritian women is approximately 78 years. What does this figure mean?
options: No woman born in Mauritius will ever live beyond 78
Every woman currently aged 78 will die within the year
A girl born today can expect, on average, to live to about 78
Women earn 78% of the male average wage in Mauritius
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: A girl born today can expect, on average, to live to about 78
acceptableAnswers: A girl born today can expect, on average, to live to about 78
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Life expectancy is an average projected from current health conditions.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Life expectancy at birth is an average: it projects, based on current mortality rates, how long a newborn is likely to live. Some individuals will live shorter lives, others longer.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Why do women in Mauritius (as in most countries) have a higher life expectancy than men?
options: Men are required by law to retire earlier, shortening their lives
Biological factors and differences in risk-taking behaviour and occupational hazards
Men leave Mauritius permanently at age 50 on average, removing them from statistics
Women have access to better healthcare only from the age of 60
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Biological factors and differences in risk-taking behaviour and occupational hazards
acceptableAnswers: Biological factors and differences in risk-taking behaviour and occupational hazards
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: The gender gap in life expectancy is a global pattern, not unique to Mauritius.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Women have a longer life expectancy worldwide due to biological advantages and because men are statistically more likely to engage in risky behaviour and work in dangerous occupations.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What is the main reason Mauritius has an ageing population?
options: The government compulsorily relocated young people to Rodrigues
A massive wave of elderly immigrants has arrived from Europe
Birth rates have risen dramatically in the last decade
Birth rates have fallen while people live longer due to better healthcare
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Birth rates have fallen while people live longer due to better healthcare
acceptableAnswers: Birth rates have fallen while people live longer due to better healthcare
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: An ageing population requires both fewer young people being born AND older people surviving longer.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Mauritius has both falling birth rates and rising life expectancy. Together these produce an ageing population: the proportion aged over 60 grows as fewer children are born and people live into old age.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which economic challenge is directly linked to an ageing population in Mauritius?
options: Building more primary schools to accommodate the rising number of children
Recruiting more young immigrants to fill unskilled manufacturing jobs
Funding pension and healthcare costs from a proportionally smaller working-age tax base
Expanding sugar production to feed a growing elderly rural population
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Funding pension and healthcare costs from a proportionally smaller working-age tax base
acceptableAnswers: Funding pension and healthcare costs from a proportionally smaller working-age tax base
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: More old people need more support; fewer working people pay the taxes for it.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: As more Mauritians live into old age, the cost of pensions and public healthcare rises. But the working-age population that pays taxes to fund these services is proportionally shrinking, creating fiscal pressure.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: A Mauritian worker moves from the village of Mahebourg to work in an office in Port Louis. What type of migration is this?
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Internal migration
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Both places are in the same country.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Moving within a country's borders is internal migration. Moving from Mahebourg to Port Louis stays within Mauritius, so no international border is crossed.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What has been the dominant direction of internal migration in Mauritius since the 1970s?
options: From towns to rural areas as people escape urban overcrowding
From all coastal areas toward the central forest reserve
From rural areas to towns and cities, especially the Port Louis corridor
From the main island to Rodrigues for agricultural opportunities
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: From rural areas to towns and cities, especially the Port Louis corridor
acceptableAnswers: From rural areas to towns and cities, especially the Port Louis corridor
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Think about where the new factories and offices were built.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: EPZ factories and service sector jobs concentrated in and around Port Louis and the northern urban corridor, drawing workers from rural sugar estates — a classic rural-to-urban internal migration pattern.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: A Mauritian graduate moves to France because French universities offer better PhD programmes. Is this a push or pull factor?
options: A push factor, because something in Mauritius forced the person to leave
A pull factor, because the attraction is in the destination
Both equally: push and pull factors never apply to education
Neither: education migration is not classified as migration at all
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: A pull factor, because the attraction is in the destination
acceptableAnswers: A pull factor, because the attraction is in the destination
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Ask: is the reason about fleeing the home or being drawn to the destination?
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Better PhD programmes at the destination draw the graduate toward France — a classic pull factor. Push factors would be problems at home that drive the person away.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which combination correctly pairs a push and a pull factor?
options: Push: high wages in the destination — Pull: unemployment at home
Push: political persecution at home — Pull: democratic safety in the destination
Push: family reunion in the destination — Pull: low wages at home
Push: better climate in the destination — Pull: war at home
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Push: political persecution at home — Pull: democratic safety in the destination
acceptableAnswers: Push: political persecution at home — Pull: democratic safety in the destination
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Pushes are negative conditions at home; pulls are positive conditions at the destination.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Political persecution (push) drives people away from home; democratic safety (pull) draws them to the destination. The other options have the push/pull labels reversed.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Under international law, which organisation is responsible for protecting refugees?
options: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
acceptableAnswers: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: The clue is in the title — it names refugees directly.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The UNHCR (United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees) is the international body mandated to protect refugees and find durable solutions — repatriation, local integration or resettlement.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: The 1951 Refugee Convention defines a refugee as a person who has fled their country due to a well-founded fear of persecution based on which grounds?
options: Race, religion, nationality, political opinion or membership of a particular social group
Natural disaster such as a cyclone or earthquake in their home country
Poverty alone, or the desire for a better-paid job in another country
Failure to obtain a valid passport or travel document
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Race, religion, nationality, political opinion or membership of a particular social group
acceptableAnswers: Race, religion, nationality, political opinion or membership of a particular social group
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: The Convention is specific about the grounds — economic hardship is not enough.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The 1951 Convention protects people fleeing persecution for race, religion, nationality, political opinion or membership of a particular social group. Economic migrants and disaster-displaced people are not automatically covered.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Approximately how far is Rodrigues from the main island of Mauritius?
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: About 560 km to the east
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: It lies well to the east, not just offshore.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Rodrigues is approximately 560 km east of the main island — far enough that it needs its own local governance, given the distance and infrequent transport links.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What is the main economic activity of Rodrigues?
options: Small-scale agriculture, fishing and emerging tourism
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Small-scale agriculture, fishing and emerging tourism
acceptableAnswers: Small-scale agriculture, fishing and emerging tourism
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Rodrigues lacks the flat land and scale for sugar or the infrastructure for finance.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Rodrigues relies on small-scale agriculture (lentils, onions, garlic), fishing and a growing tourism sector attracted by its relative isolation and natural environment.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What traditional economic activity has historically supported the small population of Agalega?
options: Deep-sea fishing for the Japanese market
Tourism from Europe and South Africa
Coconut production and the export of copra
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Coconut production and the export of copra
acceptableAnswers: Coconut production and the export of copra
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Coconut palms dominate the landscape of both islands.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Agalega's economy has traditionally centred on coconut cultivation and the export of copra (dried coconut meat used for oil), managed historically by the Mauritius government as a state enterprise.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What is the main transport link between Rodrigues and the main island of Mauritius?
options: A bridge that was completed in the 1990s
A submarine tunnel used by both vehicles and rail
Daily high-speed ferry from Port Louis
Regular flights and a weekly cargo/passenger ship service
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Regular flights and a weekly cargo/passenger ship service
acceptableAnswers: Regular flights and a weekly cargo/passenger ship service
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: For a small island 560 km away, both air and sea links are used.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Rodrigues is served by regular flights from Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam Airport and a weekly ship (the MV Mauritius Trochetia), which carries cargo and passengers. There is no bridge or tunnel.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which service is hardest to provide adequately on the outer islands because of their remoteness?
options: Primary school education for children aged 5–11
Retail shops selling basic food products
Specialist hospital care requiring advanced equipment
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Specialist hospital care requiring advanced equipment
acceptableAnswers: Specialist hospital care requiring advanced equipment
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Some services need large facilities that cannot exist on a small remote island.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Specialist hospital care (surgery, intensive care, specialist consultants) requires costly equipment and staff that a small remote island cannot sustain. Patients must be evacuated to the main island, which is expensive and sometimes dangerous.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which warning class indicates that a cyclone is at its most dangerous level in Mauritius?
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Class IV
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Classes run from I to IV; the highest number is the most severe.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Class IV is the highest alert level, indicating that a very intense cyclone is either over or very close to Mauritius. Residents must remain indoors and all outdoor activity ceases.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Why are cyclones particularly damaging to small island nations like Mauritius?
options: A small island has no large land mass to weaken a cyclone before it reaches settled areas
Mauritius lacks a meteorological service capable of tracking cyclones
Cyclones only ever form directly above small islands in the Indian Ocean
Small islands always produce stronger cyclones than large countries
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: A small island has no large land mass to weaken a cyclone before it reaches settled areas
acceptableAnswers: A small island has no large land mass to weaken a cyclone before it reaches settled areas
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Think about how cyclones weaken when they cross land.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Cyclones weaken when they move over land. A small island offers no large land mass to dissipate a storm's energy, so it hits settled areas close to full strength. The whole island is within the damage radius.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What long-term infrastructure change followed the destructive cyclone Carol in 1960?
options: The closure of all beaches to tourism for ten years
The construction of an underground bunker network across the island
A major programme to replace wood and iron housing with concrete construction
The permanent evacuation of all coastal villages to the central plateau
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: A major programme to replace wood and iron housing with concrete construction
acceptableAnswers: A major programme to replace wood and iron housing with concrete construction
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: The lesson from mass destruction is to build more durably.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Cyclone Carol's devastation accelerated a government-backed shift to concrete housing, which could withstand high winds far better than the traditional wood and corrugated iron structures.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: How does climate change threaten Mauritius's tourism industry specifically?
options: Climate change is predicted to strengthen the reef, reducing its visual appeal
Rising sea levels and beach erosion reduce the coastal assets that attract visitors
Warmer temperatures drive tourists away to colder destinations exclusively
Climate change increases rainfall, making outdoor activities impossible year-round
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Rising sea levels and beach erosion reduce the coastal assets that attract visitors
acceptableAnswers: Rising sea levels and beach erosion reduce the coastal assets that attract visitors
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Mauritius sells its beaches and reef — both are coastal.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Tourism in Mauritius depends heavily on beaches and coral reefs. Rising seas erode beaches and more intense storms damage reefs, directly threatening the natural assets the industry is built on.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which commitment has Mauritius made under international climate agreements?
options: To build a nuclear power station with French assistance
To reduce greenhouse gas emissions and transition toward renewable energy
To increase coal production to diversify its energy supply
To ban all tourism as it produces too much carbon dioxide
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: To reduce greenhouse gas emissions and transition toward renewable energy
acceptableAnswers: To reduce greenhouse gas emissions and transition toward renewable energy
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Small island states are among the most vulnerable to climate change and most vocal advocates for action.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Mauritius is a signatory to the Paris Agreement and has committed to reducing emissions and expanding renewable energy (solar, wind) to reduce its dependence on imported fossil fuels.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What is one measure individuals can take to reduce environmental damage in Mauritius?
options: Increasing car use to avoid public transport congestion
Reducing single-use plastic waste and recycling where facilities exist
Cutting down native forest to plant more sugar cane
Releasing treated sewage directly into coastal lagoons
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Reducing single-use plastic waste and recycling where facilities exist
acceptableAnswers: Reducing single-use plastic waste and recycling where facilities exist
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Individual action targets consumption choices.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Reducing single-use plastic prevents litter from entering the ocean and harming marine life. Mauritius has introduced regulations on plastic bags as part of broader environmental policy.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: The MV Wakashio ran aground off Mauritius in 2020, causing an oil spill. What did this event highlight about the island's vulnerability?
options: The incident proved that coral reefs are entirely immune to oil pollution
Mauritius has such a large coastline that a spill affects very little of it
A single incident can cause catastrophic damage to a small island's fragile marine ecosystem
Oil spills are beneficial because they fertilise coral growth
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: A single incident can cause catastrophic damage to a small island's fragile marine ecosystem
acceptableAnswers: A single incident can cause catastrophic damage to a small island's fragile marine ecosystem
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Small places have less capacity to absorb large shocks.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The Wakashio spill demonstrated that a single environmental incident can affect a significant proportion of a small island's coastline, damaging tourism, fisheries and biodiversity in ways that take years to recover.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: How is the President of Mauritius chosen?
options: Elected by the National Assembly, not by a direct popular vote
Elected directly by all citizens in a national presidential election
Chosen by the Prime Minister alone without any parliamentary vote
Appointed by the British monarch as a legacy of the colonial period
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Elected by the National Assembly, not by a direct popular vote
acceptableAnswers: Elected by the National Assembly, not by a direct popular vote
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Mauritius is a parliamentary republic, not a presidential one.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The President is elected by the National Assembly. Mauritius has a parliamentary system in which the Prime Minister holds executive power and the President performs a largely ceremonial role.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: In the Mauritian electoral system, what is the "Best Loser" system designed to ensure?
options: That the best-performing losing party automatically forms the government
That the Prime Minister is always from the party with the most seats
That ethnic minority communities are represented in the National Assembly
That losing candidates in sports competitions receive a prize
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: That ethnic minority communities are represented in the National Assembly
acceptableAnswers: That ethnic minority communities are represented in the National Assembly
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: It is a constitutional mechanism specific to Mauritius's multicultural society.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The Best Loser system allocates up to eight additional seats to candidates from under-represented ethnic communities, helping to ensure that all major communities have a voice in Parliament.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: How often must a general election be held in Mauritius (at most)?
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Every 5 years
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Five years is the standard parliamentary term in Commonwealth nations.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The Mauritian constitution requires a general election at least every 5 years. The Prime Minister may call one earlier if necessary, but cannot delay beyond the five-year term.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which chapter of the Mauritian Constitution protects fundamental rights such as freedom of speech and religion?
options: The Chapter on the Appointment of Judges
The Chapter on the Protection of Fundamental Rights and Freedoms
The Chapter on Foreign Affairs and Trade Treaties
The Chapter on Public Finance and Taxation
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: The Chapter on the Protection of Fundamental Rights and Freedoms
acceptableAnswers: The Chapter on the Protection of Fundamental Rights and Freedoms
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: The Constitution protects rights in a dedicated section.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The Chapter on the Protection of Fundamental Rights and Freedoms guarantees rights including freedom of expression, freedom of religion and the right to a fair trial — enforceable through the courts.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What happens if an Act of Parliament contradicts the Mauritian Constitution?
options: The Prime Minister chooses which document to follow
The Constitution is automatically amended to accommodate the Act
The Act is declared void by the Supreme Court
The Act takes effect for five years until the next election
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: The Act is declared void by the Supreme Court
acceptableAnswers: The Act is declared void by the Supreme Court
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: The Constitution is the supreme law — no ordinary law can override it.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The Supreme Court can strike down any Act of Parliament that contradicts the Constitution. This constitutional supremacy is the foundation of the rule of law in Mauritius.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which institution is responsible for interpreting the Constitution of Mauritius?
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: The Supreme Court
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Courts, not politicians, interpret the law.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The Supreme Court is the highest court in Mauritius and the body constitutionally mandated to interpret the Constitution and rule on whether legislation complies with it.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What type of tax is applied to goods and services purchased in Mauritius?
options: Import duty on all goods, including locally made ones
A flat poll tax per adult per year
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Value Added Tax (VAT)
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: VAT is collected at each stage of production and at the point of sale.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Mauritius has a Value Added Tax (VAT) applied to most goods and services at the point of sale. The MRA collects VAT along with income tax, customs duty and corporate tax.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Why is paying taxes a civic responsibility rather than just a legal obligation?
options: Taxes are paid only by the wealthy and do not affect ordinary citizens
Taxes fund the public services — schools, hospitals, roads — that benefit everyone
Taxes are completely voluntary and no one is compelled to pay them
Tax revenue goes directly to the President's personal account
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Taxes fund the public services — schools, hospitals, roads — that benefit everyone
acceptableAnswers: Taxes fund the public services — schools, hospitals, roads — that benefit everyone
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Think about where public services come from.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Taxes are the means by which citizens collectively fund public goods — education, healthcare, infrastructure — that would not exist if everyone only paid for what they personally used.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: When was the universal old age pension introduced in Mauritius?
options: After 2000 as part of a modern reform
It has not yet been introduced as of 2024
Only in 1992 when Mauritius became a republic
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: 1950s — before independence
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Mauritius built its welfare state remarkably early.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Mauritius introduced a universal old age pension in the 1950s — one of the earliest such provisions in the developing world, paid to all citizens above retirement age regardless of employment history.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What makes Mauritius's public health system a "welfare" system?
options: Patients pay a fee for every consultation and procedure
Only workers who pay into a special insurance fund receive treatment
It provides care to all citizens free at the point of use, funded by general taxation
Only children and the elderly receive free care; all adults pay full costs
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: It provides care to all citizens free at the point of use, funded by general taxation
acceptableAnswers: It provides care to all citizens free at the point of use, funded by general taxation
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: A welfare system is universal and tax-funded.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Mauritius operates a universal public health service: any citizen can walk into a government hospital or clinic and receive treatment at no direct charge, with costs met from general tax revenue.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What does the principle of the "presumption of innocence" mean in Mauritian law?
options: Judges presume that all police reports are accurate and complete
An accused person is assumed innocent until the court finds them guilty
A person is assumed guilty if they cannot immediately prove their innocence
The government presumes that every citizen is obeying the law at all times
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: An accused person is assumed innocent until the court finds them guilty
acceptableAnswers: An accused person is assumed innocent until the court finds them guilty
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: This is a cornerstone of criminal law in all democratic countries.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The presumption of innocence means the prosecution must prove guilt; the accused does not have to prove innocence. It protects citizens from arbitrary conviction.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What is the role of an independent judiciary in a democratic state like Mauritius?
options: To advise the Prime Minister on which laws to introduce to Parliament
To apply the law impartially, without influence from the government or any other party
To collect taxes on behalf of the Mauritius Revenue Authority
To implement the policies of whichever political party wins the election
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: To apply the law impartially, without influence from the government or any other party
acceptableAnswers: To apply the law impartially, without influence from the government or any other party
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Independence means judges follow the law, not politicians.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: An independent judiciary applies the law impartially: judges cannot be removed for their decisions, ensuring that even government actions can be challenged legally.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which of the following is an example of digital (online) media?
options: A news website updated in real time
A radio bulletin broadcast on FM
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: A news website updated in real time
acceptableAnswers: A news website updated in real time
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Digital media is delivered via the internet.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: A news website is digital media — accessed online. Print, radio and television are traditional media, even when their content is also available online.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What distinguishes social media from traditional broadcast media?
options: Traditional media has been entirely replaced by social media since 2010
Social media is only available in printed form
Social media is regulated more strictly than any other type of media
Social media allows users to both receive and produce content; traditional media is one-way
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Social media allows users to both receive and produce content; traditional media is one-way
acceptableAnswers: Social media allows users to both receive and produce content; traditional media is one-way
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Think about who can speak in each model.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Traditional broadcast media is one-to-many (one source, many readers/viewers); social media is many-to-many, allowing any user to produce and share content as well as consume it.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: A newspaper investigates corruption in a government ministry and publishes its findings. Which media role does this illustrate?
options: The entertainment role — amusing and distracting readers
The watchdog role — holding power to account
The advertising role — promoting commercial products
The educational role — teaching readers technical skills
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: The watchdog role — holding power to account
acceptableAnswers: The watchdog role — holding power to account
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Investigating wrongdoing by those in authority is the defining watchdog function.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The watchdog role means the press scrutinises those in power and reports wrongdoing, providing a check on government and corporate behaviour that is fundamental to democracy.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What is the risk of "media concentration" — when one owner controls most of the media?
options: Media concentration increases journalistic independence and reduces censorship
News may reflect the owner's interests rather than the public interest, reducing scrutiny of power
Competition between outlets always increases when one owner controls them all
Audiences gain access to a wider range of viewpoints and perspectives
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: News may reflect the owner's interests rather than the public interest, reducing scrutiny of power
acceptableAnswers: News may reflect the owner's interests rather than the public interest, reducing scrutiny of power
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: An owner with business interests may not want those interests reported critically.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: When one owner controls multiple outlets, editorial decisions may favour the owner's interests, suppressing coverage critical of them and narrowing the range of views the public hears.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which of the following is an example of media supporting learning positively?
options: Reading only posts from friends rather than any educational content
Spending six hours a day playing online games instead of studying
Watching a documentary on climate change as part of a geography lesson
Sharing exam answers on a messaging application
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Watching a documentary on climate change as part of a geography lesson
acceptableAnswers: Watching a documentary on climate change as part of a geography lesson
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Media supports learning when it extends or reinforces what is taught.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: A documentary used in class extends learning beyond the textbook with visuals, expert interviews and real-world examples — a productive use of media in education.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Research shows a link between heavy social media use and lower self-esteem among teenagers. What mechanism best explains this?
options: Low self-esteem is caused entirely by a lack of physical exercise, not by screens
Teenagers who use social media are simply less intelligent than those who do not
Comparing oneself to the idealised images others post online can create unrealistic standards
Social media physically damages the brain cells responsible for self-confidence
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Comparing oneself to the idealised images others post online can create unrealistic standards
acceptableAnswers: Comparing oneself to the idealised images others post online can create unrealistic standards
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Social media shows curated highlight reels, not everyday reality.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: People share their best moments on social media; comparing one's ordinary life with others' curated highlights creates unrealistic expectations and can lower self-esteem.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which term describes a family in which only a single parent lives with the children?
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: A lone-parent family
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: One adult, not two, heads the household.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: A lone-parent family consists of one parent (mother or father) living with one or more children. It may result from separation, divorce, bereavement or a choice not to form a partnership.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What is a "reconstituted" family?
options: A family consisting of grandparents raising their grandchildren only
A family in which both parents work full-time outside the home
A traditional family where both parents were born on the same island
A family formed when two adults with children from previous relationships combine into one household
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: A family formed when two adults with children from previous relationships combine into one household
acceptableAnswers: A family formed when two adults with children from previous relationships combine into one household
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Think of the prefix "re-" meaning again — a new family assembled from existing ones.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: A reconstituted family (also called blended or step-family) forms when partners who each have children from earlier relationships join together, creating a new household with step-siblings and step-parents.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which of the following is an economic function of the family?
options: Collecting taxes on behalf of the Mauritius Revenue Authority
Providing financial support and pooling income to meet household needs
Deciding the national budget and setting interest rates
Building and maintaining public roads and schools
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Providing financial support and pooling income to meet household needs
acceptableAnswers: Providing financial support and pooling income to meet household needs
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: The economic function is about money within the family unit.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Families pool income and share resources to pay for housing, food, education and healthcare — a fundamental economic safety net for individual members.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What is the "reproductive function" of the family, as sociologists define it?
options: Producing goods and services for sale to other families
Recreating the same family structure identically each generation
Bearing and raising children to ensure the continuation of society
Reproducing the family's income level in the next generation
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Bearing and raising children to ensure the continuation of society
acceptableAnswers: Bearing and raising children to ensure the continuation of society
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Reproduction here means producing the next generation, not just biology.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The reproductive function encompasses both having children and raising them to become productive members of society — without which the population and social order could not continue.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Traditional gender roles in Mauritius often assigned cooking and childcare to women. What type of factor are these roles?
options: Legal — they are set by the Mauritian constitution
Biological — they are determined by genetics at birth
Social and cultural — they are learned, not biological
Economic — they are determined by the labour market only
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Social and cultural — they are learned, not biological
acceptableAnswers: Social and cultural — they are learned, not biological
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: If roles differ between societies and change over time, they cannot be purely biological.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Gender roles are socially constructed: they are learned through upbringing, culture and media. Because they vary across societies and have changed dramatically over decades, they are cultural rather than biological.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Despite high female labour-force participation in Mauritius, women are still under-represented in senior management roles. What term describes this barrier?
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: The glass ceiling
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: You can see the top but cannot reach it.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The glass ceiling describes the invisible barrier that prevents women from advancing to the highest levels of organisations, despite formal equal opportunities and visible presence in the workforce below.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: How has globalisation acted as a force of social change in Mauritius?
options: It has caused Mauritius to completely abandon all its traditional cultural practices
It has reduced the standard of living of all Mauritians since independence
It has isolated Mauritius from the rest of the world by cutting trade links
It has introduced new values, consumption patterns and cultural influences from abroad
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: It has introduced new values, consumption patterns and cultural influences from abroad
acceptableAnswers: It has introduced new values, consumption patterns and cultural influences from abroad
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Globalisation connects societies, bringing cultural exchange.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Globalisation brings foreign media, products and ideas, changing tastes, family structures and values. In Mauritius this is visible in fashion, music, food and the growing influence of digital culture.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: How does education act as a force of social change?
options: It reduces social mobility by keeping people in the occupations of their parents
Education has no measurable effect on social change in any society
It always preserves traditional society by transmitting only existing values to the next generation
It equips individuals with knowledge and skills that allow them to question traditions and take on new roles
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: It equips individuals with knowledge and skills that allow them to question traditions and take on new roles
acceptableAnswers: It equips individuals with knowledge and skills that allow them to question traditions and take on new roles
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Educated people can access new information and opportunities.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Education develops critical thinking and opens access to new occupations, enabling individuals to challenge inherited roles, change social class and contribute to wider social transformation.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What makes a social movement different from a political party?
options: A social movement seeks to change society without necessarily seeking to hold government office
There is no difference — social movements and political parties are the same thing
A social movement must be registered with the electoral commission
A social movement is only allowed to operate during election campaigns
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: A social movement seeks to change society without necessarily seeking to hold government office
acceptableAnswers: A social movement seeks to change society without necessarily seeking to hold government office
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Environmental groups, student movements and labour unions are social movements, not parties.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: A social movement organises citizens around a cause — environmental protection, education rights, workers' rights — without the primary aim of winning government power, which distinguishes it from a political party.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which of the following is an example of informal social control?
options: Friends and family expressing disapproval of someone's behaviour
A judge sentencing someone to community service
A police officer arresting a person for speeding
Parliament passing a new law against littering
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Friends and family expressing disapproval of someone's behaviour
acceptableAnswers: Friends and family expressing disapproval of someone's behaviour
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Informal control uses social pressure, not law.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Informal social control operates through social pressure — the disapproval of peers, family or community. It does not involve the formal legal system and is often more immediately powerful than the law.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What is the difference between upward and downward social mobility?
options: Upward mobility means moving to a higher social position; downward means moving to a lower one
Upward mobility means moving to a wealthier city; downward means returning to a village
Upward mobility is always permanent; downward mobility always temporary
They are opposite terms for the same experience, depending on who is reporting it
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Upward mobility means moving to a higher social position; downward means moving to a lower one
acceptableAnswers: Upward mobility means moving to a higher social position; downward means moving to a lower one
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Up and down refer to social position, not physical movement.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Upward social mobility (e.g. through education, promotion) raises a person's social position; downward mobility (e.g. through job loss, illness) lowers it. Both are possible across generations or within a lifetime.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Aapravasi Ghat in Port Louis is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. What historic role did it play?
options: It was the site where Mauritius's independence was proclaimed in 1968
It was the seat of government during British colonial rule
It served as the main sugar export terminal until 1970
It was the landing point for Indian indentured labourers arriving after 1834
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: It was the landing point for Indian indentured labourers arriving after 1834
acceptableAnswers: It was the landing point for Indian indentured labourers arriving after 1834
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: It processed people arriving on a specific labour system.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Aapravasi Ghat was the immigration depot through which around half a million Indian indentured labourers entered Mauritius after the abolition of slavery in 1835. Its World Heritage status recognises the indenture system as a defining migration in world history.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Why did the abolition of slavery in 1835 lead directly to indentured labour from India?
options: Britain prohibited all further migration to Mauritius after 1835
The abolition was immediately followed by full mechanisation of all sugar production
Freed slaves voluntarily chose to continue working on estates under the same conditions
Sugar estate owners needed a replacement workforce and turned to contracted labour from India
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Sugar estate owners needed a replacement workforce and turned to contracted labour from India
acceptableAnswers: Sugar estate owners needed a replacement workforce and turned to contracted labour from India
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Sugar production continued — so who did the work?
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: When slavery was abolished, estate owners could no longer rely on unpaid labour. They recruited indentured workers from India under fixed-term contracts — a system that brought hundreds of thousands to Mauritius over the following decades.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What proportion of Mauritius's population today is of South Asian (mainly Indian) descent?
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: About two thirds
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: The indenture system brought the largest single group to the island.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Approximately two thirds of Mauritius's population descends from Indian indentured labourers — the largest group, which is why Hindi, Tamil, Telugu and Urdu are spoken alongside French, English and Creole.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: How does the African diaspora maintain cultural links with Mauritius today?
options: Through Creole language, Sega music and shared cultural practices rooted in the African slave experience
Mauritius has no cultural links with Africa because all African cultural practices were lost
Through compulsory African history lessons taught in every Mauritian school by law
Through formal political unions between African states and Mauritius
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Through Creole language, Sega music and shared cultural practices rooted in the African slave experience
acceptableAnswers: Through Creole language, Sega music and shared cultural practices rooted in the African slave experience
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Culture survived even when people were separated from their origins.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Mauritian Creole and Sega music are rooted in the experience of enslaved Africans and Malagasy people, preserved and developed over generations as living links to African cultural heritage.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which religion brought by French settlers remains widely practised in Mauritius today?
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Roman Catholicism
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: French colonists brought the religion of their home country.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Roman Catholicism was introduced by French settlers and remains the religion of the majority of the general population (Creole and Franco-Mauritian communities), with major churches dating from the colonial period.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: How do Mauritius's legal and educational systems reflect both French and British colonial legacies?
options: All laws are entirely French and all education is entirely British with no overlap
The French legacy is limited to cuisine; the British legacy covers everything else
Civil law follows the French Napoleonic Code while government and examinations follow British parliamentary and educational traditions
Both systems were abolished at independence and replaced with a unique Mauritian system
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Civil law follows the French Napoleonic Code while government and examinations follow British parliamentary and educational traditions
acceptableAnswers: Civil law follows the French Napoleonic Code while government and examinations follow British parliamentary and educational traditions
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: France ruled first (law); Britain ruled second (government and schools).
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Mauritius has a hybrid legal system: civil law (property, family, contracts) follows the Napoleonic Code from French rule, while the parliamentary system, public examinations (Cambridge) and use of English reflect British rule.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What does COMESA stand for, and what type of organisation is it?
options: Council of Mediterranean and Sub-Saharan Associations — a cultural body
Commonwealth of Middle Eastern and South Asian states — a defence alliance
Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa — a regional trade bloc
Commission on Migration and Economic Security for Africa — a development fund
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa — a regional trade bloc
acceptableAnswers: Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa — a regional trade bloc
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: The key word is "Common Market".
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: COMESA is the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa, a regional economic community promoting trade and investment among its member states. Mauritius is a member and benefits from preferential trade access.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Why is Mauritius a member of both SADC and COMESA, two regional bodies that partly overlap geographically?
options: The two organisations have identical rules, so membership of one automatically confers membership of the other
Membership of multiple organisations maximises trade access and diplomatic influence for a small state
International law requires every African country to join all regional bodies
SADC and COMESA have never had any overlapping members
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Membership of multiple organisations maximises trade access and diplomatic influence for a small state
acceptableAnswers: Membership of multiple organisations maximises trade access and diplomatic influence for a small state
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: A small country gains more from multiple memberships than from exclusivity.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: A small island state gains wider market access and stronger diplomatic standing by belonging to multiple regional bodies. Despite some duplication, each membership opens different trade preferences and forums.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: How does membership of the Indian Ocean Commission (IOC) benefit Mauritius?
options: It gives Mauritius the right to claim all ocean resources within 5 000 km
It enables cooperation with neighbouring island states on environmental, economic and security issues
It automatically settles all maritime sovereignty disputes in Mauritius's favour
It requires France to pay compensation for its former colonial rule
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: It enables cooperation with neighbouring island states on environmental, economic and security issues
acceptableAnswers: It enables cooperation with neighbouring island states on environmental, economic and security issues
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Regional bodies are about cooperation, not unilateral rights.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The Indian Ocean Commission brings Mauritius, Réunion, Comoros, Madagascar and Seychelles together for joint management of environmental challenges, economic opportunities and regional security.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: What is a preferential trade agreement and how does Mauritius benefit from having one with the European Union?
options: It means EU countries automatically invest in Mauritian infrastructure projects
It requires Mauritius to buy all its imports exclusively from EU member states
It allows Mauritian goods to enter the EU market with lower or zero tariffs, making them more competitive than non-member exports
It gives Mauritius the right to set all tariff rates for goods entering the EU from any country
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: It allows Mauritian goods to enter the EU market with lower or zero tariffs, making them more competitive than non-member exports
acceptableAnswers: It allows Mauritian goods to enter the EU market with lower or zero tariffs, making them more competitive than non-member exports
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Preferential = better than the standard terms.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: A preferential trade agreement reduces tariff barriers for Mauritian exports — sugar, textiles, seafood — giving them a price advantage over competitors from outside the agreement in the EU market.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Sugar cultivation belongs to which sector of the economy?
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: The primary sector
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: The primary sector extracts or grows raw materials directly from nature.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Growing sugar cane involves taking directly from the land, making it primary sector activity. Processing it into refined sugar would be secondary; selling it in a shop would be tertiary.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: The quaternary sector is sometimes listed as a fourth economic sector. Which activity belongs to it?
options: Research and development, information technology and knowledge-based services
Assembling mobile phones in a factory
Selling those phones in a retail shop
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Research and development, information technology and knowledge-based services
acceptableAnswers: Research and development, information technology and knowledge-based services
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: The quaternary sector deals in knowledge and innovation, not goods.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The quaternary sector covers knowledge-intensive activities — ICT, research, consulting, finance. As Mauritius moves up the value chain, this sector is becoming increasingly important.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: Which of the four factors of production refers to human effort in the production process?
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Labour
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: It is the human input — what workers provide.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: Labour is the human effort — physical or mental — that contributes to production. Land provides natural resources; capital is machinery and buildings; enterprise is the organising and risk-taking function.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: A new technology company sets up in Mauritius. Which factor of production does the company's founding entrepreneur represent?
options: Capital — since the entrepreneur provides the startup funding
Enterprise — organising the other factors and taking the risk of the venture
Labour — since the entrepreneur also works in the company
Land — since the entrepreneur owns the office building
grade9-social-modern-studies.answer: Enterprise — organising the other factors and taking the risk of the venture
acceptableAnswers: Enterprise — organising the other factors and taking the risk of the venture
grade9-social-modern-studies.hint: Enterprise is the factor that brings the others together.
grade9-social-modern-studies.explanation: The enterprise factor is provided by the entrepreneur who organises land, labour and capital, makes strategic decisions and accepts the financial risk of starting the business.

grade9-social-modern-studies.question: A clothing manufacturer wants to open a new factory in Mauritius. Which factor would most influence the choice of location?
options: The colour of the buildings in the nearest village
Proximity to a labour supply and good road links to the port
The number of primary schools within 50 km
The age of the district's oldest resident
